Marcel Duchamp adopted this feminine persona for photographs made by Man Ray and used it as a pseudonym in his art. The persona is also associated with Duchamp’s readymade Why Not Sneeze? What was the name?
Rrose Sélavy appears in portraits in which Marcel Duchamp posed in feminine clothing. Which American artist and photographer took those portraits, and was also known for his Dada and Surrealist work?
A three-story pavilion in Kyoto’s Rokuon-ji complex stands beside Mirror Pond, with its upper two stories covered in gold leaf. What is this landmark commonly known by its Japanese name?

Kinkaku-ji inspired the setting of a Japanese novel centered on novice Mizoguchi, who ultimately sets the pavilion on fire. The novel’s author also wrote *Confessions of a Mask* and died by seppuku after a failed coup; who was he?

What drawing technique builds tone by laying one set of strokes over another so the lines intersect, with denser intersections producing darker shadows and textured depth? It is commonly used in pencil illustration and printmaking.

In contrast to cross-hatching, what shading method uses parallel strokes running in one direction, with their spacing or density adjusted to make areas appear lighter or darker? Its strokes do not cross a second set of lines.

Archaic Greek kouroi often place one leg forward in a stiff advancing pose, echoing earlier Egyptian statuary. What human action did this pose suggest and that Alberto Giacometti later explored in his elongated figures?
Within the sculptural theme of Walking, which Swiss sculptor became known for tall, attenuated figures that seem to stride forward, including a famous 1960 bronze of a solitary man?
This American architect and urban planner coauthored a 1909 blueprint for Chicago and helped organize the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition. What was his name?

Daniel Burnham and Edward H. Bennett prepared a 1909 civic proposal for the Illinois metropolis on Lake Michigan, featuring radial boulevards, parks, and a redesigned lakefront. By what title is this proposal commonly known?

This Austrian Symbolist painter became the first president of the Vienna Secession in 1897. He is known for using real gold leaf in ornate works such as a painting of two lovers embracing on a flower-covered cliff. Who was he?
Gustav Klimt created this three-wall allegorical cycle for a 1902 Vienna Secession exhibition. It honored the composer whose Ninth Symphony inspired it. What is this work called?

Composed in 1876 in support of the Serbian people during their conflict with the Ottoman Empire, this patriotic orchestral march draws on Serbian folk melodies and later quotes the Russian imperial anthem “God Save the Tsar.” What is the work’s title?
Marche slave was written by the Russian composer who also created the 1812 Overture, The Nutcracker, and the Sixth Symphony, commonly known as the Pathétique. Who was this composer?

In July 1937, the Nazi regime opened a Munich exhibition of confiscated modern artworks, displaying them in a deliberately mocking arrangement. What familiar English name is given to this campaign and exhibition?
A German veteran of World War I, this painter created the antiwar triptych *The War* and the 1926 portrait *Sylvia von Harden*. Which artist’s works were condemned in the Degenerate Art campaign?
A winged, pensive figure sits among tools, a truncated polyhedron, a sphere, and a magic square in a 1514 engraving often associated with intellectual frustration. What is the title of this work?

In Melencolia I, a winged figure surrounded by tools and geometric forms appears in a famous 1514 engraving. Which German Renaissance artist created this print and also produced Knight, Death, and the Devil?

In a major scale built on G, this note is the second scale degree, and its natural minor key has no sharps or flats. An oboe traditionally sounds it to give an orchestra its tuning reference. What is the note?

Orchestras commonly use the musical note A as a tuning reference; under standard concert pitch, the reference is set to 440 Hz in the octave immediately above middle C. What is this pitch designation?
This American jazz pianist, composer, and arranger worked for decades with Duke Ellington and wrote the orchestra’s enduring theme about the quickest way to reach Harlem. Who was he?

Billy Strayhorn was the longtime collaborator of this bandleader, whose orchestra was associated with Harlem’s Cotton Club. A Paul Gonsalves solo during the bandleader’s 1956 Newport Jazz Festival performance of “Diminuendo and Crescendo in Blue” helped revive his career; who was he?

Which Italian Baroque painter became renowned for dramatic chiaroscuro and naturalistic religious scenes? He painted both *The Cardsharps* and a scene in which a shaft of light illuminates a tax collector as Christ calls him.
In a painting by Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, Christ gestures toward a bearded tax collector seated at a table while a beam of light cuts into the dim room. What is the title of this work?
What 1940 jazz standard, introduced in the Broadway revue *Two for the Show*, was composed by Morgan Lewis with lyrics by Nancy Hamilton?
*How High the Moon* was introduced in the 1940 Broadway revue *Two for the Show* and was written by a pair of collaborators. Nancy Hamilton wrote its lyrics; which composer supplied its music?

Which leading ancient Greek sculptor created the chryselephantine statue of Athena Parthenos and was renowned for monumental cult statues? He was also entrusted with supervising major sculpture projects in Athens during the age of Pericles.

Phidias supervised major sculptures for this temple dedicated to Athena, which stands on the Acropolis in Athens. Designed by Ictinus and Callicrates, it was badly damaged by an ammunition explosion in 1687; what is the temple called?

This American composer and lyricist wrote the score for a 1934 Broadway musical set aboard an ocean liner, where “You’re the Top” and “I Get a Kick Out of You” became signature numbers. He also wrote “Night and Day”; who was he?
Cole Porter wrote this song for the 1935 Broadway musical Jubilee, and Artie Shaw’s 1938 big-band recording helped make it a hit. What song is it?
Which ballet, premiered in St. Petersburg in 1890 and choreographed by Marius Petipa, follows Princess Aurora after the fairy Carabosse curses her and the Lilac Fairy helps protect her?
The Sleeping Beauty’s score was written by which Russian Romantic composer, who also composed Swan Lake and The Nutcracker?
An Austrian late-Romantic composer, he wrote expansive symphonies and song cycles including *Kindertotenlieder* and *Das Lied von der Erde*. Who was this composer?

Which work by Gustav Mahler includes a movement titled “The Solitary One in Autumn” and a scherzo-like third movement that makes extensive use of the pentatonic scale? Its six movements evoke the beauty of nature.

Born in 1898, this American sculptor first trained as a mechanical engineer before developing both moving abstract constructions and fixed monumental forms. He created the 53-foot red steel stabile *Flamingo*, unveiled in Chicago in 1974. Who was he?

Alexander Calder used his engineering training to make abstract sculptures whose suspended parts shift in response to air currents, unlike his stationary stabiles. What name did Marcel Duchamp give to these moving works?

Which French painter, born in 1798, became a leading figure of the Romantic school and favored dramatic subjects, expressive brushwork, and bold color? He created The Barque of Dante and The Death of Sardanapalus.
Eugène Delacroix painted this 1830 canvas in response to the July Revolution in France. An allegorical woman in a Phrygian cap raises the tricolor above a barricade as fighters advance around her.

After traveling in North Africa, Eugène Delacroix painted this 1834 scene of three female figures in a richly furnished room, with a hookah nearby and a servant at the doorway. What is the painting called?
Commonly made from hickory or maple, these handheld, tapered percussion implements are often used in pairs to strike drumheads and cymbals. What are they called?
Some drumsticks replace the usual wooden tip with a molded synthetic one, often chosen for a brighter, more consistent sound on cymbals. What material is used for this type of tip?

At Kyoto’s Ryōan-ji, visitors look from a veranda across pale gravel and a sparse arrangement of stones, with no pond or dense planting. What traditional Japanese landscape-design form uses such restrained dry compositions to evoke landscapes and water?

The best-known Japanese rock garden stands at a Kyoto Zen temple whose name is often translated as “Temple of the Peaceful Dragon.” Its fifteen stones are arranged in five groups across a bed of white gravel. What is the temple?

Founded in 1848 by John Everett Millais, Dante Gabriel Rossetti, and William Holman Hunt, this English artists’ movement favored vivid color, meticulous natural detail, and compositions inspired by early Italian painting. What was the movement called?

A leading work associated with the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood shows a young woman from Shakespeare’s *Hamlet* floating in a stream, surrounded by flowers, after drowning. Painted by John Everett Millais, what is this painting called?

Two monumental standing Buddhist figures were carved into cliffside niches in central Afghanistan in the sixth century. The Taliban destroyed them in 2001; what is the collective name of these sculptures?
The Buddhas of Bamiyan were carved into a cliff in the Hindu Kush region of which landlocked country? Its capital is Kabul.

Emerging in the United States after World War II, this movement emphasized spontaneous gestures, emotional intensity, and the physical process of making art. It became internationally influential in the 1950s, with artists including Jackson Pollock and Mark Rothko. What was the movement called?
In 1946, this critic applied the term Abstract Expressionism to American art. Who was he?
Which critic described the canvas in Abstract Expressionism as an “arena in which to act,” a phrase associated with action painting?

Born in West Chester, Pennsylvania, in 1910, this American composer created an orchestral elegy adapted from the second movement of his String Quartet, Op. 11. He also won the Pulitzer Prize for Music for an opera that premiered at the Metropolitan Opera in 1958. Who was he?

Which orchestral work by Samuel Barber was premiered in 1938 by Arturo Toscanini and the NBC Symphony Orchestra? Adapted from the slow central movement of Barber’s 1936 quartet, it later became a widely performed memorial piece.
Written in 1895 by Banjo Paterson, this Australian folk song follows a wandering bush worker camping beside a billabong who steals a jumbuck. What is the song’s title?
In Waltzing Matilda, the central wanderer carries his belongings in a bundle over his shoulder and camps beside a waterhole before making off with a sheep. What is this itinerant bush worker called?

This Native Hawaiian performance tradition expresses mele through movement, with gestures portraying natural scenes such as waves and trees or feelings such as affection and longing. It may be performed seated or standing and has served storytelling and ceremonial purposes. What is this dance practice?

One of Hula’s two principal categories preserves a pre-Western style, using chant and traditional instruments rather than the songs and Western instruments associated with later forms. What is this category?
This later category of Hula developed under Western influence and is commonly accompanied by songs and instruments such as guitar, ʻukulele, and double bass. What is this category?
This Wisconsin home and studio of a leading American architect was rebuilt several times after fires and is associated with both Prairie and Usonian work. What is the name of the estate?
Taliesin was the Wisconsin home and studio of which architect, who also designed Fallingwater and built a later studio in the Arizona desert?

Which Russian Romantic composer began his education for a civil-service career before graduating from the Saint Petersburg Conservatory in 1865? His works include the First Piano Concerto and the Sixth Symphony known as the Pathétique.

Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky wrote this ceremonial work to commemorate Russia’s defense against Napoleon in 1812. Its finale is known for cannon fire and a musical clash between “La Marseillaise” and “God Save the Tsar.” What is the work?
In Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky’s ballet, Odette is cursed by Rothbart, and the sorcerer’s daughter Odile impersonates her at a ball. What ballet features these characters?

In this Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky ballet, Clara’s godfather Drosselmeyer stages a midnight battle between soldiers and mice. Clara then travels with her companion to the Kingdom of Sweets. What ballet is it?

Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky adapted this opera from a verse novel by Alexander Pushkin. It includes a scene in which the shy Tatyana writes a letter to a worldly aristocrat, and a duel in which the poet Lensky is killed. What is the opera’s title?

Charles Ives’s 1908 orchestral work places sustained, contemplative strings beneath recurring trumpet calls, while a small woodwind group offers increasingly discordant replies. What is this composition called?
In The Unanswered Question, four players from which high-pitched woodwind instrument family provide the increasingly agitated replies to the trumpet’s statements?
What rich yellow hue evokes a warm metallic sheen and takes its name from a precious metal? Artists often use this color to make important figures stand out.

In works such as *Judith Beheading Holofernes* and *Salome with the Head of John the Baptist*, this Italian Baroque painter used gold-colored dresses to emphasize her female protagonists. She also created *Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting*. Who was she?
Which European artistic period followed the Renaissance and preceded Rococo, becoming known for dramatic compositions, ornate detail, emotional intensity, and rich textures?
During the Baroque period, which Italian painter created a dramatic scene of Judith and her maidservant killing Holofernes and also painted herself as the Allegory of Painting?

W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan’s comic opera follows a young man whom a nursemaid mistakenly apprentices to a band of sea raiders rather than to a pilot. He is expected to serve until his twenty-first birthday; what is the title of this work?
In The Pirates of Penzance, whose apprenticeship to a pirate band began when Ruth mistook the word “pilot,” and whose February 29 birth means his indenture lasts until his eighty-fourth year?

What is the name of Maurice Ravel’s three-movement solo piano suite based on prose poems by Aloysius Bertrand? Its movements are titled “Ondine,” “Le Gibet,” and “Scarbo,” with the last being a notoriously difficult virtuoso showpiece.
In Gaspard de la nuit, the technically punishing finale depicts a goblin-like sprite and was conceived as a challenge to surpass Balakirev’s Islamey. Which French composer wrote the suite?

Born in Baghdad in 1950, this Iraqi-born British architect became the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2004. Her designs include the Guangzhou Opera House and London Aquatics Centre. Who was she?

Zaha Hadid’s first full-scale realized building was completed in 1993 on a furniture company’s campus in Weil am Rhein, Germany. Its sharply angled concrete forms brought her experimental designs into built architecture. What is the name of this building?

This early-20th-century movement began in Paris and was pioneered by two painters who broke subjects into geometric facets rather than showing them from a single fixed viewpoint. Its artists reassembled objects through multiple perspectives, creating deliberately fragmented images. What is the movement?

This French painter worked with Picasso to pioneer Cubism and painted Houses at L’Estaque, a landscape whose geometric houses helped prompt a critic to describe the work as being made of cubes. Who was the artist?

This large monochrome anti-war painting applies Cubism’s fractured forms to the 1937 bombing of a Basque town during the Spanish Civil War. Its imagery includes a wounded horse, a bull, and a woman mourning her child. What is the painting?

This Spanish painter became a leading figure in Cubism, developing carefully ordered still lifes with crisp, interlocking planes. He is also associated with the movement’s so-called crystal phase. Who was the artist?
A body of paintings based on Mercedes-Benz models was later extended through commissions involving BMW and Daimler. What is the title by which this automobile-centered series is known?
In Andy Warhol’s Cars, the BMW commission was based on a Group 4 racing coupe and became the fourth vehicle in BMW’s Art Car project. Which model did Warhol paint in 1979?

In this history painting, a victorious commander accepts the keys of a Dutch stronghold from its defeated governor, while ranks of soldiers and a forest of upright pikes fill the background. What work by Diego Velázquez commemorates the stronghold’s capitulation in 1625?

In The Surrender of Breda, the central commander receives the keys from Justin of Nassau with a gesture often read as magnanimous rather than humiliating. What Genoese-born general led the Spanish forces that captured the Dutch city in 1625?

This German-American modernist architect designed Chicago’s Lake Shore Drive Apartments and helped shape the International Style. He also led the Bauhaus during its final years before moving to the United States; who was he?
Ludwig Mies van der Rohe was the final director of this German school of art, design, and architecture, founded by Walter Gropius in 1919 and closed in 1933. What was the school called?
This famous floor artwork was found in the House of the Faun in Pompeii and depicts a Macedonian king pursuing the Persian ruler Darius III. What is it called?
In the Alexander Mosaic, Alexander’s Macedonian forces confront Darius III’s Persian army in a battle fought in 333 BCE near the Gulf of İskenderun. What battle does the mosaic portray?

Completed in 1804, this expansive Beethoven work in E-flat major, Op. 55, places a funeral march between its forceful opening movement and scherzo, then closes with variations on material from his ballet *The Creatures of Prometheus*. What is the work’s best-known title?

At the public premiere of Beethoven’s Symphony No. 3 in E-flat major, Op. 55, at Vienna’s Theater an der Wien in 1805, which nobleman was the work’s documented dedicatee, despite its earlier association with Napoleon?
This fretted string instrument is central to Spanish flamenco and appears in many Mexican musical traditions. Related regional forms include the vihuela and bajo sexto; what is the instrument?
In norteño music from northern Mexico, this large, typically 12-string guitar is often paired with the accordion and provides bass and rhythmic accompaniment. What is this instrument called?
Richard Strauss’s comic opera, with a libretto by Hugo von Hofmannsthal, centers on the Marschallin, Octavian, and Sophie. What is the opera in which Octavian presents Sophie with a silver rose?

The composer and librettist of Der Rosenkavalier also created an opera about a princess who seeks vengeance for her father Agamemnon’s murder. She is the sister of Orestes, and the opera is named for her. What is its title?

Born in Tuscany, this Italian polymath trained in Florence under Andrea del Verrocchio, later worked for Ludovico Sforza in Milan, and spent his final years in France. Which Renaissance artist created the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper?

Leonardo da Vinci painted this large refectory mural at Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, arranging the apostles in animated groups as Jesus announces that one of them will betray him. What work depicts this meal?

In a notebook drawing by Leonardo da Vinci, a nude male figure appears in two overlapping poses, with his limbs fitting both a circle and a square. The image explores human proportions in relation to ideas attributed to the Roman architect Vitruvius; what drawing is it?

Leonardo da Vinci’s portrait of a Florentine woman, traditionally identified as the wife of silk merchant Francesco del Giocondo, hangs in the Louvre and is famous for the sitter’s enigmatic expression and distant landscape. What painting is this?

Leonardo da Vinci painted Cecilia Gallerani in a portrait now held at the Czartoryski Museum in Kraków; she holds a white-furred animal with a slender body against her chest. What is the painting’s established English title?

What title belongs to Norman Rockwell’s painting series that turned principles from Franklin D. Roosevelt’s January 6, 1941 address to Congress into scenes of everyday life? The Saturday Evening Post published the paintings in 1943, each accompanied by an essay.
In Norman Rockwell’s The Four Freedoms, which panel depicts a festive meal shared by three generations? The people posing as the family in this scene were not all biologically related.

In Jewish holiday customs, what term refers to money traditionally given to children, especially during Hanukkah? It is also commonly represented by foil-wrapped chocolate coins used in dreidel games.

During Hanukkah, gelt may be wagered on this spinning top, which bears Hebrew letters corresponding to the phrase “A great miracle happened there” in many diaspora versions. What is this game piece called?
What singular term describes a child whose parents have died or are permanently absent? This status means the child no longer has parental care from either parent.
In Lemony Snicket’s darkly comic novel series, Violet, Klaus, and Sunny become orphans after a fire destroys their home and then face Count Olaf’s schemes. What is the name of this series?
Cultivated in flooded paddies and also on dry uplands, this annual grass produces a grain eaten as a staple by more than half the world’s population. What is this crop called?
The rice plant grown widely across Asia is an annual, semi-aquatic grass, distinct from the African domesticated rice species. What is the scientific name of the Asian species?
Made by infusing processed leaves of Camellia sinensis, this beverage became deeply established in Chinese culture during the Song period. What is it?

Tea cultivation and consumption became deeply established in China during which dynasty, whose reformer Wang Anshi implemented the baojia system of local law enforcement? The dynasty was later defeated by Kublai Khan and replaced by the Yuan.

In city-states that used the drachma and held festivals such as the Panathenaia, paid sexual services took several forms; some women known for cultured companionship worked independently or in brothels. What aspect of everyday life does this describe?
In Ancient Greek prostitution, what term described women who provided paid companionship and could work independently or in brothels?

When feudal lordships and the Latin Church shaped everyday life, rulers and mints across many kingdoms issued metal money in denominations for purchases and obligations. This historical subject also encompasses the small-denomination pieces invoked in a famous criticism of indulgence fundraising. What is the subject?

In accounts of Medieval European Coinage, a traditional criticism of indulgence payments claimed that a sound in the collection chest marked a soul’s release. What inexpensive small-denomination pieces with a reddish cast, unlike silver issues, does the saying refer to?
What early-childhood educational level typically comes before first grade and takes its name from a German phrase meaning “children’s garden”?
Which 19th-century German educator coined the name kindergarten in 1840 and promoted learning through play and hands-on activities for young children?
In the Jazz Age of the 1920s, what name was given to young women associated with shorter skirts, bobbed hair, and greater social freedom?
Among hairstyles associated with flappers, what short, close-cropped style did Josephine Baker popularize in the 1920s?

What dairy beverage is a colloid in which fat globules and other particles are dispersed throughout water? Homogenization is commonly used during its production to keep the fat from separating into a cream layer.

In processing milk, what treatment forces it through tiny openings under pressure to break large fat globules into smaller ones? This helps keep the fat evenly dispersed rather than allowing cream to rise to the top.
Made by churning cream, this dairy fat is commonly spread on bread and used to cook foods. Combined with flour, it also forms the traditional base of a roux; what ingredient is it?
In classic sauce-making, butter is cooked with flour in roughly equal proportions to form a thickening base, which may be cooked to a pale, blond, or darker color. What is this preparation called?
This U.S. ten-cent coin has featured Franklin D. Roosevelt on its obverse since 1946. Its reverse shows a torch flanked by olive and oak branches in a design by John R. Sinnock. What is this coin?

Before the Roosevelt portrait appeared on the United States dime in 1946, its obverse showed a liberty goddess wearing a winged cap. What familiar nickname is given to that earlier design, whose winged cap led observers to mistake the liberty figure for a male classical deity?
This variety of legume has tan seeds marked with reddish-brown speckles, which often fade during cooking. It is widely eaten in Mexico and is frequently used in traditional dishes.
Pinto beans are often the base for this Mexican preparation, in which cooked beans are mashed and seasoned, then served as a side dish or filling for other foods.

What dietary practice is centered on plant foods and excludes meat, poultry, and seafood, while some versions still permit eggs and dairy? People may follow it for ethical, religious, environmental, or health-related reasons.
Within vegetarianism, what stricter dietary pattern uses only plant foods and excludes eggs and dairy as well as meat, poultry, and seafood?
Founded in Jeffersonville, Indiana, this American restaurant chain built its brand around the slogan “Better Ingredients. Better Pizza.” What company is it?
From 2010 through 2018, Papa John's was the official pizza of this U.S. professional sports league, whose teams compete for the Lombardi Trophy. Which league was it?

Aunt Polly assigns Tom Sawyer a chore that gives the household's wooden boundary a bright, chalky finish, but he makes the punishment seem like a privilege and persuades other boys to take turns. What is the chore called?
In the episode Whitewashing a Fence, Tom persuades this boy that working on the fence is a special privilege rather than a chore. Which boy offers Tom an apple to get his turn?
This amusement-park ride sends a train of cars along a fixed track through hills, drops, and turns, sometimes using a lift hill or launch to give it starting energy. What kind of ride is it?
In 1884, this influential early American roller coaster opened at Coney Island and helped LaMarcus Thompson establish the gravity-ride industry. What was the ride called?

In Britain and many former colonies, this convention has motorists use the side of a two-way road opposite the one customary in the United States. Cars designed for it generally place the steering wheel on the vehicle's right. What is this road-traffic convention called?

In 2009, which Pacific island nation changed from driving on the right to adopting left-hand traffic? The switch was intended in part to make it easier for residents to obtain cars imported from Australia and New Zealand.
Chef Carly Pii created this brightly colored bottled condiment, which drew notoriety when early bottles were shipped unrefrigerated despite containing dairy. What was this product called?
Pink Sauce gets its vivid hue from the edible growth of a tropical cactus blended with honey. Its white or magenta flesh is dotted with tiny black seeds. What is this ingredient called?

Mammals are characterized by this feature, which is produced by follicles in the dermis. In people, follicles make both fine vellus strands and thicker terminal strands, and the material is composed largely of a structural protein. What is this body feature called?

Human hair consists chiefly of a fibrous protein whose chains coil into a helical structure; this protein also contributes to the structure of nails and the outer layer of skin. What is this protein called?
In Sikh practice, people who keep human hair uncut as a religious commitment may use one of the Five Ks, a small wooden comb carried to keep it neat. What is this comb called?

Georges Perec’s Oulipo novel *A Void* is famously written without this letter. In music, the major key named for it has four sharps, and its lowercase form represents the base of natural logarithms. What is the fifth letter of the English alphabet?
The letter E is conspicuously absent from *A Void*, a lipogrammatic novel originally published in French as *La Disparition* in 1969. Which Oulipo writer authored it?

During a winter holiday, many households display an evergreen decorated with lights and ornaments, often topped with a star or angel. In the ballet The Nutcracker, this festive centerpiece grows to enormous size.
In this ballet by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, a Christmas tree grows gigantic during the first-act celebration as midnight arrives and mice fill the room. What ballet is it?
What consumer service lets people borrow films, television programs, or games for a limited time rather than buying them, often through a store or kiosk?
Which company challenged Blockbuster’s video rental business by mailing DVDs to customers in distinctive red envelopes before becoming known for streaming series such as *Stranger Things*?

What form of payment lets shoppers make purchases against a borrowing account, with the charges later appearing on a statement for repayment? Its familiar plastic form commonly includes a magnetic stripe or EMV chip and a three-digit security code.
On Visa credit cards, what three-digit security value printed in the signature panel is commonly requested for card-not-present purchases? It is distinct from both the card number and the PIN.

Serrano, jalapeño, and poblano are familiar varieties of this culinary ingredient, while Hatch types are associated with New Mexico and the Carolina Reaper is known for its extreme heat. What broad food category do these varieties belong to?
Among chile peppers, which New Mexico variety is named for a village that holds an annual festival celebrating its harvest, and is often roasted at roadside stands in late summer?

Robert F. Kennedy was shot at the Ambassador in Los Angeles, and Martin Luther King Jr. was killed at the Lorraine in Memphis; both were commercial lodging properties serving travelers. The Washington Hilton is another example of this kind of establishment—what is its common name?

In 1964, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Congress could apply the Civil Rights Act to a Georgia hotel that served interstate travelers and refused lodging to Black guests, rejecting the owner's Commerce Clause challenge. What case is associated with this ruling?
answer: Heart of Atlanta Motel, Inc. v. United States

question: What common household appliance keeps food cold by removing heat from an insulated compartment and releasing it into the surrounding room? It uses a reversed heat-pump process to move that heat.

In a refrigerator’s cooling loop, which heat exchanger absorbs heat from the storage compartment as the circulating refrigerant evaporates? It is on the cold side of the system, unlike the warm-side exchanger that releases heat into the room.

Made from wax or another combustible material around a wick, these portable lights produce a flame when lit and are used in religious observances, celebrations, and power outages. What are they called?

During Kwanzaa, seven candles representing the seven principles are arranged on a special holder, with a black candle in the center, three red candles on one side, and three green candles on the other. What is this holder called?

In 2014, Maine’s highest court ruled that a school district violated state law by barring a transgender girl from using the facility matching her gender identity. What type of shared sanitation facility was the subject of that landmark decision?

After Gloucester County’s school board barred him from the boys’ bathrooms, this Virginia transgender student sued in a closely watched case that reached the U.S. Supreme Court in 2017. Which person’s fight over Public Restrooms is being described?

What activity is the pursuit of wild animals as game, practiced both for recreation and as a profession? It is central to Saki’s “The Interlopers” and gives Richard Connell’s “The Most Dangerous Game” its deadly premise.

In this Richard Connell story, a professional hunter is stranded on Ship-Trap Island, where his aristocratic host turns hunting into a contest in which humans are the prey. What is the title of the work?
This traditional Japanese garment is made with straight seams and wraps left side over right. Extra fabric can be folded beneath the waist sash to adjust its length. What is this garment called?
On a kimono, what is the name of the sash wrapped around the waist to hold the garment in place?
Items in this everyday-life category are worn to cover or adorn the body. Their absence is associated with the “sky-clad” ascetic practice of some Digambara Jains. What is this category?
Clothing is renounced by some male ascetics in one of Jainism’s two major sects, whose name means “sky-clad”; the other major sect is Svetambara. What is this sect?

What baked dessert has a pastry crust enclosing a filling, with familiar varieties made from pecans, pumpkin custard, or Key lime? In the United States, it is often served in wedges and is strongly associated with Thanksgiving.

Which pie associated with the Florida Keys is made with juice from the region’s small, aromatic citrus fruit and sweetened condensed milk in a tart filling, commonly set in a graham-cracker crust? It is often finished with whipped cream or meringue.

What recurring periodicals report current events, with The Daily Mail and The New York Times as well-known examples? A character in Harold Pinter’s The Dumb Waiter reads a report about a car accident in one.

In which absurdist play by Harold Pinter do hitmen Ben and Gus wait in a basement as food orders arrive through a service hatch? During the play, one of them reads a car-accident report in newspapers.

After studying at Le Cordon Bleu in Paris, this American cook coauthored the 1961 volume *Mastering the Art of French Cooking* with Simone Beck and Louisette Bertholle. She later brought French techniques into American homes as host of the PBS series *The French Chef*; who was she?

Julia Child hosted this WGBH cooking series beginning in 1963, demonstrating recipes from her Cambridge home kitchen, which is now preserved at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History. What was the series called?

This psychoactive plant contains cannabinoids, including THC, which can alter brain activity and produce a high. Its dried flowers and leaves are used in a range of preparations. What is the plant commonly called?

In South Asian religious and cultural practices, Cannabis can be prepared as an edible mixture and sometimes blended into a drink. This preparation is associated with some Holi observances and Hindu traditions connected to Shiva. What is it called?
Before pursuing a dream of treasure, Santiago earns his living guiding a flock through the Spanish countryside and caring for the sheep. What traditional pastoral occupation does he practice?

In Paulo Coelho’s *The Alchemist*, Santiago is a young shepherd who repeatedly dreams of treasure near the Egyptian pyramids and meets people who encourage him to pursue his fate. What does the novel call the unique destiny each individual is meant to fulfill?
Casinos, lotteries, sports books, and private card tables all offer this activity, in which participants risk money or other valuables on uncertain outcomes. What is this broad form of recreation?

In gambling, players place bets on a felt layout while a croupier spins a numbered wheel and sends a small ball around its rim. The winning result is determined by the pocket where the ball comes to rest. What is this casino game?
Jim Dillingham Young owns a valuable gold example of this portable timekeeping device, which he sells to buy a gift for Della. What is the object?
In O. Henry’s short story, Jim sells his gold watch to buy a set of hair combs for Della, while she sells her long hair to buy a chain for his watch. What is the story’s title?
This trained emergency responder uses specialized equipment to control fires, protect people from smoke and heat, and rescue those in danger. What occupation is responsible for these duties?

In Ray Bradbury’s dystopian novel, a firefighter works in a society where his crew burns books instead of extinguishing fires. After meeting Clarisse McClellan, the protagonist begins questioning his role; what is his name?
What color is associated with calmness and reduced aggressiveness, and whose Baker-Miller shade was studied for a possible effect on violence in correctional settings?
Which researcher helped popularize claims about Pink’s calming effects by advocating tests of the Baker-Miller shade in correctional facilities?
Founded in 1851 by Henry Jarvis Raymond and George Jones, this American daily newspaper became known for its national and international reporting. Its crossword debuted in 1942. What is its name?

In 2022, The New York Times added this popular game to its Games portfolio. Players have six attempts to guess a five-letter word, with colored tiles showing whether each letter is correct and in the right position. What is the game?

In June 1970, one year after the Stonewall uprising, LGBTQ+ activists held public commemorative marches in cities including New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago. What name is commonly given to these celebrations of LGBTQ+ identity, community, and progress?

The first Pride parades in 1970 commemorated protests in Greenwich Village in late June 1969, which followed a police raid on a popular gay bar and helped catalyze the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement. What is the name of that event?
What name is given to the traditional rural horsemen of Argentina and Uruguay’s plains, whose improvised payada ballads influenced José Hernández’s epic poem Martín Fierro?
Besides the Pampas, what vast southern region—extending from the Colorado River to Tierra del Fuego—was also home to gauchos and is associated with the Indigenous Tehuelche people?

Founded in Seattle in 1971 as a retailer of coffee beans and equipment, this company later became an international coffeehouse chain. Its unionization efforts have drawn attention from the Jorts social-media account. What is the company’s name?

At Starbucks, former CEO Howard Schultz accused a federal agency of improperly influencing union votes. Established under the Wagner Act, this agency oversees workplace rules and union representation matters. What is its name?

Founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, this U.S. technology company built a digital marketplace that matches riders with independent drivers. It later expanded from passenger trips into local delivery. What is the company’s name?

Uber Technologies, Inc. also connects customers with local restaurants, grocers, and other merchants through a service that matches orders with delivery couriers. What is the name of this delivery brand?

In Mexican cuisine, this handheld dish consists of a tortilla folded around a filling. It can be topped with ingredients such as salsa, onion, cilantro, or lime, and comes in many regional varieties. What is it called?
In tacos, what thin, round flatbread—commonly made from corn or wheat flour—is warmed and folded around the filling?

This Swedish retailer began in Älmhult in 1943 and grew into a global furniture chain renowned for customer-assembled flat-pack products; its stores also sell Swedish-style meatballs. What company is being described?
IKEA was founded by this Swedish entrepreneur in 1943, initially as a small mail-order business selling goods such as pens and wallets before it expanded into furniture. Who was he?

What collective name is used for the many distinct Indigenous communities of the mainland continent and Tasmania, with their own languages, laws, customs, and identities, whose cultures predate European colonization? The term is distinct from that used for the Indigenous communities of the Torres Strait islands.

In descriptions of Aboriginal peoples of Australia, what culturally expansive concept refers to connected lands, waterways, and seas, and also encompasses law, language, spiritual belief, cultural practice, family, and identity?
Unlike sweet, sour, salty, and bitter, this basic taste is associated with glutamate and is often described as savory. What is its natural name?
In 1908, this Japanese chemist investigated the savory flavor of kombu broth and linked it to glutamate. Whose research helped establish umami as a distinct taste?

This staple baked food is usually made from flour and water. Charred crumbs found at Shubayqa 1 in Jordan show that people made an early form of it about 14,400 years ago, before farming became widespread. What is this food?
Charred crumbs provide evidence of bread-making at this archaeological site in Jordan about 14,400 years ago. What is the name of the site?
Typically made by fermenting malted barley or wheat and often flavored with hops, what alcoholic beverage is enjoyed around the world?
More than seven million liters of beer are served annually at Oktoberfest. In which southeastern German city, the capital of Bavaria, is the festival held?

A toy promotion tied to a Tim Burton superhero film was cancelled in 1992 because the movie was considered too graphic, and a later offer of Teenie Beanies led to crowd-control problems. What children’s combo, often packaged with a toy and offering choices such as Chicken McNuggets, was involved in these promotions?
In 2010, which California city passed an ordinance restricting free toys in children’s meals that failed specified nutrition standards, a measure associated with the McDonald’s Happy Meal?

Charles Lindbergh’s 1927 solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic and Amelia Earhart’s record-setting flights made them famous in this occupation. What is the occupational term for a person who operates an aircraft?
In 1927, the aviator Charles Lindbergh flew a custom-built Ryan monoplane nonstop from New York to Paris, winning the Orteig Prize. What was the aircraft’s name?
What natural staple fiber develops around the seeds of plants in the genus Gossypium and is harvested worldwide as a major textile crop? It has long been used to make clothing and household fabrics.

Cotton fiber is harvested from plants in what botanical genus? Its cultivated species include upland cotton, which supplies most of the world's cotton, and a species prized for extra-long staples used in Egyptian cotton.
In print, this typographic style inclines letters to the right and is commonly used to signal emphasis or titles. It was popularized in early printing by the Aldine Press. What is this style called?
The right-leaning type style called italics became widely known through a late-15th-century Venetian printing house founded by Aldus Manutius. By what name was Manutius's Venetian workshop known?
This device is mounted on a for-hire passenger car or another automobile and produces an audible warning to alert nearby pedestrians or drivers. What is this familiar road-safety device called?
In the orchestral work *An American in Paris*, four taxi horns evoke a familiar sound of Parisian street traffic. Which American composer wrote the work?

Founded as a single Chicago drugstore in 1901, this American pharmacy and retail chain grew into a nationwide operator with pharmacy counters and retail goods in its stores. Which company later partnered with Theranos to offer its blood-testing service in stores?

Walgreens partnered with this Silicon Valley blood-testing startup and planned to install its devices in stores. Its Edison analyzer was promoted as being able to run many tests using only a small finger-prick sample.

A celebrated Persian example bears the name of an Iranian town and has a central medallion with two lamp motifs; Hans Holbein also placed a red one on a table in *The Ambassadors*. What broad class of decorative floor textiles includes coverings used by Muslims during prayer?

Among Persian carpets, a 16th-century masterpiece was woven for the shrine of Shaykh Safi al-Din in northwestern Iran, and its central medallion is accompanied by two hanging-lamp motifs. What is this named textile?

This Swiss multinational food and beverage company sells products ranging from packaged foods to bottled water, including water sold under the Arrowhead brand. It has faced criticism over its environmental practices and supply-chain labor conditions. What company is it?

What term, coined by Jay Westerveld in a 1986 essay about hotel towel-reuse prompts, describes making environmental claims that create a greener image without matching action? The term is often used in criticism of Nestlé’s environmental marketing.
What familiar ionic compound is sprinkled on food as a seasoning and used in curing to draw moisture from provisions? Its everyday role has made it a staple of kitchens and food preservation.

In sodium chloride’s naturally occurring mineral form, salty water loses moisture and leaves crystals that commonly have cube-like shapes; thick deposits can become underground rock-salt beds. What is this evaporite mineral called?
This Gregorian-calendar holiday falls on January 1 and marks the start of a new calendar year. It is often welcomed with midnight celebrations and countdowns. What holiday is it?
A common custom associated with New Year's Day is to set a personal goal—such as exercising more or saving money—to pursue during the coming year. What is this kind of annual pledge called?
Which common daily habit involves drawing emissions from a tobacco product or electronic cigarette into the lungs? It can damage lung tissue and contribute to respiratory disease.

In discussions of Smoking and EVALI, investigators linked many cases of lung injury to the acetate form of a fat-soluble antioxidant found in some THC vaping products. Which substance is this, whose most prevalent form is alpha-tocopherol?

What kind of public facility keeps living animals in managed habitats for visitors to observe and supports education, research, and conservation? Guadalajara’s prominent example is noted for its extensive exhibit devoted to animals active at night.
At Guadalajara’s zoo, what is the name of the extensive exhibit area focused on animals adapted to nighttime activity? Its Spanish name refers to a place associated with nocturnal creatures.
What scented preparation is worn on the body and commonly classified by fragrance families such as chypre and fougère, as well as by aromatic-oil concentration, from eau de toilette to extrait?
Which 1921 perfume, composed by Ernest Beaux and noted for its prominent aldehydic floral character and minimalist rectangular bottle, became one of the most famous fragrances in fashion history?

Built around a long blade joined to a hilt, this hand-held weapon is controlled by a grip and often has a guard to protect the hand. Its blade may be straight or curved and designed for cutting, thrusting, or both. What is this weapon?
On a typical sword, what is the name of the fitting at the end of the grip opposite the blade? It can help balance the weapon and secure the hilt’s components.
What military aviation occupation involves flying combat aircraft designed to intercept and engage other aircraft? Those who hold it are trained for missions that establish control of the air.
In the 2022 sequel to *Top Gun*, what is the call sign of the veteran U.S. Navy fighter pilot who returns to the elite school to train a new generation of aviators for a dangerous mission?
What term describes the consumption of human flesh, a practice that appears in the Greek myths of Procne serving Tereus a meal made from their son Itys and Tantalus serving a human meal to the gods?

In Greek myth, cannibalism is central to the story of the king who served his son Pelops to the gods at a feast. For this crime, he was condemned to stand in water beneath fruit he could never reach; who was he?

This Korean staple is made by fermenting salted vegetables—most famously napa cabbage or radish—with seasonings such as garlic, ginger, and chili. What is this dish, often prepared in large batches for winter storage?
Kimchi is often prepared in a communal late-autumn activity in which families make large batches of vegetables to preserve for winter. What is the Korean name for this tradition?

What kind of public establishment is depicted in Vincent van Gogh’s 1888 Arles interior with a billiard table at its center? Such venues commonly serve coffee and other drinks, and may also offer light meals.
Which 1888 Vincent van Gogh painting, set in Arles, shows a billiard table in the middle of a vividly colored café interior after dark?

This taproot vegetable gives many versions of borscht their deep crimson color, and its pigments can stain hands and cutting boards. It is also commonly eaten roasted, pickled, or grated into salads. What is this vegetable?
Associated especially with Ukrainian and other Eastern European cuisines, this soup often gets its vivid red color from beet and may be served with sour cream and dill. What is this soup?

Founded by software engineer Rob Rhinehart, this food company develops nutritionally formulated meal replacements intended to cover a range of dietary needs. Its offerings have included ready-to-drink bottles, bars, and powdered mixes; what is the company’s name?
Soylent was founded by this software engineer and entrepreneur, who described his experiments with replacing conventional meals in a 2013 essay titled “How I Stopped Eating Food.” What is his name?
It is a piece of cloth marked with distinctive colors, patterns, or emblems and used to represent a nation, group, institution, or cause. What is this symbol called?
In Eugène Delacroix’s *Liberty Leading the People*, the central figure raises a flag above the barricades during the July Revolution of 1830. What national flag is she carrying?

This edible cereal grain is a staple food worldwide and is sold in varieties such as long-grain and basmati. It forms the base of Saudi kabsa and of pilaf-style dishes known as pulao; what ingredient is it?

In South Asian cooking, this dish centers on the rice grain combined with meat and aromatic spices, and it is associated with Mughal culinary traditions. Often assembled in layers before cooking, it is distinct from a simple pilaf; what dish is it?

People bring food from home and eat it informally in an open-air setting such as a park or the countryside, often sitting on the ground rather than at a dining table. What kind of meal or social gathering is this?
At a picnic, what small social insects may form orderly trails to crumbs or sugary spills, with workers following chemical scent trails back to their nest?
Developed at Washington State University in 1952 by crossing Bing and Van, this sweet stone-fruit cultivar has yellow skin with a red blush. What cultivar is it?
The Rainier cherry is a bicolored sweet cultivar, with yellow skin and a red blush. In which U.S. state was it developed?
This natural animal fiber is obtained primarily by shearing sheep and is valued in textiles for its warmth and ability to trap insulating air. What is this fiber?
In wool processing, this waxy substance from sheep’s sebaceous glands is removed during scouring and is also used in cosmetics and skin-care products. What is it called?

In Greek myth, Philomela conveyed Tereus’s crime to Procne by creating a cloth that told the story after he had cut out her tongue. Penelope famously delayed choosing a suitor by working on Laertes’s shroud by day and undoing it at night; what craft did both women use?

In Ghanaian weaving, this vividly patterned textile is traditionally made from narrow woven strips sewn together and is associated especially with Akan and Ewe communities. What is this ceremonial cloth called?

At fairs and amusement parks, this ride carries passengers in cabins along a circular path around a tall rotating frame, raising them high above the ground for views of the surroundings. What is this ride called?

This landmark Ferris wheel stands on the South Bank of the River Thames, opposite the Houses of Parliament. It opened to the public in 2000 as part of the millennium celebrations; what is its familiar name?

What kind of public-service building accepts letters and parcels for mailing and offers services such as stamps and mail collection? Historic examples include Dublin’s landmark on O’Connell Street, occupied during the 1916 uprising, and monumental mail-service buildings in New York City.
Among Ireland’s historic post offices, which building on O’Connell Street became the insurgents’ headquarters during the 1916 Easter Rising? Its façade still bears visible scars from the fighting.

This family of rice dishes is prepared by simmering rice in seasoned liquid, often with aromatics and additions such as meat or vegetables. Related names across cuisines include pulao and plov; what is this style of dish called?
In pilaf, cooks often toast rice with aromatics before simmering it until the liquid is absorbed. What savory liquid, commonly made from meat or vegetables, provides moisture and flavor?
What is the name of the hard, dense material chiefly obtained from elephant tusks and prized for intricate carving, including Chinese puzzle balls?

Carved ivory heads and other court objects from this African kingdom were taken during the 1897 British punitive expedition. Its cast-brass plaques and sculptures, often called “bronzes,” depict the kingdom’s oba rulers; what kingdom is this?

This lignin- and cellulose-rich material comes mainly from the stems and branches of trees and other woody plants. It is widely used for building houses, making furniture, and producing paper. What is this material?
In wood, soft-rot fungi secrete enzymes that break down a glucose polymer found in plant cell walls. What is this polymer?

What sweet, chiefly sucrose commodity was extracted from cane and refined on Caribbean plantations, where its production relied heavily on enslaved labor and supplied ingredients for rum and molasses?

In 1791, this English abolitionist published a widely circulated pamphlet urging consumers to give up West Indian sugar produced through enslaved labor. His appeal helped make household purchasing a tool of antislavery protest; who was he?

Ty Inc. introduced this collectible plush line in 1993, using plastic pellets rather than ordinary fiber stuffing to give the toys a distinctive feel. Collectors also prized the toys’ heart-shaped swing tags; what was the line called?

During the 1997 Beanie Babies craze, the fast-food chain represented by the Golden Arches offered miniature Teenie Beanies alongside its children’s combination of food, drink, and a toy. What was that child-focused promotion called?

A probably apocryphal French saying, traditionally attributed to Marie Antoinette, is said to have been her response when told that peasants had no bread. What four-word quotation became a lasting symbol of aristocratic indifference?

The saying “Let Them Eat Cake” is traditionally attributed to this Austrian-born queen consort, although historians doubt the story. She was the wife of Louis XVI and was guillotined during the French Revolution in 1793. Who was she?
In birds, this reproductive structure encloses an embryo and its nutrient reserves. The chicken form is also a familiar food and a common baking ingredient; what is it called?
In Jonathan Swift’s *Gulliver’s Travels*, the emperor of Lilliput requires his subjects to crack eggs at the smaller end. What name is given to the faction that follows this rule?

What common term names a social gathering held to celebrate an occasion or simply enjoy company, often with invited guests, refreshments, and entertainment? It is the event named in a Václav Havel drama set in a garden and a Harold Pinter drama centered on a birthday.

Which British playwright wrote the absurdist drama in which a quiet lodger named Stanley Webber stays at a seaside boarding house, where the arrival of Goldberg and McCann turns a birthday party into a menacing ordeal?

Wang is one of the most common examples of the hereditary kind in China; what is the collective term for these labels used for individuals?

Which ancient Chinese philosopher argued that social order depends on people acting in accordance with the roles represented by their personal names and titles, a view called the rectification of names? His teachings are recorded in the Analects.

Iceland and England later fought the Cod Wars over access to it. What is this practice of catching aquatic animals for commercial, subsistence, or recreational purposes?

In fishing disputes, what term under UNCLOS names the maritime area extending up to 200 nautical miles from a coastal state’s baselines, where that state has rights to natural resources? Its limits figured prominently in conflicts such as the Cod Wars.

In many Northern European traditions, this seasonal celebration is associated with the summer solstice, bonfires, maypoles, and flower crowns. What is the common name for this period and its festivities?

This Shakespeare comedy follows four Athenian lovers and a troupe of amateur actors into a forest where Oberon, Titania, and Puck meddle in their affairs. The plot’s supernatural confusion unfolds during the Midsummer festivities; what is the play?

North American logging-camp folklore features “fearsome critters” such as the Axehandle Hound, said to lurk around workers in the woods. What are the traditional name for the people who cut and haul timber in these stories?
In tall tales about Lumberjacks, which giant woodsman is paired with a blue ox named Babe and is said in one legend to have carved the Grand Canyon by dragging his axe?
Founded in Kimberley, South Africa, in 1888, this company grew from the region’s diamond mines into a dominant force in mining and trading diamonds worldwide. What company is it?
Copywriter Frances Gerety created a 1947 advertising line for De Beers that helped make an expensive gemstone ring a customary symbol of engagement. What four-word slogan did she write?
These retail outlets sell donated or previously owned goods, giving usable items a second life. Many are operated by charitable organizations that use sales to support their programs.

At thrift stores across the United States, which nonprofit organization was founded in Boston in 1902 by Reverend Edgar J. Helms and is known for selling donated goods and supporting job training and employment services? Its familiar name is also used for a large network of local retail outlets.
This everyday handheld tool leaves marks by depositing liquid or gel ink, commonly through a ball, roller, or nib. What is this writing instrument called?
Among mass-produced pens, this model is recognizable by its clear, hexagonal plastic barrel, which reveals the ink tube inside, and a small hole in its cap. What is this long-running design called?

This African American ethnic group has longstanding communities in the coastal Lowcountry and Sea Islands of South Carolina and Georgia. Its English-based creole reflects African linguistic influences and developed in part on plantation rice islands; what is this group called?
The Gullah people have long-established communities in this state, including around Charleston, the Santee River, and Hilton Head Island. Which state is it?

Which draped wool garment served as the distinctive formal attire of male Roman citizens, including senators? It was wrapped around the body and arranged over the shoulder.
What was the name of the Roman toga edged with a purple border, worn by magistrates and by freeborn boys before they came of age?
Paint mixtures of red and blue often produce this color, which in antiquity was associated with exceptionally costly dye made from sea snails. What color is it?

Wham-O adopted this trademarked name in 1957 for a shallow, thick-rimmed plastic flying disc, following its purchase of the rights to Walter Morrison’s Pluto Platter. What is the name of the toy used in backyard catch and organized disc sports?

In a residential real-estate purchase, this dwelling may be listed on websites such as Zillow or Redfin, with buyers comparing its square footage, bedrooms, and bathrooms. The purchase is often financed with a mortgage; what is this type of home called?

At the monastery in Umberto Eco’s novel, Malachi holds an office overseeing the abbey’s guarded book collection, and Bernard serves as his assistant. What is the name of this library profession?

Which Umberto Eco novel features the librarian Malachi and his assistant Bernard dying after encountering a poisoned manuscript, while Adso of Melk and William of Baskerville investigate at an abbey with a jealously guarded library?

What term describes urban retail venues where producers sell fresh produce, meat, and other goods directly to shoppers, often from stalls in a dedicated hall or district rather than through conventional grocery stores? Made by coagulating milk, often with rennet, this dairy food ranges from hard, aged varieties to soft-ripened styles. Cheddar, Swiss, Brie, and paneer are all examples of what food?

Which nonprofit reproductive-health organization traces its origins to Margaret Sanger’s American Birth Control League and developed into a provider of reproductive health care?

This household savings container accepts coins through a narrow slot and may have to be opened or broken to retrieve them. What commonly animal-shaped object is it?

Domesticated in the Andes, this tuber was carried to Europe after transatlantic contact and eventually became an important staple there. It also provides vitamin C; name the crop.

This powered household appliance draws dust and debris through a nozzle by creating lower pressure inside its housing, then traps the material in a bag or canister. What is this common cleaning device called?

An international organization for viticulture defines this beverage as the product of partially or completely fermenting fresh grapes or grape must. Chemical analysis of jars from archaeological sites in Georgia indicates that it was being made there around 6000–5800 BCE. What is this beverage?

This manufactured nutritional product is designed to meet a baby's dietary needs when breast milk is unavailable or not used. It is commonly sold as powder, liquid concentrate, or ready-to-feed liquid. What is this product?

During the 2022 U.S. infant formula shortage, the federal government arranged for military aircraft to transport supplies from overseas to the United States. What was the name of this emergency import initiative?

The traditional cuckoo clock is strongly associated with a mountainous, heavily wooded region in southwestern Germany, where villages became known for clockmaking. What is the name of this region?

In botany, this is the reproductive structure of an angiosperm, often containing petals and sepals around stamens and carpels. It may attract pollinators and enable the plant’s reproduction.

What dish consists of poultry coated in seasoned breading or batter and cooked in hot oil, and is especially associated with Southern American cuisine and chains such as KFC and Chick-fil-A?

The white-suited founder of a fast-food chain specializing in fried chicken later became its mascot, with his portrait serving as a central brand symbol. By what name is this entrepreneur widely known?

What is the traditional name for an expedition, especially in Africa, undertaken to observe or hunt wild animals? Ernest Hemingway’s “The Snows of Kilimanjaro” includes a big-game journey of this kind.

Which South African writer, awarded the 1991 Nobel Prize in Literature, wrote “The Ultimate Safari,” a short story about a Mozambican girl and her family fleeing civil war through Kruger National Park? What kind of reference work lists words and may provide their definitions, pronunciations, usage information, or translations? Readers commonly consult it to check a word’s spelling or meaning.

This confectionery product is meant to be chewed for its flavor or texture rather than swallowed, and some varieties are designed to produce bubbles. What is this product?
Many sugar-free varieties of chewing gum use this sugar alcohol as a sweetener; it is also associated with helping reduce the risk of tooth decay. What is this ingredient?
Among achromatic colors, this hue is the darkest and is traditionally paired with white in descriptions of early monochrome cinema. What color is it?

The topic Black appears as the final word in the title of a Netflix prison drama adapted from Piper Kerman’s memoir. What is the name of the fictional federal women’s prison where the series’ main characters are held?

People wear these decorative personal adornments as necklaces, bracelets, rings, or earrings, often made from precious metals and gemstones. What broad product category includes all of these forms?

In the jewelry trade, what international initiative launched in 2003 requires participating countries to verify shipments of rough diamonds, aiming to keep conflict diamonds out of legitimate commerce?

These institutions organize books and other recorded materials so people can find and use them, while preserving knowledge for future readers. Many also provide reading spaces, reference assistance, or borrowing services. What are they called?

Among the ancient world’s best-known libraries, this Ptolemaic-era institution in Egypt was associated with the Mouseion and became famous for its ambitious effort to collect writings from across the known world. What was it called?
In many funeral traditions, professionals may inject preservative fluid and treat tissues to delay decomposition before viewing or burial. What is this postmortem preservation process called?

In this form of communication, a written note is sealed inside a watertight container and set adrift, often with no known recipient in mind. What is this method called?

Which American author wrote an early sea tale in which a shipwreck survivor boards a mysterious vessel and casts his written account into the ocean? The 1833 story won a contest held by the Baltimore Saturday Visiter and uses the same chance-at-sea delivery method as a Message in a Bottle.

Founded in Los Angeles in 1984 by Do Won Chang and Jin Sook Chang, this American fast-fashion retailer became known for inexpensive, trend-driven clothing and bright yellow shopping bags. What retailer is it?

Forever 21’s distinctive yellow shopping bags carried a biblical citation on the bottom, referring to the verse commonly recognized by the words “For God so loved the world.” What citation was printed there?
In Homer, Hephaestus crafts an elaborate defensive object depicting the heavens and scenes of human life. What kind of object is commonly carried alongside a sword or spear to block attacks?
In Greek mythology, what is the name of the divine shield associated with Athena and Zeus, famed for bearing the head of Medusa?

During a July festival honoring Saint Fermín, participants race through narrow streets in front of a herd of charging cattle, following a route that ends at the city’s arena. What is this annual event called?

This Japanese craft repairs broken ceramics with lacquer mixed with or highlighted by metallic powder. Instead of disguising the cracks, it makes the repaired seams a visible feature. What is this technique called?
In Kintsugi, what traditional Japanese adhesive, made from the sap of Toxicodendron vernicifluum, is used to join and finish repaired ceramics?

In this South Asian rice dish, spiced meat and partially cooked rice are often layered and finished together over low heat. Hyderabadi and Lucknowi preparations are well-known regional versions of it. What is the dish?

Biryani is linked to the culinary traditions of an empire that ruled much of the Indian subcontinent from the 16th to the 19th centuries. Which empire’s court culture is commonly associated with the dish’s development?

Two joined triangular pennants form a crimson concave pentagon bordered in blue, making this national banner unlike any other country's. Adopted in its modern form in 1962, it displays a white crescent and sun. What is this banner?

What craftsperson traditionally heats iron or steel in a forge and shapes it with hammer blows, often making tools, hardware, or horseshoes?

This rounded, voluminous hairstyle forms when tightly curled hair is allowed to grow naturally outward from the head. Widely embraced as an expression of Black pride and self-fashioning, what is this style called?
In Lorraine Hansberry’s *A Raisin in the Sun*, which member of the family adopts an Afro after rejecting hair straightening? She is an aspiring doctor, and Joseph Asagai is among her suitors.

In Chris Burden’s performance piece *Trans-Fixed*, the artist was secured to one of these self-propelled road vehicles. Jim Reinders also used them to create a Stonehenge-inspired installation in Nebraska. What general class of vehicles are they?

Co-founded in 2012 by Logan Green and John Zimmer, this San Francisco-based technology company operates a prominent app-based ridesharing service. Which company is it?
In 2018, Lyft acquired Motivate, the company that operated New York City’s blue, station-based cycle-rental service. What was the service called?
What is the name for a ceremony or set of social, cultural, or religious rites held to honor and mourn a deceased person and address the handling of their remains?
The poem “Funeral Blues” calls for clocks to be stopped and telephones to be silenced, then imagines the stars being extinguished in the speaker’s grief. Which poet wrote it?

What field encompasses the design and creation of clothing and other wearable styles? A celebrated 1960s example saw a French couturier translate a Dutch painter’s geometric imagery into A-line dresses.
In fashion history, which Dutch painter’s geometric compositions of black lines and primary-color rectangles were adapted by Yves Saint Laurent into A-line dresses in 1965?
These nonalcoholic beverages are commonly sweetened and often carbonated. The category includes East Germany’s Vita Cola and the German-created Fanta; what is it called?
Within the history of soft drinks, what orange-flavored brand was created by Coca-Cola’s German operation during World War II after wartime restrictions cut off its supply of Coca-Cola syrup?
Which U.S. automaker, established in 1903, built an enormous manufacturing complex on the Rouge River near Detroit and brought moving assembly-line production to mass-market carmaking?
Ford Motor Company introduced which low-priced automobile in 1908, a rugged model nicknamed “Tin Lizzie” that helped popularize car ownership in the United States?

These red, fleshy stone fruits grow on trees in the genus Prunus, alongside related fruits such as plums and peaches. When preserved in sugar syrup and colored, they can be served as a garnish in beverages. What are they?
Which sweet variety of cherries was developed in Washington state and named after a mountain near Seattle? It is one of the types used to make maraschino cherries.

A gaucho might carry this bladed tool for everyday cutting and, at times, for fighting. Swiss Army versions combine its folding blade with tools such as a screwdriver and a can opener; what is this tool called?
In gaucho culture in Argentina and Uruguay, this long knife was carried for practical tasks and could also be used in a fight. What is the traditional name for this distinctive gaucho blade?

This Danish toy brand’s construction system uses small plastic bricks with studs that connect to matching tubes beneath them. Its name comes from the Danish words meaning “play well.” What is the brand?
Introduced by LEGO in 1978, this small character has a cylindrical head, movable arms and legs, and accessories that can be swapped between figures. What is this type of character called?

In 1291, Venice ordered artisans’ furnaces moved to a nearby lagoon island to reduce the risk of fires in the city. The island’s makers became renowned for both ornamental pieces and household vessels; what is this craft tradition commonly called?

Murano glassmakers became renowned in the 15th century for producing an especially transparent, colorless glass, credited to master Angelo Barovier and made to resemble rock crystal. What was this glass type called?

What widely eaten Italian dish consists of a leavened wheat-dough base commonly topped with tomato and cheese, then baked at high heat?
Which Neapolitan pizzaiolo is often credited with creating the modern form of pizza in the late 19th century?

Which European Union food-quality designation did Neapolitan pizza receive in 2009, as an alternative to geographical-origin labels such as PDO and PGI? This recognition is distinct from UNESCO’s later recognition of Neapolitan pizza-making as intangible cultural heritage.

Schools often organize these student social gatherings in gyms or halls, with music and dancing as the main activities. They may be casual themed evenings or formal milestone events such as prom and homecoming; what are they called?

The 18th Amendment and the Volstead Act prohibited the manufacture and sale in the United States of this broad class of beverages, including beer, wine, and distilled spirits. What is this beverage category?

Passengers use an app or similar platform to request transportation, and participating drivers carry them in their own vehicles instead of using a company fleet. What is this service commonly called?
In ridesharing, which company began in San Francisco in 2009 and became known for its app’s Black and XL ride options, while also operating a food-delivery service with “Eats” in its name?

In everyday food terminology, this protein-rich category usually means edible flesh from mammals such as cattle, pigs, and sheep, while poultry and seafood are often grouped separately. Which for-hire passenger-transport sector centers on licensed cabs and has been associated both with deadly operator conflicts near Cape Town and with valuable operating permits in U.S. cities?

What term describes a food business with no customer-facing dining room that takes orders primarily online for delivery or pickup, often preparing meals in an existing restaurant’s back-of-house facilities or a shared food-preparation space? It may operate as a separate virtual brand without a standalone storefront.

One food brand sold through ghost kitchens was developed by a YouTube creator whose legal name is Jimmy Donaldson, known for elaborate challenge videos and philanthropy. What is the name of this delivery-first restaurant brand?

The Gregorian calendar reform was formally promulgated by Gregory XIII in a papal bull dated 24 February 1582. What Latin title did that document bear?

This Japanese alcoholic beverage is made by fermenting rice with koji rather than by distilling it. In a traditional wedding ritual, the couple and their families take turns drinking it from three cups.
Sake is traditionally offered at shrines in this indigenous Japanese religion, whose deities are known as kami. What is this religion called?

In some recipes for mole, bitter, unsweetened seeds that can later be processed into chocolate are toasted or ground with chiles and spices. What are these seeds called?
This South Asian staple is made by simmering dried, split pulses—often lentils, peas, or beans—until they form a seasoned dish or stew. What is this preparation called?

What is the name of the prearranged practice in which two people faced one another in armed combat under agreed customs to settle an insult or defend personal honor?

In *The Baby-Sitters Club*, Kristy Thomas forms a club whose members include Stacey and Claudia. What is the common name for people who temporarily care for children while their parents or guardians are away?

This massive arkose sandstone monolith rises about 345 metres above the plains of Australia’s Northern Territory and measures roughly 9.4 kilometres around its base. Sacred to the Anangu, what is its natural name?

This Spanish island is the second most populous in its archipelago, after Mallorca. Its resorts and internationally prominent electronic dance music nightlife attract visitors from around the world. What island is it?

The Danish capital and largest city sits on Zealand and is linked across the Øresund to Malmö by a fixed crossing opened in 2000. Its waterfront is home to the statue of the Little Mermaid, inspired by a Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale. Which city is it?

Its western boundary is largely traced by a major river that shares its name, and its southern edge reaches the Gulf of Mexico. Jackson is both this state's capital and largest city. Which state is it?
At 807 feet above sea level, this summit in Tishomingo County near Iuka is the highest point in Mississippi. What is this geographic feature?
In central Mississippi, this city is both the state's capital and its largest city. It lies on the Pearl River and is named for the seventh U.S. president. What city is it?
Which northeastern Ukrainian administrative region lies along the country’s border with Russia and also borders Donetsk region? Its administrative center is Ukraine’s second-largest city.

During Ukraine’s September 2022 advance in Kharkiv Oblast, forces retook this strategic city on the Siverskyi Donets River after months of Russian occupation. It is also a major transport hub in the region; which city is it?

This landlocked East African country began moving its capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2018. It borders Lake Tanganyika and Rwanda, Tanzania, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo; which country is it?
Burundi’s western boundary includes part of the shore of this long, deep African Great Lake, shared by four countries. Its northern end lies near Bujumbura; what is the lake’s name?

This luxury resort on the Las Vegas Strip opened in 1998 and takes inspiration from a lakeside town in northern Italy. It is known for a large artificial lake with choreographed musical fountains. What is the resort’s name?
In the Bellagio’s lobby, Dale Chihuly created a colorful ceiling sculpture from thousands of hand-blown glass flowers. What is the name of this installation?

What landlocked country in Central Europe has 26 cantons with their own constitutions and governments, and recognizes German, French, Italian, and Romansh as national languages? Its historic official title preserves an older political name, although it has been a federal state since 1848.

In Switzerland, which of its three major geographical regions lies between the Alps and the Jura and contains the country’s highest concentration of populated areas? In German, this region is commonly called the Mittelland.
