Built in stages from roughly 3100 to 1600 BCE on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, this prehistoric monument has an outer circle of upright sarsens topped by horizontal lintels and smaller stones within. The surviving structure is aligned with the sun at both solstices. What landmark is described?

At Stonehenge, the great outer sarsen uprights are fitted to their horizontal lintels using a woodworking technique that locks a projecting peg into a matching cavity. What is the name of this connection?
Stonehenge stands on this broad chalk landscape in Wiltshire, about two miles west of Amesbury; the same prehistoric landscape contains hundreds of burial mounds. What is this region called?

Stonehenge and the nearby prehistoric landscape of Avebury were inscribed together in 1986 on an international designation recognizing places of outstanding cultural or natural significance. What is this designation?

Admitted to the Union in 1816 as its 19th state, this Midwestern state reaches Lake Michigan at its northern edge and is bounded by the Ohio River to the south. It lies between Illinois and Ohio, with Kentucky across the river.
In Indiana, which city was designated the state capital in 1821? State government moved there in 1824, and the city is near the center of the state.

Occupying much of southern Greece, this large peninsula was historically linked to the mainland by the narrow Isthmus of Corinth. It is now cut off from the mainland by a canal through that neck; what is the peninsula’s natural name?

The Peloponnese is separated from mainland Greece by a navigable passage excavated through its narrow northeastern land bridge. Opened in 1893, the 6.3-kilometre cut links the Saronic Gulf to the gulf immediately west of that bridge; what is this passage called?

This North Atlantic island west of Great Britain has a low central plain ringed by coastal mountains and is politically shared between a sovereign state and a region of the United Kingdom. What is the island’s natural name?
On Ireland, this County Kerry summit rises to 1,039 meters and is the highest point on the island. What mountain is it?
Ireland’s longest river runs about 360.5 kilometers, from County Cavan through Limerick toward the Atlantic. What is this river’s name?
Ireland is politically divided, and this region occupies the northeastern part of the island while remaining part of the United Kingdom. Belfast is its capital. What is the region called?
This sea lies between Ireland and Great Britain, and ferry routes connect ports such as Dublin and Holyhead across it. What body of water is it?
Which historical region of central Romania lies within the arc of the Carpathian Mountains? It was historically associated with the Kingdom of Hungary and later existed as a principality.
Within Transylvania, which city is the region’s largest urban center and home to Babeș-Bolyai University? Its central Union Square is dominated by the Gothic Church of St. Michael.

What Canadian province is the country’s largest by area and the only one with a majority French-speaking population? It was also the center of a major 1960s social transformation and a lasting sovereignty movement.

In Quebec, what name is given to the 1960s period of rapid modernization, expanding provincial government, and declining influence of the Catholic Church? It reshaped the province’s society and helped fuel its sovereignty movement.
This western U.S. state contains much of the Great Basin and is home to both Las Vegas and Reno. Its western boundary includes a large alpine lake shared with California; what state is it?
Shared by Nevada and California, this deep alpine lake lies in the Sierra Nevada and drains through the Truckee River toward Reno. What lake is known for its clear water and shoreline resorts?
Established in 1864 during the Civil War, this major U.S. military cemetery occupies Robert E. Lee’s former estate across the Potomac from Washington, D.C. What is its name?

Within Arlington National Cemetery stands a Greek Revival mansion designed by George Hadfield and completed in 1818 for George Washington Parke Custis, the adopted grandson of George Washington. Robert E. Lee later lived there after marrying Custis’s daughter; what name is now used for this historic residence?

Two headstreams, the Vorderrhein and Hinterrhein, meet at Reichenau in Switzerland to form this river. It flows through or along several countries before reaching the North Sea through the Netherlands. What is the river?
The Rhine River crosses from Germany into the Netherlands near this border locality, where it divides into delta waterways including the Waal, Nederrijn, and IJssel. What is the locality?
This landlocked country occupies much of the Horn of Africa and shares borders with six countries, including Kenya, Sudan, and Somalia. Its capital is Addis Ababa. What country is it?
In Ethiopia’s northwestern highlands, this is the country’s largest lake and the source of the Blue Nile. The city of Bahir Dar lies on its southern shore. What is the lake’s name?

This Southern Plains state became the 46th member of the Union on November 16, 1907, when a western territory was joined with the remaining Indian Territory to its east. What state was formed by that union?
Oklahoma lies where this broad physiographic region meets the Central Lowlands. Within the state, it includes the Panhandle and a narrow strip along the western border; name the region.
Which southwestern European landform contains modern Spain and Portugal and is separated from the rest of Europe by the Pyrenees? It lies between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.
On the Iberian Peninsula, what centuries-long Christian campaign sought to reclaim territories ruled by Muslim states and concluded with the capture of Granada in 1492?
This Mid-Atlantic state borders Chesapeake Bay, has Annapolis as its capital, and has Baltimore as its largest city. What state is it?
In Maryland, which city is the state capital and the home of the U.S. Naval Academy, located on the Severn River near Chesapeake Bay?
Which town in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, is associated with the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103? The disaster’s wreckage fell across the town and surrounding countryside.
Lockerbie is associated with the destruction of which Pan Am passenger flight in December 1988? The aircraft was travelling from Frankfurt to Detroit via London and New York.

A Dutch settlement called Fort Orange began at this site in 1624, and the English renamed it after taking control in 1664. New York made this Hudson River city its permanent capital in 1797. What city is it?
The original route of this 19th-century waterway opened in 1825, connecting Albany with Buffalo and linking the Hudson River to New York’s interior. What was this waterway called?

This volcanic chain of roughly 300 islands arcs southwest from Alaska toward Russia across the North Pacific. It forms part of the boundary between the Bering Sea and Pacific Ocean and belongs to the Pacific Ring of Fire. What is this island chain called?

For more than 9,000 years, the Aleutian Islands have been the homeland of this Indigenous people. Their traditional communities are associated with the island chain extending westward from the Alaska Peninsula. What people are they?
In South Asia, what is the name for the seasonal pattern in which prevailing winds reverse direction, bringing moisture-laden air inland from the ocean and producing heavy summer rains?

During the South Asian monsoon, moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea rise over this mountain range that parallels India’s coast beside that sea, bringing heavy rain to its seaward slopes and leaving the Deccan Plateau inland comparatively dry. What is this range called?

Which Ecuadorian archipelago in the eastern Pacific lies astride the equator and includes volcanic islands such as Isabela, Santa Cruz, and Española? Its endemic giant tortoises and marine iguanas are among the wildlife that made it renowned as a natural laboratory of evolution.
Established in 1959, this protected area encompasses nearly all the land on the Galápagos Islands, while a separate marine reserve safeguards surrounding waters. What is its name?

This West Asian country has coastlines on the Caspian Sea to the north and the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman to the south, with land borders that include Iraq, Turkey, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. Historically known as Persia, what country has Tehran as its capital?
Iran’s largest city and main economic hub lies at the southern foot of the Alborz Mountains. It became the country’s capital under Qajar ruler Agha Mohammad Khan in 1786; name this metropolis.

Iran’s southern coastline borders this major petroleum-shipping route, which connects eastward to the Gulf of Oman through the Strait of Hormuz. Its northern shore includes Iran, while several Arab states lie along its southern shore; name this body of water.
In central London, which major public gathering place is known for a column honoring Admiral Horatio Nelson, four lions at its base, and a plinth used for changing contemporary-art commissions?
The four lions at the base of Nelson’s Column in Trafalgar Square were designed by which 19th-century British animal painter and sculptor? His works include the painting *The Monarch of the Glen*.
This transcontinental country lies mainly on the Anatolian Peninsula in West Asia, with a smaller region in southeastern Europe. Its territory has coasts on the Black, Aegean, and Mediterranean seas.
Turkey’s capital is located on the central Anatolian plateau, while Istanbul is the country’s largest city. It became the capital of the republic in 1923.
In Turkey, this narrow waterway passes through Istanbul and connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara. It also separates the city’s European and Asian sides.
This strait in Turkey connects the Aegean Sea with the Sea of Marmara and runs alongside the Gallipoli Peninsula. In antiquity, it was known as the Hellespont.
This volcanic massif in eastern Turkey is the country’s highest mountain and lies near the borders with Armenia and Iran. It is traditionally associated with the resting place of Noah’s Ark.

This East African country has an Indian Ocean coastline and contains the Serengeti and Mount Kilimanjaro. Its present-day state was formed in 1964 by the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, and its capital is Dodoma. What country is it?

In northeastern Tanzania, this dormant volcanic massif rises to 5,895 meters, making it Africa’s highest peak. It is also the world’s highest free-standing mountain above sea level. What mountain is it?
Off mainland Tanzania, this Indian Ocean island group includes Unguja and Pemba and has a long history of Swahili and Indian Ocean trade. What is this island group called?

In northern Tanzania’s Ngorongoro Conservation Area, this steep-sided ravine is an important paleoanthropological site where Mary and Louis Leakey made major discoveries. Finds there include the Paranthropus boisei specimen known as OH 5. What site is it?

Alexander the Great founded this Egyptian Mediterranean settlement in 331 BCE, and it became the Ptolemaic Kingdom’s capital after the wars of the Diadochi. What city later stood at the center of Hellenistic scholarship?

In Alexandria, an enormous ancient beacon was built on the island of Pharos to guide ships into the harbor. Earthquakes eventually damaged this structure, which was counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World; what was it called?

This central Canadian city is Alberta’s capital and largest city, and it lies along the North Saskatchewan River. It is also associated with a shopping complex known as North America’s largest mall, which contains a large indoor lake. What city is it?
Edmonton serves as the capital of this western Canadian province, which has been kept free of rats since the 1950s through an extensive control program. What province is it?

In Jerusalem’s Old City, this ancient structure is the best-known surviving section of the retaining perimeter that once enclosed the Second Temple complex. It is a major Jewish place of prayer where visitors traditionally leave written petitions in gaps between its stones. What landmark is this?

In Jewish tradition, the elevated sacred precinct above the Western Wall is associated with the location of the ancient Israelite sanctuary. Its present-day compound contains the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque. What is this precinct commonly called in Jewish usage?
Known to the ancient Egyptians as Waset, what city became a major political capital and religious center and was restored as Egypt’s capital during Tutankhamun’s reign?
Within Thebes, which vast religious precinct was expanded by successive pharaohs and centered on the worship of Amun?

The U.S. Census Bureau counts this broad region as one of the nation’s four major regions. It extends from the Atlantic seaboard westward to Texas and is associated with the former Confederate states and a distinct historical-cultural identity. What region is it?

Within the American South, what cultural-geographic area is associated with especially high Protestant church attendance, particularly in evangelical congregations, and covers nearly all of the region?

In the American South, what subregion is commonly associated with Alabama and Mississippi, as well as Louisiana, Georgia, and South Carolina, and with slavery’s historic influence on plantation agriculture?
Which city is Azerbaijan’s capital and largest urban center, situated on the Absheron Peninsula along the western shore of the Caspian Sea?
Baku lies on the western shore of which endorheic body of water, often described as the world’s largest lake despite its traditional name as a sea, and fed by the Volga River?

This Wayne County city lies just west of Detroit and contains Ford Motor Company’s world headquarters and its major Rouge manufacturing complex. It is also associated with Henry Ford and has a large Arab American and Muslim population. What city is it?

Opened in Dearborn in 2005, this cultural institution affiliated with ACCESS interprets the heritage and history of a diaspora whose roots span 22 nations across the Middle East and North Africa. What is its official name?

This roughly 80-kilometer waterway crosses a Central American isthmus, sparing ships the longer journey around South America. Completed by the United States after an earlier French effort failed, it opened to shipping in 1914 and connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. What is it?
Along the Panama Canal, ships are raised by locks from sea level to a man-made lake about 26 meters above sea level before continuing across the isthmus. What is the name of this lake?

This 3,776-meter stratovolcano on Honshu is Japan’s highest peak and rises about 100 kilometers southwest of Tokyo. For centuries, pilgrims have traveled to its summit, and it became a prominent subject of Japanese art.

Which ukiyo-e artist created the early-19th-century series *Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji*, which includes *The Great Wave of Kanagawa* and *Fine Wind, Clear Morning*? The series helped make the mountain’s image widely known beyond Japan.

Which Central American country borders Mexico to the north and Guatemala to the west and south, with a Caribbean coastline and a significant Garifuna community in Dangriga? Its offshore islands include Ambergris Caye.
Belize’s largest island lies off its northeastern coast, near the Belize Barrier Reef, and its principal town is San Pedro. What is the island’s name?

Located between the Caucasus and Central Asia, this inland body of water is bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan. Though traditionally called a sea, it is also the world’s largest lake; what is its natural name?

The Caspian Sea receives its main freshwater inflow from this river, which crosses Russia and is the longest river in Europe. It reaches the sea through a broad delta at its shallow northern end; name the river.
This Azerbaijani capital lies on the Caspian Sea’s western shore, on the Absheron Peninsula. Its long history of oil production helped it become a major city in the South Caucasus; what is its name?

Of the five countries bordering the Caspian Sea, this Central Asian country has the longest coastline along its northeastern shore. It is also the world’s largest landlocked country, and its capital is Astana; name the country.

This federally administered system of protected areas preserves representative natural landscapes and ecosystems across Canada. Banff, established in 1885, was its first member; what is this system called?
Among Canadian national parks, this Alberta site was first set aside in 1885 under the name Rocky Mountains Park, becoming Canada's oldest national park. What is its current name?
This biome is defined by very low precipitation and sparse vegetation rather than by heat alone; it can occur in both hot and cold regions. What landscape type includes the Sahara and the Gobi?

China’s largest desert located entirely within its borders occupies much of the Tarim Basin in Xinjiang, west of Lop Nur. Which desert lies between the Tian Shan to the north and the Kunlun Mountains to the south?
This country is the world’s largest by area and stretches across Eastern Europe and northern Asia. Its territory spans eleven time zones; what country is it?
Russia shares its longest international land border with this Central Asian country, whose capital is Astana. It is also the world’s largest landlocked country; name it.

Russia has a Baltic exclave located between Poland and Lithuania, with no land connection to the rest of the country. What is this region, whose administrative centre is a major port on the southeastern Baltic coast?
This range runs through Russia and is commonly used as the boundary between Europe and Asia. Extending south toward Kazakhstan, it separates European Russia from Siberia; what range is it?
Russia borders the northern part of this vast inland body of water, which is also bordered by Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan. What is the world’s largest enclosed body of water?

Located in Tuscany, this historic city was a major center of medieval and Renaissance art and gave its name to a distinctive school of painting. Its civic palace contains Ambrogio Lorenzetti’s fresco cycle depicting good and bad government.
Siena’s powerful medieval rival, this Tuscan city later became the center of Medici rule and is home to the Uffizi Gallery. Which city is it?

This landlocked Central Asian republic is the world’s largest landlocked country by area and the ninth-largest country overall. It was also the last constituent republic of the Soviet Union to declare independence, doing so in 1991. Name it.
Kazakhstan has an extensive shoreline on this landlocked body of water, the world’s largest inland body of water. It forms much of Kazakhstan’s western boundary and is shared by five countries.
Kazakhstan moved its capital here from Almaty in 1997. The city was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019, then returned to its current name in 2022. What is it called today?
This island country is the largest in the Caribbean by area, and its capital and largest city is Havana. What country lies where the Caribbean Sea, the Gulf of Mexico, and the Atlantic Ocean meet?
Cuba lies immediately west of this Greater Antillean island. The island is divided between Haiti and the Dominican Republic; what is it called?
Cuba lies east of this Mexican landmass, whose northern coast includes the resort city of Cancún. What region extends between the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea?
Cuba’s second-largest island lies southwest of its main island, across the Gulf of Batabanó. Formerly known as the Isle of Pines, what is this island called today?
In urban geography, what are the ethnic enclaves marked by concentrations of Chinese immigrants, businesses, institutions, and cultural life?
Among the world’s Chinatowns, which Manila district is widely regarded as the oldest, dating to its establishment under Spanish rule in 1594?
This Upper Midwest state became the 32nd member of the Union in 1858. It borders two Canadian provinces and contains the headwaters of the Mississippi River; name the state.
In Minnesota, the Mississippi River’s commonly recognized source is at the outlet of this lake in a state park, where visitors can cross the young river on stepping stones. Name the lake.
Minnesota includes a small northern projection beyond the 49th parallel, whose land route to the rest of the state passes through Canada. What is this region called?
Minnesota’s western boundary with North Dakota follows much of this river, which begins near Wahpeton and Breckenridge and empties into Lake Winnipeg in Manitoba. Name the river.

This river is the Columbia River’s largest tributary and flows through a deep gorge along part of the Idaho–Oregon border. Its hydroelectric dams have been controversial because they impede salmon migration. What river is it?

The Snake River cuts through this steep, rugged landform along the Idaho–Oregon border, where high walls enclose the river. The area is often described as North America’s deepest river gorge. What is this landmark called?
Located on the eastern shore of Lake Champlain, this is Vermont’s most populous city. What city is it?
Burlington’s waterfront faces a long, narrow freshwater lake that forms much of Vermont’s western boundary and extends north into Quebec. What is this lake called?

This protected Wyoming landscape lies immediately south of Yellowstone and includes part of a broad valley in the state’s northwest. It is named for the highest summit in a rugged mountain range along Wyoming’s western border. What is this site?
Grand Teton National Park encompasses part of a broad Wyoming valley that lies between the Teton Range and the Gros Ventre Range. What is this valley called?

This ancient, roughly 2,500-kilometer range runs north to south through western Russia and extends into northern Kazakhstan. Its ridgeline is commonly used as part of the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia. What is this range called?
The Ural Mountains’ highest summit rises about 1,895 meters above sea level and lies in the Subpolar Urals of Russia. What is the name of this peak?

This subterranean passage network in Kentucky has been surveyed for hundreds of miles, making it the longest known underground system of its kind in the world. It is protected within a national park that bears its name; what is the system?
Mammoth Cave National Park protects the famous underground system, while a major river also flows through the park before joining the Ohio River. What is the river’s name?

Stretching along South America’s western edge from Venezuela and Colombia south toward Tierra del Fuego, this is the world’s longest continental mountain range and includes high plateaus such as the Altiplano. What range is it?
Within the Andes Mountains, this Argentine summit rises to about 6,961 meters, making it the highest point in South America. What peak is it?

The Andes Mountains encompass this broad high plateau in Bolivia and Peru, around Lake Titicaca; it is commonly identified as the world’s second-highest plateau after the Tibetan Plateau. What plateau is it?
What overseas department and region of France occupies the northeastern coast of South America? It is also home to a major European rocket-launch site near the equator.
In French Guiana, what coastal town west of Cayenne is the site of the Guiana Space Centre, where the European Space Agency launches rockets?
This federally recognized tribal entity is the largest in the United States, with a reservation spanning parts of Arizona, New Mexico, and Utah. Its capital is Window Rock. What is its name?

The Navajo Nation’s capital is a community in northeastern Arizona, near the New Mexico border. It is named for a natural sandstone formation with a large opening. What community serves as the nation’s capital?
In Roman times, this northern Italian city was called Mediolanum and expanded substantially under Emperor Maximian. It was also the city where St. Ambrose served as bishop; identify it.

Milan gives its name to a 313 imperial proclamation that established religious toleration in the Roman Empire. Which emperor, after defeating Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge in 312, issued it alongside Licinius?

This sovereign country comprises the mainland of its namesake continent, Tasmania, and many smaller islands. It is a federation of six states and ten territories, with its national capital distinct from its two largest cities; name the country.

Australia's two most populous cities are Sydney and Melbourne, but neither is its national capital. Which inland city, situated in the Australian Capital Territory, serves as the seat of the federal government?
In western Australia, this capital city lies beside the Swan River near where it meets the Indian Ocean. Kings Park overlooks the city’s central area; name the city.
Separated from mainland Australia by Bass Strait, this island is the only Australian state not on the mainland. Its capital is Hobart; name the state.
Along Queensland's northeastern coast in Australia, this vast coral formation extends for more than 2,000 kilometers and is visible from space. What is its established name?

This landscape in California’s Sierra Nevada contains a U-shaped valley carved by glaciers, along with granite landmarks such as El Capitan and Half Dome. Congress gave it federal protection in 1890, following advocacy by John Muir and others.

Yosemite National Park lies within this mountain range in eastern California. Stretching for hundreds of miles along the state’s eastern side, the range includes Mount Whitney, the highest peak in the contiguous United States.

Founded in 1703 by a Russian tsar at the eastern end of the Gulf of Finland, this city later served as the Russian Empire’s capital. What city was renamed Petrograd and then Leningrad before its historic name was restored?

Saint Petersburg was founded under the direction of this tsar, who studied shipbuilding in the Netherlands during his Grand Embassy to Western Europe. The city’s famous Bronze Horseman monument commemorates him.

This Central American country is the region’s most populous nation and borders Mexico, Belize, Honduras, and El Salvador. It has coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea. What country is it?
Guatemala shares its longest international land border with this neighboring country, whose states of Chiapas and Tabasco meet the frontier. What country is it?

This landlocked Mountain West state has high plains to the east and Rocky Mountain ranges in the west. It contains Yellowstone and Grand Teton national parks, and its capital is also its most populous city. What state is it?
In Wyoming, this city became an important railroad town after the transcontinental line reached the region in 1867. It is both the state's capital and its most populous city. Name it.
Wyoming contains most of this vast protected area, established in 1872. It is famous for Old Faithful’s predictable eruptions and the colorful Grand Prismatic Spring. Name the area.

In 1906, Theodore Roosevelt used the Antiquities Act to give federal protection to this northeastern Wyoming landmark near the Belle Fourche River. This igneous formation is known for its steep sides marked by long vertical columns. Name it.
This Portuguese volcanic archipelago lies in the North Atlantic, near the meeting point of the Eurasian, North American, and African tectonic plates. What is it called?

On one of the Azores’ islands, a volcanic summit rises about 2,351 meters above sea level, making it Portugal’s highest point and one of the places where the Mid-Atlantic Ridge emerges above the ocean. What is this summit called?

This mountainous island lies in the western Pacific between Japan and the Philippines, and its north–south Central Mountain Range separates river systems flowing toward its eastern and western coasts. The Republic of China government relocated there in 1949 and has exercised effective jurisdiction there since; what island is it?

On Taiwan’s southwestern coast, Dutch colonists built a fortress at Anping in 1624 that became a center of Dutch rule and trade. Koxinga captured it when he expelled the Dutch in 1662; what was this fortress called?

This domed landmark on a rise east of the National Mall in Washington, D.C., houses both chambers of the United States Congress. It was reportedly the intended destination of United Airlines Flight 93 before passengers resisted the hijackers on September 11, 2001. What is the building called?

Although United Airlines Flight 93 was reportedly headed for the United States Capitol, passenger resistance brought it down in a field in Pennsylvania. What national site near the crash area commemorates the passengers and crew?

Spanning southern Mongolia and northern China, this vast inland cold, arid region receives little ocean moisture, with the Himalaya adding a rain shadow. Its landscape includes rocky plains, mountains, steppe, oases, and dunes rather than an unbroken sea of sand. What region is it?

Compared with the varied rocky plains of the Gobi Desert, which desert occupies much of the Tarim Basin in Xinjiang and is bounded by the Tian Shan to the north and the Kunlun Mountains to the south? Its shifting sand dunes make it one of the world's largest sandy deserts.

This Central American country lies between Costa Rica and Colombia, with Caribbean coastline to the north and Pacific coastline to the south. Its territory includes the Darién Gap and the interoceanic waterway linking the two oceans; what country is it?
In Panama, what artificial lake was formed by damming the Chagres River and became a major reservoir along the route of the interoceanic canal?

This southeastern U.S. state stretches from the Atlantic coast and the Outer Banks to the Appalachian Mountains, with the Coastal Plain, Piedmont, and Blue Ridge as its three main geographic regions. Its capital is Raleigh, and Mount Mitchell is its highest point.
Along North Carolina’s coast, this chain of narrow barrier islands separates the Atlantic Ocean from sounds such as Pamlico Sound. Buxton and Avon are among the communities located on these islands.

This U.S. state was the site of Jamestown, the first permanent English settlement in North America, and its colonial assembly became the House of Burgesses. Richmond is its capital, and it borders both the Atlantic Ocean and Kentucky. Identify the state.
Virginia’s eastern shore faces this large estuary, whose mouth is between Cape Charles and Cape Henry and whose watershed extends across six states. What is this body of water?
Which northeastern U.S. state has Albany as its capital, borders Canada, and reaches both the Atlantic Ocean and the Great Lakes?
In New York State, which river flows through the valley named for it and meets the Mohawk River near Albany before continuing south toward New York Harbor?
Which New York State range includes Mount Marcy, the state’s highest peak, and Lake Tear of the Clouds near that peak?
In central New York State, what regional name is given to a series of long, narrow north–south bodies of water that includes Cayuga and Seneca?

Centered on Earth’s highest major plateau, this historical and cultural region of western East Asia is commonly described as the world’s highest region by average elevation. Its historic political and religious center is Lhasa; what region is it?
Tibet’s highest point is also the world’s highest mountain above sea level, with its summit on the border between Nepal and China’s Tibet Autonomous Region. What mountain is it?
In Tibet, what city on the Kyichu River became a traditional political and religious center and is home to both the Potala Palace and Jokhang Temple?
This Balkan country in southeastern Europe lies between Montenegro and Greece and has coastlines on both the Adriatic and Ionian seas. Its capital and largest city is Tirana. What country is it?
Albania’s western coast meets this sea, which also borders Italy to the east and is connected to the Ionian Sea by the Strait of Otranto. What sea is it?
Along Albania’s eastern border with North Macedonia, this peak is the highest point in both countries and is the namesake of a surrounding mountain range. What is the peak?

This major city in central China is the capital of Hubei Province and encompasses the historic urban centers of Wuchang, Hankou, and Hanyang. It lies at the meeting point of the Han and Yangtze rivers. What city is it?
Wuhan stands where this river receives the Han River, and the waterway continues east across China toward Shanghai and the East China Sea. Which river is it?
This Himalayan peak stands on the Nepal–India border and is the world’s third-highest mountain. Its name is traditionally associated with five treasures of snow. What is the mountain?
Kangchenjunga lies along the Nepal–India frontier within this vast South Asian mountain range. Mount Everest, the world’s highest peak, is also part of it. What is the range?

This landlocked East Asian country shares the Gobi Desert with China and is known for nomadic traditions. What country also hosts the annual festival featuring traditional wrestling, archery, and horse racing?
In Mongolia, this annual festival is celebrated with traditional wrestling, archery, and horse racing, often called the “three manly games.” What is the festival’s name?
Which city in western Saudi Arabia was the destination of Muhammad’s migration from Mecca and is considered Islam’s second-holiest city? It is also the place where Muhammad is buried.
About 300 miles south of Medina, which Saudi Arabian city contains the Kaaba and the Masjid al-Haram?
Honshu and Hokkaido are two of the major landforms in the Japanese archipelago, which comprises thousands of them. What geographic feature do they exemplify?
Among the world’s islands, which is the largest by area and lies between the Arctic and North Atlantic oceans? It is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

Stretching from British Columbia through Washington and Oregon into northern California, this volcanic mountain chain includes Mount Rainier, Mount Hood, and the volcano that erupted catastrophically in 1980. What is this mountain chain called?
In Washington's Cascade Range, which volcano underwent a major explosive eruption on May 18, 1980, after an earthquake triggered a massive north-flank landslide and a lateral blast?
This chain of barrier islands lies off North Carolina and separates Pamlico Sound from the Atlantic Ocean. What is the name of this coastal island chain?

On the Outer Banks, this Dare County town is commonly associated with the Wright brothers’ first powered flight, although their 1903 flights actually took place several miles south at Kill Devil Hills. What town is it?

Situated between Nicaragua and Panama on the Central American isthmus, this country is home to the Monteverde Cloud Forest. It abolished its military in 1948 and is widely associated with the phrase “Pura Vida.” What country is it?

Costa Rica shares its northern border with this Central American country, and the San Juan River forms part of their boundary. The 1858 Cañas–Jerez Treaty established the border, though disputes over its interpretation have continued. Which country is it?
Which major American city is home to a botanical garden whose Climatron is a geodesic dome, and to the Wainwright Building, a terracotta-clad landmark designed by Dankmar Adler and Sullivan?
St. Louis sits on the western bank of this major river, which meets the Missouri River just north of the city and forms much of Missouri’s eastern border. What river is it?

This country in northwestern South America is bordered by Colombia to the north and Peru to the east and south, with the Pacific Ocean along its western coast. Its capital is Quito, and its territory includes an archipelago roughly 1,000 kilometers offshore.

Ecuador includes this volcanic archipelago, organized as a province and located about 1,000 kilometers west of the mainland. Its distinctive wildlife and plants helped make it a landmark in Charles Darwin’s studies of evolution.

This is Ecuador’s highest mountain, an Andean volcano whose summit is often described as the point on Earth’s surface farthest from the planet’s center because of the equatorial bulge. What is its name?
Which major city in southeastern Germany is Bavaria’s capital and most populous city? It stands on the Isar River and hosts the annual Oktoberfest.
Munich lies along this river, which flows north from the Alps through the city before joining the Danube near Deggendorf. What is the river’s name?

Munich’s sports complex on Oberwiesenfeld was built for this 1972 international multisport gathering, which became associated with the hostage-taking and murder of members of the Israeli delegation. What event was held there?

This low, gently sloping limestone landform in southeastern Mexico lies between the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea. It includes Cancún on its Caribbean coast and Chichén Itzá inland, and its broader extent reaches into Belize and Guatemala. What is this landform?

On the Yucatán Peninsula, porous limestone allows much of the rainwater to seep underground, leaving few surface rivers. What are the characteristic water-filled sinkholes formed when limestone caves or cavities collapse?
This South American river carries more water than any other river on Earth and drains the world’s largest river basin. Flowing through Brazil before reaching the Atlantic, what is this river?
The Amazon River delivers roughly one-fifth of the river water discharged into the world’s oceans. Into which ocean does it empty?
Near Manaus, the Amazon River meets a dark-water tributary at the famous Meeting of Waters. What is the tributary’s name?
A 2014 study revised the long-held identification of the Amazon River basin’s farthest source, locating it in headwaters in central Peru. Which river was identified as that source?

What Tuscan city northwest of Rome was a wealthy medieval center of trade and finance? Scholars often identify it as a birthplace of the Renaissance, and it is now Tuscany’s capital and most populous city.
In Florence, which art museum houses Artemisia Gentileschi’s *Judith Slaying Holofernes*? It is one of the city’s major cultural institutions and is often mentioned alongside Palazzo Pitti.
In Florence, which landmark houses one of the city’s major museum collections? It is often named alongside the Uffizi when describing the city’s leading art institutions.

Which powerful banking family ruled Florence during periods of religious and republican upheaval and patronized artists such as Artemisia Gentileschi? One of its notable members was Lorenzo the Magnificent.
Florence served as the capital of an Italian state from 1865 to 1871. What was the name of that state?
What is the name of the civic park and monumental core in Washington, D.C., that extends between the U.S. Capitol and the Lincoln Memorial and contains the obelisk honoring George Washington?
At the western end of the National Mall, which temple-like landmark honors the 16th U.S. president with a monumental seated statue and inscriptions of his speeches?

This cold stream of Atlantic water travels northward along southwestern Africa, carrying nutrient-rich water toward Namibia and western South Africa. Wind-driven upwelling along its path sustains exceptionally productive fisheries, and the cool water helps generate fog along the Skeleton Coast. What is this oceanic flow called?

The Benguela Current contributes to cool, foggy coastal conditions across an arid region extending along Namibia and into southwestern Angola. Its landscape includes the famed dune fields around Sossusvlei. What is this region called?
What city on the Llano Estacado in Northwest Texas is the birthplace of Buddy Holly and a major regional hub along Interstate 27?

Lubbock is home to the main campus of which university whose athletic teams compete in the Big 12 Conference and whose live mascot is the Masked Rider? The institution also operates the National Ranching Heritage Center.
Which West African country borders Côte d’Ivoire, Burkina Faso, and Togo, and has a coastline on the Gulf of Guinea? Its capital is Accra.
In Ghana, which coastal city serves as the national capital and is the country’s largest urban center?
Measured above sea level, this Himalayan peak was assigned an elevation of 8,848.86 meters by a joint Nepalese-Chinese survey in 2020. Its summit lies on the Nepal–China border. What is the mountain?

On the standard southeast route from Nepal toward Mount Everest, climbers navigate this constantly shifting glacier passage, notorious for crevasses and collapsing seracs. What is this hazardous section called?

During Mount Everest’s first documented summit ascent in 1953, this Sherpa mountaineer reached the top alongside Edmund Hillary. Earlier in his career, he worked on Himalayan expeditions as a porter and high-altitude guide. Who was he?

On Lebanon’s Mediterranean coast, this ancient Phoenician port was an important center of trade and is regarded as one of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities. Its Greek name later became associated with a word for a book or sacred text. What city is it?
The Greek name of Byblos is linked to the Greek term *ta biblia*, meaning “the books.” What familiar English name for the Christian scriptures reflects this connection?

Begun by William the Conqueror after the Norman Conquest, this fortress stands beside the River Thames in England’s capital. Its royal complex is linked to the disappearance of two young princes in 1483. What historic landmark is it?

An exhibit at the Tower of London marks the place where a captured conspirator was interrogated after the failed 1605 attempt to destroy the Houses of Parliament. Which English Catholic plotter was discovered guarding explosives beneath Parliament?

This vast South Florida wetland is often called a “river of grass,” though its water spreads across a broad landscape rather than flowing in a single channel. Its habitats include sawgrass marshes and coastal mangrove forests. What is this landscape called?
The Everglades historically receives southbound water from this broad, shallow lake just to its north, the largest lake wholly within Florida. What is the lake’s name?

This artificial reservoir straddles the Nevada–Arizona border and was created when a major dam impounded a southwestern river. By water capacity, it is the largest reservoir in the United States. What is it?
Lake Mead was formed by a concrete dam near Boulder City that was completed in 1935 and was once the world’s tallest dam. What is the dam’s present-day name?
Lake Mead stores water behind a dam on this river, which forms part of the boundary between Arizona and California and eventually reaches the Gulf of California. What is the river’s name?
This Scottish city is the country’s largest and grew along the River Clyde, becoming a major center of shipbuilding and trade. Which city is it?
In Glasgow, Celtic and Rangers have contested one of the most prominent rivalries in Scottish football for generations. What is this rivalry known as?
Commissioned by cereal heiress Marjorie Merriweather Post and completed in 1927, this oceanfront Palm Beach estate later became a private club owned by Donald Trump. What historic landmark is it?

In August 2022, agents acting under a federal warrant entered Mar-a-Lago, and the inventory they filed listed government records with classification markings. What specific federal action at the estate became a major national news story?

A Central African geographic name appears in the official titles of two neighboring countries: one is a republic whose capital is Brazzaville, and the other is a democratic republic whose capital is Kinshasa. The same name is used for a major river and basin in the region; what is this shared geographic name?

In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this capital lies across the river from Brazzaville, the capital of the neighboring Republic of the Congo. The two cities face each other across Pool Malebo; what is the name of this capital?
Located in northern Utah, this large, shallow saline lake has no outlet to the ocean, causing dissolved minerals to concentrate as water evaporates. What is this inland body of water called?
In 1970, artist Robert Smithson built a massive coil of basalt rock and earth extending into the northeastern shore of the Great Salt Lake. What is the name of this celebrated land-art work?

This broad northwestern African region is commonly defined to include Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, and Libya. Its name derives from an Arabic term for “the west,” reflecting its position at the western edge of the Arab world. What is the region called?
Within the Maghreb, this highland chain extends through Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia. Its highest summit, Toubkal, rises in Morocco. What is the name of the chain?

At roughly 6,300 kilometers long, this is China’s longest river, flowing east from the country’s western highlands to the East China Sea near Shanghai. The Three Gorges Dam spans its course. What river is it?

In the mountainous upper reaches of the Yangtze River in Yunnan, the river cuts through deep gorges while running roughly parallel to the Mekong and Salween. What name is used for this stretch of the river?
Founded by Spain in 1565 on Florida’s Atlantic coast, this city is commonly regarded as the oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the continental United States. What city is it?
When St. Augustine was founded in 1565, this Spanish admiral led the expedition and became the first governor of Spanish Florida. Which person was he?
What is the largest city in Nevada, known internationally for its resort hotels, casinos, live entertainment, and major convention industry?

In Las Vegas, which hotel and casino features a giant musical fountain on an artificial lake said to be inspired by Italy’s Lake Como? It also houses Fiori di Como, Dale Chihuly’s largest glass sculpture.
Which major river of central Italy rises in the Tuscan Apennines, flows through Rome, and reaches the coast near Ostia?
The Tiber River flows through Rome and reaches the coast near Ostia. What sea does it empty into there?

Stretching from northeastern China and Mongolia through Eastern Europe, this vast belt of temperate grassland is credited with facilitating the spread of horse riding and wheeled transport. What is this geographic region called?
The Eurasian Steppe is crossed in its western reaches by a long line of highlands often used as the boundary between Europe and Asia. What is this range called?
Which city is the capital and largest urban center of Western Australia, located where a major river meets the Indian Ocean? Its attractions include Kings Park and a botanical garden on Mount Eliza.
Perth stands on the banks of this river, which flows through the city before reaching the Indian Ocean near Fremantle. What is the river called?

This is the world’s second-largest ocean, lying between the Americas to the west and Europe and Africa to the east. Its waters also reach the coasts of Angola and South Africa. What ocean is described?

A vast underwater mountain chain runs down the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, where tectonic plates move apart and new seafloor forms. Iceland is one of the few places where this feature rises above sea level. What is this mountain chain called?

This New Orleans neighborhood is the city’s original historic core, laid out in a street grid in 1722 by engineer Adrien de Pauger. Its central public square was first planned as Place d’Armes, and its Creole townhouses are known for wrought-iron balconies and rear courtyards. Name this district.

Within the French Quarter, this plaza was originally planned as Place d’Armes and was officially renamed in 1851. It occupies the district’s central public space near the Cathedral-Basilica of Saint Louis. What is its name?

Founded on the site of Byzantium and inaugurated as the Roman Empire’s new capital in 330 under Constantine the Great, this city later remained the principal center of the Eastern Roman Empire. It stands beside the Bosporus and the Sea of Marmara, and its historic core is now part of Istanbul. What city is it?

At Constantinople, what name is given to the defensive works built under Theodosius II along the city’s vulnerable western landward approach? Their multiple lines of fortification were backed by a moat, helping protect the city during sieges.

In 1204, a Western Christian expedition originally bound for the Holy Land instead captured and sacked Constantinople after becoming embroiled in Byzantine political disputes. Its conquest led to the creation of the short-lived Latin Empire; which crusading expedition was it?
This independent city on the northwest shore of Chesapeake Bay is Maryland’s most populous city, and its historic Inner Harbor lies near Camden Yards. What city is it?

Baltimore is an independent city rather than part of a county, and it is the most populous city in this state. Annapolis is the state capital, and the state’s name supplies the “M” in the DMV region. What state is it?

During the War of 1812, British forces bombarded this star-shaped military installation guarding Baltimore’s harbor. The defense inspired Francis Scott Key to write the poem that became the U.S. national anthem. What was it?

This Haitian island lies off the northern coast of the country’s northwestern peninsula. In the seventeenth century, it became a major refuge and base for French buccaneers and other Caribbean pirates. What is the island called?
Around 1640, French leader François Levasseur established a defensive stronghold near Tortuga’s southern anchorage. What was this installation called?
What is the name of Canada’s largest island, located in Nunavut in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago? It lies east of the mainland’s Melville Peninsula and west of Greenland.
On Baffin Island, what is the highest summit of the Baffin Mountains? It rises about 2,147 metres on the Cumberland Peninsula.

What name is given to a medieval or early modern world map that may combine geographic information with religious symbolism, biblical history, and legendary material? Such a work often presents the world through a culturally meaningful picture rather than a strictly measured survey.

A famous Mappamundi made around 1300 is among the largest surviving medieval world maps and is displayed in an English cathedral. Its inscription associates it with Richard of Haldingham and Lafford; what is this map commonly called?
This Vermont city serves as the state capital and has the smallest population of any U.S. state capital, with fewer than 10,000 residents. What is it called?
Montpelier is the capital of which northeastern U.S. state, nicknamed the Green Mountain State and situated between New York and New Hampshire?
Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania lie along the eastern shore of a northern European sea. What collective regional name is commonly used for these three countries?
Among the Baltic states, which is the northernmost country, with Tallinn as its capital and land borders with Latvia and Russia?

Which South Asian country has Islamabad as its capital and shares land borders with India, Afghanistan, Iran, and China? Its territory stretches from the Arabian Sea coast to the Karakoram, Hindu Kush, and Himalayan ranges.
In Pakistan, what body of water forms the country’s southern coastline, lying between the coasts of Oman and western India and opening into the wider Indian Ocean?

In Pakistan’s northwest, what historic mountain route runs through the Safed Koh range and connects the Peshawar area with Afghanistan near Torkham? For centuries, it has served for trade, migration, and military movement between South and Central Asia.

Pakistan’s Gilgit-Baltistan region contains which 8,611-meter peak in the Karakoram, second only to Everest in elevation? Its first successful ascent was made in 1954 by Italian climbers Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni.
Which New England state borders Vermont, Maine, Massachusetts, and Canada? Its capital is Concord.
In New Hampshire, what highland region contains the Presidential Range and Mount Washington, a peak famous for its severe weather?
Which New York City borough lies north of Manhattan and is the only one situated primarily on the mainland of the United States?
Along the western edge of The Bronx, this tidal waterway separates the borough from Manhattan and connects the Hudson and East Rivers. What is it called?

On the central-western Italian Peninsula, this city grew beside the Tiber and became the political center of the Roman Republic and Empire. It has been Italy’s capital since 1871, and Vatican City lies within its municipal boundaries; what city is it?

Rome stands along this river, which flows south through the city before turning west toward the Tyrrhenian Sea near Ostia. Roman legend says the twins Romulus and Remus were abandoned in it; what is the river’s name?

Within the municipal boundaries of Rome, this landlocked sovereign state is enclosed by the Italian capital and has the pope as its head of state. Its territory includes St. Peter’s Square and Basilica; name this independent country.
Rome hosted this international multisport event in 1960, when Ethiopian runner Abebe Bikila won the marathon barefoot. What edition of the modern Games was held there?

In Rome, this ancient venue occupied the valley between the Palatine and Aventine hills and hosted chariot races. A long central barrier called the spina divided its racing track; what was the venue’s name?

Located within Beijing’s Summer Palace, this large artificial body of water was created as a centerpiece of an imperial garden landscape. The Seventeen-Arch Bridge crosses it. What is this lake called?
On Kunming Lake in Beijing’s Summer Palace, this ornate stone crossing connects the eastern shore to Nanhu Island and is adorned with carved stone lions. What is this crossing called?
Which mountain in central Greece rises above Delphi and is associated with Apollo and the Muses? In Greek myth, it was also the refuge where Deucalion and Pyrrha came ashore after the great flood.
On the southern slopes of Mount Parnassus, which ancient Greek sanctuary was famed for the Pythia’s prophecies, the Castalian Spring, and an omphalos said to mark the world’s center?
This Nordic republic in Northern Europe shares land borders with Sweden, Norway, and Russia. Its southern coast faces a gulf across the water from Estonia. What country is it?
Finland’s capital is also its largest city, and it lies on the shore of the gulf that separates the country from Estonia. What city is it?
Finland’s western coastline faces this northern arm of the Baltic Sea, with Sweden on the opposite shore. What body of water is it?

This landlocked southwestern state occupies part of the Four Corners region and borders Texas and Oklahoma. The Rio Grande runs north to south through its center, and its capital is Santa Fe. What state is it?
New Mexico’s capital was founded in 1610 and is often described as the oldest state capital in the United States. What city serves as the state capital?

In New Mexico, this major river and its fertile valley form a north–south corridor through the center of the state. The river also continues south into Mexico before reaching the Gulf of Mexico. What river is it?

New Mexico hosted this 1945 event at the Alamogordo Bombing and Gunnery Range, marking the first detonation of a nuclear weapon. Conducted as part of the Manhattan Project, what was this event called?

This Wisconsin city on the western shore of Lake Michigan was home to early-20th-century Socialist reformers whose emphasis on clean, efficient municipal services inspired the phrase “sewer socialism.” Emil Seidel was elected mayor here in 1910, becoming the first Socialist mayor of a major American city. What city is it?

In Milwaukee, which Socialist politician became the first Socialist mayor of a major American city after winning the 1910 election? After losing reelection, he joined Eugene V. Debs’s 1912 presidential ticket as its vice-presidential nominee.
Which Texas Gulf Coast island city became a major nineteenth-century port before a catastrophic 1900 hurricane killed thousands and helped shift commercial prominence toward Houston?

After Galveston's 1900 hurricane weakened its commercial position, which nearby Texas city became the state's leading port, aided by a ship channel connecting it to the Gulf of Mexico? It is now Texas's most populous city.
Which Southcentral Alaska city lies at the head of Cook Inlet and is the state’s most populous? Its growth was spurred by serving as the Alaska Railroad’s construction headquarters in 1914–15.

Anchorage hosts the ceremonial downtown start of an annual sled-dog race, but that short segment does not count toward the timed competition. What city on the southern Seward Peninsula is the race’s finish line?

Which large reservoir on the Colorado River stretches through Glen Canyon along the Utah–Arizona border, near the natural Rainbow Bridge? It was created when a major dam near Page, Arizona, was completed.
Lake Powell is held back by which concrete arch-gravity structure on the Colorado River near Page, Arizona? Completed in 1966, its construction created the reservoir.
A historic stone crossing in southwestern Beijing spans the Yongding River. Its balustrades are famed for their many carved stone lions. Which landmark is this?
The Marco Polo Bridge spans this river on Beijing’s southwestern outskirts. Historically called the Wuding River, it was renamed during the Qing dynasty; what is its present-day name?
First documented in the 13th century, this city is Germany’s capital and largest city. During the Cold War, a wall divided it into eastern and western sectors. What city is it?
This waterway runs through Berlin and flows into the Havel in the city’s western district of Spandau. What river is it?
Berlin is home to this UNESCO-listed complex on an island in the Spree, where five major institutions include the Pergamon and Neues. What is the complex called?

On Mainland in Scotland’s Orkney archipelago, this Neolithic monument is a large circular arrangement of standing stones set between the Lochs of Stenness and Harray. What is the name of this prehistoric site?

The Ring of Brodgar is one of several major prehistoric monuments grouped with Skara Brae, Maeshowe, and the Stones of Stenness in a UNESCO World Heritage property. What is the name of that archaeological landscape?

This Scottish capital is known for its medieval Old Town and Georgian New Town, with a historic fortress standing on Castle Rock above its central streets. Each August, it fills with performers during a celebrated month-long arts festival.
Edinburgh is Scotland’s capital, but what is the country’s largest city, located on the River Clyde and home to the football clubs Celtic and Rangers, whose rivalry is known as the Old Firm derby?

Wind deposits loose grains into these landforms, which may build into ridges and shift as prevailing winds change. They occur in settings ranging from the shores of Lake Michigan in Indiana to the base of mountains in Colorado.
At this Colorado site, the Sand Dunes rise against the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, and Star Dune reaches about 750 feet from its base, making it North America’s tallest dune. Which site is it?
answer: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve

question: This landmark is a three-part cascade along the Canada–United States border, between New York and Ontario. Its sections are named Horseshoe, American, and Bridal Veil; the Niagara River divides around Goat Island, and most of its flow plunges over the largest section. What is this landmark?

Niagara Falls lies on this north-flowing river, which connects Lake Erie to Lake Ontario and forms part of the U.S.–Canada border. Near the falls, the river splits around Goat Island. What river is it?
Which city is Lebanon’s capital and largest urban center, set on the country’s Mediterranean coast? Its port was the site of a catastrophic explosion in August 2020.
Beirut is located on Lebanon’s western coastline and has long been an important seaport. Along which major body of water does the city lie?

Which Central Texas city is the seat of Travis County and the state capital? Its historic street grid was laid out between Waller Creek and Shoal Creek, with Congress Avenue leading from the river toward Capitol Square.

In Austin’s historic street plan, Congress Avenue runs from this river toward Capitol Square. This Central Texas waterway flows southeast through the Highland Lakes before reaching the Gulf of Mexico near Matagorda Bay.
This southeastern U.S. state has a peninsula between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean, and it borders both Georgia and Alabama. What state is it?
Florida’s state capital sits in the Panhandle, near the Georgia border, and serves as the seat of the state government. What city is it?
Founded by Spain in 1565, this Florida city is the oldest continuously inhabited European-established settlement in the United States. What city is it?
Along Florida’s Keys, this living coral barrier formation is the only one of its kind in the continental United States. What is it?
In Florida, this vast South Florida wetland is often called the “River of Grass” and receives slow-moving water from Lake Okeechobee. What natural region is it?
Which Mid-Atlantic state lies between New York and Pennsylvania, fronts the Atlantic Ocean, and has its capital in Trenton? It is the most densely populated state in the United States.

In New Jersey, which city is the state capital and sits on the Delaware River, directly across from Morrisville, Pennsylvania? Its historic State House is among the oldest state capitol buildings in the country.

In New Jersey, what large forested region in the south is characterized by acidic sandy soils, extensive cedar swamps, and a distinctive fire-adapted ecosystem? Local folklore associates this region with a legendary creature bearing the state's name.
Which city is the capital of the Philippines and lies on Luzon at the mouth of the Pasig River? Its historic center includes a Spanish-era walled quarter and Fort Santiago.

Within Manila, what historic walled district was the center of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines? It includes Fort Santiago and is known for its preserved stone walls and colonial-era churches.

This New England state has Boston as its capital and an Atlantic coastline that includes a prominent sandy peninsula. It ratified the U.S. Constitution on February 6, 1788, becoming the sixth state to join the Union. What state is it?
In Massachusetts, this sandy peninsula arcs southeast into the Atlantic and borders a large bay on its northern side. Provincetown sits at its northern tip, while a canal crosses its narrow base.

What waterfall in Venezuela plunges from Auyán-tepui in Canaima National Park? With a total height of about 979 meters and an uninterrupted drop of about 807 meters, it is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall.
Angel Falls takes its English name from which American aviator? His 1933 flight over the Venezuelan tepui region helped bring the waterfall to wider attention.

Located in northeastern Jiangxi Province, this city developed a centuries-old ceramic industry and became renowned for blue-and-white wares decorated with cobalt. What city is known as China’s porcelain capital?

Wares made in Jingdezhen are famed for this ceramic material, traditionally produced with kaolin and fired at very high temperatures. It is dense and hard, and can have a white, slightly translucent body. What is this material?
This Northern European sea is bordered by Poland, Estonia, Latvia, and several other countries. It connects to the North Sea through the Kiel Canal.

The Baltic Sea connects to the North Sea through this artificial waterway in northern Germany, opened in 1895, which runs from Brunsbüttel to the Baltic coast and lets ships avoid sailing around Jutland.

Which constituent country of the United Kingdom occupies the northeastern part of the large island separated from Great Britain by the North Channel? It shares a land border with the independent state to its south, consists of six traditional counties, and has Belfast as its capital.
In Northern Ireland, which lake is the largest in the British Isles by surface area and lies west of Belfast? Its shores touch the counties of Antrim, Down, Armagh, Tyrone, and Londonderry.

Which major tributary of the Paraná River flows through southern Brazil and northeastern Argentina before forming a vast waterfall system along their border? The river shares its name with that waterfall system.

The Iguazu River forms a famous waterfall along the boundary between Argentina’s Misiones Province and the Paraná state of which neighboring country? The city of Foz do Iguaçu lies on this country’s side of the falls.

This landlocked Central European country has Prague as its capital and borders Austria, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia. It became independent when Czechoslovakia peacefully dissolved at the end of 1992. What is this country’s natural English name?
Which historic land forms the western and largest part of Czechia, alongside Moravia and Czech Silesia? Its name also inspired a term for an artist or way of life associated with nonconformity.
Which country lies east of Czechia and was the other constituent republic of Czechoslovakia before its peaceful dissolution in 1992?

What transboundary groundwater reservoir lies beneath parts of Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Argentina, and is named for the Indigenous people of the region? It is considered one of the world’s largest underground freshwater reserves.
The Guarani Aquifer extends beneath this landlocked South American country, whose capital is Asunción and which shares the Itaipu Dam with Brazil on the Paraná River. What country is it?

This western Mexican city is the capital of Jalisco and the country’s second most populous city. Its historic center is known for a cathedral that combines Gothic and Baroque influences. What city is it?

In Guadalajara’s historic center, this landmark’s twin spires are among the city’s best-known skyline features, and its design blends Gothic and Baroque influences. What is this religious landmark commonly called?

A dam on the Amstel gave this Dutch city its name, and a 12th-century fishing settlement there grew into a major port during the Dutch Golden Age. It is the Netherlands’ largest city and official capital, although the national government sits elsewhere. Which city is it?

In Amsterdam, this planned 17th-century expansion is made up of three concentric waterways, including the Herengracht, Keizersgracht, and Prinsengracht. Its historic canal district is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site; what is the Dutch name for this canal ring?

In Amsterdam, this institution began operating in 1602 under the Dutch East India Company, whose shares could be bought and sold there. It is often described as the earliest modern securities market; what institution was it?

Set in a valley along the Miljacka River and surrounded by the Dinaric Alps, this city became the focus of a nearly four-year siege during the Bosnian War. It is also where Gavrilo Princip assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914. What city is it?

During the 1990s siege of Sarajevo, this informal name referred to an exposed stretch of Ulica Zmaja od Bosne and Meša Selimović Boulevard, where civilians risked fire from hidden gunmen while crossing the city. What was this notorious route called?

This arm of the Mediterranean lies between Italy and the Balkan Peninsula, with Croatia, Montenegro, and Albania among the countries along its eastern shore. At its southeastern end, it connects to the Ionian Sea through the Strait of Otranto. What sea is it?
On the Adriatic Sea’s eastern coast in southern Croatia, this historic city is famous for its medieval walls enclosing a UNESCO-listed Old Town. Which city is it?
This East African country has Nairobi as its capital and largest city, borders South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia, Tanzania, and Uganda, and has a coastline on the Indian Ocean. What country is it?
Kenya shares this African lake with Uganda and Tanzania. It is the continent’s largest lake by surface area, and its northern outlet sends water onward into the Nile system. Name the lake.
Kenya’s second-largest city is also its oldest major city and a major Indian Ocean port. It is situated on an island linked to the mainland by bridges and ferries. What city is it?

What is the geological landform called when an extraterrestrial body strikes a planetary surface, excavating a depression that may have a raised rim? The well-preserved Barringer feature in Arizona is a classic example.
The Chicxulub impact crater, linked to the asteroid strike that caused the end-Cretaceous extinction, lies beneath the Mexican landform that includes Cancún and Mérida. What is this landform called?
At the meeting of the Huangpu and Yangtze rivers near the East China Sea, this municipality grew into a major treaty port and financial center. What Chinese city is it?

In the age of sail, unscrupulous recruiters sometimes got incapacitated men aboard departing ships, where they were forced into service as crew. What maritime practice, whose name is linked to Shanghai, was this?
Which Southeast Asian country occupies the eastern side of the Indochinese Peninsula and borders China, Laos, and Cambodia? Its capital is Hanoi, and its largest city is Ho Chi Minh City.
Vietnam shares its western border with this landlocked Southeast Asian country, whose capital is Vientiane. The Mekong River forms part of its border with Thailand.

Vietnam’s eastern coastline faces this marginal sea of the Pacific Ocean, which lies between mainland Southeast Asia and the Philippines. The Paracel and Spratly island groups are located in these waters.
Centered in California’s Santa Clara County, this region grew into a global center of the American technology industry. By what name is it commonly known?
Within Silicon Valley, which city is the region’s largest by population and the third-largest city in California? Located at the southern end of San Francisco Bay, it is also home to the SAP Center.

The 1989 Romanian Revolution centered on this city, where Nicolae and Elena Ceaușescu fled the Communist Party headquarters after a mass rally turned against them. Today, it is Romania’s capital and largest city. What city is it?
Bucharest is the capital and largest city of this European country, which has a Black Sea coastline and includes the Danube Delta at the river’s mouth. What country is it?
This northwestern European country has a North Sea coastline and land borders with Germany and Belgium. Its nominal capital is also its most populous city. What is the country?

In the Netherlands, the monarch and cabinet are based in a city often confused with the capital, although Amsterdam holds that formal designation. The city is also home to the Binnenhof complex and the International Court of Justice. What is it?

Roughly a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, and centuries of drainage and land reclamation have made many enclosed tracts usable for farming and settlement. What is the geographic term for these reclaimed lands?
The Netherlands has a long coastline on this marginal sea of the Atlantic, situated between Great Britain and the continental coasts of Belgium, Germany, Denmark, and Norway. Identify the sea.
In the Netherlands, which northern province has a distinct West Frisian-speaking community and is the only province where that language has official status alongside Dutch?
This fog-bound, shipwreck-strewn stretch of Namibia’s Atlantic-facing shoreline in southwestern Africa runs from near the Kunene River to near the Swakop River. What is this region called?

The Skeleton Coast lies along Namibia’s western edge, where the cold Benguela Current contributes to heavy coastal fog. Which ocean borders this coast and also washes the shores of Angola and South Africa?
On Tanzania’s Lake Tanganyika shoreline, this protected area became renowned for decades of research into wild chimpanzee behavior, including tool use. What is its name?
At Gombe Stream National Park, a British primatologist began a long-term study of chimpanzees in 1960 and documented their use of grass stems to collect termites. Who led this research?

This Dare County town occupies the northern Outer Banks of North Carolina and is widely associated with the Wright brothers’ first powered flight. The 1903 flight itself took place several miles to its south; what town is commonly credited with it?
Kitty Hawk is often linked to the Wright brothers’ first powered flight, but their December 1903 flights took place farther south. In which Outer Banks town is the flight site located?

Which peninsula forms much of the urban mainland of Hong Kong and lies across Victoria Harbour from Hong Kong Island? Its name is also associated with a famous walled enclave that existed within the city.

On the Kowloon Peninsula, what densely populated enclave remained under Chinese jurisdiction during British rule of Hong Kong, despite being surrounded by colonial territory? It was demolished in the 1990s, and its site later became a park.

Located on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula, this major ancient Maya city is known for a stepped pyramid called El Castillo and for one of the largest ceremonial ball courts in Mesoamerica. What archaeological site is it?
At Chichén Itzá, what monumental playing arena has long parallel walls decorated with ballgame reliefs, including a scene of a decapitated player?
Alaska’s capital lies on the mainland shore of Gastineau Channel in the Panhandle, hemmed in by the Coast Mountains and lacking a road connection to the rest of the state. Which city is it?
Juneau fronts this waterway, which separates the city from Douglas Island and runs through the heart of its waterfront. What is the waterway’s name?
This Central European city is both the capital and largest city of Czechia, and it historically served as the capital of Bohemia. It developed along the Vltava River; what city is it?

In Prague, this medieval stone crossing spans the Vltava between the Old Town and Malá Strana. Construction began in 1357 under a Bohemian king who later became Holy Roman Emperor, and rows of statues line its parapets; what is it called?
Founded in Prague in 1348 by a Bohemian king who later became Holy Roman Emperor, this institution is considered the oldest center of higher education in Central Europe. What is its established name?

Which Habsburg emperor made Prague his principal residence around the turn of the 17th century, drawing artists, scholars, and alchemists to his court? His reign, from 1576 to 1612, is associated with a flourishing of the city's court culture.

In Prague's Old Town Hall, this medieval timepiece combines an astronomical dial with a calendar display and an hourly procession of figures. First installed in 1410, it is among the city's best-known historic mechanisms; what is it called?

This pre-Columbian Mississippian urban center near present-day St. Louis was one of the largest cities north of Mexico before European contact. Its central precinct includes the continent’s largest pre-Columbian earthen mound. What is the name of this historic site?
At Cahokia, this massive, flat-topped earthen structure rises about 100 feet and covers roughly 14 acres. It is the largest pre-Columbian earthwork in North America. What is it called?
This Nordic kingdom occupies much of the Scandinavian Peninsula and has Stockholm as its capital. It shares land borders with Norway and Finland; what country is it?
Along Sweden’s eastern coast, this northern arm of the Baltic Sea separates the country from Finland and narrows toward the north. What is this body of water called?
In Sweden’s constitutional monarchy, this unicameral legislature meets in Stockholm and exercises the country’s legislative authority. What is the name of this parliament?

What landform forms when a river enters a standing body of water and slows enough to deposit its sediment? Its surface is often triangular or fan-shaped, and branching distributary channels may cross it.
The river delta at the northern edge of Egypt spreads into the Mediterranean and has major distributary outlets historically associated with Rosetta and Damietta. What is this delta called?
Which southern U.S. state is the second-largest by area and includes both Dallas and Houston? Its capital is Austin.
In Texas, which major Gulf Coast city is home to the octagonal Rothko Chapel, whose interior contains fourteen paintings by Mark Rothko? It is also the state’s most populous city.
What is the largest of the historic lands that make up Czechia, occupying its western part and containing Prague? Mountain ranges form much of its borders with Germany and Austria.
In Bohemia’s capital, Prague, this river flows beneath the Charles Bridge and continues north to meet the Elbe at Mělník. What is it?
This jointly operated hydroelectric dam spans the Paraná River along the border between Brazil and Paraguay. It is one of the world’s largest power-generating facilities; what is it called?
The Itaipu Dam is shared by Brazil and this landlocked South American country, whose capital is Asunción and which lies north of Argentina. What country is it?

This continent is bordered by the Mediterranean Sea to the north, the Atlantic Ocean to the west, and the Indian Ocean to the east. It is the world’s second-largest continent and is crossed by both the equator and the prime meridian. What continent is it?
Which country in Africa is the continent’s largest by area? It stretches across much of the Sahara and has a Mediterranean coastline, with its capital also named for the country.

The African Union, which brings together countries across Africa, has its headquarters in this Ethiopian capital. The city also hosts the headquarters of the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa. What city is it?
In Fyodor Dostoevsky’s *Crime and Punishment*, the student Raskolnikov is convicted of murder and sentenced to penal servitude in a vast region of northern Asia. What is the name of that region?

Siberia lies on the Asian side of the traditional divide between Europe and Asia in Russia. Which north–south highland chain is commonly treated as Siberia’s western boundary and as that continental divide?
Situated between New Brunswick and Nova Scotia on Canada’s Atlantic coast, this bay is famous for some of the world’s highest tides. What is its name?

On the New Brunswick shore of the Bay of Fundy, this coastal attraction features tall, flowerpot-shaped sea stacks sculpted by erosion. Visitors can walk around their bases at low tide, when the ocean floor is exposed; what are these formations called?

Which Southern European country occupies most of a boot-shaped peninsula projecting into the Mediterranean, has the Alps along its northern land frontier, and includes Sicily and Sardinia? Its capital is Rome.
Italy’s largest Mediterranean island is separated from Calabria by the Strait of Messina and has Palermo as its largest city. What is this island?
