Italy shares its northeastern land border with which country, whose capital is Ljubljana and whose short Adriatic coastline lies south of Trieste?
Italy completely surrounds this independent republic, whose historic center and three towers crown Mount Titano. Name the republic.
Italy includes this large island west of its mainland, the second-largest in the Mediterranean Sea. Its capital is Cagliari; name the island.
This constituent country occupies the central and southern part of Great Britain, with Scotland along its northern border and Wales to its west. Which country is it?
England’s northern land boundary reaches from the Solway Firth in the west to the North Sea in the east. Which neighboring country lies across that border?
South of England, this body of water separates Great Britain from northern France and connects the Atlantic Ocean with the North Sea. What is it called?

This Indonesian stratovolcano on Sumbawa Island produced a catastrophic eruption in April 1815, triggering a massive caldera collapse and global cooling. Which volcano’s eruption led to the Year Without a Summer?

The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora sent ash and aerosols into the atmosphere, contributing to severe cooling and crop failures across the Northern Hemisphere in 1816. What is this famously cold period called?

Lebanon’s second-largest city is also a major port on the eastern Mediterranean, about 85 km north of Beirut. Its historic center includes Mamluk-era souks and a hilltop citadel associated with the Crusader Raymond de Saint-Gilles. What city is this?

Just off Tripoli, Lebanon, this protected area encompasses three small islands and surrounding waters. Established in 1992, it serves as a nesting site for loggerhead sea turtles and a stopover for migratory birds. What is this site?

This incorporated village sits along the Hudson River in Westchester County, just north of Tarrytown. Formerly called North Tarrytown, it adopted its present name in 1996, drawing on the title of a famous Washington Irving story. What is the village called?

The village of Sleepy Hollow is closely tied to a short story by this 19th-century American author, who also wrote “Rip Van Winkle.” Both tales appeared in his collection *The Sketch Book of Geoffrey Crayon*. Who was the author?

This West African country borders Sierra Leone, Guinea, and Côte d’Ivoire and has an Atlantic coastline. Its flag has red-and-white stripes with a single white star in a blue canton; what country is it?
Liberia’s capital is a major Atlantic port at the mouth of the Mesurado River. Named in honor of U.S. President James Monroe, what city is it?
This is Ethiopia’s largest lake and the source of the Blue Nile. The river leaves it over a waterfall before flowing onward toward Sudan. What is the name of this lake?
Lake Tana feeds the Blue Nile, which leaves the lake over a waterfall in Ethiopia. What is the name of this waterfall?

This Northern Triangle country is the smallest sovereign state in mainland Central America and has a Pacific coastline but no Caribbean shore. It borders Guatemala to the west and Honduras to the north and east. What country is it?

On El Salvador’s southeastern Pacific coast, this gulf is shared with Honduras and Nicaragua. The Salvadoran port city of La Unión lies on its shore, and its islands include Meanguera. What is the gulf called?

This long, narrow country occupies South America's Pacific-facing edge between the Andes and the ocean, stretching from the Atacama region in the north toward Tierra del Fuego in the south. Its capital is Santiago, and it administers Easter Island; name the country.
Chile's capital and largest city is also its seat of government, where the Palacio de La Moneda stands. Located in a basin between the Andes and the Coastal Range, what city is it?
Chile's long western mainland coast faces this ocean, whose waters also separate South America from Easter Island. Name the ocean.
Chile shares an especially long boundary with this neighbor to its east, with the Andes forming much of the frontier. The two countries also divide the island of Tierra del Fuego; name the neighbor.
Chile's far north includes this hyperarid expanse, lying between the Pacific coast and the Andes. It is famous for nitrate deposits and exceptionally clear skies; what is this region called?

This major South Asian river flows through Varanasi and is revered in Hinduism as the goddess Ganga. Its waters join the Brahmaputra system through the Padma to help form the delta of Bangladesh. What river is this?
The Ganges flows through this Indian city in Uttar Pradesh, renowned for its riverside ghats and temples. Historically, the city has also been known as Benares. Name this city.
Established on March 1, 1872, this protected area became the first of its kind in the world. Its hydrothermal landmarks include Old Faithful and Grand Prismatic Spring; name the protected area.

Yellowstone National Park lies almost entirely in one U.S. state, with smaller portions extending into Montana and Idaho. National Park Service figures place about 96% of the park in this state, whose capital is Cheyenne; name it.

This New England state occupies the northeasternmost corner of the contiguous United States and includes Aroostook County along its Canadian border. Its coast also contains Mount Desert Island, home to New England’s only national park. What state is it?
On Maine’s Mount Desert Island, which protected area includes Cadillac Mountain and a network of carriage roads financed by John D. Rockefeller Jr.?
Which Michoacán volcano famously began erupting in a farmer’s cornfield in 1943, forming a new cinder cone and eventually burying a nearby town?
Parícutin’s 1943 lava flows overwhelmed a settlement in Michoacán near Uruapan. The spires of the town’s church remained visible above the hardened lava; what was the settlement called?
This historic coastal city in Georgia is a major Atlantic port and was the destination of Sherman’s March to the Sea in 1864. What is the city?
During the 1779 Siege of Savannah, which Polish-born Continental Army officer led a cavalry charge and was mortally wounded?
At 14,115 feet, this mountain rises just west of Colorado Springs and is the tallest summit in Colorado’s southern Front Range. What is its name?
Pikes Peak rises just west of this city, whose Garden of the Gods park is known for sandstone formations called the Kissing Camels and Cathedral Spires. What city is it?
This national capital stands at about 2,240 meters on the Mexican Central Plateau and was rebuilt over the ruins of a Mexica city after the Spanish conquest. What is this city?
Mexico City lies within this high-altitude basin, a broad geographical region surrounded by mountains in central Mexico. What is the basin called?
Mexico City occupies the site of this Mexica island capital, founded around 1325 in Lake Texcoco and captured after a Spanish siege in 1521. What was the name of the capital?

This remote Polynesian island is administered by Chile and lies about 3,700 kilometres from the South American mainland. Its volcanic landscape is famous for monumental stone figures carved by its Indigenous people.
On Easter Island, this volcanic quarry supplied much of the tuff used to carve the monumental statues. Unfinished figures on its slopes offer evidence of how the statues were made.

This hyperarid region in northern Chile is widely regarded as the driest nonpolar area on Earth. It lies west of the Andes, where the mountains’ rain shadow helps limit precipitation. What is this region called?
In the Atacama Desert, a coastal fog forms when moist air is cooled by the cold Humboldt Current and becomes trapped beneath a temperature inversion. What is this fog called?
This island is the largest in Greece and the second-largest island in the eastern Mediterranean after Cyprus. Its mountainous interior and long coastline lie south of the Greek mainland.

On Crete, this major Minoan palatial center lies near modern Heraklion and was extensively excavated by Arthur Evans beginning in 1900. Its remains include a large central court and elaborate frescoes.
This ancient Greek sanctuary and settlement stood in Phocis near Mount Parnassus and was renowned throughout the Greek world for Apollo’s oracle. What was its name?
At Delphi, what was the title of the priestess who delivered Apollo’s prophecies from the sanctuary, traditionally seated on a tripod in his temple?

This coastal city in southeastern India is the capital of Tamil Nadu and a major port on the Bay of Bengal. It is also the center of the Tamil-language film industry often called Kollywood. What is the city’s natural name?

In Chennai, this fortified complex was established by the English East India Company in 1644 and became an early center of British power on the Coromandel Coast. Today it houses a museum and the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. What is it called?
This terrain develops where groundwater dissolves soluble bedrock, producing sinkholes, caves, and underground drainage. What is the name of this landscape type?
In Karst terrain, which calcium-carbonate-rich sedimentary rock is commonly dissolved by groundwater and can be transformed into marble by metamorphism?
Its capital is Jefferson City, and it entered the Union in 1821 under the terms of the 1820 compromise that admitted Maine as a free state. Which U.S. state is it?
In Missouri, which major city sits on the Mississippi River near its confluence with the Missouri River and is marked by the Gateway Arch?
Located on Honshu in the Kanto region, this city is Japan’s national capital and its largest metropolitan center. It is home to districts such as Shinjuku and Shibuya. What city is it?
What 634-meter broadcasting and observation tower in Tokyo opened in 2012 and became Japan’s tallest structure?
This large South Asian country has land borders with Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar. Its coastline touches both the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal; name the country.
India’s modern national capital is a purpose-built administrative city that contains Parliament and the offices of the central government. What is this capital?
India shares much of its eastern border with this low-lying country, whose landscape includes the vast Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta. Dhaka is its capital; name the country.
A belt of shifting dunes and sparse rainfall in northwestern India crosses into Pakistan; most of its Indian extent lies in Rajasthan. What is this region called?
Along India’s Arabian Sea-facing coast, this mountain chain forms a steep escarpment along the edge of the Deccan Plateau. It is also recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot; name the range.

This long, narrow island forms the central borough of New York City, with the Hudson River to its west and the East River to its east. It contains Central Park and is home to neighborhoods such as Washington Heights and the Upper East Side. What island is it?
On Manhattan Island, this neighborhood is associated with the Apollo Theater on 125th Street and was a major center of African American culture during the 1920s. What neighborhood is it?

What name is given to the long underwater mountain system formed where oceanic plates move apart and new seafloor is created? It typically extends through an ocean basin and may have a central rift valley.
The Gakkel Ridge is a slow-spreading segment of the global mid-ocean ridge system beneath this polar ocean. Which ocean is it?

Once the center of the Tamna kingdom, this volcanic island province lies south of the Korean Peninsula and is part of South Korea. It is known for its distinctive local culture and prominent central mountain. What is the island’s name?
Rising near the center of Jeju Island, this dormant shield volcano is the highest mountain in South Korea. Its summit crater lake is called Baengnokdam. What is the volcano’s name?

Rising in the San Bernardino Mountains near Cajon Pass, this Southern California river passes Victorville and Barstow before reaching an inland basin. Its flow is intermittent, and much of its channel runs underground through the desert. What river is it?
The Mojave River’s northeastern course ends at this dry lake bed near Baker, where floodwaters may collect before evaporating. What is the name of this playa?

This East Asian country occupies the northern part of the Korean Peninsula, with Pyongyang as its capital. It shares land borders with China and Russia and is separated from its southern neighbor by the Korean Demilitarized Zone.
A substantial stretch of North Korea’s northwestern border with China follows this river. It flows into Korea Bay near the cities of Sinuiju and Dandong.

This provincial-level municipality in northern China is mostly surrounded by Hebei Province and borders Tianjin to the southeast. It served as the country’s political center for much of the past eight centuries; what is its name?

In Beijing, this vast walled complex was the residence of emperors from the Ming through Qing dynasties and now houses the Palace Museum. What traditional English name refers to this former imperial precinct, where ordinary people were once barred from entering?

In Beijing, emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties held ceremonies at this religious complex to pray for good harvests. Its best-known building is the circular Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests; what is the complex called?
This former imperial retreat in Beijing is known for its expansive Kunming Lake and the Long Corridor, a covered walkway decorated with paintings. What is the name of this lakeside garden complex?
This active composite volcano rises beside the Bay of Naples in southern Italy. Its eruption in 79 CE buried Pompeii and Herculaneum beneath volcanic deposits. What is its natural name?

During the 79 CE eruption of Mount Vesuvius, this Roman author observed events from across the Bay of Naples and later described them in letters to the historian Tacitus. His account gave its name to a distinctive explosive eruption style. Who was he?
What geographic coordinate measures angular distance east or west from the Prime Meridian, which passes through Greenwich, England?
Earth rotates 360 degrees in roughly 24 hours, so a one-hour difference in local solar time corresponds to what amount of longitude? Give the value to the nearest degree.
This landlocked Central European country occupies much of the Carpathian Basin and has Budapest as its capital. It borders seven countries, including Austria and Romania. What country is it?

In Hungary, this capital city was formed from the historic cities of Buda and Pest, which sit on opposite banks of the Danube. It is also the country’s largest city and principal cultural and economic center. What city is it?
This major European river flows through Hungary and divides Budapest’s historic Buda and Pest sides. From there, it continues southeast toward Serbia and the Black Sea. What river is it?
Hungary’s northern neighbor is a landlocked country whose capital, Bratislava, lies on the Danube. It was part of Czechoslovakia until that country’s peaceful dissolution in 1993. What country is it?
In western Hungary, this large freshwater lake is often called the “Hungarian Sea.” Its north shore includes the Tihany Peninsula, and its southern shore is lined with resort towns. What lake is it?

This rugged range lies between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea and forms part of the boundary between Europe and Asia. Its peaks include Mount Elbrus, often considered Europe’s highest mountain. What is the range called?

The Caucasus Mountains reach from the Black Sea in the west to this body of water in the east. Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, stands on its shore, and it is the world’s largest inland body of water. What is it?

This French overseas department occupies a volcanic island in the Mascarene group east of Madagascar. Its capital is Saint-Denis, and a flaperon from Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 washed ashore there in 2015. What island is it?

Réunion lies about 200 kilometers southwest of this sovereign island country in the Mascarene group. Its capital is Port Louis, and its extinct flightless dodo has become a national symbol. What country is it?
Formed in Germany’s Black Forest by the meeting of the Brigach and Breg, which European river flows through or beside Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade before reaching the Black Sea?

At the Black Sea, the Danube River spreads into a vast network of channels, lakes, and reed beds, mostly in Romania but extending into Ukraine. What UNESCO-listed wetland region there is a major habitat for pelicans?

This large marginal sea of the Atlantic is bordered by the southern United States, the Yucatán Peninsula, and Cuba. It connects to the Caribbean Sea through the Yucatán Channel and to the Atlantic through the Straits of Florida; what is it called?

Within the Gulf of Mexico, a warm-water circulation feature carries Caribbean water into the basin and onward through the Straits of Florida toward the Gulf Stream. Its path changes over time; what is this feature called?
This is the 50th state admitted to the United States and the only state made up entirely of islands. Its capital is Honolulu, in the central Pacific Ocean. What state is it?
Hawaii’s capital and largest city is located on Oʻahu, near the famous Waikīkī neighborhood. What city is the seat of the state government?
About two-thirds of Hawaii’s residents live on this island, which is also home to the state capital. It is the third-largest of the main Hawaiian Islands. What island is it?
Hawaii’s largest island lies at the southeastern end of the main island chain and is often called the Big Island. What is its proper name?

Hawaii lies entirely south of this named latitude line, located at approximately 23.5 degrees north. It marks the northernmost latitude where the Sun can appear directly overhead. What is the line called?

This Indonesian volcanic island sits in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra. Its 1883 eruption generated enormous explosions, tsunamis, and atmospheric effects recorded around the world. What is its natural name?
Krakatoa lies in the waterway separating Java from Sumatra, between the Java Sea and the Indian Ocean. What is this strait called?

This mountain range forms a long arc between the Indo-Gangetic Plain to the south and the Tibetan Plateau to the north. It stretches across several countries in Asia and formed as the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates collided. What is its natural name?

Within the Himalayas, this summit is the highest point on Earth and lies on the Nepal–China border. Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent of it in 1953. What is the mountain’s name?
The Himalayas formed as the Indian tectonic slab moved north and collided with the continental mass underlying much of Europe and Asia. What is the name of that mass?

What collective name is given to planned artificial archipelagos built off the coast of the United Arab Emirates? Their layouts resemble a tree with a broad central trunk and curved rows of fronds extending from it.
The Palm Islands sit offshore from this city, the most populous in the United Arab Emirates and home to the Burj Khalifa. Which city is it?
What named stretch of the Indian Ocean lies between Madagascar and the coast of southeastern Africa?

The Mozambique Channel receives the waters of a major southern African river that forms a large delta on Mozambique’s coast. The same river flows through Zambia and is the site of Victoria Falls; what is it called?
Which Southeast Asian country moved its national capital from Yangon in 2005? Mandalay lies within its borders, and the Irrawaddy River flows through it toward the Andaman Sea.
In Myanmar, which purpose-built inland city replaced Yangon as the national capital in 2005? It is located in a purpose-designated union territory near the country’s geographic center.
This great circle encircles Earth at zero degrees latitude and divides the planet into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. What is it called?
The Equator crosses this South American country, whose capital is Quito and largest city is Guayaquil. The Galápagos Islands are also part of its territory; what country is it?

Rising in the Rocky Mountains, this river flows southwest across the arid plateaus of the American Southwest, carved the Grand Canyon, and approaches its delta at the Gulf of California. Which major river of the American Southwest is it?
The Colorado River carved this immense Arizona gorge, whose North and South Rims overlook a landscape more than a mile deep in places. What natural feature is it?
Completed in 1935 across the Colorado River near Black Canyon, this dam created Lake Mead and was named for a U.S. president. What dam is it?
In 1869, this one-armed Civil War veteran led an expedition through the rapids of the Colorado River’s Grand Canyon; he later led a second expedition in the region. Who was he?

The Colorado River’s extensive system of allocations and management draws on interstate compacts, federal laws, court decisions, and an international treaty with Mexico. What collective name is commonly given to this framework?

This Great Plains state entered the Union in 1889, with its admission listed as either the 39th or 40th because President Benjamin Harrison shuffled the statehood papers. It also shares the Standing Rock Indian Reservation with its southern neighbor.
In North Dakota, which river is impounded by Garrison Dam to form Lake Sakakawea? The same river flows through South Dakota and joins the Mississippi near St. Louis.

Which southwestern European country occupies the western part of the Iberian Peninsula and shares its only land border with Spain? Its capital is Lisbon, and its territory also includes two autonomous Atlantic archipelagos.
Portugal includes an autonomous Atlantic archipelago made up of nine main volcanic islands, among them São Miguel, Terceira, and Pico. What is this island group, located far west of the mainland?
Portugal’s only land neighbor occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula and borders it to the north and east. Which country has Madrid as its capital?

A major northern California city sits on a peninsula between the Pacific Ocean and its namesake bay, and its government combines municipal and county functions. The Embarcadero, Chinatown, and cable cars are among its familiar features. What city is it?
In San Francisco, this suspension span opened in 1937 and carries U.S. Route 101 across the strait between the city and Marin County. What structure is it?

San Francisco’s bay contains this small island, which served as a federal penitentiary from 1934 to 1963 and held inmates including Al Capone. Native American activists occupied it beginning in 1969. Name the island.

On San Francisco’s Embarcadero, this landmark opened in 1898 as the city’s main passenger terminal for boats crossing the bay. Recognizable by its clock tower, it now houses a food marketplace. What is it?

In San Francisco, this neighborhood takes its name from an 18th-century Spanish religious outpost founded in 1776. It is known for murals along Balmy Alley and for Dolores Park. Name the neighborhood.

This sacred island in the Cyclades was regarded in Greek mythology as the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. It also housed the treasury of an alliance of Greek city-states that took its name from the island. What is the island?
After the Persian Wars, this alliance of Greek city-states continued the campaign against Persia under Athenian leadership. Its treasury was initially kept on Delos; what was the alliance called?

This protected area straddles the North Carolina–Tennessee line in the southern Appalachians. Its landscape is famed for a bluish haze created by natural emissions from its vegetation. What is this federally protected site?

Within Great Smoky Mountains National Park, this summit is the highest point in both the park and Tennessee. A paved trail leads to an observation tower near its peak. What is the summit’s current name?

This country occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula and also includes island territories in both the Atlantic and Mediterranean. Its capital is Madrid, and its autonomous communities include Catalonia and the Basque Country; name the country.

In Spain, the country's capital and largest city lies near the center of the Iberian Peninsula along the Manzanares River. It is also the seat of the national government and gives its name to a surrounding autonomous community; what city is it?
Spain's Atlantic archipelago lies off the northwest coast of Africa and includes Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, and La Palma. What is this island group called?
Spain's North African autonomous city on the southern side of the Strait of Gibraltar borders Morocco and lies across the water from Andalusia. What is this Spanish city called?

Spain's northeastern border runs through the Pyrenees with a small landlocked co-principality whose heads of state are the French president and the Bishop of Urgell. Which neighboring country is this?

Which Central European federal republic is organized into 16 constituent states and stretches from the North and Baltic seas in the north to the Alps in the south? It shares land borders with nine countries, including Denmark, Poland, and France.
Germany’s national capital is also its most populous city and one of its 16 constituent states. The city lies on the River Spree and is home to the Reichstag building.
Germany shares part of its eastern boundary with this country, whose capital is Warsaw. The Oder and Lusatian Neisse rivers mark substantial stretches of their border.

Germany has coastlines on two northern seas; its northeastern shore, including the coast near the island of Rügen, meets which sea? Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland also have coastlines along this body of water.
Germany’s highest point is a peak in the Wetterstein Mountains near the Austrian border. A cog railway from Garmisch-Partenkirchen provides access to this summit.

This Pacific Northwest state became the 33rd state in the Union on February 14, 1859. Its northern boundary follows the Columbia River in part, and its Willamette Valley drew many nineteenth-century migrants traveling west by wagon. What state is it?
In Oregon, this stratovolcano is the state’s highest point and rises southeast of Portland. Timberline Lodge, on its slopes, was used as a filming location for *The Shining*. What mountain is it?
In southern Oregon, federally protected land surrounds a deep blue lake filling the caldera left by Mount Mazama; Wizard Island rises from the water. What is this place’s full name?
Along South Africa’s eastern edge, this mountain range forms the highest section of the Great Escarpment and includes the dramatic basalt highlands bordering Lesotho. What is this range called?
The Drakensberg’s highest summit rises to about 3,482 metres in Lesotho and is also the highest point in southern Africa. What is this summit called?
This semiarid sandy savanna covers roughly 900,000 square kilometers across Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa. What major landform of southern Africa is it?

In 2002, thousands of San people were evicted from land in the Kalahari Desert that was valuable for mining these exceptionally hard gemstones, often used in rings. What gemstones were at the center of the dispute?
In the Kalahari Desert, what vast Botswana wetland forms when a river flowing north from Angola spreads across the interior and disappears into the sands without reaching the sea?

A landlocked Central European country lies in the Eastern Alps and was the heartland of the Habsburg monarchy. Its capital is also one of its nine federal states, and in 1867 it formed a dual monarchy with Hungary. Name this country.

Austria’s national capital is also a federal state in its own right. Which city on the Danube served as the Habsburgs’ seat and became the Holy Roman Empire’s administrative capital in the 16th century?

After a decade of Allied occupation following World War II, Austria regained full sovereignty in 1955 through an agreement signed by the occupying powers and the government in Vienna. What is the agreement commonly called?
Of Austria’s eight neighboring countries, which small Alpine principality borders both Austria and Switzerland and has Vaduz as its capital?

Most of Austria’s mountainous territory lies within the eastern division of a major European mountain system, whose ridges continue into nearby Italy, Switzerland, and Slovenia. What is the name of this regional division?

Between Great Britain to the west and Norway, Denmark, Germany, and the Low Countries to the east, this sea forms part of the northeastern Atlantic. The Statfjord field lies beneath it, and its southern end connects to the English Channel; what sea is being described?

In the Norwegian sector of the North Sea, this giant offshore oil development began production in 1979. Its infrastructure includes three major concrete platforms designated A, B, and C; what is its name?
This mainland Southeast Asian country shares land borders with Thailand, Laos, and Vietnam. Its southern coast opens onto the Gulf of Thailand, and its capital is Phnom Penh. What country is it?
Cambodia’s capital and largest city lies at the meeting point of the Mekong, Tonlé Sap, and Bassac rivers. What is this city called?
Cambodia contains Southeast Asia’s largest lake, whose size expands greatly during the monsoon season as its water flow reverses. What is the lake’s name?
Cambodia’s southwestern coastline opens onto this shallow arm of the South China Sea, which lies between the Indochinese Peninsula and the Malay Peninsula. What body of water is it?

What are the tall structures fitted with lights that guide ships toward harbor entrances and warn them away from dangerous coastlines? They are often painted in contrasting stripes so they stand out to passing vessels.
In the broader topic of lighthouses, identify the historic tower in Maryland County, Liberia, that guided vessels into the port of Harper.

Located in Lower Galilee, just north of the Jezreel Valley, this city is traditionally identified in Christian accounts as the place where Jesus grew up. It is also home to the Basilica of the Annunciation, a major pilgrimage site associated with the angel Gabriel’s visit to Mary. What is the city’s name?

In Nazareth, this Roman Catholic church stands above a grotto traditionally identified as the place where Gabriel announced to Mary that she would bear Jesus. The present monumental structure was consecrated in 1969; what is the church called?

What is the name of the heavily forested coastal plain region in the southern part of the state whose capital is Trenton, known for acidic, nutrient-poor soils and extensive wetlands? It is also closely associated with a famous winged creature of local folklore.
Within the New Jersey Pine Barrens, local folklore centers on a winged, hoofed creature whose origin story places its birth to Deborah Leeds in 1735 at Leeds Point. What is this creature called?

This major waterway rises in the Adirondacks, flows south through eastern New York, and empties into New York Harbor. It was an important steamboat route between New York City and Albany. What river is it?
In 1807, a commercial steamboat made a landmark voyage from New York City to Albany on the Hudson River. Which American engineer and entrepreneur developed and promoted the vessel?

This landlocked country in East Africa borders five countries and has a long northern shoreline on Lake Victoria. Its capital is Kampala, and its Entebbe airport became famous as the site of a 1976 hostage-rescue raid. What country is it?
In Uganda, what aviation facility on the northern shore of Lake Victoria was the destination of Air France Flight 139 after its hijacking and the site of the 1976 hostage-rescue raid?

Which western Canadian province has Edmonton as its capital and includes Calgary and Red Deer among its major cities? An aggressive control program has kept it free of established rat populations since the 1950s.

Which city in Alberta is the provincial capital and sits on the North Saskatchewan River, north of Red Deer along the main urban corridor toward Calgary? It is also home to a major shopping and entertainment complex known for its indoor lake and water park.

This large, persistent body of land ice flows under its own weight after snow accumulation exceeds melting and other losses over many years. Unlike sea ice, it originates on land and can carve valleys as it moves. What is it?

A glacier can carve a deep, steep-sided U-shaped valley, and after the ice retreats, seawater may flood it. Norway's coastline is especially famous for these long, narrow inlets; what are they called?
At the head of an alpine glacier, ice erosion can excavate a steep-walled, bowl-shaped hollow; after retreat, that hollow may hold a small lake called a tarn. What is this glacial landform called?
What geographic term describes a natural inland body of standing water, typically occupying a basin and bounded by land? Unlike a river, it does not generally flow from end to end.
A small lake occupying a bowl-shaped hollow high in the mountains is often associated with glacial erosion. What specific term is used for a lake resting in a cirque?

This Indonesian metropolis is the country’s capital and largest city, occupying the northwestern coast of Java. Its low-lying terrain, land subsidence, and rising sea levels put it at risk of severe flooding.

Jakarta sits along the northern shore of this sea, which lies between the island that contains Indonesia’s capital and Borneo and connects westward to the South China Sea. What is this body of water called?

Across a dry plateau in southern Peru, ancient makers removed dark surface stones to expose lighter ground, forming enormous figures such as a hummingbird, spider, and monkey that are best seen from above. What is the name of this famous geoglyph complex?
Which German-born mathematician and archaeologist spent decades studying and helping preserve the Nazca Lines, earning the nickname “Lady of the Lines”?

Earth’s southernmost and fifth-largest continent lies almost entirely south of the Antarctic Circle and contains the geographic South Pole. Its land is mostly buried beneath an ice sheet that holds about 70 percent of the world’s freshwater. What continent is described?
On Antarctica, this Norwegian explorer led the first expedition to reach the geographic South Pole, arriving on December 14, 1911, ahead of Robert Falcon Scott’s party. Who was he?

A system for governing Antarctica grew from an international agreement signed in Washington in 1959 and put into force in 1961. It reserves the continent for peaceful purposes and bars military activity, mining, nuclear explosions, and nuclear-waste disposal; what is this system called?

Beneath Antarctica’s East Antarctic ice sheet, this vast subglacial lake lies under nearly four kilometers of ice near the continent’s Pole of Cold. It is named for a Russian research station situated above it; what is the lake called?
This Pacific Coast state was ceded by Mexico to the United States in 1848 and entered the Union two years later as its 31st state. Which state became a free state upon admission?
California’s capital was a major supply center during the 1849 Gold Rush, and its downtown stands near the confluence of the American River and the state’s largest river by discharge. Name this city.

California’s broad agricultural interior runs between the Coast Ranges and the Sierra Nevada, across lowlands drained by the Sacramento and San Joaquin rivers. Extensive irrigation supports huge production of fruits, nuts, and dairy; what is this region called?
This protected area in California’s southern Sierra Nevada contains General Sherman, the world’s largest tree by volume, and lies just south of Kings Canyon. Name it.
This protected desert area in California’s Mojave Desert includes Badwater Basin, the lowest point in North America, as well as extensive salt flats. What is it called?

This major river of northeastern Africa is formed by the meeting of two major headstreams at Khartoum. It flows north through Sudan and Egypt before emptying into the Mediterranean Sea. What river is it?
The Blue and White branches of the Nile River meet in Sudan at a city that is also the country’s capital. What is this city?
The Blue Nile, one of the great headstreams of the Nile River, begins at this Ethiopian lake and flows out over Tis Abbay Falls. What is the lake?
Completed in 1970 under Gamal Abdel Nasser, this dam on the Nile River created Lake Nasser and led to the relocation of the Abu Simbel temples. What is the dam’s name?
Near the Mediterranean end of the Nile River, this broad alluvial region is divided by distributaries including the Rosetta and Damietta branches. What is this region called?

Which city in Provence, southern France, lies along the Rhône and preserves a Roman amphitheatre and theatre alongside medieval monuments? Its Roman and Romanesque heritage was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1981.

In Arles, which Romanesque church is known for its sculpted west portal and a cloister whose galleries show a transition from Romanesque to Gothic styles? The church and cloister are among the city’s UNESCO-listed monuments.

This ancient chain of ridges runs southwest to northeast across eastern North America, extending from central Alabama to Newfoundland. Its alternating highlands and valleys have long shaped east–west travel across the region. What is this range called?
Within the Appalachian Mountains, this summit in North Carolina’s Black Mountains reaches 6,684 feet, making it the highest peak in the entire range. What is the summit’s name?
This roughly 2,175-mile hiking route crosses the Appalachian Mountains, linking Springer Mountain in Georgia with Mount Katahdin in Maine. What is the route called?

These depressions commonly form in karst regions when groundwater dissolves soluble bedrock such as limestone or when the ground above an underground cavity collapses. What are these landforms called?

Like sinkholes, these underground spaces are common in karst landscapes, where groundwater can dissolve limestone or dolomite to create passages. Stalactites and stalagmites may form inside them, and spelunkers explore them. What are they called?

This long, narrow tropical sea lies between northeastern Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. At its northern end, the Sinai Peninsula divides it into the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba; at its southern end, it connects to the Gulf of Aden. What is this sea called?
At the southern entrance to the Red Sea, this narrow passage separates Yemen from Djibouti and Eritrea and leads into the Gulf of Aden. What is the name of this strategic strait?

This constituent country of the United Kingdom occupies the northern part of Great Britain and shares a land border with England to the south. Its mainland includes the Highlands, Lowlands, and Southern Uplands, and its Scottish Gaelic name is Alba.

Scotland’s capital stands on the Firth of Forth and is home to the Scottish Parliament building designed by Enric Miralles. Its historic Old Town and Georgian New Town together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Scotland’s largest and most populous city grew along the River Clyde and is home to Celtic and Rangers, whose rivalry is known as the Old Firm derby. Which city is it?
In Scotland’s Highlands, this mountain rises to 1,345 metres, making it the highest peak in the British Isles. It stands near Fort William, at the western end of the Great Glen.

This island group lies off the western coast of Scotland and is divided into Inner and Outer sections. The Isle of Skye belongs to the former, while Lewis and Harris are among the largest islands in the latter.
The mainland of this Nordic country occupies the northern part of the Jutland Peninsula, and its capital lies across the Øresund from Malmö. What country is the southernmost of Scandinavia?
In metropolitan Denmark, which island is the largest and most populous? It is separated from Funen by the Great Belt and is the island where Copenhagen is principally located.
Denmark has only one land border, a short boundary at the base of Jutland. Which country lies immediately south of it?
Denmark's capital and largest city spans Zealand, Amager, and the small islet of Slotsholmen, and sits across the Øresund from Malmö. What city is it?

This mainland Southeast Asian country borders Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, and Malaysia, and its territory reaches the Andaman Sea to the west and a gulf to the east. Formerly known as Siam, it adopted its current name in 1939. What is the country?
Thailand’s southern peninsula has one coast facing the Gulf of Thailand and another facing a sea that also borders Myanmar and the Nicobar Islands. Which sea lies along Thailand’s western shore?

This marginal sea of the western Pacific lies east of Vietnam and west of the Philippines. Its disputed waters include an archipelago at the center of overlapping maritime claims and the area marked by the nine-dash line. What is this sea called?

In the South China Sea, this archipelago of more than 100 islands, reefs, and shoals is claimed in whole or in part by several countries, including China, the Philippines, and Vietnam. What is the archipelago called?

This major Ukrainian port city in Donetsk Oblast lies on the northern coast of the Sea of Azov and is one of Ukraine’s key seaports. Its devastating siege during the 2022 Russian invasion made it a symbol of the war’s destruction; name the city.
Mariupol lies on the northern shore of this inland sea, which connects to the Black Sea through the Kerch Strait. What sea is it?
Rebuilt with planned Pombaline streets after the devastating earthquake of 1755, this city stands on the Tagus near the Atlantic coast. It is Portugal’s capital and largest city. What city is it?
Lisbon lies beside the estuary of this river, which flows west across the Iberian Peninsula to the Atlantic. What river is it?
Which city in southwestern Tennessee sits on a bluff overlooking the Mississippi River and is famed for Beale Street and its blues heritage?
In Memphis, Ida B. Wells used this newspaper to report on racial violence and challenge lynching. What was the paper’s title?

This 8,611-meter peak in the Karakoram is the world’s second-highest mountain, surpassed only by Mount Everest. Its steep, dangerous climbing routes have earned it the nickname “Savage Mountain”; what is its commonly used name?

K2 lies on an international border in the Karakoram, with its southern side in the region of Gilgit-Baltistan. Which country, whose capital is Islamabad and whose national language is Urdu, shares that border?

Which coal-rich historical region of eastern Ukraine lies principally across the oblasts named for the cities of Donetsk and Luhansk? Its name is also commonly spelled with a double final “s” in English.
Within the Donbas, which eastern Ukrainian oblast was officially called Voroshilovgrad Oblast from 1970 until 1990? It had also borne that name earlier in the Soviet period.
Which archipelagic country in Southeast Asia lies between the Indian and Pacific oceans and includes Java, Sumatra, and part of Borneo?
More than half of Indonesia’s population lives on this island, which is also home to the city of Jakarta. The Sunda Strait separates it from Sumatra.
Indonesia shares this large island with Malaysia and Brunei; its Indonesian portion is known as Kalimantan. What is the island’s name?
Indonesia’s largest city sits on the northwest coast of Java and is known for severe land subsidence, linked in part to groundwater extraction. What is the city’s name?
This island is the second-largest in the Greater Antilles after Cuba. Haiti occupies its western portion, while the Dominican Republic occupies its eastern portion; what is the island’s name?
The eastern end of Hispaniola is separated from Puerto Rico by this narrow waterway, which connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Caribbean Sea. What is it called?

On South Africa’s southern peninsula, this prominent headland is historically associated with the maritime route between the Atlantic and Indian oceans. Its discoverer first gave it an ominous name that Portugal’s King John II later replaced with a more hopeful one. What landmark is it?

Which Portuguese navigator rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488 on the return leg of an expedition, initially naming it the Cape of Storms? His voyage reached southern Africa but turned back before a later Portuguese expedition completed the sea route to India.
Which island in San Francisco Bay became known as the site of a former federal penitentiary and a 19-month occupation by Native activists that began in 1969?
During the 1969–1971 occupation of Alcatraz Island, what activist group claimed the island under the Treaty of Fort Laramie and proposed building a Native American cultural center there?
This ocean is the third-largest by area, with East Africa along its western side, southern Asia along its northern rim, and Australia to the east. Tanzania’s coastline lies on it. What is it?

Along the northeastern edge of the Indian Ocean, this broad inlet is bordered by India and Bangladesh to the west and north, and Myanmar to the east. The Ganges and Brahmaputra river systems empty into it. What is this body of water?
This city is both the capital and largest urban center of South Korea, and its metropolitan area includes the well-known Gangnam district. Which city is it?
Seoul is built along a river formed by the confluence of the Bukhan and Namhan rivers; the waterway then runs westward to the Yellow Sea. What is this river called?

Congress set aside Yellowstone in 1872 as the first federally protected area of its kind, and places in this group preserve landscapes, wildlife, and cultural resources for public enjoyment. What are these protected places in the United States commonly called?

Among U.S. national parks, this vast area spans Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho and is famous for geysers such as Old Faithful. Congress established it in 1872 as the first national park in the country. What is it?
Which city in South Holland lies between The Hague and Rotterdam and gave its name to a blue-and-white tin-glazed pottery tradition? It is associated with both Johannes Vermeer and Carel Fabritius.
Which Dutch Golden Age painter was born in Delft in 1632 and spent most of his career there? He created *Girl with a Pearl Earring* and the cityscape *View of Delft*.

Extending up to 200 nautical miles from a coastal state’s baselines, this maritime area gives that state special rights to explore, exploit, conserve, and manage natural resources in the waters and seabed. What is this area called?
The Exclusive Economic Zone is one of the maritime zones governed by this treaty, adopted in 1982 in Montego Bay and brought into force in 1994. What is the treaty’s name?
answer: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea

question: This branching tidal inlet in northwestern Washington borders the Seattle–Tacoma area and helps define the eastern edge of the Olympic Peninsula. Its waters connect with the Pacific Ocean through a passage at the state’s northwestern edge. What is this inlet called?

Puget Sound borders the eastern side of this large landform in northwestern Washington. Its mountainous interior includes a national park and extends westward toward the Pacific coast. What is this landform called?
This rugged subrange of the southern Appalachians straddles Tennessee and North Carolina and contains a national park known for its misty ridgelines. What is the range commonly called?
Within the Great Smoky Mountains, this 6,643-foot summit is the highest point in Tennessee. A circular observation tower stands at its top, and its current name comes from Cherokee.

Traditionally traced to a lake in northern Minnesota, this river flows roughly 2,340 miles south through the central United States before reaching the Gulf of Mexico near New Orleans. What is this second-longest river in the United States?

The Mississippi River is traditionally traced to this small lake in northern Minnesota, whose outlet marks the river’s beginning. The lake lies in a state park near the town of Park Rapids. What is it called?
The Mississippi River meets this major tributary near St. Louis. This river’s headwaters are in the Rocky Mountains near Three Forks, Montana. What river is it?

In 1863, Union forces led by Ulysses S. Grant captured a heavily fortified city on the Mississippi River after a siege that lasted more than six weeks. This victory, together with the fall of Port Hudson, gave the Union control of the river; what Civil War operation was it?

The Mississippi River inspired the settings of several works by this American author, including Adventures of Huckleberry Finn. His pen name came from a riverboat call indicating water two fathoms deep. What name did he write under?

This ancient Mesopotamian city stood on the Euphrates and flourished under rulers including Hammurabi and Nebuchadnezzar II. It is also associated with a monumental blue-brick gate and the legendary Hanging Gardens. What city is it?
In Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar II commissioned a monumental blue-glazed-brick entrance decorated with bulls and dragons and dedicated to a goddess of love and war. What was this structure called?

Off the southern coast of Cape Cod, this island in Dukes County is reached by ferry from Woods Hole and includes the towns of Edgartown and Oak Bluffs. It is a popular summer resort and a vacation destination for U.S. presidents. What island is it?
Martha's Vineyard lies off the southern coast of this U.S. state, whose capital is Boston and whose southeastern coastline includes Cape Cod. Which state is it?

In the traditional division of the Pacific, this is the largest of the three major island regions and is often described as a vast triangle with Hawaiʻi, New Zealand, and Rapa Nui near its corners. What is this region called?
At the eastern edge of the roughly triangular region of Polynesia lies an island under Chilean control, famed for monumental stone figures called moai. What is the island commonly called in English?

This flourishing Roman commercial town in Campania stood near the Gulf of Naples and was buried when Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE. Its streets, houses, and public buildings were later uncovered through excavations that began in the mid-18th century. What city was it?
Pompeii occupied raised ground formed by ancient lava flows near the mouth of this river, which reaches the Gulf of Naples. What river was it?

This major watershed boundary follows the Rocky Mountains through western Canada and the United States and continues along the Andes farther south. It separates runoff ultimately reaching the Pacific from runoff ultimately reaching the Atlantic; what is it called?

At a Montana summit in Glacier National Park, the Continental Divide of the Americas intersects the Northern Divide, so precipitation can drain toward the Pacific, Atlantic, or Arctic. What is this summit called?

On Tasmania’s Tasman Peninsula, this former British penal settlement housed convicts in a major nineteenth-century prison complex. Its preserved ruins are now part of the Australian Convict Sites World Heritage property. What is the site called?
The 1996 mass shooting at Port Arthur killed 35 people and became one of the deadliest attacks in modern Australian history. Which gunman carried out the attack?

Founded by French colonists in 1718, this Louisiana port city stands along the Mississippi River near the Gulf of Mexico. What city is renowned for its historic quarter, distinctive cuisine, and jazz heritage?
This major North American river flows past New Orleans and runs south from Minnesota to its delta at the Gulf of Mexico. What river has long made the city an important port?

Within New Orleans, this historic district includes Jackson Square and the Cathedral-Basilica of Saint Louis, and its architecture reflects Spanish and Creole influences. What district is also known for Bourbon Street nightlife?
In August 2005, this powerful storm caused catastrophic flooding in New Orleans after levee failures, displacing thousands of residents. What storm devastated the city?

Which landlocked country in the African Great Lakes region has Kigali as its capital and borders Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo? It was the site of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.
Along Rwanda’s western border, this deep freshwater lake is shared with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Its methane-rich waters are also used for energy production.

What broad transportation term describes constructed routes used by motor vehicles, ranging from local streets to numbered interstate routes? These routes may be maintained by transportation departments and can include toll facilities.

Among roads in the United States, what toll route crosses the Allegheny Mountains and opened in 1940 as an early long-distance, limited-access highway that helped inspire the design of the Interstate system?

This influential ancient Greek polis stood on the narrow land bridge joining the Peloponnese to mainland Greece and controlled an important overland route between them. Traditionally founded by Sisyphus, it hosted an athletic festival held at the isthmus; which city was it?
At Corinth, a Panhellenic athletic festival was held at a sanctuary on the isthmus in honor of Poseidon. What was this festival called?

Each sovereign country uses one of these symbols as an emblem. Familiar examples include the United States’ Stars and Stripes, France’s blue-white-red tricolor, and Japan’s red sun on a white field. What are these symbols called?
Among national flags, which country’s design shows an AK-47 crossed with a hoe above an open book, all beside a red triangle?

Known as the “Garden of England,” this county occupies England’s southeastern corner, with a northern coastline along the Thames Estuary and a southern shore on the English Channel. What county is it?
In Kent, which port town faces Calais across the narrowest part of the English Channel? It is also known for its white chalk cliffs and a castle overlooking the harbor.
Rising in the Swiss Alps, this river flows through Lake Geneva and southeastern France, passing Lyon and Avignon before reaching the Mediterranean near the Camargue. What major European river is it?
The Rhône River forms a delta in this protected wetland region of southern France, known for its lagoons, salt flats, and flamingos. What is this region called?
Often described as the longest river in the United States, this major Great Plains waterway begins in the Rocky Mountains and flows eastward to meet the Mississippi near St. Louis. What river is it?

The Missouri River is impounded in western North Dakota by Garrison Dam, creating a large reservoir named for the Shoshone woman who served as an interpreter on the Lewis and Clark expedition. What is the reservoir called?

This landlocked Mountain West state includes much of the Southern Rocky Mountains and the western edge of the Great Plains. It became the 38th U.S. state in 1876, fifteen years after becoming a territory. Name it.
Colorado shares a region with Arizona, New Mexico, and Utah where their state boundaries converge. What is that region called?
In Colorado, which city is both the state capital and its largest city? It is also known as the Mile High City because its elevation is about one mile above sea level.
This Michigan city is the state’s largest and a major port on the Great Lakes. It stands on the river that connects Lake St. Clair with Lake Erie; what is the city’s name?
The Ambassador Bridge connects Detroit with Windsor across the Detroit River. Which Canadian province, whose capital is Ottawa and whose largest city is Toronto, lies on the other side of the bridge?
Chile’s capital and largest city lies in the Central Valley, between the Andes and the Coastal Range. Founded by Pedro de Valdivia in 1541, what city is the country’s political and economic center?
In Santiago, what hill is a major urban park and lookout, with a summit sanctuary crowned by a statue of the Immaculate Conception? Visitors can reach its summit by funicular or cable car.
This island city is the seat of the United Arab Emirates’ federal government and the capital of its namesake emirate. It is also the base of the country’s airline Etihad Airways; what is the city?
Abu Dhabi is home to a vast white-marble Islamic place of worship distinguished by 82 domes, four minarets, and a hand-knotted carpet in its main prayer hall. What is this landmark called?
Stretching from Asia and Australia in the west to the Americas in the east, this is the largest ocean on Earth. It also contains the islands of Polynesia. What ocean is it?
The Pacific Ocean contains this major island region, whose name means “many islands.” Samoa, Tonga, and the Society Islands are among its island groups. What region is it?

This West African country on the Gulf of Guinea moved its national capital from its largest city to an inland planned city in 1991. Abuja is its capital today, while Lagos remains its largest city; what country is described?
Nigeria’s northern neighbor is a landlocked Sahelian republic whose territory reaches deep into the Sahara. Its capital is Niamey; name this country.
Nigeria’s eastern neighbor stretches from the Sahel to the Gulf of Guinea. Its capital is Yaoundé, and both French and English are official languages; what country is it?
Nigeria’s western neighbor is a narrow, north–south republic on the Gulf of Guinea. Porto-Novo is its official capital, while Cotonou is its largest city and seat of government; name the country.
Nigeria’s northeastern land border meets a landlocked Sahelian country. Its capital, N’Djamena, lies near the confluence of the Chari and Logone rivers; what country is it?
Rising in the Angolan highlands, this southern African river flows southeast through Namibia before terminating in an inland delta in Botswana instead of reaching the sea. What is the river’s name?

The Okavango River flows into this landlocked southern African country, where its waters spread into an inland delta rather than reaching the ocean. Its capital is Gaborone, and it borders Namibia, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and South Africa. What is this country?

This Pacific Northwest state borders British Columbia to the north, Idaho to the east, Oregon to the south, and the Pacific Ocean to the west. Its most populous city is Seattle, while its capital is Olympia. What state is it?
Within Washington State, what glacier-carved inlet is bordered by Seattle and Tacoma and connects to the Pacific Ocean through the Strait of Juan de Fuca?
What active stratovolcano in Washington State is its highest point, rising about 14,410 feet above sea level? It is also the namesake centerpiece of a national park southeast of Seattle.
Florida’s most populous city lies in the state’s northeast, with the St. Johns River running through its urban core in Duval County. It is also the eastern terminus of Interstate 10. What city is it?
Which river flows through downtown Jacksonville and runs northward across northeast Florida before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean near Mayport?

This long desert trough in eastern California includes North America’s lowest point, where the salt-crusted Badwater Basin lies about 282 feet below sea level. It is also known for extreme summer heat and gives its name to a national park. What is this place?
Within Death Valley, a broad salt flat marks the lowest elevation in North America, roughly 282 feet below sea level. What is this salt flat called?
In a cave, water dripping from the ceiling can leave behind mineral deposits that gradually grow downward. What are these formations called?
Stalactites form as dripping water leaves minerals on cave ceilings. The most common mineral in these deposits is a crystalline form of calcium carbonate also found in limestone; what is it called?

Founded in 1854 by antislavery settlers organized by the New England Emigrant Aid Company, this town became a major Free-State stronghold during the territorial slavery conflict. Pro-slavery forces sacked it in 1856, and William Quantrill’s guerrillas raided it in 1863. What city is it?

On May 21, 1856, a pro-slavery posse led by Sheriff Samuel J. Jones entered Lawrence, Kansas, destroyed the presses of two antislavery newspapers, and burned the Free State Hotel. What is this attack commonly called?

This island in the Seine lies at the historic heart of Paris and is connected to both riverbanks by several bridges. Its landmarks include a Gothic cathedral and the royal chapel commissioned by Louis IX, now famous for its stained-glass windows.

On the Île de la Cité, this Gothic cathedral is distinguished by its twin square towers, flying buttresses, and large rose windows. Its spire was destroyed in a 2019 fire, and the cathedral reopened after restoration in 2024.

This federal republic has 50 states, including a noncontiguous state in the northwest and an island state in the Pacific; its capital is a federal district rather than a state. Its contiguous states lie between Canada and Mexico. What country is described?
The United States of America shares its longest international land boundary with which country, whose territory lies immediately north of the contiguous states and also borders Alaska?

In the geography of the United States of America, which state is separated from the contiguous states by Canadian territory and shares land boundaries with Yukon and British Columbia? It is also separated from Russia by the Bering Strait.
On the United States of America–Canada border, which Great Lake is largest by surface area and sends its outflow through the St. Marys River toward Lake Huron?
Which river forms part of the boundary between the United States of America and Ontario after leaving Lake Ontario, then flows northeast toward the Atlantic?

In China's Xinjiang region, this vast sandy expanse fills much of a lowland bordered by the Tian Shan to the north and the Kunlun Mountains to the south. Historic Silk Road routes skirted its margins through oasis towns such as Kashgar. What is this landform called?

The Taklamakan Desert occupies much of this immense inland depression in Xinjiang, lying between the Tian Shan and Kunlun mountain systems. Rivers in the depression drain inward rather than reaching the ocean. What is this lowland called?

Roman writers applied this name to the lands beyond the Rhine and Danube, where numerous Germanic peoples lived outside the empire’s direct rule. In a first-century ethnographic account, Tacitus described groups including the Ingaevones; what region was he describing?

In 9 CE, three Roman legions led by Publius Quinctilius Varus were destroyed in Germania after the Cheruscan leader Arminius turned against Rome. Augustus was said to have mourned the loss of those legions; what battle was this?

This kingdom occupies most of the Arabian Peninsula and has coastlines along a sea to its west and a gulf to its east. Its capital is Riyadh, and its modern state was proclaimed in 1932 by Abdulaziz ibn Saud. What country is it?

Saudi Arabia’s western coast stretches along this body of water, which separates the Arabian Peninsula from northeast Africa. The Suez Canal at its northern end connects it to the Mediterranean Sea. What is it?

Saudi Arabia’s southern land border runs along this country, whose capital is Sana’a. This neighbor occupies the southwestern corner of the Arabian Peninsula and also has a coastline on the Red Sea. What country is it?

Saudi Arabia meets this country at its southeastern border, and the two share terrain near the Rub’ al Khali. Its capital is Muscat, and it also controls the Musandam Peninsula near the Strait of Hormuz. What country is it?

Which city is Ireland’s capital and largest city, on the island’s east coast where the River Liffey reaches the sea? Its position beside the river mouth and a sheltered bay helped make it an important harbor and crossing point.
Dublin’s English name is traced to an older name for a pool on the River Liffey. In this place-name, the element dubh may mean “deep” rather than “black”; what is the older name?
Which city near the southern end of the Front Range is home to Garden of the Gods, where sandstone formations include the Kissing Camels, and hosts a major U.S. Olympic training facility?

This mountain west of Colorado Springs is the highest summit in the southern Front Range and lent its name to a Gold Rush-era prospecting slogan, although little gold was found near its slopes. What is it called?

In this lagoon city, artificial waterways form a historic transport network used by gondolas and other boats. The best-known waterway in the network cuts through the urban center. What is the network called?

Within the Canals of Venice, one major waterway curves in an S-shape through the historic center and is crossed by the Rialto Bridge. It divides the city into two principal sides; what is this waterway called?
This is Colorado’s capital and largest city, located in the South Platte River valley just east of the Front Range. Its official elevation is exactly one mile above sea level. What city is it?
Denver is the capital and most populous city of this state, admitted to the Union in 1876 and nicknamed the Centennial State. Which state is it?
Denver was founded during the 1858 Gold Rush at the confluence of Cherry Creek and this river. From Denver, it flows northeast across Colorado toward Nebraska. Name the river.

This historic Chinese artificial waterway system links the Yellow River and Yangtze River basins, with its present main route running between the northern capital and Hangzhou. What is this major north–south transportation network?
The Grand Canal’s present Jing–Hang route begins in this city, which is also China’s capital and home to Tiananmen Square and the Forbidden City. What city is it?
The Grand Canal links the basin of this northern Chinese river, known for its sediment-rich waters, with that of the Yangtze. The river flows into the Bohai Sea. What river is it?
In the 10th century, this Song official and engineer invented the pound lock, enabling canal boats to negotiate changes in elevation on routes including the Grand Canal. Who was he?

Launched as part of Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, this planned development in the kingdom’s northwest includes the proposed linear city The Line and the mountain resort Trojena. What is the name of this development?
Within NEOM, what is the planned high-altitude tourism destination designed to offer mountain recreation, including skiing?
Which Windward Island in the eastern Caribbean is the main island of the independent country that also includes the Grenadines? It is historically associated with the Garifuna language.
On Saint Vincent, what active stratovolcano at the island’s northern end erupted explosively in 1902 and again in 2020–21, prompting evacuations?
This Caribbean island country is the third-largest island in the Greater Antilles, lying south of Cuba and west of Hispaniola. Its capital and largest city is Kingston. Which country is it?
Jamaica is part of this northern Caribbean island group, which also includes Cuba, Hispaniola, and Puerto Rico. What is the name of the group?

Jamaica’s capital and largest city sits on the island’s southeastern coast beside a large natural harbor. It became the island’s main port after an earthquake devastated nearby Port Royal in 1692. What city is it?

Jamaica lies south of Cuba and west of this island, the second-largest in the Greater Antilles. Haiti and the Dominican Republic occupy its western and eastern portions, respectively. What is the island called?
Jamaica is located south of this island, the largest in the Caribbean. Havana is its capital, and the island lies just south of Florida. What island is it?
Completed in 1931, this 102-story Art Deco skyscraper held the title of the world’s tallest building until 1970. What building is it?
The Empire State Building stands in the New York City borough that includes Times Square and Central Park and is bordered by the Hudson and East rivers. What borough is it?

This island is the largest and most populous in the Mediterranean and one of Italy’s five autonomous regions. It lies south of the Italian Peninsula, separated from Calabria by a narrow strait. What is it?
On Sicily’s eastern side, this stratovolcano rises above the surrounding landscape and is the tallest active volcano in Europe. Name it.
Sicily is separated from Calabria by this narrow waterway, whose namesake city lies at the island’s northeastern tip. What is the waterway?
Sicily’s capital and largest city sits on its northwestern coast. Its Norman-era palace chapel and cathedral are celebrated examples of the island’s Arab-Norman heritage. Name the city.
Off Sicily’s northern coast, this volcanic archipelago includes Lipari and Stromboli; the latter gave its name to a type of intermittent volcanic eruption. Name the island group.

What ancient Egyptian waterway linked the Nile to the Red Sea through the Wadi Tumilat and is regarded as a predecessor of the Suez Canal? Inscriptions describe its reopening during the Achaemenid period.
The Canal of the Pharaohs was restored during the Achaemenid period. Which Persian king is named in an inscription describing a water route from the Nile to the Red Sea?

What is the name for a long, narrow coastal inlet with steep sides, formed when a glacier-carved valley is flooded by the sea? These features are especially common in Norway and other parts of Scandinavia, and their name comes from Old Norse.

The steep-sided walls of fjords were carved by what massive moving bodies of ice? These bodies can form alternating light and dark ogives, lose mass through ablation, and shed icebergs through calving.

This southeastern European country has a Black Sea coastline and borders Ukraine, Moldova, Bulgaria, Serbia, and Hungary. Its capital is Bucharest, and its historic regions include Transylvania, Moldavia, and Wallachia. What country is it?
In Romania, what large wetland region occupies the northeastern Black Sea coast, where the country's major river divides into a maze of channels and lagoons before reaching the sea?

This Central African river drains the continent’s largest river basin and carries more water than any other African river. It flows westward to the Atlantic Ocean and is the continent’s second-longest river. What is it?

The Congo River separates this capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of the Congo. The city lies on the river’s south bank and is one of Africa’s largest urban centers. What is it?
Which self-governing North Atlantic archipelago in the Kingdom of Denmark lies north of Scotland, between Iceland and Norway? Its parliament is called the Løgting.
On the island of Streymoy, this settlement is the capital of the Faroe Islands and home to the archipelago’s parliament, the Løgting. What is its name?
This sprawling city is the capital and largest urban center of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It lies across the Congo River from the capital of the Republic of the Congo.
Kinshasa faces this national capital across the Congo River. It is the capital of the Republic of the Congo and lies on the river’s northern bank.
This island lies in the eastern Caribbean and is the smallest of the Greater Antilles. The United States acquired it from Spain in 1898, and its capital is San Juan; what is it?

In Puerto Rico, what mountain range forms the island’s mountainous spine and contains Cerro de Punta, its highest point? These highlands also help make the north generally humid and the south semi-arid.

In August 2017, this Atlantic storm made landfall on the Texas coast and then lingered near the Houston area, bringing torrential rain and catastrophic flooding. Its damage made it one of the costliest tropical cyclones in U.S. history. What storm was it?

Hurricane Harvey caused catastrophic flooding in this Texas city, the state’s largest, after extreme rainfall overwhelmed streets and waterways. Buffalo Bayou runs through its downtown area. What city is it?

Which two neighboring New England states were parties to the Supreme Court dispute over their boundary in the Piscataqua River near Portsmouth Naval Shipyard? The disagreement concerned the river boundary around the island that contains the shipyard.

In the boundary dispute involving Maine and New Hampshire, what island in the Piscataqua River contains Portsmouth Naval Shipyard? The Supreme Court resolved the states’ disagreement over the river boundary around it.

This landlocked Mountain West state includes part of the Great Basin and is known for its varied desert and mountain landscapes. It became the 45th U.S. state in 1896, and its capital and largest city is Salt Lake City. What state is it?

In Utah, this closed-basin lake is the largest remnant of prehistoric Lake Bonneville and lies west of the Wasatch Range. Its mineral-rich waters support brine shrimp, and it has no outlet to the sea. What lake is it?

Utah’s main population corridor follows the western base of a north-south mountain range, extending from Brigham City through Salt Lake City to Provo. Roughly two-thirds of the state’s residents live in this region. What is this corridor called?

This landlocked state in the northern Great Plains is divided by the Missouri River into East River and West River regions, and its capital lies on that river. It borders six states, including Nebraska, Wyoming, and Minnesota. What state is it?

In South Dakota, this major river divides the state into East River and West River regions. It also forms reservoirs such as Lake Oahe and flows eastward to join the Mississippi near St. Louis. What river is it?

In southwestern South Dakota, this pine-covered upland is sacred to the Sioux and contains both Mount Rushmore and the Crazy Horse Memorial. It is an isolated mountain range surrounded by the Great Plains. What is it called?

South Dakota's state government is based in this small city on the Missouri River, near the geographic center of the state. It is one of the least populous state capitals in the country. What city is it?

In South Dakota's Black Hills, this federally protected site is renowned for boxwork, a delicate honeycomb-like mineral formation found in its extensive underground passages. Established in 1903, it was the first U.S. site in the federal system of protected natural areas created specifically to preserve an underground natural system. What is it called?
Which major river of northern China rises in Qinghai, carries a heavy load of eroded soil across the North China Plain, and empties into the Bohai Sea?

The Yellow River receives much of its fine, yellow-brown sediment from this elevated region in north-central China, located in the river’s middle basin and known for thick deposits of windblown soil. What is this named landform?
Located in Ontario near the Quebec border, this city is the seat of Canada's federal government and home to Parliament Hill. Which city is the country's capital?
In 1935, unemployed men from relief camps began a Depression-era protest march whose intended destination was Ottawa, but police stopped the marchers in Regina. What was this protest known as?

This landlocked South American country includes the southeastern shore of Lake Titicaca and is bordered by Brazil, Peru, Chile, Argentina, and Paraguay. Sucre is its constitutional capital, while La Paz is the seat of government.
Bolivia shares its longest international boundary with which country, which lies to its north and east and is the largest country in South America by area?

These natural underground voids may form as groundwater dissolves rock or as erosion opens passages beneath the surface. In suitable conditions, dripping mineral-rich water builds formations on their ceilings and floors. What are these landforms called?

Among the caves of Georgia’s Caucasus Mountains, one in the Arabika Massif became the first known to extend more than 2,000 meters underground. It was once recognized as the world’s deepest known cave. What is its name?

Among the caves of Kentucky, this extensive limestone system is the longest known in the world, with hundreds of miles of passages mapped. It shares its name with the national park that protects it. What is it called?
Many caves form when groundwater slowly dissolves this sedimentary rock, whose main mineral is calcite. Metamorphism of the same rock can produce marble. What is it?

Caves, sinkholes, and disappearing streams commonly occur in this kind of landscape, formed when water dissolves soluble bedrock. Its name comes from a limestone region spanning parts of Slovenia and Italy. What is this terrain called?

This West Asian federal republic has Baghdad as its capital and is bordered by Iran, Turkey, Syria, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the Persian Gulf. Much of its landscape is formed by the fertile plains of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers. What country is it?

This historic region, whose name comes from Greek words meaning “between rivers,” was home to early civilizations including Sumer, Akkad, and Babylonia. Centered on the Tigris-Euphrates plain, it includes much of modern Iraq. What is this region called?
Iraq shares a southern border with this small monarchy at the head of the Persian Gulf. Its occupation by Iraqi forces in August 1990 triggered the First Gulf War. What country is it?
New York State’s largest island holds the New York City boroughs of Brooklyn and Queens and extends east to the resort communities of the Hamptons. What is this island called?
On Long Island, which New York City borough contains both LaGuardia and John F. Kennedy International airports, as well as Flushing Meadows–Corona Park, site of two World’s Fairs?
This remarkably preserved Neolithic settlement on Scotland’s Orkney Islands contains stone-built houses associated with the Grooved Ware culture. What is the settlement called?
Skara Brae stands beside this Orkney bay, where a storm in 1850 exposed the buried settlement beneath the sand. What is the bay called?

After a speech at the Host Breakfast, Squeaky Fromme, a member of the Manson Family, attempted to assassinate President Gerald Ford in this city. Which city, also the state capital, was the site of the incident?
In Sacramento, California, which river flows west from the Sierra Nevada and joins the Sacramento River near Discovery Park? Folsom Dam impounds this river to form Folsom Lake.
Which historic county in northern England is exceptionally large by English county standards, has a major coal-mining heritage, and is now represented by several separate administrative counties?

In Yorkshire, the National Union of Mineworkers opposed the National Coal Board’s proposed pit closures in a national confrontation that began in 1984 and lasted about a year. What is the name commonly given to this British industrial dispute?
What sovereign state in northwestern Europe consists of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, and includes the island of Great Britain and the northeastern part of Ireland?
The United Kingdom shares a land border with this neighboring sovereign state, which occupies most of the island west of Great Britain and has Dublin as its capital. What is the state?
