The United Kingdom is a sovereign state, while this island within the British Isles contains England, Scotland, and Wales but not Northern Ireland. What is the island called?
This sovereign state is Europe’s second-largest country by area and has coastlines on both the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov. Kyiv is its capital.
Ukraine’s capital and largest city stands on the Dnieper River and has served as a major political and cultural center of the region for centuries. What city is it?
Ukraine has a long southern coastline along this sea, which connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosporus and the Sea of Marmara. What sea is it?
Ukraine’s southwestern neighbor is bordered by Romania on its west and has Chișinău as its capital. Name this country.
Ukraine shares a northern border with this country, whose capital is Minsk and whose territory lies between Poland and Russia. What country is it?

This Scandinavian kingdom occupies the western and northern parts of the Scandinavian Peninsula and shares land borders with Sweden, Finland, and Russia. Its extensive coastline faces the North Sea, Norwegian Sea, and Barents Sea; name the country.
In Norway, which capital and largest city lies at the northern end of the Oslofjord and serves as the country’s main political and cultural center?
Norway’s Arctic territory includes this archipelago between mainland Europe and the North Pole. Its largest island is Spitsbergen, and its settlement of Longyearbyen is home to the Global Seed Vault.
This Canadian province is the country’s smallest by area and lies in the Gulf of St. Lawrence. Its capital is Charlottetown. Which province is it?
A 12.9-kilometre fixed link opened in 1997 to carry the Trans-Canada Highway across the Northumberland Strait between Prince Edward Island and New Brunswick. What is this crossing called?
Which Greek mountain reaches 2,918 meters at its summit of Mytikas, making it the country’s highest peak? Ancient tradition also placed the home of the Olympian gods there.
In Greek mythology, which god ruled the divine court on Mount Olympus and was commonly depicted wielding a thunderbolt?

On the Argentina–Brazil border near the meeting point with Paraguay, this immense waterfall system includes hundreds of cascades and a U-shaped chasm known as the Devil’s Throat. What is this waterfall system called?
Iguazu Falls interrupt a river that flows along part of the Argentina–Brazil boundary and empties into the Paraná near the Triple Frontier. What is this river called?

Which southeastern German state has Munich as its capital and was ruled by Ludwig II, who commissioned Neuschwanstein Castle? Its beer traditions are also associated with the Reinheitsgebot and Oktoberfest.
In Bavaria, what city is the state capital and home to BMW’s headquarters? It also hosts the world’s largest Oktoberfest celebration.

This hook-shaped peninsula projects from southeastern Massachusetts into the Atlantic and is separated from the mainland by a man-made ship canal. Provincetown stands near its northern tip, while Nantucket Sound borders much of its southern shore. What is this landform?
At Cape Cod’s northern tip, this town lies near Race Point and is marked by a 252-foot granite tower commemorating the Pilgrims’ 1620 arrival in its harbor. What town is it?

This southeastern European country occupies much of the eastern Adriatic coast and includes the historic coastal region of Dalmatia. Its territory also encompasses more than a thousand islands and islets.
Croatia’s western coastline borders this arm of the Mediterranean Sea, which lies between the Balkan Peninsula and the Italian Peninsula. The city of Venice sits at its northern end.

This East Asian region is bounded by the Yellow Sea to the west and the Sea of Japan to the east, with China and Russia to the north and Japan across a strait to the southeast. What region is shared geographically by North Korea and South Korea?

On the Korean Peninsula, this volcanic peak is the region’s highest mountain and lies on the border between North Korea and China. Its summit caldera contains a lake often called Heaven Lake. What is the peak’s name?
South of the Korean Peninsula, this is the region’s largest island and is known for Hallasan, a shield volcano rising near its center. What island is it?

Along the Korean Peninsula’s northwestern edge, this river forms much of the boundary between North Korea and China before flowing into the Yellow Sea. It is also known by its Korean name, Amnok. What river is it?

On the Korean Peninsula, this buffer strip was established after the 1953 armistice and separates North Korea from South Korea. Despite its name, it is heavily guarded on both sides. What is this area called?

This East Asian island country lies in the Pacific Ocean off the northeastern coast of the Asian mainland. Its archipelago stretches roughly 3,000 kilometers from northeast to southwest, and its rugged, forested terrain concentrates much of its population in coastal lowlands. What country is it?
Japan’s largest island is separated from Hokkaido by the Tsugaru Strait and includes both Tokyo and Mount Fuji. What is this island called?
Japan’s northernmost main island is known for cold, snowy winters, and its largest city is Sapporo. What is this island?
Japan’s largest freshwater lake lies in Shiga Prefecture, northeast of Kyoto. What is the lake’s name?
Mountains in Japan’s Chūgoku and Shikoku regions help shield this body of water from seasonal winds, contributing to its mild climate. What sea lies between Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu?

This major metropolis in northern India encompasses historic Shahjahanabad, the walled Mughal city founded under Shah Jahan, and the planned national-capital district developed under British rule. The Yamuna runs along its eastern side, and it has served as a center of imperial power as well as the seat of India’s national government.

In Delhi’s historic Shahjahanabad, Shah Jahan commissioned this immense walled imperial palace, built from sandstone, to anchor his new Mughal capital. Its design blended Islamic, Persian, Timurid, and Hindu traditions, and the Lahori Gate is a prominent entrance.
Which modern country occupies the northwestern corner of South America and has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean? Its capital, Bogotá, stands high in the Andes.

In Colombia, geographers count this among six natural regions, alongside the Andean, Caribbean, Pacific, Amazonian, and Insular regions. Located in the east, it is characterized by expansive plains and savannas associated with the Orinoco basin; what is it called?

At the mouth of the Persian Gulf, this narrow passage separates Iran from Oman and connects the Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, opening onward to the Arabian Sea. What is this strategically important strait?

The Strait of Hormuz is narrowed on its southern side by an Omani territory that projects north toward Iran and is separated from the rest of Oman by the United Arab Emirates. What is this territory called?

Designed as a countryside-like retreat for residents of a rapidly growing city, this 843-acre Manhattan landscape combines lawns, woodlands, lakes, and roads that let cross-town traffic pass without dominating its open spaces. What is this urban landscape called?
A predominantly African American community stood on land that is now part of Central Park before the park’s construction displaced its residents. What was this community called?

On the southeast coast of the Arabian Gulf, this is the most populous city in the United Arab Emirates and the main urban center of its namesake emirate. Its historic core grew around a natural harbor that divides Deira from the older district on its western side; what city is it?
In Dubai, what natural waterway divides the historic districts of Deira and Bur Dubai? Its harbor helped the city develop as a center for fishing, pearling, and trade.

This sovereign state in Western Europe has metropolitan territory bordering Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Andorra, and Spain. Its coasts reach the Atlantic Ocean, Mediterranean Sea, English Channel, and North Sea. What country is it?
France’s overseas region on the South American mainland lies between Suriname and Brazil and has a coastline on the Atlantic Ocean. What is this region called?
France has a small overseas collectivity in the North Atlantic, just south of Newfoundland and off Canada’s coast. What is this territory called?
France shares a northern land border with a country whose capital is Brussels and whose coast faces the North Sea. Name this neighboring country.
France meets this Iberian country across much of the Pyrenees, with the border extending toward the Mediterranean at the range’s eastern end. Its capital is Madrid. What country is it?

On the southwestern shore of Lake Michigan, this city is Illinois’s most populous and serves as the seat of Cook County. It was incorporated in 1837 near a portage linking the Great Lakes watershed with the Mississippi River system. What city is it?
Chicago stands on the southwestern shore of this Great Lake, the only one of the five Great Lakes located entirely within the United States. Its shoreline touches four U.S. states. What lake is it?
Chicago is the seat of this northeastern Illinois local government area, the most populous of its kind in the state. Evanston and Oak Park also lie within its boundaries. What is it?
Chicago is the most populous city in this Midwestern state, whose capital is Springfield. The state’s southern boundary follows the Ohio River. What state is it?

Chicago’s primary commercial aviation hub is located northwest of downtown and has often ranked among the world’s busiest by passenger traffic. It is one of two major air-travel gateways serving the city, alongside Midway. What is it?
This sovereign state occupies the Southern Levant on the eastern Mediterranean coast and declared independence on 14 May 1948, following the end of the British Mandate. What country is it?
Israel’s western coast fronts this sea, which lies between southern Europe and North Africa and connects to the Red Sea through the Suez Canal. Name the sea.
Israel shares a border with this kingdom to its east, whose capital is Amman and which signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994. Name the country.

Israel’s government seat and proclaimed capital is a city revered by Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Its Old City includes such sites as the Western Wall and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. Name the city.
At Israel’s southern tip, this port city sits on the Gulf of Aqaba, an arm of the Red Sea. It is the country’s principal access point to that sea. Name the city.
This North Texas city is the western anchor of the metropolitan area shared with Dallas, which lies to its east. It is also home to Texas Christian University.
In Fort Worth, the Clear Fork and West Fork converge near downtown to form the main channel that continues east through Dallas. Which river is this?

This Ecuadorian volcano is the country’s highest mountain, with a summit about 6,263 meters above sea level. Though lower than Everest in elevation above sea level, its summit is the point on Earth’s surface farthest from the planet’s center; identify the mountain.

Mount Chimborazo’s summit lies farther from Earth’s center than Everest’s, despite being lower above sea level. What is the name of the planet’s outward widening around the equator that accounts for this difference?

In northern Tanzania, this roughly 20-kilometer-wide volcanic basin formed when a large volcano collapsed, creating one of the world’s largest intact calderas. What is this feature’s established name?

Within the broader landscape around Ngorongoro Crater, this steep-sided ravine in Tanzania is renowned for hominin fossils and stone tools that have helped researchers study human origins. What is the site’s established name?

Which eastern Mediterranean island country, with Nicosia as its capital, is internationally recognized as the government of the island even though its administration does not extend into the Turkish-controlled north?
In the Republic of Cyprus, what UN-patrolled buffer zone separates the government-controlled south from the Turkish-controlled north and runs through the divided capital of Nicosia?

This fortified, steep-sided rocky summit rises above the city and was first enclosed by a Mycenaean wall in the 13th century BCE. Later it became a sanctuary associated with Athena and was crowned by monuments such as the Parthenon and Erechtheion; what is the site’s natural name?

At the Acropolis of Athens, gunpowder stored inside its best-known fifth-century temple detonated during a Venetian bombardment, badly damaging the building and scattering architectural fragments around the hill. What is this destructive event commonly identified by its year?

This ancient city in the Southern Levant stands on a plateau between the Mediterranean Sea and the Dead Sea. It is sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam, and its Old City includes the Western Wall and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. What city is it?
Jerusalem lies on a plateau in the Southern Levant, within a highland chain between the Mediterranean Sea and the Dead Sea. What is this chain called?
In 1538, during the reign of this Ottoman sultan, Jerusalem’s Old City walls were rebuilt. His rule also saw the empire expand across much of Hungary and Iraq. Who was he?

In northern Arizona, this steep-sided gorge extends 277 miles, reaches up to 18 miles wide, and is more than a mile deep. Its exposed rock layers preserve nearly two billion years of geological history. What landform is it?
Recent studies suggest this river established its course through the Grand Canyon about 5–6 million years ago, cutting downward through the rising plateau. What river carved most of the canyon?

In 1540, this Spanish explorer was sent from Francisco Vázquez de Coronado’s expedition to investigate reports of a river far to the north, becoming the first European known to view the Grand Canyon. Who was he?
What southeastern Wyoming city is the state’s third-largest by population and home to the University of Wyoming? The remains of Fort Sanders are also located nearby.
Laramie is home to this state’s flagship university; its capital is Cheyenne, and Yellowstone National Park lies in its northwestern corner. What state is it?
This Oklahoma city lies along the Arkansas River and is home to Oral Roberts University. Its historic Greenwood District is remembered as Black Wall Street. What city is it?
Tulsa stands on this river, which rises in Colorado, runs east across Kansas before entering Oklahoma, then continues southeast to the Mississippi River. What river is it?

On the western slopes of California’s southern Sierra Nevada, this protected area includes the Giant Forest and General Sherman, the world’s largest tree by volume. It lies immediately south of Kings Canyon. What is this area called?
Sequoia National Park’s high country includes this 14,505-foot summit, the highest point in the contiguous United States. What is the summit’s name?

Which vast subarctic biome forms a broad belt between tundra and temperate deciduous forests, with spruce, pine, and fir dominating its evergreen canopy? Its cold climate often leaves permanently frozen ground beneath a thin, seasonally thawed surface layer.
Within the Taiga, what is the name for persistently frozen ground beneath the seasonally thawed active layer, which can constrain tree roots and drainage?
This city in western Saudi Arabia lies in the Hejaz, about 70 kilometers inland from Jeddah. It is Islam’s holiest city and the destination of the annual Hajj pilgrimage. What city is it?
In Mecca, this vast mosque surrounds the Kaaba and is the site where pilgrims perform the circumambulation known as tawaf. Give its Arabic name, often translated as the Sacred Mosque.

In Mecca’s Great Mosque stands this cuboid shrine, which serves as the qibla—the direction Muslims worldwide face during prayer. Islamic tradition associates its construction with Abraham and Ishmael. Name this structure.
Atop Jabal al-Nour outside Mecca, this secluded natural chamber is traditionally said to be where Muhammad received the Quran’s first revelation. What is the site called?

This steel arch structure carries U.S. Route 19 over the New River near Fayetteville, West Virginia. At 3,030 feet long, it was once the longest steel arch span in the world and is the focus of an annual October event that permits BASE jumping.

The New River Gorge Bridge spans a river whose rapids attract outfitters and visitors to Fayette County. What recreational activity, graded on a scale from I to VI and commonly done in inflatable boats, is popular there?
This city is France’s capital and largest urban center, located in the Île-de-France region. Its municipal administration divides it into 20 arrondissements; what city is it?
This waterway runs through Paris and continues northwest across northern France before reaching the English Channel near Le Havre. What river passes through the capital?
A major rebuilding of Paris in the 19th century introduced broad boulevards, parks, and extensive public works during Napoleon III’s rule. Which prefect of the Seine directed that transformation?
In Paris, this former royal palace now houses a major museum, whose central entrance is marked by a glass pyramid designed by I. M. Pei. What museum displays the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo?
Paris hosted this international multisport event in 2024, a century after the event’s Paris edition in 1924. Its 2024 opening ceremony unfolded along the Seine; what event was it?

In San Francisco, this street runs between Market Street and 19th Street and gives its name to the surrounding district. The district became a nationally prominent center of LGBTQ+ life and activism; what street is it?

A business owner whose camera shop stood on Castro Street became a leading neighborhood organizer before winning election to the San Francisco Board of Supervisors in 1977. He was assassinated the following year by former supervisor Dan White; who was he?

Near Fifth Avenue and East 64th Street, this New York City zoo occupies the southeastern corner of Manhattan’s 843-acre urban green space. Its exhibits include the Tropic Zone, Temperate Territory, and Polar Circle. What is the zoo called?
The Central Park Zoo is one of several New York animal parks run by this organization, which also operates the Bronx Zoo and the New York Aquarium. What organization operates it?
What is the name of Poland’s capital and largest city, located on the Vistula River? Much of its historic center was rebuilt after World War II.
Warsaw lies on the banks of this river, Poland’s longest, which flows north to the Gulf of Gdańsk before reaching the Baltic Sea. What is the river’s name?

This southeastern U.S. state borders the Atlantic Ocean and includes the Lowcountry and Sea Islands. Its capital is Columbia, and its history includes the Nullification Crisis and the start of the Civil War. Which state is it?
In South Carolina’s Lowcountry, which Sea Island is known for its Gullah Geechee heritage and shares its name with the South Atlantic island where Napoleon spent his final years?
This East Asian country stretches from the Pacific coast across deserts and high plateaus, and its territory contains the basins of both the Yangtze and Yellow rivers. What country is it?

In China, this river carries fine loess from the Loess Plateau and empties into the Bohai Sea. Its course passes through the North China Plain, and it has historically been associated with severe floods. What river is this?
China’s capital is a northern municipality whose historic center includes Tiananmen Square and the Forbidden City. It also hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics. Name this city.
China’s northern border meets this landlocked country, whose capital is Ulaanbaatar and whose territory includes the southern part of the Gobi Desert. Which country is it?

Along China’s southwestern edge, this mountain system forms a high barrier north of Nepal and India. It includes Mount Everest, whose summit lies on the border between Nepal and China. Name the range.

Its mainland forms the southern end of the Balkan Peninsula, while thousands of islands are spread across the Aegean and Ionian seas. What southeastern European country, whose capital is Athens, is described?
Along Greece’s western side, this sea separates the mainland from Italy and gives its name to a group of Greek islands. What sea is it?
Greece’s eastern island groups, including the Cyclades and the Dodecanese, lie in this sea, which separates the country from western Turkey. What sea is it?

Greece occupies the southern end of this southeastern European landmass, which projects into the Mediterranean between the Adriatic, Ionian, and Aegean seas and extends north through Albania, North Macedonia, and Bulgaria. What geographic feature is it?
This country lies north of Greece and shares a land border with it; its coastline meets both the Adriatic and Ionian seas, and its capital is Tirana. What country is it?

This Caribbean nation occupies the western part of Hispaniola, while the Dominican Republic occupies the island’s remainder. Its mountainous landscape and pair of prominent peninsulas give its outline a distinctive horseshoe-like form. What country is this?
Haiti’s capital and largest city is situated on the Gulf of Gonâve, on the country’s western coast, and is its chief administrative center. What is this city called?

This Sea Island in Beaufort County, South Carolina, is a historic center of Gullah culture and lies near Hilton Head Island. It is also associated with the inspiration for a children’s television series about life in the Sea Islands. What island is it?

On Saint Helena Island, what African American cultural community is historically rooted in the Sea Islands and is known for a creole language shaped by West African influences, including Fulani and Mende?

This Central European country stretches from the Baltic coast to the Sudetes and Carpathian Mountains, and its capital is Warsaw. It shares borders with Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania, and Russia. What country is it?
Poland’s northern coastline lies along this sea, which is connected to the North Sea by the Kiel Canal. The Øresund strait links it to the Kattegat between Denmark and Sweden. What sea is it?
Poland’s longest river passes through Warsaw before flowing north toward the Baltic Sea. What is the name of this river?
This U.S. state is divided into a larger Lower Peninsula and a smaller Upper Peninsula, separated by the Straits of Mackinac. It borders four of the five Great Lakes.
Michigan's Upper Peninsula forms much of the southern shore of this Great Lake. It is the largest of the Great Lakes by surface area and drains toward Lake Huron through the St. Marys River.
This high-altitude lake lies in the Andes on the border between Peru and Bolivia. In Inca tradition, it was the place from which the legendary founder Manco Capac emerged. What lake is it?
In an Inca origin tradition associated with Lake Titicaca, this legendary figure emerged from its waters with Mama Ocllo. He is credited with founding Cusco, the Inca capital. Who is he?
This is the world’s largest interconnected coral ecosystem, stretching for about 2,300 kilometers along the coast of Queensland in northeastern Australia. What natural feature is it?

The Great Barrier Reef lies off Queensland within this southwestern Pacific marginal sea, bordered to the west by eastern Australia and to the east by island groups including Vanuatu and New Caledonia. What sea is it?
Located on Maine’s Mount Desert Island and nearby coastal islands, this protected area includes Cadillac Mountain and the iron-rung Beehive Loop. What is it?

Acadia National Park and Bar Harbor lie southwest of this bay, which separates New Brunswick from Nova Scotia and is known for exceptionally high tides. The city of Saint John sits on its shore. What bay is it?
What is Earth’s smallest major ocean basin, surrounding the North Pole and bordered by northern Eurasia and North America? Its surface is covered by shifting sea ice for part or much of the year.
Which named underwater feature beneath the Arctic Ocean marks the boundary between the North American and Eurasian plates? It is known for having the slowest seafloor-spreading rate on Earth.
This deep freshwater lake sits at roughly 6,225 feet in the Sierra Nevada and straddles the California-Nevada border. It is the second-deepest lake in the United States; what lake is it?
Lake Tahoe's only natural surface outlet flows northeast through Reno and Sparks before emptying into Pyramid Lake. What river carries this water?

What southeastern European region, centered on a peninsula between the Adriatic, Aegean, and Black seas, was long associated with Ottoman rule and nationalist rivalries? Before World War I, it was famously described as Europe’s “powder keg.”
Within the Balkans, which country has a short Adriatic coastline around the town of Neum, separating two stretches of Croatia’s coast? Its capital is Sarajevo.

This inland sea lies between southeastern Europe and western Asia, with Ukraine and Bulgaria on its northern and western shores and Turkey along its south. It connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and Dardanelles. What sea is it?
The Black Sea connects to the Sea of Marmara through this narrow strait, which passes through Istanbul and separates the city's European and Asian sides. What is this strait called?

In Lower Manhattan, this east–west thoroughfare runs from Broadway toward the East River and gave its name to the surrounding financial district and a broader symbol of U.S. markets. Its name recalls a defensive barrier built by Dutch colonists in 17th-century New Amsterdam. What is this thoroughfare?
At 26 Wall Street, a Greek Revival building marks the site where George Washington took the presidential oath in 1789, when New York served as the nation’s capital. What historic landmark is it?
This landlocked state spans the Great Plains and the Midwest, with Lincoln as its capital and Omaha as its largest city. What state is it?
Nebraska's elected state lawmakers sit together in one chamber, and candidates run without official party affiliation. What is the name for this arrangement?

Nebraska is one of two states that awards its electoral votes partly according to the statewide result and partly to the winner in each of its three areas represented in the U.S. House. What is this allocation system called?
Admitted to the Union on June 1, 1796, as the nation’s sixteenth state, this southeastern state is divided into East, Middle, and West Grand Divisions. Its major cities include Nashville and Memphis.
In Tennessee’s capital, a radio program that began on WSM as the Barn Dance in 1925 grew into a celebrated showcase for country music. What is the name of this long-running program?
Which Australian island state lies south of the mainland, is separated from Victoria by a narrow sea passage, and was the setting of the colonial conflict known as the Black War?
Tasmania is separated from mainland Australia by which strait, lying between the island and the state of Victoria?

The largest city in the United States, this settlement occupies the southeastern tip of its state near the mouth of the Hudson River. It consists of five boroughs, each corresponding to a county. What city is it?
In New York City, Dutch colonists established a settlement on this island in the 1620s. Today, the borough includes both the Financial District and Central Park. Which island and borough is it?
One of New York City’s five boroughs, this one lies west of Brooklyn across the Narrows and is connected to Lower Manhattan by a free ferry. Which borough is it?
Before English rule began in 1664, the Dutch settlement on Manhattan that became New York City had this name. What was it called?
This 1898 political event created the five-borough form of New York City, bringing Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island into a single municipality. What event was it?

This arm of the Arabian Sea lies between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula, with shores belonging to eight countries, including Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain. At its southeastern end, it connects with the Gulf of Oman; what is this body of water called?

The Persian Gulf connects to the Gulf of Oman through a narrow passage at its southeastern end. This important shipping route carries petroleum exports from countries along the gulf; what is the passage called?
Which landlocked country in southeastern Africa was formerly called Rhodesia? Its name is also shared by the medieval stone archaeological complex built by ancestors of the Shona people.
Zimbabwe’s northern boundary with Zambia is defined largely by which major river, which also flows over Victoria Falls before continuing east toward Mozambique?
Which major Japanese city was where Toyotomi Hideyoshi began building a great castle in 1583? It later became the site of the campaigns that ended the Toyotomi clan’s rule.

In Osaka, which Japanese leader initiated construction of the great castle in 1583 after rising to power following Oda Nobunaga’s death? He is also remembered as one of Japan’s great unifiers and for launching invasions of Korea.

This city sits on the Ohio River across from southern Indiana and is the seat of Jefferson County. It is home to the annual Kentucky Derby and a museum and factory tour devoted to its famous baseball bats. What city is it?
In Louisville, Kentucky, this thoroughbred racetrack has hosted the Kentucky Derby since 1875, and its twin spires are a recognizable landmark. What is the track called?

This East African archipelago, now part of Tanzania, includes the islands of Unguja and Pemba. Its historic trading center of Stone Town reflects the region’s Swahili and Omani heritage. What is the archipelago called?
Within Zanzibar, this is the largest island and the location of Zanzibar City, including historic Stone Town on its western coast. Pemba lies to its north. What is this island’s Swahili name?

This roughly 250-kilometer-long strip, created under the 1953 armistice, follows a line near the 38th parallel and separates the two states on the peninsula. Despite its name, it is among the world’s most heavily fortified frontiers. What is it called?

Within the Korean Demilitarized Zone, this enclave at Panmunjom has blue conference buildings that straddle the military boundary. It was the site of the April 2018 meeting between Kim Jong-un and Moon Jae-in. What is this enclave called?

Founded in 762 by Abbasid caliph al-Mansur, this city was designed as a round capital near the Tigris and later became a major center of scholarship. It is now the capital and largest city of Iraq. What city is it?
In Baghdad, this renowned scholarly institution became a center for translating Greek, Persian, and Indian works into Arabic during the Islamic Golden Age. What was this institution called?
In 1258, Baghdad was overrun by Hulagu’s Mongol forces, and much of the city was destroyed. What event is commonly known by the name of the city and the year it occurred?

Created in 1999 from part of the Northwest Territories, this is Canada’s largest and northernmost territory, centered in the eastern Arctic. Its capital, Iqaluit, has hosted cold-weather testing of the Airbus A380. What territory is it?
Nunavut’s northern coastline borders this ocean, which surrounds the North Pole and is largely covered by sea ice. What is this northernmost ocean?

An underwater eruption began in November 1963 near the Vestmannaeyjar archipelago, building a new island off Iceland’s southern coast by 1967. The island was protected from most human interference so researchers could observe how life colonizes newly formed land; what is its name?
Surtsey lies in the North Atlantic off the southern coast of which island nation? Its capital is Reykjavík, and its largest airport, Keflavík, was developed from a former U.S. naval air station.
Which city is the capital and largest urban center of Hawaiʻi, on the southeastern shore of Oʻahu? It includes a famous resort district and is served by the state’s principal international airport.
Within Honolulu, what coastal district is known for its resort hotels, long surfing tradition, and views of Diamond Head?

Located in northeastern Africa, this transcontinental country extends into southwestern Asia across a peninsula. Its capital is Cairo, and the Nile River empties into the Mediterranean Sea through its northern delta.
Egypt's western land neighbor is this North African country, whose capital is Tripoli and whose coastline stretches along the Mediterranean Sea.

Egypt's portion of southwestern Asia is a wedge-shaped region, with the Mediterranean Sea to its north and the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba forming its western and eastern sides. This land bridge connects the country's African and Asian territories.
This man-made waterway crosses Egypt between the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea. It allows ships to avoid the much longer route around the Cape of Good Hope.

Egypt's historic settlements cluster along this river, which flows north through the country and divides into distributaries before reaching the Mediterranean Sea. Its floodwaters deposited fertile silt across the surrounding valley and delta.

This cross-border cultural region occupies parts of northern Spain and southwestern France, including lands near the western Pyrenees and the Atlantic coast. Its people share a distinct identity and a language unrelated to the Romance languages spoken around them. What region is it?
The Basque Country has a northern coastline on a large Atlantic gulf between northern Spain and western France. What body of water is also called the Golfe de Gascogne in French?
Which landlocked Central European country became independent in the 1993 Velvet Divorce and has Bratislava as its capital?
Which major river flows through Bratislava in Slovakia, then passes through Vienna, Budapest, and Belgrade before emptying into the Black Sea?

This historic West Virginia town lies where the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers meet, beside a gap in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Its federal arsenal was targeted in an 1859 abolitionist raid. What is the town’s name?

At Harpers Ferry in 1859, this abolitionist led an armed raid on the federal arsenal in an effort to spark an uprising against slavery. Captured during the raid, he was later executed for treason. Who was he?

This landlocked country in Eastern Europe occupies part of the East European Plain and borders Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia. It declared independence from the Soviet Union on August 25, 1991, and its capital is Minsk. What is this country?
Belarus’s capital and largest city lies on the Svislach River. Heavily damaged during World War II, it was rebuilt as a major Soviet-style city. What is the city?

This mountainous cultural region follows much of the eastern United States, stretching from southern New York toward northern Alabama and Mississippi. Its communities are associated with distinctive folk traditions, old-time music, and a long history of coal mining. What is the region called?

In Appalachia, what string-band genre was popularized by mandolinist Bill Monroe and became widely known for Earl Scruggs’s three-finger banjo style? Its sound draws on fiddle, banjo, and other acoustic instruments. What is the genre?
This East Asian republic occupies the southern half of a peninsula divided after World War II. Its capital, crossed by the Han River, is Seoul. What country is it?
South Korea has coastlines on two marginal seas. The body of water to its west is also known as the Huang Hai and lies between the Korean Peninsula and China. What is it called?

South Korea's northern land boundary is marked by a heavily fortified, roughly 4-kilometer-wide buffer strip established under the 1953 armistice. What is this strip separating the two countries called?
This immense hot, arid expanse stretches across North Africa from the Atlantic Ocean toward the Red Sea, with the Sahel forming much of its southern boundary. What is its natural name?
Along the southern edge of the Sahara Desert lies a semi-arid belt of tropical savanna that includes areas around the Niger River valley and Sudan. What is this transitional region called?
The Sahara Desert includes this vast region in Niger, lying east of the Aïr Mountains and crossed by historic caravan routes. What is this region called?
In the Sahara Desert, a volcanic massif in northern Chad includes Emi Koussi, the desert’s highest peak. What is the name of this range?

The Sahara Desert has shifted repeatedly between desert and grassland over long periods, a pattern linked to changes in the North African monsoon. What slow cycle in the orientation of Earth’s rotational axis helps drive those changes?
Located in southeastern England along the River Thames, it is both the capital and largest city of the United Kingdom. What city is it?
London’s rapid-transit network began operating in 1863, making it the world’s oldest system of its kind. What network is commonly represented by a red-and-blue roundel?
Which church in London has served as the coronation church for English and British monarchs since 1066? Its Poets’ Corner commemorates writers including Geoffrey Chaucer.
London became the first city to host a global multi-sport competition three times, following editions in 1908 and 1948. Which 2012 edition completed that historic trio?
Which historic district forms London’s ancient core and remains a major financial center? Often called the “Square Mile,” it has its own local government, distinct from the surrounding boroughs.
Georgia’s capital and largest city was captured and burned during Sherman’s 1864 campaign, then became a major center of the civil-rights movement. Which city later hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics?

A river along the western side of the Atlanta metropolitan area rises in the Blue Ridge Mountains and flows through Lake Lanier, a major regional water-supply reservoir. Farther downstream, it joins the Flint River to form the Apalachicola; what is this river’s name?
Which ancient city in northwestern Anatolia was traditionally described as the setting of the Trojan War and the home of Priam? Its archaeological remains are identified with a site in modern Turkey.

Troy is generally identified with an archaeological site near the Dardanelles in modern northwestern Turkey. What is the name of the mound where archaeologists excavated the remains of the ancient city?

This country stretches from the Atlantic to the Pacific and northward into the Arctic. It is the world’s second-largest country by total area and has the longest coastline of any country. What country is it?

Canada shares its longest international land border with the United States, and a major portion of the boundary west of the Lake of the Woods follows this line of latitude. The 1846 Oregon Treaty helped establish the boundary along it. What is this line?
Canada and the United States share this Great Lake, the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area. Its waters flow toward Lake Huron through the St. Marys River. What lake is it?

Canada borders this U.S. state along its eastern edge, even though the state is separated from the contiguous United States. Its long southeastern panhandle reaches down the Pacific coast, and the United States purchased it from Russia in 1867. What state is it?

This is Canada’s largest island, located across Davis Strait from Greenland and separated from the mainland by Foxe Basin and Hudson Strait. Nunavut’s capital, Iqaluit, is on its southeastern coast. What island is it?
On Cuba’s southeastern coast, which bay is the site of a U.S. naval base retained under a long-term lease opposed by the Cuban government?
Guantánamo Bay is the site of a prison opened in 2002 to hold foreign terrorism suspects captured by the United States. What name is commonly used for that prison?

This large Indonesian island lies between the Indian Ocean and the Malay Peninsula, with the Strait of Malacca along its northeastern side. The Sunda Strait separates its southern end from Java. What island is it?
Associated with Sumatra, this maritime empire had its capital at Palembang and grew wealthy by managing and taxing trade through the Strait of Malacca from around 650 CE. What empire was it?

Which U.S. state is the nation’s largest by area and lies at the far northwest of North America, with the Arctic Ocean to its north and the Pacific Ocean to its south? It is separated from the contiguous United States by Canada.
Alaska’s capital lies in its southeastern panhandle and is not connected to the continent’s road network; travelers commonly reach it by air or ferry. What is this city?
Alaska’s most populous city is also a major transportation hub, with an international airport named for a former U.S. senator. What is this city?
The Iditarod sled-dog race traditionally finishes in this Alaska city on the southern coast of the Seward Peninsula. What is the city?
At 20,310 feet, this is the highest mountain in Alaska and in all of North America; its Athabaskan name is commonly translated as “the High One.” What is the mountain’s current name?
This highland chain in northern New Hampshire includes the Presidential Range and is notorious for severe, rapidly changing weather. What is the range called?
The White Mountains lie within this New England state, whose capital is Concord and whose western border meets Vermont. What state is it?

Opened in 1907 to connect local farmers directly with Seattle shoppers, this historic multilevel landmark occupies a site overlooking Elliott Bay. Its fishmongers became famous for tossing orders across the counter, and its stalls offer produce, seafood, crafts, and prepared food. What Seattle landmark is it?
At Pike Place Market, a bronze piggy bank near the main arcade serves as a beloved mascot and collects donations for the market’s nonprofit foundation. What is this sculpture’s name?

Which island country lies in the southwestern Pacific, southeast of Australia, and has Wellington as its capital? Its Indigenous Polynesian people are Māori, and Māori is one of its official languages.
New Zealand lies east of Australia across this sea. What is the name of the body of water between the two countries?
Of New Zealand’s two principal islands, this one is larger by land area and bears the Māori name Te Waipounamu. Which island is it?

This New Zealand waterway divides the country’s two main islands and is named for the British navigator who charted the coastline in 1769. A ferry route linking Wellington and Picton crosses it. What is it?
New Zealand’s most populous city occupies a narrow isthmus between Waitematā and Manukau harbors. Its metropolitan area includes numerous volcanic cones and nearby islands; what city is it?

Among the five Great Lakes, this is the only one located entirely within the United States, with shores in Wisconsin, Illinois, and Indiana. It ranks third among the Great Lakes in surface area. What lake is it?
On the northwestern side of Lake Michigan, this bay lies between the Door Peninsula and Wisconsin’s mainland. The Fox River empties into its southern end. What bay is it?

This deep waterway links Lake Michigan with Lake Huron, which hydrologically function as a single lake. A suspension bridge between Michigan’s Upper and Lower Peninsulas spans this channel. What waterway is it?
The Kuroshio near East Asia and the Canary off northwest Africa are examples of these large-scale flows of seawater. Their volume transport can be measured in sverdrups. What are they called?

Ocean currents in the Northern Hemisphere are deflected to the right, while those in the Southern Hemisphere are deflected to the left. This same planetary effect helps explain why large storms rotate in opposite directions in the two hemispheres. What is it called?

Built by the Mexica on an island in Lake Texcoco, this city became the capital of the expanding Aztec Empire in the 15th century. Its ruins now lie beneath the historic center of Mexico City. What was this city?
Tenochtitlan stood on an island in this lake in the Valley of Mexico, where water routes and nearby chinampas helped shape the city's environment. What was the lake's name?
Tenochtitlan was one of two Mexica polities on its island; this neighboring settlement was the other and was renowned for its great marketplace. Name this city-state.
Which city sits where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet to form the Ohio River? It is the setting for August Wilson’s plays The Piano Lesson and Fences.
In Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, which river begins where the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet, then flows west before turning south toward the Mississippi River?
Finland’s northernmost region includes the Arctic Circle landmark at Santa Claus Village and is renowned for Sámi culture and aurora viewing. What is this region called?
In Lapland, which city serves as the region’s administrative capital and is promoted as the official hometown of Santa Claus? The nearby Santa Claus Village lies on the Arctic Circle.

This city is the capital of New South Wales and had the largest population among Australia’s capital-city regions in the 2021 count. Its historic center grew around a sheltered harbor after the British First Fleet arrived in 1788. What city is it?

In Sydney, a landmark performing-arts venue stands on Bennelong Point, with a roof of white shell-like forms evoking sails. Which Danish architect won the design competition for this building in 1957?
Which 16th-century Flemish cartographer published a 1569 world map that showed sailing courses as straight lines? His work used a mapmaking method that became especially useful for navigation.

Gerardus Mercator introduced this cylindrical method of representing the world on a 1569 map. It represents constant-bearing sailing routes as straight lines, though it greatly enlarges regions near the poles.
Rising in Colorado’s San Juan Mountains, this river flows through New Mexico and then forms much of the Texas–Mexico boundary before reaching the coast. What river is it?
The Rio Grande empties near Brownsville and Matamoros into a body of water bordered by the southern United States, Cuba, and the Yucatán Peninsula. What is it?
Which major city in eastern Libya became internationally known after a 2012 attack on a U.S. diplomatic compound there killed Ambassador Chris Stevens?
During the 2012 attack on a U.S. diplomatic compound in Benghazi, which U.S. ambassador to Libya was killed?

This major Brazilian city lies on the Atlantic coast around Guanabara Bay, with the Christ the Redeemer statue overlooking it from Mount Corcovado. It was Brazil’s capital until 1960, when Brasília took its place.

Rio de Janeiro occupies the western shore of this broad Atlantic inlet, which Portuguese explorers named after arriving on January 1, 1502, and mistaking its entrance for a river mouth. What is this bay called?
Argentina’s capital and largest city stands on the western shore of the Río de la Plata and serves as the country’s principal political and cultural center. What city is it?

Buenos Aires is Argentina’s capital, while the country also claims a South Atlantic archipelago that it invaded in 1982, leading to a war with the United Kingdom. What archipelago was the conflict fought over?
This is the easternmost of New York City’s five boroughs and lies on Long Island. Which borough contains the neighborhoods of Flushing and Astoria?
Which Queens green space contains the Unisphere and hosted the 1939–40 and 1964–65 World’s Fairs?

This South Asian country occupies much of the Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta and is bordered on most sides by India, with Myanmar to its southeast. It became independent from Pakistan after the 1971 Liberation War; name the country.
Bangladesh’s capital and largest city lies on the Buriganga River and serves as the country’s center of government. What city is it?

This northeastern Italian city occupies islands in a shallow lagoon, with canals separating neighborhoods and bridges linking them. It served as the capital of a powerful maritime republic for centuries and is often called the City of Canals. What city is it?
In Venice, this vast shipbuilding and naval complex supported the republic’s sea power and is considered by some historians to have been history’s first factory. What is this historic complex called?

Venice is built across islands within this shallow stretch of water on Italy’s northeastern Adriatic coast, separated from the open sea by barrier islands and connected to it through narrow inlets. The city and this surrounding environment together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. What is this body of water called?

In Venice’s former republic, the elected head of state held this title instead of a hereditary royal crown. Enrico Dandolo and Andrea Gritti were among the figures who held the office. What was the title?
Venice was traditionally known by this Italian honorific, which translates as “The Most Serene.” What was this name for the city?
This nearly enclosed intercontinental sea lies between southern Europe, northern Africa, and western Asia. A narrow passage at its western end connects it to the Atlantic Ocean. What is this sea?

The Mediterranean Sea opens into the Atlantic Ocean through a narrow passage between southern Spain and northern Morocco. This passage is the only natural sea route between the two bodies of water. What is it called?

Ships traveling from the Mediterranean Sea toward the Black Sea pass through the Dardanelles, cross the Sea of Marmara, and then use this strait. It runs between the European and Asian sides of Istanbul. What is it called?

At the eastern end of the Mediterranean Sea, this artificial waterway crosses Egypt to connect with the Red Sea. Its opening in 1869 created a shorter maritime route between Europe and Asia. What is it called?
The Mediterranean Sea’s largest island by area is also home to Mount Etna and the cities of Palermo and Catania. The Strait of Messina separates it from mainland Italy. What is this island?

Planned by William Penn and surveyor Thomas Holme in 1682, this Pennsylvania city’s original core was laid out in a grid with public squares between the Delaware and Schuylkill Rivers. Its historic district includes the site where both the Declaration of Independence and the U.S. Constitution were debated and signed.

In Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, construction of this building began in 1732, when it was built as the State House of Pennsylvania. It later hosted debates and signings of the 1776 declaration announcing the colonies’ separation from Britain and the U.S. Constitution.

Most of this major Southern California city lies in a basin beside the Pacific Ocean, while other parts extend through the Santa Monica Mountains and into the San Fernando Valley. It is also the county seat and largest city of the county that shares its name. What city is it?
Los Angeles was founded in 1781 under Spanish governor Felipe de Neve on the site of a Tongva village. What was the name of that village?
Los Angeles became part of the United States in 1848 after the Mexican-American War. What 1848 agreement transferred the territory to the United States?
Completed in 1913, this project brought water from Eastern California to Los Angeles and helped enable the city’s growth. What was this water-supply project called?

Los Angeles first hosted the quadrennial international multi-sport competition in 1932, returned as host in 1984, and is scheduled to host it again in 2028. Which edition was the city’s first as host?

This island country lies in the Indian Ocean off southeastern Africa, separated from the mainland by a channel and known for its exceptionally high number of endemic species. What country has Antananarivo as its capital?
Madagascar lies east of Mozambique across this body of water, which opens into the Indian Ocean to the north and south. Name this stretch of water.
Madagascar’s capital and largest city is located in the island’s central highlands and serves as the country’s political center. Name this city.
Madagascar lies within this ocean, which stretches between Africa, Asia, and Australia. What is the name of this ocean?
This sovereign island country lies northwest of Madagascar in the Mozambique Channel region, and its capital is Moroni. What country is it?
This Balkan capital is organized around a central square named for Albania’s national hero, and it is home to the Et’hem Bey Mosque and the Cold War bunker museum Bunk’Art. What is this city?
In Tirana, this Ottoman-era place of worship on the city’s central plaza is distinguished by frescoes depicting trees, waterfalls, and bridges. What is its name?
This rugged upland forms the highest and easternmost subdivision of the Ozarks, lying chiefly in northern Arkansas and extending into southern Missouri. What is this geographic region?
The Boston Mountains include extensive areas protected within this federally managed forest in Arkansas. Named for the broader upland region to which the Boston Mountains belong, what is this forest?

Founded by English Puritan settlers on the Shawmut Peninsula in 1630, this city became the capital and largest city of Massachusetts. It lies on Massachusetts Bay and was named for a town in Lincolnshire, England. What city is it?
In Boston, what public green space established in 1634 is widely recognized as the first public park in the United States? It once served as a communal grazing ground.
Founded in Boston in 1635, this institution is identified as the first public school in the United States. What school has counted Benjamin Franklin and Samuel Adams among its alumni?
In Boston, what downtown tunnel for streetcars opened in 1897 and is recognized as the first underground rapid-transit system in the United States? It is now part of the city's Green Line.

This special administrative region occupies China’s southern coast, immediately south of Shenzhen, and includes an island, a peninsula, and a mainland area known as the New Territories. Britain’s former colony was transferred to China in 1997. What is it?

In Hong Kong, what stretch of land forms the northern side of Victoria Harbour opposite Hong Kong Island and includes districts such as Tsim Sha Tsui? Its name is also associated with a densely populated walled settlement demolished in the 1990s.
Hong Kong lies beside the estuary of which major southern Chinese river, whose delta also includes Guangzhou and Macau? Its Chinese name is Zhu Jiang.
This major city in south-central Texas is home to the NBA’s Spurs. It was also the former home of the WNBA franchise that moved to Las Vegas in 2017. What city is it?

In downtown San Antonio, this former Spanish mission and fortress was the site of a 13-day siege in 1836 during the Texas Revolution, ending in its capture by Mexican forces. What historic site is it?

In Yoruba religion, worshippers leave offerings to Oshun at these waterways; in Hindu traditions, pilgrims bathe in them during gatherings such as the Kumbh Mela. What natural features can serve as sites for offerings, purification, and pilgrimage?
Sacred rivers are central to Hindu pilgrimage, and at Prayagraj the Kumbh Mela is held at the confluence of this river and the Yamuna. What river is it?

Which major Paris railway terminus was painted by Claude Monet in 1877, with several canvases emphasizing trains beneath its iron-and-glass roof? It also appears in a celebrated Henri Cartier-Bresson photograph of a man leaping over a puddle.
At Gare Saint-Lazare, which artist painted *The Railway*, showing a girl looking through an iron railing as steam rises behind her? He also painted *Olympia* and *The Luncheon on the Grass*.
Which historic city in present-day Mali flourished as a major trans-Saharan trading center? It also became renowned as a center of Islamic scholarship.
Timbuktu was home to this historic institution of Islamic learning, associated with a mosque and renowned for attracting scholars and students. What was the institution called?
This city in western New York lies on the northeastern shore of Lake Erie. It is connected to Fort Erie, Ontario, by an international bridge across the Niagara River.

Buffalo and Fort Erie, Ontario, are connected by this international crossing over the Niagara River, opened in 1927. Its name commemorates a century of peaceful relations between Canada and the United States.
This tropical sea of the Atlantic lies between Central America and northern South America. Cuba, Hispaniola, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico line its northern side. What is this sea called?
Along the eastern edge of the Caribbean Sea, a curved island chain separates its waters from the open Atlantic. Commonly divided into the Windward and Leeward islands, what is this group called?

In caves, mineral-rich water dripping onto the floor leaves a deposit that gradually grows upward toward the ceiling. Unlike its counterpart that hangs down from the ceiling, what is this upward-growing formation called?

Stalagmites in many limestone caves build up as dripping water deposits dissolved calcium carbonate on the floor. Which mineral, a crystalline form of calcium carbonate, commonly makes up these deposits?
Comprising thousands of islands in the western Pacific and divided into Luzon, the Visayas, and Mindanao, this Southeast Asian nation has Manila as its capital. What country is it?
This bay-side city on Luzon is the Philippines’ capital and lies within the National Capital Region; nearby Quezon City is more populous. What city is it?
This is the largest island of the Philippines and the location of both Manila and the Cordillera highlands, including Ifugao’s famed rice terraces. What island is it?
This western Pacific marginal sea lies east of the Philippines, with the archipelago along its western side and the Mariana Islands farther to the east. What sea is it?
This second-largest island of the Philippines occupies the southern part of the archipelago and contains Mount Apo, the country’s highest peak, as well as Davao City. What island is it?

This major mountain system forms an arc more than 1,000 kilometres long across central and southern Europe, extending from the Ligurian Sea eastward toward Slovenia and the Adriatic. Its region spans eight countries and feeds the headwaters of rivers including the Rhine, Rhône, and Po. What is this range called?
Within the Alps, this summit on the France–Italy border is the range’s highest point and the highest mountain in Western Europe. What is its name?

This constituent country of the United Kingdom lies west of England and has a flag bearing a red dragon. Its indigenous Celtic language is still widely used, including on bilingual public signs. Name this country.
Wales’s largest city stands near the mouth of the River Taff on the Bristol Channel. It is also the country’s capital and the home of the Senedd and Principality Stadium. What city is it?
This island borough forms New York City’s southwesternmost corner, with the Arthur Kill separating it from New Jersey and the Narrows separating it from Brooklyn. What is the borough called?
On Staten Island’s eastern edge, what 1964-opened suspension crossing links the borough to Brooklyn? It bears the name of the Italian explorer who reached New York Harbor in 1524.

What cold, sparsely populated region spans southern Argentina and Chile, commonly extending from the Colorado River toward Tierra del Fuego? Its landscapes include western forests, lakes, and glaciers as well as a dry, windswept eastern steppe.
In Patagonia, what mountain range along the western side blocks moist air from the Pacific, helping create a rain shadow and drier steppe to the east?
The 96-meter structure at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London has four illuminated clock faces and is part of the Houses of Parliament complex. What is its present official name?
Inside Elizabeth Tower at the Palace of Westminster hangs a 13.7-tonne Great Bell whose deep hourly chimes are among London’s most recognizable sounds. What nickname is commonly used for that bell?
Shared by Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania, this African lake is the continent’s largest by surface area and is traditionally regarded as the source of the White Nile. What is its natural name?
In Lake Victoria, this large predatory fish was introduced in the 1950s to support commercial fishing, and its spread is associated with sharp declines in many native cichlids. What fish is it?

This Ligurian port became a powerful maritime republic whose rivalry with Venice shaped Mediterranean trade. Its citizens also supplied prominent defenders during the Ottoman siege of Constantinople in 1453.

During the 1453 Ottoman siege, troops from Genoa joined the defense of this Byzantine imperial capital, where the Genoese commander Giovanni Giustiniani was wounded as the city’s walls were breached. Its fall brought the Byzantine Empire to an end.
Built around 1450 as a high-altitude Inca citadel in present-day Peru, this site sits about 2,430 meters above sea level on a ridge above the Sacred Valley. What is the name of this landmark?
At Machu Picchu, a major river runs below the ridge and cuts a deep canyon through the surrounding region. Which river flows through this area and the Sacred Valley?
Which American explorer helped bring Machu Picchu to international attention after reaching the site in 1911, though Agustín Lizárraga had visited earlier?
Machu Picchu includes a carved ritual stone whose Quechua name is often translated as “hitching post of the sun.” What is this distinctive stone called?

This small Arab state lies on the northwestern shore of the Persian Gulf, with Iraq to its north and west and Saudi Arabia to its south. Its invasion in 1990 prompted the First Gulf War; name the country.

During the First Gulf War, the coalition used Kuwait’s southern neighbor as a major base for operations to liberate Kuwait. This country is the largest on the Arabian Peninsula and has coastlines on both the Red Sea and Persian Gulf.
Founded in 1836 on the upper Gulf coastal plain, this Texas city was established between White Oak and Buffalo bayous, roughly 50 miles from the Gulf of Mexico. What is the largest city in Texas?

Houston’s founders chose the settlement site partly because they expected this waterway to carry ships between inland Texas and the Gulf coast. Which waterway, paired with White Oak in descriptions of the city’s founding location, was it?
On the eastern bank of the Mersey estuary in northwest England, this major port city is associated with the Beatles and the Royal Albert Dock. Which city is it?
Liverpool’s waterfront borders this tidal river, with the Wirral Peninsula on its opposite side. Its name also appears in the title of Gerry and the Pacemakers’ song “Ferry Cross the ___.”
This is the most populous city in Quebec and occupies an island near the meeting of the Ottawa and St. Lawrence Rivers. It hosted the 1976 Summer Olympics; what city is it?
A prominent hill in Montréal gives the city its name and is now the centerpiece of a large urban park. A cross illuminated at night stands near its summit; what is the hill called?

What geographic discipline measures underwater depth at locations across oceans and lakes, then maps the relief of the seabed or lakebed? Its maps depict submerged terrain in much the same way topographic maps depict land.
In bathymetry, what acoustic technology measures distance by sending out sound pulses and detecting their echoes? Multibeam versions can collect depth measurements across a broad swath of seafloor.

Which Canadian province on the Atlantic coast has Halifax as both its capital and largest city? Its territory includes a large island separated from the mainland by the Strait of Canso, as well as the seaside community of Peggy’s Cove.

In Nova Scotia, what large island is separated from the mainland by the Strait of Canso and linked to it by the Canso Causeway? Its northern section contains a national park traversed by the Cabot Trail.
This southwestern U.S. state has Phoenix as its capital. It became the 48th state on February 14, 1912, after being organized as a separate U.S. territory. What state is it?

In northwestern Arizona, this river carved the Grand Canyon, cutting through a high-elevation region of broad plateaus and basins. The canyon is often cited as an outstanding example of erosion in an arid landscape. What river is it?

Located in Ethiopia’s northern highlands and bordering Eritrea, this mountainous administrative division has a distinct local culture. It was the principal theater of the war that began in 2020 between the TPLF and Ethiopia’s federal government. Which division is it?
Tigray Region’s administrative capital is a major city in northern Ethiopia. It was taken by federal forces in November 2020 during the war there; what city is it?
What vast East African savanna ecosystem, centered in northern Tanzania and extending into Kenya, is renowned for the annual migration of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles following seasonal rains?
Across the Serengeti’s grasslands, isolated rocky outcrops rise above the plains and provide shelter and lookout points for wildlife. What is the established name for these formations?
Designed by Nicola Salvi and completed in 1762, this monumental Baroque landmark in Rome features a central figure of a sea deity above a pool. What landmark is it?
At the Trevi Fountain, the central figure stands above a shell-shaped chariot drawn by sea horses and represents an ancient Roman deity associated with the world’s waters. What is the deity’s name?
At the north end of London’s Palace of Westminster, an iconic hour bell is housed in a tower officially named for Queen Elizabeth II. By what familiar name is this landmark commonly known?
Big Ben is housed in the landmark at the north end of the Palace of Westminster, which rises above the Houses of Parliament and carries four large clock faces. What is this structure’s official name?

This federally recognized tribal homeland spans the North Dakota–South Dakota border, and its tribal government is headquartered in Fort Yates, North Dakota. It drew international attention during the 2016 protests against the Dakota Access Pipeline; what is the name of this homeland?

Near the Standing Rock Sioux Reservation, a river joins the Missouri at the North Dakota community of Cannon Ball, close to a major encampment during the 2016 pipeline protests. What is the name of that tributary?

In 1507, the cartographer Martin Waldseemüller used this name on a world map for the landmass associated with the voyages of Amerigo Vespucci. What is the natural name of that landmass or continental grouping?
The name America honors this Florentine merchant and navigator, whose accounts of voyages across the Atlantic influenced Martin Waldseemüller’s 1507 map. Who was he?

In the United States, what are federally recognized areas of land held for Native American tribes and governed through both tribal and federal authority called? The Navajo Nation is the largest example, and Window Rock is its capital.

Among Indian reservations, which is the largest by land area and spans Arizona, New Mexico, and Utah? Its capital is Window Rock, and it observes daylight saving time even though most of Arizona does not.

Flowing northward along the Pacific coast of South America, this cold, nutrient-rich seawater flow supports abundant marine life and contributes to fog along the region’s arid shores. What is this ocean circulation called?

The Humboldt Current helps produce camanchaca fog along the coast of this exceptionally dry Chilean region, while the Andes create a rain shadow to its east. Mining cities such as Iquique and Antofagasta are located within it; what is this region called?

This arm of the Mediterranean lies between mainland Greece and Turkey, and its island groups include the Cyclades and Sporades. At its northeastern end, the Dardanelles provides a passage toward the Sea of Marmara; what sea is described?

The Aegean Sea connects to the Sea of Marmara through this narrow strait, whose western shore includes the Gallipoli Peninsula and whose eastern side lies in northwestern Turkey. What is this waterway called?

Located at the southern tip of Florida, this protected wilderness preserves a vast subtropical wetland of sawgrass marshes, mangrove forests, and coastal habitats. It is also known for protecting a rare region where American alligators and American crocodiles coexist. What protected area is it?

At the southern edge of Everglades National Park, this shallow tropical lagoon is dotted with mangrove islands and lies between the mainland and the chain of islands extending southwest from Miami. What is this large bay called?

This Austrian city is both the country’s capital and one of its nine states, and its historic center became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2001. It developed from a Roman military settlement on the Danube and served for centuries as a Habsburg imperial seat. What city is it?

At the Congress of Vienna, this Austrian statesman chaired negotiations that redrew Europe after Napoleon’s defeat and promoted a conservative balance of power. He later resigned during the Revolutions of 1848. Who was he?

Vienna stands on this river, which also passes through Budapest and Belgrade before emptying into the Black Sea. It rises in Germany’s Black Forest and flows eastward across Central and southeastern Europe. Name the river.
The Roman military settlement from which Vienna developed bore this Latin name. Established in the 1st century, it received Roman city rights in 212. What was this settlement called?
At 6,684 feet, this North Carolina summit is the highest point east of the Mississippi River and lies within the Black Mountains. What is its name?
Mount Mitchell belongs to which rugged subrange of the southern Appalachians, located in western North Carolina and containing several of the highest peaks in the eastern United States?

These large natural elevations usually have steep sides and may occur in long ranges, though some stand alone. Tectonic uplift, faulting, and volcanism can build them, while their height often creates colder ecosystems and leeward rain shadows; what landforms are they?

Among Earth's mountains, which summit is recognized as the highest point above mean sea level? It lies in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border, and a joint 2020 measurement put its elevation at 8,848.86 meters.
Which named mountain on Mars is the tallest known on any planet in the Solar System? A gigantic shield volcano in the Tharsis region, it rises about 22 kilometers above the surrounding plains.

Which Hawaiian mountain is often called Earth's tallest when measured from its base on the ocean floor rather than from sea level? Its dormant volcanic summit on the Big Island rises about 4,207 meters above sea level, while its base extends far below the Pacific.
Which landlocked South American country lies north of Argentina, borders Bolivia and Brazil, and has Asunción as its capital?
In Paraguay, which river forms part of the border with Brazil and is crossed by the binational Itaipu Dam?

This federal republic in southern South America is the continent’s second-largest country by area. Its territory includes the Pampas, Patagonia, and part of Tierra del Fuego, and its capital and largest city is Buenos Aires. What country is it?

Along Argentina’s western side, the Andes form a long international boundary with a narrow Pacific-facing country. The two countries also share Patagonia and divided Tierra del Fuego under an 1881 boundary treaty. Which country is it?

Argentina shares a short northeastern border with this Portuguese-speaking South American country, the continent’s largest by area. The Iguazú Falls region lies near where its border with Argentina approaches Paraguay. Which country is it?
Argentina faces this small South American republic across the Río de la Plata, with Buenos Aires opposite its capital, Montevideo. Its territory also has an Atlantic coastline. Which country is it?
Argentina’s northern boundary meets this landlocked Andean country. Its constitutional capital is Sucre, while La Paz serves as its seat of government. Which country is it?
Rising in Colorado’s Rocky Mountains, this river runs through Tulsa and Little Rock before meeting the Mississippi near the former settlement of Napoleon. What river is it?
The Arkansas River passes through this Oklahoma city, home to Oral Roberts University and the historic Greenwood District, once known as Black Wall Street. Which city is it?

This is the largest country in South America, occupying roughly half the continent and stretching across much of its eastern and central regions. It has an Atlantic coastline and borders every South American country except Chile and Ecuador. What country is it?

Brazil’s federal capital was inaugurated in 1960 as a purpose-built inland city in the country’s Federal District. Its urban plan was designed by Lúcio Costa, and many of its landmark government buildings were designed by Oscar Niemeyer. What is the capital?
Brazil contains most of the basin of this river, which carries more water than any other river system in the world. Near Manaus, its dark-water tributary the Rio Negro joins it. What river is it?
Brazil’s eastern coastline, about 7,500 kilometers long, faces this ocean. It lies between South America and Africa. Which ocean is it?
Brazil’s highest summit rises to nearly 3,000 meters in Amazonas state, close to the Venezuelan border. It is part of the Serra do Imeri. What is the mountain’s name?

Crossed by the Equator and ranked as the world’s third-largest island, this Southeast Asian landmass is shared by Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei. What island is known for tropical rainforests and Bornean orangutans?
Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei share Borneo, but the island’s Indonesian portion is commonly known by a different regional name. What is that name?

This broad South American region is centered on the basin of the continent’s largest river and includes tropical rainforest and surrounding landscapes across several countries. It extends well beyond Brazil, encompassing substantial areas of Peru and Colombia. What is its natural name?

Within Amazonia, which river carries more water by average discharge than any other river on Earth and flows east across northern South America to the Atlantic? Near Manaus, it meets the Rio Negro, whose dark waters remain visibly distinct for a stretch downstream. What is this river called?
This Gulf Coast state borders Texas, Arkansas, and Mississippi. Its capital is Baton Rouge, and its most populous city is New Orleans. What state is it?
Louisiana is the only U.S. state that uses a term rooted in its French and ecclesiastical heritage for its county-level political divisions. What are those divisions called?
Louisiana’s capital sits on the Mississippi River northwest of New Orleans. Its name translates from French as “red stick.” What city is it?
Louisiana’s legal tradition differs from the common-law system used in nearly every other U.S. state and reflects the influence of Napoleonic France. What legal system is this?

Built in Black Canyon as a key part of the Boulder Canyon Project, this concrete arch-gravity structure spans the Colorado River along the Nevada–Arizona border. It began impounding water in 1935 and was officially given its present name in 1947; what landmark is it?

Water began backing up behind Hoover Dam in February 1935, creating this vast reservoir on the Colorado River. Named for a former commissioner of the Bureau of Reclamation, it stretches across Nevada and Arizona; what is it called?

This Appalachian state joined the Union as its 35th state on June 20, 1863, after Unionist residents of its western counties organized a new state during the Civil War. Known as the Mountain State, it includes Spruce Knob, the highest point in the state.
In West Virginia, a summit in Pendleton County rises to 4,861 feet, making it the state’s highest point. What is the summit’s name?
This five-sided federal building stands in Arlington, Virginia, across the Potomac River from Washington, D.C. It serves as the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense. What landmark is it?
Construction of the Pentagon during World War II displaced this African American neighborhood in East Arlington, along with other residents. What community was displaced?
This English city stands where the River Cherwell meets the Thames and is home to a university whose scholars were involved in a notorious town-and-gown clash in 1209. Which city is it?

In 1209, scholars left Oxford after a violent dispute with townspeople, and some settled in another English city to establish a rival university. Which city on the River Cam became the home of that institution?

Located on Cuba’s northern coast along the Straits of Florida, this port city is the country’s capital and largest urban center. What city was the setting for the attack on the Presidential Palace during the Cuban Revolution?

In Havana, student members of the Revolutionary Directorate stormed this former seat of government on March 13, 1957, in an unsuccessful attempt to kill Fulgencio Batista. The building now houses the Museum of the Revolution; what was it called?
Which southeastern U.S. state has Atlanta as its capital, borders Florida to the south, and meets the Atlantic Ocean along its eastern edge?
In Georgia, which city is both the state capital and its largest city, and hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics?
Georgia’s first permanent British colonial settlement was founded in 1733 beside a river of the same name. What historic coastal city was laid out by James Oglethorpe?
Georgia’s northeastern highlands include this Appalachian subrange, which contains Brasstown Bald, the state’s highest point. What is this subrange called?
Georgia’s colonial predecessor was established in 1732 under James Oglethorpe’s trusteeship. What was the name of this last-founded and southernmost of the original Thirteen Colonies?
This North African kingdom has its capital at Rabat and coastlines along both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. What country is it?
In Morocco’s High Atlas range, this 4,167-metre summit is the highest peak in North Africa. What is its name?

This French-speaking Central African country spans much of the basin drained by Africa’s second-longest river and has a short coastline on the Atlantic Ocean. Its capital, Kinshasa, lies across that river from Brazzaville.

An urban legend about a 1998 football match claims that a single lightning flash killed all eleven players on one team. In what area of the Democratic Republic of the Congo was the match supposedly played?

In northern Greece, this major port lies at the head of the Thermaic Gulf and is the largest city in the historic region of Macedonia. It ranks second among Greek cities by population. What city is it?
Thessaloniki sits at the northwestern end of this Aegean inlet, which is bounded to the east by the Chalkidiki peninsula and opens into the northern Aegean. What gulf is it?
The second line of “Take Me Home, Country Roads” pairs the Blue Ridge Mountains with this Virginia waterway. It is the largest tributary of the Potomac; what river is it?
