In the context of Seven, which common Western scale has the interval pattern whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half, returning to its tonic at the octave?
In regression, what method chooses model parameters by minimizing the sum of the squared differences between observed values and predicted values?
The least squares method was first published in 1805 in a treatise on determining comet orbits. Which French mathematician authored *Nouvelles méthodes pour la détermination des orbites des comètes*?
A classic mechanics question asks which path lets a frictionless bead, released from rest under gravity, travel between two fixed points in the least time. What is this question called?

During the historical challenge involving the Brachistochrone Problem, which English physicist submitted a solution and later formulated the three laws of motion, including the law of action and reaction?

This conjecture extends the condition that nontrivial zeros of the zeta function lie on the vertical line with real part one-half to a broad family of arithmetic L-series. What is this conjecture called?

The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis applies beyond ζ(s) to the analytic continuations of series whose coefficients are periodic, completely multiplicative arithmetic characters modulo an integer. What is the standard name for this family?
In plane geometry, this segment in a triangle joins one vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. What is this segment called?
In a triangle, the three medians meet at one point, which lies two-thirds of the way along each median from its vertex. What is this point called?

In ordinary arithmetic, this operation combines addends to form a sum, and zero leaves any real number unchanged under it. Its real-number version is both commutative and associative, while related operations apply the same idea to equal-size matrices and directed displacements. What is this mathematical operation?

When using Addition to combine two directed vectors, one graphical construction places the starting point of the second arrow at the endpoint of the first. The resultant runs from the starting point of the first arrow to the endpoint of the second; what is this construction called?

Contestants choose clues from a board, but each clue is presented as a statement of information and their responses must be phrased as questions. What Merv Griffin-created American television quiz show uses this distinctive format?
On Jeopardy!, which Canadian-born host led the syndicated version from its 1984 premiere until 2020, becoming its longest-serving and most recognizable emcee?
In Hayao Miyazaki’s animated film *My Neighbor Totoro*, this magical, many-legged vehicle carries the sisters through the countryside and serves as a major supporting character. What is it called?
The Catbus appears in a 1988 animated film about sisters Satsuki and Mei encountering forest spirits after moving to the countryside. Which filmmaker wrote and directed the film?
Released on May 21, 2021, this 11-track debut studio album includes “drivers license,” “deja vu,” and “good 4 u.” It later won the 2022 Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album; what is the album?

On SOUR, which closing track turns toward people Olivia Rodrigo once knew who faced hardship, giving the album a compassionate ending? Rather than centering on a breakup, its lyrics offer reassurance to those people.

What dance-oriented popular genre rose to prominence in the 1970s and became closely associated with nightclubs, dance floors, and mirrored spinning ornaments overhead? Its club culture and fashion were depicted in the film *Saturday Night Fever*.

Which partner dance inspired dramatic dips in some disco music dance routines? Astor Piazzolla composed music for this dance, which developed in dance halls along the Río de la Plata and is traditionally associated with the bandoneón.

Amateur home cooks meet under a marquee to prepare breads, pastries, and desserts in three rounds each week: one based on their own recipe, one following sparse directions, and one featuring an elaborate centerpiece. Judges Paul Hollywood and Prue Leith name a standout contestant and send one person home each week. What is this reality competition called?

On The Great British Bake Off, contestants receive the same recipe, written by a judge and often offering sparse directions, and attempt to produce the assigned item without choosing their own design. What is this weekly round called?

Released in 1985 on *Hounds of Love*, which Kate Bush single pairs a pulsing synth arrangement with a plea to trade places with another person? The track later surged back onto charts after it featured in the fourth season of *Stranger Things*.

Which Netflix series featured Kate Bush’s “Running Up That Hill” as Max Mayfield’s lifeline in its fourth season, helping the 1985 song surge back onto charts? Set in Hawkins, Indiana, this supernatural drama follows a group of young friends battling threats connected to the Upside Down.

This Icelandic singer-songwriter first gained wider recognition as a member of an alternative rock group that broke internationally with “Birthday.” After the group split, she became known for adventurous solo records and surreal music videos, including the Michel Gondry-directed clip for “Human Behaviour.” Who is she?

Björk was a member of this Icelandic alternative-rock group, whose 1988 album *Life’s Too Good* introduced its sound to international audiences and included the songs “Birthday” and “Motorcrash.” What was the group called?
Which American filmmaking duo co-directed Fargo, No Country for Old Men, and True Grit? Their acclaimed work made them influential figures in modern American cinema.

After the Coen brothers began working separately, Joel Coen directed a solo adaptation of which Shakespeare play? Its title character murders King Duncan in a bid to claim Scotland’s throne, and the film stars Denzel Washington and Frances McDormand.

This 2022 science-fiction horror film follows siblings OJ and Emerald Haywood as they run their family’s horse ranch in Agua Dulce, California. Their work is disrupted by a mysterious phenomenon in the sky. What is the film’s title?

In Nope, the mysterious sky phenomenon is at the center of a film written and directed by the filmmaker who also made Get Out and Us. Earlier in his career, he performed in a sketch-comedy partnership with Keegan-Michael Key. Who is he?

This American actor became globally famous as Captain Jack Sparrow in the Pirates of the Caribbean films and also played Edward Scissorhands and Willy Wonka. In a 2022 U.S. defamation case, a jury found that his former wife Amber Heard had defamed him; who is this actor?

Johnny Depp collaborated with this filmmaker on eight films, including Edward Scissorhands, Ed Wood, Sleepy Hollow, and Sweeney Todd. The director also made Beetlejuice and the 1989 film Batman; who is he?

Before Johnny Depp rose to teen-idol fame playing an undercover young police officer on a television series set in a high school, he made his feature-film debut in this 1984 slasher film. Its villain, Freddy Krueger, attacks teenagers in their dreams; what is the film?

In Westeros, these winged, fire-breathing beasts enabled Aegon the Conqueror and his sisters to forge the Targaryen realm. After vanishing for generations, three hatchlings of this kind emerged from eggs on Khal Drogo’s funeral pyre. What are these creatures called?

In *Game of Thrones*, which exiled daughter of Aerys II receives three petrified eggs as a wedding gift from Illyrio Mopatis and later hatches them in Khal Drogo’s funeral pyre, bringing dragons back into the world?

This filmmaking technique creates movement by photographing physical figures one frame at a time, shifting them slightly between exposures. When the frames are played in sequence, the figures appear to move. What is this technique?

In stop-motion animation, which 1993 dark fantasy musical directed by Henry Selick follows Jack Skellington, the skeletal ruler of Halloween Town, and his ghost dog, Zero? Its songs include “This Is Halloween” and “What’s This?”
Founded in Toronto by rapper Drake, producer Noah “40” Shebib, and executive Oliver El-Khatib, this record label and entertainment company is strongly associated with an owl emblem. What is its name?
Which Toronto producer and engineer, whose work helped shape the atmospheric sound of many Drake recordings, co-founded OVO Sound with Drake and Oliver El-Khatib?

Released for the Game Boy in 1992, this platform game introduced a round, pink hero whose first adventure is to recover the kingdom’s stolen food from its hammer-wielding ruler. What is the game’s title?
In Kirby's Dream Land, this ruler of Dream Land steals the kingdom’s food, setting Kirby’s adventure in motion. He wields a giant hammer and serves as the game’s final boss. Who is he?
Which film genre is centered on fear, dread, and disturbing or supernatural threats? It commonly uses jump scares and often overlaps with suspense and thriller films.

In which horror film does Chris visit his girlfriend’s family and undergo hypnosis that sends him to a dark void called the Sunken Place? He uncovers their scheme to transplant the brains of older white people into young Black bodies.
In LEGO Ninjago, this wise guide trains the ninja team, carries a staff, and is especially fond of tea. He is Lord Garmadon's younger brother and a son of Ninjago's ancient creator.
Master Wu and Lord Garmadon are sons of which ancient figure, credited with creating Ninjago and devising the martial art performed through tornado-like spins?
Born in Beirut and raised in Toronto, this Canadian actor became known for playing a hacker who takes the name Neo and a retired assassin seeking revenge. Who is he?
In this 2021 science-fiction film, Keanu Reeves returned as Neo, and Lana Wachowski directed while Carrie-Anne Moss reprised her role as Trinity. What is the film’s title?

What term names a book-length work that presents an extended narrative through sequential visual panels combined with text? Unlike a single comic strip, it develops its story on a sustained, book-length scale.

Which graphic novel by Alan Moore and Dave Gibbons features Adrian Veidt teleporting a gigantic squid into New York City in an attempt to avert nuclear war? Its masked characters include Rorschach, Doctor Manhattan, and Silk Spectre.

This English guitarist became an in-demand London session musician before joining the Yardbirds in 1966. He later co-founded Led Zeppelin and used a bow on his guitar during the recording of “Whole Lotta Love.” Who is he?

Jimmy Page co-founded this English rock band with Robert Plant, John Paul Jones, and John Bonham after the Yardbirds dissolved. The band recorded “Immigrant Song” and “Stairway to Heaven.” What is its name?
This animated comedy series follows an optimistic sea sponge who lives in a pineapple in Bikini Bottom and works as a fry cook at the Krusty Krab. What is the series called?
In SpongeBob SquarePants, this pufferfish runs the local boating school and gives the title character repeated driving lessons. What is her name?
Released in 1954 and directed by Elia Kazan, this drama follows dockworker Terry Malloy as he decides to testify against corrupt union boss Johnny Friendly. What film is it?
In On the Waterfront, Terry Malloy’s hopes for an athletic career are ruined after he is pressured into deliberately losing an important match. What sport did he compete in?
What cinematic visual style is shared by The Tragedy of Macbeth, The Lighthouse, and Passing, rendering scenes through tonal gradations without color hues?

Which filmmaker directed The Tragedy of Macbeth as a black-and-white film, with Denzel Washington as Macbeth and Frances McDormand as Lady Macbeth? The 2021 adaptation was his first feature made without the brother with whom he co-directed Fargo and No Country for Old Men.
This American film director helmed the screwball comedies Bringing Up Baby and His Girl Friday, then directed the western Rio Bravo. Who was this filmmaker?
Howard Hawks directed this 1932 crime film about a ruthless Chicago gangster; its 1983 remake starred Al Pacino as Cuban drug lord Tony Montana. What is the original film’s title?

Unlike passive films, these interactive digital works let players give input through computers, consoles, mobile devices, and other electronic systems. The category includes titles such as Fortnite. What broad form of entertainment is this?

Among video games, which title developed by Epic Games became famous for its Battle Royale mode, where players land on an island and compete to be the last player or squad standing? Its modes also became known for allowing players to build structures during matches.
In Star Trek, what Starfleet rule forbids its officers from interfering with the natural development of alien civilizations? The policy shaped many of Captain Kirk’s decisions aboard the Enterprise.
The Prime Directive became a recurring source of conflict for Captain Kirk and his Enterprise crew. Which Star Trek producer is credited with establishing this rule for the series?

This HBO teen drama, created by Sam Levinson, centers on Rue Bennett as she navigates addiction and reconnects with classmates in East Highland. Its stories explore high-school relationships, identity, and the consequences of risky choices. What is the series called?

In Euphoria, which performer portrays Rue Bennett, whose struggles with addiction shape much of the series? She also played MJ in Spider-Man: Homecoming and Rocky Blue on the Disney Channel series Shake It Up.

This pop track pairs its vocals with sampled dialogue from the episode “Threat Level Midnight” of The Office. Its lyrics include the line “My doctors can’t explain my symptoms or my pain”; what is the song’s title?

My Strange Addiction, which samples dialogue from The Office episode “Threat Level Midnight,” appears on the 2019 album When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go? The performer also released the chart-topping single “Bad Guy”; who is she?

This filmmaker grew up in Modesto, California, and studied film at the University of Southern California. He expanded his student short “Electronic Labyrinth: THX 1138 4EB” into his feature-film debut, then directed a 1973 coming-of-age movie about teenagers cruising California streets.

George Lucas directed this 1973 ensemble film, set over one night in 1962, about recent high-school graduates cruising their California town before heading off to college. Its cast includes Richard Dreyfuss and Ron Howard, and its rock-and-roll soundtrack helped evoke the era.

Which American mockumentary sitcom follows employees at the Scranton branch of the fictional paper supplier Dunder Mifflin, with manager Michael Scott and salesmen Jim Halpert and Dwight Schrute among its central characters?
In The Office, what Pennsylvania bed-and-breakfast does Dwight operate on his family’s beet-growing estate, offering guests an unusual agritourism stay?

This English actor succeeded David Tennant as the Eleventh Doctor in Doctor Who and later played Daemon Targaryen in House of the Dragon. He also portrayed a vampire antagonist in the 2022 film Morbius. Who is he?

This American entertainment company began as a DVD-by-mail rental business in the late 1990s and launched its streaming service in 2007. Today, it distributes original and acquired films and television programs to subscribers around the world. What company is it?

question: What Netflix comedy-drama adapts Piper Kerman’s memoir and follows a New Yorker sent to Litchfield Penitentiary for a crime connected to a former relationship? Its ensemble portrays the friendships, rivalries, and daily routines of women incarcerated in a federal prison.

Which American stand-up comedian and UFC commentator hosts a long-running interview podcast that became one of the most prominent shows in digital media? His career also spans live comedy and mixed martial arts broadcasting.

This fictional archaeologist and adventurer searches for ancient artifacts in a series of action-adventure films. Portrayed by Harrison Ford, he is known for wearing a fedora and wielding a bullwhip. Who is he?

What Disney screen-adaptation franchise is anchored by a 1992 animated musical featuring a magic lamp and the song “A Whole New World,” and also includes a 2019 live-action remake starring Will Smith as the lamp’s wish-granting spirit?

Which Netflix comedy-drama, created by and starring Aziz Ansari, centers on Dev Shah, an actor navigating work and relationships in New York? Its second season sends Dev to Italy to study pasta-making after a breakup.

What kind of publication tells a story through framed illustrations combined with text, often using speech balloons for dialogue and captions for narration? The arrangement of its images can control pacing, while written effects such as “WHAM” can represent sounds.

This Disney musical follows Jane and Michael Banks after a magical nanny arrives at their London home, where she makes everyday chores feel enchanting. What is the title of the film?
In Mary Poppins, what Cockney chimney sweep befriends Jane and Michael Banks and joins them in the rooftop dance number “Step in Time”?

Created by David Shore, this American medical drama follows Shaun Murphy, an autistic surgical resident with savant syndrome, as he joins the staff of San Jose St. Bonaventure Hospital. What series is it?
In The Good Doctor, which English actor portrays Shaun Murphy? He also played Norman Bates in the television series Bates Motel.

This Asgardian prince, portrayed by Tom Hiddleston in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, is known for magic, shapeshifting, and schemes that repeatedly entangle Thor. He later becomes the central figure in a Marvel series about branching timelines and a temporal bureaucracy; name this trickster god.

In the television series Loki, this organization captures people whose actions create unauthorized branches in the one approved history and processes them in a retro-futurist bureaucracy. Its field agents include Mobius M. Mobius and Hunter B-15; what is the organization called?

Developed by Innersloth, this multiplayer social-deduction game pits crewmates completing tasks against hidden impostors who sabotage the ship and eliminate players. What game became a major online sensation?
In Among Us, what is the name of the original spaceship map, featuring locations such as Cafeteria, Admin, and Electrical? It came before maps including MIRA HQ, Polus, and the Airship.
This Austrian-born bodybuilding champion won the Mr. Olympia title seven times before becoming an action-film star and serving as governor of California from 2003 to 2011. Who is he?
Which 1984 science-fiction action film starring Arnold Schwarzenegger follows a cyborg sent from the future to kill Sarah Connor, while Kyle Reese travels back to protect her?
Released in 2019, this satirical coming-of-age film follows a German boy in the Jungvolk whose imaginary friend is a comic version of Adolf Hitler. What film did Taika Waititi direct?
Which New Zealand filmmaker directed Jojo Rabbit and also played the boy’s comically imagined Hitler companion? He later won an Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay for the film.

In this Nintendo crossover fighting-game series, stars such as Mario, Link, Kirby, and Pikachu meet on platforming stages instead of remaining in their own game worlds. Rather than depleting a conventional health bar, players build up damage percentages and try to launch opponents off the stage. What is this series?
The original Super Smash Bros. debuted in 1999 on the Nintendo home console that launched with Super Mario 64 and Pilotwings 64. What console was it?

This British actor played Chris Washington in Get Out and OJ Haywood in Nope. He won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for portraying Black Panther Party leader Fred Hampton in a 2021 biographical drama. Who is he?

Daniel Kaluuya earned the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for playing Fred Hampton in this 2021 film directed by Shaka King. The drama also stars LaKeith Stanfield as FBI informant Bill O’Neal and depicts the FBI’s infiltration of the Illinois chapter of the Panther Party. What is the film?

This fictional pirate captain is known for his distinctive swagger, eccentric manner, and pursuit of the Black Pearl. Portrayed by Johnny Depp, he anchors a film series that began with a 2003 adventure inspired by a theme-park attraction. Who is this character?

Jack Sparrow is the eccentric captain at the center of this Disney adventure-film franchise, whose first installment introduced the cursed crew of the Black Pearl and featured Geoffrey Rush as Barbossa. What is the name of the franchise?
This adventure game follows a journalist who catches sentient creatures combining animal traits with food. What game is set on Snaktooth Island?

In Bugsnax, a journalist investigates the disappearance of explorer Elizabert Megafig and encounters creatures that blend animal and food characteristics. What is the island where the investigation takes place called?

Formed in Paris in 1993, this French electronic duo paired Thomas Bangalter with Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo and helped bring French house to a wider audience. The duo became known for robot helmets and albums such as Homework and Discovery before announcing its end in 2021. Which duo is this?

Daft Punk released this 2013 album featuring Pharrell Williams on “Get Lucky” and “Lose Yourself to Dance,” as well as Giorgio Moroder’s spoken-word contribution on “Giorgio by Moroder.” It won the 2014 Grammy Award for Album of the Year. What is the album’s title?

A Japanese narrative genre centers on a protagonist who is transported, reincarnated, or summoned from ordinary life into a separate world, often one with fantasy rules. Its name literally means “another world.” What is this genre called?
In the isekai series Re:Zero, Subaru finds that dying sends him to an earlier point in events, while he retains memories of what happened. What is the name of this ability?

In Fallout lore, what paramilitary order was founded by Captain Roger Maxson after he exposed unethical experiments at the Mariposa military base? Its members became known for recovering and controlling powerful pre-war technology.

During its campaign in the Capital Wasteland, the Brotherhood of Steel reactivates a colossal pre-war combat robot that attacks with a laser weapon and nuclear-powered explosives. What is this robot called?

What broad term describes Japanese animation across both television series and films? Its best-known examples include a ninja’s quest to lead his village, a martial-arts saga featuring Saiyan warriors, and a story about siblings battling demons in Taisho-era Japan.
In anime, which Japanese filmmaker directed the 2001 film *Spirited Away*, about a girl trapped in a spirit world, and co-founded Studio Ghibli with Isao Takahata?

Which Montreal-born Canadian singer-songwriter and poet also published novels and wrote both “Hallelujah” and “You Want It Darker”? His estate objected when the 2020 Republican National Convention used one of his songs without permission.

Leonard Cohen first released this song on his 1984 album *Various Positions*, which Columbia initially declined to release in the United States. A later recording by Jeff Buckley helped bring the song to a much wider audience; what is its title?

What stage name belongs to the British-American rapper born Shéyaa Bin Abraham-Joseph, whose solo hit “Bank Account” helped establish his profile and who later appeared on Drake’s “Knife Talk” and “Jimmy Cooks”?

On 21 Savage’s collaborative 2016 EP *Savage Mode*, what Atlanta producer shared billing with the rapper and helped shape its dark, minimalist sound? He later reunited with 21 Savage for *Savage Mode II*.

Formed in Liverpool, this influential English rock band became a national sensation in the UK in 1963 and helped lead the British Invasion the following year. Its best-known lineup featured John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr, and it made its first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show in February 1964. What band was it?

On this 1969 Beatles album, most of the second side is a medley that includes “Mean Mr. Mustard” and “Polythene Pam.” Its cover shows the four bandmembers crossing a London street, and the album also features “Come Together” and “Here Comes the Sun.” What is the album?
What Nintendo-originated multimedia franchise began with role-playing games released in Japan in 1996 and expanded into stories about collecting, training, and battling fictional creatures?
In the Pokémon video games, what region based on Japan’s Hokkaido island is the setting of Pokémon Diamond and Pearl? Its legendary Pokémon include Dialga and Palkia.

The actor who portrayed T’Challa in *Black Panther* privately battled stage III colon cancer for four years before passing away on August 28, 2020. His passing prompted ABC to air the film without commercials; what event is described?

In the statement released after Chadwick Boseman’s death, his family said his 2016 diagnosis had advanced from stage III to stage IV over four years and affected the large intestine. What illness did they identify?

In DC Comics, this character’s identity and backstory have varied across tellings; Alan Moore and Brian Bolland’s graphic novel *The Killing Joke* depicts one possible origin involving a failed comedian and a vat of chemicals. Known as Batman’s clown-themed arch-enemy, who is he?

In Batman comics, the Joker is repeatedly confined in this Gotham institution for the criminally insane, where doctors such as Harleen Quinzel have worked. Grant Morrison and Dave McKean’s graphic novel about it is subtitled *A Serious House on Serious Earth*; name the institution.
Which American singer-songwriter recorded both “American Pie,” a long-form hit recalling the early rock-and-roll era, and “Vincent,” a ballad inspired by a Dutch painter?

Don McLean’s 1971 song “American Pie” recalls the 1959 plane crash that killed Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and the Big Bopper. What evocative phrase from the song became a common nickname for the tragedy?

Lil Nas X released this 2021 single with a music video that opens in a surreal garden, follows a pole descent into the underworld, and ends with a dramatic confrontation with its ruler. What is the song’s full title?

In the music video for “MONTERO (Call Me by Your Name),” Lil Nas X descends a pole into an underworld and gives a lap dance to a horned ruler before killing him and taking his place. Which figure from Christian tradition is portrayed as that ruler?
Which New York rock band released the 2001 debut album *Is This It* and the 2020 album *The New Abnormal*, featuring songs such as “Brooklyn Bridge to Chorus” and “Ode to the Mets”?

The Strokes’ frontman Julian Casablancas sang on “Instant Crush,” a track from this French electronic duo’s 2013 album *Random Access Memories*. The duo also recorded “One More Time” and “Get Lucky.” Which duo is it?

Which 2017 American supernatural thriller adapts a Japanese manga and anime about a notebook that can kill people whose names are written in it? Directed by Adam Wingard, the film relocates the story to Seattle and centers on high-school student Light Turner.
Which streaming service took over the 2017 Death Note film after acquiring its rights from Warner Bros.? The same service released House of Cards as its first original television series.
Born in South Africa, this technology entrepreneur founded SpaceX and leads Tesla. He also acquired Twitter, the social-media platform later renamed X. Who is he?
After Elon Musk acquired Twitter, the platform was rebranded with a single-letter name. What is the platform called now?

Founded by Nate Silver during the 2008 election cycle, this data-driven website became known for combining polling data and statistical models to publish election forecasts. It later expanded into broader data journalism. What is its name?
FiveThirtyEight’s founder first gained prominence in baseball analytics by creating PECOTA, a system for projecting player performance. Who is this statistician and election analyst?

This American chef and television personality became well known as a judge on a Food Network cooking competition built around mystery-basket ingredients. He also hosted that franchise’s dessert-focused spin-off and is known for his aversion to raw onions. Who is he?
Scott Conant hosted this Food Network dessert-focused spin-off of a cooking competition built around mystery-basket ingredients. What is the title of the series?
Which influential American hip-hop group featured Q-Tip, Phife Dawg, Ali Shaheed Muhammad, and Jarobi White? Its jazz-inflected 1991 album The Low End Theory helped define its distinctive sound.
On A Tribe Called Quest’s track “Verses from the Abstract,” which acclaimed jazz double bassist performs on the recording? He was also a member of Miles Davis’s Second Great Quintet.
In Marvel Comics, what superhero team was founded by Charles Xavier to promote peaceful coexistence between mutants and humans? Its members use their powers to protect a world that often fears them.
Within the X-Men, which mutant serves as a longtime field leader and controls his powerful optic blasts with a ruby-quartz visor?

This social-networking service launched on February 4, 2004, as a directory for Harvard students, helping them find classmates and add friends before expanding beyond campus. What platform launched that day?

In the Facebook data-privacy controversy, the FTC filed a complaint alleging that this political consulting firm used deceptive tactics to obtain users’ information for voter profiling and targeting. Which firm was named?
This American singer-songwriter and pianist performed with Wiz Khalifa on the soundtrack hit “See You Again,” and later scored a solo hit with “Attention.” Who is this artist?
Charlie Puth released his second studio album in 2018, following his debut album *Nine Track Mind*. The record includes “Attention” and “How Long”; what is its title?

Which American actor played Frodo Baggins in Peter Jackson’s film trilogy based on J.R.R. Tolkien’s novels? In 2020, he also became a memorable visitor to a player’s island in a social simulation game, where he sold turnips.

In 2020, Elijah Wood visited a player’s island to sell turnips in this Nintendo life-simulation series. Its March 2020 release, New Horizons, lets players build homes, trade items, and interact with anthropomorphic villagers. What is the series?

Released in 1957, this Swedish film by Ingmar Bergman follows knight Antonius Block during the Black Plague as he challenges a supernatural opponent to chess in hopes of delaying his fate. What is the film’s title?
In The Seventh Seal, Antonius Block encounters a pale, black-clad figure during the plague and plays chess against this personification of life’s end, hoping to buy time. What is the figure’s name?

What 2005 film adapts an Alan Moore and David Lloyd graphic novel about a masked anarchist who draws Evey Hammond into resistance against a totalitarian British government? Natalie Portman plays Evey, while Hugo Weaving performs the masked character.

In V for Vendetta, which actress plays Evey Hammond, a young woman drawn into the fight against a totalitarian regime? She also played Padmé Amidala in the Star Wars prequel films and Jacqueline Kennedy in Jackie.

An Egyptian actor became internationally known for playing Sherif Ali, the tribal leader who allies with T. E. Lawrence in David Lean’s desert epic. He later played the title character in Lean’s adaptation of Boris Pasternak’s novel about a physician-poet caught in revolutionary Russia. Who is this actor?

Omar Sharif made his international breakthrough playing Sherif Ali opposite Peter O’Toole’s portrayal of the British officer who helped unite Arab forces during World War I in this David Lean epic. What film is known for its desert setting and sweeping cinematography?

This viral catchphrase emerged around a 2022 superhero film starring Jared Leto as a scientist who becomes a living vampire. It parodies the kind of shouted transformation cue associated with the Power Rangers; what is the phrase?

The meme phrase “It's Morbin' Time” became associated with a 2022 film, although its star never says it onscreen. What Marvel antihero—a biochemist who becomes a living vampire—is the film’s title character, played by Jared Leto?
This strategy game series centers on defending a settlement from a fluid-like enemy that spreads across the map in advancing waves. What is the series called?
In Creeper World, players build defenses to protect this settlement from being overrun by the advancing fluid-like enemy. What is the city’s name?

In this NBC fantasy sitcom, four deceased humans find themselves in an apparently idyllic afterlife neighborhood, where an ethics professor tries to help a woman who was mistakenly admitted become a better person. Their attempts at moral improvement eventually become entangled with a larger scheme involving the afterlife. What show is this?
In The Good Place, what is the name of the Senegalese ethics professor who tutors Eleanor in moral philosophy? His chronic indecision makes even ordinary choices agonizing for him.

This British radio DJ and television presenter chaired *Top of the Pops* for decades and hosted a children’s wish-fulfillment show on BBC One. After his death in 2011, allegations of extensive sexual abuse made him the center of a major scandal in the United Kingdom. Who was he?

After ITV broadcast *Exposure: The Other Side of Jimmy Savile* in October 2012, the Metropolitan Police launched an inquiry into the allegations that soon widened to include other prominent figures. By what name was this investigation known?
On TikTok, this personalized feed selects videos using signals from a user's activity and preferences. It is presented separately from the feed devoted to accounts that user follows.
TikTok's For You Page is populated by a recommendation system operated by the company that owns TikTok. Founded in Beijing in 2012, this company also operates the Chinese counterpart Douyin.
This American director began his career designing sets and costumes for Broadway before becoming a filmmaker at MGM. He directed Gene Kelly in both *An American in Paris* and *Brigadoon*; who was he?

Vincente Minnelli directed this 1958 musical adaptation of a Colette novella, starring Leslie Caron as a young woman in Paris and featuring Maurice Chevalier singing “Thank Heaven for Little Girls.” Which film won the Academy Award for Best Picture?
What 1979 Ridley Scott science-fiction horror film follows the crew of a commercial ore ship after they investigate a mysterious signal and face a rapidly growing extraterrestrial threat aboard?
In Alien, what is the name of the commercial spaceship carrying ore whose crew investigates a signal and later struggles to survive after an organism gets aboard?
A streaming app can send recorded songs to someone’s headphones or speakers, where the tracks play on demand. What common activity is being described?

Released in 2016 as a swipe-through year-end story by a major streaming platform, this personalized recap tallies a listener’s top artists and songs, total minutes, and other patterns from listening to music. What is this feature called?
Released in 1983, this Eurythmics single pairs a prominent sequenced synthesizer riff with a stark drum-machine pulse and became the duo’s first U.S. Billboard Hot 100 number-one. What is the song?

On Sweet Dreams, this Eurythmics member delivers the lead vocal in a striking style featured in the song’s stark music video. She later released the solo album *Diva* and sang the Oscar-winning song “Into the West.” Who is she?

Released by Disney in 2013, this animated musical follows royal sisters Elsa and Anna in the kingdom of Arendelle. Its characters include a magically animated snowman and a mountain man who travels with a reindeer. What is the film’s title?
In Frozen, the actor who voices Kristoff also originated King George III in the original Broadway cast of Hamilton. Who is this actor?

Founded by two brothers in 1923 after a distribution contract for the Alice Comedies, this American entertainment company grew from an animation studio into a business spanning films, television, theme parks, resorts, and cruises. What is it?
The Walt Disney Company’s best-known cartoon mouse rose to prominence in a 1928 short that helped establish synchronized sound in animation. What was the short’s title?

This Cartoon Network animated series follows a blue cat and his adopted goldfish brother through surreal adventures in Elmore. Its supporting cast appears in a mix of animation styles. What is the series called?
The Amazing World of Gumball was created by a French animator who developed its premise from characters he had designed for rejected Cartoon Network Europe advertising pitches. Who is he?
Released in 2019, this is Harry Styles’s second solo studio album, following his self-titled debut. Its track list includes the singles “Watermelon Sugar” and “Adore You”; what is the album called?
On Harry Styles’s Fine Line, this track features lyrics about tasting strawberries on a summer evening and became the album’s first U.S. number-one single. What song is it?

This Beatles recording was released in 1967 and famously assembled from two takes recorded in different keys and tempos, using tape-speed changes to make them fit. John Lennon drew on childhood memories of a Salvation Army children’s home in Liverpool while writing it; what song is it?

On the Beatles’ “Strawberry Fields Forever,” the opening flute-like melody was created with a keyboard instrument that plays recorded tape loops rather than generating conventional notes. What instrument supplies that sound?

In The Lost Levels, this Nintendo character can jump higher than Mario, though he is harder to control. He also stars in a series of games about exploring haunted mansions. What is the name of Mario’s younger brother?
In the original 2001 Luigi’s Mansion, Professor E. Gadd equips Luigi with a modified vacuum cleaner for capturing ghosts. What is this device called?

In this collaborative horror-fiction setting, a secretive institution documents and contains paranormal objects, entities, and phenomena, often presenting them in clinical case-file entries. What is the name of that fictional organization?

Within the SCP Foundation, which tall, thin internet-folklore figure inspired SCP-582, an entity whose properties change according to stories written about it? Creatures found in Minecraft’s End are also partly inspired by this character.

This American reality series brings young home cooks into a competition kitchen to complete culinary challenges and have their dishes judged. It is the children’s spin-off of a cooking franchise whose U.S. judging panel includes a famously blunt British chef. What is the series called?

In MasterChef Junior, which British chef serves as a judge on the American version and also hosts Hell’s Kitchen and Kitchen Nightmares? He also appeared on Hot Ones, where he sampled ten increasingly spicy chicken wings.
In a Cartoon Network series with a mixed-media cast, which blue cat is the older brother of a pink rabbit named Anais and the adopted brother of an orange fish named Darwin?
Gumball Watterson’s family lives in a fictional town where the series combines hand-drawn, CGI, stop-motion, and live-action characters. What is the name of that town?
Which digital communication platform shifted its 2020 motto from “Chat for Gamers” to “Your place to talk”? It organizes online communities into servers with separate text, voice, and video channels.

Which videoconferencing service became widely popular during the COVID-19 pandemic and was often used alongside Discord for online gatherings? After early criticism of its digital security, it paused work on non-security features for 90 days to address concerns.

Which American rapper and actor, born Lesane Parish Crooks, made his film debut as Bishop in the 1992 crime drama *Juice*? His 1990s music and public rivalry with The Notorious B.I.G. made him a defining figure in hip-hop.
Tupac Shakur’s 1996 double album features “California Love,” “Ambitionz Az a Ridah,” and “I Ain’t Mad at Cha.” What is its title, which was also used for a 2017 biographical film about him?
Launched in 1996 with its headquarters in Doha, this Qatar-based broadcaster became a major international news network after beginning as an Arabic-language satellite news channel. What is its name?
For many years, this Palestinian-American journalist reported for Al Jazeera Arabic. She was killed while covering an Israeli military raid in Jenin in May 2022; who was she?

Released in 2017, this open-world action-adventure begins with its hero awakening after a century in the Shrine of Resurrection. He then explores Hyrule and confronts the aftermath of the Calamity. What game is it?
answer: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

question: In The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, what ancient tablet-like device lets Link view the map, take pictures, and use abilities such as Magnesis and Stasis?

Which 1952 musical follows silent-film star Don Lockwood and aspiring actress Kathy Selden as Hollywood makes the transition to talking pictures? It stars Gene Kelly, Donald O’Connor, and Debbie Reynolds, and features a comic dance number built around a diction lesson.
Singin’ in the Rain was co-directed by its star Gene Kelly and a filmmaker who later directed Charade and Two for the Road. Who was the other director?

This profession involves gathering, verifying, and presenting information about events through print, broadcast, and digital media. UNESCO describes it as a source of fact-based information and an independent watchdog in civic life. What is this profession and practice?

In journalism, which U.S. association publishes an ethics code that urges reporters to verify information, seek original sources, provide context, correct mistakes, and distinguish news from advertising?
Released in 1996, this was Tupac Shakur’s fourth studio album and his first double album. It features “California Love” and “2 of Amerikaz Most Wanted.” What is the album called?
All Eyez on Me was released through a label co-founded by Suge Knight and Dr. Dre, which also put out Dr. Dre’s The Chronic and Snoop Dogg’s Doggystyle. What was the label’s name?

In Fallout 4, this loyal German shepherd can be recruited shortly after the player reaches the Commonwealth, and he can track scents, find hidden items, and help in combat. The same name is used for canine companions in earlier entries in the series. What is this recurring companion called?
In Fallout 4, Dogmeat is found beside an abandoned service station along the road from Sanctuary Hills toward Concord. What is this location’s full in-game name?

This 2021 Ridley Scott historical drama depicts a judicial combat in medieval France, where the result was believed to reveal divine judgment. Matt Damon, Adam Driver, and Jodie Comer star in the film. What is its title?
In The Last Duel, which woman’s accusation against Jacques Le Gris prompts her husband to demand a judicial duel to settle the charge? Jodie Comer portrays her in the film.

An American internet entrepreneur, he co-founded a collaboratively edited online encyclopedia in 2001 with Larry Sanger. He later founded the fan-oriented wiki platform first called Wikia, now known as Fandom; who is he?

Jimmy Wales helped launch this online encyclopedia in 2001 with Larry Sanger, and it became a leading example of a volunteer-written nonprofit reference work. Its Women in Red project seeks to reduce the gender gap in biographies; what is the encyclopedia called?

At the 94th Academy Awards in March 2022, a presenter joked about the hairstyle of the wife of a famous actor by comparing it to G.I. Jane. The actor walked onto the stage and struck the presenter, then later won Best Actor. What is this widely discussed altercation called?

During the Will Smith–Chris Rock Oscars incident, the ceremony was held at a Hollywood venue at the Hollywood & Highland complex. It hosted the Academy Awards from 2002 to 2019 and again in 2022, and was renamed after previously carrying the name of a photography company. What is its current name?

Released in 1997 and directed by James Cameron, this romantic historical disaster film follows Jack Dawson and Rose DeWitt Bukater, whose relationship unfolds aboard a luxury British liner on its ill-fated maiden voyage. What is the film’s title?
In Titanic, which British actress portrays Rose DeWitt Bukater, the first-class passenger who falls in love with Jack Dawson? She later starred in Sense and Sensibility and The Reader.

This 1972 crime drama, adapted from Mario Puzo’s novel, follows the Corleone family as a New York crime boss’s son gradually assumes leadership of the family. It won the Academy Award for Best Picture for films released in 1972. What film is it?

In The Godfather, this youngest son of Don Vito returns from World War II as a decorated Marine and initially tells his family that their criminal business is not for him. He later takes control of the family and orders the simultaneous killing of its rivals. Who is he?

This Nickelodeon animated fantasy-adventure series follows a young Air Nomad who can master water, earth, fire, and air. After awakening from a century in an iceberg, he must help restore balance to a world threatened by the Fire Nation. What is the series?

In Avatar: The Last Airbender, the young hero is the only person capable of mastering all four elemental bending arts. What is the name of this Air Nomad, whose return gives the nations hope of ending the war?
What 2019 Taylor Swift studio album includes “Me!,” “You Need to Calm Down,” and “Miss Americana & the Heartbreak Prince”? It followed *Reputation* and preceded *folklore*.
Which singer released *Lover* in 2019, then released the albums *folklore* and *evermore* in 2020? She also directed a short film accompanying the 10-minute version of “All Too Well.”

Which 2011 film stars Brad Pitt as the Oakland Athletics’ general manager during the team’s effort to build a competitive roster using statistical analysis? It dramatizes the approach made famous by Michael Lewis’s book about the club.
In Moneyball, which Oakland Athletics general manager works to assemble a competitive team using statistical analysis despite the club’s limited budget? Brad Pitt portrays this real-life executive.

Founded in 1925, this American magazine became known for blending journalism and criticism with cartoons and short fiction. It devoted an entire issue to John Hersey’s account of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima. What is the magazine?

The New Yorker published fiction by this South African author for more than five decades, and she was selected to write a eulogy for Nelson Mandela. Her novels include July’s People, about the Smales family during upheaval in South Africa. Who is she?

Players in this video game genre coordinate button presses, taps, or dance steps with a song’s beat, often following visual cues such as scrolling notes or arrows. Famous examples include Guitar Hero and Dance Dance Revolution; what genre is this?

Within the rhythm game genre, which Konami arcade series, first released in 1998, asks players to step on a dance platform’s directional panels in time with arrows scrolling upward on screen? Its dance cabinet helped make music-driven games a staple of arcades.

Which 2012 science-fiction film directed by Ridley Scott follows archaeologists Elizabeth Shaw and Charlie Holloway to the moon LV-223 after they interpret ancient star maps as an invitation from humanity’s creators? It was developed as a prequel to the Alien franchise.

In Prometheus, what is the name of Michael Fassbender’s synthetic crew member, who watches Lawrence of Arabia during the voyage and rehearses Peter O’Toole’s mannerisms while the human passengers are in cryosleep?

Which 2017 musical film follows Hugh Jackman as P. T. Barnum builds a spectacular show, with Zac Efron and Zendaya among its cast? The film features the songs “Rewrite the Stars” and “A Million Dreams.”

In The Greatest Showman, Zendaya plays a skilled trapeze artist who performs with her brother and becomes romantically involved with Zac Efron’s character, Phillip Carlyle. What is her character’s name?

This animated fantasy-action series adapts a world created for a Riot Games video game and follows sisters Vi and Powder, who later becomes Jinx, amid conflict between Piltover and Zaun. What is the series called?

Arcane was animated in partnership with a French studio whose earlier collaborations with Riot Games included the League of Legends music videos “Get Jinxed” and “Warriors.” What is the studio’s name?
Which American pop trio of brothers released the songs “Weak,” “Bang!,” and “Sober Up”?
On AJR’s 2017 album *The Click*, which track was inspired by the sitcom *The Office* and reflects a fan’s attachment to its characters?
Written by Antônio Carlos Jobim, this Portuguese-English bossa nova standard became a jazz-pop staple and appeared on the landmark 1964 album Getz/Gilberto. What is the song’s title?

On the landmark 1964 album pairing Stan Getz’s saxophone with João’s guitar, this Brazilian vocalist sang the English-language part of “The Girl from Ipanema,” while João sang the Portuguese verse. Who was she?

Which Pakistani-Canadian actress made her acting debut as Kamala Khan in the six-episode 2022 Disney+ series about a Jersey City teenager who discovers superpowers? She later reprised the role in an MCU feature film.
Iman Vellani reprised her role as Kamala Khan in this 2023 MCU film, where Kamala’s powers become entangled with those of Carol Danvers and Monica Rambeau. What is the film’s title?

Which American media entrepreneur launched the first 24-hour cable news channel in 1980 and later owned the Atlanta Braves and the professional wrestling company WCW? Identify this broadcasting pioneer.
Ted Turner founded a cable news network that began broadcasting on June 1, 1980, and pioneered round-the-clock television news. What network was it?

On Kendrick Lamar’s 2015 album *To Pimp a Butterfly*, this track pairs a buoyant, funk-inflected beat with a refrain of resilience. It became widely associated with Black Lives Matter demonstrations and protests against police violence. Which song is it?
Kendrick Lamar’s “Alright” is the seventh track on this 2015 studio album, which also features “King Kunta,” “The Blacker the Berry,” and “How Much a Dollar Cost.” What is the album’s title?

Originally formed from Lucasfilm’s computer graphics group, this American company became independent with Steve Jobs as its majority investor before The Walt Disney Company acquired it in 2006. What company is being described?
At Pixar Animation Studios, which filmmaker directed *Toy Story* (1995), the studio’s first feature-length film, and later became its chief creative officer?

In this 2017 horror film, photographer Chris Washington visits his girlfriend’s family and discovers a scheme to place older white people’s brains into young Black people’s bodies. The film was written and directed by a comedian making his feature-film directing debut.
Get Out marked the feature-film directing debut of this comedian and filmmaker. Before directing it, he became widely known as one half of a sketch-comedy duo with Keegan-Michael Key.

Which HBO series adapts George R. R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire, following noble families fighting for power in Westeros as supernatural threats gather beyond the Wall? Its story also follows Daenerys Targaryen’s return with dragons to reclaim her family’s rule.

In Game of Thrones, what is the name of the elite army of eunuch soldiers trained from childhood in Astapor, whom Daenerys buys and then frees? Known for their skill with spears, they are later led by Grey Worm.

In Marvel Comics, this hero is a New York teenager who gains extraordinary abilities after being bitten by an irradiated laboratory specimen. He fights crime with web-shooters, and his adventures have repeatedly brought him into conflict with the vampire-like Morbius. Who is this hero?

In stories featuring Spider-Man, this scientist attempts to cure a rare blood disease through an experiment that transforms him into a living vampire. First appearing in The Amazing Spider-Man #101, he becomes a recurring foe of the wall-crawler. Who is this character?
This Canadian singer-songwriter and producer released *Dawn FM* and scored major R&B and pop hits with “Blinding Lights” and “The Hills.” What is his stage name?

What is the name of the online platform where people gather in communities centered on particular interests to share links, text posts, and comments? Its voting system lets members signal approval or disapproval, helping determine which contributions become prominent.

Reddit has hosted a collaborative art event built around a shared pixel canvas, where users could place one pixel at a time at intervals. Communities coordinated to create flags, memes, and elaborate images on the same canvas; what is this event called?
Which Compton-born rapper and producer helped define West Coast gangsta rap as a member of N.W.A., released the solo album *The Chronic* in 1992, and founded Aftermath Entertainment?
At the 2022 Super Bowl halftime show featuring Dr. Dre, which Detroit rapper performed “Lose Yourself” and took a knee afterward? He also played Rabbit in the film *8 Mile*.

This American comedian portrayed a conservative pundit on a satirical Comedy Central news program before taking over CBS’s The Late Show after David Letterman in 2015. He also delivered a sharply satirical address at the 2006 White House Correspondents’ Dinner while George W. Bush was president; who is he?

At what annual Washington gathering did Stephen Colbert deliver a famously confrontational 2006 roast of President George W. Bush before an audience of journalists and political figures? The event traditionally features both a comedian and the sitting president.
Which 1990 submarine thriller directed by John McTiernan stars Sean Connery as Soviet submarine captain Marko Ramius?

In The Hunt for Red October, which CIA analyst, played by Alec Baldwin, tries to determine why Captain Ramius is steering a Soviet submarine toward the United States? The character first appeared in a 1984 novel by Tom Clancy.

Released in 1977, this George Lucas space-opera film follows farmhand Luke Skywalker as he joins the Rebel Alliance and helps destroy the Empire’s planet-killing battle station. It launched a major film saga and introduced audiences to Darth Vader.

In Star Wars, the director adapted Joseph Campbell’s monomyth into a space adventure and drew on classic serials and samurai cinema. He had previously written and directed American Graffiti; who is he?

Designed with major contributions from Ub Iwerks, this Disney character appears as a mischievous steamboat deckhand in a sound-synchronized short that opened at New York’s Colony Theater on November 18, 1928. Two silent shorts featuring him had been made earlier, but this release became his commonly recognized screen debut. Name the character.

In Mickey Mouse’s first released film, a 1928 short that premiered at New York’s Colony Theater, the music and sound effects were synchronized with the action. The mouse works as a deckhand and turns objects and animals aboard the vessel into makeshift musical instruments. What is the title of the short?

Which animated television series follows three animal brothers—a grizzly, a bamboo-eating panda, and a white Arctic predator—as they navigate life in the San Francisco Bay Area, sometimes traveling stacked atop one another?
In We Bare Bears, which brother is a white polar bear known for speaking about himself in the third person and for his skills in cooking and martial arts?

This 1960 black-and-white psychological horror film adapts a 1959 novel by Robert Bloch and follows secretary Marion Crane after she flees with stolen money and checks into a remote motel run by Norman Bates. A startling shower murder shifts the story away from its apparent protagonist. Name the film.

Psycho’s famous shower sequence is accompanied by a piercing string cue that became one of cinema’s most recognizable musical moments. Which composer wrote the film’s score and also composed the music for Citizen Kane?

This Bronx-born singer-songwriter wrote a 1989 hit whose rapid-fire lyrics trace major people and events from the Truman era through the late 1980s. He also wrote a 1983 chart hit about a wealthy young woman drawn to a man from a very different social world. Who is this pianist and performer?

Billy Joel drew on his time playing at a Los Angeles bar for this 1973 song, whose verses introduce a bartender named John, a sailor named Davy, and other regulars. Its chorus asks the barroom pianist to provide a melody that will leave the patrons feeling all right. What song is it?

This American R&B singer began his career in Boston vocal group New Edition before becoming a solo star with hits such as “My Prerogative.” He also performed “On Our Own,” the theme song for *Ghostbusters II*; who is he?

Bobby Brown’s solo breakthrough in the late 1980s helped bring a style built from R&B vocals, funk grooves, and hip-hop production into mainstream pop. Popularized by producer Teddy Riley, what is this style called?
In this FromSoftware action role-playing game, a hunter arrives in a plague-ridden Gothic city where a mysterious illness transforms infected people into monstrous beasts. What is the game’s title?
In Bloodborne, what is the name of the Gothic city where the hunter searches for a cure as the illness turns many residents into beasts?
In print journalism, this newspaper format uses pages smaller than a traditional broadsheet and is often associated with punchy, sensational headlines. What is this format called?
Founded by Alexander Hamilton in 1801, this Rupert Murdoch-owned American newspaper runs the Page Six gossip column and is often described as a tabloid. What is the newspaper’s name?

This masked, round swordsman is one of Kirby’s recurring rivals, though he sometimes joins Kirby as an ally. His cape can transform into wings, and he is known for his skill with a sword. Who is this character?
In Kirby Super Star’s “Revenge of Meta Knight” story, Meta Knight builds a powerful battleship and uses it in a plan to conquer Dream Land. What is the name of the ship?
Born in Abbott, Texas, this singer-songwriter became a leading figure in outlaw country. He co-founded Farm Aid in 1985 with Neil Young and John Mellencamp; which artist is he?
Willie Nelson has played his road-worn Martin N-20 guitar for decades, and a large hole in its soundboard reflects years of use. What nickname does he give the instrument?
Which six-episode MCU television series debuted in June 2022 and follows Pakistani-American teenager Kamala Khan as she discovers superpowers and becomes a hero inspired by Captain Marvel?

In Ms. Marvel, which Pakistani-Canadian performer made her screen-acting debut as Kamala Khan, the Jersey City teenager whose powers emerge after she puts on a mysterious bangle? She later reprised the role in The Marvels.

Which Japanese animation studio was founded in 1985 by Hayao Miyazaki, Isao Takahata, and Toshio Suzuki? Its acclaimed films include the story of a girl who enters a spirit world and works in a bathhouse.

In this 2001 Studio Ghibli feature, a ten-year-old girl is drawn into an otherworldly realm after her parents are transformed into pigs. She takes a job at a bathhouse and is renamed Sen; what is the film’s title?

In an early arcade maze game, this round yellow character travels through corridors, eating dots while avoiding four colored ghosts. Bonus fruit can also appear in the maze. What is the name of the game and its title character?
Which arcade follow-up to Pac-Man centers on the original hero’s wife and adds pretzels, pears, and bananas to the bonus-item lineup?

Born in Compton, California, this rapper released the 2015 album *To Pimp a Butterfly*, which blends hip-hop with jazz, funk, and spoken-word elements. He later became the first rapper to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music, for his album *DAMN.*
Kendrick Lamar’s third studio album, released in 2015, opens with “Wesley’s Theory” and includes the singles “King Kunta” and “Alright.” What is the album’s title?
This power ballad from Disney’s Frozen accompanies Elsa as she builds an ice palace in the mountains. It won the Academy Award for Best Original Song.
Which Broadway performer recorded “Let It Go” for Frozen, voiced Elsa in both Frozen films, and played Elphaba in the original Broadway cast of Wicked?

This conservative commentator wrote the novel *True Allegiance* and became the youngest nationally syndicated columnist in the United States at age 17. He also helped establish a conservative news and commentary outlet. Who is he?

Ben Shapiro and filmmaker Jeremy Boreing launched this conservative media company in 2015. It later expanded beyond news and commentary into podcasts, books, and streaming entertainment. What is the company called?

Which Supercell troop appears as the yellow-haired, sword-wielding figure on the Clash of Clans app icon and also fights as a ground melee unit in Clash Royale? Its heroic counterpart is a major hero in Clash of Clans.
In Clash of Clans, the Barbarian’s heroic counterpart is a durable melee hero who becomes available when a village upgrades to Town Hall 7. What is this hero’s name?
In Marvel stories, Doctor Strange wears this mystical relic as a pendant, and in the Marvel Cinematic Universe it houses a powerful green gem. What is the artifact called?

In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the Eye of Agamotto conceals one of the six Infinity gems. Doctor Strange uses this green gem to reverse the destruction of an apple during his confrontation with Dormammu. What is its name?
This American country singer won the fourth season of *American Idol* in 2005. Her hits include “Before He Cheats” and “Cowboy Casanova”; who is she?
Carrie Underwood included this song on her 2012 album *Blown Away*. Its lyrics offer comfort after a loved one’s death, expressing hope that the separation is not final. What is the song?

Released in 1986, this action film follows U.S. Navy fighter-pilot trainees competing at an elite naval aviation school. Tom Cruise plays a brash student whose callsign reflects his independent streak; name the film.

In Top Gun, a romantic power ballad by Berlin accompanies the relationship between the pilot known as Maverick and civilian instructor Charlotte “Charlie” Blackwood. The song later won the Academy Award for Best Original Song; what is its title?
This American television journalist joined CNN in 1990 and became a longtime anchor known for hosting The Situation Room. Who is he?
Wolf Blitzer hosts The Situation Room for which cable news network, founded by Ted Turner and launched in 1980 as a 24-hour television news channel?

On Disney+’s six-episode 2022 series about Jersey City teenager Kamala Khan, a Pakistani-Canadian actor made her screen-acting debut in the title role. Who is she?

answer: When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?

question: A Japanese director made a 1954 film in which a farming village recruits seven masterless warriors to defend against bandits. He also reimagined Macbeth as a tale of samurai ambition and directed an adventure whose storytelling influenced Star Wars. Who was this filmmaker?

In a 1950 film by Akira Kurosawa, a bandit, a woman, a murdered samurai speaking through a medium, and a woodcutter provide conflicting accounts of a killing. What concept is named for this film and describes incompatible versions of the same event?

This 1986 recording by the band Berlin was written and produced by an Italian electronic-music composer before becoming a prominent love theme in *Top Gun*. It won the Academy Award for Best Original Song; what is its title?
The song “Take My Breath Away,” featured in *Top Gun*, was co-written and produced by an Italian composer whose film scores include *Midnight Express* and *Flashdance*. What is his name?

This English filmmaker entered the movie industry in 1919 as a title-card designer and made his feature-film directing debut with a silent film in 1926. Known for suspenseful thrillers and brief appearances in many of his own films, what director was nicknamed the “Master of Suspense”?

Alfred Hitchcock’s early silent thriller follows a London landlady who grows suspicious of a mysterious new tenant as a serial killer targets blonde women around the city. The film helped establish its director’s reputation; what is its title?

In this Alfred Hitchcock film, Jimmy Stewart plays former police detective Scottie Ferguson, who is hired to follow Madeleine Elster and has a severe fear of heights. A staircase scene uses a combined camera movement and zoom to convey Scottie’s disorientation; what film is it?

Modeled primarily on Hokkaido, this Pokémon region is the setting of Pokémon Diamond and Pearl and Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl. Pokémon Legends: Arceus explores its distant past under the name Hisui; what is the region called in the mainline games?

In Sinnoh, this prominent mountain cuts through the region and separates its eastern and western sides. At its summit lies Spear Pillar, where Dialga or Palkia can be encountered in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl; what is the mountain’s name?

Which 1974 American sports film follows incarcerated men who assemble an American-football team to face the prison guards? Burt Reynolds plays former professional quarterback Paul Crewe, and the film received an Adam Sandler-led remake in 2005.

The 1974 film The Longest Yard stars Burt Reynolds as disgraced former quarterback Paul Crewe, who helps form a team of prison inmates. Which director, also known for The Dirty Dozen and The Flight of the Phoenix, helmed the film?

In *She-Ra and the Princesses of Power*, this magical planet is where Adora discovers the Horde’s harm to its people and joins the Rebellion. Its elemental princesses draw their powers from magical runestones. What is the planet called?

In *She-Ra and the Princesses of Power*, the Princess Alliance’s stronghold on Etheria withstands a Horde assault in the first season. What is the name of this kingdom and rebel base, ruled by Queen Angella?

This Icelandic post-rock band is known for Jónsi’s high falsetto and bowed-guitar sound. One of its albums contains eight untitled tracks split into two groups by 36 seconds of silence; name the band.

On Sigur Rós’s album of eight untitled tracks, Jónsi used this invented vocal language in place of conventional lyrics. Its sounds were shaped to fit the music rather than convey a fixed set of words; what is the language called?
Released in 2013, this fourth studio album by Daft Punk features “Get Lucky,” “Lose Yourself to Dance,” and the multi-part track “Touch.” What is the album’s title?

On Daft Punk’s Random Access Memories, one track includes a spoken recollection of a musician’s early career over a gradually building instrumental. Which pioneering Italian producer, also known for working with Donna Summer on “I Feel Love,” delivers the recollection?

In The Amazing World of Gumball, this orange fish has legs and is part of Gumball’s family as his adopted younger brother. His cheerful nature makes him a loyal companion on the brothers’ frequent adventures. Who is this character?

Darwin Watterson and Gumball get into many of their escapades in this fictional town, where the show’s colorful residents include people, animals, and animated objects. What is the name of their hometown?

A girl with psychokinetic abilities escapes a secret laboratory in Hawkins, Indiana, and her arrival is connected to a breach into a hostile parallel realm. What Netflix series, created by Matt and Ross Duffer and first released in 2016, follows her and the local children confronting the creatures that cross over?

In Stranger Things season four, a Hawkins High senior leads the Hellfire Club and plays guitar in a band called Corroded Coffin. After Chrissy Cunningham dies in his trailer, he becomes the subject of a manhunt; what is this character’s name?

In Stranger Things, the boys’ first episode begins after they have played a tabletop role-playing game, and they later use its monsters and rules to make sense of supernatural threats. What game are they playing?
This American actor played James T. Kirk in the 2009 Star Trek reboot and its two sequels, and portrayed Steve Trevor opposite Gal Gadot in Wonder Woman and Wonder Woman 1984. Who is he?
In the Star Trek reboot films featuring Chris Pine, which actor portrays Spock, the half-human, half-Vulcan officer whose friendship with the captain is central to the story?
Which decade saw the Great Depression and New Deal reshape U.S. society while swing and big-band recordings became major popular entertainment? Bessie Smith died during this same period.
In the 1930s, which songwriter wrote “You’re the Top” for *Anything Goes* and also composed “Begin the Beguine” and “Night and Day”?

What term describes motion pictures made without synchronized recorded dialogue, which often used intertitles or title cards to convey speech and narrative information? This format flourished before synchronized sound became standard in cinema.
Which 1925 Soviet film by Sergei Eisenstein dramatizes a 1905 sailors’ mutiny and features a famous baby-carriage sequence on the Odessa Steps? It is widely regarded as a landmark among silent films.

In film editing, what technique combines separate shots into a unified sequence so that their juxtaposition creates meaning, associations, or dramatic effects? It is often discussed in connection with early Soviet cinema.

What stage name does American YouTuber and entrepreneur Jimmy Donaldson use for his videos featuring elaborate challenges and large cash giveaways?
MrBeast launched this virtual restaurant brand in 2020, using partner kitchens and delivery apps instead of its own conventional dining locations. What is the name of this chain?
Which 1999 found-footage horror film is presented as recovered recordings made by three student filmmakers who disappear while investigating a local legend?
In The Blair Witch Project, Heather, Mike, and Josh interview residents before hiking into the nearby Black Hills Forest. Which town do they visit?

Founded by Alexander Hamilton in 1801 and later acquired by Rupert Murdoch, this newspaper publishes the celebrity-gossip franchise Page Six and is known for sensationalist headlines. What is its name?

The New York Post is often described as an example of this newspaper type, known for sensationalist coverage and a compact format. Traditionally, papers in this format are folded once along a vertical spine, unlike broadsheets; what is the type called?

Opened on Cleveland’s Lake Erie waterfront in 1995, this institution preserves the history of electric-guitar-driven popular music and honors performers such as the Beatles, Aretha Franklin, and Tina Turner. What is its full name?
answer: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum

question: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum’s Cleveland building features a glass pyramid and bold geometric forms. Which Chinese-American architect, who also designed the Louvre’s glass pyramid in Paris, created it?

Sony released this home console in 2020 as the successor to the PS4, pairing a high-speed SSD with a distinctive white-and-black shell. Its launch games included Marvel’s Spider-Man: Miles Morales. What is the console’s name?

Which wireless controller launched with the PlayStation 5 and features adaptive triggers that vary their resistance, along with haptic feedback designed to convey different sensations? Its two-tone design and built-in microphone distinguish it from earlier PlayStation controllers.

This Netflix animated fantasy series follows Adora, a former Horde soldier who discovers a magical sword and becomes a warrior leading a coalition of magical allies against the Horde. What is the series’ full title?
answer: She-Ra and the Princesses of Power

question: In She-Ra and the Princesses of Power, Adora discovers her sword in the Whispering Woods, and the princesses’ powers are linked to ancient runestones found across their world. What is the name of that planet?
In Nintendo’s life-simulation series, this tanuki-like entrepreneur has served as a shopkeeper and helped players finance home expansions, usually repaid in Bells. What is this character’s name?

Tom Nook is a recurring shopkeeper and home lender in this Nintendo life-simulation franchise, where players collect Bells, decorate homes, and interact with anthropomorphic villagers. Its 2020 installment, New Horizons, places players on a deserted island; name the franchise.

Launched by Ted Turner in 1980, this American cable network became the first television channel devoted to 24-hour news coverage. Which network is it?

Released in 2022, this open-world action role-playing game was developed by FromSoftware and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment. What game is it?
Elden Ring’s worldbuilding was developed with input from an American author best known for the epic fantasy series A Song of Ice and Fire, which inspired Game of Thrones. Who is this author?

Born in Los Angeles in 1926 as Norma Jeane Mortenson, this actress adopted a stage name and became a major Hollywood star after her 1953 roles in *Gentlemen Prefer Blondes* and *Niagara*. Who was she?
Marilyn Monroe plays a Manhattan neighbor known as “The Girl” in this 1955 comedy, where a subway grate sends her white dress billowing upward. What film became famous for that scene?

In Pirates of the Caribbean, the 2003 first film pits its heroes against Captain Barbossa’s cursed, undead crew. Which filmmaker directed that original feature?

This sister filmmaking duo created the 1999 science-fiction film *The Matrix* and continued shaping its sequels, including *The Matrix Reloaded* and *The Matrix Revolutions*. By what shared professional name is this pair known?

In *The Matrix Resurrections* (2021), this actor reprises Neo, the hacker-turned-resistance hero at the center of the franchise created by The Wachowskis. He also stars in the *John Wick* films and played Ted in the *Bill & Ted* movies.

Akira Kurosawa's 1954 epic follows a drought-stricken farming community that recruits masterless warriors to resist bandits who return for the harvest. In its final scene, surviving fighters stand by graves marked with swords as villagers resume planting; name the film.

Which film franchise began with a 1993 movie about a genetically engineered dinosaur attraction on a remote island and later continued with films centered on a successor resort? Its original film was adapted from a Michael Crichton novel.
In the Jurassic Park franchise, what fictional island off Costa Rica is the site of John Hammond’s original dinosaur park, where visitors first encounter the cloned dinosaurs?

A 1955 Kraft Television Theatre episode written by this American television and radio writer, “Patterns,” dramatized a ruthless corporate succession struggle and became a landmark television drama. This American singer, rapper, songwriter, and flutist rose to wider prominence with the 2019 hit “Truth Hurts.” Her album *Special* later featured “2 Be Loved (Am I Ready)” and another chart-topping single. What is her stage name?

This 1977 Talking Heads track appeared on the band’s debut album, and its anxious narrator breaks into a repeated French question before urging someone to flee. What is the song’s title?
Psycho Killer was released by a New York group whose original core trio consisted of David Byrne, Tina Weymouth, and Chris Frantz; Jerry Harrison later joined the lineup. What is the group’s name?

This English singer-songwriter first gained broad attention after a 2010 solo audition on The X Factor led judges to group him with four other contestants into One Direction. His solo hits include “Watermelon Sugar” and “As It Was,” and he played a British soldier in Christopher Nolan’s Dunkirk. Who is he?

Harry Styles released this 2022 album, whose track list includes “As It Was” and “Music for a Sushi Restaurant.” It won both Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album at the 2023 Grammy Awards; what is its title?
What is the name of the recorded visual medium made up of moving images, whose works may be subject to censorship codes, receive motion-picture ratings, and be screened in theaters?
In film festival history, what is the highest prize of the Cannes Film Festival, first awarded in 1955 and named for the festival’s golden palm emblem?
This Marvel mutant is a powerful telepath who can transform her body into durable organic diamond. She once held the title of White Queen in the Hellfire Club. Who is she?
In Marvel comics, Emma Frost is the genetic source for five cloned telepaths named Sophie, Irma, Celeste, Esme, and Phoebe. By what collective name are these sisters known?

Released in 1982 and directed by Ridley Scott, this science-fiction film follows former police officer Rick Deckard as he hunts artificial humans called replicants. Rutger Hauer plays a replicant whose final monologue is known as “Tears in Rain.” What film is it?

This PBS Kids animated series centers on a bespectacled fourth-grade aardvark, his younger sister D.W., and friends such as Buster Baxter. Set in fictional Elwood City, it also features schoolteacher Mr. Ratburn, whose wedding to Patrick is shown in a memorable episode. What is the series?

Founded in the U.S. capital by Stilson Hutchins, this American newspaper published its first issue on December 6, 1877. It later won the 1973 Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for its reporting on the Watergate break-in and its political connections. What newspaper is it?

Announced in 2021 for Nintendo Switch, this action role-playing game takes players to an ancient version of Sinnoh, the setting of the fourth generation of main-series games. What is its full title?

answer: All My Demons Greeting Me as a Friend

question: This American filmmaker directed and starred as Charles Foster Kane in Citizen Kane, played Captain Hank Quinlan in Touch of Evil, and made the essay film F for Fake about art and forgery. Which filmmaker is this?

answer: The War of the Worlds broadcast

question: What long-running American animated sitcom follows a family living in Springfield, with Homer working at a nuclear power plant and Bart known for his mischievous pranks? Its annual “Treehouse of Horror” episodes parody horror, science fiction, and fantasy stories.

In Bridgerton, which monarch, portrayed by Golda Rosheuvel, watches over London’s social season and takes a particular interest in the debutantes seeking advantageous matches?

This scripted series about volunteers at a hospital was distributed on Hulu Plus and YouTube and received harsh criticism. In one episode, volunteer Kit stages a prom for Holden before his heart surgery; what is the series?

Formed in Los Angeles, this hard rock band features guitarist Slash and is known for “Welcome to the Jungle” and “Sweet Child o’ Mine.” What is the band’s name?
Guns N’ Roses released this 1987 debut studio album, which features “Welcome to the Jungle,” “Paradise City,” and “Sweet Child o’ Mine.” What is the album’s title?
