Nintendo’s long-running action-adventure series follows a hero who explores Hyrule, solves dungeon puzzles, and repeatedly confronts a powerful Gerudo antagonist. Its games include a 2017 open-world adventure that begins with the hero awakening after a century of sleep. What is the series called?

In The Legend of Zelda, which 1998 Nintendo 64 installment popularized lock-on targeting and follows its hero as he travels between childhood and adulthood to stop Ganondorf from obtaining the Triforce?
answer: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

question: What body of experimental moving-image work by the Pop artist includes a roughly five-hour study of poet John Giorno asleep and an eight-hour view of the Empire State Building?
Within Andy Warhol's films, which 1963 durational work shows poet John Giorno in bed for roughly five hours?

In Ridley Scott’s 1979 science-fiction horror film *Alien*, what is the Nostromo’s shipboard intelligence called? It privately relays Special Order 937 to Ash, prioritizing the return of the alien organism over the crew’s survival.

In *Alien*, which science officer aboard the Nostromo receives Special Order 937 from Mother, directing him to preserve the alien organism at the crew’s expense? He is later revealed to be an artificial being designed to resemble a human.

Set in 1926 New York, this 2016 fantasy film follows British magizoologist Newt Scamander after several magical creatures escape from his enchanted case. Its title is also the name of a guidebook about magical creatures credited to Scamander. What is the film?
answer: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them

question: In Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, which No-Maj aspiring baker meets Newt after their cases are mistakenly switched at a bank? He later becomes an ally to Newt and Tina as they search for the escaped creatures.

This armored bounty hunter was hired to assassinate Padmé Amidala and later fought Obi-Wan Kenobi on Kamino. He was killed by Mace Windu during the Battle of Geonosis, and his genetic material became the basis for the Republic’s clone army. Who is this character?

Jango Fett provided the genetic template for an army secretly produced on this ocean-covered world. Its cloners operated from Tipoca City, where Obi-Wan Kenobi investigated the creation of the clone army. What planet was it?
Released in 1990 and directed by Martin Scorsese, this crime film follows Henry Hill’s rise in organized crime and his eventual entry into witness protection. What is the film’s title?
In Goodfellas, which real-life mobster is portrayed by Ray Liotta and enters witness protection after cooperating with prosecutors?
This American actor played the title character in the 1994 film *Forrest Gump*. He also portrayed Geppetto in Disney’s 2022 live-action adaptation of *Pinocchio*. Who is he?
In Disney’s 2022 live-action *Pinocchio*, Tom Hanks portrays the woodcarver who creates the puppet and wishes for him to become a real boy. What is this character’s name?
First published in 1889, this American daily became a signature publication of Dow Jones & Company and is especially associated with business, finance, and markets reporting. What newspaper is it?
Which Australian-born media proprietor led News Corporation when it acquired Dow Jones & Company in 2007, bringing the Wall Street Journal under his company's ownership?
This 2013 biographical sports drama stars Chadwick Boseman as a pioneering baseball player and Harrison Ford as Brooklyn Dodgers executive Branch Rickey. What is the film’s title?
In 42, which Brooklyn Dodgers player made his major-league debut in 1947, becoming the first Black player in the modern era of Major League Baseball?

This 1915 silent epic, directed by D. W. Griffith, adapts Thomas Dixon Jr.’s novel *The Clansman*. It presents Reconstruction through racist stereotypes and glorifies a white supremacist group, prompting protests by the NAACP; what is the film’s title?

In *The Birth of a Nation*, this white supremacist organization is portrayed as heroic, and the film’s popularity helped its revival attract supporters. The NAACP protested the film’s screenings because of its racist portrayal of Black people; what organization is being described?
Which 2018 track from Travis Scott’s album *Astroworld* features Drake and is known for its dramatic beat switches between sections?
Sicko Mode appears on this 2018 Travis Scott studio album, his third full-length release. Its title matches that of a former Houston amusement park that closed in 2005.

Before it became the identity of a Walt Disney World theme park, what name did Walt Disney give his proposed futuristic community, a planned experiment in new approaches to urban living that his brother Roy later reshaped into a theme park?
At EPCOT, which attraction is housed inside the park’s enormous geodesic sphere and carries riders through the history of human communication, from early writing to the digital age?

Players begin at an unfamiliar point shown through panoramic street-level imagery and use visual clues such as road signs and landscapes to place a marker as close as possible on a world map. What online geography game is built around this location-identification challenge?

GeoGuessr’s standard interface draws on a widely used online mapping platform, with a familiar map-and-directions interface and panoramic street-level imagery that lets players inspect roads and surroundings. What platform also lets users search for businesses and calculate driving routes?
This English actress worked extensively on stage and screen, was married to Philip Roth, and inspired the character Eve Frame in his novel *I Married a Communist*. Who is she?
In Philip Roth’s novel about former radio star Ira Ringold, an actress writes a memoir exposing their marriage and his Communist past. Claire Bloom was the real-life model for which character?

This 1985 science-fiction film sends a teenager from Hill Valley three decades into the past in a time machine built from a DeLorean. To get home, he must help ensure his parents meet and fall in love.
In Back to the Future, which eccentric Hill Valley inventor builds the DeLorean time machine and uses a lightning strike at the clock tower to send Marty back to 1985?

Released in 1973, this song draws on its songwriter’s stint as a lounge musician at the Executive Room in Los Angeles, where patrons’ stories informed its verses. Its barroom narrator takes requests for a familiar tune, and the customers join the chorus to say he has them feeling alright. What song is it?

The 1973 song “Piano Man” was written and performed by this New York-born singer-songwriter, who also recorded “Uptown Girl” and “New York State of Mind.” Before his breakthrough, he played piano at Los Angeles’s Executive Room under the name Bill Martin. Who is this musician?

On this Food Network cooking competition, chefs race through appetizer, entrée, and dessert rounds using baskets of mystery ingredients. Judges taste each dish and eliminate one contestant after each round. What is the show called?
On Chopped, this chef and judge became known for his strong dislike of raw onions. He also hosted the dessert-focused Chopped Sweets. Who is he?

Launched on January 15, 2001, this free online encyclopedia began in English and grew through articles created and revised by volunteers. Its community standards include representing significant views fairly and grounding claims in reliable, published sources. What is this reference work?

Wikipedia is hosted and protected by a nonprofit organization that does not make editorial decisions about the encyclopedia’s contents. Volunteers, rather than this organization, decide what articles say. What is the organization?

Released in 1998, this action-adventure game follows Link after he draws a sacred sword from its pedestal and awakens seven years later. He explores Hyrule, learns melodies on a magical instrument, and confronts Ganondorf. What is the game’s title?
answer: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

question: In The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Link meets a masked Sheikah figure who teaches him songs that let him travel to distant locations. The figure later reveals that she is Princess Zelda. What name does she use while disguised?
Which Japanese anime series follows a young ninja who uses the Rasengan and can create shadow clones?
In Naruto, which young ninja possesses the Sharingan and is the younger brother of Itachi, who carried out the massacre of their clan?

In Among Us, this map places crewmates aboard a spacecraft, with Cafeteria near the top and Reactor and Security on the left side. It was the game’s first map and remains one of its primary locations. What is its name?

On The Skeld in Among Us, impostors can use this action to disappear below floor grates and reappear at connected grates elsewhere; crewmates playing as Engineers can use the same network. What is this action called?

On Hozier’s 2019 album *Wasteland, Baby!*, this song is the second track, following “Nina Cried Power.” Its lyrics weave references to classic jazz standards into a romantic song. What is its full title?
Hozier released “Almost (Sweet Music)” on his second studio album. The record also features “Movement,” “Nobody,” and “Dinner & Diatribes”; what is its title?
This 2021 Walt Disney Animation Studios musical follows a Colombian family whose enchanted home and members have magical gifts, with Mirabel as the exception. What is the film’s title?
In Encanto, which uncle has visions of the future and disappears into the walls of the family home after a troubling vision involving Mirabel?
Released in 1986, this coming-of-age drama follows four boys who set out to find the body of a missing child in Oregon. Adapted from Stephen King’s novella *The Body*, what is the film’s title?
Stand by Me was directed by the filmmaker who had previously made the mockumentary *This Is Spinal Tap* and later directed the romantic comedy *When Harry Met Sally...*. Who directed the 1986 film?
Which 1995 Pixar film follows the toys belonging to a boy named Andy? Its story centers on a cowboy doll whose place as Andy’s favorite is challenged by a newly arrived space ranger.

In Toy Story, Woody and Buzz end up at a fictional restaurant with an arcade claw machine full of little green aliens. The restaurant’s delivery truck also became a recurring Easter egg in Pixar films. What is the restaurant called?

Which 1964 black comedy depicts U.S. Air Force General Jack D. Ripper ordering a nuclear attack without authorization, while the President and his advisers struggle in the War Room to prevent global annihilation? Its title also names the wheelchair-using former Nazi scientist played by Peter Sellers.
answer: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb

question: In Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb, which filmmaker directed the film and also made 2001: A Space Odyssey and A Clockwork Orange? He also carefully designed the film’s imposing War Room.

In Frank Herbert’s Dune universe, this valuable substance is harvested from the sands of Arrakis and can give its users blue eyes. Guild Navigators consume it to help perceive safe paths through interstellar space. What is this substance called?
In the Dune universe, Spice is harvested from the vast deserts of the planet whose native Fremen also call it Rakis. What is the planet’s Imperial name?

Released in 1960 and directed by Federico Fellini, this Italian drama follows gossip journalist Marcello Rubini through Rome’s wealthy, fashionable circles. Its famous Trevi Fountain sequence became one of cinema’s defining images. What film is it?

In La Dolce Vita, which actor portrays the gossip journalist whose encounters with Rome’s glamorous society drive the film? The role became one of the best-known performances in this Italian actor’s long collaboration with Federico Fellini.
This American comedian and actor co-created and starred with Jordan Peele in a Comedy Central sketch series named for the pair. He also portrayed Coach Hines on MADtv. Who is he?

In a recurring Key & Peele sketch, Keegan-Michael Key played Luther, an “anger translator” who voiced the frustrations of the 44th U.S. president, portrayed by Jordan Peele. Which president was the character based on?

In Minecraft, this hostile mob silently approaches players and detonates at close range, often damaging terrain as well as its target. Its green appearance and unusual origin in a mis-sized pig model helped make it one of the game’s most recognizable enemies. What is it called?
A Creeper struck by lightning becomes a more powerful variant with a blue electrical aura and a larger blast. What is this lightning-enhanced form called?

The Creeper’s unusual proportions began when this Minecraft creator accidentally swapped the pig model’s height and length values; he chose to keep the result as a “creepy creature.” What is this developer’s name?

This 1979 Vietnam War film follows U.S. Army Captain Benjamin Willard on a mission upriver to find renegade Colonel Walter Kurtz. Loosely inspired by Joseph Conrad’s *Heart of Darkness*, it features a helicopter assault staged to Wagner’s “Ride of the Valkyries.” What is the film’s title?
In *Apocalypse Now*, the mission to find Colonel Kurtz echoes a novella in which seaman Charles Marlow travels up the Congo River to encounter Kurtz, an ivory agent. Who wrote that novella?
These genetically engineered soldiers were based on the DNA of bounty hunter Jango Fett and served the Galactic Republic in its war against the Separatists. What were these troops called?
Clone troopers were raised in vast facilities on a remote planet covered almost entirely by water, where Tipoca City served as a major cloning center. What was this planet called?
This Sega platform-game hero debuted in 1991, races through Green Hill Zone collecting golden rings, and faces Dr. Robotnik as his recurring foe. What is the character’s name?
In the original 1991 game starring Sonic the Hedgehog, what is the opening stage known for its checkerboard cliffs, palm trees, loops, and waterfalls?
Which Lil Nas X song blends trap production with country imagery, went viral on TikTok, and spent a record-setting 19 weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100 after a remix with a country star?
On the remix of Old Town Road that helped propel the track to a wider pop audience, which country singer added vocals after previously scoring a major hit with “Achy Breaky Heart”?
This Swedish filmmaker directed a 1957 film in which the knight Antonius Block plays chess with Death during the Black Plague, as well as Wild Strawberries and Persona. Who was this director?

In Ingmar Bergman’s 1966 psychological drama, nurse Alma cares for actress Elisabet Vogler after Elisabet suddenly stops speaking. What film explores the increasingly blurred identities of these two women?

In Gaston Leroux’s novel, a masked, disfigured musical genius secretly inhabits a celebrated Parisian theater and becomes obsessed with soprano Christine Daaé. What work centers on this figure and his efforts to control her career?
The Paris opera house at the center of The Phantom of the Opera is an elaborate Second Empire landmark commissioned by Napoleon III and opened in 1875. What is this building commonly called?

In the Pokémon franchise, this recurring criminal organization is led by a crime boss named Giovanni. Its bumbling anime agents Jessie, James, and Meowth are famous for announcing, “Prepare for trouble, and make it double.” What is the organization called?

Team Rocket’s leader also serves as the Viridian City Gym Leader and specializes in Ground-type Pokémon. In the original Pokémon games, the player’s victory over him leads him to announce that he is disbanding the organization. Who is he?
In Among Us, impostors can use connected floor openings to move between locations without walking through the intervening corridors. What is this action, which the Engineer role can also perform?
In Among Us, venting is usually associated with impostors, but one crewmate role can also use it to travel through connected openings. What is that role?

In the stage musical Hamilton, Angelica Schuyler sings this deleted number after Hamilton publishes a public account defending himself amid the Maria Reynolds affair. She rebukes him for making the scandal worse, calling his actions “a new kind of stupid.” What is the song’s title?

In the deleted Hamilton song “Congratulations,” Angelica condemns Hamilton for publicly releasing this document to defend himself after his extramarital affair became public. What is the document commonly known as?

Founded in Beijing in 2012 by a team led by Zhang Yiming and Liang Rubo, this Chinese internet company first gained prominence through a personalized news-recommendation service and later built a global short-video portfolio. It owns TikTok, while its China-focused video counterpart is Douyin. What company is this?

Among ByteDance’s products, this China-focused news and information app launched in 2012 and became the company’s early breakout service by recommending articles and other material to readers based on their interests. What is this app called?
Debuting in 2015 as an all-female Marvel superhero offshoot of the Avengers, this team includes She-Hulk as a central member. What is its name?
A-Force counted this green-skinned hero among its central members. Outside the team, she is the lawyer Jennifer Walters and the cousin of Bruce Banner. Who is she?

Released in 2015, this pop duet pairs Shawn Mendes with Camila Cabello, then a member of Fifth Harmony. Its title alludes to a 1997 teen slasher about a group of friends haunted after covering up a fatal hit-and-run; what song is it?
answer: I Know What You Did Last Summer

question: On I Know What You Did Last Summer, which Cuban-born singer shares the lead vocals with Shawn Mendes? She had previously risen to fame as a member of Fifth Harmony.
Which Northern Irish actor and director played Benedick in the 1993 film adaptation of a Shakespearean comedy that he also directed? He also directed film adaptations of Hamlet and Henry V.

In Kenneth Branagh’s 1993 film adaptation of Much Ado About Nothing, which witty bachelor is tricked into believing that Beatrice loves him? He eventually returns her affection after friends arrange for him to overhear a staged conversation.

Billie Eilish released this 2021 sophomore studio album after *When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?* It features “Therefore I Am” and “Your Power,” along with a title track that builds from a piano ballad into a guitar-driven rock outro. What is the album?

A track on *Happier Than Ever* takes its name from a famous Latin philosophical formula about existence. Its music video shows Billie Eilish wandering through an almost-empty shopping mall and eating fries. What is the song?

Created by Shonda Rhimes, this long-running medical drama begins with a surgical intern starting work at Seattle Grace Hospital after a one-night stand with a man she later discovers is an attending surgeon there. It later became the parent series of the firefighter drama Station 19. What is the series called?
Grey's Anatomy was created by a television writer-producer who later created Scandal and How to Get Away with Murder. Her production company is named Shondaland; who is she?

This American actress and singer originated the role of Elphaba in the Broadway production of Wicked, earning the 2004 Tony Award for Best Actress in a Musical. She also played Maureen in Rent and voiced Elsa in Disney’s Frozen films; who is she?

In Disney’s Frozen, Idina Menzel performs this power ballad as Elsa while the character builds an ice palace in the mountains. The song won the Academy Award for Best Original Song and a Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media; what is its title?
This platform popularized public posts called “tweets” and was historically known for a 280-character limit. It was later rebranded as X; what was its name before the rebrand?

In May 2020, Twitter labeled some of this U.S. president’s claims about mail-in voting as disputed. Which president responded by issuing an executive order aimed at changing social-media platforms’ legal protections?

In the 2022 science-fiction comedy-drama Everything Everywhere All at Once, this character is Evelyn’s husband and helps run their family laundromat. A more assertive version of him, known as Alpha, recruits Evelyn to fight a threat spanning multiple realities. Name this character.

Waymond Wang in Everything Everywhere All at Once was portrayed by this actor, who won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for the role. As a child performer, he played Short Round in Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom and Data in The Goonies. Name the actor.
This 2020 James Bond film marked Daniel Craig’s final appearance as 007. Its story finds Bond retired from active service before a new threat draws him back into action. What is the film’s title?
The title song for No Time to Die was co-written and performed by this singer, who also recorded the hits “bad guy” and “everything i wanted.” Who is she?

This American YouTuber and livestreamer is known for gaming, variety content, and large-scale online events. He drew huge attention with a monthlong Twitch subathon in 2021 and won Streamer of the Year at the 2022 Streamer Awards; who is he?

Ludwig's streams helped boost this location-guessing game, in which players study a Street View panorama to figure out where they have been dropped. Creators such as Trevor Rainbolt have also helped popularize it; what is the game's name?

This American television crime drama follows a high-school chemistry teacher who, after learning he has cancer, partners with a former student to manufacture methamphetamine. What series charts his transformation into a drug-world kingpin?
In Breaking Bad, Walter White’s former student becomes his first meth-making partner. The small-time dealer earns the nickname “Cap’n Cook” for his early batches; what is his name?
Released in February 2022, this synth-pop single became Dove Cameron’s breakout hit. Its narrator offers to treat someone better than her current romantic partner. What is the song’s title?

Dove Cameron’s “Boyfriend” pairs its flirtatious lyrics with a dark, synth-led pop arrangement. Which songwriter-producer, credited with both co-writing and producing the single, helped shape its sound?

Released in 2007 on Miley Cyrus’s album *Meet Miley Cyrus*, this pop song describes an intense connection sparked by eye contact and looks ahead to a reunion. A Rock Mafia remix later helped it find a new audience on TikTok. What is the song?
Miley Cyrus’s “See You Again” received a remix from this production team associated with Antonina Armato and Tim James. What is the team’s name?
Which American media personality founded a conspiracy-focused media outlet and was found liable for defamation after falsely portraying the 2012 shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School as a hoax?
Alex Jones founded a media outlet in 1999 that became the main platform for his conspiracy-focused broadcasts. What is the outlet’s name?

This Howard University-trained actor made his film breakthrough portraying Jackie Robinson in *42*, then played James Brown in *Get on Up* and Thurgood Marshall in *Marshall*. He later became widely known for portraying the king of Wakanda in Marvel films. Who was he?

Chadwick Boseman starred as Jackie Robinson in this 2013 biographical sports drama, which also featured Harrison Ford as Brooklyn Dodgers executive Branch Rickey. What is the film’s title, given as a number?

In this world, the four elemental arts are ordinarily divided among different peoples, but a reincarnating guardian can master all four and is charged with preserving balance. What is this guardian’s title?

Within Avatar lore, one past incarnation lived during the era of Fire Lord Sozin and was Sozin’s childhood friend before their paths diverged. Which incarnation traveled with the dragon Fang and preceded Aang?

This Canadian actress won an Emmy for portraying several distinct clone characters in the science-fiction series Orphan Black. She later played attorney Jennifer Walters, who becomes She-Hulk, in a Disney+ Marvel series. Who is she?

Tatiana Maslany portrayed a group of genetically identical women, including Sarah Manning and Alison Hendrix, in this Canadian science-fiction television drama. Its story follows their discovery that they are part of a cloning experiment. What is the series?

Released in 2000, this black-comedy psychological thriller follows a wealthy Manhattan investment banker whose polished public image hides a violent private life. Christian Bale plays the lead, and Mary Harron directed the adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis’s novel. What film is it?
American Psycho was directed by a filmmaker whose earlier feature, I Shot Andy Warhol, dramatized the life of Valerie Solanas. What is the director’s name?

In 1923, this animator and his brother Roy started a Hollywood production operation making Alice Comedies. He conceived Mickey Mouse, whose public debut came in the synchronized-sound short Steamboat Willie in 1928; what was his name?
Walt Disney pursued this California destination as a place where guests could visit themed lands, and it opened in Anaheim on July 17, 1955. What was the name of the park?

This round, pink Nintendo hero lives on Planet Popstar and is celebrated as one of Dream Land’s protectors. By inhaling enemies, the character can copy their abilities and use powers such as Sword or Ice. Who is this hero?
Kirby lives in this colorful celestial world, the setting associated with Dream Land and the pink hero’s adventures. What is the name of his home world?

In this 2019 South Korean film, the economically disadvantaged Kim family uses forged qualifications and staged circumstances to get jobs throughout the wealthy Park household. The family’s infiltration turns a story of class tension into a sharp blend of comedy and suspense. What film is it?

Parasite was directed by a South Korean filmmaker whose earlier films include Memories of Murder and The Host. He also directed Snowpiercer and won the Academy Award for Best Director for Parasite; who is he?

Which British period-romance television series adapts Jane Austen’s unfinished novel about a seaside resort? Its story follows a young woman from Willingden as she becomes involved in the resort’s fortunes and its residents’ affairs.
In Sanditon, a young woman from Willingden travels to the developing seaside resort with the Parker family after helping them following a carriage accident. What is her name?

This 1993 historical drama depicts a German industrialist using his factory and influence to protect Jewish people during the Holocaust. It is largely filmed in black and white, with a girl in a red coat standing out during the liquidation of the Kraków ghetto. What film is it?
Schindler's List portrays Oskar Schindler's efforts to save Jewish workers during the Holocaust. Its director had previously made Jaws and later directed Saving Private Ryan; who was he?

In common English usage, this Islamic modesty practice names a headscarf that covers the hair and neck while leaving the face visible. Some wear it as an expression of faith or identity, while whether it is religiously required is debated. What is it called?
Unlike the hijab commonly worn with the face visible, this garment covers the lower face as well as the hair, usually leaving the eyes exposed. What is this face covering called?

In Mark’s account, Jesus shares bread and a cup with his disciples at a final meal before his arrest and crucifixion, and tells them that one of those present will betray him. What New Testament scene is this?
The Last Supper is connected in Christian worship to a rite involving bread and wine that recalls Jesus’s body and blood. What Greek-derived term, associated with thanksgiving, names this rite?
He killed the Minotaur in King Minos’s Labyrinth on Crete, using a thread supplied by a princess to find his way out. This Greek hero later became the legendary king of Athens. Who was he?
In the Theseus myth, this daughter of King Minos gives the hero a thread to guide him through the Labyrinth after he enters to face the Minotaur. What is her name?

Ancient tradition credits Theseus with bringing the separate communities of Attica under Athenian rule and uniting them as one political community. What term, meaning roughly “dwelling together,” names this act?
In Greek mythology, which goddess was associated with witchcraft, ghosts, crossroads, and the underworld? She also served as the handmaiden of Demeter’s daughter, who became queen of the dead.
In Greek myth, which goddess did Hecate serve as handmaiden, accompanying her in the underworld after her abduction by Hades? She was the daughter of Demeter and became queen of the dead.
Which Arcadian nymph was pursued by Pan and transformed into reeds near the river Ladon? Pan gathered the reeds and made the panpipe, an instrument named for her.
In the myth of Syrinx, which Greek pastoral god fashioned reed pipes after the nymph was transformed while fleeing him? Those pipes became known as the panpipe.
At the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, which Greek goddess of strife threw a golden apple among Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite, setting in motion a dispute over who was fairest?

The golden apple cast by Eris at the wedding of Peleus and Thetis led Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite to seek a mortal prince’s verdict. What is the name of the episode in which that prince chose Aphrodite, who promised him Helen?

In the Hebrew Bible, this is a sacred poem or song, and the biblical collection named for this form includes the poem that begins, “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.” What is this form of devotional verse?

Which American poet wrote “A Psalm of Life,” whose speaker insists that life is earnest and that the grave is not its goal? The same writer also composed “The Wreck of the Hesperus,” about a ship caught in a storm.

In the Mahabharata, this third Pandava prince is traditionally said to be the son of Indra and is renowned for his skill with a bow. At Kurukshetra, he hesitates when he sees relatives and teachers among the opposing army.

Arjuna’s battlefield conversation with his charioteer Krishna addresses his reluctance to fight and explores duty and spiritual knowledge. What is the name of this dialogue, a pivotal section of the Mahabharata?
In Tibetan Buddhism, traditions are often identified with red- and yellow-hat labels, while Muslims may wear a skullcap called a taqiyah during prayer. What broad category connects these items?
Among religious head coverings, which Tibetan Buddhist school is known as the Yellow Hat tradition? It was founded by Tsongkhapa, and the Dalai Lama lineage belongs to it.
What sacred Vedic drink was consumed by priests in ritual and believed to grant immortality to the gods? Its name also refers to the deity associated with the offering.
In the Rigveda, which thunder-wielding god is repeatedly praised for drinking Soma? He uses the vajra to slay the serpent Vritra and release the waters.
In the Odyssey, Hermes gives Odysseus a protective herb before he enters Circe’s home, where her potion would otherwise transform him. What is this herb called by its Greek name?
In the Odyssey’s episode involving moly, which Olympian messenger meets Odysseus on Aeaea, gives him the herb, and explains how to withstand Circe’s enchantment?

In Roman foundation legend, what animal suckled the abandoned twins Romulus and Remus after they were left by the Tiber? Greek myth describes Lycaon being transformed into the same animal after Zeus punished him.
In Roman legend, the Wolf’s nursing of the abandoned twins precedes one twin’s rise as Rome’s founder and first king. Which twin became that founder and king?
In the biblical account, this prophet confronts Pharaoh, leads the Israelites out of Egypt, and receives divine law at Sinai. What is his name?
In Exodus, Moses says he is not eloquent and asks for help speaking before Pharaoh. Which brother is appointed to speak on his behalf and later serves as Israel’s high priest?
Moses was allowed to view the Promised Land from across the Jordan but died in Moab before entering it. What mountain is named as the site of his final vantage and death?
Moses was tending a flock near Horeb when he saw flames that did not consume a shrub and heard a call to return to Egypt. What miraculous sign marked this encounter?
As an infant, Moses was placed in a papyrus basket among riverbank reeds to hide him from Pharaoh’s order against Hebrew boys; Pharaoh’s daughter found him there. Which river was he set adrift on?
A German inquisitor wrote this Latin treatise in the late 15th century, arguing that witchcraft was heresy and should be prosecuted. What is the treatise called?
The Malleus Maleficarum repeatedly cites a 13th-century Dominican Scholastic theologian whose Summa Theologica is a major synthesis of Catholic theology. Which saint is this?
Which pope issued the 2015 encyclical Laudato si’, calling for care of our common home, and later published the post-synodal exhortation Querida Amazonia after the Synod for the Amazon?

Pope Francis used this 2015 encyclical to criticize a “throwaway culture” and connect environmental damage with social injustice. Its Italian title echoes the opening words of the Canticle of the Sun by Francis of Assisi; what is the encyclical called?
In Islamic eschatology, this is the promised abode of the righteous and is contrasted with Jahannam. Descriptions associate it with gardens and houris.
In Islamic accounts of the Prophet Muhammad’s heavenly ascent, this lote tree stands at the furthest boundary of the heavens. Which named tree is described as marking the upper boundary of Jannah?

In Japanese myth, Susanoo discovered this blade inside the tail of an eight-headed serpent and later presented it to Amaterasu. It became one of the three objects of Japan’s Imperial Regalia; what is the sword’s traditional name?

In the mythology surrounding Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi, Susanoo defeats a monstrous serpent with eight heads and eight tails after getting it drunk with sake. The sword is found in the creature’s tail; what is the serpent called?
In Islamic belief, this archangel brought the Qur'anic revelations to Muhammad, beginning with the command to recite. What is the name by which this messenger is commonly known in English?
Islamic tradition says Gabriel conveyed the Qur'an to this prophet, whose migration from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE became the starting point of the Islamic calendar. Who was he?

This Hindu observance falls on the second lunar day of the bright fortnight after Diwali and marks the close of the festival period. Sisters traditionally place a ceremonial mark on their brothers’ foreheads, pray for their well-being, and share a meal with them; what is this festival called?
According to a traditional legend associated with Bhai Dooj, which Hindu god visited his sister Yamuna on this day and was welcomed with a ceremonial mark and a meal?

This swift heroine was the only woman among the hunters pursuing the Calydonian Boar, and she drew first blood before Meleager awarded her the animal’s hide. She later lost a footrace after her suitor distracted her with objects scattered along the course. Who was she?

In the myth of Atalanta, Hippomenes relied on three gifts from Aphrodite, tossing them one by one along the course to make the swift huntress pause and retrieve them. What objects turned the footrace in his favor?
In Catholic teaching, what is the remission of temporal punishment due for sins whose guilt has been forgiven? The sale of these remissions became a major target of criticism during the Reformation.
Which German Augustinian friar made the sale of indulgences a central target in his 1517 Ninety-Five Theses, traditionally associated with Wittenberg’s Castle Church?

After the 1534 Act of Supremacy, this established English church broke with papal jurisdiction under Henry VIII. It became the mother church of Anglicanism and is led by the Archbishop of Canterbury; what is it?

The Church of England adopted this liturgical book, first issued in 1549 during Edward VI’s reign and largely compiled by Thomas Cranmer, to standardize worship in English. What is the title of this work, later influential across Anglican churches?

This Israelite king asked God for an understanding heart rather than long life or riches, and his judgment between two women disputing a baby became a famous test of wisdom. He also built the First Temple in Jerusalem during the united monarchy. Who was he?

In the biblical account, this ruler traveled to Jerusalem with a caravan bearing spices, gold, and precious stones to test Solomon with difficult questions. After hearing his wisdom and seeing the prosperity of his court, she praised Israel’s God. Who was this ruler?

What Christian denomination was formerly known as the Religious Society of Friends? Its members emphasize an inward “inner light” and direct communion with God without requiring a separate priesthood.
Which present-day U.S. state did William Penn establish in part as a refuge for Quakers? Philadelphia became its largest city, and Swarthmore College was later founded near it.

In Ovid’s account, a serpent fatally bites this bride on the ankle while she walks with the Naiads. Her husband persuades the rulers of the Underworld to let her follow him toward the surface, but she vanishes when he looks back before they reach the upper world. Who is she?

In the story of Eurydice’s attempted return, this poet’s singing and lyre-playing persuade the rulers of the Underworld to let her follow him toward the living. Forbidden to look behind him before reaching the upper world, he turns near the exit and loses her again. Who is this musician?

In Hindu tradition, this goddess embodies wisdom, learning, music, and the arts, and is traditionally described as the wife of Brahma. Often depicted holding a veena, she is one of the prominent goddesses of the Tridevi. Name this goddess.

Saraswati is often depicted holding a stringed instrument associated with Indian classical music, which also symbolizes her connection to the arts. What is this instrument, commonly described as a type of lute?
This central Christian feast concludes Holy Week and the Lenten season. It commemorates Jesus rising from the dead on the third day after his burial.

The movable date of Easter is traditionally associated with a rule involving the first Sunday after the spring full moon. Which 325 gathering under Emperor Constantine is credited with establishing that rule?
The seven-week season that begins on Easter Sunday and concludes with Pentecost is known by what name? It is a period of celebration in the Christian calendar.
At many Easter Vigils, this large wax light is marked with a cross, the Greek letters Alpha and Omega, and the current year. What is it called?

Across Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and other Indian traditions, this principle links intentional deeds to their consequences rather than treating outcomes as mere chance. It can shape a person's present circumstances and, in traditions that teach rebirth, the conditions of a future existence. What is this principle called?

Traditional Hindu accounts divide karma according to how and when its effects unfold. What is the term for the portion of accumulated past action whose results have begun to ripen in a person's present life?
In traditional Hindu classifications, karma from prior deeds can be understood as a stock accumulated across lifetimes. What is the name for this store of accumulated karma?

Karma is often discussed as influencing the repeated process of birth, death, and rebirth in Indian religions. What Sanskrit term names this continuing cycle, which liberation is said to bring to an end?

This Greek centaur was celebrated for wisdom and healing rather than the violence associated with many of his kind. Ancient accounts make him a mentor to Achilles and Jason and commonly name Cronus and Philyra as his parents. Who is this mythological figure?
An ancient Greco-Roman ring gem at the Walters Art Museum depicts Chiron teaching young Achilles an artistic skill. What stringed instrument is Achilles learning to play?

The canonical Passion accounts place this execution at Golgotha, outside Jerusalem, and describe the condemned figure flanked by two others. It became a central event in Christian theology and a recurring subject in religious art; what event is this?

Salvador Dalí’s 1954 painting of the Crucifixion of Jesus sets Christ against an unfolded net of a four-dimensional hypercube, formed from eight cubes. Gala appears below the figure; what is the painting called?
Which Roman war goddess was honored at a temple near the Circus Flaminius, outside the pomerium, that Appius Claudius Caecus vowed during the Third Samnite War and dedicated in 296 BCE?
During the Roman festival called Dies Sanguinis, ecstatic priests of Bellona lacerated themselves and offered their blood to the war goddess. What were these priests called?
In Norse tradition, what is the name of the symbolic writing system Odin learned after hanging from Yggdrasil? These symbols were used both for writing and for divination.
What is the name of the Norse world-tree from which Odin hung himself, pierced by his spear, to gain knowledge of the runes? It is described as connecting the worlds.
What supreme Jewish religious and judicial assembly was traditionally composed of 71 members and met in Jerusalem’s Temple?
The Sanhedrin is traditionally said to have met in this Jerusalem sanctuary, whose first-century version was destroyed by Roman forces in 70 CE. What was that sanctuary called?

This fifth-century Christian bishop wrote the Confessio and a letter concerning the soldiers of Coroticus, and later became Ireland’s patron saint. Though tradition credits him with Christianizing the island, Christian communities were already present there. Who is he?
Sent to Ireland in 431 as a bishop, this missionary preceded Saint Patrick and is evidence that Christianity was already present on the island before Patrick’s mission. What was his name?
In American tall tales, this enormous ox travels as the companion of the giant lumberjack Paul Bunyan. What is the ox’s folkloric name?

In the stories featuring Babe the Blue Ox, this giant lumberjack was said to have been delivered to his parents by five giant storks. One tale credits his dragging an ax across the ground with carving the Grand Canyon; who is this lumberjack?

In Roman legend, these twin sons of Rhea Silvia and Mars were exposed on the Tiber and suckled by a she-wolf. After surviving, they quarreled over where to establish a city, and one killed the other. What are the names of the twin brothers?

In the story of Romulus and Remus, what Vestal Virgin was their mother and the daughter of Numitor, the rightful king of Alba Longa? Her uncle Amulius seized the throne and forced her into the priesthood to prevent her from having heirs.

Founded in Detroit in 1930 by Wallace Fard Muhammad, this African American religious and political movement grew under Elijah Muhammad’s leadership and became known for its teachings on Black identity and self-reliance. What is the movement’s natural name?
This leader headed the Nation of Islam from 1934 until 1975, mentored Malcolm X, and was the father of Warith Deen Mohammed. Who was he?

Medusa’s gaze could turn victims to stone, and Zeus ended the impossible chase between Laelaps and the Teumessian Fox by turning both animals to stone. What is the name for this supernatural transformation or fate in myth?

In accounts of mythological petrification, which king of Seriphos demanded Medusa’s head from Perseus, only for Perseus to use the severed head against him? Perseus had avoided Medusa’s gaze by viewing her reflection in a bronze shield.
In Christian tradition, this figure is portrayed as a rebel against God and as the tempter of Jesus in the wilderness. Revelation also depicts him as a dragon who is ultimately defeated.
In Revelation, this archangel leads the heavenly forces in battle against the dragon associated with Satan. The dragon and its angels are defeated and cast out of heaven.
Revelation says Satan is bound for a thousand years, briefly released, and then cast into this final fiery place. The beast and the false prophet are also condemned there.
In John Milton’s epic, Satan gathers the fallen angels in Pandemonium and declares that it is better to reign in Hell than serve in Heaven. What is the title of this poem?
Jesus often taught by telling brief stories about familiar situations that invited listeners to infer a moral or spiritual lesson. What is this kind of teaching story called?

In this parable, a younger son takes his inheritance, squanders it in a distant land, and returns home hoping to be treated as a servant. His father welcomes him with a feast, while the older brother objects to the celebration. What is this story commonly called?
In Genesis, this patriarch fathered twelve sons who became the eponymous ancestors of the Tribes of Israel. He was married to Leah and Rachel. Who was he?
After Jacob wrestled through the night at Penuel, the biblical account says he received a new name reflecting that he had striven with God and with men. What was this name?

In this widespread European folk tale, an abused young woman receives supernatural help to attend a royal ball, and a prince eventually identifies her through a token she leaves behind. What is the tale’s natural name?

Which pair of German folklorists included a Cinderella variant called Aschenputtel in their collection *Children’s and Household Tales*? In their version, birds near a tree planted on the heroine’s mother’s grave help her.

This fifth-century Christian position rejected the claim that Adam’s fall left all people inheriting a condition that prevents them from choosing moral good. It emphasized human freedom in making moral choices. What is this theological position called?

During the fifth-century controversy over Pelagianism, which North African bishop and theologian argued that inherited sin made divine grace essential for salvation? He wrote *Confessions* and *The City of God* and became a major voice against the position.

This Jewish festival commemorates the thwarting of Haman’s decree against the Jews of the Persian Empire, and its name refers to the lots he cast to choose the date. Observed on the 14th of Adar, it includes a public reading of the Book of Esther. What is the festival called?

During Purim, most communities celebrate on the 14th of Adar, while Jerusalem and other traditionally walled cities observe the festival on the 15th, recalling the extra day of fighting in the Persian capital. What is this later observance called?

Born Sétanta, this Ulster hero earned a new name after killing the smith Culann’s guard dog and volunteering to serve in its place until a replacement was raised. At seventeen, he defended Ulster alone against the forces of Connacht. What name is he best known by?
Cú Chulainn traveled to Dún Scáith on the Isle of Skye to receive martial training from this famed woman warrior. Who was his teacher?
Cú Chulainn’s legendary spear was described as having multiple barbs that opened inside a victim, making its removal devastating. What was this weapon called?

In the Ulster Cycle, this Irish epic tells of Queen Medb’s attempt to seize the Brown Bull of Cooley and Cú Chulainn’s defense of Ulster against her forces. What is the work’s traditional Irish title?

These supernatural craftsmen in Norse mythology made wondrous treasures for the gods, including a self-replenishing ring and a ship that could be folded up and carried in a pouch. What are these beings commonly called?

In a famous tale about Dwarves, the brothers Brokkr and Sindri forged this weapon for Þórr after Loki wagered his head. Loki disrupted the work, leaving its handle shorter than intended; name the weapon.
Dwarves Fjalarr and Galarr killed the wise being Kvasir and mixed his blood with honey to make this drink, which grants poetic skill to those who consume it. What is the legendary beverage called?

In Zoroastrian worship, this sacred element is ritually maintained in temples and associated with purity, wisdom, and light. Its properly tended flame and ash also figure in purification practices. What is this sacred fire called?
Atar is associated with this Amesha Spenta, one of six divine beings created by Ahura Mazda whose domain includes fire and moral order. Which divine being is it?

Zoroastrian communities maintain Atar in places of worship, with smaller temples distinguished from grand temples classified as Atash Behrams. What is the established name for a smaller Zoroastrian fire temple?

This broad religious tradition, whose Sanskrit name means “Great Vehicle,” became visible in India in the early centuries CE and later encompassed East Asian schools such as Zen and Pure Land. Its defining aspiration joins the pursuit of Buddhahood with compassionate efforts to free all beings from suffering. What tradition is this?
In Mahayana Buddhism, practitioners following this principle aspire to Buddhahood while cultivating wisdom and compassion to help all beings become free from suffering. What is this path called?
His birth name was Vardhamana, and Jains revere him as the 24th and final Tirthankara of the present cycle. Who was this ascetic teacher whose teachings emphasized nonviolence and self-discipline?
Mahavira renewed rather than originated a Jain lineage that was already established. Which earlier Tirthankara, traditionally numbered 23rd, is associated with that preexisting community?

In John’s Gospel, Jesus gives this Galilean fisherman a name translated from Cephas as “the Rock.” Christian tradition remembers him as a leading apostle martyred in Rome and regards him as the first pope. Who is this apostle?

Saint Peter was called by Jesus alongside this brother, who also worked as a Galilean fisherman. In John’s Gospel, this apostle first follows Jesus after encountering John the Baptist, then brings his brother to Jesus. Who is he?

This monotheistic Abrahamic faith arose in western Arabia in the early seventh century, and its followers are known as Muslims. Its central scripture is the Qur’an, and its worship includes five foundational acts.

In Islam, this annual pilgrimage to Mecca is one of the Five Pillars and is performed during the month of Dhu al-Hijjah. Its rites include circumambulating the Kaaba and gathering at the plain of Arafat.
In Islam, this term refers to the Prophet Muhammad’s normative example, including his conduct and teachings. Hadith reports preserve accounts that help document this source of guidance.

In Islamic history, this city was the destination of Muhammad’s migration from Mecca in 622, an event known as the Hijra. Formerly called Yathrib, it is the city where Muhammad is buried and is Islam’s second-holiest city.
According to Islam, Muhammad received his first Qur’anic revelation around 610 CE while in the Cave of Hira near Mecca. Which angel is said to have delivered it?
Islamic jurisprudence uses this Arabic term for actions or things prohibited by religious law, with pork and alcohol commonly cited as examples. What is this category called?
In Islamic jurisprudence, conduct labeled haram is assessed in light of this central scripture, which is organized into surahs and begins with Al-Fatiha. What is the scripture called?
In Irish folklore, what mischievous fairy is traditionally portrayed as a small, bearded shoemaker and associated with hidden wealth?
In modern stories about the Leprechaun, what colorful arc in the sky is said to mark the distant endpoint where concealed treasure may be found?

Which Hindu philosophical school, traditionally associated with Samkhya, pursues liberation through disciplined practice and shares its name with a system commonly associated with meditation and postures?
In Hindu philosophical discussions associated with Yoga, what Sanskrit term names the individual self or soul, whose existence is affirmed by many orthodox schools?

What Buddhist tradition developed in the Himalayan region, combines Mahayana philosophy and the bodhisattva ideal with Vajrayana practice, and includes lineages such as Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya, and Gelug? These lineages share teachings and transmissions rather than forming completely separate religions.

Within Tibetan Buddhism, which major translated collection contains texts regarded as the Buddha’s own words, in contrast to its companion collection of commentaries by Indian masters? It is paired with the Tengyur.

Originating in the Punjab in the late 15th century, this monotheistic Indian religion was founded on the teachings of Guru Nanak and developed through a line of ten human gurus. What is this religion?
In Sikhism, which founder was born in 1469 at Rai Bhoi di Talwandi, now known as Nankana Sahib? His teachings emphasized devotion to one creator and the equality of all people.
In Sikhism, what order did Guru Gobind Singh establish in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib? Its members are associated with the ideal of the saint-soldier and with a formal initiation ceremony.
In Sikhism, what scripture did the tenth and final human leader designate as his successor? Sikhs regard it as their eternally living 11th spiritual authority.
In Sikhism, what is the name for the free communal meal served at a gurdwara? Open to people of every background, it expresses the values of equality and selfless service.

A Pauline letter calls this associate of Paul “the beloved physician,” and early Christian tradition credits him with two New Testament works addressed to Theophilus: one recounting Jesus’ life and the other the spread of the early church. Who is this associate?

Luke the Evangelist is traditionally credited with writing this New Testament sequel to his Gospel, addressed to Theophilus and tracing the early Christian community’s growth from Jerusalem through Paul’s journeys to Rome. What is this book?
The sea hazards called the Planctae and Symplegades, the marker of the world’s center at Delphi, and the burden in Sisyphus’s endless uphill task all belong to what shared mythological subject?
In accounts of Rocks in Greek mythology, which clashing pair blocked the Argonauts’ route at the entrance to the Black Sea? A dove tested the gap before the crew attempted to pass.

What collective name is given to the three primordial giants Cottus, Gyges, and Briareus, children of Gaia and Uranus who fought alongside Zeus against the Titans? Each was described as having one hundred hands and fifty heads.
Among the Hecatoncheires, which member does Homer say the gods called by one name while mortals knew him as Aegaeon? He was one of the giants whose strength helped the Olympians defeat the Titans.

European folklore describes this undead, human-like being as feeding on the blood or vital essence of the living. Some accounts say it returned to its former community to bring mischief or death. What creature is meant?
In Romanian folklore, what is the regional name for a vampire-like undead being, distinct from Albania’s shtriga and Greece’s vrykolakas?
Which 1872 novella by Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu became a notable early work about a female vampire, published before Bram Stoker’s Dracula?

In a traditional Christian diocese, which church serves as the bishop’s official seat? These buildings are often distinguished by monumental architecture, including soaring spires and stained-glass windows.
Among Mexico’s cathedrals, the central church in the capital of Jalisco blends Gothic and Baroque influences. What is this second-most-populous city in Mexico?

In the Völsunga saga, this son of Hreiðmarr takes possession of the cursed treasure won from the dwarf Andvari and transforms into a dragon to guard it. Sigurd later kills him while he drinks from a stream, striking from a trench beneath his path. Which figure is described?

In the Völsunga saga, this hero kills Fáfnir by waiting in a trench along the dragon’s route to a watering place and striking from below. Afterward, he roasts the dragon’s heart and gains the ability to understand birds. Which hero is this?

Which traditional East Asian system repeats every twelve years, assigning each year one of twelve animal signs popularly linked with personality, compatibility, and fortune? Its animals include the rat, ox, tiger, and dragon.

In one convention for marking a new sign in the Chinese zodiac, the cycle turns over at a movable lunar-calendar festival rather than at the start of spring. Celebrated with family reunions and red envelopes, this holiday falls between late January and mid-February. What is it?
The Chinese zodiac includes one creature that is legendary rather than an ordinary animal, and its sign is fifth in the cycle, following the rat, ox, tiger, and rabbit. Which creature is it?

In the origin story commonly told about the Chinese zodiac, this heavenly ruler organized a race whose finish order established the sequence of animal years. The rat took first place after riding on the ox and leaping ahead near the finish. Who hosted the race?
Which principal Hindu deity is identified as the Preserver in the Trimurti alongside Brahma and Shiva? The meaning of this deity’s name is commonly glossed as “All-Pervasive.”
Which avatar of Vishnu advises the prince Arjuna while serving as his charioteer during the Kurukshetra War? Their conversation is preserved in the Bhagavad Gita.
In traditional depictions, Vishnu rests on the coils of which serpent in the Ocean of Milk? This serpent is also associated with time.
What Christian title for Jesus presents him as the blameless sacrificial victim, drawing on Jewish sacrificial imagery and Isaiah 53’s description of a servant led to slaughter like an animal?
Which figure identifies Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world? He had baptized Jesus in the Jordan River.

In religious eschatology, what name is given to the anticipated cosmic ending or transformation of the world’s present order, which may bring renewal rather than mere annihilation? The term derives from a Greek word meaning “unveiling” or “revelation.”
In Zoroastrian accounts of the apocalypse, the world’s final consummation defeats evil, raises the dead, and renews creation. What is this final renovation called?

In Sophocles’ tragedy often regarded as a model of Greek tragedy, this king of Thebes investigates the murder of Laius to end a crisis in his city. His inquiry reveals that he unknowingly killed Laius and married Jocasta; name the central figure.

In the Oedipus myth, what winged creature with a human face and a lion’s body threatens Thebes with a riddle? Oedipus defeats it by answering “man,” whose life progresses from crawling to walking to using a staff.

In the Devi Mahatmya, this fierce Hindu goddess emerges from Devi’s forehead during battle and helps defeat demons. She is often shown with dark skin, an extended tongue, and a garland of severed heads; who is she?
In a famous battle story involving Kali, this demon’s blood creates a new demon whenever a drop reaches the ground. Kali drinks his blood to prevent the multiplying from continuing; what is his name?

The rules governing which land animals may be eaten require them to chew the cud and have split hooves, while permitted fish must have fins and scales. What is the name of this Jewish dietary-law system, which also includes rules for keeping meat and dairy separate?
Under Kashrut, what term describes foods that are neither meat nor dairy and form a distinct category in Jewish dietary practice?

In Islamic dietary practice, this designation marks food that Muslims are permitted to consume under religious law; beyond food, it can describe permissible conduct more generally. What is this designation called?

In discussions of Halal alongside other Islamic practices, what is the name of the ritual washing Muslims ordinarily perform before prayer, involving washing specified parts of the body? Its dry substitute, tayammum, uses clean earth when water cannot be used.

Born in 1469 in the Punjab region, this poet and spiritual teacher became the first of Sikhism’s ten successive spiritual teachers. His hymns and teachings about one God and human equality helped establish the faith. Who was he?

Guru Nanak’s teachings use this brief expression to affirm one divine reality present throughout creation and embodying eternal truth. It appears at the opening of the Mul Mantar; what is this foundational Sikh formula?
Guru Nanak’s 38-pauri composition appears near the beginning of Sikhism’s central scripture and is recited by Sikhs as part of daily morning prayers. What is its title?

In Norse prophecy, this cataclysmic sequence begins with Fimbulwinter and culminates in a battle where Odin and Thor die. After the world is burned and submerged, it rises again, and the human survivors Líf and Lífþrasir repopulate it. What is this foretold event?
During Ragnarök, which thunder god fights the world-serpent Jörmungandr, kills it, and then dies after taking nine steps from its venom? His hammer is called Mjölnir.

Which 13th-century collection, compiled from earlier traditional sources, is a principal source for accounts of Ragnarök? It preserves Norse mythological poems and is distinct from Snorri Sturluson's prose handbook.
In Greek myth, this divine bird was sent to the Caucasus to consume Prometheus’s liver, which grew back each day. Zeus also took the form of this bird to carry Ganymede to Olympus.
In the myth involving the Eagle, which Trojan youth did Zeus carry to Olympus to serve as the gods’ cupbearer?
In Islamic practice, this devotional discipline involves abstaining from food and drink, and its obligatory observance takes place during Ramadan. What is the Arabic name for this practice?
Islamic fasting is obligatory during a lunar month that concludes with Eid al-Fitr. What is the name of that month?

This foundational K’iche’ Maya sacred narrative combines a creation account with the adventures of the Hero Twins, Hunahpú and Xbalanqué, and a chronicle of K’iche’ history. It also recounts their encounters with the underworld Xibalba; what is the name of this work?
An 18th-century Spanish Dominican friar documented the Popol Vuh by producing a K’iche’ transcription alongside Spanish translations. What was this friar’s name?

The title of the Popol Vuh is translated as “Book of the Community” or “Book of Counsel,” and its name refers to an object that served as a royal throne and symbolized communal unity in ancient K’iche’ society. What was this object?

In this recurring mythological pattern, a culture hero or trickster obtains a life-changing flame from a god or other supernatural keeper and brings it to human beings. The act may lead to punishment by its original owner; what is this motif called?

Within the Stealing Fire motif, which Greek Titan defied Zeus by carrying the divine flame to humanity and was later bound to a mountain as an eagle repeatedly ate his liver? His story is among the best-known classical examples of this motif.

This Egyptian goddess was famed for magic and healing, and was worshipped as a protective mother. In the Osiris myth, she gathered and restored her murdered husband’s remains and later bore and protected his heir. Name her.
A major sanctuary of Isis stood on an island in the Nile near Aswan and drew worshippers from both Egypt and Nubia. What was this island temple complex called?

In Egyptian myth, Isis concealed and raised this falcon-associated son after Osiris’s death; as an adult, he fought Set to claim his father’s kingship. What is the name of this god, whom pharaohs were understood to embody?

The husband and brother of Isis, this god was murdered and dismembered by Set, then restored sufficiently to rule over the dead rather than return to earthly kingship. Who is this central figure of the Egyptian afterlife?
After Perseus decapitated Medusa, this winged horse sprang from her blood alongside Chrysaor. Later associated with Bellerophon and the Chimera, what was this horse called?
With Athena’s help, which Greek hero captured Pegasus at the Peirene fountain and rode him against the Chimera?
On Mount Helicon, Pegasus was said to have brought forth this spring with a strike of his hoof. What was the spring called?

Mongol ruler Altan Khan bestowed this title on Sonam Gyatso in the sixteenth century; it was later applied retroactively to two earlier teachers, making Sonam the third holder. What is the title of this Tibetan Buddhist reincarnate lineage?
In Tibetan Buddhist tradition, Dalai Lamas are regarded as manifestations of this bodhisattva of compassion, who is often depicted with multiple arms. What is the bodhisattva’s name?

In ancient Egyptian funerary belief, this organ was retained as evidence of the deceased’s conduct. After death, it was weighed against the feather of Ma’at to assess the person’s moral worthiness. What is the organ?

The heart in ancient Egyptian afterlife judgment is weighed in a scene associated with a New Kingdom funerary compilation. This work developed from earlier traditions represented by the Pyramid Texts and Coffin Texts; what is it commonly called in English?

This religious practice is a way of communicating with or worshipping a deity, and it may be performed individually or communally. In the Baháʼí Faith, some forms are obligatory, while Muslims perform it five times each day at appointed times.

In Islam, this formal prayer is performed five times daily at prescribed times, and its beginning is traditionally announced by a muezzin’s call to worship. What is this Arabic-named practice, distinct from informal personal supplication?

In the standard Akkadian epic, this king of Uruk survives the slaying of Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven but is shaken when his close companion dies. His journey to find Utnapishtim leads across the Waters of Death and ends with a rejuvenating plant being stolen by a serpent; name this Mesopotamian hero.

Gilgamesh’s companion was created by the goddess Aruru as a wild man to challenge the king, then became his friend after they wrestled. The gods sentenced him to die after the killing of Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven, prompting Gilgamesh to seek everlasting life; identify this figure.
In Greek mythology, this hybrid being has a human upper body and a horse’s body and legs. Myths place these creatures in Thessaly and include figures such as Nessus.
Unlike many members of his kind, this centaur was famed for his wisdom and taught heroes including Achilles and Jason. In one myth, he surrendered his immortality so Prometheus could be freed.
The centaur race’s attempted abduction of Hippodamia at her wedding to Pirithous led to a battle with the Lapiths. What is the conventional name for this conflict?

In some Arthurian legends, wearing one of these objects makes Perceval or Gareth invulnerable. More broadly, this recurring mythological and literary object can grant protection, transformation, or other supernatural powers. What is it called?

In Tolkien’s legendarium, Sauron forged this magic ring in the fires of Orodruin to control the other Rings of Power. Its inscription is in Black Speech, and bearing it can make a person invisible. What is its name?

This Abrahamic monotheistic religion began in first-century Judaea and is centered on the life, teachings, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Its four canonical accounts of his life are Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. What is this religion?

In 325, Emperor Constantine summoned bishops within Christianity to resolve the Arian controversy, rejecting the claim that the Son was created and declaring him of the same substance as the Father. What major event established this formulation?

Within Christianity, what term describes efforts to foster unity and cooperation among churches separated by different traditions and institutions? Such efforts can include dialogue among Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant communities.

What term describes existence that continues without end, whether imagined as the survival of a soul, a spirit-like form, or a body restored after death? It is more specific than an afterlife, which does not necessarily last forever.
Which Qin ruler reportedly took mercury pills in pursuit of immortality and unified the Warring States to found the Qin dynasty? His burial complex is famous for its army of terracotta soldiers.

In the Catholic Church, beatification is a preliminary step, and the final process may involve confirmation of miracles attributed to a deceased person's intercession. What is the formal process that declares that person a saint?
During the canonization of Hungary's first king in 1083, this pope was pontiff; he is also remembered for his conflict with Emperor Henry IV during the Investiture Controversy. Who was he?

What corpus of ancient Egyptian funerary spells was inscribed on the walls of royal burial chambers during the Old Kingdom? Its earliest known examples appear in the burial complex of Unas at Saqqara.
Within the Pyramid Texts, which composition portrays the deceased king consuming gods to acquire their powers? Its modern name reflects this striking imagery.
Preached during the First Great Awakening in 1741, this sermon warned listeners of divine judgment and used the image of a spider suspended over a fiery pit. What is the sermon called?
answer: Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God

question: At Enfield, Connecticut, in 1741, this sermon became one of the best-known addresses of the First Great Awakening. Which minister preached Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God?

In Acts, after a sound like a rushing wind at Pentecost, Jesus’s followers produce utterances that visitors from many regions recognize as their own languages. What Christian ecstatic practice, also discussed alongside interpretation in Paul’s letters to Corinth, is described by this episode?

In Pentecostal teaching, speaking in tongues is often cited as evidence that a believer has been baptized by which member of the Trinity? Christian art commonly depicts this divine person as a dove, including in scenes of Jesus’s baptism.

In The Prophet, Almustafa’s closing address describes a feared passage as a brief rest on the wind before renewal, and compares fear of it to a shepherd trembling before a king. What existential subject does he discuss?

Which Lebanese-American poet and painter wrote The Prophet, whose closing lecture on death includes Almustafa’s assurance that “another woman shall bear me”? The book frames his farewell through conversations with the citizens of Orphalese.
What term names the purported use of supernatural or magical powers, a concept historically associated with accusations, persecutions, and witch hunts?

Within the history of witchcraft, what 1692 Massachusetts episode began after Betty Parris and Abigail Williams reported afflictions and led to the execution of 19 people accused of practicing forbidden magic?

The animal that produces this meat is singled out in Leviticus because it has a split hoof but does not chew its cud. Both Jewish dietary law and Islamic dietary law prohibit eating it. What is this meat commonly called?
In Jewish law, pork is forbidden under a broader system governing which foods and preparation methods are permitted. What is the Hebrew name for this system of Jewish dietary laws?

In Jewish homes, these are traditionally kindled shortly before sunset on Friday to welcome the weekly day of rest. Their lighting is accompanied by a blessing and often takes place near the table prepared for the evening meal.

At the close of the weekly day of rest, a braided flame is held over wine and then extinguished as part of a rite marking the transition to the coming week. This ceremony follows the period welcomed by lighting Shabbat candles; what is it called?
What ritual practice, associated in several Indo-European traditions with kingship and warfare, is exemplified by Rome’s Equus October and the Vedic Ashvamedha?
In Vedic tradition, which royal Horse Sacrifice sent a consecrated stallion to roam for a year under a ruler’s protection, with the rite asserting the ruler’s sovereignty?

This worldwide Christian communion includes the Latin Church and 23 autonomous Eastern churches, with local communities organized into dioceses or eparchies led by bishops. Its bishop of Rome is regarded as the successor of Saint Peter and has a primary pastoral role over the church headquartered in Vatican City. What is this church called?

The Roman Catholic Church used this 16th-century ecumenical assembly to respond to Protestant challenges, reaffirm doctrines such as the sacraments, and pursue internal reforms. It met in phases from 1545 to 1563 in a city in northern Italy. What was this assembly called?
In the Roman Catholic Church, what Greek-derived term names the central sacrament celebrated at Mass in which Catholics believe consecrated bread and wine become Christ’s body and blood?

The Roman Catholic Church’s central governing offices are based in this independent enclave surrounded by Rome, whose sovereignty was recognized by the Lateran Treaty of 1929. What is this state, the world’s smallest by area?
Which medieval Icelandic work, compiled by Snorri Sturluson, begins with Gylfaginning and preserves the account of Baldr’s death?
In the Prose Edda’s Gylfaginning, which chief god joins his brothers Vili and Vé in slaying the primordial giant Ymir, and elsewhere hangs himself from Yggdrasil to gain wisdom?

In Japanese folklore, what is the name for fox spirits that can transform into human beings and are often portrayed as messengers of a kami? Some legends give the wisest among them as many as nine tails.

Kitsune are closely associated with which kami, traditionally linked with rice, agriculture, and prosperity? This kami is honored at a major shrine complex in Kyoto and is often represented by fox messengers.
What Japanese ascetic practice involved Buddhist monks enduring extreme fasting and ritual austerities before death in hopes that their bodies would be preserved after death?

Sokushinbutsu is often discussed in the context of a Japanese mountain-ascetic tradition whose practitioners, called yamabushi, train in sacred mountains and perform esoteric Buddhist rites. What is this tradition called?
This is the Quran’s second and longest surah, and it includes the account of Harut and Marut. What is its Arabic name?
In Al-Baqarah, which verse at 2:255 is widely recited for protection and describes God’s authority over the heavens and the earth?

This Akan and broader West African trickster is usually depicted as a spider and is famed for securing the world’s stories from Nyame through a series of difficult tasks. His tales later became influential in African American and Caribbean folklore. Identify this figure.
Anansi obtained the world’s stories from this Akan sky deity by capturing Onini the python, Osebo the leopard, and the Mmboro hornets as payment. What is the name of the deity who set that task?

Anansi’s storytelling legacy crossed into African American folklore, where this clever, long-eared trickster is covered in pitch and thrown into a briar patch. He appears in Joel Chandler Harris’s Uncle Remus stories alongside figures such as Br’er Fox. Identify this character.
In Rastafari, this name for God is derived from a shortened form of the Hebrew divine name represented by the tetragrammaton. What is this name?

This Afrocentric Abrahamic movement developed in Jamaica in the early 20th century. Its followers use the name Jah for God and many regard Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie I as the second coming of Christ; what is the movement called?

In Haitian Vodou’s Rada tradition, this elderly lwa is associated with crossroads and acts as a mediator between people and other spirits. He can grant permission to approach or speak with other lwa; who is he?

Papa Legba is the Rada lwa associated with crossroads, but he is not the same figure as his counterpart in another nation. What distinct crossroads divinity does Duke University’s Sacred Arts project associate with the Petwo nation?

This Celtic or Gallo-Roman deity is commonly depicted with antlers and is associated with animals, the natural world, and fertility. One of his best-known ancient representations appears on a monument erected by Parisian boatmen.

Cernunnos appears on this Gallo-Roman monument commissioned by the boatmen of ancient Paris during the reign of Emperor Tiberius. Its carved blocks were discovered beneath Notre-Dame Cathedral in 1710.

This major Jewish festival begins on 15 Nisan, with its first Seder held after sunset on the preceding evening. Its name recalls the tenth plague, when marked Israelite doorways were spared in Egypt. What is this festival?
At a Passover Seder, participants use this ritual book to guide the proceedings and retell the Exodus story. Its Magid section is devoted to recounting that story. What is the book called?

During Passover, this Hebrew term names leavened foods that observant Jews are forbidden to eat or possess. It includes leavened grain products excluded in favor of unleavened matzah. What is the term?

In Inca religion, which deity embodied the Sun and served as a divine source of imperial legitimacy, with Inca rulers tracing their ancestry to him? His principal sanctuary stood in Cusco at Qorikancha.

In Cusco, what Inca temple complex served as the principal sanctuary of Inti and was famed for walls once sheathed in gold? Its Quechua name is commonly translated as “Golden Enclosure,” and its foundations now support the Church of Santo Domingo.

In Homer’s Odyssey, this six-headed sea monster lurked in the Strait of Messina and seized six of Odysseus’s sailors as his ship passed. It guarded the passage opposite the whirlpool Charybdis. What is the monster’s name?
Scylla was one of two perils Odysseus faced while sailing through the Strait of Messina. What was the name of the opposing threat, a whirlpool that could swallow ships?

Written in response to claims that Christianity caused Rome’s troubles after the city’s sack in 410, this treatise contrasts a community shaped by love of God with one shaped by earthly ambitions. What work by Augustine examines history and the destinies of these two cities?

The City of God was written by the North African bishop who described stealing pears as a young man in his spiritual memoir, Confessions. What theologian recounted his conversion from Manichaeism in that work?

In Dante’s medieval poem, Virgil guides the pilgrim through this realm, which is divided into nine circles where sinners receive punishments suited to their misdeeds. Christian theology also describes it as the place of punishment for the wicked after death. What is this place?
In Dante’s depiction of Hell, which ancient Roman poet guides the pilgrim through the Inferno and represents human reason, but cannot accompany him into Paradise?
In Japanese religious practice, what sacred rope, traditionally made from rice straw or hemp, is placed around trees, rocks, and shrine spaces to mark their sacred status?
Shimenawa are often hung around places or natural objects believed to be inhabited by what beings in Shinto, whose name is commonly translated as gods or spirits?
