In Greek mythology, she was the only mortal among the three Gorgons, whose other two sisters were Euryale and Stheno. Perseus beheaded her using Athena’s reflective shield to avoid her petrifying gaze; who was she?

This son of Danae and Zeus received a reflective shield from Athena and winged sandals from Hermes, which helped him approach Medusa without looking directly at her. After beheading her, he later rescued Andromeda from a sea monster; who was this hero?

In ancient Greek art, what term names the image of Medusa’s severed head, used on shields, armor, and buildings as a protective emblem to ward off evil? The motif takes its name from the Gorgon whose gaze was said to turn onlookers to stone.
Founded in Seoul in 1954 by Sun Myung Moon, this Christian-derived movement became especially known for mass wedding ceremonies called Blessings. What is the movement’s natural name?

The Unification Church’s central doctrinal text describes its account of creation, the fall of humanity, and restoration. It also presents the movement’s teachings about the Messiah’s mission and the establishment of ideal families. What is this text called?

The Unification Church honors this woman and Sun Myung Moon together as the movement’s “True Parents.” Moon’s wife, she later became a leading figure in the Family Federation for World Peace and Unification. Who is she?
Which biblical book recounts a vision of four beasts and a little horn, and interprets a ruler’s dream of a statue made from gold, silver, bronze, iron, and clay?
In the Book of Daniel, this Babylonian king dreams of a colossal statue whose golden head represents his own kingdom. Daniel interprets the statue as a succession of kingdoms; who is the king?

This Greek goddess, daughter of Zeus and Leto, is the twin sister of Apollo and is associated with hunting, wilderness, and childbirth; later tradition also connected her with the moon. Which deity is described?
In a famous myth involving Artemis, a hunter came upon her bathing and was transformed into a stag; his own hounds then killed him. What hunter met this fate?
Dedicated to Artemis in an ancient Ionian city on the western coast of Asia Minor, this monumental sanctuary was counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. What famous structure was it?
Which Trojan princess, daughter of Priam and Hecuba, was granted the power to foresee the future but cursed so that no one would believe her prophecies, even when she warned of Troy’s destruction?
In the Cassandra myth, which Greek god associated with light and prophecy, and twin brother of Artemis, gave her the gift of foresight and cursed her after she rejected his advances?

In Aztec mythology, this earth-and-mother goddess was sweeping when a ball of feathers miraculously impregnated her. She later gave birth to Huitzilopochtli and the Centzon Huitznahua; what was her name?

In the myth of Coatlicue’s miraculous pregnancy, this group of four hundred siblings joined their sister Coyolxauhqui in attacking the newborn Huitzilopochtli. Associated with the southern stars, what were they collectively called?
In Greek mythology, this daughter of Coeus and Phoebe was pursued by Hera during her pregnancy and found refuge on the island of Delos, where she gave birth to Apollo and Artemis. Who was she?

According to Greek myth, this island gave Leto refuge when other lands feared Hera’s anger, and it was where she gave birth to Apollo and Artemis. What island later became a major sanctuary of Apollo?

At the marsh of Lerna in the Argolid, this many-headed serpent was the target of Heracles’ second labor. In later versions of the myth, cutting off one head caused two to grow back. What creature was it?

Which hero fought the Lernaean Hydra as the second of the twelve labors imposed by Eurystheus? He defeated it with help from his nephew, who cauterized the severed necks to stop them from regenerating.
During the fight with the Lernaean Hydra, Heracles’ nephew used fire to cauterize the monster’s necks after its heads were cut off. What was the nephew’s name?

Convened by Pope Pius IX, this major Catholic gathering began in December 1869 at Saint Peter’s Basilica in Rome. Its proceedings were suspended in 1870 as the Kingdom of Italy seized the city. What was this gathering?

At the First Vatican Council, delegates adopted an 1870 dogmatic constitution on the primacy and teaching authority of the Roman pontiff, including certain definitive rulings made ex cathedra. What was the Latin title of this constitution?

What is the natural name of the Hindu grouping that brings together Saraswati, Lakshmi, and Parvati as the feminine counterpart to the Trimurti? It is a triad of major goddesses rather than a grouping of male deities.

Within the Tridevi, which goddess is associated with wisdom and learning, is traditionally the consort of Brahma, and is commonly depicted playing a veena? Her musical attribute links her to the arts as well as knowledge.

In Aztec religion, which powerful deity was associated with night, fate, rulership, sorcery, and conflict with Quetzalcoatl over who would serve as the sun? This figure was also known by an epithet meaning “Smoking Mirror.”
In Aztec accounts of successive suns, this feathered-serpent deity clashed with Tezcatlipoca over control of the sun and was also associated with wind. Which deity is described?

In Jewish, Christian, and Islamic traditions, this practice is condemned as treating a created thing as divine, and the First Commandment prohibits it. In Islam, it is called shirk. What is this practice?

In Exodus, Moses returns from Sinai with the tablets and finds the Israelites worshiping an image Aaron made from their jewelry; he smashes the tablets in anger. What object became a famous biblical example of idolatry?

An American religious leader born in Sharon, Vermont, in 1805 organized a new church in New York on April 6, 1830, and became its first president. He was killed by a mob at Carthage, Illinois, in 1844; who was he?
In the account associated with Joseph Smith, an ancient record he said was engraved on gold plates was translated by divine power and published in 1830. What is the title of that scripture?
In Polynesian mythology, a magical jawbone implement is used in stories of catching the sun and, in some traditions, hauling islands up from the sea. What is this object commonly called?
Māui’s fish hook is used in one Polynesian myth to snare a celestial body and restrain its movement, giving people more daylight. Which celestial body is it?

After Semele died while pregnant with Zeus’s child, the ruler of Olympus rescued the unborn god and carried him sewn into his own body until gestation was complete. What is the name of this unusual episode in the god’s origin myth?
In the myth of Dionysus’s Second Birth, the infant god was carried until it was ready to be born. Into which body part did his father, the ruler of Olympus, sew the fetus?
In Hindu tradition, which grouping brings together three major deities associated respectively with creation, preservation, and destruction? Its members are Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
Within the Trimurti, which deity is associated with preservation and is worshipped through incarnations such as Rama and Krishna?
In Hesiod’s account, this Greek goddess of love and beauty arose from sea foam after Kronos cast Ouranos’s severed genitals into the sea. Which goddess is described?
In Hesiod’s account of Aphrodite’s arrival after emerging from the sea, she reached this island before continuing to Cyprus. The island’s name is also reflected in her epithet Cytherea; what is it?

Luke 1:26–38 places this event in Nazareth, where a heavenly messenger tells Mary she will bear Jesus, called the Son of God. Mary asks how this can happen before accepting the message; what is the name of this event, commemorated by Christians on March 25?
In the Annunciation narrative in Luke 1:26–38, which angel visits Mary and tells her that she will conceive through the Holy Spirit? Mary asks how this can happen before accepting the message.

In a Tibetan Buddhist funerary rite, the deceased is brought to a designated site and the body is exposed to scavenger birds, traditionally vultures, rather than buried or cremated. What is this practice called by its Tibetan name?
During Jhator, Tibetan ritual attendants prepare the exposed remains by cutting the body into pieces so scavenger birds can consume it. What are these attendants called?
In Jewish practice, this blessing is recited over wine or grape juice to sanctify Shabbat and festivals, often at the first meal on Friday night. What is this blessing called?
At the Friday-night Shabbat meal, the Kiddush is traditionally recited while this braided bread is covered; it is uncovered afterward for the meal. What is the bread called?

After King Oeneus failed to include Artemis in his offerings, a monstrous animal ravaged the countryside around his city. Meleager assembled renowned heroes to pursue it; a skilled archer wounded it first, and Meleager delivered the fatal blow. What Greek mythic episode was this?

During the Calydonian Boar Hunt, this famed huntress wounded the beast first, though Meleager struck the fatal blow. He awarded her the animal’s pelt, provoking a dispute with his uncles; who was she?

Sent by Agenor to search for his abducted sister Europa, this Phoenician prince consulted Apollo’s oracle at Delphi and followed a cow to the site of a new city in Boeotia. He became that city’s founder and first king after slaying a dragon sacred to Ares. Who was he?

In the Theban foundation story associated with Cadmus, Athena advised him to sow the teeth of the dragon he had slain. What name was given to the armed warriors who sprang from the earth, some of whom became ancestors of Theban noble families?
This Norse deity is a shape-shifter who engineered Baldr’s death and was later bound beneath a venom-dripping serpent, while Sigyn caught the venom in a bowl. Name this trickster figure.
To delay construction of Asgard’s wall, Loki transformed into a mare and mated with the stallion Svaðilfari. What eight-legged horse was born from that union and later served as Odin’s mount?
In accounts of Loki’s binding, what goddess remains beside him with a bowl to catch the serpent’s venom, emptying it only when the bowl fills?
What jötunn is identified as the mother of Hel, Fenrir, and Jörmungandr, the three children she bore with Loki?

Haitian and Louisiana traditions under this name are related African diasporic religions, but they developed in different places and have distinct histories and practices. What is the natural name for this broad religious topic?
In Haitian Voodoo, this transcendent creator stands above the lwa, who are approached through offerings, divination, and ceremonies. What is the name of this supreme being?

In Haitian Voodoo, this lwa is associated with crossroads and serves as a mediator who opens the way for communication between people and spirits. He is often depicted as an elderly man carrying a cane; who is he?
In Haitian Voodoo, ceremonies may take place in a dedicated temple led by an oungan or a manbo, rather than in a family setting or secret society. What is this kind of temple called?
Many Haitian Voodoo practitioners took part in this late-18th-century uprising against French colonial rule, which culminated in Haiti’s independence in 1804. What is this uprising called?

This Christian liturgical season is marked by prayer, fasting, repentance, and acts of generosity as worshippers prepare for Easter. Its traditional forty-day pattern recalls Jesus fasting and facing testing in the desert.

In the Western Christian calendar, Lent opens on this weekday, when worshippers may receive a cross of ashes on the forehead as a reminder of mortality. It falls 46 days before Easter Sunday, with Sundays omitted from the season’s traditional forty-day count.
This Greek king’s ten-year homecoming after the Trojan War is the central story of a Homeric epic. Known for his cunning intelligence, he is the hero of that poem. Who is he?

In Homer’s Odyssey, Odysseus returns to this wife after she has kept the suitors at bay by promising to choose a husband once she finishes weaving a burial shroud for Laertes, then secretly undoing the work each night. Who is she?
In the opening books of the Odyssey, Odysseus’s son travels to Pylos and Sparta to seek news of his missing father, consulting Nestor and Menelaus. What is this young prince’s name?
Odysseus’s home is this Ionian island kingdom, where Penelope waits through his absence and where he finally returns in disguise before confronting the suitors. What is the island called?

A seer foretold that this beautiful son of the river god Cephissus would live to old age only if he never came to know himself. In Ovid’s tale, he becomes captivated by his image in a pool and dies, after which a flower grows in his place. What youth is this?

After Narcissus rejects his admirers, one spurned youth prays that he too may experience unrequited love. In Ovid’s version, which goddess of retribution answers that plea, bringing about the episode at the pool?

In 1835, a revolt in Salvador, Brazil, was named using a term for members of this West African faith community. Estevanico and Bilali Fula are among the earliest documented people of this community in North America; what are its adherents called?
In January 1835, enslaved and freed West Africans, many of them Muslims, rose up in Salvador, Bahia, against slavery and colonial rule. What is this uprising known as?
This magical gold ring belonged to the Norse god Odin. Forged by the dwarven brothers Brokkr and Eitri, it produced eight identical rings every ninth night. What was the ring called?

In Norse mythology, Draupnir was one of the treasures delivered to this one-eyed Aesir god after Loki’s wager with the dwarf smiths. This god was also Baldr’s father, and Draupnir was placed on Baldr’s funeral pyre. Who was he?

Genesis locates this paradise eastward and describes a river there splitting into four branches. God places the first human there to tend it, and the narrative ends with the human pair expelled after eating from a forbidden tree. What is this place called?
In the Garden of Eden account, one branch of the river is described as flowing east of Assyria and is named immediately before the Euphrates. What is this river?
Which ancient Egyptian goddess was worshipped at Bubastis and associated with cats, protection, and fertility? She was often depicted with feline features.
Which city in the eastern Nile Delta was Bastet’s principal cult center and hosted a major annual festival in her honor?
Which major Mesopotamian goddess of love, war, and fertility is identified with the Sumerian goddess Inanna? In the Epic of Gilgamesh, she sends the Bull of Heaven after Gilgamesh rejects her.
After Gilgamesh rejects Ishtar, she asks Anu to unleash this divine beast against Uruk. Gilgamesh and Enkidu ultimately kill it.

In ancient Egyptian belief, this major deity traveled across the sky in a solar barque and continued through the underworld at night, with the voyage’s return marking the sun’s rebirth. He was associated with creation and kingship and was often depicted as a falcon-headed man wearing a sun disk. Who was this deity?

During Ra’s nighttime passage through the underworld, this great serpent attacked his solar boat and threatened the return of sunrise. The gods aboard the vessel fought this embodiment of chaos to preserve the voyage. What was the serpent called?
This nineteenth-century pontiff reigned from 1846 until his death in 1878. During his papacy, the Papal States were annexed by the Kingdom of Italy, and he issued the Syllabus of Errors; who was he?

During the reign of Pope Pius IX, papal authorities removed a six-year-old boy from his Jewish family in Bologna in 1858 after learning that a household servant had baptized him as an infant. What was the boy’s name?

In Greek myth, this king of Athens was the father of Theseus and arranged for his son to sail home from Crete with white sails if his quest succeeded. When the returning ship still bore black sails, he mistakenly believed his son had died. Who was this king?

Aegeus left a sword and sandals beneath a great rock at Troezen, telling his unborn son to retrieve them once he was strong enough to move it. Which woman, daughter of King Pittheus and the boy’s mother, raised him there?
In Hindu mythology, what name is given to serpent beings associated with water and fertility, sometimes depicted with human bodies and cobra hoods? Shesha and Vasuki are two named examples.
Among the nāgas, which serpent was wrapped around Mount Mandara and used as the rope when gods and asuras churned the Ocean of Milk to obtain amrita?
During Hajj, pilgrims cast small stones at three pillars in Mina, reenacting Ibrahim’s refusal to yield to Satan. What is this ritual commonly called?
The Stoning of the Devil is performed at three jamarat during Hajj. In what place near Mecca are these pillars located?
A self-governing peninsula in northern Greece is home to twenty Eastern Orthodox monasteries and has long been a major center of hesychasm. What is this mountain and monastic community called?
Mount Athos’s oldest monastery was founded in 963 by Athanasius the Athonite and stands at the peninsula’s southeastern end. What is this monastery known as?

In Revelation’s vision of four horsemen, this is the rider on the pale horse, following the figures associated with conquest, war, and famine. The text names him directly and says the realm of the dead follows behind him. Who is this rider?

In Revelation’s four-horse vision, Death rides a pale horse, and another figure follows him as a personification of the realm of the dead. What is the name of this figure, also known in Greek mythology as the ruler of the underworld?

In Norse cosmology, what is the fiery, rainbow-like bridge that links Asgard, the realm of the gods, with Midgard, the world of humans? It is guarded by a watchful god and is prophesied to be destroyed during Ragnarök.

Which Norse god guards Bifröst, the bridge between Asgard and Midgard, and is said to sound the Gjallarhorn at the beginning of Ragnarök? His extraordinary sight and hearing make him a vigilant divine sentinel.

What Hebrew term names the immigration of Jews to the Land of Israel, understood literally as an act of “going up”? In modern Israel, this migration is supported by a national law granting Jews the right to immigrate.
Aliyah is supported by an Israeli law passed in 1950 that grants Jews the right to immigrate to the country. What is this law called?

Associated especially with the Coptic, Syriac, Armenian, and Ethiopian Orthodox churches, this Christological position describes Christ’s divinity and humanity as united in one incarnate nature, without teaching that his humanity was swallowed up by divinity. What is this doctrine called?

Miaphysitism is often contrasted with a definition that Oriental Orthodox churches do not accept. Which gathering of bishops, held in Bithynia in 451, defined Christ as existing in two natures, divine and human?
Recognized at age two as his predecessor’s successor, enthroned in Lhasa in 1940, and awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989, Tenzin Gyatso is known by what numbered title in Tibetan Buddhism?
Tibetan Buddhist belief regards the 14th Dalai Lama as a manifestation of the bodhisattva of compassion, known in Tibetan as Chenrezig. What is this bodhisattva’s Sanskrit name?

Developed in Brazil from African religious traditions and local influences, this religion centers on the worship of orishas. Its communal ceremonies are held in temples known as terreiros. What is this religion?

Many orishas venerated in Candomblé come from the religious heritage of a people whose traditional homeland, Yorubaland, lies mainly in southwestern Nigeria and extends into neighboring Benin. Which people are they?

In Greek mythology, which Titan is credited in some accounts with shaping humans from clay and is famous for giving humanity the gods’ fire? Zeus punished him by binding him to a rock, where an eagle repeatedly consumed his regenerating liver.
Prometheus defied Zeus by taking what substance from the gods and giving it to humanity? In myth, this gift enabled human beings to keep warm, cook food, and develop their crafts.
In the traditional account of Prometheus’s punishment, what bird returned each day to eat his liver as it regrew? Zeus had chained the Titan to a rock in the Caucasus for his defiance.

Which 1818 novel by Mary Shelley explores a scientist who assembles a living being from body parts and then recoils from his creation? Its frame narrative includes Arctic explorer Robert Walton’s letters to his sister, and its subtitle alludes to Prometheus.
This diverse South Asian religious tradition has no single founder or central doctrinal authority, and its beliefs include karma, rebirth, and liberation. What is the name of this tradition?

In Hinduism, this Sanskrit text presents a dialogue in which Krishna advises the warrior Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. It forms a section of the Mahabharata and is often studied as a work in its own right. What is this text?

In Hinduism, this concept describes liberation from samsara, the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth. It is regarded as a spiritual goal beyond simply attaining a more favorable rebirth. What is this liberation called?
In Hinduism, this collection comprises four ancient sacred texts: the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda. What is the collective name for these texts?

This first-century Jewish preacher from Roman Judaea is the central figure of Christianity, and the canonical Gospels are the principal accounts of his life. Islam also recognizes him as the Messiah and a prophet, while rejecting his divinity. Who is he?

In the Gospels, Jesus Christ grows up in this town in Galilee after Joseph returns there with Mary and the child from Egypt. Christian tradition also associates the town with the Annunciation. What is it called?
According to the canonical Gospels, this Roman prefect of Judaea approved Jesus Christ’s execution by crucifixion after his trial. Who was the prefect?
Good Friday commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ, while Easter Sunday celebrates the event Christians regard as foundational to their faith. What is that event called?

Jesus Christ selected a core circle of disciples who traveled with him and were sent out to preach; Gospel lists include Simon Peter, Andrew, James, and John among them. What collective name is given to this group?
The New Testament contains accounts traditionally named for Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, recounting Jesus’s life, teachings, death, and resurrection. What collective title is given to these books?

In The Four Canonical Gospels, Matthew places this set of blessings in chapter 5 as part of the Sermon on the Mount. It begins, “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” What is this set of blessings called?

This Christian observance opens the penitential season before Easter. Worshipers traditionally receive a cross on the forehead and hear a reminder, echoing Genesis, that human life returns to dust. What is the day called?
Ash Wednesday opens this roughly 40-day Christian season of penitence, which leads toward Easter and recalls Jesus’ fasting in the wilderness. What is this liturgical season called?

Which Hebrew Bible book is set at the Persian royal court and tells how a Jewish woman who became queen, aided by her cousin Mordecai, helped thwart a decree against her people? Its events are traditionally associated with the Jewish festival of Purim.

In the Book of Esther, which royal vizier becomes enraged when Mordecai refuses to bow to him and devises a plan to destroy the Jews throughout the Persian Empire? The plot is reversed, and he is executed on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai.

In 325 CE, Emperor Constantine convened bishops in Bithynia to address a dispute over Arius’s teaching about Christ. The gathering also produced an early formulation of a creed still central to many Christian traditions; what was this gathering called?

The First Council of Nicaea produced the initial version of this Christian statement of faith, later expanded and recited in many churches. It affirms that the Son is of one substance with the Father; what is the statement commonly called?

In ancient Egyptian funerary practice, priests performed a ceremony on a mummy or statue to restore its bodily and sensory abilities for life beyond death. What ritual was intended to let the deceased eat, drink, breathe, and speak in the afterlife?

During the Opening of the Mouth ceremony, priests used a distinctive forked ritual implement, often made of flint in early examples, to symbolically restore the deceased’s ability to use the mouth. What was this implement called?

Classical tales recount the violent story of Procne, Tereus, and Philomela, whose human forms are changed into winged creatures. A separate tale gives a similar fate to the sisters who lose a singing contest against the Muses. What mythological topic brings these narratives together?

In Bird Metamorphoses in Greek Mythology, which group of sisters challenged the Muses to a singing contest and was turned into birds after losing? Unlike Procne and Philomela, these challengers were punished for their musical hubris.
Rooted in Iranian traditions, this spring festival is celebrated at the vernal equinox and often includes family visits and a symbolic haft-sin table. What is the festival called?
In the Bahá’í calendar, Nowruz begins the new year and follows a 19-day observance in which believers refrain from eating and drinking between dawn and sunset. What is this annual period called?
Founded in 1830 by Joseph Smith and headquartered in Utah, this restorationist Christian church became closely associated with Brigham Young after Smith’s death. What is the church’s natural name?
answer: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

question: In the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, which leader succeeded Joseph Smith as head of the largest group of followers and led their migration west to the Salt Lake Valley?

The Greek underworld river Phlegethon was said to flow with this substance, and the phoenix represents its power to destroy and renew by rising from its ashes. What did Prometheus steal from the gods and give to humanity?
Within myths of Mythological Fire, which Titan stole the gods’ flame for humanity and was punished by Zeus with an eagle devouring his liver each day?
In traditional Christian teaching, this group consists of the principal vices commonly named as lust, wrath, pride, greed, envy, gluttony, and sloth. What is this group called?

A precursor to the familiar list of the Seven Deadly Sins, this fourth-century Christian monk described eight destructive thoughts while living among the monks of the Egyptian desert. His scheme included vainglory and dejection, and later influenced John Cassian. Who was he?

In Greek myth, this goddess’s grief when her daughter was taken to the underworld caused crops to fail, while her daughter’s return brought renewed growth. She was worshipped with her daughter in secret initiation rites at Eleusis and was associated with grain and the harvest.
In the Great Eleusinian Relief, this youth appears beside Demeter, who holds a scepter and ears of grain. He is associated with being sent to teach people the cultivation of grain; what is his name?

In the Norse story of Baldr’s death, Loki disguised as the giant Þökk refuses to perform this act, preventing Baldr’s return from Hel. The same act is associated with Freyja, whose tears are said to become red gold. What is the act?
In Norse mythology, this goddess’s tears are said to become red gold when her husband Óðr is away. Which figure connects the topic of crying with this mythic transformation?

Which legendary island civilization was said to lie beyond the Pillars of Hercules and to have grown powerful before earthquakes and floods submerged it? Plato recounts its conflict with ancient Athens in two dialogues.
Which ancient Athenian philosopher recounts the story of Atlantis in the dialogues *Timaeus* and *Critias*, presenting it through a chain of reported conversations involving Solon?

In Genesis 2–3, one member of this pair is formed from the ground, and the other is created as his partner. After they eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, they are expelled from the garden; what is the name of this first human pair?

In the Genesis account of Adam and Eve, four rivers flow from this sacred place, including the Pishon and Gihon. After the pair is expelled, cherubim and a flaming sword guard its entrance; what is this place called?

In Hindu traditions, what spiritual goal is reached when a person is freed from karma and the cycle of rebirth? It is often compared with nirvana in Buddhism, though the traditions explain these goals differently.

In Sikh teachings, this term names liberation from the cycle of rebirth and karma, a goal associated with overcoming the Five Thieves through the Five Virtues. What Sikh term is commonly compared with moksha?

In Greek tradition, this god personified the Sun and was said to drive a chariot across the heavens each day. He was also traditionally named as the father of Phaethon, whose disastrous attempt to steer that chariot appears in Ovid’s *Metamorphoses*. Who is this god?
In the myth of Helios, this son asks to guide his father’s solar chariot, loses control of it, and is killed by Zeus to prevent the earth from burning. What is the name of this figure?
An Aztec creation narrative recounts four earlier worlds destroyed by catastrophe before the present cosmic age. What is this account commonly called?

In the Aztec Five Suns account, the present age is associated with a calendrical day sign whose name means “movement,” and it is said to end in earthquakes. What Nahuatl name was given to this fifth cosmic age?
At the wedding feast in Cana, Jesus changed this substance into wine; in another Gospel account, he walked across it on the Sea of Galilee. What substance is shared by these two miracles?

In early Christian communities, Water was used in an initiation rite associated with repentance and entry into the community, sometimes administered by immersion and sometimes by pouring. What rite is described?
In Christian worship, a formal spoken address may interpret scripture and urge listeners to reflect on moral or theological questions. What is this kind of religious discourse called?

During the First Great Awakening, Jonathan Edwards delivered a sermon in 1741 that pictured a person suspended like a spider above a fiery pit to warn of divine judgment. What is the title of that sermon?
answer: Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God

question: Which ancient Egyptian deity was commonly shown as a black canine or as a human with a canine head? He protected graves and guided the deceased into the afterlife.
During funerary judgment attended by Anubis, the organ associated with a person’s character and deeds was set on a scale opposite the feather associated with Ma’at. What is this ritual called?
Anubis was associated with preparing the deceased’s body for burial by preserving it through treatment and wrapping. What is this funerary practice called?
Artists often depicted Anubis in black, a color linked both to the darkening of a corpse during funerary preparation and to fertile soil deposited along this river. Which river is meant?

In Roman mythology, the winged god of desire carries a bow and uses slender weapons to influence affection. Their gold-tipped form is said to make anyone struck experience sudden romantic attachment; what are these mythological weapons called?

In Roman myth, Cupid's arrows do more than wound: the gold-tipped kind is said to make their target feel an overwhelming desire for someone. What emotion do these enchanted weapons traditionally kindle?
In Zoroastrian teaching, this final renovation defeats evil, restores the dead, and makes creation perfect and immortal. What is this cosmic renewal called?
In Zoroastrian accounts of Frashokereti, what title is given to the future savior associated with the resurrection of the dead and the world's final purification?

In Jain ethics, this principle is the first of five vows, preceding truthfulness, non-stealing, chastity, and non-possession. It extends non-harming to thought, speech, and action, including harm one causes or consents to rather than performs personally; what is this principle called?
In Jain practice, a motionless standing meditation posture is understood as an expression of Ahimsa, since stillness helps prevent harm even to tiny creatures. What is this posture called?

In one European folktale, a royal visitor’s exceptional sensitivity is revealed by a tiny object hidden beneath many mattresses. In an Italian story, a cloven-footed youth wins the hand of this same kind of royal bride after befriending a talking eel; what is this female royal role called?

In Hans Christian Andersen’s tale about a princess, a queen places a small object beneath twenty mattresses and twenty featherbeds to test whether the visitor is truly royal. What object does the visitor detect?
In Genesis, this city is paired with Gomorrah in the account of a destruction by fire and sulfur. Abraham pleads for it to be spared if enough righteous people can be found there. What is the city?
In the Genesis account involving Sodom, this man is Abraham’s nephew and escapes the city with his daughters before its destruction. His wife becomes a pillar of salt after looking back. Who is he?

In classical monotheism, this supreme, uncreated being is understood as the creator and sustainer of the universe. Christian theology also describes this figure as the Father and source of creation. What is this deity commonly called?

This medieval theologian developed an influential argument for God’s existence that begins with the idea of a being than which none greater can be conceived. Which monk and later archbishop wrote the work *Proslogion*?
In the traditional English wording of the Lord’s Prayer, worshippers address God with a two-word phrase immediately before the words “hallowed be thy name.” What is that opening address?

In Genesis, God calls this patriarch to leave his country and kindred for a land that will be shown to him, promising to make him into a great nation. What biblical figure, originally named Abram, receives this call?

This ethnoreligious community traces its ancestry to ancient Israelites and preserves a Torah-based religious tradition that identifies a mountain near Nablus—not Jerusalem—as Israel’s chosen sanctuary. Its members maintain their own priesthood and continue a Passover sacrifice at that sacred site; what is the community called?
For the Samaritans, this mountain near Nablus is the divinely selected center of worship, and their community still gathers there for its annual Passover sacrifice. What is the mountain’s name?

In Islamic tradition, what is the name of Muhammad’s miraculous episode that begins with a journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and continues with an ascent through the heavens? The two-part account is associated with the sacred precinct in Jerusalem marked by the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque.

In the Isra and Mi'raj, what is the name of the mount on which Muhammad traveled from Mecca to Jerusalem? Hadith descriptions characterize it as a white creature larger than a donkey but smaller than a mule.

In Aztec accounts of humanity’s beginnings, this deity journeys into Mictlan to retrieve the bones of earlier people and mixes them with his own blood to create humans. He is also represented as a feathered serpent and associated with wind, learning, and civilization. Which deity is this?

Codex images show Quetzalcoatl and Xolotl wearing this wind-associated breastplate, made from a conch shell cut across its cross-section to create a spiral. What is the Nahuatl name for this distinctive object?

Quetzalcoatl and this deity are both linked with Venus, but the latter is distinguished as a psychopomp who guides the dead. Codex images also show him wearing the spirally cut conch-shell breastplate associated with wind. Which deity is he?
Among the deities associated with Venus alongside Quetzalcoatl and Xolotl, this god is distinguished as a rain deity and ally of the feathered serpent. Which god is this?
Some post-conquest records conflated Quetzalcoatl with this legendary ruler of Tollan, while historians debate whether the narratives about him preserve historical events. What is the ruler’s name?

This New Testament letter, attributed to Paul, develops an extended argument about God’s righteousness and justification through faith while examining the relationship between law and grace. It also discusses Israel’s place in God’s purposes and was addressed to a Christian community Paul had not yet visited. Which letter is described?
Near the end of the Epistle to the Romans, the letter’s scribe steps out of the background to offer a greeting in his own name. In Romans 16:22, what is this scribe called?

A mythic object taken from Andvari is used to cover the final hair on the pelt of the slain otter Otr as ransom. Odin’s Draupnir is another example, producing eight copies of itself every ninth night. What kind of objects connect these stories?

Among magical rings in Norse mythology, this one belongs to Odin and produces eight copies of itself every ninth night. Brokkr and Eitri forged it as one of the gifts made during their contest with Loki. What is it?

Which Roman goddess, associated with the household hearth and the stability of the state, was honored through a perpetual flame in her sanctuary in the Forum? Her priestesses were responsible for ensuring that the fire never went out.

In the worship of Vesta, what was the title of the six priestesses chosen as girls who guarded the goddess’s sacred flame and observed a vow of chastity? Their service traditionally lasted thirty years.

In Acts, this woman is identified as a seller of purple goods. After hearing Paul preach near a river, she and her household were baptized, and she persuaded the missionaries to stay at her home. Who was she?

Lydia of Thyatira appears in Acts during Paul’s visit to this Macedonian city, where she and her household were baptized. The same city’s magistrates later ordered Paul and Silas beaten and jailed. What city was it?

Lord Raglan’s comparative study assigns this archetypal protagonist a sequence of 22 traditional incidents. Joseph Campbell’s monomyth likewise follows this kind of figure through departure, trials, and return. What is this legendary protagonist called?

Joseph Campbell’s 1949 work of comparative mythology organizes the monomyth around departure, initiation, and return, including a descent into and return from the underworld. Which book is a foundational account of the Mythic hero archetype?
answer: The Hero with a Thousand Faces

question: Which tenth and final human leader of the Sikhs established a collective through the 1699 initiation at Anandpur Sahib and declared that scripture, rather than a human successor, would serve as the community’s eternal spiritual authority?
In 1699, Guru Gobind Singh inaugurated a distinct Sikh order at Anandpur Sahib and prescribed the Five Ks as visible markers of its discipline. What was this order called?
What was the historical Hindu practice, followed in some regions and periods, in which a widow was expected or chose to die on her deceased husband's funeral pyre?
Which British governor-general of India issued the 1829 regulation prohibiting sati in the Bengal Presidency?

This Hindu deity is known as Mahadeva and is associated with destruction and transformation. A blue throat, a third eye, and a place in a triad with Brahma and Vishnu are among the traditional clues to this god’s identity. Who is this deity?

Many South Indian bronzes show Shiva encircled by a ring of flames, with one leg raised and the other pressing down on a dwarf representing ignorance. What name is given to this iconic form of the dancing god?
Shiva’s role as destroyer is grouped with Brahma’s role as creator and Vishnu’s role as preserver in a well-known Hindu triad. What is this three-deity grouping called?
Shiva is often worshipped not through a humanlike statue but through a smooth, upright emblem, frequently installed in a circular base associated with Shakti. What is this aniconic emblem called?
At many Shiva temples, a seated bull is placed facing the inner shrine, and stories identify the animal as Shiva’s mount and devoted attendant. What is this sacred bull called?
Which mythological king ruled Crete and required Athens to send young people as tribute? He commissioned a maze to imprison the offspring of Pasiphaë and a bull.

Minos commissioned this ingenious craftsman to design the winding structure at Knossos that held the Minotaur. After helping Theseus escape, the craftsman fled Crete with his son using wings made from feathers and wax.

During the Ramayana, this vanara crosses the ocean to Lanka in search of Sita, later setting part of the city ablaze with his burning tail. When Lakshmana is gravely wounded, he carries back a mountain bearing healing herbs; name this devoted ally of Rama.

In the Ramayana, Hanuman crosses the sea to find this prince’s abducted wife, Sita, and later aids his campaign against Ravana. The prince is exiled for fourteen years and is revered in Hindu tradition as the seventh avatar of Vishnu; who is he?
Vaishnava traditions call Hanuman the son of this celestial deity, whose Sanskrit name denotes the wind and who is associated with life-breath. What is the name of this wind-god?
Founded by L. Ron Hubbard in the 1950s, this modern religion teaches a cosmology involving an extraterrestrial ruler who brought beings to Earth long ago. What religion is it?

In Scientology’s account of humanity’s distant past, an extraterrestrial ruler brought billions of people to Earth about 75 million years ago and arranged their deaths in a mass killing involving volcanoes and hydrogen bombs. What is this ruler’s name?
In Norse mythology, Loki transformed into this domesticated riding animal to distract the stallion Svaðilfari, and their offspring became Odin’s eight-legged mount. What animal was Loki?
The topic Horse appears in Norse mythology as this eight-legged steed, born from Loki and the stallion Svaðilfari and owned by Odin. What is the steed’s name?

This ancient Sanskrit Hindu epic, traditionally attributed to a poet-sage, follows a prince sent into a fourteen-year forest exile with his wife and brother. Its plot turns on the wife’s abduction by the ruler of Lanka and the campaign that ends with the ruler’s defeat.

In traditional accounts of the Ramayana, this sage-poet is credited with composing the Sanskrit epic and appears as the hermit who shelters Sita and instructs her sons, Lava and Kusha. A related legend connects his first poetic verse to grief after a hunter kills one of a pair of krauncha birds.

This major ancient Egyptian deity was commonly shown as a falcon or as a human with a falcon’s head and was closely associated with kingship. In the familiar Osirian tradition, he was the son of Isis and Osiris and challenged Set to avenge his father. Who is this god?

Ancient Egyptians used this stylized eye emblem for protection and healing, and its mythological origin is tied to Horus’s injury and restoration during his conflict with Set. What is this protective symbol called?

Horus’s earliest recorded form served as the tutelary deity of an Upper Egyptian city whose archaeological site is commonly known by the Greek name Hierakonpolis. What was the city’s ancient Egyptian name?
In a syncretic solar form, Horus was combined with Ra and associated with the sun at the horizon. What is this composite deity called?

This Christian tradition recognizes the bishop of Rome as its supreme earthly pastor and teaches that bishops carry on the apostles’ ministry. Its worship includes seven sacraments, among them the Eucharist and confession. What is this tradition?

In Roman Catholicism’s history, this gathering of church leaders met in several sessions from 1545 to 1563 as the church responded to the Protestant Reformation. It clarified teachings on justification and the sacraments and promoted reforms in clergy education. What was this gathering?
In Arthurian tradition, this queen of Britain is the wife of King Arthur. Her relationship with Lancelot becomes a source of conflict in many later versions of the legend. Who is she?

Guinevere’s husband is the legendary British king whose court is associated with Camelot and whose fellowship is known as the Knights of the Round Table. Linked to the wizard Merlin and the sword Excalibur, what is this king commonly called?
At the center of Mecca’s Masjid al-Haram stands a cuboid sanctuary that Muslims face during prayer and circle seven times during Hajj. What is this sacred structure called?
During Hajj, pilgrims perform a rite at the Kaaba by making seven circuits around it, starting and ending near the Black Stone. What is this circumambulation called?

In Revelation, as the Lamb opens the opening seals of a scroll, riders appear on white, red, black, and pale horses. They are commonly associated with conquest, war, famine, and death. What collective name is given to these figures?

A famous woodcut made around 1497–98 depicts the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse charging through a scene from Revelation and became a landmark of Western religious art. Which artist created this print?

Described in an ancient Sanskrit treatise on performing arts, this sacred dance is especially associated with Shiva and may convey moods beyond destructive fury. In Shiva’s cosmic imagery, it evokes the recurring forces of creation, preservation, and destruction. What is this dance called?

Which ancient Sanskrit treatise on drama, music, and dance describes Tandava, the dance especially associated with Shiva? Traditionally attributed to Bharata Muni, it is a foundational work on Indian performing arts.

Which Middle Eastern folk tale follows an impoverished young man who discovers a magical vessel inhabited by a genie? It entered the European Thousand and One Nights tradition through Antoine Galland’s early-18th-century French edition.

The European version of Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp is often traced to an oral account given to Antoine Galland in Paris in 1709. Which Syrian storyteller from Aleppo is credited with telling him the tale?

In Indigenous North American traditions, especially those of the Pacific Northwest, this powerful supernatural bird is associated with thunder and lightning. In some stories, its wingbeats produce thunder. What is this being called?

Thunderbird features in the traditions of an Indigenous people whose homeland includes a large archipelago off British Columbia’s northern coast. Their artists are also known for carved cedar poles bearing family crests. Which people are these?
In Irish folklore, this female spirit is associated with a particular family and is believed to announce an imminent death through a mournful cry. What is this spirit called?
In accounts of the Banshee, her warning is often described as a mournful vocal lament, like the cries heard in traditional Irish mourning. What is the term for this lamenting practice?

What doctrine in Jewish and Christian theology holds that God brought the universe into existence without any preexisting matter? It is commonly associated with interpretations of the opening account of the world's origins in Genesis.

In discussions of Creation ex nihilo, which book of the Hebrew Bible opens with an account in which God creates the heavens and the earth? Its first chapter describes creation unfolding over six days, followed by a day of rest.

At the Passover Seder, wine is drunk at the opening, after the retelling, after the meal, and at the conclusion, in a ritual linked to God's promises of redemption in Exodus. What is this ritual set known as?

The Four Cups at the Passover Seder are associated with four divine promises: bringing Israel out of Egypt, rescuing them, redeeming them, and taking them as God's people. In which biblical passage are these promises stated together?

In Thomas Malory’s *Le Morte d’Arthur*, this sword is given to Arthur after his first sword breaks. Its magical scabbard prevents its wearer from bleeding, even when badly wounded. What is this legendary sword associated with King Arthur?
In Thomas Malory’s account, Merlin directs Arthur to a barge beside a lake after Arthur’s first sword has broken. Which mysterious figure gives Arthur Excalibur there?

In the Odyssey, which one-eyed son of Poseidon lives on an island with other Cyclopes and is blinded when an intruder drives a sharpened stake into his eye? The hero escapes after telling him his name is “Nobody.”
In the Odyssey episode involving Polyphemus, which Ithacan king gives the Cyclops the name “Nobody” and later escapes the cave by hiding beneath a sheep?

In the foundation legend of the city on the Tiber, this animal found two abandoned infant brothers and nursed them before a shepherd took them in. What legendary creature became an enduring emblem of that city?

In the legend associated with the She-wolf of Rome, these twin brothers were abandoned as infants and later became central to Rome’s foundation story, with one eventually credited as the city’s founder. What are their names?

It is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, beginning and ending according to the sighting of the crescent moon. Muslims observe it with fasting from dawn to sunset, prayer, reflection, and charity; what is this month called?
During Ramadan, Muslims end each day's daylight fast with an evening meal, often beginning with dates and water before the sunset prayer. What is this meal called?
During Ramadan, Muslims may eat this meal before dawn, before the day's fast begins. It is distinct from the meal that breaks the fast after sunset; what is it called?
Muslims associate Ramadan with a night described in the Quran as better than a thousand months, commemorating the beginning of the Quran's revelation to Muhammad. What is this night called?

During Ramadan, many Muslims perform special congregational prayers after the obligatory night prayer, often reciting substantial portions of the Quran across the month. What are these additional prayers called?

In Jewish worship, what wind instrument is traditionally fashioned from a ram’s horn and sounded during Rosh Hashanah and other sacred occasions? Its piercing blasts are associated with calls to repentance and communal remembrance.
Which Jewish holy day, known as the Day of Atonement and observed with fasting and prayer, concludes with a final shofar blast after nightfall?

The canonical Gospels place her among Jesus’s followers, and Luke says seven demons had been driven out of her. In John’s account, she finds the tomb empty and encounters the risen Jesus. Who is this woman?
Mary Magdalene mistakes the risen Jesus for a gardener before recognizing him when he speaks her name. Which New Testament account recounts this encounter?
After King Laius dies, this queen of Thebes marries the man who succeeds him, unaware that he is the infant son she had once sent away to avert a prophecy. What is her name?

Raised in Corinth after being exposed as an infant, this Theban king kills Laius at a crossroads and solves the Sphinx’s riddle before marrying Jocasta, unknowingly his birth mother. Which mythological figure is described?

A late-antique Christian thinker from Roman North Africa shaped Western theology through writings on grace, evil, and the human will. He recounted his spiritual conversion in an influential autobiographical work; who was he?

Augustine of Hippo wrote this theological history in response to claims that Christianity had caused Rome’s troubles after the sack of the city in 410. It contrasts communities ordered by love of self with those ordered by love of God; what is the work?

This ancient Egyptian funerary collection contains spells intended to help the deceased navigate the afterlife and became especially prominent during the New Kingdom and later periods. It was often copied onto papyrus and placed in burials.

In a famous judgment scene associated with the Book of the Dead, an organ belonging to the deceased is weighed against the feather of Ma’at before Osiris’s tribunal. Which organ is tested as a measure of the person’s conduct in life?
In mythology, the dead enter this realm, ruled by Hades and Persephone. Its geography includes the Fields of Asphodel, Elysium, and Tartarus. What is this realm called?

Within the Greek underworld, what vast abyss served as a prison for the Titans after Zeus and the Olympians defeated them? Ancient accounts place it at an immense depth beneath the world of the living.

Reports of this legendary livestock-attacking creature became prominent in Puerto Rico in the mid-1990s before spreading to Mexico and the U.S. Southwest. Early accounts described an upright, gray, spiny being, while later versions often depict a four-legged canine-like animal. What creature is it?

Wildlife specialists have suggested that many later, four-legged chupacabra sightings involve coyotes or other animals with a condition that causes severe hair loss and crusted skin. What condition is commonly cited to explain these appearances?

What collective term covers both mermaids and mermen, folklore beings commonly imagined with human upper bodies and fish tails? Traditions portray them with varied origins and personalities, and they appear in stories and European map art.
In the Smithsonian’s account of merfolk traditions, this Babylonian god is identified as the earliest recorded half-human, half-fish figure. What is the name of this god?

Which ancient city in northwestern Anatolia, identified with Hisarlik in modern Turkey, is traditionally the setting of the war fought over Helen? In one account of its fall, sea serpents attack the priest Laocoön and his sons.
In the stories centered on Troy, which son of Peleus and Thetis leads the Myrmidons? In the Iliad, he kills Hector to avenge the death of his companion Patroclus.
Which ancient Egyptian emblem depicts a stylized eye with distinctive markings and was worn as a protective amulet associated with healing and restoration?
In Egyptian mythology, the Eye of Horus was injured during the struggle with Set and then restored through the intervention of which ibis-headed god associated with wisdom and writing?
In Roman legend, twin sons of Rhea Silvia were abandoned near the Tiber and suckled by a she-wolf. Which brother won the augury contest over where to establish a city and became its first king?

In the founding story of Rome, Romulus and his twin brother argued over the new city’s boundary after competing in an augury contest. According to the common account, which brother was killed after crossing or mocking the wall?

The Gospels describe this Jewish prophet preaching repentance in the wilderness, dressed in camel hair and eating locusts and wild honey. Luke identifies him as Elizabeth’s son, and he baptized Jesus in the Jordan; who is he?
John the Baptist baptized Jesus in a river that flows from the Sea of Galilee southward into the Dead Sea. What is the river’s name?

During the Jewish festival commemorating the rededication of the Second Temple, families light a special candleholder with eight lights for the festival’s nights and a ninth used to kindle them. What is this ritual candleholder called?
On a Hanukkah menorah, the ninth candle is set apart from the eight festival lights and is used to kindle them each night. What is this helper candle called?
In the Warriors series, the spirits of deceased Clan cats form an ancestral community that sends guidance and prophecies to medicine cats in dreams. What is this afterlife community called?

In the original forest territories of the Warriors series, medicine cats seeking StarClan traveled to a cave and touched noses to a pale quartz formation that shone in moonlight. What was this sacred object called?
Muslims commonly recite this Arabic invocation before reading scripture or beginning another good action. Its meaning is “In the name of God.” What is the invocation?
This Qur’anic chapter contains the invocation Bismillah at its opening and again in verse 30, as part of Solomon’s letter to the Queen of Sheba. What is the chapter?

In the Babylonian version of the Epic of Gilgamesh, which flood survivor tells Gilgamesh that a god’s warning led him to build a vessel and preserve life? The gods later grant this figure immortality after he survives the deluge.
Utnapishtim recounts his flood survival in which ancient Mesopotamian literary work? Its central hero, a king of Uruk, undertakes a journey after the death of his companion Enkidu.

In Chinese philosophy and cosmology, what concept describes complementary, interdependent forces whose opposition is dynamic rather than absolute? Their balance is commonly shown in a circular black-and-white symbol with a dot of each color in the opposite half.
In depictions of yin and yang, what is the traditional name for the circular black-and-white diagram divided into two curved halves, each containing a dot of the opposite color?

In Greek mythology, Echo belongs to a group of feminine spirits connected with the natural world, and Naiads and Dryads are named members of that group. What is the general term for one of these spirits?
Among Greek Nymphs, which type is associated with freshwater places such as springs and rivers, rather than trees or mountains?
In Greek myth, this Amazon queen possessed a prized belt that Eurystheus assigned Heracles to obtain as his ninth labor. What was the name of the queen?
In the myth of Hippolyta, Heracles traveled to the Amazon stronghold where she ruled to seek her belt during his ninth labor. What was the name of that city?

In the Roman world, this execution method involved fastening a condemned person to a wooden cross, often by nails or ropes, and leaving them suspended until death. According to the New Testament, Pontius Pilate ordered this method for Jesus. What is it called?

After suppressing Spartacus’ revolt, Crassus had thousands of captured rebels put to death by crucifixion along a road leading from Capua to Rome. What ancient Roman road became the site of these executions?

Founded in nineteenth-century Iran by a religious leader born in 1817, this monotheistic religion teaches that the world’s major religions share a spiritual source and emphasizes the unity of humanity. Its founder also revealed three forms of Obligatory Prayer, one of which believers recite each day. What is this religion?
In the Baháʼí Faith, who is regarded as its founder and a messenger of God? Born in 1817, he emerged from the Bábí movement and revealed the three forms of Obligatory Prayer.

In the Chinese zodiac’s repeating twelve-animal cycle, this sign comes ninth, after the goat and before the rooster. It is associated with the legendary martial hero whose adventures are told in *Journey to the West*. Which sign is it?

In *Journey to the West*, the Monkey sign’s best-known mythological counterpart is a stone-born trickster who masters transformations, rebels against Heaven, and wields an extendable magical staff. What is this character’s name?

What Chinese tradition encompasses both philosophical teachings and organized religious practices? Its classical writings include the Daodejing and the Zhuangzi, and its teachings emphasize harmony with the natural course of existence.
In Daoism, what principle is often translated as “nonaction,” though it means acting without forceful striving rather than simply doing nothing? It describes responding in harmony with circumstances.

Jason was ordered by Aeëtes to sow these in Colchis as one of his tasks for winning the Golden Fleece, and Cadmus later sowed them after killing a serpent near the future site of Thebes. In both myths, the planted objects sprouted into armed warriors; what are they called?
Which Phoenician prince, sent by Agenor to search for Europa, killed Ares's serpent near a Boeotian spring and sowed Dragon's teeth from its body before founding Thebes?
A Phoenician princess was carried from her homeland by Zeus, who had taken the form of a bull. She became the mother of Minos, and her name is associated with the naming of a continent. Who was she?
In the myth of Europa, which of her sons became king of Crete and father of Ariadne and Phaedra? His palace at Knossos was associated with the labyrinth.

What independent Black Christian denomination was organized in the United States in 1816 after Black congregants faced racial segregation at a Philadelphia church? Richard Allen was chosen as its first bishop.

In 1819, Richard Allen gave this Philadelphia-born itinerant preacher permission to preach, making her the first woman authorized to preach in the African Methodist Episcopal Church. She later published an autobiography about her religious conversion and travels as an evangelist. Who was she?
This princess of Colchis used her knowledge of magic to help a foreign hero obtain the Golden Fleece, later leaving her homeland to become his wife. What figure from Greek mythology is described?
In the story of Medea, which Greek hero led the Argonauts to Colchis in search of the Golden Fleece and received the princess’s magical aid before marrying her?

In Islamic belief, this Arabian preacher received the Qur’anic revelations through the angel Gabriel and is regarded as the final prophet in a line that includes Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. Who is this central figure of Islam?

In 622, Muhammad and his followers left Mecca for Yathrib, the city later known as Medina, where they established a Muslim community. What is the name of this migration, which marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar?

Among the religious rites of the empire based at an island capital in Lake Texcoco, captives—sometimes taken during Flower Wars—were offered to the gods in ceremonies performed by priests. Accounts describe victims’ hearts being removed with a blade; what ritual practice is this?

Aztec human sacrifice was performed at major ceremonial sites in this island capital, built where tradition says an eagle landed on a cactus. The city’s ruins lie beneath present-day Mexico City; what was its name?
In Shinto, what water-purification rite is exemplified by a creator deity’s bathing after returning from Yomi? Shrine visitors also perform this kind of purification before approaching the kami.

In the Kojiki, which creator deity bathed in a river after escaping Yomi, in a mythic act associated with Misogi? Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo were born from parts of his body during this purification.

A Marian teaching in Catholic theology concerns a status said to hold at the conception and birth of Jesus and to continue through the rest of his mother’s life. What is the natural name of this teaching?

The Perpetual virginity of Mary concerns one aspect of traditional Marian teaching; a different Catholic doctrine says that at the end of her earthly life, she was taken, body and soul, into heavenly glory. What is this doctrine called?

These supernatural beings in Islamic tradition are created from smokeless fire rather than from clay or light. They may be benevolent or harmful, and stories sometimes depict them confined by magic; what are they called?
Islamic accounts distinguish Jinn from humans, who are associated with clay, and angels, who are associated with light. What fiery substance is named as the origin of Jinn?

At the end of the Trojan War, the city ruled by Priam is captured and sacked after the Greeks gain entry through a deception. Aeneas escapes this catastrophe and eventually travels to Italy, as recounted in the opening of Virgil’s *Aeneid*. What legendary event is this?
During the Fall of Troy, Greek warriors hide inside a huge wooden structure left outside the city as an apparent offering. What famous stratagem enabled them to enter Troy?

This king of Sipylus, a son of Zeus, was condemned after serving his own son to the gods at a banquet. In the underworld, he stood in water beneath fruit that receded whenever he tried to drink or eat. Which mythological figure is described?

In the myth of Tantalus, the gods restored the son whom the king had served to them as a meal. Demeter had unknowingly eaten part of his shoulder, so it was replaced with ivory. What was the son’s name?

In Christian Eucharistic theology, this doctrine holds that the consecrated bread and wine truly become or contain Christ’s body and blood, rather than serving only as symbols. Catholic theology explains this doctrine through a change in substance, while some other traditions affirm it without specifying how the change occurs. What is the doctrine?

In Catholic theology of the Real Presence, what term names the change in which the substance of the bread and wine becomes Christ’s body and blood while their outward appearances remain unchanged? The Fourth Lateran Council affirmed this teaching in 1215.

In Islamic tradition, what sacred drink is associated with a spring said to have appeared in the Meccan valley for Hajar and her infant son? Pilgrims visiting the sanctuary commonly drink it and carry it home.
The story of Zamzam water tells of a mother running between Safa and Marwa in search of water for her infant son. What was the name of this woman, the wife of Ibrahim and mother of Isma'il?

In Confucian ethics, what virtue names the duty to honor, respect, and care for parents and elders, with obligations often extending to rites for ancestors? Its Chinese name is built around the character *xiao*, a foundational ideal of family conduct.
Filial piety is the subject of a short Confucian text, traditionally presented as a dialogue between Confucius and his disciple Zengzi. What is the English title of this work?

In Japanese mythology, one of these sheltered Amaterasu after a conflict with Susanoo, leaving the world dark until she emerged. In Greek myth, another on Mount Ida sheltered the infant Zeus while Amalthea raised him. What kind of setting appears in both stories?
Among caves in mythology, what is the Japanese cave where Amaterasu hid after Susanoo’s offense, prompting the other deities to devise a way to draw her back out?
This legendary British ruler is associated with Camelot and the Knights of the Round Table, and medieval accounts link his story to Merlin, Guinevere, and Excalibur. What is the name of this king?

In Geoffrey of Monmouth’s account, this enchanter explains the red and white dragons beneath Vortigern’s collapsing tower and later serves as an adviser to King Arthur. What is the name of this wizard?
In many Arthurian tellings, King Arthur receives this enchanted sword from the Lady of the Lake, and its scabbard is said to protect its bearer from losing blood. What is the sword’s name?
In Arthurian romance, this queen is the wife of King Arthur, and her affair with Lancelot helps bring about the downfall of his court. What is her name?
Geoffrey of Monmouth places King Arthur’s final battle against Mordred at this site; afterward, the wounded king is taken toward Avalon. What is the name of the battlefield?
In Chinese mythology, this supreme celestial ruler presides over Heaven and its vast hierarchy of divine officials. Often honored in Daoist and popular religious traditions, who is this sovereign?

In many Chinese communities, worshippers honor the Jade Emperor on the ninth day of the first lunar month, with temple ceremonies and offerings marking the occasion. What annual observance is celebrated on that date?

In Chinese tradition, this legendary ruler controlled a devastating flood by channeling its waters, succeeding where his father Gun had failed. He is also remembered as the founder of the Xia dynasty; who was he?
Yu the Great is traditionally credited with establishing the first hereditary line of rulers in ancient China. What was this early royal house called?
In the Mahabharata, these five brothers are led by Yudhishthira and include Bhima and Arjuna. They oppose the Kauravas and are sent into exile after losing a game of dice; what are they called?
The Pandavas and Kauravas fight at Kurukshetra in this ancient Indian epic, which also contains the Bhagavad Gita. What is the name of the epic?

What 1517 set of propositions challenged the theological basis of indulgences and criticized the practice of selling them? Martin Luther is traditionally said to have posted them on the door of All Saints’ Church in Wittenberg.

The Ninety-Five Theses were written by this German theologian and Augustinian friar, whose dispute over indulgences helped launch the Protestant Reformation. He taught at the University of Wittenberg.
Created by Maulana Karenga in 1966, this weeklong African-American and Pan-African holiday is observed from December 26 through January 1. What is it?
During Kwanzaa, families may display a candleholder with seven spaces for candles: one black candle in the center, flanked by three red and three green candles. What is this candleholder called?

In ancient Egyptian funerary belief, this female monster waited beside the scales where a deceased person’s heart was weighed. Depicted with a crocodile’s head, lion’s forequarters, and hippopotamus’s hindquarters, what being consumed a heart judged unworthy?
In the judgment scene that could end with Ammit devouring the condemned heart, which jackal-headed god oversees the weighing of the deceased’s heart and guides the dead?

This annual observance falls on the tenth day of Tishrei and concludes the Ten Days of Repentance that begin with Rosh Hashanah. Traditional practice includes a full fast and extended synagogue services. What is this Jewish holy day?

On the eve of Yom Kippur, the opening evening service takes its name from an Aramaic declaration concerning vows. The declaration’s title is also commonly used for the service itself. What is it called?
At Yom Kippur’s final service, worshippers recite a special fifth Amidah as the liturgy portrays heaven’s gates as closing; a final shofar blast marks the service’s end. What is this service called?
During Yom Kippur, the afternoon service traditionally includes a reading from the biblical book about a reluctant prophet who flees toward Tarshish and later warns Nineveh. What is the book?

In Hawaiian tradition, this deity is associated with fire and volcanoes, and her power is said to both destroy existing land and create new volcanic landscapes. Stories place her home at Halemaʻumaʻu crater on Kīlauea; what is her name?
In one Hawaiian moʻolelo, Pele travels from an ancestral homeland to the Hawaiian Islands, though accounts differ about the details of her journey. What is that homeland called?

Born fully armed from Zeus’s head, this Olympian goddess was associated with wisdom, crafts, and strategic warfare. After competing with Poseidon by giving the city an olive tree, she became its patron deity; what goddess was she?
In a myth about Athena, what double-reed woodwind instrument did she fashion and then discard after seeing that playing it made her cheeks bulge?
In Sikh teaching, what collective name is given to the inner vices of lust, anger, greed, attachment, and ego that obstruct spiritual development?
In Sikh teaching, the Five Thieves hinder spiritual progress, while cultivating the Five Virtues helps overcome them. What is the name for liberation from the cycle of rebirth and karma?
In Zoroastrianism, one of the six Amesha Spentas personifies truth, right order, and righteousness, and is closely associated with sacred fire. What is the name of this divine being?

Asha Vahista’s association with sacred fire is reflected in Zoroastrian temple traditions. What is the name of the highest grade of consecrated fire, installed through elaborate purification and consecration rites?

Geoffrey of Monmouth shaped this Arthurian figure by blending Welsh prophetic traditions associated with Myrddin and Emrys. In the familiar legends, he is a magician and prophet who advises Uther Pendragon and later mentors Arthur. Who is he?

In one popular French prose tradition, this enchantress is Merlin’s student and eventually seals him away in a supernatural prison after he falls in love with her. What title is commonly given to this figure?
Which 12th-century cleric and historian helped shape the familiar version of Merlin by combining Welsh traditions about Myrddin and Emrys? He also wrote *Historia Regum Britanniae*.

In Genesis, this Egyptian enslaved woman in the household of Sarai and Abram bears Abram’s son, who is named Ishmael. After fleeing into the wilderness while pregnant, she calls God the one who sees her; who is she?

After Isaac’s birth, Sarah has Hagar and her son sent away into the wilderness. When their water runs out, God hears the boy and shows Hagar a well; what is the boy’s name, explained in Genesis in connection with God hearing?

In this Hindu myth, devas and asuras rotate Mount Mandara as a rod, with the serpent Vasuki serving as their rope. Their effort produces amrita as well as the deadly halahala poison; what is this episode called?
answer: Churning of the Ocean of Milk

question: During the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, Mount Mandara began sinking into the cosmic waters. Which tortoise incarnation of Vishnu supported the mountain from below?
In Greek myth, this exceptionally handsome mortal was beloved by Aphrodite and died after a boar wounded him during a hunt. What was his name?
In one account of Adonis’s death, his blood gave rise to a flower whose name comes from the Greek word for wind and whose genus belongs to the buttercup family. What flower is it?

Across many Indigenous religious traditions of the Americas, this recurring figure is a clever, often shape-shifting trickster. Its stories place it among animal beings rather than human heroes. What is the figure’s familiar name?

Like Coyote, this figure appears as a trickster in Indigenous religious traditions, but Lakota tales portray it in spider form and associate it with the origin of netted hoops used as protective charms for children. What figure is it?
In Norse mythology, what is Odin’s great hall in Asgard, where valkyries bring warriors slain in battle? Its residents feast and train for the final battle of Ragnarök.
At Valhalla, what name is given to the slain warriors who dwell there, feast, and prepare to fight at Ragnarök?

In Matthew’s account of Jesus’ teaching on a mountainside, a sequence of brief declarations calls different groups blessed and pairs each with a promise, such as inheriting the earth or receiving mercy. What is the traditional name for this set of blessings?

The Beatitudes appear near the opening of a New Testament book that presents Jesus’ Sermon on the Mount and is traditionally attributed to one of the Twelve who had worked as a tax collector. Which of the four canonical accounts of Jesus’ life is it?

In Greek accounts of the war between the Greeks and the people of Troy, the Greeks left a huge wooden object outside the city as if it were an abandoned trophy. Soldiers concealed inside it emerged at night and helped open the way for the city’s sack. What was this object called?
In stories of the Trojan Horse, this Trojan princess and prophetess warned her people not to trust the Greeks’ apparent gift, but Apollo’s curse ensured that her warnings were ignored. Who was she?

In Greek cosmology, this primordial abyss lay below Hades, as far beneath it as heaven was above earth. It served as a prison for the Titans and a dungeon for exceptionally wicked beings; what was it called?
After their defeat in the Titanomachy, Zeus confined this older generation of gods in Tartarus, making them its best-known prisoners. What collective name is given to these deities?
Two major Islamic holidays share this name: the Lesser one ends Ramadan, and the Greater one commemorates Abraham’s willingness to sacrifice his son. What is the shared name?
Among the holidays known collectively as Eid, which one begins after Ramadan’s month of fasting ends? Its observance includes a charitable contribution given before the communal prayer.
An American pulp-fiction author published *Dianetics: The Modern Science of Mental Health* in 1950 and later established Scientology. What was the name of this religious founder?
L. Ron Hubbard introduced this self-help system in a 1950 book subtitled *The Modern Science of Mental Health*. It uses auditing and describes the goal of becoming “Clear.” What is the system called?

In Hawaiian religious tradition, this goddess is associated with the ceremonial performance of hula, an art combining chant, gesture, and dance. Which deity is traditionally regarded as the patron of this art?
Laka is revered in Hawaiian tradition in connection with a performance art whose traditional kahiko style is accompanied by chanting. What is this Hawaiian art form?
In ancient Egyptian religion, which goddess was associated with love, fertility, motherhood, music, and joy? She was often depicted with a solar disk set between cow horns.
In myths involving Hathor and the Osirian family, which falcon-associated god avenged his father Osiris by defeating his uncle Set? He was also closely connected with Egyptian kingship.

What 16th-century Radical Reformation movement rejected infant baptism and taught that baptism should follow a person’s conscious profession of Christian faith, with later communities including the Amish and Mennonites?

Among the Anabaptists, which Dutch theologian from Friesland was a former Catholic priest who left the priesthood in 1536 and became an influential organizer of peaceful congregations? His writings helped shape the movement in the Low Countries.

Classical accounts by Julius Caesar and Pliny the Elder describe these figures as religious authorities among Celtic peoples. Pliny also associates them with ritually gathering mistletoe from oak trees. What were these figures called?

Modern groups inspired by Druids have held ceremonies at this prehistoric monument on Salisbury Plain, though archaeological evidence does not establish a link to ancient Celtic priests. Built in stages beginning more than 4,000 years ago, what famous stone circle is it?

This fictional giant lumberjack took shape in mid-19th-century Great Lakes logging-camp lore, and early-20th-century advertising helped make him a widely recognized American folk hero. Tales credit him with shaping waterways and other natural landmarks through feats of impossible scale. Who is this figure?
Paul Bunyan stories circulated among loggers before a 1914 promotional pamphlet helped bring the character to a wider audience. Which Westwood, California-based firm issued that booklet?
An English theologian and priest, he became a leading figure in the Oxford Movement while still an Anglican. He later entered the Catholic Church and was made a cardinal by Pope Leo XIII; who was he?
John Henry Newman wrote this 1864 spiritual autobiography in response to Charles Kingsley’s accusations about his truthfulness. What is the title of the work?
