In the Hebrew Bible, this formidable sea creature is described in Job as impossible for humans to capture or master, and God calls it unrivaled. It also appears in Psalm 104 among God’s creatures and in Isaiah 27 in a prophecy of its destruction. What is it?
Which entry in the Bible’s collection of 150 sacred songs depicts God crushing the heads of Leviathan and giving it as food to creatures of the wilderness, recalling a divine victory over chaos?
In Haitian Vodou, this prominent loa is associated with death, cemeteries, and the realm of the dead. He is often depicted in a black tailcoat and top hat, with dark glasses and a cigar.

In Haitian Vodou, Baron Samedi is associated with death, while another widely invoked loa is linked to crossroads and opens the way for communication with the spirits. Which intermediary is commonly depicted carrying a cane?

A winged monster from the folklore of the state whose capital is Trenton is said to roam its southern forests, and is often described with a horse-like head, batlike wings, and cloven hooves. What is this creature?

In stories about the Jersey Devil, the creature’s home is a vast, sparsely settled expanse of southern New Jersey characterized by sandy soil, scrub-oak woodland, and cedar swamps. By what name is this region commonly known?

In Homer’s *Iliad*, Athena throws this fearsome divine emblem over her shoulders before battle; it is fringed and associated with the Gorgon’s head. Linked to Zeus as well as Athena, what is this protective object called?
In Greek myth, this hero used a reflective shield to avoid looking directly at Medusa as he slew her. He later gave her severed head to Athena, whose Aegis could bear the Gorgon’s image. Who was he?
Across many religious and mythological traditions, this realm is associated with punishment, the dead, or the underworld, though its nature varies. What is this general afterlife concept?

In Greek mythology, the ruler of the underworld was a son of Cronus and Rhea, a brother of Zeus and Poseidon, and the husband of Persephone. What deity is associated with the realm often discussed under the concept of Hell?

In Shang China, specialists inscribed questions on animal bones or turtle shells and interpreted cracks formed by heating them; Roman augurs also read signs in birds’ behavior. What is the broad practice of seeking hidden knowledge or guidance by interpreting such signs called?

In ancient China, divination practitioners inscribed questions on these materials, heated them, and interpreted the resulting cracks. Surviving examples sometimes record the question and the outcome of the consultation. What are these inscribed objects called?

In Christian theology, what is the name of the inherited human condition traced to Adam and Eve’s first disobedience, understood in Catholic teaching as a wounded nature inclined toward wrongdoing rather than each descendant’s personal commission of their act? The doctrine helps explain humanity’s shared need for salvation through Christ.

In Catholic accounts of original sin, which North African bishop gave the doctrine an influential fifth-century formulation while arguing against Pelagius and his followers? He also wrote *Confessions* and *The City of God*.

This sacred-text collection of Zoroastrianism is written in an ancient Iranian language and preserves liturgical compositions, hymns, and religious teachings. Its surviving contents include a 72-chapter ritual collection and the tradition’s oldest poetic hymns. What is this collection called?

Within the Avesta, these seventeen Old Avestan poetic hymns are arranged in five groups and form the oldest layer of the collection. They are part of the Yasna liturgy and are traditionally attributed to Zoroaster; what are they called?

This religious tradition included deities such as Osiris, Isis, and the jackal-headed guide of the dead, and its funerary beliefs included mummification. It also portrayed the dead being judged by weighing their hearts against the feather of Ma’at. What tradition is this?

In Ancient Egyptian mythology, which god is commonly shown with green skin and rules over the underworld? After being murdered by his brother Seth, he is restored by Isis and becomes a symbol of resurrection.

In Genesis, this vessel is built at God's command to carry its builder's family and representatives of the animals through the Great Flood. After the waters recede, it comes to rest in the mountains of Ararat. What is the vessel called?
After Noah and his family leave Noah's Ark, God establishes a sign in the clouds as a promise never again to destroy all life with a flood. What visible sign is named in Genesis?

This 17th-century Catholic theological movement drew on Augustine to emphasize the necessity of divine grace and the limits of human freedom in overcoming sin. Its adherents became embroiled in a major dispute over propositions attributed to a posthumously published treatise on grace and predestination. What was this movement called?

The movement called Jansenism takes its name from this Dutch-born Catholic bishop and theologian. His posthumously published work *Augustinus* advanced an influential account of grace and predestination. Who was he?

This final book of the Christian New Testament opens with messages to seven churches in Asia before unfolding visions of seals, trumpets, and events preceding the Second Coming. Traditionally attributed to John of Patmos, what is this book’s natural name?
The narrator says he was on this Aegean island when he received the visions and sent messages to churches in the Book of Revelation. Which island does the text name as his location?
In the Book of Revelation, the fourth seal releases a rider on a pale horse, and the text explicitly identifies this horseman by name. What is that name?

In the Book of Revelation, chapters 2 and 3 contain messages to Christian congregations in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. What collective name is commonly given to these recipients?

This late-fourth-century Latin spiritual autobiography recounts its author’s early involvement with Manichaeism and his conversion to Christianity. It also reflects on a teenage episode in which he stole pears he did not even want. What is this work?

In Confessions, which North African bishop describes hearing a child’s voice say “take and read” before his conversion in Milan? The same author recalls stealing pears as a teenager and later became a major Christian theologian.

In Māori stories, this culture hero is credited with stealing fire from Mahuika and slowing the sun. In a famous fishing feat, he used his grandmother’s jawbone as a hook to haul the North Island from the sea. Who is this figure?
In a Hawaiian story about Māui snaring the sun to lengthen daylight, the feat takes place at which volcanic summit on the island of Maui?

In 451, bishops met in a city across the Bosporus from Constantinople to settle disputes about the nature of Christ. The assembly affirmed that Christ is one person with distinct divine and human natures, a position rejected by Oriental Orthodox churches. What was this ecumenical gathering called?
The Council of Chalcedon issued a formula affirming Christ as one person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion or separation. What is the doctrinal statement commonly known as?

In Greek myth, this legendary queen of Sparta was married to Menelaus, and her departure with Paris became the spark for the Greek expedition to the city ruled by Priam. What figure is often remembered as the face that launched a thousand ships?

Helen of Troy is associated with the famous phrase about a face that launched a thousand ships, but the wording comes from a later English play rather than Homer. Which Elizabethan dramatist wrote it in *Doctor Faustus*?

In Chinua Achebe’s novel, Mr. Brown and the hostile Mr. Smith belong to this profession. Its members ask for land in Umuofia and receive a plot in the Evil Forest; one communicates through an interpreter who says “my buttocks” when he means “myself.” What is this profession?

Christian missionaries arrive in Umuofia and unsettle the community’s social order in this novel. After protagonist Okonkwo hangs himself, a District Commissioner considers including him in a book about the “pacification” of “primitive tribes.” What is the novel?

In ancient Egyptian afterlife belief, the deceased’s central organ, regarded as the seat of thought and moral character, was placed on a scale opposite a feather representing Ma’at, the principle of truth and order. This judgment took place in the Hall of the Two Truths and determined whether the deceased could enter the afterlife. What was this judgment called?
During the Weighing of the Heart, Anubis oversees the scales and Osiris presides over the judgment. Which ibis-headed god records the result?

In Greek mythology, what male woodland spirit accompanied Dionysus and was depicted with human features and animal traits, such as goatlike legs or horse-like ears and a tail? These spirits also formed the chorus in comic plays performed after tragic dramas.
Satyr figures often appear in the retinue of this Greek god, who was associated with wine, theater, and ecstatic celebration. Known as Bacchus in Roman tradition, who is he?

In Sikhism, this title denotes an authoritative spiritual guide who conveys divine wisdom. Ten human figures held it in succession, beginning with Nanak and ending with Gobind Singh; after 1708, Sikhs recognized scripture as the continuing spiritual authority. What is this title?

In 1708, the final human Guru ended the personal succession and vested continuing spiritual authority in a sacred text. What is the name of that scripture, which enshrines the teachings of the Sikh Gurus?
Which deity was worshipped in a Roman mystery cult whose initiates advanced through seven grades? The cult’s central ritual depicted this deity killing a bull.
In the Roman mystery cult centered on Mithras, what is the name for the central ritual and image depicting the deity killing a bull? The term is derived from the Greek word for bull sacrifice.

Its founder, Zarathustra, taught that people face an ethical choice between truth and order on one side, and falsehood and disorder on the other. Centered on Ahura Mazda, what is the name of this ancient Iranian religion?
In Zoroastrianism, the oldest and most central hymns belong to a larger sacred-text tradition that also contains liturgical material. What is the name of this collection, which includes the Yasna?
In Zoroastrianism, what concept denotes truth, right order, and righteousness, in contrast to druj, or falsehood and disorder?
Within Zoroastrianism’s liturgy, what are the ancient hymns traditionally attributed to Zarathustra that form the oldest and most central portion of the Avesta? They are part of the Yasna.

In the Egyptian judgment of the dead, this object was an ostrich plume symbolizing Ma’at and served as the counterweight against a deceased person’s heart. What is this funerary symbol commonly called?

During the Egyptian weighing-of-the-heart ceremony, the Feather of Ma’at was placed on one side of the scales opposite the deceased person’s heart. Which jackal-headed god associated with mummification performed the weighing?
In Chinese mythology, ten suns once appeared in the sky together, scorching the earth. Which legendary archer shot down nine of them to save the world?
In the legend involving Houyi, which woman drank an elixir of immortality and ascended to the moon?

This is the second-largest branch of a major monotheistic faith founded in Arabia in the seventh century, and it has communities including the Alawites of Syria. Its adherents regard Ali and his descendants as the rightful successors to Muhammad. What is this branch called?

In Twelver Shia Islam, the twelfth Imam is believed to have entered occultation and to return before the end of time to establish justice. What title is given to this expected restorer, a title also used by a 19th-century Sudanese religious leader who led a revolt against Egyptian rule?
What is the Jewish weekly observance that begins on Friday evening and ends on Saturday evening? It is marked by rest and religious observance on the seventh day of the week.
During Shabbat, what is the Friday-night ritual in which a blessing is recited over wine or grape juice to sanctify the day? The challah is traditionally covered while this blessing is said.

Around 1000 CE, a ruling at the Althing shifted the island from Norse pagan religion to Christianity, with law speaker Thorgeir Thorkelsson overseeing the decision. What is this religious transformation known as?

During the Christianization of Iceland, which law speaker at the Althing is traditionally said to have deliberated beneath a cloak before declaring the island’s new religious law? Later accounts associate him with casting pagan idols into Goðafoss.
In some European and gothic folk traditions, a dark-furred cat is treated as a portent of misfortune rather than an ordinary animal. What is the natural name for this body of beliefs?
European folklore associated with Black Cat Superstitions sometimes portrays a cat as a witch’s supernatural attendant and magical helper. What established term names such an animal companion?
In Hinduism, this final samskara is performed after a person dies and traditionally centers on cremation, accompanied by rites for the deceased. What is this funeral rite called?
During a traditional Antyesti, the deceased’s body is placed on this structure, typically made of stacked wood, and cremated. What is this structure called?
What term describes the blending of beliefs, rituals, or symbols from multiple faiths into a shared tradition? The combination of Catholic and Yoruba elements is one example of this phenomenon.
A well-known example of religious syncretism is this Afro-Cuban religion, which combines Yoruba-derived orisha traditions with Catholic elements and saints. What is this tradition commonly called?

This Christian feast commemorates the birth of Jesus, though the Gospels do not establish the exact date of his birth. Many churches observe it on December 25 with worship services, including midnight liturgies. What is this feast called?

In the New Testament Nativity accounts, Mary and Joseph travel to this town, where Jesus is born; Luke connects their journey with a census. The town is in Judea and is associated in Hebrew scripture with King David. Which place is central to the Christmas Nativity story?

In Western Christian practice, Christmas is preceded by this season of preparation, which begins on the fourth Sunday before the feast and marks the start of the liturgical year in many churches. Its name derives from a Latin word meaning “coming.” What is this season called?

The traditional twelve days of Christmas are reckoned from December 25, and this named observance is associated with January 5 in many Western customs, immediately before Epiphany. What is the name of this closing observance?

Christian teaching treats Christmas as a celebration not merely of Jesus’s birth but of God taking human nature in Jesus. What theological doctrine, whose name derives from a Latin word for “becoming flesh,” describes this?
What is the name for the grape-derived beverage used alongside bread in Christian Eucharistic celebrations, where it represents or, in some traditions, becomes the blood of Christ?

In Graham Greene’s novel set in Tabasco during a revolutionary government’s persecution of the Church, a fugitive priest nicknamed the “whisky priest” struggles to continue celebrating Mass. Which novel features his efforts to obtain sacramental wine?

Which English Anglican minister became an exceptionally prominent itinerant evangelist in the eighteenth century, preaching to huge audiences on both sides of the Atlantic? His ministry helped make the colonial evangelical revival a transatlantic phenomenon.

In the 1730s and 1740s, a wave of evangelical revivals swept Britain’s North American colonies, with George Whitefield and Jonathan Edwards among its leading preachers. What is this revival movement called?

In Haitian Vodou, the lwa are spirits who may be approached in ceremonies, while the supreme creator is generally regarded as distant from human affairs. What is the name of this supreme deity, derived from a French phrase meaning “good God”?
Bondye is the supreme deity in Haitian Vodou, but practitioners more directly interact with a class of spirits through ritual and mediation. What is the Haitian Vodou term for these spirits?
Founded by L. Ron Hubbard, this religious organization developed from his teachings on Dianetics and includes the goal of attaining a state known as “clear.” What is the organization’s name?

Within the Church of Scientology, what name did L. Ron Hubbard give to the system he introduced in a 1950 book? It describes the reactive mind and uses auditing as a method for addressing its influence.

Ancient Egyptian physicians belonged to the priesthood of this goddess, whose lioness-headed form linked her to war and pestilence as well as healing. Her name means “the powerful one,” and her destructive force could be turned toward protection when she was appeased. Which goddess is described?
Hundreds of statues of Sekhmet were made for the mortuary temple of which New Kingdom pharaoh? A surviving statue from his reign, found at the Temple of Mut at Karnak, is now in Turin’s Museo Egizio.

Tradition identifies this ancient Iranian teacher as the founder and prophet of Zoroastrianism, a faith centered on Ahura Mazda. The Gathas, the oldest hymns in the Avesta, are traditionally attributed to him. What is his name?

Zarathustra’s religious tradition preserves hymns, liturgical prayers, and ritual instructions in a sacred collection, with the Gathas forming its oldest and most revered portion. What is this collection called?
In Greek cosmogony, this primordial sky deity was the consort of Gaia and father of the Titans. His son Kronos overthrew him in the mythic succession of divine generations. Who was this deity?

In Greek myth, Gaia and Uranus had three monstrous sons with a hundred hands and fifty heads. Cottus, Gyges, and Briareus belonged to this group, which later aided the Olympians against the Titans; what were these beings called?
In religious traditions, these supernatural beings are often regarded as agents of evil or punishment. Exorcism is traditionally used to drive them from a person. What are they called?

In some medieval Christian interpretations of demons, this sea creature was associated with punishing envious sinners. The Book of Job also describes it as a fearsome creature whose power emphasizes God's might. What is it called?

In Greek myth, which queen of Thebes boasted that her seven sons and seven daughters outnumbered Leto’s children, prompting Apollo and Artemis to kill them? She was ultimately turned to stone as she wept.
Niobe’s boast about her fourteen children provoked Apollo and Artemis to avenge their mother. Which goddess, who bore the twins on the island of Delos, was she mocking?
In the Jewish calendar, this period opens with Rosh Hashanah and concludes with Yom Kippur, the fast of atonement. What is this period of observance called?
Within the High Holy Days, which observance begins on the first day of Tishrei, marks the Jewish New Year, and is traditionally celebrated with the sounding of the shofar?

This Jewish ritual slaughter method is performed on permitted animals by a trained practitioner using a carefully inspected, exceptionally sharp knife and a swift, uninterrupted cut at the neck. What is the method called?

During Shechita, the practitioner must use a blade checked for imperfections and make the prescribed cut. What is the Hebrew title for the trained person who performs the slaughter, rather than someone who only supervises it?

Which legendary English outlaw and folk hero is portrayed as leading a band of companions known as the Merry Men from a forest refuge? He is a central figure in English ballads and tales of resistance to corrupt authority.
In tales of Robin Hood, what historic woodland in Nottinghamshire serves as the outlaw’s refuge and the setting for many of his adventures?
In traditional Jewish practice, a non-Jew might be hired to perform tasks prohibited to Jews on the weekly day of rest, such as tending a fire. What is the familiar two-word term for this helper?
In accounts of the Shabbos goy, impoverished women who served in this role were sometimes paid with a piece of this braided bread traditionally eaten on the Sabbath. What is the bread called?

In Genesis, this son of Jacob and Rachel is sold by his brothers into Egypt, where he interprets Pharaoh’s dreams of seven healthy cows and seven thin cows as predicting years of plenty followed by famine. Pharaoh appoints him to oversee Egypt’s food preparations.
In the Genesis account of Joseph, which woman is his mother and also the mother of his younger brother Benjamin? She was Jacob’s beloved wife and died while giving birth to Benjamin near Ephrath.

This Thracian bard was famed for music so powerful that it could move stones and charm wild animals. In the best-known account of his descent into the Underworld, he looked back before reaching the surface and lost his wife a second time; name this musician and poet.

Orpheus descended into the realm of the dead to retrieve the woman he had married, but lost her again after turning back before they reached the upper world. What was the name of this wife, whose death is often linked to a snakebite while fleeing Aristaeus?
Orpheus joined the expedition that sailed aboard the Argo in quest of the Golden Fleece, and his music helped the crew resist the Sirens. Which Thessalian leader commanded this band of Argonauts?
A collection of devotional poems invoking Greek gods and powers was attributed to Orpheus and used in rites influenced by the religious tradition bearing his name. What is this collection called?

In one version of the myth, Orpheus’s persistent mourning after Eurydice’s loss angered a group of frenzied women devoted to Dionysus, who tore him apart. By what collective name were these ecstatic female followers known?

In the biblical account, a series of plagues ends with the death of Egypt’s firstborn, after which an enslaved people depart under the leadership of a prophet. Their journey includes a miraculous crossing of the sea and decades of wandering in the wilderness; what is this episode called?
During the Exodus, which Israelite leader confronted Pharaoh, guided the people out of Egypt, and later ascended Mount Sinai to receive the commandments?

In a story told in Luke, a wealthy man dressed in purple and fine linen feasts sumptuously while a sore-covered beggar lies at his gate, hoping for scraps. After both die, one is carried by angels to a patriarch’s side while the other suffers across an uncrossable chasm; what story is this?
answer: Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus

question: In the Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus, what traditional phrase names the place of comfort where the beggar is carried after death, in contrast with the rich man’s torment?
In Hindu mythology, this concept is associated with the goddess Kali and with the ruler of Naraka, who judges the departed. What concept is being described?
In Hindu accounts of Death and the afterlife, which god rules Naraka and is named as the father of Yudhishthira, the eldest of the five Pandava brothers?

Which Mexican Marian title is associated with a reported appearance of the Virgin Mary on Tepeyac Hill in 1531? The image linked to this devotion is traditionally said to have appeared on Juan Diego’s tilma, and its basilica is a major pilgrimage destination in Mexico City.
In the traditional account of Our Lady of Guadalupe, which Indigenous convert reported encountering Mary at Tepeyac Hill in 1531 and presenting roses to the bishop in his tilma?
At this marriage ceremony in communities that revere Ahura Mazda, a priest blesses the couple’s bond and the partners perform symbolic acts for good fortune. What is this ceremony called?
In Zoroastrian weddings, the partners sprinkle this grain on one another as a sign of good luck and marital union. What grain is used in this exchange?

At a Jewish festival lasting eight nights, a new light is added to a special branched holder each evening; the lights are arranged from right to left and kindled from left to right. What are the ritual lights at the center of this practice called?

Hanukkah candles include an additional light used to kindle the others, set apart from the lights corresponding to the festival nights, often by being placed higher or lower. What is this helper light called?

In a Brothers Grimm fairy tale, a prince transformed into this animal is restored to human form after a princess kisses him. Egyptian mythology also depicts Kek, a personification of primordial darkness, in this animal's form. What animal is it?
In Egyptian mythology, the frog-headed goddess Heket is associated with this river. One account says its waters originated from Isis's tears shed while mourning Osiris. Which river is it?

Which Afrocentric religious and cultural movement emerged in Jamaica during the 1930s and interprets Africa, especially Ethiopia, as Zion while using Babylon as a name for oppressive colonial or Western systems? Its early development was shaped by an Ethiopian ruler’s 1930 coronation.
In Rastafari, which Ethiopian emperor’s 1930 coronation was interpreted by early adherents through biblical prophecy, and whose pre-coronation title gave the movement its name?

At the Passover Seder, this Jewish liturgical text lays out the order of the ceremony and provides its readings and rituals. What is the name of this text, which guides participants as they recount the Israelites’ Exodus from Egypt?

During a Passover Seder guided by the Haggadah, participants recount the calamities inflicted on Egypt and traditionally remove a drop of wine from their cups for each one. How many plagues are recalled—a number also associated with the commandments given to Moses at Sinai?
In Greek religion, which goddess personifies divine retribution and vengeance against those who overstep proper bounds? She was especially associated with a sanctuary at Rhamnous in Attica.
In one tradition, this nurse cared for the infant Zeus while the Curetes’ clashing weapons drowned out his cries. Her name was also used as an epithet of Nemesis; what was her name?
Shia Muslims mark the fortieth day after Husayn ibn Ali’s martyrdom with an annual observance centered on Karbala, drawing travelers from across the region. What is this event called?
The Arba'een Pilgrimage brings pilgrims to Karbala, the city where Husayn ibn Ali was martyred in 680 CE. In which present-day country is Karbala located?

What was the name of the central Jewish sanctuary complex built on the hilltop sacred precinct in the ancient capital of Judah? Its first sanctuary is traditionally linked to Solomon, and its later sanctuary was destroyed by Roman forces in 70 CE.
Which 71-member Jewish council, regarded as the highest court in ancient Jewish tradition, is described as meeting in the Temple in Jerusalem and appointing the High Priest?

In Acts 8, Peter and John travel to Samaria, where they pray for recently baptized believers to receive the Holy Spirit; the narrative says the Spirit comes after a particular ritual gesture. This same Christian practice is also used in blessing, healing, and ordination—what is it called?

In Christian ordination, the laying on of hands symbolizes a doctrine that traces episcopal authority through an unbroken chain back to the apostles. What is the name of that doctrine, invoked by Rome to explain the special standing of the church associated with Peter?

In medieval Christian Europe, this kind of religious community housed monks who followed a shared rule of life and gathered for prayer. Its residents might also preserve learning by copying manuscripts. What is this institution called?

Founded by Benedict of Nursia in sixth-century Italy, this monastery became the mother house of the Benedictine order. Allied bombing heavily damaged it during the Italian campaign in 1944, after which it was rebuilt. What is its name?

Sent to ravage an Aetolian kingdom after its king neglected to include a goddess in his offerings, this monstrous animal became the quarry of heroes such as Meleager and Atalanta. What creature is it?
In the Calydonian Boar myth, which goddess sent the beast to punish King Oeneus for failing to include her in his sacrifices? She was also associated with the hunt and wilderness.

In Greek religion, what collective name is given to the divine personifications of the directional winds? Its members include the north wind associated with winter and the west wind associated with gentler breezes.
Among the Anemoi, which personification of the north wind abducted Oreithyia, an Athenian princess? He was often portrayed as a winged, bearded god associated with cold winter weather.

In Chinese household practice, tablets bearing the names of deceased relatives may be placed at domestic shrines and receive offerings. What collective term describes these family members who continue to be honored?
In Chinese tradition, relatives visit and clean graves during this spring observance, which falls about 15 days after the spring equinox. What festival honors ancestors in this way?
Set into the eastern corner of the Kaaba, this sacred object is traditionally touched or kissed by pilgrims as they circle the shrine. What is this revered object called?

In the pilgrimage rite associated with the Black Stone, worshippers make seven circuits around the Kaaba, with the circuits beginning and ending at the shrine’s eastern corner. What is this circumambulation called?
In Greek mythology, this enchantress lived on the island of Aeaea and transformed members of a visiting crew into animals. She later detained their leader on her island.
Circe kept this Greek hero on Aeaea for a year after he arrived with his crew. Homer’s epic recounts his long journey back to Ithaca after the Trojan War.
In Twelver Shia Islam, this honorific is used for especially learned, high-ranking clerics. Its holders may be authorized to issue influential interpretations of Islamic law; what is this title?

The title Ayatollah became widely associated with the leader of the 1979 Iranian Revolution, who returned from exile in France and became the Islamic Republic’s first Supreme Leader. What was this cleric’s name?

Luke's infancy narrative depicts Gabriel announcing to this woman that she will bear Jesus, and later records her visit to Elizabeth. It also places on her lips a canticle beginning “My soul magnifies the Lord”; who is she?
In Luke's Gospel, Mary, Mother of Jesus, sings this canticle during her visit to Elizabeth; its opening words are often translated “My soul magnifies the Lord.” What is the canticle commonly called?
Many Christian traditions call Mary, Mother of Jesus, by a Greek title meaning “God-bearer” or “Mother of God,” famously affirmed at the Council of Ephesus in 431. What is this title?

In Catholic teaching, this dogma says that Mary, Mother of Jesus, was preserved from original sin from the very beginning of her life; it concerns her own sinlessness, not Jesus's virginal birth. What is the doctrine called?

In the Tibetan sky-burial rite of jhator, rogyapa prepare these remains for vultures, sometimes grinding the bones with tsampa. Zoroastrian funerary customs have also exposed them on dakhmas rather than burying or burning them. What are the deceased remains at the center of these rites called?

In Zoroastrian rites for human corpses, these circular funerary structures expose the dead to scavenging birds while keeping them from contact with sacred earth and fire. By what English name are these structures commonly known?
Which 664 Northumbrian church council, held at Abbess Hilda’s monastery, settled a dispute between Ionan and Roman customs by accepting the Roman method of calculating Easter?
At the Synod of Whitby, which Northumbrian king chose Roman customs after hearing arguments from Colman and Wilfrid?

In Hindu thought, what is the collective name for the four proper aims of human life represented by dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa? This framework encompasses duty, material prosperity, desire, and spiritual liberation.
Within Puruṣārtha, which aim refers to liberation from the cycle of rebirth and the attainment of spiritual freedom? It is distinguished from the aims associated with duty, prosperity, and desire.

Tradition identifies this ancient Chinese sage as the author of the Tao Te Ching and associates him with the teaching of wu wei, or non-forcing action. Later accounts portray him as a contemporary of Confucius. Who is he?

Laozi is traditionally credited with composing this classic Chinese text, arranged in 81 short chapters on the Dao and virtue. Its title is commonly translated as “The Book of the Way and Its Virtue.” What is the work?

Observed in China in early April, about 15 days after the spring equinox, this holiday is marked by families tending ancestral graves and presenting offerings to the dead. What is this observance called?
During the Qingming Festival, families may burn this imitation currency as an offering for deceased relatives. What is this traditional item called?

This Pauline letter addresses a church in a prosperous Greek port where the apostle had helped establish the community. It discusses spiritual gifts, describes love as patient and kind, and devotes a later chapter to resurrection; what letter is it?

In First Corinthians, Paul responds to factional disputes and practical questions raised by a congregation in a major port on the isthmus between mainland Greece and the Peloponnese. What city was home to that church?

What branch of Christian theology examines the person and nature of Jesus, especially how his divinity and humanity are related? It also addresses terms such as “person” and “nature” when explaining who Christ is.

In Christology, which gathering held in 451 affirmed that Jesus is one person in two natures, divine and human, “without confusion” or “division”? Its definition is rejected by Oriental Orthodox churches.

Centered on a mother’s search for her abducted daughter, these secret initiation rites were held at Eleusis and connected with teachings about death and the afterlife. What were these ancient Greek rites called?
Within the Eleusinian Mysteries, initiates honored a goddess associated with grain and agriculture whose daughter was abducted by Hades. Which goddess was central to these rites?
Genesis 2 describes this first human as formed from dust and placed in Eden to cultivate and guard the garden. His name is associated with the Hebrew word for ground or soil; what is his name?
In Genesis, after Adam is placed in Eden, God creates this woman from one of his ribs as a companion. She later eats fruit from the tree of knowledge and gives some to him; who is she?
In the Qur’anic account, God tells the angels that He will place Adam in this earthly role, a term commonly rendered “successor” or “vicegerent.” What Arabic title names the role?

In Hindu mythology, this avatar appears with a human body and a lion’s head to protect the devoted prince Prahlada. At twilight, he kills Prahlada’s father, Hiranyakasipu, on a threshold, circumventing the demon king’s protections.
In the Narasimha story, what is the name of the young devotee who remains faithful despite his father Hiranyakasipu’s attempts to destroy him, and whom Narasimha rescues?
This vessel carried Jason and his band of heroes toward Colchis on their quest for the Golden Fleece. What was the ship called?
During the voyage of the Argo, a dove was sent ahead to test a pair of rocks that slammed together and threatened to crush passing ships. What were these rocks called?

In Jewish dietary law, this Hebrew adjective describes food that is fit for consumption by observant Jews. It is commonly contrasted with *treif* and is roughly comparable to *halal* in Islam. What is this designation?

Under kosher dietary rules, most insects are forbidden, but this kind is traditionally permitted. It appears as the eighth plague in Exodus and is described as food eaten by John the Baptist in the wilderness. What is it?
In K’iche’ Maya mythology, what underworld realm below the earth is governed by death-associated lords? In the Popol Vuh, the Hero Twins travel there and defeat those rulers through cunning.

A foundational K’iche’ Maya narrative describes the Hero Twins’ journey to Xibalba and their contest with its death-associated lords. Its title is commonly rendered in English as “Book of Counsel”; what is this work called?

Catholic teaching distinguishes this event from the Immaculate Conception, which concerns Jesus’s mother’s own conception. What doctrine holds that, at the end of her earthly life, she was taken body and soul into heavenly glory?
The Assumption of Mary was formally defined as Catholic dogma by Pope Pius XII in 1950 through an apostolic constitution. What is the title of that document, taken from its Latin opening words?
What is the devotional practice of abstaining from food, and sometimes other activities, as an act of worship? It includes Islamic observances and Christian abstinence during Lent.
In religious fasting, which ninth month of the Islamic calendar commemorates the first revelation to Muhammad? Muslims fast from dawn until sunset during this month, which ends with Eid al-Fitr.

In the Gathas associated with Zoroaster, this uncreated, wise, and benevolent deity is described as creator and upholder of truth and right order. Achaemenid king Darius also credited this deity with creating the world and supporting his kingship. Who is this supreme deity of Zoroastrianism?

In the Gathas, this principle is the truth and right order upheld by Ahura Mazda, contrasted with druj, or falsehood and disorder. It also guides proper conduct and the just ordering of the world. What is this central Zoroastrian concept?

This king of Ephyra, later known as Corinth, angered Zeus after revealing to Asopus that Zeus had abducted his daughter Aegina. In another episode, he temporarily stopped death by trapping Thanatos. Who was he?

Sisyphus is traditionally credited with founding this ancient Greek city, located near the isthmus connecting the Peloponnese with mainland Greece. The city gave its name to the athletic festival held there in honor of Poseidon.
The adjective derived from Sisyphus’s name describes labor that is strenuous, repetitive, and ultimately futile. What is this adjective?
A legendary Chinese archer is said to have shot nine of ten suns from the sky after they appeared together and scorched the world. What is his name?
In the Chinese legend of Hou Yi, ten blazing celestial bodies appeared together and scorched the world. How many did the archer shoot down, leaving just one?

In Homer’s *Iliad*, this Corinthian hero appears in the family history of Glaucus as his son and the grandson of Sisyphus. Sent to Lycia by King Proetus, he defeated the Chimera and the Amazons before surviving an ambush; who was he?

In later versions of Bellerophon’s myth, this winged horse is captured at a spring and carries him toward Mount Olympus. Zeus sends a gadfly to sting it, causing Bellerophon to fall; what is the horse’s name?
Which Olympian, son of Zeus and Leto and twin brother of Artemis, was worshipped at Delphi as Pythios and associated with prophecy, music, and archery?
At which sanctuary, where a priestess delivered Apollo’s prophetic responses and an omphalos marked the world’s center, did ancient Greeks seek divine guidance?
Apollo pursued which nymph after Eros’s arrow kindled his desire; she appealed to her river-god father Peneus, who transformed her into a laurel tree?
Which stringed instrument, often shown in Apollo’s hands and said in one myth to have been fashioned by Hermes from a tortoise shell, accompanied song and poetry?
At Delphi, what title was given to the priestess who served Apollo by delivering the sanctuary’s prophetic responses, traditionally seated on a tripod?

In ancient Egyptian mummification, four vessels received the liver, lungs, stomach, and intestines after they were removed from the body. The Egyptians believed the preserved organs would be needed by the deceased in the afterlife. What were these funerary vessels called?
Canopic jars were protected by the Four Sons of Horus, each associated with a particular organ. Which baboon-headed guardian was linked to the lungs?
In Norse myth, this serpent-like dragon gnaws at the roots of the world-tree. The poem Völuspá also depicts it emerging from below with corpses in its wings; what is its name?

Which immense ash tree stands at the center of the Norse cosmos, with roots reaching into multiple realms? Níðhöggr gnaws at one of its roots, while the squirrel Ratatoskr runs along its trunk carrying messages.

In Valmiki’s Sanskrit epic, this prince is born in Ayodhya to King Dasaratha and Queen Kausalya, marries Sita, and spends 14 years in forest exile before defeating Ravana. Who is this seventh avatar of Vishnu?
In the story of Rama, what ancient city in present-day Uttar Pradesh is his birthplace and the capital of Kosala, whose throne he assumes after his forest exile?
Which Hindu festival of lights is associated with Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana returning to Ayodhya after 14 years of exile and Rama’s victory over Ravana?
In Apollonius of Rhodes’s epic, Jason sails to Colchis in search of the Golden Fleece with a company of Greek heroes. What is the traditional name for this band?
Jason led the Argonauts on a voyage aboard a ship built by Argus with Athena’s help. What was the vessel called, whose prow was said to contain a prophetic beam of oak from Dodona?

What major South Asian festival is marked by lighting oil lamps and candles, decorating homes with rangoli, and celebrating the triumph of light over darkness? In one Hindu tradition, it also commemorates Rama and Sita’s return to Ayodhya.
During Diwali, Hindus commonly perform a puja for this goddess of prosperity, who is often depicted seated on a lotus and is the consort of Vishnu. Who is she?
What Sikh observance celebrated alongside Diwali commemorates Guru Hargobind’s release from Mughal imprisonment and his return to Amritsar?

Across religions, water is used in bodily rites that prepare worshippers for sacred acts; Islam’s wudu is one familiar example, while related practices appear in Judaism, Christianity, and Hinduism. What general term names this practice of ritual bodily purification?

Ablution in Islam is often carried out before salah through a prescribed sequence that includes washing the face and arms, wiping the head, and washing the feet. What Arabic term names this specific preparatory rite?

In Christian moral teaching, which capital vice names sexual desire when it becomes excessive or disordered? Dante offers a literary example through Paolo and Francesca, condemned among the souls in the second circle.
In Dante Alighieri’s Divine Comedy, the second circle is associated with Lust, and Paolo and Francesca are swept through it in an unending storm. What is the title of this first part of the poem?

Beginning on the 15th of Tishrei, this Jewish harvest festival recalls the Israelites’ wilderness wanderings. Participants traditionally dwell in temporary booths and use a set of four species that includes a palm branch and a citron. What is this festival called?

During Sukkot, families may eat—and sometimes sleep—in a temporary outdoor booth with a roof made from plant material, built so that the sky remains visible through gaps. What is this structure called?
This Mahayana Buddhist tradition developed in China as Chan and emphasizes meditation, direct insight into Buddha-nature, and disciplined practice. What tradition is it?
In Zen Buddhism, practitioners may sit upright and attend to posture and breath as part of a central meditation discipline. What is the Japanese name for this seated practice?
Zen Buddhism traces its Chinese precursor, Chan, to traditions that credit a semi-legendary monk—described as Indian or Central Asian—with bringing the teaching to China. What was the monk’s name?

Daughter of Demeter and Zeus, she was carried into the underworld by Hades, and her recurring return to her mother was linked to the seasonal renewal of vegetation. Who is this Greek goddess and queen of the underworld?
Persephone and Demeter were central figures in these initiation rites at Eleusis, whose participants were promised a more hopeful fate after death. What were these ancient Greek rites called?
In Greek cult, Persephone was also worshipped under this title, which means “the Girl” and emphasizes her maiden aspect. What was this name?
Persephone was worshipped as a goddess of marriage and childbirth in this ancient Greek settlement in southern Italy, located in what is now Calabria. What was the settlement called?

In most Christian churches, this initiation rite applies water by immersion, pouring, or sprinkling, and often invokes the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. It marks entry into Christian life and community; traditions differ on whether it is administered to infants or only to people who profess their faith. What is this rite?
The Gospel accounts place Jesus’ baptism by John in this river. It flows through the region of the Sea of Galilee and empties into the Dead Sea. What river is it?
In Greek religion, she presided over lawful marriage and childbirth and held the rank of queen among the Olympians. She was both sister and wife of Zeus. What goddess is described?
Hera’s Roman counterpart was the wife of Jupiter and a goddess associated with marriage and women. What was her Roman name?
In stories about Hera, the hundred-eyed Argus Panoptes was associated with a bird whose tail feathers were said to preserve his eyes after his death. Which sacred bird is described?

What term describes controversial religious or ideological groups often marked by intense leadership, unusual beliefs, and strong demands for members’ allegiance? The Branch Davidians and the group whose members died in a 1997 mass suicide known as Heaven’s Gate are often discussed in this context.
Among cults associated with events of the 1990s, which group based at the Mount Carmel Center near Waco, Texas, was besieged by federal agents in 1993?

In the Gospel of Matthew, this extended discourse attributed to Jesus opens with a series of blessings and includes teachings on prayer, almsgiving, and the Lord’s Prayer. By what traditional title is this collection of teachings known?
Within the Sermon on the Mount, what is the name for the series of blessings that begins with “Blessed are the poor in spirit” and includes the promise that the meek shall inherit the earth?
What archetypal figure of learned supernatural magic is represented by Merlin, who aids Arthur, and by the deceptive Archimago in Edmund Spenser’s *The Faerie Queene*?
In *The Faerie Queene*, which deceptive wizard sends a false dream that makes Redcrosse Knight suspect Una’s chastity and leads to their separation?

This marriage rite is treated as a samskara, a major life-cycle observance, and joins a couple’s families as well as the couple. Vows may be made before a sacred fire understood as Agni, beneath a pavilion called a mandap; customs vary by region and family. What is this practice?

During Hindu marriage, one rite has the couple take seven steps together while making commitments associated with their shared household and life. Its name is often translated as “seven steps,” and in some traditions it is distinct from separately circling the fire. What is this rite?

What subject unites the Navajo tradition of two deities who debated what to name their invention and the Hopi story of a grandmother figure who helped create humanity? Both traditions center on sacred, web-weaving beings.

Within Spiders in Mythology, which mortal Lydian weaver challenged Athena to a tapestry contest, depicted the gods’ misdeeds in her work, and was transformed into a web-spinning creature after the goddess destroyed the tapestry?

An ancient Egyptian god associated with the dead, resurrection, vegetation, and the afterlife was murdered and dismembered by his brother before being restored through the rites of his wife. He was then revered as ruler of the underworld and is often shown as a wrapped, mummiform king holding a crook and flail. Who is this deity?

In the central myth of Osiris, this goddess searched Egypt for his scattered body parts and used magic to restore him. She was both his sister and wife and later became the mother of Horus. Which goddess is she?

In the Osiris myth, this brother murders and dismembers him, then later becomes the rival whom Horus must overcome. Egyptian tradition also associates this deity with disorder and depicts him defending the sun god Ra against Apep. Name this god.

The posthumous son of Osiris, this falcon-headed deity avenges his father in a struggle against Set and becomes a central emblem of legitimate kingship. Egyptian rulers were linked with this god in life, while the dead king was associated with Osiris. Identify the deity.
Osiris is often pictured wearing a tall white headdress framed by two ostrich feathers, distinguishing it from the striped nemes cloth. What is the traditional name of this headdress?

A prince of the Shakya clan, this teacher left a sheltered life, pursued spiritual practice, and became known for teaching a way out of suffering and rebirth. What name is commonly used for the historical founder of Buddhism?
Traditional biographies of Gautama Buddha place his birth in a garden grove at a site in modern-day Nepal, later marked by an Ashokan pillar. What is the name of this birthplace?

Traditional accounts say Gautama Buddha attained awakening beneath a tree after abandoning extreme asceticism; a major pilgrimage complex commemorating the event stands in present-day Bihar. What is the name of that site?

In a sermon associated with Deer Park, Gautama Buddha set out a teaching framework that diagnoses suffering, traces its origin, declares its cessation possible, and prescribes a way to that cessation. What is this framework called?
Gautama Buddha’s approach is often described as avoiding the extremes of luxurious sensual indulgence and punishing self-mortification. What is the name of the balanced course he taught?
This Protestant denomination emerged from the Millerite movement of the 1840s and observes Saturday as its Sabbath. Its world headquarters are in Silver Spring, Maryland; what is it called?
A prominent 19th-century pioneer of the Seventh-day Adventist Church, this American author reported religious visions and wrote *Steps to Christ* and *The Great Controversy*. Who was she?
In the Volsunga Saga, this legendary Valkyrie teaches Sigurd magical runes. After Sigurd dies, she joins him on his funeral pyre; what is her name?
Brynhild teaches magical runes to the dragon-slaying hero whose funeral pyre she later joins. In the Volsunga Saga, what is this hero’s name?

In Greek mythology, this eldest son of Cronus and Rhea received the realm beneath the earth when he and his brothers divided the cosmos after defeating the Titans. He was associated with both the dead and riches hidden underground.

Hades’s wife was taken to his realm, and her mother Demeter’s grief was said to harm the earth’s fertility. After eating pomegranate seeds below, she had to spend part of each year there and the rest with her mother.

At the entrance to Hades’s realm, this monstrous watchdog kept the dead from leaving and the living from entering. It was famed for its three heads, and Heracles had to bring it to the surface as one of his labors.
In Hades’s underworld, the gods swore binding oaths upon this river’s waters. Thetis dipped the infant Achilles into it, leaving vulnerable the heel by which she held him.

Hades was also worshipped under this Greek title, meaning “the wealthy one” and emphasizing his connection with riches beneath the earth. Its Latinized form later became a familiar Roman name for the god.

In Greek mythology, this beast terrorized a district in the Peloponnese, and its golden hide could not be pierced by mortal weapons. Heracles defeated it by strangling it, then used one of its own claws to remove the hide; what creature was this?

The Nemean Lion was the first opponent in a sequence of twelve tasks imposed on a Greek hero after he was ordered to serve a Mycenaean king. What is the hero’s Greek name, also rendered in Latin as Hercules?
After the Nemean Lion became the first task in Heracles’ labors, the hero continued serving the ruler who had commissioned the whole series. What king of Mycenae and Tiryns was that?
The Nemean Lion took its name from the ancient Greek site where it dwelled; that same place later gave its name to panhellenic games held in Zeus’s honor. What was the site’s name?

What 1949 comparative mythology study by Joseph Campbell, published by Pantheon Books in the Bollingen Series, argues that stories across cultures often share a recurring narrative pattern? It describes the pattern’s broad movement as departure, initiation, and return.
answer: The Hero with a Thousand Faces

question: In The Hero with a Thousand Faces, Joseph Campbell used a term borrowed from James Joyce for the recurring hero-story pattern he traced across myths and folklore. What is this term for a pattern that can involve departure, trials and transformation, and a return with a boon?
In Roman mythology, which god personifies love and desire and corresponds to the Greek god Eros? He is also the lover of Psyche in a famous myth.
In the myth of Cupid and Psyche, Cupid asks Jupiter to make Psyche immortal. What divine food does she receive, distinct from nectar?
In Islamic practice, this ritual washing of specified body parts is ordinarily performed before prayer. When water is unavailable, a dry alternative using clean earth may be used instead.
In Islamic practice, what dry purification rite serves as an alternative to Wudu when water is unavailable or its use would be harmful? It uses clean earth, such as dust, rather than water.

Chinese Chan tradition credits this semi-legendary monk with bringing its lineage from India, and legends say he spent nine years meditating while facing a wall. He is also traditionally associated with the Shaolin Temple. Who was he?

A later Chan account says this disciple stood in the snow outside Bodhidharma’s cave until accepted, then cut off his arm to demonstrate his resolve. He became the Second Patriarch of Chan in China. Who was he?

In Judges 13–16, this Israelite judge is dedicated to God as a Nazirite before birth, and his strength is associated with his uncut hair. After being captured and blinded by the Philistines, he brings down the pillars of a temple where they are gathered. Who is this figure?
In the closing episode of Samson’s story in Judges, the Philistines gather at a temple to celebrate their capture of him. Which deity are they honoring when Samson pulls down the temple’s pillars?
This Greek monster had a lion’s head and body, a goat projecting from its back, and a serpent for a tail. It terrorized Lycia before being slain by a hero riding Pegasus; name the creature.
In Greek myth, King Iobates sent a hero to destroy the Chimera after it ravaged Lycia. With Athena’s aid, the hero rode Pegasus and defeated the monster; who was he?

Traditionally attributed to Luke, this fifth book of the New Testament continues the story told in the Gospel of Luke. It begins with Jesus’ ascension and the gathering of his followers, then ends with Paul preaching under guard while awaiting trial. What book is it?

In Acts of the Apostles, Jesus’ followers gather in Jerusalem for a Jewish festival when the Holy Spirit comes upon them, and they begin speaking in languages understood by visitors from many lands. What event marks this moment in the early church’s story?

In Acts of the Apostles, Paul arrives under guard at this imperial capital and spends two years in rented lodging, receiving visitors and preaching while awaiting trial. Which city is the setting of the book’s final scene?

In the Kojiki, Izanami enters this realm after dying while giving birth to the fire deity Kagutsuchi. Her husband later journeys there in an attempt to bring her back to the land of the living. What is this realm called?
In the myth of Yomi, which creator deity travels to the realm to retrieve his wife, then flees after seeing her decayed body? He seals the entrance behind him with a massive boulder.

In Hindu tradition, which manifestation of Vishnu is depicted with a horse’s head and revered as a divine source of knowledge? This figure is also closely connected with the preservation of sacred scriptures.

Hayagriva is associated with safeguarding and transmitting these foundational Hindu scriptures, traditionally grouped into four collections and including hymns, chants, and ritual formulas. What are these scriptures called?

This ancient Egyptian god was associated with the Red Land, deserts, storms, and disorder. In a major succession myth, he murdered and dismembered his brother, then faced his nephew in a struggle for the throne; elsewhere, he helped defend the solar barque on its nightly voyage. Who is this god?

In Egyptian myth, Set murdered and dismembered this god, whose wife and sister gathered his scattered body parts and restored him long enough to conceive their son. He thereafter ruled the dead as lord of the underworld. Who is this god?

On Ra’s nightly passage through the underworld, Set defends the sun god against this enormous serpent, whose attack threatens the sun’s return at dawn. Egyptians portrayed the creature as a force of primordial chaos that had to be defeated for the solar cycle to continue. What is the serpent’s name?
What is the name of the marriage system in which a person has more than one spouse at once? Many Latter-day Saints historically practiced it before the mainline church renounced it in 1890.
In 1890, this president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints issued a declaration that led the mainline church to renounce polygamy. Who was he?
Embalmers removed internal organs, dried the body with a mineral substance, and wrapped it in linen to prepare it for the afterlife. What funerary process was this?
During ancient Egyptian mummification, embalmers used a naturally occurring salt mixture to draw moisture from the body. What was this drying agent called?

In the Gospel of John, this brother of Mary and Martha is called out of his tomb after four days, and Jesus famously weeps before the miracle. Which New Testament figure is at the center of this miracle?

In the account of Lazarus of Bethany, Mary and Martha are associated with a village east of Jerusalem that is now identified with a town in the West Bank. What is the modern town, whose Arabic name is often rendered “the place of Lazarus”?

The account of Lazarus of Bethany’s four-day burial and restoration appears in the chapter of the Fourth Gospel that includes Jesus’ words “I am the resurrection and the life.” What is the chapter reference?

Matthew places this address to God in the Sermon on the Mount, following Jesus’ warning against ostentatious devotion. Its petitions ask for God’s kingdom, daily bread, forgiveness, and deliverance from evil. What is this central Christian formula called?

The Lord’s Prayer is also recorded in this early Christian instructional text, which tells readers to pray it three times daily. Its version differs in wording from the forms in Matthew and Luke. What is the text called?

In Greek mythology, this group assessed the souls of the dead and determined their posthumous destinations, including the Elysian and Asphodel Fields. Minos and Rhadamanthus are among its best-known members. What is this group called?
Among the Judges of the Underworld, which former king of Crete demanded tribute from Athens after the death of his son Androgeus? His myths also connect him with the Minotaur and the labyrinth.
In the traditional Hindu varna order, this group is ranked above the Kshatriyas and is associated with religious learning and ritual duties. What is the name of this priestly varna?
Brahmins officiated in this Vedic royal horse sacrifice, in which a consecrated stallion was allowed to roam before the rite was completed. What is the name of this ritual?
In Norse mythology, what episode recounts the chief god surrendering one of his eyes at a well in exchange for a drink that would grant wisdom and knowledge?
In the account of Odin's Eye Sacrifice, what is the name of the spring beneath the roots of Yggdrasil where the god gives up an eye for a wisdom-granting drink?

In the medieval Danse macabre, this figure draws people of every rank into a final dance; in a 1957 Ingmar Bergman film, it plays chess with the knight Antonius Block. What anthropomorphic personification is represented by this figure?

In this 1957 Swedish film, Antonius Block returns from the Crusades during the Black Plague and tries to prolong his life in a chess match with Death. Directed by Ingmar Bergman and starring Max von Sydow as Block, what film closes with a famous silhouetted dance procession?

In 1 Samuel, a heavily armored champion from Gath came forward for forty days, challenging Israel to settle the conflict through single combat. Which Philistine warrior was felled by a stone before the young challenger used his sword?
In the familiar 1 Samuel account, this young shepherd refuses King Saul’s armor and faces Goliath with a sling and smooth stones. What future king of Israel knocks the champion down with one stone?

A passage in 2 Samuel 21:19 credits this Bethlehemite with killing Goliath the Gittite, while 1 Chronicles 20:5 describes the slain warrior as Goliath’s brother. What warrior is named in the wording of 2 Samuel?

In Scientology’s account of events roughly 75 million years ago, this ruler of a Galactic Confederacy transported billions of people to Earth, where they were killed with hydrogen bombs. What is this figure’s name?
In Scientology, the account of Xenu’s mass killing appears in a confidential advanced teaching often nicknamed the “Wall of Fire.” What is the name of this level, commonly abbreviated OT III?

In Norse myth, this wise figure was beheaded during a conflict between two groups of gods, yet Odin preserved the head and consulted it for secret knowledge. The figure is also associated with a famous source of wisdom beneath Yggdrasil. Who is he?
Mímir’s name is reflected in this well at the roots of Yggdrasil, whose water was associated with wisdom. Odin sacrificed an eye to drink from this source; what is the well called?
Mímir is attested in this medieval collection of mythological poems, which includes Völuspá and Hávamál. What is the collection called, as distinguished from Snorri Sturluson’s prose handbook?

Medieval Icelandic sources preserve accounts of a treasure-guarding being slain by Sigurd, a world-encircling adversary of Thor at Ragnarök, and a creature that gnaws at a root of Yggdrasil. What mythological topic brings these figures together?
answer: Serpents and Dragons in Norse Mythology

question: In Serpents and Dragons in Norse Mythology, which being coils around Midgard and is foretold to fight Thor at Ragnarök? Their encounter ends with each killing the other.
What is the natural name for the body of traditional stories that includes Nüwa repairing the sky, Pangu emerging from a cosmic egg, and tales of an archer who shot down nine suns?

In Chinese mythology, which figure drank an elixir of immortality obtained by her husband and became associated with the Moon? Her story is traditionally recalled during the Mid-Autumn Festival, when people eat mooncakes.
Created by H. P. Lovecraft, this Great Old One is said to sleep beneath the Pacific in a sunken city. Its monstrous form is commonly depicted with wings and a tentacled head; what is its name?
In the Cthulhu Mythos, what sunken city beneath the Pacific is described as the place where Cthulhu sleeps?

This ethnoreligious community practices a Gnostic tradition in which repeated immersion in flowing water is central, and its members revere John the Baptist as the final prophet. What is the community’s name?
The Mandaeans practice a Gnostic religion whose central ritual is masbuta, a baptism performed in flowing water. What is the name of this religion?
In Norse mythology, which goddess is Odin’s wife and is associated with marriage, family life, prophecy, and clairvoyance? She is also the mother of Baldr.

Frigg is married to which Norse god, the ruler of the Aesir associated with wisdom, war, poetry, and magic? In myth, he gives one eye for a drink from Mimir’s well and hangs from Yggdrasil to gain knowledge of the runes.

This annual Islamic pilgrimage takes place in Mecca during the final month of the lunar calendar. It is one of the Five Pillars and is required once in a lifetime for Muslims who are physically and financially able to undertake it. What is it?
During Hajj, pilgrims gather on the ninth day of Dhu al-Hijjah for a vigil at this open expanse east of Mecca, considered the pilgrimage’s central rite. What is this site?

Before performing the sacred rites of Hajj, pilgrims enter a state of consecration that involves specific restrictions; many men also wear two simple, unstitched white cloths. What is this state and associated dress called?

Which mythical beings appear in folklore around the world, often combining serpentine bodies with traits such as wings and claws? Depending on the tradition, they may be benevolent or hostile and are commonly associated with great strength, flight, fire, or treasure.

In one East Asian tradition, Dragons are associated with rain, the sea, and other forms of water. Beginning in the Han dynasty, they also became emblems of imperial authority; what culturally specific kind of dragon is described?
In Germanic legend, which former giant transformed into one of the Dragons to guard a hoard of gold? Siegfried slew him, and tasting his blood gave the hero the ability to understand birdsong.
This Israelite lineage supplied the royal house of David, from which Solomon also came. Revelation evokes it with the image of a lion associated with messianic victory. What is this lineage?

The Tribe of Judah is linked to this shepherd-king, who captured Jerusalem and made it his capital. Biblical tradition also presents him as the founder of a dynasty promised an enduring throne. Who was this king?

In Norse mythology, which Aesir deity guards the rainbow bridge connecting Midgard and Asgard and watches for threats approaching the gods’ stronghold? He is also famed for extraordinarily keen sight and hearing.
Heimdallr keeps a horn whose blast will be heard throughout the worlds when Ragnarök begins. What is this instrument called?

Genesis identifies this figure as Abraham’s son by Hagar and recounts that he and his mother were sent into the wilderness, where God heard and protected them. The Qur’an calls him a messenger and prophet and describes him joining his father in raising the foundations of the House; name this figure.

In the Genesis account of Ishmael, this Egyptian servant of Sarah is his mother, and she is sent with him into the wilderness after Sarah demands their departure. God provides for them there; name this woman.

In ancient Phocis, this sanctuary and settlement stood near Mount Parnassus and drew pilgrims to the Castalian Spring to consult its priestess, the Pythia. A sacred stone here was called the omphalos, marking the place where Zeus’s two eagles met.
At Delphi, the Pythia served in the sanctuary of this Olympian god, who was said to have slain the Python. He was also the twin brother of Artemis and the Greek god of music and archery.

Sent by King Pelias to retrieve the Golden Fleece from Colchis, this hero sailed aboard the Argo with a company known as the Argonauts. With Medea’s help, he overcame the challenges set by King Aeëtes; who was he?

During Jason’s quest for the Golden Fleece, which daughter of King Aeëtes used her knowledge of magic to help him yoke the fire-breathing bulls and defeat the guardian of the fleece? She later left Colchis with the leader of the Argonauts.

What is the collective name for the four ancient Sanskrit sacred collections central to Hindu traditions, traditionally revered as śruti, or “what is heard”? These texts were preserved chiefly through careful oral recitation.

Within the Vedas, which collection arranges many verses drawn from the Rigveda for melodic chanting in ritual settings? Its musical organization distinguishes it from collections chiefly focused on hymns or sacrificial formulas.

In many Aboriginal Australian traditions, an ancestral being’s journeys are said to shape waterways and other landforms, and it is associated with the Dreaming, rain, and fertility. What broad name is commonly used for this creator being, despite communities having distinct names and stories?
In western Arnhem Land, what name is used for the Rainbow Serpent in Kuninjku traditions? It is associated with creating sacred sites and may be depicted with features of several animals.

In Shinto tradition, this solar kami rules Takamagahara and is counted among the Three Precious Children born to Izanagi. She is also regarded as the divine ancestress of Japan’s imperial line; what is her full honorific name?
Amaterasu Ōmikami is principally worshipped at a celebrated Shinto sanctuary in Ise, Mie Prefecture; its Naikū precinct is dedicated to her. By what common name is this sanctuary known?

Amaterasu Ōmikami sent this grandson from the heavenly realm Takamagahara to rule the earthly land, and Japanese imperial mythology traces the imperial line through him. What is the name of this grandson?

A fourth-century Christian bishop from Lycia became renowned in later traditions for secret acts of generosity toward the poor. He is widely regarded as the historical inspiration for the gift-bringing figure associated with Christmas. Who was this bishop?
A later legend places Saint Nicholas of Myra at this 325 CE assembly of bishops, where he allegedly struck Arius during a dispute over Christ’s nature. What gathering is this?

Which Mexica patron deity was associated with warfare and the sun, though not identical to the sun deity Tonatiuh? Honored in the southern shrine of Tenochtitlan’s great temple, this deity was often depicted as a hummingbird or an eagle.
In Tenochtitlan’s central ceremonial precinct, what major structure had a southern shrine dedicated to Huitzilopochtli and a northern shrine dedicated to Tlaloc?

In Islamic eschatology, what title is given to the expected end-times redeemer who will establish justice before the final judgment? Belief in this figure is found in several Muslim traditions, though details of his identity and role vary.
Which Sudanese religious leader proclaimed himself the Mahdi in 1881 and led a revolt that captured Khartoum in 1885?

In Norse mythology, the goddess Iðunn keeps these fruits to preserve the gods’ youth. In Greek mythology, a dragon guards them in a garden at the edge of the world. What are these mythic fruits called?
A Greek heroine famous for outrunning her suitors stopped to retrieve three golden apples during a footrace, allowing her challenger to win and marry her. Who was the huntress?

In Hesiod’s account, Zeus orders this first woman to be fashioned from earth and water, with other gods contributing her gifts and adornments. She opens a jar whose escaping contents bring suffering into the world, while Hope remains inside.
Pandora was sent to this Titan, who accepted her despite a warning from his brother not to accept gifts from Zeus. He later became the husband of Pandora in the Greek myth.
Which Cretan princess, daughter of Minos and Pasiphae, gave Theseus a ball of thread so he could retrace his route through the Labyrinth after slaying the Minotaur?
After Theseus abandons Ariadne on Naxos, which god finds her and, in a familiar account, marries her and makes her immortal?

In Greek myth, this legendary conflict pitted Achaean forces against the city of Troy. It was traditionally sparked when Paris took Helen from Menelaus and, in its famous ending, the Greeks entered the city using a wooden horse. What was this war called?

The Trojan War is the setting for this Homeric epic, which opens with an appeal to the Muse to sing of a warrior’s rage. Rather than recounting the entire decade-long siege, it focuses on events in its tenth year, including the quarrel between Achilles and Agamemnon and the death of Hector. What is this poem?

Although the historicity of the Trojan War remains debated, most scholars identify Troy’s archaeological location with this ancient mound in modern Turkey, near the Dardanelles. Excavations there uncovered successive layers of settlement associated with the city. What is the site’s name?
In Hindu traditions, this major goddess is described in some accounts as Sati reborn. She is Shiva’s consort and the mother of Ganesha and Skanda. What is her name?
One Hindu legend says Parvati formed this deity from dirt rubbed from her body, after which Shiva brought him to life. Which deity, often depicted with an elephant’s head, is described in this story?
In the Hebrew Bible, which book tells of a prophet who tries to escape his commission by sailing toward Tarshish, then is sent to warn a great city of its coming destruction?
In the Book of Jonah, which great Assyrian city receives the prophet’s warning, after which its people fast and turn from their evil ways?

What historical label is applied to the major, regionally varied waves of evangelical Protestant revival that began in British North America in the 1730s and returned in a second major surge beginning in the 1790s in the early United States?
Within the history of the Great Awakenings, which famous 1801 Kentucky camp meeting near Paris drew thousands to several days of outdoor worship and became a defining episode of the Second Awakening?

Which river of the Greek underworld was the boundary crossed by the dead and the river on which the gods swore oaths they could not break? In another myth, a mother dipped her infant son into its waters to protect him.
Which Nereid, the mother of Achilles, dipped her infant son into the Styx to make him invulnerable, but held him by one spot that remained vulnerable?

In Sophocles’ tragedy about a king investigating a plague in Thebes, this blind prophet initially refuses to reveal what he knows. He eventually tells the king that he killed Laius and has unknowingly married his own mother. Who is the prophet?
In which Sophoclean tragedy does Tiresias warn the ruler of Thebes that his search for Laius’s killer will expose his own past? The play ends with the ruler blinded and Jocasta dead.

In Norse myth, the gods begin to age after Loki lures this Asgardian goddess away from her home. The giant Þjazi carries her off with the fruit she keeps, and the gods recover their youth after rescuing her; name the goddess.

In the Iðunn myth, this jötunn forces Loki to lure the goddess beyond Asgard and carries her and her apples away to Þrymheimr. After the gods rescue her, they kill him as he pursues them, leading his daughter Skaði to demand compensation; name the giant.

What name is given to the archetypal mythic catastrophe in which deities inundate the world or civilization, often followed by a culture hero’s survival and the renewal of humankind? Related versions appear in Genesis, Mesopotamian epics, and Greek mythology.
In Mesopotamian traditions of the Great Flood, what Akkadian epic, dated to the 18th century BCE, recounts a version of the catastrophe? It is named for its exceptionally wise human protagonist.

In the Greek tradition of the Great Flood sent by Zeus, which man survived with his wife Pyrrha and helped restore humanity by casting stones behind them? The couple were the only survivors of the deluge.
Which aquatic flowering plant, with blossoms that rise above muddy water, is a major Buddhist symbol of purity and awakening and is often depicted as the seat beneath Buddhas?
The sacred lotus is echoed in the name of a Chinese Buddhist religious organization associated with the 14th-century Red Turban Rebellion. What was this organization called?
In Zoroastrian belief, what is the name of the postmortem crossing where souls face judgment? It is guarded by a deity.
Which Zoroastrian deity is associated with guarding the Chinvat Bridge, the crossing encountered by souls after death?

In Shinto, this Japanese term refers to a broad class of sacred presences rather than a single kind of being. It can describe named deities, ancestors, and extraordinary natural features such as mountains or rivers. What is the term?

One of the best-known kami in the Kojiki, this solar goddess appears when Izanagi purifies himself after returning from Yomi. She rules the heavenly realm of Takamagahara and is associated with the Japanese imperial line. Who is she?

In Ovid’s account, this gifted mortal from Lydia earns fame for her weaving and challenges a goddess to a contest at the loom. After the goddess destroys her tapestry and she tries to hang herself, she is transformed into a web-spinning creature; who is she?

In the story of Arachne, which Greek goddess accepts the mortal weaver’s challenge and makes a tapestry depicting divine power and warnings against defying the gods? She destroys her rival’s work and transforms her into a spider.
What broad Christian movement emerged from the 16th-century Reformation and rejected papal authority? In France, its adherents during the Wars of Religion were known by a distinct name.

Within Protestantism, what name was given to French Calvinists who fought for religious rights during the French Wars of Religion from 1562 to 1598? Their ranks included Henry of Navarre, who later became King Henry IV.
A German Augustinian friar and theologian, he challenged the sale of indulgences associated with Johann Tetzel. His criticism helped launch the Protestant Reformation. Who was this reformer?

In 1517, Martin Luther set out propositions criticizing indulgences and inviting debate about their power and use. Traditionally, the writings were posted on the door of All Saints’ Church in Wittenberg. What are they called?

In the Qur’anic account of Adam’s creation, God commands the angels to prostrate before Adam, but one figure refuses and is described as arrogant. Which rebellious figure later becomes a tempter and adversary of humanity?
The Qur’an’s account of the prostration before Adam groups Iblis with the angels, but Qur’an 18:50 explicitly identifies him as belonging to another class of beings. What is that class called?

In Genesis, this nephew of Abraham lives in Sodom and is led out before the city’s destruction, accompanied by his wife and daughters. His wife’s fate after she looks back is one of the best-known details of the escape narrative; who is the man?
In Genesis, Lot and his family are told to flee this city before it is destroyed alongside Gomorrah. The same city is the setting for the visitors whom Lot welcomes into his home; what is its name?
