At a traditional Japanese shrine, this freestanding structure marks the threshold between the everyday world and sacred grounds. Its familiar form often consists of two upright pillars supporting one or more horizontal beams.

Torii stand at the entrances to sacred precincts in this indigenous Japanese religion, whose practices include reverence for kami and whose major sites include Ise Grand Shrine. What is the religion called?
In one Gospel miracle, Jesus fed four thousand people with seven loaves and a few fish. In Christian Eucharistic theology, this staple food is identified with Christ’s body; what is it?
In Christian worship, Bread and wine are shared in remembrance of a final meal Jesus held with his disciples before his arrest. At what meal did Jesus institute this practice?
In Scandinavian folklore, this humanoid supernatural being is often linked to mountains. Some tales describe it with a tail and say sunlight can turn it to stone. What creature is described?

A Henrik Ibsen play follows Peer Gynt, whose encounter with a Troll king inspired a famous orchestral passage. Which Norwegian composer wrote the incidental music later arranged into suites that include “Morning Mood” and “In the Hall of the Mountain King”?

This biblical anthology contains 150 religious poems, songs, and prayers in Jewish and Western Christian traditions. It is the first book of Ketuvim, the third section of the Tanakh, and many of its poems are traditionally associated with King David. What is its natural name?

Many poems in the Book of Psalms are traditionally attributed to this king, though that attribution is not considered historically established for the entire collection. He defeated the Philistine giant Goliath and was the father of Solomon; who was he?
The Book of Psalms is also known by this Hebrew title, used for the collection of hymns and prayers. The title means “praises”; what is it?

This son of Zeus and Hera was one of the Twelve Olympians and embodied battle’s physical courage as well as its brutality. Unlike his sister Athena, he was associated less with military strategy than with the violence of combat. Which Greek god is described?

Ares fathered this deity with Aphrodite, and the name of this figure became a word for an intense feeling of alarm. He was paired with his brother Deimos, whose name is associated with dread. Who is this god?

Ares’s affair with Aphrodite was exposed when her husband trapped the lovers in an unbreakable net and displayed them before the other gods. Which Olympian god of metalworking and craftsmanship devised the trap?
In Buddhism, this state of liberation brings an end to suffering and the cycle of rebirth. Its name is commonly interpreted as meaning “blowing out.” What is this state called?

The Greek skeptic from Elis whose ideal of ataraxia is sometimes compared with Buddhist Nirvana traveled with Alexander the Great’s expedition to India. He was also the teacher of Timon of Phlius. Who was he?

After Joseph Smith’s death, this religious leader became the second president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and guided its members westward. He selected the site for a major settlement in the Salt Lake Valley and later served as governor of Utah Territory. Who was he?

During Brigham Young’s leadership, Congress established this U.S. jurisdiction in 1850, and he served as its first governor. Initially much larger than the present-day state, it encompassed much of the Great Basin. What was it called?

In churches that trace bishops’ spiritual and ecclesiastical authority through an unbroken line back to Christ’s apostles, this doctrine supports the legitimacy of the episcopate. What is the doctrine called?
In Catholic episcopal ordination, what body parts does the consecrating bishop place on the candidate as a sign of transmitting authority in the tradition of apostolic succession?
In Greek myth, this creature had a lion’s body and a human head, and it challenged travelers near Thebes with a riddle. Oedipus ended its threat by answering correctly.
The Sphinx posed a famous riddle to this Theban hero, who answered it and became king of Thebes. In Sophocles’ tragedy, he is the son of Laius and Jocasta.

In Islam, this body of religious law and ethical guidance draws on the Quran and the Prophet Muhammad’s traditions, informing both worship and everyday conduct. What is this framework commonly called?
Within Sharia, Islamic classifications distinguish forbidden acts and foods from those that are permitted. What Arabic term is commonly used for food that Muslims are allowed to consume?

Which Kurdish ethno-religious community follows a distinct faith in which Melek Tawûs is revered as chief among seven Holy Beings rather than as an evil figure? Its major sacred site is Lalish in northern Iraq, and its people were targeted in the 2014 ISIL assault on Sinjar.

Among the Yazidis, what is the name of the secluded valley in northern Iraq that serves as the community’s principal pilgrimage destination and contains the shrine and tomb associated with Sheikh Adi ibn Musafir?
Born around 480 in the central Italian town of Norcia, this monk lived as a hermit near Subiaco before shaping communal monastic life with a practical guide of 73 chapters. What is his name?

After leaving Subiaco, Benedict of Nursia established this monastery around 529 on a hill in the Italian region of Lazio. Its abbey became closely associated with the monastic tradition shaped by his Rule. What was the monastery called?

This Christian movement grew from Bible-study groups associated with Charles Taze Russell in the 1870s and adopted its present name in 1931. Its members are known for house-to-house evangelism and for rejecting the doctrine of the Trinity. What is this movement called?
Jehovah’s Witnesses developed from Bible-study groups associated with Charles Taze Russell during the 1870s. In which Pennsylvania city did Russell’s group begin?
Which English family centered on Susanna, daughter of Samuel Annesley, included two sons whose preaching and hymns helped establish the Methodist movement?
Within the Wesley family, which son became a prolific Methodist hymn writer, composing thousands of hymns including “And Can It Be” and “O for a Thousand Tongues to Sing”?

In Egyptian religion, what is the name of the solar deity’s personified power, which could manifest as a goddess to punish his enemies? It belongs to a divine tradition related to, but distinct from, Horus’s restored wedjat.

In a myth involving the Eye of Ra, which lioness-headed goddess was sent to punish humanity after people conspired against Ra? Her rampage was halted when she drank beer colored red to resemble blood.
What term names the position that either denies that any gods exist or holds that belief in gods is unwarranted? It includes both explicit rejection of divine existence and broader nonbelief.

In discussions of atheism, what philosophical movement is associated with Albert Camus and Jean-Paul Sartre? Sartre characterized it as “a humanism,” distinguishing it from a position concerned only with belief in gods.

After a military draft reaches her family, this Chinese folk heroine takes her father’s place by joining the army under a male disguise. She serves for years, then declines official honors and returns home. Which legendary woman is described?
Mulan is the heroine of an anonymous Chinese folk poem that recounts her father’s conscription, her years of military service, and her return home. What is this poem commonly known as in English?
During Ramadan, Muslims abstain from food and drink from dawn until sunset. What is the name of the evening meal that ends each day's fast, traditionally beginning with dates?
At Iftar, the evening meal that ends the Ramadan fast, what fruit is traditionally eaten to break the fast, following a practice associated with the Prophet Muhammad?

This 18th-century New England Congregationalist minister became a leading preacher and theologian of the First Great Awakening. He served the church in Northampton, Massachusetts, and later became president of the College of New Jersey, now Princeton University. Who was he?

Jonathan Edwards delivered this sermon in Enfield, Connecticut, in 1741, warning listeners about divine judgment with images of a bow aimed at them and a spider held over a fire. What is the sermon’s title?
answer: Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God

question: In Celtic traditions and other folklore, these purported practitioners were believed to wield magic. Many people accused of practicing it were targeted in medieval and early modern persecutions. What are they commonly called?
Which 15th-century Latin treatise by Heinrich Kramer portrayed Witches as a serious religious threat? Its title is commonly translated as “The Hammer of Witches.”

This Sikh scripture contains hymns by Sikh religious leaders as well as devotional poets from other traditions. Sikhs regard it not simply as a sacred text but as their eternal, living spiritual guide. What is it called?
The original compilation of the Guru Granth Sahib was completed in 1604 and installed at the Harmandir Sahib. Which fifth Sikh Guru oversaw its compilation?

Which Hebrew Bible wisdom book, traditionally attributed to Solomon, opens by describing its purpose as imparting wisdom and instruction and teaches that reverence for the Lord is the beginning of knowledge?
In the Book of Proverbs, especially chapter 8, what female personification calls out to the inexperienced and says she was present before the earth’s foundations were laid?
Many traditions feature two closely linked heroic siblings who face dangers or accomplish great deeds together. What recurring motif is exemplified by Hunahpu and Xbalanque in the Popol Vuh?
In the mythological-twins motif, which K’iche’ Maya sacred narrative tells of Hunahpu and Xbalanque descending to Xibalba, where they face trials and challenge the underworld’s lords?

In Norse mythology, this god is Odin’s son and Sif’s husband, and he wields the hammer Mjölnir. He rides in a chariot drawn by two goats and is fated to fight the Midgard Serpent at Ragnarök. Which god is described?
This hammer wielded by Thor was forged by dwarves, and its unusually short handle is explained by Loki interfering with their work. What is the name of Thor’s weapon?
In Hymiskviða, Thor uses an ox’s head as bait while fishing with the giant Hymir, drawing up a serpent that encircles the world. Which monster is fated to fight Thor at Ragnarök?

An Old Norse poem tells how a jötunn steals Thor’s hammer and demands Freyja as his bride, only for Thor to disguise himself as the bride and retrieve the weapon at the wedding feast. What is the poem’s title?
Old English sources use this name for the Germanic thunder god corresponding to Thor, and the name is reflected in the origin of the weekday Thursday. What is this Old English god-name?

In Genesis, this patriarch is called by God to leave his father’s household for Canaan and receives a covenant promising descendants and land. He is traditionally described as the father of Isaac and Ishmael and is revered in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam; who is he?

According to Genesis, Abraham buys a burial property from Ephron the Hittite near Hebron so Sarah can be buried there. What is the name of the subterranean burial chamber at this site, also associated with the patriarchal family?
Genesis says that after Sarah’s death Abraham married this woman, who bore six sons, including Midian. What is her name?

In the Chinese zodiac, this animal occupies the fourth position, after the tiger and before the dragon. In lunar mythology, its jade counterpart is often depicted with a mortar and pestle beside the immortal Chang’e. What animal is it?
In the Chinese myth associated with the Rabbit sign, this immortal is said to dwell on the moon with a jade animal that pounds herbs in a mortar. Who is she?
These ordained renunciants traditionally wear robes, live in a sangha, and follow a monastic code known as the Vinaya. What are they commonly called?
Buddhist monks follow this collection of disciplinary rules, which guides monastic conduct and forms one of the three divisions of the Buddhist canon. What is it called?

In folklore from the state whose Upper and Lower Peninsulas are linked by the Mackinac Bridge, what cryptid is described as a large, canine-like biped resembling a werewolf? Its howl is said to sound like a human scream.
The Michigan Dogman legend gained wider attention after a 1987 song called “The Legend” aired on Traverse City’s WTCM-FM. Which Michigan radio personality wrote and recorded the song?

In Roman tradition, this deity combined military power with protection of agriculture and was honored as a guardian of the state. He was also said to father the twins at Rome’s legendary founding. Who was this god?
On the Tiber’s bend outside ancient Rome’s sacred boundary, this extensive public plain served for military drills and assemblies and was dedicated to Mars. What was this place called?
Augustus built a temple in his forum to Mars under a Latin epithet meaning “Avenger,” commemorating a vow tied to the defeat of Caesar’s assassins at Philippi. What was this specific title of Mars?

This star lies at the center of the Solar System, and nuclear fusion in its core powers the light and heat that reach Earth. In one Japanese myth, the return of a goddess from a cave restores its light to the world.

In Japanese Shinto mythology, this goddess hides in a cave, plunging the world into darkness and concealing the Sun. The other deities lure her out with a lively celebration, restoring light to the world; name this goddess.
Which Trojan prince was granted immortality by the dawn goddess but not eternal youth? As he grew old and withered, myth said he became a cicada.
In the myth of Tithonus, which goddess fell in love with him, carried him away, and asked Zeus to grant him immortality without asking that he remain young?

This beloved Aesir is the son of Odin and Frigg and is renowned for his beauty and goodness. His death at the hands of the blind Höðr, after Loki’s manipulation, becomes one of the events leading toward Ragnarök. Name this god.

After nearly everything had sworn not to harm Baldr, this shape-shifting god learned that Frigg had overlooked a young plant and guided the blind Höðr into using it. Which Norse trickster was responsible for the fatal scheme?
In European legend, this horse-like creature is distinguished by a single horn rising from its forehead. It is often associated with purity, magic, and healing. What is this mythical creature called?
In medieval lore about the Unicorn, its single horn was believed to have healing powers and to protect against poison. What is the traditional name for this horn?

Muslims regard this Arabic scripture as revelation given to Muhammad, and its text is organized into 114 chapters called surahs. It is central to Islamic prayer and recitation. What is this sacred text called?
Islamic tradition says this angel conveyed the Quran’s revelations to Muhammad over roughly 23 years. The same angel is associated with announcing Jesus’s birth to Mary. Who is this angel?
The Quran begins with a seven-verse surah whose name is commonly translated as “The Opening.” It is recited in every unit of the canonical Muslim prayer. What is the name of this surah?

After Muhammad’s death, Abu Bakr ordered an initial collection of Quranic material, while a later caliph is credited with standardizing the text and distributing official copies. Which caliph was responsible for that standardization?

In ancient Greek religion, these female devotees of Dionysus were associated with ecstatic frenzy and rites that could include tearing apart a living victim and eating its flesh raw. By what name are they commonly known?
In descriptions of Maenads’ rites, this Greek term refers specifically to tearing a living victim apart, rather than consuming its flesh raw. What is the term?
This eagle-like king of birds is born to Vinata and is described as the sworn enemy of the nāgas. He serves as the divine mount of Vishnu; name this figure from Hindu mythology.
Garuda, as Vishnu’s mount, is the sworn enemy of these serpent beings in Hindu mythology. Their king, Shesha, is depicted as the serpent on whom Vishnu rests; what are these beings called?
In Greek mythology, this three-headed hound guards the entrance to the Underworld and prevents the dead from leaving. Heracles captured it as the final task of his twelve labors. What is its name?
In the myth of Cerberus, which Greek hero captured the Underworld’s guardian as the final task among his twelve labors? He was the son of Zeus and the mortal woman Alcmene.
Cerberus is said to be the offspring of Echidna and which monstrous father? This serpent-featured giant battled Zeus for control of the cosmos.

During Odysseus’s long absence in Ithaca, this queen keeps his suitors at bay by promising to choose one after finishing a textile for his father, then secretly undoing each day’s work at night. What is the name of Odysseus’s faithful wife?

To delay the suitors, Penelope vowed not to choose a husband until she had finished a funeral textile for Odysseus’s elderly father. Each night, she secretly undid the work she had completed during the day; who was the textile intended for?

In Roman religion, this goddess was honored with Jupiter and Minerva as part of the Capitoline Triad. In Virgil’s Aeneid, her hostility toward the Trojans drives the epic’s opening conflict. Who is she?
In Book 1 of the Aeneid, Juno approaches this ruler of the winds and persuades him to unleash a storm against Aeneas’s fleet. In return, she promises him the nymph Deiopea. Who is he?

In East Asian mythology, what serpentine legendary creature is associated with rain, clouds, water, and power, and also appears as one of the twelve animals of the zodiac? It is often portrayed as benevolent and life-giving, unlike many treasure-hoarding monsters in European stories.

In the four-guardian cosmology associated with the Chinese dragon, which blue-green celestial creature guards the East? It is paired with the Vermilion Bird of the South, White Tiger of the West, and Black Tortoise of the North.

Worshippers often invoke this Hindu deity before beginning undertakings, and he is associated with auspicious beginnings and the removal of obstacles. Depicted with an elephant's head on a human body, he is widely revered as a son of Shiva and Parvati. Who is this deity?
Ganesha is honored in an annual Hindu festival whose celebrations can include public processions and carrying images to the coast for immersion. What is the name of this festival?

Achilles’ immortal pair Balius and Xanthus, and the flesh-eating animals Heracles took from Diomedes, belong to what topic in Greek mythology? What natural name groups these creatures and related figures?
Within Mythological Horses, what Greek sea creature has the forequarters of a horse and the tail of a fish, and is often shown drawing Poseidon’s chariot?

In Buddhism, practitioners take refuge in three foundational supports: the awakened teacher, the teaching, and the community that preserves it. What collective name is given to these objects of refuge?
Within the Three Jewels, which one refers to the Buddhist community that preserves and practices the teachings, traditionally centered on ordained monks and nuns?

Which Indian religious and philosophical tradition began in the eastern Gangetic plain around the fifth century BCE, follows teachings attributed to Siddhartha Gautama, and seeks liberation from dukkha through awakening?
In Buddhism, what canonical framework identifies dukkha, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to that cessation?
Which major branch of Buddhism, whose name means “Teaching of the Elders,” is prominent in Sri Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia and emphasizes the attainment of nirvana?
Which influential Mahayana scripture in Buddhism has a title referring to a flowering aquatic plant, teaches the universal potential for Buddhahood, and is central to Nichiren Buddhism?
This office is held by the Bishop of Rome, who leads the worldwide Catholic Church. What is the title commonly used for its holder?

The Pope’s political independence is based in a small city-state whose sovereignty was established by a 1929 agreement between the Holy See and Italy. What agreement also settled the long-running dispute between the papacy and the Italian state?

The Pope’s formal definitions of faith or morals made under narrowly defined conditions are covered by a doctrine defined at the First Vatican Council in 1870. What is this doctrine, which does not apply to every statement a pope makes?
This Christian sacrament commemorates the Last Supper through the ritual sharing of bread and wine, and its name comes from a Greek word meaning “thanksgiving.” What is it called?
In Catholic teaching about the Eucharist, what doctrine holds that the bread and wine become Christ’s body and blood in substance, while their sensory appearances remain unchanged?

In Jewish observance, this drink is used for the blessing marking Shabbat and for the four cups at Passover; Christian communities also use it in the Eucharist alongside bread. What fermented grape beverage is central to these rituals?
In Jewish practice, a blessing that sanctifies Shabbat is commonly recited over a cup of wine at the Friday-evening meal, and it is also used on festivals. What is this blessing called?

In Catholic devotion, this name refers both to a strand of prayer beads with a crucifix and to the prayer practice counted on them. Its customary five-decade form pairs ten Hail Marys with meditation on a Mystery in each decade.
Pope John Paul II added this group of meditations to the Rosary in 2002; it focuses on Jesus’ public ministry, including the wedding at Cana. What is this set called?
Which Japanese folk hero is said to have been born from a giant peach found by an elderly couple and later set out with a dog, monkey, and pheasant to battle ogres?
In the Momotaro story, what is the traditional name of the island where the hero and his animal companions confront the ogres?
In European folklore, this supernatural being is often described as magical and associated with an otherworldly realm. What is the common name for this kind of being?
In Shakespeare’s *A Midsummer Night’s Dream*, this mischievous fairy serves as Oberon’s jester and transforms Nick Bottom’s head into that of a donkey. What is the character’s name?
This traditional Chinese form of geomancy uses the arrangement and orientation of buildings, tombs, and other spaces to harmonize them with their surroundings. Its name literally means “wind-water.”
In feng shui, this term refers to the cosmic current whose movement through a place may be affected by landscapes, bodies of water, and the arrangement of structures. What is this current called?

Feng shui debates in Hong Kong have focused on this I. M. Pei-designed skyscraper, completed in 1990, whose angular, triangular framework was said to direct harmful energy toward neighboring buildings. What is the building’s name?

In Indian religions, what is the Sanskrit-named devotional rite carried out through offerings, prayers, and other ceremonial acts? Jain practice distinguishes its inward, intention-centered form, bhava, from its material form, dravya.
During which South Asian festival, often called the festival of lights, is Lakshmi puja commonly performed on the third day? Jains also associate this holiday with the nirvana of Mahavira.
At the wedding of this mortal king and sea goddess, a golden apple set in motion the Judgment of Paris. Their son became the foremost Greek warrior in the Trojan War. Which pair is described?
In the myth of Peleus and Thetis, their son fought as the leading Greek champion in the Trojan War and killed Hector after Hector slew Patroclus. What was this hero’s name?

In Hesiod’s *Theogony*, this youngest child of Cronus and Rhea was hidden while his father swallowed a wrapped stone in his place. He later freed his siblings and became the chief of the Olympian gods; who was he?
In Hesiod’s *Theogony*, Rhea concealed the infant Zeus on this Mediterranean island and arranged for the Curetes to drown out his cries. Which island was it?

In this funerary rite, a corpse is taken to an elevated enclosure rather than buried or cremated, avoiding contamination of the elements considered sacred. Scavenger birds consume the remains before the bones are collected. What is this practice called?
In Zoroastrian sky burial, the body is placed in a circular, open-air funerary structure, traditionally built of stone and used for exposure to scavenger birds. What is this structure called?
In Greek myth, Hera’s interference with Heracles’ birth allows this cousin to be born first and gain the throne of Mycenae. He later requires Heracles to complete the twelve labors. Who is this king?

Among the tasks assigned by Eurystheus, Heracles must defeat a many-headed monster from Lerna whose heads grow back when severed. With Iolaus’ help, he prevents them from regrowing by cauterizing the necks. What is the monster called?

In Norse cosmology, an immense ash tree stands at the center of the universe, with roots reaching distant wells and branches stretching into the heavens. The Nine Worlds are arranged around it, and the gods gather at its base; what is this cosmic tree called?
According to Norse tradition, the chief god of the Aesir hangs from Yggdrasil for nine nights, wounded by his own spear, to gain knowledge of the runes. What is this god’s name?
A squirrel associated with Yggdrasil races along its trunk, carrying messages between an eagle in its crown and a dragon at its roots. What is the squirrel called?
One creature associated with Yggdrasil gnaws at the tree’s roots and is linked in Norse poetry to the dead at Náströnd. What is this dragon or serpent called?
One root of Yggdrasil reaches a well associated with a wise being whose severed head advises Odin; Odin sacrifices an eye to drink from it. What is the well called?
In Greek mythology, which beautiful youth was loved by Apollo and accidentally killed when a jealous wind-god diverted a discus? Apollo caused a flower to grow from the youth’s blood.
In the myth of Hyacinthus, which personification of the west wind, jealous of Apollo’s affection for the youth, redirected the discus that struck him?

In Greek worship, this deity ruled the sea and was also linked to earthquakes, floods, and horses; sailors sought his favor for safe voyages. Artists commonly identified him with a trident, and in a contest for Athens he produced a salt-water spring before losing to a rival’s olive tree. Who is this god?

In the Athenian patronage contest, Poseidon struck the Acropolis with his trident and produced salt water, while his rival offered an olive tree that the judges preferred. Which goddess won the contest and became the divine protector of Athens?

A celebrated African American railroad ballad tells of a steel-driving worker who hammered a hand drill into rock and outlasted a steam-powered drill during tunnel construction. In the familiar legend, he dies from the effort after winning the contest. What is the name of this legendary worker?
The ballad about John Henry places his contest with a steam-powered drill at a railroad passage cut through rock near Talcott, West Virginia. By what name is that passage best known?
In Norse cosmology, this is the realm inhabited by humans and one of the nine worlds. Its name is often translated as “Middle Earth,” and it is connected to the gods’ realm by a rainbow bridge.
In Norse mythology, what is the rainbow-like bridge that connects Midgard, the human realm, with Asgard, the realm of the gods? It provides passage between these two worlds.

In Greek mythology, this nymph incurred Hera’s curse after distracting her with conversation during Zeus’s affairs, leaving her able only to repeat the last words spoken to her. She later fell in love with a beautiful youth who rejected her, until only her voice remained.
In the myth of Echo, this beautiful youth rejected her love and became transfixed by his own reflection in a pool. His name is also used for someone who is excessively self-admiring.
In Vedic and Hindu mythology, which deity rules the Devas and wields the thunderbolt known as the Vajra? He is also traditionally shown riding the white elephant Airavata.

Indra is praised more often than any other deity in which ancient Sanskrit collection of hymns, considered the oldest of the four Vedas? This text is a foundational source of Vedic ritual and religious tradition.
In Hopi ceremonial tradition, this carved figure represents a katsina spirit and is often given to children to help teach them about these beings. What is this figure called?
A kachina doll represents a katsina spirit in Hopi religious and ceremonial traditions. What kind of tree provides the wood traditionally used to carve these figures?

In traditional accounts of Israel's future, which awaited figure is expected to gather the diaspora back to Israel, restore its national life, rebuild the Temple, and reestablish the Sanhedrin? Historical claimants to this role have included Sabbatai Zevi and Simon bar Kokhba.

The Jewish Messiah is the subject of the twelfth item in the Thirteen Principles of Faith, and the traditional hymn “Ani Ma'amin” draws on that principle. Which medieval Jewish philosopher and legal scholar formulated those principles?

In Hindu practice, Antyesti is described as the “last sacrifice,” while Jewish mourners may tear a garment in keriah and Catholic observances may include a Requiem Mass. What broad kind of rite honors the dead and oversees the disposition of their remains?
In a Hindu funeral, this Sanskrit-named rite is often translated as “last sacrifice” and is regarded as the final samskara, or rite of passage. What is this rite?
In Arthurian legend, which enchantress gives Arthur a sword from the lake, later receives it back after his death, and helps carry him to Avalon?

In Arthurian legend, the Lady of the Lake gives Arthur a magical sword after the Sword in the Stone is broken. What is the name of the blade that is later returned to the water after Arthur’s final battle?
In Jewish mourning, a bereaved person may tear or cut a garment after the death of a close relative, making grief visible through damaged clothing. What is this mourning practice called?
Kriah is an outward sign of Jewish mourning; what is the name of the traditional seven-day mourning period after burial, when mourners commonly remain at home and receive visitors?
In Mexican Día de Muertos art, these skull and skeleton figures appear in satirical prints, painted decorations, and sugar offerings. What is the Spanish plural name for them?
Which Mexican printmaker created the etching *La Calavera Garbancera*, an elegant skeleton later popularized as La Catrina and frequently featured in calaveras imagery?
This queen of Sparta was approached by Zeus in the form of a swan and, in one common account, became the mother of Helen of Troy and Clytemnestra. Who was she?
In many accounts of Leda’s children, this daughter married Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, and later killed him after his return from the Trojan War. Who was she?

In Acts, a divine presence arrives among Jesus’ gathered disciples with a sound like a rushing wind and enables them to speak in languages they had not learned. Christian doctrine identifies this presence as the third person of the Trinity, distinct from the Father and the Son; what is it called?

In Acts, the Holy Spirit descends on Jesus’ disciples while people from many regions are gathered in Jerusalem, and the crowd hears them speaking in its own languages. Which Christian feast commemorates this event and is traditionally observed fifty days after Easter?

Its Five Suns creation story describes worlds destroyed and renewed, while a feathered serpent retrieves bones from Mictlan to create humanity. Which mythological tradition also recounts the rivalry between that deity and the god known as the Smoking Mirror?

In Aztec mythology, this deity’s epithet means “Smoking Mirror,” and he is associated with obsidian, night, and jaguars. He repeatedly opposes the feathered serpent in stories about the succession of the Suns; who is this god?

In Genesis’s Table of Nations, this ruler is identified as a son of Cush and credited with beginning a kingdom that included Babel, Erech, and Akkad in Shinar. The text also describes him as a mighty hunter before the Lord. Who is this ruler?

In Jewish and Islamic interpretive traditions, Nimrod’s conflict with this patriarch culminates in the ruler ordering him cast into a fire, from which he is miraculously saved. In the Quranic account of this figure’s reflections on the stars, moon, and sun, he rejects their worship and turns to the Creator. Who is this patriarch?

In the Odyssey, one famous animal of this kind recognizes Odysseus when he returns to Ithaca and dies soon afterward. Another, Laelaps, is fated to catch whatever it pursues, even when chasing the Teumessian Fox, which cannot be caught. What topic of ancient myth includes these figures?

In stories about Dogs in Greek mythology, Zeus resolves the chase between Laelaps, destined always to catch its prey, and the Teumessian Fox, destined never to be caught, by transforming the pair into what kind of celestial objects?
In Homer’s Odyssey, what nymph, traditionally described as a daughter of Helios, keeps Odysseus on an island for seven years before the gods compel his release?
In the Odyssey, Calypso keeps Odysseus for seven years on what island, where he remains until Hermes delivers Zeus’s order to let him go?

Her Roman associations included love, beauty, desire, fertility, prosperity, and victory; Roman tradition also made her the divine mother of Aeneas, linking her to Rome’s legendary ancestry. Which goddess was later regularly equated with the Greek Aphrodite?

Roman mythology names Venus as the mother of this Trojan refugee, who escaped the destruction of Troy and traveled to Italy. Virgil’s epic poem about his journey presents him as an ancestor of the Roman people. Who is this hero?

In 46 BCE, Julius Caesar dedicated a temple in his new Forum to Venus under a title emphasizing her role as divine mother and ancestress of the Julian family. What Latin cult title did the temple honor?
The Roman calendar placed this wine-related festival on August 19. It honored Jupiter and Venus and was associated with the vintage and the opening of the grape harvest. What was the festival called?

During Jesus’ visit to the home of two sisters, this woman sits at his feet and listens while her sister complains that she has been left to serve alone; elsewhere in John, she is identified as the sister of Martha and Lazarus. What is her name?
Mary of Bethany had a brother whose illness and death brought Jesus to Bethany. In John’s Gospel, Jesus calls him out of his tomb after he has been buried for four days; what was his name?
In the Hebrew Bible, this singular deity makes a covenant with Abraham and his descendants and tells Moses at the burning bush a name often rendered “I am who I am.” Which deity is described?
In Jewish reading practice, the four-letter Hebrew name of God is traditionally not spoken as written; readers commonly substitute Adonai. What Greek-derived term names this four-consonant form?

Which Sanskrit work within the Mahabharata presents a dialogue on dharma, knowledge, devotion, and action as a war is about to begin? Its central scene has a charioteer advising a warrior on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.
In the Bhagavad Gita, which divine charioteer counsels the troubled Pandava warrior before the Kurukshetra War and explains the paths of knowledge, devotion, and disciplined action?

In the Book of Exodus, Moses and Aaron confront Pharaoh with a sequence of divinely sent disasters intended to force him to release the Israelites from slavery. What is the traditional name for this sequence, which begins with the Nile turning to blood and concludes with the death of Egypt’s firstborn?
Among the Ten Plagues, which calamity left Egyptians unable to see one another for three days, while the Israelites had light in their dwellings?
The Gospels describe Jesus driving demons called Legion out of a possessed man. What is the name for a ritual or action intended to expel demons or evil spirits?
In the Gospel account of an exorcism by Jesus, a possessed man gives a collective name when Jesus asks what the spirits are called, explaining that many have entered him. What name does he give?
In Greek mythology, this creature had a human body and a bull’s head and was born to Pasiphaë after she mated with a bull. Theseus eventually slew it in Crete. What was this creature called?
In the Minotaur’s story, which daughter of King Minos gave Theseus a thread to help him find his way out of the maze after the fight?
The Minotaur was confined in a maze built at King Minos’s command. Which skilled craftsman designed that maze and later escaped Crete with his son using wings made of feathers and wax?
What elaborate maze, designed by Daedalus at King Minos’s command, held the Minotaur at its center?
Introduced in China in 1992, this modern spiritual movement combines meditation and slow exercises with moral teachings and the idea of a Dharma wheel. What is the movement called?
Falun Gong was introduced publicly in 1992 by this Chinese teacher, who later wrote *Zhuan Falun*, a central text of the movement. Who was he?

In Greek myth, this Ethiopian princess was the daughter of Cepheus and Cassiopeia, whose boast about surpassing the sea nymphs provoked Poseidon’s punishment. Chained to a rock as a sacrifice to a sea monster, she was freed by Perseus, who married her; name this princess.

In the myth of Andromeda, this Ethiopian queen’s boast that she surpassed the sea nymphs in beauty provoked Poseidon to send a flood and a sea monster against her kingdom. She was the mother of the princess chained as a sacrifice; who was this queen?

A Zoroastrian tradition enumerates 101 of these, while the Hebrew Bible’s four-consonant divine designation is commonly represented as YHWH. What general category of religious designation is being described?
Within the topic of Names of God, which deity is regarded as the supreme being in Zoroastrianism and is central to the Avesta? The name is often translated as “Wise Lord.”

This Indian religion teaches that spiritual purity is attained through disciplined ethics and ascetic practice. Its tradition is guided by 24 tirthankaras, with Mahavira regarded as the last; what is it called?
In Jainism, this renunciant is regarded as the 24th and final tirthankara and lived around the sixth or fifth century BCE. He was a contemporary of the Buddha; who was he?

Jainism’s five great vows include a commitment to avoid harming living beings, shaping practices such as vegetarianism and careful conduct toward even small creatures. What is the Sanskrit name of this ethical principle?

In Jainism, this doctrine holds that reality has many aspects and that no single viewpoint fully captures the truth. It encourages intellectual humility when considering complex questions; what is the doctrine called?
Jainism teaches that souls can escape karmic bondage and the cycle of rebirth by attaining this ultimate spiritual state. What is this liberation called?

In Norse mythology, these supernatural women choose warriors slain in battle and escort some of them to Odin’s hall. Their name is commonly translated as “choosers of the slain”; what are they called?
In Norse mythology, Valkyries bring warriors chosen from the battlefield to Odin’s great hall, where the fallen feast as they prepare for Ragnarök. What is this hall called?

In Buddhist traditions and other religious practices, people may repeatedly recite or chant this sacred syllable, word, or phrase as part of devotion or meditation. What is this kind of sacred expression called?
A widely recited Tibetan Buddhist mantra consists of six syllables and is especially associated with Avalokiteshvara, the bodhisattva of compassion. What is this sacred phrase?

In Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions, this process may involve successive births in different bodies, with karma shaping future circumstances in some accounts. Many followers seek liberation from the repeated cycle rather than treating it as an end in itself. What is this process called?

In Hindu accounts of reincarnation, this Sanskrit term for “action” or “deed” names the moral principle through which a person’s conduct can shape the circumstances of a later birth. What is the term?
Which Greek nymph fled Apollo after Eros’s arrow made the god fall in love with her? When she prayed to her father, he transformed her into a laurel tree.
In the myth of Daphne’s escape from Apollo, which river god was her father and transformed her into a laurel tree after she prayed to him?

Jacob’s blessing compares one of his sons to a wolf that devours prey in the morning and divides its spoil in the evening. This youngest son of Jacob and Rachel became the ancestor of one of the Tribes of Israel. Who was he?
A man from Benjamin’s tribe, the son of Kish, was chosen by the prophet Samuel and became the first king of Israel. What was his name?
A high-ranking priest in an African diasporic religion shakes this hand-held, bead-covered ritual object to make sound during ceremonies and engage with spirits. What is the object called?
The Ason is used by houngans and mambos, whose ritual work includes interacting with spirits known as lwa. In which religion is this beaded ceremonial rattle used?

This 13th-century Italian Dominican friar and Scholastic philosopher argued that faith and reason could both contribute to understanding truth, and he brought Aristotelian ideas into Christian theology. His unfinished theological writings helped shape Catholic thought for centuries; who was he?

Thomas Aquinas wrote commentaries on this ancient Greek philosopher’s works and incorporated ideas about causation and nature into medieval Christian scholarship. Medieval writers sometimes referred to this thinker simply as “the Philosopher”; who was he?

From 1265 to 1274, Thomas Aquinas composed this unfinished, question-and-article-organized work as a comprehensive guide to Catholic theology. Its opening section includes his Five Ways; what is the work called?

What raised Zoroastrian funerary structure receives bodies for exposure to scavenging birds rather than burial or cremation, reflecting concern that corpses could pollute sacred earth, water, and fire?
Which surviving Tower of Silence is a roofless circular adobe structure on a high hill beside the Amu Darya in present-day Uzbekistan?
Japan’s indigenous religious tradition has no single founder or central authority, and its practices center on kami, sacred places, shrines, and ritual purity. What is this religion’s natural name?
In Shinto, supernatural beings or sacred presences are believed to inhabit forces of nature, prominent landscapes, and other things. What is the Japanese term for these entities?
In Shinto, public worship sites are commonly staffed by priests who oversee offerings of food and drink to the enshrined kami. What Japanese term names these shrines?
Shinto’s early written traditions include a Japanese chronicle completed in 712 that recounts the origins of the islands and stories about kami such as Amaterasu. What is the title of this work?

For centuries, Shinto and Buddhism were often practiced together in Japan, with kami and Buddhist figures linked or interpreted in relation to one another. What is the Japanese term for this historical blending?

Within the faith whose scripture is the Quran, this subject concerns beings said to be created from light, and belief in them is commonly presented as the second of the six articles of faith. Jibril’s role in conveying the Quran to Muhammad is one of its central examples. What topic is this?
In Angels in Islam, Harut and Marut are mentioned in which Quranic chapter, often translated as “The Cow”? It is the Quran’s longest surah and also contains the Throne Verse.

It opens both the Hebrew Bible and the Christian Old Testament, and it is the first of the Torah’s five books. Its opening chapters recount creation, the Flood, and the scattering of peoples before turning to the stories of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. What is this book?
In Genesis, what name is given to the construction project whose builders sought to reach heaven, after which God confused their language and scattered them across the earth?

Which Roman deity was portrayed with two faces, allowing him to look in opposite directions, and presided over doors, gates, beginnings, and transitions? His association with both war and peace made him central to Roman ideas of passage between contrasting states.

A structure in Rome associated with Janus had doors that tradition held were left open during war and closed when the state was at peace. Which named sanctuary near the Forum was governed by this striking custom?

A native of Tarsus who first persecuted Jesus’ followers, this missionary underwent a vision and temporary blindness while traveling to Damascus before becoming a major missionary among non-Jewish communities. His letters to the Romans and Corinthians became central New Testament writings; who is he?

Addressed to Theophilus, this New Testament book follows the Gospel of Luke and recounts the early Christian community, including Stephen’s stoning and Saul’s conversion during his journey to Damascus. What book also narrates the missionary work of Paul the Apostle?

While Paul the Apostle was in Philippi, this seller of purple cloth listened to his preaching near a river and was baptized along with her household. She then persuaded the travelers to lodge at her home; who was she?
Which warrior queen ruled Connacht and launched an invasion of Ulster to obtain the Brown Bull of Cooley? She is a central figure in the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology.
In the Táin, Medb’s husband and co-ruler of Connacht owned the White-Horned Bull, whose worth became part of a comparison of their wealth. What is his name?
Observed beginning at sundown before Tishrei 1 and traditionally continuing through Tishrei 2, this Jewish New Year opens the High Holy Days and the Ten Days of Repentance. What is this observance?
During Rosh Hashanah synagogue services, a ram’s horn is sounded in blasts known as tekiah, shevarim, and teruah. What is this ritual instrument called?
This Vanir goddess is the daughter of Njörðr and sister of Freyr. She rules a field where she receives half of those who die in battle, while Odin receives the rest. What is her name?
Freyja receives half of the battle-slain in this heavenly field, while Odin receives the other half in Valhalla. What is the field called?
In stories about Freyja, this treasured gold necklace is associated with her, and Loki is said to have stolen it. What is the necklace called?
Freyja is credited with teaching this Norse magical practice to the Æsir. Associated with prophecy and influencing the future, it was also practiced by Odin. What is this form of magic called?
Which Greek hero, son of Zeus and Danaë, beheaded Medusa and later rescued Andromeda from the sea monster Cetus? His exploits also made him the ancestor of the Perseid dynasty.
In the Perseus myth, which king of Seriphos wanted to marry Danaë and sent her son to fetch a Gorgon’s head? His scheme was intended to get Perseus out of the way.
Perseus came upon this princess chained to a rock as an offering to Cetus after her mother boasted that she surpassed the Nereids in beauty. What was the princess’s name?

Perseus accidentally brought about the death foretold by an oracle when his discus struck this king during athletic games. This ruler of Argos was Danaë’s father and had tried to prevent the prophecy by locking her away.

During Perseus’s search for Medusa, which three sisters—born old and sharing one eye and one tooth—were forced to disclose the route to the nymphs who held his needed equipment? In some versions, he seized the eye while they passed it between themselves.

This American UFO-oriented religious movement was led by Marshall Applewhite and Bonnie Nettles, who used the names Do and Ti among followers. In 1997, 39 members died at a California residence, believing that death would let them join a spacecraft traveling behind a bright comet.
This bright celestial visitor appeared in the night sky in 1997 and was linked to Heaven's Gate's belief that a spacecraft was traveling behind it. What was its name?

This enchanted weapon is Odin’s named spear in Norse mythology and is famed for never missing its target. Snorri Sturluson’s Prose Edda credits the dwarves called Ívaldi’s Sons with forging it. What is the spear’s name?
In Snorri Sturluson’s Prose Edda, the dwarven craftsmen who made Gungnir also forged the ship Skíðblaðnir and Sif’s golden hair. What is this group called?

This legendary, large, hairy, ape-like humanoid is said to inhabit forests across North America, especially the Pacific Northwest. Its popular name refers to the enormous tracks attributed to it, and Sasquatch is an alternate name.

In stories and alleged sightings of Bigfoot, what is the name of the 1967 film shot near Bluff Creek, California, which appears to show a hairy figure walking through a clearing? The footage became the best-known motion-picture evidence claimed by enthusiasts.

Bigfoot enthusiasts who investigate animals whose existence is unverified are often associated with this pseudoscientific field. What is the term for that pursuit, whose name combines Greek roots meaning “hidden” and “animal”?

Odin cast this enormous sea serpent into the ocean surrounding Midgard, where it grew until it could circle the world and grasp its own tail. Norse prophecy says that when it releases its tail, Ragnarök begins. What is this serpent called?
At Ragnarök, Jörmungandr and this thunder god are fated to kill one another. The god wields Mjölnir and once used an ox’s head as bait while fishing for the serpent. Who is he?
Jörmungandr’s image of a serpent encircling the world while biting its own tail resembles this ancient circular motif. What is the name for a serpent or dragon depicted consuming its own tail?

In Irish mythology, Queen Medb’s campaign in the Táin Bó Cúailnge begins with a quest to seize Donn Cúailnge, while Heracles must capture Geryon’s herd in Greek myth. What kind of domesticated animals link these stories?

In the Irish epic about Queen Medb’s cattle raid from Connacht into Ulster, she seeks a famed bull from Cooley, and at the story’s end it fights Findbennach, the White-Horned Bull of Connacht. What is the name of the animal at the center of Medb’s raid?
Which Greek hero, the son of the sea nymph Thetis and King Peleus, is the foremost Greek warrior in the Trojan War? He kills Hector after the death of his companion Patroclus.

In this Homeric epic, Achilles withdraws from battle after Agamemnon takes Briseis, then returns to fight after Patroclus is killed. The story includes Achilles’ slaying of Hector and his return of Hector’s body to Priam.
Which companion of Achilles grew up alongside him and later entered battle wearing Achilles’ armor to rally the Greeks? Hector killed this warrior, prompting Achilles to return to combat.
What band of warriors from Phthia does Achilles command in the Trojan War? In Greek myth, the group’s name is commonly linked to the word for ants.

In Islam, this house of worship is arranged for communal prayer facing the qibla, the direction of Mecca. Its prayer hall commonly includes a mihrab marking that direction. What is this type of building?

After Ottoman forces captured Constantinople in 1453, this monumental former Byzantine cathedral was converted into a mosque. Its enormous central dome remains one of its most recognizable features. What is the building?

Unlike spontaneous supplication, this prescribed Islamic practice uses set recitations and bodily postures and is performed at five appointed times each day. What formal ritual practice is one of the Five Pillars of Islam?
A muezzin recites this Arabic announcement to mark the beginning of a scheduled daily Salat. It is distinct from the announcement made immediately before congregational prayer begins.

In Job 40, God describes this creature while challenging Job to recognize the limits of human power. It eats grass like an ox, rests among river reeds, and has a tail compared to a cedar. What is it called?
In later Jewish traditions, Behemoth is paired with a sea-dwelling monster in accounts of a future banquet for the righteous. What is the name of its aquatic counterpart?

This Chinese ethical, philosophical, and religious tradition emphasizes filial piety, ritual propriety, learning, and the cultivation of virtue in order to foster harmonious relationships. It is associated with an ancient teacher whose conversations with disciples became a foundational classic. What is this tradition called?

Sun Myung Moon, founder of the Unification Church, reportedly drew on Confucianism after reading this classic in childhood. The work preserves sayings and conversations associated with Confucius and became a foundational text of the tradition. What is the work?

This monotheistic Abrahamic religious and cultural tradition is associated with the Jewish people and is understood by its adherents as a way of observing a covenant with God. Its central scriptural collection is divided into the Torah, Nevi’im, and Ketuvim. What is this tradition?
In Judaism, what is the name of the central scriptural collection also known as the Hebrew Bible, whose three divisions are the Torah, Nevi’im, and Ketuvim?
In Judaism, what term names the body of Jewish law and is commonly translated as “the Way”?

This Greek god presided over wine, festivity, theater, and ecstatic ritual, and his followers included maenads and satyrs. Traditions called him twice-born after Zeus carried him to term following his mortal mother’s death.

In Aristophanes’ comedy, Dionysus travels to the underworld with his servant Xanthias to bring back a tragedian. The play’s climax features a contest between two dead playwrights, and Dionysus must choose which one should return to the living.

In the Theban birth story, Dionysus’ mortal mother was persuaded by Hera to ask Zeus to reveal himself in his full divine splendor. The sight killed her, and Zeus carried their unborn child in his thigh until he was ready to be born.
Dionysus’ followers carried this distinctive staff, traditionally made from a fennel stalk and associated with ivy and a pinecone. It could signify both blessing and destructive power.
In the Hebrew Bible, this sacred chest held the stone tablets and served as a sign of God's presence among the Israelites. What object accompanied them during their wilderness journey?

In the Exodus account associated with the Ark of the Covenant, Moses shattered the first stone tablets after finding the Israelites worshipping a golden calf, then received a replacement set. What set of laws did the tablets bear, including prohibitions on idolatry and murder?
In Aboriginal Australian traditions, what legendary creature is said to inhabit billabongs and other waterways, where it may devour unsuspecting people?

Unlike the Bunyip, this figure is associated with rainfall in Aboriginal Australian Dreamtime stories. What ancestral being is said in many traditions to have shaped rivers and waterholes as it moved across the land?

In Hesiod’s *Theogony*, a bronze anvil takes nine days to fall from this mountain to Earth. Bellerophon also tries to reach it astride Pegasus but falls after Zeus sends a gadfly to startle the winged horse; what is this divine home of the Olympian gods?
The ruler of Mount Olympus overthrew his father Cronus and became king of the gods, wielding the thunderbolt as his signature weapon. Who is he?

This contemplative practice trains attention and awareness, using either a chosen focus such as the breath or a mantra, or open observation of present experience. It has major roles in Buddhist and Hindu traditions and is also practiced in secular health settings. What is this practice?
The earliest recorded examples of dhyāna, a term associated with meditation, appear in these ancient Indian philosophical texts that form part of the Vedic tradition. What are these texts?

In Buddhist meditation, this practice cultivates insight by observing bodily sensations, feelings, and mental states in the present moment. It is associated with the Satipatthana Sutta and is often contrasted with samatha, which emphasizes tranquility. What is this form of meditation?

In the Bhagavad Gita, this Hindu deity serves as the charioteer and spiritual teacher of a hesitant Pandava prince, then reveals his divine form. Traditionally regarded as an avatar of Vishnu, which deity is this?
In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna counsels this third Pandava prince when he hesitates to fight his relatives on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. Which archer receives that instruction?
Which Jewish scripture comprises Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy? Traditionally copied onto a scroll and read during synagogue services, it is known as the Five Books of Moses.
What Hebrew-named pointer, often shaped like a hand, lets a reader follow the text of a Torah scroll without touching its parchment?
In many Hindu traditions, cattle are venerated, and their slaughter is taboo in numerous parts of India. What familiar term describes the revered bovine symbol at the heart of this belief?
The Sacred Cow tradition reflects Hindu reverence for cattle. In depictions of Shiva, what is the name of the white bull he rides?

In Hindu tradition, this goddess is associated with wealth, prosperity, good fortune, beauty, and fertility, and is widely revered as the consort of Vishnu. Artistic depictions often show her with a lotus, a symbol connected with abundance and life-giving waters. What is her name?
Lakshmi is commonly described as the consort of this Hindu deity, who is associated with preservation and is one of the Trimurti alongside Brahma and Shiva. Which deity is it?

In the Synoptic Gospels, Jesus shares this meal with the Twelve before his arrest and crucifixion. Christians commemorate it in the Eucharist, and Leonardo da Vinci’s famous mural depicts it; what is the event called?

The Last Supper is the subject of a 1490s mural created for the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, known for its experimental perspective and deteriorating paint. Which Renaissance artist created the work?
In Abrahamic traditions, what supernatural beings serve as intermediaries between God and humanity, acting as messengers, attendants, protectors, or guides?
Among Angels named in Abrahamic scripture, which one tells Mary in the Christian account of the Annunciation that she will bear Jesus?
In traditions about Angels, which named archangel leads the heavenly forces against the dragon in the Book of Revelation?
In some Abrahamic accounts of Angels, what high-ranking order does Isaiah describe as having six wings and calling “Holy, holy, holy” around God’s throne?
In teachings about Angels, what term names the personal heavenly protectors believed to watch over and guide individual people?
In Islamic tradition, Hajar searched for water in the barren valley of Mecca for her infant son, Isma'il. What sacred source of water is associated with her search and is visited by Muslim pilgrims?
The Zamzam Well is tied to a Hajj rite in which pilgrims travel seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah, recalling Hajar’s search for water. What is this rite called?

In a mosque’s congregational prayer, this person leads worshippers through the prescribed movements and recitations. The Arabic title means “leader” and, in this setting, does not by itself mean one of the divinely appointed figures in Twelver Shi'a belief. What is the title?

In Twelver Shi'a Islam, the line of twelve Imams begins with this cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, regarded as his first divinely appointed successor. He is also recognized in Sunni history as the fourth Rashidun caliph. Who is he?

In church worship and art, this emblem refers to the instrument on which believers hold that Jesus was crucified, and it is associated with sacrifice, salvation, and hope of life beyond death. In its plain form, it has no figure of Jesus. What is this symbol?

In Christian devotional art, the Christian cross sometimes bears an image of Jesus rather than remaining figureless. What is the established name for this form, commonly contrasted with a plain cross?

This major ethnic group is concentrated in southwestern Nigeria and neighboring parts of West Africa. Its traditional religious practices center on divinities called orishas and helped shape Candomblé and other African diasporic religions. Which people are described?

In the traditional religion of the Yoruba people, these divine beings are honored through rituals and offerings, and many are associated with aspects of nature or human life. They are also central figures in Candomblé. What are these beings collectively called?
In Jain cosmology, an eternal cycle is divided into an ascending utsarpini and a descending avasarpini. What does this cycle measure?
Within Time in Jainism, the current avasarpini is traditionally said to have begun three years after the death of which 24th tirthankara? He is revered as a central teacher of the Jain tradition.
In Zen Buddhist training, what is the name for a brief paradoxical question, statement, or exchange intended to unsettle ordinary reasoning and prompt insight through meditation?
Koans are practiced in Zen, a tradition belonging to which broad Buddhist branch often translated as the “Great Vehicle” and contrasted with Theravada?

At the Last Supper, Jesus foretold that one of the Twelve would hand him over. The disciple later identified Jesus to the arresting party with a kiss after agreeing to a payment from the chief priests; what apostle was he?
In the Gospel narrative, Judas Iscariot accepts payment from the chief priests in return for delivering Jesus to them. What numbered quantity of coins does Matthew name as the payment?
In Norse mythology, this one-eyed chief of the Æsir is the husband of Frigg and father of Thor and Baldr. He is associated with wisdom, war, poetry, magic, and the dead. Who is he?
Odin gave up one of his eyes to drink from the well associated with this wise figure, whose severed head later counseled the chief god. Name that figure.
To gain knowledge of the runes, Odin hung himself for nine nights, wounded by his own spear, from this immense tree that links the worlds. What is this world tree called?
Odin’s famed spear was crafted by dwarves and is said never to miss its mark when thrown. What is the name of this weapon?
At Ragnarök, Odin leads the slain warriors of Valhalla into battle but is swallowed and killed by this monstrous wolf, later avenged by Odin’s son Vidar. Name the wolf.

A legendary aquatic creature is said to inhabit a large lake in the Scottish Highlands, and modern depictions often show it lifting a long neck above the water. Reports and a celebrated photograph helped bring it worldwide attention in the 1930s; what creature is it?
The Loch Ness Monster’s best-known 1934 photograph was later exposed as a staged hoax rather than evidence of an animal. What model craft, disguised with putty, was used to create the image?

Which Hindu spring festival is celebrated with bonfires, communal gatherings, and playful showers of brightly colored powder and water? Its festivities are associated with the triumph of good over evil.
In the legend associated with Holi’s bonfire ritual, this young devotee of Vishnu was cast into a fire alongside his aunt, who perished while he emerged unharmed. What was his name?

Which collective name refers to the Indigenous communities of the continent south of Indonesia and its southern island of Tasmania, whose diverse cultures and traditions predate European colonization? Their spiritual traditions include songlines and stories of the Rainbow Serpent.

Which British naval captain charted Australia's east coast during his 1770 voyage aboard the Endeavour and claimed it for Britain? His arrival became a pivotal event in the colonial history of Aboriginal peoples of Australia.
This late seventh-century Umayyad shrine stands on Jerusalem’s Temple Mount and is distinguished by its octagonal structure and richly decorated exterior. What is the shrine called?
At the center of the Dome of the Rock is a sacred rock associated in Islamic tradition with Muhammad’s ascent during the Night Journey. What is this rock commonly called?

In the Kojiki’s account of Japan’s origins, this primordial goddess joins her brother-husband in creating the islands of Japan. She dies after giving birth to the fire deity Kagutsuchi, prompting her husband to pursue her into the realm of the dead. Who is she?

After Izanami dies in childbirth, her husband enters this shadowy realm to bring her back, but she has already eaten food cooked there and cannot return to the world of the living. What is the Japanese land of the dead called?
In Greek mythology, what is the name of the food of the gods, often associated with immortality and distinguished from the divine drink called nectar?
In traditions that describe ambrosia as the gods’ food, what is the name of the divine fluid said to flow through their veins instead of mortal blood?
What traditional Catholic prayer begins with a greeting drawn from Luke’s account of the Annunciation and ends by asking for intercession at the hour of death?

The Hail Mary incorporates the greeting delivered to Mary in Luke’s account of the Annunciation, where a heavenly messenger announces that she will conceive Jesus. What is the traditional name of that archangel?

Founded by a circle of university companions in Paris in the 1530s, this Catholic order was formally recognized by Pope Paul III in 1540 and became known for its schools and overseas missions. What is the order’s natural name?

The Society of Jesus was formally approved by Pope Paul III in 1540 after a group of companions proposed a new apostolic order. Which former Spanish soldier, injured during the 1521 defense of Pamplona and later author of the Spiritual Exercises, was its central founder?

The Hebrew Bible places this foundational covenant code at Mount Sinai after the Israelites’ exodus from Egypt, then gives a version with some differences in Deuteronomy 5. Its rules include prohibitions on murder, adultery, theft, and bearing false witness; what is this code commonly called?

In Exodus 32, Moses descends from the mountain with the first stone tablets associated with the Ten Commandments and sees the Israelites worshiping this cast-metal image. He smashes the tablets in response; what object had the people made from their jewelry?
In the Fenian Cycle, this legendary Irish warrior leads the Fianna and gains supernatural wisdom after burning his thumb while cooking a captured salmon. What is his traditional Irish name?
Fionn mac Cumhaill’s son is a warrior-poet of the Fianna and narrates the tale of Diarmuid and Gráinne. In another famous story, he journeys with Niamh to Tír na nÓg; what is his name?

This fourth canonical New Testament account opens with a prologue about the Word’s existence before creation and its relation to God. It presents Jesus’s ministry through a distinctive sequence of seven signs, culminating in the raising of Lazarus; what is the book’s natural title?

In the Gospel of John, which Greek term names the Word described as being with God in the beginning and becoming flesh? The term also had associations with reason and ordering principle in Greek thought.

In the Gospel of John, which disciple says he will not believe the resurrection report unless he can see the nail marks and place his hand in Jesus’s side? When Jesus appears, this disciple addresses him as “My Lord and my God.”
In the Gospel of John, what Galilean village hosts a wedding where Jesus turns water in stone jars into wine, the first of the book’s signs? The same village is identified as Nathanael’s hometown.

In Islamic scholarship, what is the collective name for reports preserving the Prophet Muhammad’s sayings, actions, and approvals, which serve alongside the Quran as a source for understanding religious practice?
Which ninth-century Sunni compilation of Hadith was assembled by Muhammad ibn Ismail and is often regarded as the most authoritative collection in Sunni Islam?

In an alkene’s C=C unit, the component beyond the end-to-end overlap is formed by side-by-side overlap of parallel p orbitals, with electron density above and below the axis joining the carbon atoms. What is this type of covalent interaction called?

A Pi bond does not provide the direct overlap along the line joining two nuclei that forms the other component of an ordinary double bond. What is the bond type formed by this head-on orbital overlap?

This broad class of vehicles travels through Earth's atmosphere using propulsion and aerodynamic lift or other aerodynamic surfaces. Fixed-wing and rotary-wing machines are both examples; what is this class called?
Among early aircraft, this powered biplane made the first successful sustained, controlled flight by a heavier-than-air machine at Kitty Hawk in 1903. What was this machine called?

More than 100 diseases fall under this name: cells acquire genetic changes and proliferate without normal control, and malignant forms can invade nearby tissues or spread to distant organs. Unlike benign growths, they can metastasize; what is this group of diseases called?

In cancer, this process occurs when cells from a primary tumor travel through blood or lymph and establish secondary tumors in distant organs. It is one reason a cancer’s stage and prognosis depend on how far the disease has spread; what is this process called?

When cancer is suspected, imaging can locate an abnormal mass, but this diagnostic procedure removes a tissue sample so pathologists can examine cells under a microscope and determine whether it is malignant. What is the procedure called?
Persistent infection with high-risk types 16 and 18 of this virus is responsible for most cervical cancers, and vaccination against it can prevent many of those cases. What virus is it?

A cervical cancer sample collected at Johns Hopkins in 1951 without the patient’s knowledge or consent led to an immortal cell line used widely in research. Which African American woman was the source of those cells?

In this heat-machine category, a fuel-air mixture burns inside the working chamber, and expanding gases produce mechanical work through pistons or a rotor. What broad category powers most gasoline and diesel cars?

One rotary design of an internal combustion engine replaces reciprocating pistons with a roughly triangular rotor whose tips trace a curved housing, creating moving chambers for intake, compression, power, and exhaust. What design is associated with Mazda’s RX-7 and RX-8?

These compounds contain carbon, chlorine, and fluorine, and were widely used as refrigerants, aerosol propellants, and solvents before international controls phased them out. What is this family of chemicals?

Chlorofluorocarbons can release chlorine radicals that catalytically destroy a protective stratospheric gas made of three oxygen atoms. Depletion of this gas is especially severe over Antarctica each spring; what is it?

When a book rests on a table, the table exerts a contact push that keeps the objects from passing through each other. The push is at a right angle to the shared surface, and on a ramp it points away from the ramp rather than straight upward. What is this perpendicular contact effect called?

When two surfaces slide past one another, the standard introductory model calculates the resisting interaction by multiplying a dimensionless coefficient by the magnitude of the normal force. The interaction acts parallel to the contact surface and opposes the sliding; what is it called?

A cervical-tumor biopsy taken at Johns Hopkins Hospital in 1951 produced this human cancer culture, which continued multiplying in laboratory conditions when many earlier human tissue samples quickly died. Its name uses the first two letters of its donor’s first and last names; what widely used research culture is it?

The HeLa cell line originated from a cervical-tumor biopsy taken while this 31-year-old patient was receiving treatment in Baltimore in 1951; the cells were collected without her knowledge or consent. What was the patient’s name?

In the mitochondrial matrix, this cyclic pathway oxidizes acetyl-CoA through a sequence of enzyme-catalyzed reactions and regenerates oxaloacetate at the end. It produces NADH and FADH₂, which carry electrons toward ATP production; what is this pathway called?

At the entry step of the Citric Acid Cycle, this enzyme joins the acetyl group carried by coenzyme A to four-carbon oxaloacetate, yielding a six-carbon intermediate and releasing coenzyme A. What enzyme catalyzes this reaction?

An American physician and immunologist, he directed the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases from 1984 to 2022. He also advised U.S. presidents on public health and became a prominent figure during the COVID-19 response. Who is he?
In 2008, Anthony Fauci received the Presidential Medal of Freedom for his contributions to public health. Which U.S. president presented him with the award?

This extensive membrane network is continuous with the nuclear envelope, while its interior forms a compartment separate from the cytosol. One region looks granular because ribosomes attach to it, while another lacks those ribosomes; what organelle is this?
After leaving the endoplasmic reticulum in transport vesicles, many newly processed proteins arrive at this organelle for further modification and sorting. What is this organelle?

For a point mass, this quantity is the mass multiplied by the square of its perpendicular distance from a rotation axis. It is the rotational counterpart of mass and relates applied torque to angular acceleration.
For a rigid body's moment of inertia, shifting the rotation line a distance d from one through its center of mass changes the value by adding Md². What theorem gives this correction?
For a given object, the axis through this point has the smallest moment of inertia among parallel axes. In a uniform gravitational field, this point is also where the object can be balanced.
On many leaves, a thin hydrophobic covering lies outside the epidermal cells and helps limit water loss to the air. What is this surface barrier called?

The plant cuticle slows water loss across much of a leaf’s surface, but plants also regulate gas exchange through microscopic openings in the epidermis. What are these pores called, each controlled by a pair of guard cells?

This is Neptune’s largest natural satellite, and its orbit carries it around the planet opposite Neptune’s rotation. During Voyager 2’s 1989 flyby, it was found to have active geysers and distinctive, irregularly patterned cantaloupe terrain. What is this moon?
Triton was discovered on October 10, 1846, just 17 days after Neptune itself was discovered. Which British astronomer made the observation?

Newton’s first law says that an object at rest remains at rest and a moving object continues in a straight line at constant speed unless a net external force acts. What is the name for matter’s tendency to resist changes in its motion?

Inertia increases with this quantity, which is measured in kilograms and remains the same whether an object is on Earth or the Moon. Unlike weight, it does not depend on local gravity; what physical quantity measures an object’s resistance to acceleration?

This phylum consists of typically unsegmented animals with a complete tubular gut, and its members occur in soil, freshwater, and marine habitats. It includes the laboratory organism commonly abbreviated C. elegans. What is the phylum’s natural scientific name?
One widely used genetic and developmental model within Nematoda is a transparent, free-living soil species whose adult hermaphrodite has 959 somatic cells. What is its binomial name?
Nematoda belongs to this animal clade, whose name alludes to the molting of its members and which also contains arthropods and tardigrades. What is the clade called?
A Pittsburgh-based medical researcher led a field trial involving nearly two million children, and in 1955 his vaccine against poliomyelitis was declared safe and effective. Who was this researcher?

Jonas Salk’s injectable preparation used virus particles treated with formalin so they could not replicate, unlike later oral preparations made with weakened live virus. What type of immunizing preparation did he develop?
This group is defined by having its first carbon–carbon double bond three atoms from the terminal methyl end of a molecule’s carbon chain. EPA and DHA belong to it. What is the group called?
Among omega-3 fatty acids, which 22-carbon molecule has six double bonds and is an important component of membranes in the brain and retina?

These biological preparations expose the immune system to weakened or killed microbes, toxins, or selected pathogen proteins so it can mount a protective response during later encounters. Their widespread use helped eradicate smallpox worldwide and sharply reduce diseases such as polio, measles, and tetanus. What are these preparations?

In the history of vaccines, this English physician described how cowpox could protect against smallpox and tested that idea in 1796. His pioneering work produced the first vaccine, and the word “vaccine” derives from a term meaning cowpox. Who was he?

The science of developing and producing vaccines has a specific name. It refers to the field of research and manufacture, not to vaccination, the act of administering a vaccine. What is this field called?

In quantitative laboratory analysis, a measured volume of a prepared solution is added to a sample until a reaction endpoint is reached. What is this method for determining the sample’s concentration called?

In a titration, what is the name of the solution with a known concentration that is added to react with the sample? Its measured volume is used to calculate the concentration of the substance being analyzed.
In a titration, what term refers to the substance in the sample whose concentration is being determined? It is distinguished from the standard solution added during the analysis.
During a titration, what calibrated glass instrument uses a stopcock to dispense measured volumes of liquid, often drop by drop? It is commonly mounted vertically above the sample being analyzed.
In electrostatics, what is the name of the type of charge whose field lines conventionally point outward and that attracts negative charge?
Which 18th-century American experimenter proposed a one-fluid theory of electricity and helped establish the positive/negative terminology used to describe positive electric charge?

In the tissues of trees, grasses, and flowering herbs, this rigid extracellular layer lies outside each plasma membrane and helps resist internal turgor pressure. It is composed mainly of cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin. What is it?
