A major structural polymer in the plant cell wall consists of long chains of glucose assembled into fibers that provide strength. It is the characteristic wall polysaccharide of plants, in contrast to chitin in fungi. What is this polymer?

This thick, mostly solid, silicate-rich layer lies beneath the planet’s crust and above its core, extending roughly 2,900 kilometers to the core boundary. Its rock deforms and creeps slowly, transferring heat that helps drive plate motion. What is this layer called?
At the top of Earth’s mantle, this seismic boundary separates the crust from the underlying mantle and is recognized by a change in seismic-wave speeds. What is this boundary commonly called?

For a converging lens, this distance runs from the lens’s principal plane to the point where incoming rays parallel to the optical axis meet. For a diverging lens, it is measured to the point from which those rays appear to spread. What is this optical quantity called?

In geometrical optics, a lens’s optical power is the reciprocal of its focal length when the length is expressed in meters. What unit, equal to one inverse meter and commonly used to state the strength of eyeglasses, measures that power?

Chemists commonly define this measure as half the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded or adjacent atoms. It generally increases down a group and decreases from left to right across a period; what is this measure called?

In discussions of atomic radius, what effect describes the progressive shrinkage in the sizes of elements as protons are added across a stretch of the periodic table where 4f orbitals are being filled? The added 4f electrons shield the increasing nuclear charge poorly.

These preventive products were developed to protect against illness caused by SARS-CoV-2, and CDC recommendations extend to people as young as six months. New York nurse Sandra Lindsay was the first American to receive one, an event later recognized with the Presidential Medal of Freedom. What are these products?

As COVID-19 vaccines were being deployed, public health agencies tracked a coronavirus variant first detected in Botswana in 2021. Its BA.5 sublineage later became the dominant strain in the United States, and the variant spread more readily than Delta. What was this variant?

In analyzing the motion of tiny oil droplets in Millikan and Fletcher’s experiment, researchers needed a rule for the viscous drag on a slowly moving sphere. Which law gives that drag in terms of the fluid’s viscosity, the sphere’s radius, and its speed?

In a 1909 experiment, researchers suspended tiny charged droplets between plates and adjusted the electric field to balance each droplet’s weight; their motion calculations used Stokes’ law. What experiment determined the electron’s charge?

This short-period icy body follows a highly elongated orbit and typically returns to visibility from Earth every 75–76 years. After linking observations from 1531, 1607, and 1682, an English astronomer correctly predicted its return in 1758; what is its common name?

During its 1986 encounter with Halley’s Comet, this European Space Agency spacecraft captured the first close-up images of a comet nucleus. Its observations revealed the nucleus’s shape and active jets; what was the spacecraft called?

Marie Curie’s research on radioactivity and Rosalind Franklin’s X-ray diffraction studies are examples of work in this profession. What are professionals called when they systematically observe, experiment, and analyze to investigate the natural world?
Scientists have included this Polish-born physicist and chemist, who shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics and won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for her work on radioactivity. Who was she?

Born in Pretoria, this entrepreneur became known for ventures spanning electric vehicles and private spaceflight, founding a rocket company and leading a major electric-car maker. In 2022, he completed the acquisition of Twitter, which was later renamed X.
Developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, this three-core launch vehicle made its first flight in February 2018 carrying a Tesla Roadster and a mannequin nicknamed Starman. What rocket was it?
What pale-blue, pungent-smelling gas is a less-stable triatomic allotrope of oxygen, produced when ultraviolet light or electrical discharges act on ordinary molecular oxygen?
In discussions of ozone, what stratospheric region has an especially high concentration of this gas and absorbs most incoming solar ultraviolet radiation, helping shield life at Earth’s surface?
Ozone columns are often quantified using what measure, equal to the amount of ozone that would form a 0.01-millimeter layer at standard temperature and pressure?
What 1987 international agreement phased out chlorofluorocarbons after evidence that these compounds catalyzed stratospheric ozone depletion, including the Antarctic springtime thinning?
What term names a substantial loss or complete absence of hearing? It can affect communication and access to spoken language.

In the context of Deafness, which Washington, D.C., school has a Daniel Chester French memorial depicting a seated instructor teaching Alice Cogswell, and was founded in 1864 as the first college for deaf students?
What seafloor openings release heated, mineral-rich water and sustain ecosystems powered by chemical energy rather than sunlight?
At hydrothermal vents, which iconic invertebrates live in long pale casings, have red plumes, and rely on chemosynthetic bacteria instead of a functional digestive tract as adults?

This naturally occurring volcanic material is glassy rather than crystalline because lava cools so quickly that crystals have little or no time to form. Often dark and capable of breaking into exceptionally sharp edges, what is this rock called?

Obsidian is brittle and can break along curved, shell-like surfaces rather than along mineral cleavage planes. What is the name of this characteristic breakage pattern, also found in flint and other glassy materials?

These contagious respiratory pathogens belong to the Orthomyxoviridae family and carry segmented, single-stranded RNA genomes. Types A and B cause seasonal epidemics in people, while type A is also known to cause pandemics; what group of pathogens is described?
Influenza viruses are classified into subtypes using the H and N versions of two surface proteins. Which protein, represented by H, binds to host-cell receptors and helps the virus attach to a cell?

Created by legislation signed by President Dwight D. Eisenhower on July 29, 1958, this U.S. civilian agency began operating that October after the Soviet Union’s Sputnik launch. It took over much of an earlier federal committee’s aviation research and runs crewed and robotic missions beyond Earth; what is the agency’s name?

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration launched this infrared observatory aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana on December 25, 2021; it began releasing its first full-color science images the following July. Located near the Sun–Earth L2 point, what mission uses a segmented 6.5-meter primary mirror to study the early universe and exoplanet atmospheres?

In programming, these classifications determine what kinds of values a variable can hold and which operations are valid for those values. Compilers and runtimes can use them to check whether assignments and computations are appropriate.
Among common data types, this one represents a logical condition rather than a number or a sequence of characters. In many programming languages, its two values are written as `true` and `false`.

What term describes light produced by living organisms through internal chemical reactions, rather than reflected from an external source? In some deep-sea animals, symbiotic microorganisms help generate this glow.
In discussions of bioluminescence, which deep-sea predator is known for a modified dorsal-fin ray that forms a lure, sometimes lit by symbiotic bacteria to attract prey?
NASA places this hue near 700 nanometers, at the long-wavelength edge of the visible spectrum. In additive display systems, it is a primary light that combines with green light to appear yellow.
Red is a family of hues rather than one fixed pigment. What named pigment can be made from the mineral cinnabar or produced synthetically?
What kind of one-way algorithm maps data of any length to a fixed-size digest? It is designed to make both recovering the original input and finding two inputs with the same digest difficult.

A cryptographic hash function designed by Ron Rivest in 1992 produces a 128-bit digest and was once widely used for checksums and password storage. Practical collision attacks have made this algorithm unsuitable for security-sensitive use; what is its name?

In a narrow glass tube, water often rises at the walls and dips at the center because attraction to the glass outweighs cohesion within the liquid; mercury forms the opposite curve. In laboratory glassware, the volume is conventionally read at eye level from the bottom of this curved surface. What is this feature called?

When a technician reads a graduated cylinder, the meniscus should be viewed with the eye level aligned horizontally to its bottom; looking from above or below shifts the apparent level relative to the scale. What is this viewing-related measurement effect called?

Which corrosive nitrogen-containing compound is produced industrially by oxidizing ammonia in the Ostwald process, often over a platinum-rhodium catalyst? It is also a major reagent in fertilizer and explosives manufacture.
When nitric acid is mixed with hydrochloric acid, the resulting corrosive mixture can dissolve gold, a metal resistant to either acid alone. What is this mixture called?

This evergreen conifer is native to the mountains of the eastern Mediterranean and develops a broad, tiered crown as it matures. It is depicted at the center of the flag of the country whose capital is Beirut. What tree species is it?
The Lebanon cedar belongs to the same genus as the deodar cedar and the Atlas cedar. What is the genus that includes these three conifers?

This aromatic hydrocarbon has the molecular formula C₆H₆, with six carbon atoms arranged in a planar hexagon and one hydrogen attached to each carbon. Its delocalized π-electron system makes it the simplest aromatic hydrocarbon. What is it?

Benzene has six π electrons in a planar, cyclic, conjugated ring, meeting a condition often written as 4n+2 when n=1. What named rule predicts aromatic stabilization for rings with this electron count?

The six-membered ring structure of benzene is commonly associated with this 19th-century German chemist. A famous anecdote says that a vision of a snake seizing its own tail helped inspire his ring-shaped model. Who was he?
In compressible-flow calculations, this dimensionless ratio is found by dividing an object's speed by the local speed of sound. What is it called?

In discussions of Mach number, an aircraft traveling faster than the local speed of sound produces shock waves that can arrive at an observer as a sudden, sharp report. What is this audible phenomenon called?
What property is ranked by testing whether one substance can scratch another? On the Mohs scale, talc is at 1 and diamond is at 10.
In the context of mineral hardness, which hydrated magnesium silicate sits at the bottom of the Mohs scale, with a value of 1? Its soft, white form is ground into baby powder.
What natural structural material, found chiefly in the stems and branches of trees and other woody plants, is rich in cellulose and lignin and widely used in construction?
In wood, what complex polymer in plant cell walls helps bind structural fibers and gives the material rigidity? It is the other major component commonly named alongside cellulose.

Astronomers place this kind of observatory beyond Earth’s atmosphere to avoid atmospheric turbulence and absorption when collecting images of celestial objects. What is this instrument category called?
Which space telescope, launched in December 2021 to observe primarily in infrared, released its first science images in July 2022, including a deep-field view of SMACS 0723?
In physics, this quantity is used to order events, compare intervals, and measure rates of change. Relativity treats it as one dimension alongside the three dimensions of space.
For measuring time, the SI base unit is defined by fixing the frequency of the cesium-133 hyperfine transition at exactly 9,192,631,770 hertz. What unit is this?

In special relativity, comparing measurements of elapsed time and length for an object moving at constant speed uses a dimensionless multiplier denoted by γ. The multiplier grows as the object's speed approaches the speed of light; what is it called?

In quantum electrodynamics, this American physicist developed diagrams of particle interactions in which antiparticles can be interpreted as moving backward along the time axis. Which Caltech theorist is associated with these diagrams?

For civil tracking of time, this system of dating was promulgated under Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 and revised the Julian leap-year rule: century years are omitted unless divisible by 400. What system is it?
In an ionic crystal, a vacant anion site can trap an electron, forming a point defect that often gives the crystal color. What is this defect called?
In alkali-halide crystals, an F-center consists of an electron trapped at an anion vacancy. What is the conventional name for the defect when a second electron occupies that same vacancy?

Which application-layer standard defines how web clients and servers exchange requests and responses to transfer resources? Browsers commonly rely on it to retrieve pages and other content from servers.
In HTTP, which request method asks a server to return a representation of a resource and is defined as safe and idempotent?

Formed from buried organic remains under heat and pressure over geologic time, this underground fossil fuel consists mostly of CH₄ and is burned for building heat, electricity generation, and industrial processes. Because it is odorless before treatment, distributors commonly add a sulfur-based odorant to help people detect leaks. What fuel is this?
Natural gas is a mixture, but which molecule, with the formula CH₄, usually makes up its largest share? It has one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms and is the simplest alkane.

This butterfly-shaped endocrine organ lies at the front of the neck and releases T3 and T4, hormones that help regulate the body’s energy use. It also contains parafollicular cells that secrete calcitonin. What is this organ?
The thyroid gland’s parafollicular cells secrete this hormone, which helps lower blood calcium and opposes the action of parathyroid hormone. What is this hormone?
In a program, this named entity lets code refer to data used in calculations and instructions; assigning a new value can replace one stored earlier. What programming construct is this?

In JavaScript, a variable declared with `let` or `const` is accessible only within the enclosing pair of braces where it is declared, unlike a `var` declaration's function-level behavior. What is this restriction on where the variable's identifier can be used called?
These large, hoofed mammals were domesticated to carry people and goods across arid regions. The group includes a one-humped species and a two-humped species; what animal is this?
Among camels, which domesticated species has two humps and a thick coat that helps it withstand Central Asia’s frigid winters and hot summers?

This typically single, long neuronal process carries electrical impulses away from the cell body toward other neurons, muscles, or glands. Unlike dendrites, it transmits signals outward from the soma. What is it?
Along a myelinated axon, what are the regularly spaced gaps in the insulating sheath where ion channels cluster and the electrical signal is renewed during saltatory conduction?
A physicist imagined an agent controlling a tiny door between two chambers of gas, letting faster molecules pass one way and slower molecules the other. What is this thought experiment called?
Maxwell's demon was first described by its originator as a “finite being” that sorts molecules. Which 19th-century physicist later gave the agent its familiar supernatural name?

Maxwell's demon helped inspire questions about the relationship between information and thermodynamics. What principle, named for a German-American physicist, sets a minimum heat cost for erasing information?

This bacterial sexually transmitted infection can begin with a painless sore, progress to a rash that may affect the palms or soles, and later cause serious damage to the heart or nervous system if untreated. What is this curable infection?
In Syphilis, the primary-stage lesion is often a firm, painless ulcer at the site where the infection entered the body, and it may heal without treatment. What is this characteristic sore called?

This nonmetal is the lightest member of group 15 and makes up about 78% of Earth’s atmosphere; at standard conditions, it occurs mainly as colorless, odorless diatomic molecules. What element has atomic number 7 and symbol N?

In 1772, a Scottish physician studying air isolated nitrogen by removing oxygen and carbon dioxide, and described the remaining gas as unable to support combustion or respiration. Which scientist is credited with this first isolation?

In industrial nitrogen fixation, this process combines atmospheric nitrogen with hydrogen to produce ammonia under high pressure using an iron catalyst. Named for the chemist and engineer who developed it, what process enabled large-scale synthetic fertilizer production?
Nitrogen bonded to three hydrogen atoms forms this colorless, pungent-smelling compound, which is a crucial feedstock for fertilizer manufacture and for producing nitric acid. What compound is it?

This American chemist helped discover ten transuranium elements and shared the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Edwin McMillan. The synthetic element with atomic number 106 was later named in his honor; who was he?
Glenn T. Seaborg and his colleagues discovered this synthetic element in 1949. With atomic number 97, it was named for the university where the discovery took place; what is it?

Which Swedish naturalist, born in 1707, developed a hierarchical system for classifying organisms and helped standardize the use of two-part scientific names? His influential work *Systema Naturae* was first published in 1735.
Carl Linnaeus made this convention central to scientific naming: each species receives a two-part Latinized name consisting of its genus and a specific epithet. What is this naming system called?

In quantum mechanics, a moving particle is assigned a spatial period inversely proportional to its momentum, with Planck’s constant as the proportionality constant. What is this matter-wave quantity called?

In the de Broglie wavelength relation, Planck’s constant is divided by a property of the particle that measures its motion. What is this quantity, whose increase makes the associated wavelength shorter?

This practice involves cultivating crops and raising livestock, from preparing fields and planting seeds to harvesting food and tending animals. Over time, advances such as mechanized equipment, synthetic fertilizers, and high-yield crop varieties have transformed how it sustains human populations. What is this practice and industry?

Established in 1962, this European Union framework coordinates farm support and markets for farm produce among member states. A dispute over its financing helped prompt France’s withdrawal from European Community meetings during the 1965–66 Empty Chair Crisis. What is this framework, which shapes agriculture across Europe?
What name is given to an aircraft that rises because the air inside its envelope is heated? During the Siege of Paris, craft of this kind carried mail and passengers beyond the Prussian blockade.
During the 1870–71 Siege of Paris, this French politician escaped the encircled city by hot-air balloon and traveled to Tours to help organize resistance to the Prussians. Who was he?

At a liquid’s boundary, cohesion makes its exposed layer behave somewhat like a stretched elastic film. This effect rounds droplets and can support water striders on ponds; what physical property is being described?

Surface tension decreases when certain molecules gather at the boundary between water and air. These agents have a water-attracting part and an oil-attracting part, helping oily grime mix with water; what class of substances are they?

An empirical numerical rule estimates the planets’ distances from the Sun using a sequence based largely on doubling terms. Its predicted gap between Mars and Jupiter helped prompt a search for a missing body. What is this historical rule called?

The Titius–Bode Law suggested that an object should orbit roughly 2.8 astronomical units from the Sun, between Mars and Jupiter. Discovered in 1801, this body is now classified as a dwarf planet and is the largest object in the asteroid belt. What is it?

This supernova remnant lies in the constellation Taurus and consists of debris from an explosion that Chinese astronomers recorded in 1054 CE. A rapidly rotating neutron star at its center powers the surrounding cloud of glowing gas. What object is this?
The Crab Nebula is the expanding remnant of a stellar explosion recorded by Chinese astronomers in 1054 CE. What class of cataclysmic stellar event produced it?

In mechanics, this device consists of a mass suspended from a fixed pivot. When displaced, gravity pulls it back toward equilibrium, producing oscillation; its small-swing period depends mainly on its length and the local acceleration due to gravity. What is it?
A pendulum clock was invented in 1656 by this Dutch mathematician and astronomer, who later published the treatise *Horologium Oscillatorium*. Who was he?
Before quartz standards displaced it in the 1930s, this precision timekeeping device, built around a free pendulum, achieved accuracy of about one second per year. What was it?

In physical chemistry, this relation expresses a reaction’s rate constant as a pre-exponential factor multiplied by an exponential term involving the negative activation energy divided by the gas constant and absolute temperature. What equation, named for a Swedish chemist, is it?
In the Arrhenius equation, which quantity appears in the exponent divided by the product of the gas constant and absolute temperature, is commonly written as Ea, and is measured in joules per mole?
This orange-red red supergiant marks one of Orion the Hunter’s shoulders, and astronomers have directly imaged its changing surface. Its brightness varies semiregularly. Which star is it?
In late 2019 and early 2020, Betelgeuse underwent a dramatic temporary fading after dust formed from ejected gas obscured it. What is this episode commonly called?

This 19th-century French astronomer formulated a criterion for when a satellite may be torn apart by a planet’s tidal forces. A division in Saturn’s ring system is also named in his honor; who was he?

Édouard Roche’s work on tidal forces helps describe the critical distance from a planet inside which a satellite held together mainly by its own gravity can be torn apart. What is this orbital threshold called?

Astronomers identify familiar emission or absorption lines in an object’s spectrum and compare their observed wavelengths with the same lines measured in a laboratory. What is the name for the displacement toward longer wavelengths, often represented by the symbol z?
Redshift describes a spectral shift toward longer wavelengths, while the opposite effect moves spectral features toward shorter wavelengths. What is this opposite shift called?

This transition metal occupies atomic number 26 and group 8 of the periodic table. It is exceptionally abundant by mass on Earth, makes up much of the planet’s core, and is a principal ingredient in steel. What element is it?
In the human body, most Iron is found in a heme-containing protein packed into red blood cells. What protein binds oxygen for transport from the lungs to tissues?

When Iron is exposed to both oxygen and water, it forms a flaky reddish-brown corrosion product that does not protect the underlying metal, allowing corrosion to continue. What is this product commonly called?
During the Great Oxygenation Event, ancient oceans deposited distinctive alternating layers of iron oxides and silica. What geological deposit type is named for these iron-rich layers?

Fungi, bacteria, and detritivores such as earthworms can obtain nutrients by breaking down dead organic matter. What ecological role describes an organism that performs this process and helps return nutrients to ecosystems?
In decomposer ecology, some fungi that digest lignin and termites feed on this structural material found in tree trunks and branches. What is this material?
What model explains macroscopic properties, such as pressure and temperature, through the motion and interactions of microscopic particles? It often idealizes those particles as hard spheres.

In the Kinetic Theory of Gases, idealized hard spheres affect one another only during brief interactions that exchange momentum; kinetic energy is conserved when these interactions are elastic. What is the name for one such interaction between particles?

In structural geology, what is a break or zone of breaks in Earth’s crust where movement has displaced rock on either side? Normal, reverse, and strike-slip are common types, classified by the direction of that movement.

Faults can offset segments of mid-ocean ridges, where new oceanic crust forms. What process describes this crust gradually moving away from the ridge, as proposed in the Vine–Matthews–Morley hypothesis?

What term describes fossilized remains of extinct human relatives that researchers use to study human evolution? Examples discovered in Olduvai Gorge include remains assigned to Homo habilis, Homo erectus, and Paranthropus boisei.

Among hominin fossils from Olduvai Gorge, what catalog designation identifies the Paranthropus boisei skull that Mary Leakey discovered in 1959? Its large molars inspired the nickname “Nutcracker Man.”

These vascular-plant organs usually extend into soil, anchoring the plant while absorbing water and dissolved mineral nutrients. Some also store food or form partnerships with fungi. What are these organs called?

In plant roots, the endodermis contains a waterproof band of suberin that blocks movement through cell walls and intercellular spaces, making water and dissolved solutes cross a cell membrane before entering the vascular cylinder. What is this band called?
Some mangrove plant roots grow vertically above oxygen-poor, waterlogged sediment, exposing gas-exchange surfaces to the air. What are these upward-projecting respiratory roots called?

Plant roots of many species exchange sugars with fungi for mineral nutrients such as phosphorus, in a symbiosis that may form either inside root cells or around the root surface. What is this association called?

Born in the German Empire in 1879, this theoretical physicist published four landmark papers in 1905 and later received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for explaining a light-induced electron phenomenon. His theories of special and general relativity and the equation E = mc² reshaped modern physics; who was he?

Albert Einstein published landmark papers on Brownian motion, the photoelectric effect, special relativity, and mass–energy equivalence during 1905. What Latin phrase is commonly used to describe this unusually productive year in his career?

Albert Einstein’s 1905 paper treated light as discrete energy quanta and explained why shining light on a material can eject electrons only when the light exceeds a threshold frequency. What phenomenon did this explanation address, for which he later received the Nobel Prize?

Albert Einstein’s 1915 theory describes gravity through the curvature of spacetime rather than as an ordinary force, and it accounts for the anomalous precession of Mercury’s orbit. What theory is this?

Albert Einstein helped formulate a quantum counting rule for indistinguishable particles that can share the same state; photons obey this rule, unlike electrons. What statistical framework describes their distribution?

What mechanical quantity describes the intensity of forces carried inside a material when it is loaded? For a uniform force perpendicular to a cross-section, it is calculated by dividing the force by the area and is measured in pascals.
In the simple uniform case of Stress, what SI derived unit measures force per area? It is equivalent to one newton per square metre and is abbreviated Pa.
In June 1963, a Soviet cosmonaut made a solo orbital flight aboard Vostok 6, becoming the first woman to travel in space. What was her name?
Valentina Tereshkova flew aboard which spacecraft, launched on June 16, 1963, that orbited Earth 48 times before landing nearly three days later?

In organic synthesis, a partially poisoned palladium reagent selectively hydrogenates alkynes to cis-alkenes while helping prevent further reduction to alkanes. What named reagent is commonly prepared with palladium supported on calcium carbonate?

Lindlar's catalyst is commonly deactivated with quinoline and a divalent salt of the heavy metal historically used in plumbing, paired with a carboxylate derived from ethanoic acid. What is this poisoning additive?

This computational technique defines a problem in terms of smaller instances of that same problem. For factorial, it expresses n! as n × (n − 1)! and uses 0! = 1 as a stopping point. What is this technique called?

In recursion, a function may execute itself on progressively smaller inputs while earlier invocations wait for the results. What runtime structure stores each unfinished invocation’s state and return point, then resumes those invocations in reverse order?
An Italian astronomer and physicist, he reported in 1610 that Jupiter has four orbiting moons, and his observations of Venus’s phases challenged the traditional Earth-centered model. Who was he?
Galileo Galilei described the Moon’s rugged surface and four satellites orbiting Jupiter in this Latin work, published in 1610. Its title translates as “Starry Messenger.” What is the work?

This collaborative NASA, ESA, and ASI mission became the first spacecraft to orbit Saturn. It also delivered a lander that descended through the atmosphere of Saturn’s largest moon. What was the mission’s name?

The lander delivered by Cassini–Huygens descended through this moon’s dense, nitrogen-rich atmosphere and sent data from its surface. The moon is Saturn’s largest and has lakes of liquid hydrocarbons near its poles. What is it called?
What water-saturated mixture of soil and fine sediment can be carried in lahars after volcanic eruptions? When it flows downslope, it can bury buildings and farmland.

Azerbaijan’s Gobustan State Reserve is known for its numerous mud volcanoes near the shore of this inland body of water. The Volga River empties into it, and it is technically the world’s largest lake.

Unlike photons, this massless spin-1 gauge boson carries the charge of the interaction it mediates, allowing it to interact with itself as it binds quarks inside hadrons. What is this particle called?
Gluon interactions are described by the Standard Model theory of the strong interaction, which is built on an SU(3) gauge symmetry associated with three color charges. What is this theory called?

In this analytical method, a strong applied field separates energy states of nuclei such as hydrogen-1 and carbon-13, while radiofrequency radiation can drive transitions between them. Chemists use the resulting signals and chemical shifts, typically reported in ppm, to infer molecular structure. What is this method?

In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, the proton chemical-shift scale assigns zero to a commonly used reference compound made of four methyl groups bonded to a central silicon atom. What is this reference compound?
These vast stellar systems have a flattened disk and a central bulge, with winding arms extending outward. Their distinctive shape can be modeled using density wave theory. What are they called?

In spiral galaxies, some central bulges are crossed by elongated structures of stars and gas. In Hubble’s tuning-fork classification, galaxies with this feature are marked “SB.” What are these structures called?

In angiosperms, this reproductive structure commonly has sepals and petals surrounding pollen-producing and ovule-bearing parts. After fertilization, its ovary can develop into a fruit. What is this structure?
In a flower, what term names a group of individual blossoms arranged on a shared axis, such as a lilac’s branched cluster?
In a flower, which male reproductive organ consists of an anther borne on a filament and produces pollen?
In a flower’s reproductive cycle, what is the transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma called? Wind or animal visitors can help carry it, and it can occur between flowers or within one flower.
In a flower, which part of the pistil encloses the ovules before fertilization and commonly matures into the fruit afterward?

What computational model consists of layers of simple processing units connected by adjustable weights and learns patterns by modifying those weights? Its design is loosely inspired by information processing in the brain.

During training of an Artificial Neural Network, what algorithm sends an output error signal back through earlier layers and uses the chain rule to calculate gradients for updating connection weights?

When a system at chemical equilibrium is disturbed by a change in concentration, pressure, or temperature, its equilibrium position shifts in a way that tends to counteract the disturbance. What principle describes this response?

When applying Le Chatelier’s principle, chemists can compare the equilibrium constant with a value calculated from the mixture’s current concentrations, with each concentration raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. What is this current-composition value, commonly symbolized by Q?

This three-carbon organic compound is produced when certain bacteria ferment sugars in milk, giving cultured dairy its characteristic tang. Its repeating units can also be polymerized into a biodegradable plastic used in 3-D printing; what compound is it?

When lactic acid formed by anaerobic glycolysis in muscle is carried to the liver and used to regenerate glucose, that glucose can return to muscle for further metabolism. What is the name of this liver-muscle metabolic pathway?

Which iron-containing protein gives red blood cells their oxygen-carrying capacity? It is a tetramer whose four subunits each contain an iron-bearing porphyrin group, and carbon monoxide binds to it far more strongly than oxygen does.

In hemoglobin, what named physiological effect explains why rising carbon dioxide and falling pH in active tissues reduce oxygen binding and encourage oxygen release? In the lungs, where carbon dioxide is expelled and pH rises, the same relationship favors oxygen loading.

In this desalination method, a direct-current electric field moves dissolved cations and anions through alternating selective barriers, producing neighboring salt-depleted and salt-enriched streams. What is the process called?
In electrodialysis, what family of selective barriers is arranged in alternating layers, with one type permitting cations and another permitting anions, to create dilute and concentrate compartments?
Which state of matter has particles that move freely and are spaced far apart, with no fixed shape or volume? It expands to fill its container and is readily compressed.
In a sealed container holding a gas, what quantity results from particle collisions with the container walls? It is force per unit area and is commonly measured in pascals.
Which mixture of gases, composed mostly of nitrogen and oxygen, surrounds Earth and is what people breathe? It is a mixture rather than a single pure substance such as neon.

In the Golgi reaction, a small subset of neurons takes on a dark appearance that gave the procedure its traditional name. In light and optics, what achromatic color is perceived when visible light is absent or completely absorbed?

In discussions of Black as an optical appearance, what silver-chromate histological technique impregnates only a small subset of neurons, revealing their cell bodies, axons, and dendrites against a pale background?

In Hamiltonian mechanics, this abstract framework assigns a point to every complete instantaneous state of a dynamical system. For a one-dimensional particle, its coordinates can be position and momentum, and the system’s evolution traces a path through it. What is this framework called?

In phase space, a particle’s state is commonly described using position and a conjugate quantity that, for ordinary translational motion, equals mass times velocity. Its change is measured by impulse, and translational symmetry can make it a conserved quantity. What is it?
In an isolated system, this type of impact preserves total linear momentum, even though some kinetic energy is transformed into heat, sound, or deformation. What is it called?

In an inelastic collision, this dimensionless quantity compares the objects’ relative speed after impact with their relative speed before impact. It is zero when the objects stick together and move as one.

African spiny mice can restore damaged skin with much less scarring than most mammals, and salamanders can replace amputated limbs by rebuilding complex structures. What is this general biological process?
During salamander limb regeneration, what mass of cells forms at the injury site and develops into the replacement structures?

This numeral system assigns place values that double as you move from right to left, allowing quantities to be written with just two symbols. It is widely used in computing, where patterns of its digits can encode numbers and other data. What is this system?
In Binary, what is the name for one individual digit that can be either 0 or 1? A collection of these units forms patterns, and n such units can represent 2ⁿ distinct combinations.
In this form of asexual reproduction, an embryo develops from an unfertilized egg. What is this reproductive process called?
A triploid freshwater crustacean reproduces through parthenogenesis, with embryos developing from unfertilized eggs. What is this animal, whose common name refers to its patterned appearance?

Friedrich Bessel inferred that this star had an unseen companion from irregularities in its motion, and the companion was later identified as a white dwarf. It is the brightest star in the night sky and a main-sequence member of Canis Major. What is the star’s name?
Sirius A is a hydrogen-fusing main-sequence star, but its much fainter companion is an Earth-sized stellar remnant with roughly the Sun’s mass. What class of star is that companion?

These social insects belong to the genus Apis and live in colonies organized around a queen. Workers forage among flowers for nectar and pollen, while the colony stores nectar-derived food in wax comb. What are they called?

Honey bees returning from a food source can communicate its direction and distance to nestmates by repeating a figure-eight pattern, with the angle and duration of the central run conveying information. What is this behavior called?

What scientific theory explains how inherited genetic material changes in populations over generations and how life’s diversity arose through branching descent from shared ancestors? Its explanations are supported by evidence from fossils, DNA, and anatomical similarities.
Within the theory of evolution, what mechanism makes inherited traits more common over generations when individuals with those traits tend to survive and reproduce more successfully than others?
Which large constricting snake is native to South and Southeast Asia and has established an invasive population in Florida's Everglades, where it threatens native wildlife?
The Burmese python has become invasive in which vast subtropical wetland region of southern Florida, famous for its sawgrass marshes and mangrove habitats?

Which photoreceptor in the retina is especially sensitive in dim light and contributes strongly to peripheral vision? It favors sensitivity over color discrimination rather than providing detailed color perception.
In a rod cell, which light-sensitive G-protein-coupled receptor is also known as “visual purple”? Absorbing a photon changes its retinal chromophore and initiates phototransduction.

What scientific theory holds that Earth’s rigid outer shell is divided into large, moving sections whose interactions shift continents and form ocean basins, while also driving earthquakes and volcanoes?

In the context of plate tectonics, what prehistoric supercontinent was proposed by Alfred Wegener after evidence such as matching continental coastlines and Glossopteris fossils suggested that today’s continents were once joined? Its name combines Greek roots meaning “all” and “Earth.”

What type of aircraft uses powered rotors to generate lift, allowing it to take off and land vertically, hover in place, and maneuver without a runway? Unlike a fixed-wing aircraft, it can remain nearly stationary over a location.

In a helicopter, what emergency descent procedure can help a pilot land after engine failure by adjusting the rotor blades so upward airflow keeps the rotor turning? This maneuver is taught to pilots because it can preserve control even when the engine is no longer driving the rotor.
These forms of an element have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, giving them different mass numbers. What are they called?
Among the isotopes of hydrogen, which stable form has one proton and one neutron in its nucleus? Its neutral atom also has one electron.

An international collaboration involving the European Union, China, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia, and the United States is constructing this experimental fusion facility at Saint-Paul-lès-Durance in France. Its tokamak is designed to produce 500 megawatts of fusion power from 50 megawatts of heating input, demonstrating high-performance plasma operation rather than generating commercial electricity. What is the project’s name?

ITER’s planned high-performance experiments use a reaction that combines two hydrogen isotopes and yields a helium-4 nucleus and a 14.1-MeV neutron. A lithium-bearing blanket is intended to help breed one of those isotopes for the fuel cycle. What is this reaction called?

A* and Dijkstra’s algorithms are commonly used in video games and mapping software to solve this computational task. It involves finding a route between locations, often seeking the least-cost route through a graph. What is this task called?
In Pathfinding, a map can be modeled as a network whose connections carry numerical costs, so traversing one connection may count more than another. What kind of network is this?

This bright-yellow nonmetal has atomic number 16 and the chemical symbol S; its atoms commonly form crown-shaped rings of eight. Known historically by a name meaning “burning stone,” what is this element?
The largest commercial use of sulfur is producing a highly corrosive liquid with the formula H₂SO₄, used extensively to make phosphate fertilizers. What compound is it?
In sulfur chemistry, which colorless gas has the formula H₂S and is notorious for its rotten-egg odor? It can be produced when organic matter decays without oxygen.
In proteins such as keratin, sulfur-containing links between cysteine residues help strengthen hair, skin, and feathers. What are these covalent S–S links called?

In vertebrate zoology, this diverse group consists of non-ape primates and includes New World capuchins and howlers as well as Old World macaques. The supernatural figure Sun Wukong from *Journey to the West* is popularly associated with this group; what are these animals called?

Many New World monkeys, including spider monkeys, can wrap the tip of this elongated appendage around branches and use it as a fifth gripping limb while climbing. What is this grasping adaptation called?

Members of the family Culicidae begin as eggs, pass through aquatic larval and pupal stages, and emerge as winged adults. In blood-feeding species, females take blood meals to obtain protein for producing eggs; what is the common name for these insects?
In mosquitoes, infected females of this genus transmit human malaria, though only a minority of its species commonly do so. What genus includes these malaria vectors?

These marine cnidarians often live in colonies of tiny polyps that secrete calcium-carbonate skeletons. Their reef-building habitats support highly diverse ecosystems, and warming seas can cause them to lose their symbiotic algae. What are these animals called?

In many corals, these photosynthetic dinoflagellates live within the animal’s tissues and provide much of its energy. Heat stress can disrupt the partnership and cause the coral to lose them, leaving it pale. What are these symbionts commonly called?
What condition is an open sore in the mucous membrane of the stomach or upper digestive tract, and can arise when excessive use of certain pain relievers reduces protective mucus production?
In the context of a peptic ulcer, what class of anti-inflammatory pain relievers—including ibuprofen and naproxen—inhibits cyclooxygenase and can increase the risk of stomach-lining damage?

At a 1654 demonstration in Regensburg, Otto von Guericke evacuated air from two joined copper shells, and teams of horses could not pull them apart. What name is given to the hemispherical apparatus used in this demonstration?

In the Magdeburg hemispheres demonstration, pumping air from the joined shells left the surrounding air pushing inward far more strongly than the gas inside pushed outward. What supplied the inward force that held the shells together?
These filaments grow from follicles in the skin, and the scalp typically bears many of them. Their visible shafts are made largely of a tough structural protein. What are these strands called?
In human hair, which tough structural protein makes up most of the shaft and is also a major component of fingernails? Its strength helps the strands withstand everyday grooming.

This chemical sense detects airborne odorants through receptor neurons in the nasal epithelium. Its first central relay sends signals toward the piriform cortex without an initial stop in the usual thalamic relay. What is this sensory system?

In olfaction, receptor neurons send axons to this paired forebrain structure, where they converge in glomeruli; output neurons then project to regions including the piriform cortex. What is this first major central processing station?

This artificial orbital facility is designed to keep people living and working in orbit for extended periods, rather than carrying them on only a brief journey. What is the general name for this kind of facility?
Which U.S. space station, launched in 1973 as America’s first, hosted three crews before reentering Earth’s atmosphere in 1979?
This emergency procedure is used when a person suffers cardiac arrest, combining chest compressions with usually rescue breathing to help maintain circulation and oxygenation. What is it called?

During cardiopulmonary resuscitation, rescuers may use a portable device that analyzes the person’s heart rhythm and provides voice prompts. If it detects a shockable rhythm, the device can deliver an electrical shock; what is it called?
This surface-extraction process reaches shallow mineral deposits by removing long bands of overlying earth. It can leave extensive landscape disruption and increase soil erosion. What is this method?

Unlike strip mining, coal can also be transported through pipelines after being mixed with water into a pumpable suspension. What is this mixture, associated with the deadly 1972 Buffalo Creek flood in West Virginia?

This soft, silvery Group 1 metal has atomic number 11 and is rarely found uncombined because it reacts vigorously with water and air. Its characteristic flame-test emission is intense yellow-orange light near 589 nanometres. What element is it?
Sodium was first isolated in 1807 when this English chemist used electricity to decompose sodium hydroxide. The same scientist also isolated potassium by electrolysis that year. Who was he?

This progressive neurodegenerative condition is the most common cause of dementia in older adults. Its characteristic brain pathology includes beta-amyloid plaques and tau-containing neurofibrillary tangles. What is it?

In research on Alzheimer’s disease, radioactive tracers can help map brain metabolism or reveal pathological protein deposits in living patients. Which imaging technique detects paired photons produced after the tracer decays?
In mechanics, what is the repeated motion in which a system moves back and forth around an equilibrium position, as a pendulum does? It often recurs in regular cycles.

For a pendulum undergoing oscillation, what term names the time required to complete one full cycle and return to the same point in its motion? It is the reciprocal of frequency and is commonly represented by T.

Located above the stratosphere and below the thermosphere, this atmospheric layer is the coldest part of the atmosphere. It is also where many meteors heat up and ablate as they enter Earth’s atmosphere. What is this layer called?
In the Mesosphere, delicate blue-white ice-crystal formations can remain illuminated against the dark sky after sunset. What are these formations called?

Astronomers use this graph to compare stars by intrinsic brightness and surface temperature, often represented by spectral class or color. Its customary layout places hotter stars to the left and brighter stars higher up, revealing distinct stellar groupings. What is this graph called?

On the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram, what is the diagonal band of stars powered by hydrogen-to-helium fusion in their cores, extending from hot, luminous stars at the upper left to cool, faint stars at the lower right?

This Dutch theoretical physicist shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pieter Zeeman for research into the influence of magnetism on radiation. His name is also attached to a relativistic factor used in calculations of time dilation and length contraction. Who was he?

Hendrik Lorentz provided a theoretical explanation for the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field, following its experimental observation by another Dutch physicist. Which scientist made that observation and shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Lorentz?
This alkaline-earth metal has atomic number 38 and is used to produce vivid red colors in fireworks. Which element is it?
A radioactive isotope of strontium released in nuclear fallout can accumulate in bones because the body treats it like calcium. Which isotope is this?
What is the name of the helical coil of wire whose successive turns reinforce one another’s magnetic fields when current passes through it, producing a field along its axis?

In discussions of a solenoid, which French physicist gave the device its name and is also honored in the SI unit of electric current? His work established foundational relationships between electric currents and magnetism.
This is the world’s largest living fish and inhabits tropical and warm-temperate oceans, where it sieves tiny organisms from the water. What species is it?
The whale shark takes in seawater containing tiny food particles, then expels the water while retaining the food. What method of obtaining food does it use?

In population genetics, this idealized model predicts genotype frequencies of p², 2pq, and q² from allele frequencies p and q. Under its assumptions, allele and genotype frequencies remain constant across generations; what is the model called?
In Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, the term 2pq gives the expected frequency of individuals with two different alleles at a gene locus. What genotype class do these individuals belong to?
In materials science, this property can be measured by indentation tests that yield Vickers values or by scratch tests. What property describes a material’s resistance to being scratched or indented?
Hardness can be compared using an ordinal mineral scale in which talc is assigned 1 and diamond 10. What is this scale called?

When two contacting surfaces slide, roll, or are on the verge of moving, this force opposes their relative or attempted motion. It can transform mechanical energy into heat and has static and kinetic forms. What is this force?
The scientific field that studies friction, wear, and lubrication draws on mechanics and materials science. What is this field called?
In microscopic explanations of friction, contact between surfaces is concentrated at tiny peaks that touch and deform. What are these microscopic surface projections called?
In a simple dry-contact model, the magnitude of friction is related to the normal force by a dimensionless quantity commonly represented by the Greek letter μ. What is this quantity called?
Friction experiments may measure the force between contacting materials under controlled conditions of load and motion. What instrument is designed for this purpose?

This ancient Greek mathematician and engineer came from a city in Sicily and wrote influential works on geometry, hydrostatics, and mechanics. He is associated with the law of the lever and a screw pump, and was killed during the Roman siege of his city. Who was he?
Archimedes of Syracuse is associated with a hydrostatic rule stating that an immersed body experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces. What is this named principle?

Archimedes of Syracuse is associated with a water-lifting device built around a helical surface wrapped around a central cylinder. Turning the device carries water upward through its tube; what is this machine called?
In qualitative analysis, dissolved ions combine to form an insoluble solid that separates from the surrounding solution. What type of chemical process is this?
In a precipitation reaction, which negatively charged ion from dissolved table salt forms insoluble compounds with lead, silver, and mercury ions?
Radio static can mask a spoken broadcast, and random fluctuations in measurements can conceal a trend even when no sound is involved. What general kind of unwanted variation is being described?

When noise interferes with a measurement, engineers can quantify how clearly the desired content stands out by comparing signal strength with the interference level; larger values usually indicate a cleaner result. What is this comparative quantity called?

At 20°C, the value of this quantity in dry air is commonly rounded to 343 meters per second. Oceanographers also note that the SOFAR channel is a depth region where it reaches a minimum. What quantity is this?

A jet moving at twice the local speed of sound has a value of 2 for this dimensionless measure. It compares an object's velocity with the speed of sound, accounting for the fact that sound travels at different speeds in different conditions. What is this measure called?
This phylum consists of marine invertebrates that swim using eight rows of fused cilia, which can create shimmering, iridescent bands. What phylum includes these comb-bearing animals?
In Ctenophora, eight longitudinal rows of fused cilia help propel the animal through the water and may appear iridescent as they beat. What are these specialized rows called?

This group of RNA viruses copies its genetic information into DNA after entering a cell, then inserts that DNA into the host genome. Lentiviruses, including HIV, are members of this group. What is the group called?
In a retrovirus, which enzyme makes a DNA copy from the viral RNA genome? It performs the RNA-to-DNA conversion before a separate enzyme helps insert the viral DNA into the host genome.

When cytokines bind their receptors, receptor-associated Janus kinases phosphorylate latent DNA-binding proteins that then pair and enter the nucleus to regulate gene expression. What is this cellular mechanism called?
In the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, which STAT transcription factor is activated downstream of interleukin-6 signaling and promotes expression of acute-phase response genes?
This endocrine organ sits at the base of the brain and produces or releases hormones such as human growth hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone. What is its natural name?
Made in the hypothalamus but released by the posterior pituitary gland, this peptide hormone is associated with childbirth and social bonding between parents and newborns. What is it?

Which theory is built on the postulates that physical laws take the same form in every inertial frame and that all inertial observers measure the same vacuum speed of light? It replaces Galilean transformations for high-speed motion and predicts effects such as changes in measured length and elapsed time.

In Special relativity, what effect makes a rapidly moving object's measured extent along its direction of travel smaller than its rest-frame extent? The pole-and-barn paradox illustrates how the object's fit inside a barn can differ between observers.
Special relativity predicts that a clock moving relative to an inertial observer is measured to tick more slowly than a clock at rest in that observer's frame. What is this phenomenon called?

In Special relativity, what set of coordinate equations relates space and time measurements made in two inertial frames moving at constant relative velocity, while preserving the vacuum speed of light? These equations replace the Galilean rules at relativistic speeds.

This is the largest living toothed cetacean and is renowned for extreme deep dives. It is traditionally identified as the species represented by the enormous white animal pursued in Herman Melville’s Moby-Dick. What species is it?

In the sperm whale’s massive head, what waxy substance was historically extracted for use in candles and ointments? It was once confused with a reproductive fluid, which helped give the whale its common name.

In most bacteria, this load-bearing cell-wall mesh is built from alternating sugar units linked to short peptide chains, with neighboring strands cross-linked for strength. What is this polymer that gives bacterial cell walls much of their rigidity?
Alexander Fleming discovered this family of antibiotics, which blocks enzymes that cross-link peptidoglycan during bacterial cell-wall assembly. What is the antibiotic family?

This exact SI constant has a value of 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ joules per kelvin and converts thermodynamic temperature into energy per particle. Its fixed numerical value is used to define the kelvin; name the constant.

In statistical physics, the Boltzmann constant appears in a relation that expresses this thermodynamic state function as the constant multiplied by the natural logarithm of the number of accessible microstates. Name the quantity represented by S in the relation S = k ln Ω.

This sterol is an essential component of animal cell membranes and serves as a precursor to steroid hormones, bile acids, and vitamin D. Elevated levels carried by LDL can contribute to atherosclerosis; what is this molecule?
In 1769, which French investigator first identified cholesterol in solid form in gallstones? His observation preceded the later naming of the compound.
Which French chemist gave cholesterol the name “cholesterine” in 1815?
This tropical bromeliad produces an edible compound fruit formed from many flowers fused together. James Dole helped make it an important plantation crop in Hawaiʻi; what is the crop’s common name?
Pineapple cultivation became a major plantation industry in this Pacific U.S. state, where the “Big Five” corporations once held substantial economic and political power. Which state is it?

This German mathematician, physicist, and astronomer made major contributions to number theory and geometry. His name is also associated with a method for solving systems of linear equations and a law of magnetism.

Carl Friedrich Gauss’s work in electromagnetism is connected to a surface integral that measures the net field passing through a boundary. According to the Maxwell equation stating that field lines have no sources or sinks, what quantity is zero across every closed surface?
Which group of fat-soluble antioxidant compounds includes alpha-tocopherol and occurs in foods such as plant oils? Its acetate derivative was implicated in cases of vaping-associated lung injury.
During investigations of EVALI, the lung injury associated with e-cigarette or vaping use, which ester form of Vitamin E was implicated in many THC-containing vape products?

In Jhumpa Lahiri’s short story “A Temporary Matter,” the utility company schedules one-hour evening interruptions beginning at 8 p.m. What is a temporary loss of electrical service of this kind called?

During the power outages in Jhumpa Lahiri’s “A Temporary Matter,” which character tells his wife Shoba the sex of their stillborn child? The revelation comes during the couple’s final evening without electricity.

This English physician and polymath used a double-slit experiment to demonstrate interference in light. His name is also attached to a measure of how a material deforms under stress. Which scientist was he?

Thomas Young’s work ranged from optics to the mechanics of solids. In the elastic range, what property is calculated as normal stress divided by longitudinal strain and measures a material’s stiffness?

This nucleotide is produced by the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis and consumed during the Calvin cycle to help drive carbon fixation. It is a principal molecule for transferring usable chemical energy within cells. What is it?

During photosynthesis, adenosine triphosphate is spent in a series of reactions in the chloroplast stroma that fixes carbon dioxide and helps form carbohydrate precursors. What named pathway is named for the American chemist who helped elucidate it?

Often silent until a fracture occurs, this condition develops when bone breakdown outpaces replacement, thinning the inner honeycomb-like structure and weakening bones; hip, spine, and wrist fractures are common. What is this disease?
For people with Osteoporosis, clinicians commonly use this low-dose X-ray examination to measure bone mineral density and help estimate fracture risk. What is this examination called?

In continuum mechanics, this vector assigns a direction and magnitude to the motion of a liquid or gas at each point. It is the time rate of change of a parcel’s position and is commonly expressed in meters per second; what is it called?

For a small sphere moving slowly through a fluid, Stokes’ law relates drag to the sphere’s radius, Fluid Velocity, and a property of the fluid measured in pascal-seconds. What is this property, which describes the fluid’s internal resistance to flow?
In programming, what is the common term for an error or flaw in code that can make a program behave in an unintended way?

A story often told in connection with the term software bug concerns a moth removed from the Harvard Mark II in 1947 and taped into its logbook. Which U.S. Navy computer scientist, who later became a rear admiral and helped develop COBOL, recounted this episode?

Web authors use this language to control colors, typography, spacing, and layout while leaving an HTML document’s content structure intact. It expresses rules by matching selectors to declarations, with conflicts resolved by factors such as specificity and source order; what is this language?

Cascading Style Sheets can use this conditional mechanism to apply different rules depending on conditions such as viewport width, screen orientation, or whether a document is being printed. Often used to adapt layouts for different devices, what is this feature?

What propagating disturbances in spacetime curvature, predicted by general relativity, are emitted by accelerating massive systems such as close-orbiting black holes and cause tiny changes in distances as they pass?

The first direct detection of gravitational waves came from two black holes spiraling together, with the signal recorded in 2015 by a project that uses laser interferometry and perpendicular four-kilometer arms. What U.S. observatory project made the detection?

NASA’s infrared observatory launched from French Guiana on December 25, 2021, and has a 6.5-meter primary mirror made of 18 gold-plated beryllium segments. Designed to study early galaxies, stars, and exoplanetary systems, what is this observatory called?

The James Webb Space Telescope reached a region about 1.5 million kilometers from our planet in January 2022, where it orbits the Sun and keeps the Sun and Moon on the same side of its sunshield. What is this second Lagrange point in the Sun–planet system called?

The James Webb Space Telescope uses this thermal barrier, made of Kapton membranes, to block heat from the Sun, Earth, and Moon and help keep the observatory below 50 kelvins. What is this protective assembly called?
This non-ionizing part of the electromagnetic spectrum has wavelengths longer than microwaves and carries signals used for AM and FM broadcasting. What is this type of radiation called?
A German physicist experimentally demonstrated radio waves in the late 1880s, confirming James Clerk Maxwell’s prediction that electromagnetic waves could propagate through space. What was his name?
A small rocky body may create a bright streak as it passes through Earth’s atmosphere; what is the surviving fragment that reaches the ground called?
A massive iron Meteorite discovered near Grootfontein, Namibia, in 1920 remains at its discovery site and is regarded as the largest known intact specimen. By what name is this object known?

In a covalent structure, this connection is represented by two lines and accounts for four shared electrons. In the usual orbital model, it comprises one component formed by head-on overlap and another formed by sideways overlap.

A double bond contains one component formed by sideways overlap of p orbitals, placing electron density above and below the internuclear axis. Rotation that disrupts this overlap weakens this component; what is it called?

In human genetic genealogy, which male-specific component of the nuclear genome is typically transmitted from father to son, making it useful for tracing a direct paternal lineage? It carries DNA involved in male development.

Which DNA sequence on the Y chromosome produces a transcription factor that helps direct the embryonic gonad to develop as testes, initiating the typical male sex-determination pathway? When this sequence is nonfunctional, a person with a Y chromosome may develop gonads differently.

In vascular plants, this usually flattened organ grows laterally from a stem and contains chlorophyll-bearing tissues and veins. It is a major site of photosynthesis and exchanges gases through microscopic pores. What is this plant organ?

On many terrestrial plants, these microscopic pores are especially common on the lower surface of a leaf. They regulate the exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen, as well as the loss of water vapor. What are these pores called?
Beneath the upper epidermis of many leaves, this tissue consists of elongated, closely packed cells that carry out much of the organ’s photosynthesis. What is this tissue?
Lycophytes have this kind of leaf, distinguished by a single vein and an evolutionary origin different from that of broad leaves with complex venation. What is this leaf type called?

This physical phenomenon involves fields that exert forces on magnetic dipoles, and it allows a compass needle to align with Earth’s field. It also accounts for the attraction and repulsion associated with north and south poles. What is this phenomenon?

Within magnetism, what type of ordering occurs when neighboring atomic magnetic moments align spontaneously into domains, producing a strong response that can persist after an external field is removed? Above its Curie temperature, this ordered state disappears.
When Venus or Mercury lies on the near side of the Sun along a line connecting Earth and the Sun, the planet can appear in its new phase. What is this named orbital alignment?

An inferior conjunction does not always produce this rare event, because the planet usually passes above or below the Sun’s disk in our sky. In 2012, a small dark disk crossed the Sun’s face as seen from Earth, and the next such passage is expected in 2117; what is this event called?
In fluid mechanics and thermodynamics, this quantity is defined as force distributed over a unit area. Atmospheric measurements of it may be reported in pascals, torr, or pounds per square inch.
Pressure and volume vary inversely for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, so their product remains constant. Which gas law is commonly written as P₁V₁ = P₂V₂?

This four-resistor circuit compares an unknown resistance against known resistors in two branches, with a detector joining their midpoints. At balance, no current flows through the detector, and the resistance ratios can be used to find the unknown value. What is this circuit called?

The Wheatstone bridge is named for the scientist who brought it wider attention in 1843, but a British scientist had described the arrangement in 1833. Historical accounts differ on whether this earlier author originally intended it for measuring resistance. Who was he?

In this quantitative neutralization procedure, a solution of known concentration is added gradually from a burette to a measured sample of unknown concentration. An indicator color change or an instrumental reading marks the endpoint, allowing the sample’s concentration to be calculated; what is this technique called?

During an acid–base titration, what is the theoretical stage at which the acid and base have reacted in exact stoichiometric proportions, such as equal mole amounts for a monoprotic acid and a monohydroxide base? It is conceptually distinct from the observed indicator endpoint, which may occur slightly before or after it.

This naturally occurring five-carbon sugar alcohol has the formula C₅H₁₂O₅ and is used as a lower-calorie sweetener in many sugar-free products. Because oral bacteria do not readily ferment it, it is also commonly included in products intended to support dental health. What compound is it?
Xylitol is often used as a sugar substitute in this chewy confection. Orbit, Extra, and Big Red are well-known brands of it, and some varieties are designed for blowing bubbles. What is this product?

In the Sun and other stars, this reaction joins light nuclei into heavier ones, and changes in binding energy can release energy. Unlike fission, which splits heavy nuclei, what is this process called?

In nuclear fusion research, this toroidal magnetic-confinement device uses powerful magnetic coils and a plasma current to confine hot plasma. ITER is being built around this design; what is the device called?

In nuclear fusion experiments, a widely used performance measure combines plasma temperature, particle density, and energy-confinement time, often represented as nTτ_E. What is this three-factor measure called?
In supervised learning, this model tests feature values at internal nodes and sends each example along a branch until it reaches a terminal node that provides a prediction. What is this model called?
In a Decision Tree classifier, what impurity measure for a group is calculated from the class probabilities using the negative sum of each probability multiplied by its logarithm?

A population’s inherited characteristics change across generations, while changes within an individual’s lifetime do not constitute this process. Mutations, genetic drift, and gene flow can all contribute, with natural selection being only one mechanism. What is this process?

During biological evolution, this mechanism changes allele frequencies by chance rather than because a variant improves survival or reproduction. Its effects are especially strong in small populations and include founder and bottleneck effects. What is this mechanism?

This single-stranded transcript is made from a DNA template and carries codons that are read during translation to determine the order of amino acids. What molecule serves as the template for building a protein?

After messenger RNA reaches the cytoplasm, it associates with a molecular machine made of small and large subunits. This machine reads the transcript’s codons and links amino acids into a growing polypeptide; what is it?

When an ionic solid is in equilibrium with its dissolved ions, adding a soluble compound that supplies one of those same ions decreases the solid’s solubility and may cause precipitation. What is this named phenomenon?

In a saturated PbCl₂ solution, adding ordinary table salt (NaCl) supplies an anion already present in the dissolved solid and can promote precipitation. Under the Common Ion Effect, what negatively charged ion supplied by table salt is shared with PbCl₂?

In its small-unit form, this energy measure is defined as the heat needed to raise one gram of water by one degree Celsius, and it is approximately 4.18 joules. Food energy is often expressed in multiples of this unit.
In measurements using the calorie, a mass-normalized thermal property of liquid water is about one calorie per gram per degree Celsius. What property does this value describe?

Early humans deliberately maintained this phenomenon to cook food, warm shelters, illuminate darkness, and harden wooden tools such as hunting spears. What natural phenomenon became one of humanity’s foundational technologies?

Evidence associated with the controlled use of fire was found at a South African archaeological site in the Northern Cape, where researchers identified microscopic ash in ancient sediments. What is the name of this site?
Goblet cells lining respiratory passages release this viscous secretion, which humidifies inhaled air and traps dust and microbes. What substance is carried toward the throat as cilia beat?
In the trachea’s ciliated lining, mucus is released by a specialized epithelial structure with an expanded, cup-shaped apical end. What is this structure called?

In this arrangement, every component is connected between the same two nodes, so each branch shares the same potential difference. For resistors, the reciprocal of the total resistance equals the sum of the reciprocals of the branch resistances; what electrical arrangement is described?
In a parallel circuit, branches connect to the same two nodes, so this electrical quantity has an identical value across every branch even when branch currents differ. What quantity is it?

In this data structure, the most recently added element is the first one removed, following a last-in, first-out rule. Its standard insertion and removal operations are called push and pop. What is this structure?
A Stack can track nested function calls when a computation repeatedly solves smaller instances of the same problem. What programming technique is this called?
Built mainly from successive eruptions of fluid basaltic lava, this broad landform develops gently sloping sides as long-traveling flows spread outward. What kind of landform is described?
Among the shield volcanoes of Hawaiʻi, which one forms much of the Big Island and is recognized as the world’s largest active volcano by volume?

A Cambridge geneticist who worked with William Bateson on Mendelian heredity, he devised the grid used to predict offspring combinations from parental crosses. He also studied poultry genetics and agricultural breeding. Who was he?
Reginald Punnett’s poultry genetics research pursued a way for breeders to identify newly hatched birds’ sex from visible plumage differences. What is this approach called?

This circuit network selectively attenuates parts of a signal according to frequency, with its behavior described in relation to a cutoff frequency. Its common varieties pass frequencies above or below that boundary. What is this circuit network?

An electronic filter can be built from a resistor paired with this passive component to form an RC network. It stores energy in an electric field and is often represented by two parallel plates in a circuit diagram. What is the component?

In basic circuit analysis, this empirical relationship connects the voltage drop across a component with the current through it and its resistance. It is commonly written as V = IR and can be rearranged to solve for any one of those three quantities. What is this electrical law?
The experiments underlying Ohm's law were carried out by a 19th-century German physicist whose surname also names the SI unit of electrical resistance. Who was this scientist?

In programming, a single letter, digit, punctuation mark, or newline can be represented using an encoding such as ASCII or Unicode. Sequences of these text units form strings; what is one unit called?
In many programming languages, this text data type stores an ordered sequence of characters and can represent an empty sequence. In Python, values of this type are immutable; what is the type called?
This hard, lustrous transition metal has atomic number 24 and is often added to steel to improve corrosion resistance. Its presence gives ruby its characteristic red color. What element is it?
A compound of chromium has the formula CrO₃ and is typically purple, but turns orange when wet. What is this compound called?

In language-processing systems, this kind of information is commonly stored as strings of characters rather than as audio waveforms or numeric measurements. Pipelines may split it into tokens, reduce word forms with stemming, and represent it with embeddings.

When processing Textual Data, what preprocessing operation divides a character sequence into units such as words, subwords, or punctuation marks before later modeling? Unlike stemming, it does not reduce words to their root forms.

The Moon has broad, dark plains created when ancient volcanic eruptions flooded large impact basins. Despite their dry, rocky surfaces, these features were named with a Latin word meaning “seas.” What are they called?
Lunar maria are darker than the Moon’s highlands and consist mainly of volcanic rock. What rock, also widespread in Earth’s oceanic crust, forms most of these plains?
This compound has the formula H₂O and covers about 71% of Earth’s surface. Near Earth’s surface, it occurs naturally as a solid, liquid, and gas. What is it?

Water molecules are polar, and attractions between neighboring molecules help explain why water has a higher boiling point than many similarly small molecules. What is this type of intermolecular attraction called?
Water moves among oceans, land, ice, and the atmosphere through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, and runoff. What is the name for this connected circulation?
At the boundary between water and air, cohesive attractions create a taut layer that can support small insects and make drops bead up. What is this property called?

This small, bean-shaped organ lies along channels that return excess tissue fluid to the bloodstream, where it traps debris and provides a meeting place for immune cells. It may become enlarged during an infection; what is this organ?
