A lymph node filters a clear fluid that drains from tissues through a network of one-way vessels before returning to circulation. What is this fluid called?

Produced by B cells, this Y-shaped immune protein consists of two heavy chains and two light chains. Its variable-region binding site recognizes a specific epitope on an antigen. What is this molecule?
An antibody recognizes an antigen through a binding site formed by its variable regions, rather than its constant regions. What is this antigen-binding site called?

More than 350 breeds belong to this domesticated bird lineage, which people have kept for food, companionship, and message delivery. Its urban populations are generally feral rather than domesticated.

The domestic pigeon descends from which wild, cliff-nesting bird native to parts of Europe, North Africa, and western Asia? Unlike the many breeds of its domesticated relative, this ancestor is a wild species.

This American behaviorist studied the domestic pigeon, teaching birds to play ping-pong through operant conditioning and proposing that they guide missiles during World War II. Who led that Navy-sponsored effort?

What loose granular material, composed chiefly of mineral or rock particles, forms extensive areas of the Sahara and is also used in the berm separating Moroccan-controlled Western Sahara from the Sahrawi-controlled area?
This vast sandy expanse stretches across northern Africa from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea and is the largest hot region of its kind on Earth. What is it?

In a deterministic dynamical system, two trajectories that begin almost identically can separate rapidly, making long-term prediction difficult even though the system follows fixed rules. What is this property called?

In the study of chaos, what exponent measures the average growth rate of the separation along the most unstable direction between nearby trajectories? A positive value indicates sensitive dependence on initial conditions.
At a convergent boundary, this process occurs when one tectonic plate descends beneath another, commonly producing deep ocean trenches and volcanic activity. What is this geological process called?
In regions shaped by subduction, what is the name for a chain of volcanoes that forms on the overriding plate, often inland and roughly parallel to an ocean trench? The Cascade Range is one example.

In general relativity, what term in Einstein’s field equations represents a uniform energy density of empty space and can influence the universe’s expansion? Often denoted by the Greek letter lambda, it was added to allow a static-universe model.

In 1917, which physicist added the cosmological constant to his field equations to balance gravity in a model of a static universe? His work also includes the theory of special relativity and the equation E = mc².
Which nonmetallic element, identified by atomic number 6 and symbol C, sits in group 14 and can form four covalent bonds, enabling a vast range of compounds?
At standard temperature and pressure, which allotrope of Carbon is thermodynamically most stable? Its black, layered structure makes it soft, electrically conductive, and useful in pencil cores.

Which allotrope of Carbon forms a rigid three-dimensional crystal in which each atom bonds to four neighbors? Its exceptional hardness and poor electrical conductivity distinguish it from the layered conductive form.

Which radioactive isotope of Carbon, with a half-life of roughly 5,700 years, is used to estimate the age of once-living archaeological material? Unlike the two stable naturally occurring isotopes, it decays over time.

What is the name of the single-atom-thick allotrope of Carbon whose atoms are arranged in a flat hexagonal honeycomb lattice? Its electrical conductivity and exceptional strength have made it prominent in nanoscale research.
Which precision laboratory instrument measures very low gas pressures by trapping a known volume of gas, compressing it with mercury, and comparing mercury-column heights?
A McLeod gauge measures the pressure of this condition, in which sound cannot travel and which occupies the space above the mercury in a Torricelli barometer. What is this condition?
What group of cancers affects blood-forming tissues and can disrupt normal blood-cell production in the bone marrow? Its forms are often classified as acute or chronic and as lymphoid or myeloid.

In chronic myeloid leukemia, what named abnormal genetic structure results when material is exchanged between the long arms of genetic carriers numbered 9 and 22, creating the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene? It is named for the U.S. city where it was first identified.

This muscular organ has papillae on its surface and is moved by intrinsic muscles as well as muscles attached to structures such as the hyoid bone. A shortened or unusually restrictive frenulum beneath it can cause ankyloglossia; what is this organ, which helps with taste, speech, and swallowing?
Which fluid secreted by the parotid and submandibular glands moistens the tongue, carries dissolved chemicals to taste receptors, and contains the digestive enzyme amylase?

Some are triggered by runaway fusion in a white dwarf, while others follow the collapse of a massive star’s core after fusion can no longer resist gravity. What is the general name for these brilliant stellar explosions, which can briefly rival an entire galaxy in brightness?
A supernova observed by Chinese astronomers in 1054 left behind a glowing, expanding remnant in the constellation Taurus. What is the name of this famous remnant?
The 1987 supernova designated SN 1987A was the first supernova visible to the naked eye since Kepler’s in 1604. In which satellite galaxy of the Milky Way did it occur?

A procedure locates a target by comparing it with the middle element of an ordered collection, then discarding the half that cannot contain the target and repeating. When the collection is sorted, its worst-case running time is logarithmic. What is this algorithm called?

In the array version of binary search, each comparison can eliminate one side of the remaining range without overlooking the target. What property must the array’s values have for this halving strategy to work?

When coherent disturbances overlap, their displacements combine according to relative phases, so the resulting amplitude can increase or decrease. This phenomenon occurs with light, sound, water, and radio signals; what is it called?

Wave interference produces the fringes formed when monochromatic light passes through two narrow, closely spaced openings, a classic demonstration of light’s wave nature. What named optical setup is associated with the British polymath who carried out this demonstration?
Wave interference in reflected light can create concentric alternating bright and dark circles when a plano-convex lens rests on a flat glass plate. What is this classic optical pattern called?

This woody perennial flowering plant belongs to the genus Rosa and is widely grown for its colorful, fragrant blossoms. It grows as both shrubs and climbers and is famously associated with romantic love. What plant is it?

The rose belongs to this botanical family, alongside apples, strawberries, and cherries. Many plants in this family have flowers with five petals and produce fruits such as pomes or drupes. What family is it?

On a rose stem, the sharp projections often called thorns are botanically distinct from true thorns: they arise from the plant’s outer tissues rather than from modified branches. What are these projections properly called?

This family of enveloped RNA viruses includes pathogens responsible for SARS and MERS, as well as the agent behind COVID-19. Its name refers to the crownlike appearance of its surface spike proteins. What is this family?
Among the coronaviruses, which virus was identified in 2019 and causes COVID-19? It is the seventh known coronavirus to infect humans and the third to cause a major disease outbreak in humans.

A Polish-born, naturalized French physicist and chemist, she coined the term for the phenomenon she investigated and became the first woman to receive a Nobel Prize. She later became the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, in Physics and Chemistry; who was she?
Marie Curie and Pierre Curie isolated this radioactive element from pitchblende, and she chose its name to honor her native Poland. Which element was it?
During World War I, Marie Curie organized mobile radiography units that carried X-ray equipment to field hospitals and helped train operators. By what nickname were these vehicles commonly known?

This Russian physiologist investigated digestion in dogs, including how digestive glands secreted their fluids. His research earned the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, and his later experiments became foundational to classical conditioning. Who was he?
Ivan Pavlov distinguished an innate response from one acquired when a signal was repeatedly paired with food. What term did he use for the acquired response, such as salivation to the signal alone?

What class of chemical substances donates protons under the Brønsted–Lowry definition or accepts electron pairs under the Lewis definition? Their aqueous solutions generally have a pH below 7 and can turn blue litmus red.
When measuring the concentration of an unknown acid, what laboratory method involves adding a solution of known concentration gradually until an indicator shows that the endpoint has been reached?
Among acids found in the digestive system, which strong mineral acid is a major component of gastric juice and is also commonly used in laboratory experiments?
Which chemist defined acids as electron-pair acceptors and bases as electron-pair donors? His name is also attached to diagrams that represent covalent bonds with pairs of dots.
Which industrial acid was historically produced by the lead chamber process, is used as the electrolyte in lead-acid batteries, and is now commonly manufactured by the contact process?
When a lineage encounters many unoccupied ecological niches, it may rapidly diversify into multiple species, each adapted to a different way of life. What evolutionary process describes this pattern?

A classic example of adaptive radiation is the diversification of finches with different beak shapes suited to different food sources. On what Pacific archipelago did Charles Darwin observe these birds?

It retains a definite volume but changes shape to match its container. This state of matter can form when a gas condenses, and cohesion between its molecules can help produce droplets. What is this state?

In a liquid, this phenomenon can draw fluid upward through a narrow tube against gravity, as when water rises through plant xylem. It results from the interplay of adhesion to the tube walls and cohesion within the fluid. What is this phenomenon?

This aqueous solution forms when the colorless gas hydrogen chloride dissolves in water, and it ionizes almost completely into hydronium and chloride ions. Parietal cells secrete it into gastric juice, and industry uses it to remove oxide scale from steel. What is this corrosive aqueous solution called?

When hydrochloric acid is mixed with nitric acid in a traditional 3:1 volume ratio, the resulting corrosive reagent can dissolve gold, which resists either acid alone. What Latin name is given to this mixture?
Which trauma-related psychiatric disorder can follow exposure to a shocking or threatening event and involve persistent intrusive memories, avoidance of reminders, and heightened arousal?

For post-traumatic stress disorder, which psychotherapy pairs recalling traumatic memories with guided side-to-side eye movements or other bilateral stimulation to help reduce distress associated with those memories?
At the center of the Milky Way, stellar orbits around a compact radio source reveal roughly four million solar masses packed into a tiny region. What is the name of this supermassive black hole?

In 2022, a planet-scale network of millimeter and submillimeter radio observatories released the first image of Sagittarius A*, revealing emission around its shadow. What is the name of this collaboration?

A recurring climate pattern features unusually warm waters across the central and eastern tropical Pacific and shifts weather far beyond that basin. Its warm phase can bring wetter conditions to the southern United States while contributing to drier conditions in parts of Southeast Asia. What is this phase called?
El Niño is one phase of a recurring coupled ocean–atmosphere pattern that also has a cool phase called La Niña. What is the name of this larger pattern, often abbreviated ENSO?

Unlike compressional P-type seismic motion, these transverse seismic disturbances move material perpendicular to their direction of travel. Because they cannot pass through liquids, they create a shadow zone beyond Earth’s liquid outer core; what are they called?

S waves are absent from a broad region on the far side of Earth because they cannot cross this liquid layer beneath the mantle. Motion in this layer is also central to the dynamo theory of Earth’s magnetic field; what is the layer called?

In a classification system developed by Edward Henry, loops, whorls, and arches are recorded as identifying patterns on each digit. Modern biometric sensors also compare these ridge arrangements to verify a person’s identity. What are these patterns called?

Forensic examiners use this chemical reagent to reveal latent fingerprints on porous surfaces. It reacts with amino acids in residue left by the skin, producing a purple compound known as Ruhemann’s purple. What is the reagent?

This human ability turns intended words into meaningful spoken utterances through coordinated breathing and movements of the vocal folds, tongue, and lips. Its neural basis involves language-related regions such as Broca’s and Wernicke’s areas, and impairment can occur in aphasia. What is this ability called?

In discussions of Speech and aphasia, damage to a region in the dominant frontal lobe is associated with slow, effortful, nonfluent output, often with comprehension more intact than expression. Named for a French physician who studied patients with this pattern, which brain region is it?

A standardized measure of spark-ignition fuel compares its resistance to knocking under compression against reference fuels, one assigned 100 and another assigned 0. In the United States, the pump figure commonly averages results from research and motor tests; what is this measure called?
U.S. Octane rating labels combine results from two standardized tests. Which test is conducted at a higher air temperature and engine speed than the research test?

Unlike classical tracks around a nucleus, these quantum-mechanical states describe where an electron is likely to be found, with the squared magnitude of a wavefunction giving the spatial probability distribution. Their familiar types are labeled s, p, d, and f.
In the description of atomic orbitals, which numerical label, denoted by ℓ, determines the subshell type and shape? Its values 0, 1, 2, and 3 correspond to s, p, d, and f, respectively.

Introduced globally by Bayer in 1899 after a pure, stable preparation was developed in 1897, this medicine relieves pain and fever and inhibits platelet aggregation. Its antiplatelet action also supports its use in reducing the risk of some clot-related cardiovascular events. What is this drug commonly called?

Aspirin’s synthetic history began before Bayer’s later commercial production: in 1853, this French chemist first prepared acetylsalicylic acid, though the product was not yet made in a pure, stable form. Who was he?

Aspirin is generally avoided in children with certain viral infections because its use has been associated with this rare, serious condition involving brain and liver swelling. What is this condition called?

This rocky world is the fourth planet from the Sun and has a thin atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide. Its northern plains, cratered southern highlands, and planet-wide dust storms have made it a major focus of robotic exploration. What planet is it?
Mars’s first successful spacecraft flyby occurred in 1965, when this NASA probe returned the first close-up images of the planet. What was the spacecraft’s name?

On Mars, this immense canyon system stretches about 4,000 kilometers near the equator, east of the Tharsis volcanic region. Its name derives from the spacecraft program whose ninth mission mapped the planet from orbit. What is this feature called?
Mars’s Tharsis region contains a shield volcano that rises about 21.9 kilometers above the surrounding terrain and is the largest volcano in the Solar System. What is its name?
Which metallic element has atomic number 28? Its close chemical resemblance to iron makes it difficult to distinguish during qualitative analysis.

In qualitative analysis, which organic reagent is added to an ammoniacal solution containing nickel ions to produce a characteristic rose-red precipitate? It is commonly used as a specific test for Nickel.

In Newton’s second law, the net force on an object equals its mass multiplied by this vector quantity. It is the change in velocity per unit time and can occur when an object changes direction, even if its speed stays constant. What quantity is described?
Acceleration is measured in a derived SI unit that describes how velocity changes each second. Its symbol is m/s²; what is the unit’s name?

Launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957, this polished metal sphere weighed about 83.6 kilograms and sent repeating radio pulses that could be detected on Earth. It was the first human-made object to orbit Earth, and its success is often treated as the start of the Space Age. What satellite was it?

Sputnik 1 was launched while scientists across dozens of countries coordinated observations of Earth and its atmosphere under a program that ran from July 1957 through December 1958. What was this named scientific initiative?
What phenomenon describes the continual, irregular movement of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid, caused by collisions with the fluid’s molecules?
Which physicist’s 1905 theoretical analysis of Brownian motion related a suspended particle’s mean-square displacement to elapsed time and provided evidence for the molecular nature of matter?
In circuit analysis, this scalar quantity compares electric potential at two points and is measured in volts. Ohm’s law gives it as the product of current and resistance.
Voltage is measured in this SI derived unit, equal to one joule per coulomb. Its symbol is V.
Voltage across a circuit component is measured with this instrument connected in parallel. Ideally, its internal resistance is very high so it draws negligible current.
The signed sum of voltage rises and drops around a closed circuit loop is zero under this rule. It expresses conservation of energy in circuit analysis.

For ideal, steady flow of an incompressible, frictionless fluid along a streamline, this relation balances pressure, kinetic, and gravitational potential energy per unit volume. At constant height, it predicts that faster-moving fluid has lower static pressure; what principle is this?

Aircraft use this instrument to infer airspeed by comparing pressure measured at a forward-facing opening with the surrounding static pressure. Bernoulli’s principle helps explain the relationship between the pressure difference and fluid speed; what is the instrument called?

For a fixed amount of gas held at constant pressure, this law says volume varies directly with absolute temperature, so doubling the temperature in kelvins doubles the volume. It is named for a French physicist and ballooning pioneer who studied hydrogen-filled balloons; what gas law is it?

Charles's Law requires temperature to be expressed on this absolute scale when using the direct volume–temperature relationship. Its zero is absolute zero, and its degree-sized units match the Celsius scale; what is it called?

In a binary mixture, a special composition can melt at a lower temperature than either pure component. At that composition, the mixture changes between solid and liquid at a single temperature; what is this type of mixture system called?

The eutectic system formed by tin and the dense metal with atomic number 82 has a special composition that melts at about 183 °C, below the melting point of either pure metal. What conventional solder recipe, specified by mass percentage, corresponds to that composition?

What logarithmic unit is commonly used to express sound levels as well as signal gain or attenuation in electronics? For power ratios, an increase of ten units corresponds to a tenfold increase in power.
In acoustics, the Decibel scale is often used for a quantity calculated from an acoustic wave’s RMS amplitude relative to the standard 20-micropascal reference in air. What is this quantity called?

These periodic changes in sea level are driven mainly by the Moon’s gravity, with the Sun also contributing. Their ranges are greatest around new and full moons, producing the spring variety, and smaller during neap periods. What are these ocean movements called?
Tides reach their greatest ranges when the Sun, Earth, and Moon lie roughly along one line, near either a new or full moon. What is this astronomical alignment called?

This proposed extension of particle physics pairs each elementary boson with a fermionic counterpart and each fermion with a bosonic counterpart, with the paired particles differing in spin by one-half unit. It has also been studied as a way to stabilize the Higgs mass, though no such counterpart has yet been observed. What is the name of this symmetry?

In supersymmetry, cancellations between bosonic and fermionic quantum-loop contributions can help keep the Higgs mass near the electroweak scale despite much larger fundamental scales. Which naturalness puzzle about the enormous gap between the electroweak and Planck scales is this mechanism intended to address?

Which set of three principles describes planets moving in ellipses with the Sun at one focus, sweeping out equal areas in equal time intervals, and having orbital-period squares proportional to the cubes of their orbital sizes?

In Kepler’s Laws of Planetary Motion, the equal-area rule says that a line from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times. What conserved orbital quantity, commonly symbolized by L, accounts for this rule?

This body is our planet’s only natural satellite and takes about 29.5 days to pass through its familiar sequence of phases as seen from our planet. Its rotation is tidally synchronized with its orbit, so the same near side generally faces us. What is it?
In 1969, Apollo 11’s landing site at roughly 0.7° north and 23.5° east on Earth’s Moon was located in a broad, dark basalt plain on the near side. What is the plain’s Latin name?
In December 1968, this mission carried the first crew to orbit Earth’s Moon. Its crew included Frank Borman, Jim Lovell, and William Anders. What mission was it?

A leading explanation for Earth’s Moon’s formation proposes that a Mars-sized protoplanet struck the young Earth around 4.5 billion years ago, casting debris into orbit that later assembled into the satellite. What name is commonly assigned to the hypothesized impactor?

Gravity surveys of Earth’s Moon have found localized positive gravitational anomalies over several large impact basins; dense basaltic fill can perturb low-orbiting spacecraft. What short geophysical term describes these anomalies?

In plants, this unbranched structural polysaccharide consists of glucose units joined by β(1→4) linkages, with alternating glucose units flipped over to create extended chains. The chains hydrogen-bond into bundles that reinforce plant cell walls and are abundant in wood and paper. What is this substance?
In plant cell walls, neighboring cellulose chains align and hydrogen-bond together to form these strong bundles, which help the walls resist pulling forces. What are these bundles called?
A power-station fuel can be ground into fine particles, combined with water, and pumped over long distances through dedicated pipelines. What is this pumpable suspension called?
In February 1972, a coal-waste impoundment failed in Logan County, West Virginia, and a destructive surge containing coal slurry killed 125 people. What is this disaster known as?
What ideal reversible heat-engine process, consisting of two isothermal and two adiabatic steps, establishes the maximum possible efficiency for engines operating between hot and cold reservoirs?
The Carnot cycle takes its name from which French engineer and physicist whose 1824 treatise *Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire* laid foundational analysis of heat engines?
What endogenous timing system runs on an approximately 24-hour cycle and helps regulate recurring patterns of sleepiness and wakefulness?

The circadian rhythm is synchronized largely by a small structure in the hypothalamus that lies above the optic chiasm and receives light-related signals from the retina. What is this structure, often called the body’s master clock?

Compton and Rayleigh are names attached to two forms of this physical process, in which particles or electromagnetic radiation are deflected from their original paths through interactions with matter. What general process is being described?

In the context of Scattering, the process named for Lord Rayleigh redirects shorter visible wavelengths more strongly than longer red wavelengths as sunlight passes through Earth’s atmosphere. What color does this make a clear daytime sky appear?

When comparing ecosystems, an ecologist may tally how many distinct kinds of organisms occur without weighting them by relative abundance. This component of biodiversity is often considered alongside evenness; what is it called?
Species richness counts how many kinds occur, while this index also incorporates each kind’s proportional abundance and is commonly expressed as −Σpᵢ ln pᵢ. What is the index called?

These species may be atoms, molecules, or ions, and a dot beside a formula can indicate their defining electronic feature. Their unpaired electrons make many of them reactive and allow them to be detected by EPR spectroscopy; what are they called?
When a covalent bond breaks to form free radicals, what type of process divides the bonding electron pair evenly, leaving one electron with each fragment?

These repetitive DNA-protein structures cap the ends of chromosomes, helping prevent chromosome damage or fusion. They typically become shorter with repeated cell divisions, and their loss can limit further division.

Telomeres shorten as many cells divide, but an enzyme can lengthen them by adding repeated DNA sequences to chromosome ends using its own RNA template. What is this enzyme, which is active in many germ cells and cancer cells?

In this theoretical framework, elementary particles are not treated as dimensionless points; their properties arise from different vibrational modes of tiny one-dimensional entities. What framework is this?

String theory has been used to account for features of the thermodynamics of certain extremely compact astronomical objects. What are these objects, whose gravity creates a boundary beyond which light cannot escape?

Born Augusta Ada Byron and later known by a title inherited through marriage, this British mathematician wrote extensive notes on Charles Babbage’s proposed Analytical Engine. Those notes included instructions for a calculation regarded as an early computer program. By what name is this pioneer of computing best known?

In Note G of Ada Lovelace’s notes on Charles Babbage’s Analytical Engine, she set out operations to calculate a particular sequence of rational numbers used in formulas for sums of powers. What sequence was the algorithm intended to produce?

In this separation technique, a mixture passes through a porous medium that lets the fluid through while retaining suspended solid particles. In laboratory settings, filter paper is commonly used, and applying vacuum can speed the process.

During vacuum-assisted filtration, what piece of laboratory glassware has a broad, straight-sided cylindrical cup above a perforated plate for supporting filter paper, and connects to a side-arm flask?

Which naturally occurring gas is the simplest hydrocarbon and is released by sources such as wetlands and livestock digestion? Over a 100-year period, its heat-trapping effect is substantially greater than carbon dioxide’s.
Methane contains one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms. Which standard molecular formula summarizes this composition?

What is the apparent deflection of moving air, water, or other objects when viewed from Earth’s rotating surface? It turns motion to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.
The Coriolis effect is named for the French scientist who published a mathematical expression for the associated force in 1835. What was his name?
The Coriolis effect produces horizontal deflection that is strongest near the poles and decreases to zero at a particular latitude line. What is that line called?

This two-carbon organic alcohol has a terminal hydroxyl group and is the intoxicating alcohol in beer, wine, and spirits. It is also used as a solvent and fuel, and yeast can produce it by fermenting sugars. What is this substance?

When ordinary distillation is used to separate ethanol from water, the mixture reaches a composition that boils without changing the ratio of its vapor and liquid, preventing complete separation. What is this kind of mixture called?
This mammalian order includes lemurs, tarsiers, bush babies, monkeys, apes, and humans. Many of its members have grasping hands or feet and forward-facing eyes. What is this order?

Within Primates, this group is native to Central and South America and is distinguished from its African and Asian relatives by widely spaced, outward-facing nostrils. Some members, such as capuchins, have prehensile tails. What group is it?

Introduced in 1955, this preventive medical intervention included a formulation made with inactivated poliovirus. It was developed to protect against a disease that can cause paralysis; what is this intervention called?
The polio vaccine announced as effective in 1955 used inactivated poliovirus. Which American physician developed that formulation and led the large field trial that tested it?

In the order Diptera, adults characteristically have one functional pair of wings, while their hindwings are reduced to balancing organs called halteres. What common name is used for insects in this order?

In a poem by a reclusive 19th-century American poet, a Fly’s “Blue—uncertain—stumbling Buzz” breaks the “Stillness in the Room” as the speaker dies. Which poet, whose works are often identified by their opening lines, wrote it?

This cellular molecular machine consists of small and large subunits containing ribosomal RNA and proteins. It reads codons on a messenger RNA template and links amino acids into a polypeptide chain. What is it?
Within a ribosome, this RNA molecule carries codons that provide the template for translation. It is transcribed from DNA and read as the ribosome moves along it. What type of RNA is it?
The ribosome was first observed in 1955 by this Romanian-American cell biologist, known for his research on cell ultrastructure. Who was he?
These small, soft-bodied insects pierce plants and feed on their sap. Many are tended by ants, which collect a sugary substance they excrete; what are these insects commonly called?
In the relationship between aphids and ants, what is the sugar-rich liquid that aphids excrete after feeding on plant sap and that ants collect?

Inside each cylinder of a reciprocating engine, combustion pressure pushes this close-fitting component along the bore, while rings help seal the gap and a connecting rod carries its motion onward. What is this component?
In an engine that uses a piston, each connecting rod applies force to offset crankpins on this shaft. Its rotation converts the piston’s repeated linear strokes into rotary motion.
This quantity arises from the weight of the air above a location and is about 101.3 kilopascals at sea level. What force per unit area generally decreases as altitude increases?
Atmospheric pressure is commonly measured by an instrument whose classic mercury design balances a column of liquid in a glass tube against the surrounding air. What is this instrument called?

This is an organized collection of linked pages and related resources, usually grouped under one domain name. It is distinct from a single page displayed in a browser and from the server that hosts the content. What is this collection called?

On a website, this address can identify a resource and may include a scheme such as HTTPS, a domain name, and a path. Hyperlinks can point to it, but it is the locator rather than the clickable link itself; what is it called?

In the relation E = hν, a photon’s energy is proportional to its frequency, with h as the proportionality factor. This universal constant played a central role in quantizing blackbody radiation. What is it?
In quantum mechanics, dividing Planck's constant by a particle’s momentum gives a length scale associated with its matter-wave behavior. What is this quantity?
What is the name for an interconnected network of conductors and devices that provides a complete path through which charge can move from a source such as a battery?
In an electric circuit, what arrangement connects components one after another along a single branch, so the same current passes through each component?

This elementary subatomic particle has a negative electric charge and a mass about 1/1,836 that of a proton. In atoms, its quantum states help determine chemical properties, and when mobile in a metal it carries electric current. What particle is it?

In 1927, a beam of electrons scattered from a nickel crystal produced intensity peaks consistent with the wave behavior predicted by de Broglie. What is this demonstration of electron diffraction called?
An atom’s electron or electrons in its outermost occupied shell are especially available to be shared or transferred during chemical reactions. What are these electrons called?

To measure the elementary charge carried by an electron, researchers balanced the electric force on tiny charged liquid droplets suspended between parallel plates against gravity. What is this early-20th-century measurement known as?

What laboratory technique separates or characterizes materials by spinning samples and observing how their components sediment? It can distinguish ribosomal subunits by their sedimentation behavior rather than by measuring their physical dimensions.

In centrifugation, what named measure reports a particle’s sedimentation coefficient, as in the values assigned to ribosomal subunits? Despite describing sedimentation behavior, it is not a measure of physical size.
This large semiaquatic reptile is distinguished from alligators by its generally narrower, V-shaped snout. When its mouth is closed, its lower teeth remain visible. What is it?

In Egyptian mythology, this creature has the head of a crocodile, the forequarters of a lion, and the hindquarters of a hippopotamus. It waits to devour the souls of those judged unworthy during the weighing of the heart. What is its name?

What is the collective anatomical name for four paired, air-filled cavities in the frontal, ethmoid, sphenoid, and maxillary bones? These cavities connect with the nasal cavity and are lined with mucous membrane.
What condition is inflammation of the paranasal sinuses, often causing nasal congestion and facial pressure or headache?

At fixed temperature and pressure, this thermodynamic potential is calculated as enthalpy minus temperature times entropy. A negative change in it indicates that a process is spontaneous under those conditions. What is this quantity?
In the defining relation for Gibbs free energy, ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, the state-function term represented by H is also defined as internal energy plus pressure times volume. What is this quantity called?

For Gibbs free energy, the relation ΔG° = −RT ln K links the standard reaction free-energy change to a dimensionless quantity formed from product and reactant activities, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. What is K called?

Gibbs free energy sets the upper limit on useful work, apart from pressure–volume work, that a closed system can deliver at fixed temperature and pressure. That limit can be attained only through what kind of process?
This Hungarian-born mathematician emigrated to the United States, made foundational contributions to game theory, and helped establish the stored-program design of computers. Who was he?

John von Neumann's report helped shape the design of an early electronic computer developed at the University of Pennsylvania as a successor to ENIAC. It used binary arithmetic and stored-program control; which machine was it?
This naturally occurring methylxanthine is found in coffee and tea, and it promotes alertness in part by blocking receptors for a sleep-promoting neuromodulator. What is its common name?
In 1819, after Johann Wolfgang von Goethe encouraged him to investigate coffee beans, this German chemist isolated caffeine. Who was he?

In a Rankine-cycle power plant, this working fluid is produced by heating water in a boiler and then expanded through turbine blades to turn a generator. What gaseous form of water transfers the heat into mechanical motion?

Steam engines were already being used to pump water from mines when this Scottish engineer devised a separate condenser that greatly reduced fuel consumption. His improvements helped make steam power practical for wider industrial use; who was he?

In chemical kinetics, this quantity describes how quickly reactant concentrations decrease or product concentrations increase as a process proceeds. It is measured by concentration change per unit time.

In Reaction Rate kinetics, which classification is indicated when a plot of the natural logarithm of a reactant’s concentration against time is a straight line, and the half-life does not depend on the initial concentration?

In solution chemistry, the law of mass action commonly uses a concentration scale that divides the amount of dissolved substance, measured in moles, by the total solution volume in liters. What is this concentration measure called?

Unlike molarity, which uses liters of total solution, what concentration scale divides moles of solute by kilograms of solvent? It is useful in calculations involving temperature changes, such as boiling-point elevation.

These membrane-bound structures can be wrapped in clathrin coats built from triskelion-shaped proteins. Their surface SNAREs help them recognize and fuse with target membranes as they transport cargo or store substances. What are they?

Vesicles carrying proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum can deliver them to this organelle, where cargo is modified, sorted, and packaged for onward transport. Its name honors the Italian biologist who first described it. What is this organelle?

This clastic sedimentary rock is made mainly of sand-sized grains, typically about 0.0625 to 2 millimeters across, that have been compacted and cemented together. What is this rock, which commonly forms prominent cliffs and mesas in desert landscapes?
During sandstone formation, loose grains are buried, compacted, and bound together by mineral cement. What is the general geological process that turns loose sediment into solid sedimentary rock?

This New York-born theoretical physicist earned his doctorate at Princeton and shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physics with Julian Schwinger and Sin-Itiro Tomonaga for work on quantum electrodynamics. Who was he?

Richard Feynman served on this presidential panel convened after the 1986 loss of the Space Shuttle Challenger. Its investigation highlighted the gap between NASA management’s reliability estimates and engineers’ concerns about the shuttle’s solid rocket booster O-rings. What was this panel called?

Which neurodevelopmental condition involves differences in social communication and interaction alongside restricted or repetitive behaviors and interests? Its traits and support needs can vary widely from person to person.
Which Austrian-born psychoanalyst promoted the now-discredited claim that autism spectrum disorder resulted from emotionally cold parenting, an idea associated with the phrase “refrigerator mothers”?

What broad extractive activity recovers a valuable metal from mined ore or from placer deposits in river gravel? In California, a major boom in this work followed James Marshall’s 1848 discovery at Sutter’s Mill.
In gold mining, what water-fed trough uses riffles to catch dense particles while gravel and sediment wash through? It can process a steady flow of material, unlike a hand-held pan.
Which disease is characterized by painful swelling of the lymph nodes, producing lumps called buboes? It is commonly transmitted to people through the bites of infected fleas.
Bubonic plague is caused by a bacterium first isolated in Hong Kong in 1894 by Alexandre Yersin. What is its current scientific name?

In diploid inheritance, a version of a gene may be carried without affecting the visible trait when paired with a dominant version. What class of gene versions typically produces its characteristic phenotype only when two copies are present?

In experiments involving recessive alleles, this American geneticist studied fruit flies and showed that a gene for white eyes was linked to the X chromosome. His work helped establish that genes are carried on chromosomes; who was he?

China’s first independently conducted Mars mission launched in 2020 with an orbiter, lander, and rover aboard a single spacecraft. It entered Mars orbit in February 2021 and later delivered a rover to the planet’s surface; what was the mission called?
Tianwen-1’s lander touched down in the southern part of Utopia Planitia in May 2021. What was the name of the solar-powered rover it delivered to the Martian surface?

Produced by mammary glands during lactation, this nutrient-rich fluid nourishes newborns and supplies them with immune protection. Oxytocin can trigger its let-down reflex, while prolactin supports its production. What is this substance?
Human breast milk contains an antibody that helps protect an infant by coating mucosal surfaces and providing passive immunity. Which antibody is especially associated with this protection?

When two surfaces slide past one another, a contact force acts opposite their relative motion. In the usual model, its magnitude is the product of the normal force and a coefficient determined by the surfaces; what is this force called?
For kinetic friction, the standard equation relates the force’s magnitude to the normal force by multiplying it by a dimensionless factor. What is that factor called?

Which laboratory instrument uses a sealed, rigid vessel immersed in a water bath to measure heat released by combustion or another reaction? Since the vessel cannot expand, the measurement is made under fixed-volume conditions.

In a bomb calorimeter, water absorbs energy from the sealed reaction vessel, and its temperature increase can be converted to energy using a property measured in joules per gram per degree Celsius. What is this property called?

Which SI base unit of mass is used in molality to express the mass of the solvent rather than the volume of the solution? Its symbol is kg, and its modern definition is linked to a fixed value of a fundamental constant.
Since 2019, the kilogram has been defined by fixing the numerical value of which fundamental constant, measured in joule-seconds? This definition replaced reliance on a physical metal prototype.

In the traditional computer memory hierarchy, this persistent magnetic storage device sits below main memory and stores data on rotating rigid media. Its three-word name is commonly abbreviated HDD; what is it?
Inside a Hard Disk Drive, data is recorded magnetically on one or more rigid circular disks that rotate around a central spindle. What is each recording disk called?
A mixture contains a weak acid and its conjugate base, and can absorb small additions of acid or base with little change in pH. What is this mixture called?
For a buffer solution, this equation calculates pH using the acid’s pKa and the logarithm of the conjugate-base concentration divided by the weak-acid concentration. What is the equation called?
Which silvery rare-earth metal has atomic number 39? Its compounds are used in advanced ceramics, including materials developed for high-temperature superconductivity.

Which ceramic copper-oxide superconductor made from Yttrium, barium, copper, and oxygen became famous for superconducting above liquid nitrogen’s boiling point? It is commonly known by a four-letter acronym.

An ecosystem can support only a limited number of individuals of a species before competition for food, water, or space slows population growth. What is the environment-dependent maximum population that can be sustained over time called?

Ecological carrying capacity appears as a constant in the logistic population-growth model, where the model predicts zero net growth when the population reaches that limit. Which letter conventionally represents it?
What term describes an interaction that pulls two objects toward each other, as happens between opposite electric charges or unlike magnetic poles?

For an attractive force between two point charges, which electrostatic law says the force’s magnitude is proportional to the product of their charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them?
In some vertebrates, including cats and foxes, the eye’s central opening is elongated instead of round. This shape can narrow sharply in bright light; what is this eye feature called?
Slit pupils in animals such as cats can help reduce an optical flaw in which different wavelengths of light do not focus at the same point. What is this flaw called?

This nonmetal is element 53 and the heaviest stable member of the halogen family; when heated, its solid forms a vivid violet vapor. The body needs it to make thyroid hormones, and it turns starch-containing mixtures dark blue. What element is it?

In 1811, a French chemist and saltpeter manufacturer noticed violet fumes while treating seaweed ash with sulfuric acid. His work is credited with identifying iodine as a previously unknown element; who was he?

An aqueous mixture of iodine and potassium iodide has long been used to test for starch, turning deep blue-black when starch is present. What is this reagent commonly called, after the 19th-century French physician associated with it?

This radioactive isotope of iodine is taken up by thyroid tissue and used to treat overactive thyroid cells and some thyroid cancers. It emits beta particles and has a physical half-life of about eight days; which isotope is it?

After a radiotracer emits positively charged particles that meet ordinary electrons, paired gamma rays are detected and used to reconstruct a three-dimensional map of tracer uptake. This functional imaging technique helps measure metabolism and visualize biological processes in the body; what is it called?

In positron emission tomography, this radiotracer combines a glucose analog with fluorine-18 and is commonly used to map glucose metabolism. Because many tumors take up glucose avidly, areas with increased uptake can appear as areas of increased signal; what is the tracer’s standard abbreviation?

This Austrian monk carried out controlled crosses of pea plants at St. Thomas’s Abbey in Brno and published his results in an 1866 paper on plant hybrids. His experiments established principles now known as segregation and independent assortment. Who was he?

In Gregor Mendel’s account of inheritance, what term describes a version of a gene whose effect is hidden when paired with a dominant version and appears in an organism’s observable traits only when both inherited copies are alike?

In mammals, this sex produces ova and commonly supports developing offspring through gestation, placental exchange, and lactation. These reproductive roles distinguish it from the sex that produces sperm. What is this sex?
In discussions of female sex and unequal reproductive costs, which evolutionary biologist introduced the concept of parental investment in a 1972 paper on sexual selection?

What physical quantity describes how heavy a single molecule is, rather than an entire sample? It is commonly expressed in daltons, while practical chemical measurements may report it in grams per mole.
Chemists use a non-SI unit abbreviated Da to report molecular mass at the scale of individual molecules. What is this unit called?

In a paper chromatography demonstration, soluble colorants in an ink sample can separate into distinct bands as solvent rises through the paper. What class of substances is widely used to impart color to textiles, paper, food, and hair?

A mixture of Dyes is spotted near the base of a cellulose sheet, and a solvent climbs through it, carrying components different distances to reveal separate bands. What planar separation technique is being used?
This relatively small class of celestial bodies includes ordinary main-sequence members, compact white remnants, and brown or hypothetical black forms. What is this broad class called?
Among the different forms of a dwarf star, what kind is Sirius B, the faint, compact companion to Sirius A whose gravitational effect was inferred by Friedrich Bessel?

In this coordination-chemistry model, surrounding ligands exert electrostatic forces that split the energy levels of a metal ion’s d orbitals. It is used to explain properties such as the colors and magnetic behavior of transition-metal complexes. What is the model called?

In Crystal Field Theory, six ligands occupy positions along three perpendicular axes around a metal ion, producing lower-lying t₂g orbitals and higher-lying eᵍ orbitals. What is the separation between these two orbital sets called?
In clinical laboratories, this instrument holds blood tubes in a rotor and spins them rapidly so denser blood cells separate from the liquid portion. What is this device called?

A centrifuge can separate this pale-yellow liquid fraction of anticoagulated blood from blood cells and platelets. Unlike serum, it still contains clotting proteins such as fibrinogen; what is this fraction called?
This lobe-finned fish lineage was known from fossils and believed to have vanished about 60 million years ago until a living specimen was identified in South Africa in 1938. What fish is it?

When a fishing trawler brought an unusual coelacanth to East London in 1938, the local museum curator preserved it and alerted ichthyologist J.L.B. Smith. Which curator’s discovery brought the supposedly extinct lineage to scientific attention?

Born in Vienna in 1844, this Austrian physicist used probability and molecular microstates to explain thermodynamic behavior and helped establish statistical mechanics. His 1877 combinatorial work treated equilibrium as the most probable macroscopic state; who was he?

In Ludwig Boltzmann’s kinetic theory of gases, this result shows that a quantity associated with the molecular velocity distribution decreases or remains constant under collisions, providing a statistical account of the approach to equilibrium. What is this result called?

This selectively permeable boundary separates the cytoplasm from the extracellular fluid and is built mainly from a phospholipid bilayer. Its proteins help regulate transport and communication between the interior and surrounding environment. What is this structure?
In animal cells, the cell membrane contains this sterol interspersed among phospholipids, helping moderate the bilayer’s fluidity as temperature changes. What molecule is this?
The cell membrane’s main bilayer-forming molecules have water-attracting heads and water-repelling tails, so they arrange into two layers in an aqueous environment. What class of molecules are they?
The cell membrane is described by this model, which portrays its lipid bilayer as laterally mobile and its proteins as embedded in or associated with it. What is the name of this model?
Water crosses the cell membrane especially rapidly through these selective channel proteins, which form pores for water molecules rather than pumping them with ATP. What protein family is this?

In a water molecule, the central oxygen atom is bonded to two hydrogen atoms and has two lone pairs, giving the molecule a bond angle of about 104.5°. What is the name of this molecular shape, with the two bonds angled away from the central atom?
Bent molecular geometry can be predicted by a model that treats electron domains around a central atom as repelling one another. What is this model called?

For a neutral atom in the gas phase, this threshold is associated with removing its least tightly bound electron and leaving a singly charged ion. For a hydrogen-like atom, the Bohr-model value scales with the square of nuclear charge; what atomic quantity is it?

Among neighboring period-2 elements, this quantity is higher for the atom with a half-filled 2p subshell than for oxygen, whose paired 2p electrons repel one another and make an electron easier to remove. Which element is it, in this comparison of first ionization energy?

These self-gravitating spheres of hot plasma shine by releasing energy from nuclear fusion, usually converting hydrogen into helium during their active lives. Their properties and evolutionary stages are often plotted on a Hertzsprung–Russell diagram. What are these objects called?
Among stars visible from Earth at night, this one is the brightest. It lies in Canis Major and has a well-known white-dwarf companion designated B. What is its name?
This constellation is recognized by a three-star asterism known as its belt. Its prominent stars include the red supergiant Betelgeuse and the blue-white Rigel. Which constellation is it?

Mitochondria and chloroplasts have bacterial-like features, including their own DNA, and this evolutionary explanation proposes that they began as free-living bacteria incorporated into ancestral cells. What is this theory called?
Which American evolutionary biologist made a landmark case for Endosymbiotic Theory in the 1967 paper “On the Origin of Mitosing Cells” and later became one of its most prominent advocates?

This orthopedic principle explains why bones can become denser along lines of repeated loading and lose mass when mechanical loading is reduced. What named law describes this adaptation of bone structure to stress?
Under Wolff's law, repeated loading can influence the balance between bone formation and resorption. Which bone-resorbing cell type breaks down bone tissue?

This renewable resource draws on Earth’s interior warmth, accessed through wells that bring hot water or steam to the surface. It can generate electricity or supply warmth directly to buildings and industrial processes. What is it called?

This system uses the ground’s relatively stable shallow temperature, drawing warmth indoors during winter and moving indoor warmth back into the ground in summer. What building climate-control technology uses geothermal energy this way?
This heavy noble gas has atomic number 54 and was long considered chemically inert. It became the first element in its group shown to form a stable compound. Which element is it?

In 1962, chemist Neil Bartlett reacted this noble gas with platinum hexafluoride, producing an ionic compound that challenged the idea that noble gases could not form compounds. What compound resulted from the reaction with Xenon?

This was the first U.S. effort to send people into space, selecting seven military test pilots as astronauts. Its first crewed flight sent Alan Shepard on a suborbital journey in May 1961. What was this initiative called?
In the Mercury Program, what was the name of the spacecraft Alan Shepard flew on May 5, 1961, during the first American crewed spaceflight?
What simple machine has an inclined plane wrapped helically around a cylinder, converting rotation into linear motion? Besides fastening materials, versions of it can lift liquids or heavy loads.
A screw can serve not only as a fastener but also as a water elevator. What ancient water-lifting device uses a rotating helix within a trough to carry water upward?

What spectroscopic method uses microwave absorption in a swept magnetic field to characterize materials whose atoms or molecules have unpaired spins? Its signal appears when the field tunes the spin-state energy separation to the microwave frequency.

In electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, what highly reactive atoms or molecules with unpaired electrons are being detected? Stable examples include TEMPO and Fremy’s salt, and their single-electron bond cleavage is commonly depicted with fishhook arrows.
What is the name for the temperature pattern in which a densely built metropolitan area is warmer than nearby rural surroundings because pavement, roofs, and buildings absorb and store solar energy?
In studies of the Urban Heat Island Effect, what term describes the fraction of incoming sunlight that a surface reflects, helping explain why dark asphalt absorbs more solar energy than a pale roof?

This circuit component has two nearby conductors separated by an insulating material, or dielectric. When charged, its conductors hold equal and opposite charges, and energy is stored in the electric field between them. What is the component?
A capacitor’s ability to store charge for a given voltage is defined by the relation C = Q/V. What SI unit measures this quantity and equals one coulomb per volt?

For a repeating motion or wave, this quantity counts complete cycles per unit time and is the reciprocal of the period. Its SI unit is the hertz, with one hertz equal to one cycle per second; what is it?

Frequency is the reciprocal of this quantity, which gives the time needed for one complete cycle or oscillation. In SI, it is measured in seconds and commonly represented by T; what is this interval called?
What cardiovascular measurement is routinely written as a pair of values in millimeters of mercury, such as 120/80, corresponding to ventricular contraction and relaxation?

During short-term regulation of blood pressure, stretch-sensitive baroreceptors in the carotid sinus and aortic arch send signals to this central nervous system region. It consists of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata; what is it?

A global biotic crisis about 66 million years ago, at the end of the final period of the Mesozoic and the start of the first period of the Cenozoic, wiped out non-avian dinosaurs while birds survived. What is the name of this boundary-marking event?

The Cretaceous–Paleogene Extinction Event is strongly linked to a roughly 180-kilometer impact structure buried beneath Mexico’s northern Yucatán Peninsula, with a ring of cenotes tracing part of its rim. What is the name of this impact structure?

What laboratory practice uses dyes or other reagents to make cells, tissue sections, or microorganisms easier to see and distinguish under a microscope? It can reveal structures that would otherwise blend into the background.

In biological staining, which silver-based method uses potassium dichromate and silver nitrate to darken a small subset of neurons, revealing their complete outlines and branching processes within crowded nervous tissue?

Among the six flavors of one family of fundamental particles, this third-generation member is denoted by t and has a mass far greater than the others. Its lifetime is so brief that it decays before it can bind into a hadron.
The top quark decays so quickly that it does not bind with other quarks to form a hadron. What is the name of the process of binding quarks into hadrons?

In neutron-star interiors, competition between the strong force and electrostatic repulsion is predicted to make ultra-dense matter form rods, slabs, tubes, and bubbles instead of ordinary spherical nuclei. What is the collective name for these exotic phases?
Nuclear Pasta is predicted to occupy a transitional layer of a neutron star, beneath its thin surface layer of nuclei and electrons and above the uniform-matter core. What is this layer called?

During World War II, a U.S. military research effort explored placing trained birds in a missile nose cone so they could peck at an image of a target and help guide the weapon. What was this program called?

Which psychologist devised and led Project Pigeon, applying operant conditioning to train pigeons to peck at projected target images? He is also known for research on learning and behavior using an operant-conditioning chamber.
In a colony of Apis mellifera, this male caste develops from an unfertilized egg and has only one set of chromosomes. Unlike female workers and queens, it lacks a stinger; what is this bee called?
A honey bee drone develops from an unfertilized egg and carries one set of chromosomes rather than paired sets. What is this one-set chromosome condition called?
What geological material forms when mineral or organic particles accumulate and are then compacted or cemented together? Its strata can preserve fossils and provide a record of past environments.
In a discussion of sedimentary rock and soil formation, what is the name of the fertile soil layer commonly designated the A horizon? It typically contains abundant humus and lies near the surface.

On Borneo, DDT-driven losses of these insect-hunting animals helped caterpillar numbers rise. Many members belong to Hymenoptera and build papery nests from wood fibers chewed and mixed with saliva; what is this group’s common name?
In the Borneo food-web disruption, DDT reduced wasps that preyed on these leaf-eating insect larvae, allowing their numbers to surge. What are the larvae called?

This inherited disorder is commonly associated with deletion of phenylalanine at position 508 in a protein involved in chloride transport. The resulting thick secretions can obstruct the lungs and pancreatic ducts. What is the disorder?
In cystic fibrosis, mutations in which gene can disrupt an epithelial chloride channel that regulates salt and water movement? This gene is located on chromosome 7.

What term describes the hypothesized emergence of living organisms from nonliving matter? Some proposed accounts place this transition in the chemical conditions of Earth’s early oceans, sometimes called a primordial soup.

Which laboratory study relevant to abiogenesis exposed a mixture of gases thought to resemble Earth’s early atmosphere to electrical sparks and produced amino acids? Conducted in 1953, it was named for its two researchers.
In classical mechanics, this quantity for a body's translational motion is calculated as one-half its mass multiplied by the square of its speed, and its SI unit is the joule. What is it called?

The rotational form of kinetic energy for a rigid body spinning about a fixed axis is one-half this quantity multiplied by angular speed squared. For point masses, it is calculated by summing each mass times the square of its distance from the axis; what is this rotational analogue of mass?

When a curved lens rests on a flat glass plate, the changing thickness of the thin air film between them produces concentric bright and dark fringes under illumination. What is this interference pattern, named after the physicist associated with it?

In Newton’s rings observed in reflected light, the film thickness at the center is zero, but the center appears dark. What wave-optics effect explains this when reflection causes one of the rays to undergo a phase reversal?

What distributed version control system records project history in commits and lets collaborators exchange changes through pushes and pulls? It also supports branching and merging so developers can work on changes independently.
In Git-based collaboration, which web platform launched in 2008 and became a major host for software repositories and pull requests? Microsoft acquired it in 2018.

The C-value paradox describes how the amount of this material in an organism need not track its biological complexity. A 13-year international effort mapped the complete human version, including both genes and noncoding DNA. What is an organism’s complete set of genetic information called?
Which international research initiative, launched in 1990 and declared complete in 2003, coordinated the sequencing and mapping of the genome of our species?

This wave phenomenon occurs when waves spread around an obstacle or after passing through an opening, and it is especially noticeable when the obstacle or opening is about the same size as the wavelength. It explains why sound can be heard around a doorway and why light passing through narrow slits forms patterns. What is this phenomenon?

In diffraction from regularly spaced crystal planes, this named relation predicts constructive peaks by connecting the planes’ spacing, the scattering angle, the wavelength, and an integer order. It is commonly written as nλ = 2d sin θ. What is this relation called?

What atmospheric formation is marked by rounded, pouch-like protrusions hanging from its underside, often beneath the anvil of a thunderstorm? It is associated with turbulent air near strong convection.

Mammatus clouds can appear beneath the broad, flattened top of a powerful thunderstorm. What is the name for this upper cloud feature, formed when rising air spreads outward after reaching a stable layer?

An international project began in 1990 and was declared complete in 2003, producing a reference sequence of roughly three billion DNA bases organized into 23 chromosome pairs. What landmark scientific initiative was it?

In 1996, sequencing centers involved in the Human Genome Project adopted a policy of promptly releasing DNA sequence data to public databases, generally within 24 hours. What name is given to this data-sharing agreement?

Which prominent constellation depicts a hunter from Greek mythology and is especially visible on winter evenings in the Northern Hemisphere? Its recognizable pattern includes three bright stars aligned in a short, straight row.

In Orion, which red supergiant dimmed dramatically in late 2019 and early 2020, with observations pointing to surface cooling and dust as contributing factors? It marks one of the hunter’s shoulders and is usually the constellation’s second-brightest star.
In Orion’s sword is a fuzzy patch visible to the unaided eye, cataloged as M42 and illuminated by the young stars of the Trapezium Cluster. What nearby star-forming region is it?
Which annual meteor shower has its radiant in Orion and typically peaks in October? Its meteors are debris left behind by Halley’s Comet.
Launched in 1999, this NASA sample-return mission used aerogel to capture particles during a 2004 flythrough of a comet’s coma. Its return capsule landed in Utah in 2006; what was the mission called?

The Stardust spacecraft passed through this short-period body’s coma in 2004 and collected particles that were later returned to Earth. Discovered in 1978 and catalogued as 81P, it was the target of that mission’s sample collection; what was it?

This mostly aquatic animal phylum is characterized by radial symmetry and specialized stinging cells that contain nematocysts. Its members include animals that may occur as polyps or medusae. What is this phylum?
In Cnidaria, what specialized cell type houses the stinging organelle used to capture prey or deter predators? The organelle itself is called a nematocyst.

Two atoms share bonding electrons, but one attracts the shared electron cloud more strongly because of a difference in their ability to attract electrons. This unequal sharing creates partial charges rather than transferring a full electron. What type of chemical connection is this?

In a polar covalent bond, the shared electron cloud shifts toward the atom with the higher value of this property. Linus Pauling’s scale is a familiar way to assign numerical values to it. What is this property?

When two surfaces touch but have not begun sliding, this contact force opposes their impending relative motion and can provide the grip that lets a shoe push off the ground. Its magnitude increases as needed up to a limit set by the normal force and a property of the surfaces; what force is it?

For static friction, what dimensionless property of a pair of contacting surfaces is multiplied by the normal force to give the maximum possible resisting force? Often written as μₛ, it is not itself a force.
For an idealized, nonrotating black hole, what is the name of the characteristic distance marking its event horizon? In terms of the black hole’s mass M, this distance is 2GM/c².

The Schwarzschild radius takes its name from the German physicist who found an exact, spherically symmetric solution to Einstein’s field equations. He did this while serving on the Eastern Front during World War I; who was he?

What term describes an illness that develops after someone consumes a meal contaminated with disease-causing organisms or their toxins? It includes illnesses caused both by microbial infection and by toxins already present when the meal is eaten.

In food poisoning linked to improperly canned goods, what severe paralytic illness is caused by a toxin that blocks acetylcholine release at nerve endings? It can begin with blurred vision and difficulty swallowing and progress to respiratory failure.
What statistical modeling method estimates relationships between variables and, in its linear form, represents the relationship with a fitted straight line through observed data?
In regression analysis, what coefficient-estimation method minimizes the total squared residuals while giving each observation equal weight?
In saturated carbon compounds, what bonding scheme combines one s orbital and three p orbitals into four equivalent directional orbitals, as occurs when carbon forms four single bonds?
When carbon uses sp³ hybridization to bond to four hydrogen atoms, methane has four equivalent C–H bonds and H–C–H angles of about 109.5°. What three-dimensional arrangement do the atoms form?
What astronomical object is a densely packed, roughly spherical collection of old stars? These systems are typically rich in stars with low abundances of elements heavier than helium.
Stars in this stellar category are generally old and have relatively low abundances of elements heavier than helium. Which stellar classification is commonly found in globular clusters?

This pale, long-beaked freshwater cetacean was endemic to the Yangtze River and was the sole living member of the family Lipotidae. A 2006 survey failed to find any individuals, and it is widely regarded as the first cetacean species driven to extinction by human activity; what species was it?

An international team spent six weeks in 2006 surveying the main channel of China’s longest river aboard two vessels, searching for the Baiji but finding no confirmed individuals. What was this survey called?

On nutrition labels, this category of dietary lipids appears separately from monounsaturated and polyunsaturated varieties. Its constituent chains have only carbon–carbon single bonds, with hydrogen filling the remaining bonding capacity.
Among saturated fats, which 16-carbon compound, designated C16:0, is especially abundant in palm oil? Its common name derives from the oil of this tropical palm.

When electrons in a covalent molecule are shared unequally, atoms can acquire fractional electrostatic values, conventionally marked δ− and δ+, without becoming full ions. What are these values called?

In water, partial charge on oxygen and hydrogen does not cancel because the molecule is bent. What vector-valued molecular quantity, commonly expressed in debyes, measures the resulting separation of positive and negative charge?

A reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol can produce this family of compounds along with water. Methyl salicylate, associated with wintergreen’s scent, and many compounds responsible for fruity aromas are members of this group; what is the family called?
Among esters, which compound is formed by reacting salicylic acid with methanol and is associated with the characteristic scent of wintergreen?

Born in Delft in 1632, this Dutch microscopist made his own lenses and used compact, single-lens instruments to observe microorganisms and red blood cells. He shared his findings through letters to the Royal Society over several decades. Who was he?
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was born in 1632 and died in 1723 in the same Dutch city, where he made many of his observations. What city was it?
This blue supergiant marks the foot of the celestial hunter and is commonly described as the brightest star in its constellation. What is its name?

Rigel belongs to a constellation identified by the three aligned stars Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka, which form its belt. In Greek mythology, this constellation depicts a hunter. What is the constellation?

This phosphorus-and-oxygen moiety has one phosphorus atom bonded to four oxygen atoms, with one oxygen connecting it to the rest of a molecule. It is added during phosphorylation and helps form the sugar-linked backbone of DNA and RNA. What is this?

During phosphorylation, enzymes in this class transfer a phosphate group—often from ATP—to a target molecule. This modification can change a protein’s activity in cell signaling. What is this enzyme class?
In wave physics, what property describes waves whose phase relationships remain fixed over time? For light, this property is associated with a well-defined frequency and a stable phase relationship.

Coherence keeps the phase relationship between overlapping light waves stable over time. What optical phenomenon forms a persistent pattern of bright and dark regions as the waves reinforce or cancel one another?

This hypothetical gas is modeled as particles with negligible volume and no intermolecular forces. Its pressure, volume, amount, and temperature are related by the equation PV = nRT; what is the model called?
For an ideal gas with a fixed amount of substance at constant temperature, pressure changes inversely with volume. Which named law describes how halving the volume doubles the pressure?
What clear liquid circulates through the brain’s ventricles and around the brain and spinal cord, cushioning the central nervous system and helping remove waste?
In cerebrospinal fluid physiology, what is the name of the enlarged subarachnoid space below the conus medullaris that contains the cauda equina and is commonly accessed for spinal taps?

After a Sun-like star expels its outer layers, its Earth-sized, extremely dense core can remain as a dim stellar remnant. It resists gravitational collapse through electron degeneracy pressure and has an upper mass threshold near 1.4 times the Sun’s mass; what kind of remnant is it?

For a white dwarf, what is the name of the roughly 1.4-solar-mass upper bound on stability, beyond which electron degeneracy pressure can no longer support it against gravitational collapse? Named for the Indian-American astrophysicist whose calculations established it, this mass threshold is associated with the conditions leading to a Type Ia supernova.

A mnemonic rule in electromagnetism predicts the circular field around a straight current-carrying wire by aligning a thumb with conventional current and curled fingers with the field. What is this rule?

The Right-Hand Rule is used to resolve q(v × B) for a positive charge moving through a field. Align the index finger with the charge’s velocity and the middle finger with B; the thumb indicates the direction of which vector quantity?
Worn over the mouth and nose, these protective coverings help reduce the spread of respiratory infections such as COVID-19. What is the common name for these public-health items?

Among face masks, this commonly used U.S.-certified type is rated to filter 95% of airborne particles and is designed to seal closely to the face, unlike loose-fitting surgical coverings. What is it called?
A rapidly moving rod is measured by a stationary observer to be shorter along its direction of motion than it is in its own rest frame. What is this relativistic effect called?

Length contraction is one consequence of a framework in which the speed of light in vacuum is invariant for inertial observers. Einstein later extended this framework to account for gravity; what is the original theory called?

What term describes a state in which an orbiting body rotates once for each orbit around its parent, causing the same side to continually face that parent? Earth's Moon exhibits this relationship with Earth.
Tidal locking is mutual in a famous pair of outer Solar System bodies: each keeps the same hemisphere facing the other, and the primary was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006. What is the pair?

In the Warriors novels, the four Clans are made up of wild members of this mammal group, while house-dwelling animals are called “kittypets.” In zoology, the name also covers domestic forms and small wild felids such as ocelots and servals; what is the group’s common name?

In the Warriors books, medicine cats among the Cats can receive guidance from this spiritual Clan, believed to consist of the deceased ancestors of the living Clans. What is the name of that ancestral Clan?
In science fiction, what is the standard name for an artificial being designed to resemble a human? Ash in *Alien* and the replicants in *Blade Runner* are examples of this character type.
In Ridley Scott’s 1979 science-fiction film, the android Ash serves aboard the Nostromo, where a creature first latches onto Kane’s face. What is the film’s one-word title?

This potentially life-threatening infection is caused by parasites in the genus Plasmodium and is usually transmitted by bites from infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. In humans, the parasites develop first in liver cells and then multiply in red blood cells, causing recurring fevers. What disease is it?
Among the five parasite species known to cause human malaria, which one causes the deadliest form and can lead to severe illness if untreated?

Astronomers describe how far a celestial object lies from an observer or another object using units such as light-years and parsecs. Nearby values can be inferred from parallax, while larger-scale estimates may use standard candles or redshift; what is this measured quantity?
In astronomical distance measurements, what unit is defined as the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends an angle of one arcsecond? It is equivalent to roughly 3.26 light-years.

Discovered in 2010, this sophisticated worm targeted industrial control systems rather than ordinary desktop files. It manipulated Siemens software controlling Iranian enrichment centrifuges while hiding the changes from operators; what was this worm called?

Stuxnet’s best-known industrial target was this underground Iranian uranium-enrichment facility, where the attack manipulated centrifuge operation and concealed abnormal behavior from operators. What was the facility called?
Named from a Greek word for “seahorse” because of its curved shape, this paired structure lies in the medial temporal lobes and helps consolidate newly formed memories. What brain structure is it?
