The hippocampus helps consolidate experiences and facts into a form retained well beyond the brief period in which information is actively held in mind. What term describes this durable store?

Which psychosurgical procedure was popularized by Portuguese neurologist Egas Moniz and later adapted in the United States by Walter Freeman and James Watts? It involved severing connections in the frontal lobes.
In the history of lobotomy, which Portuguese neurologist developed prefrontal leucotomy and received the 1949 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for that work?

What intrinsic physical quantity measures an object's resistance to acceleration and contributes to its gravitational attraction? It is conventionally measured in kilograms and remains unchanged when the object moves from Earth to the Moon.
What SI base unit is used to express mass and is represented by the symbol kg? Its modern definition is based on fixing the numerical value of the Planck constant.

An object's mass stays the same when it travels from Earth to the Moon, but the force exerted on it by gravity becomes weaker. What is the name of this force, which depends on both the object's mass and the local gravitational acceleration?
In classical mechanics, mass quantifies an object's resistance to changes in its velocity when a net force acts on it. What is this property called?
In the Standard Model, coupling to a pervasive scalar field gives many elementary particles their mass. What particle is the quantum excitation associated with that field?

Which English theoretical physicist developed a relativistic wave equation for spin-one-half particles that predicted the existence of antimatter? He also proposed a model in which positrons could be understood as holes in a filled sea of states.
Paul Dirac’s relativistic theory implied a positively charged counterpart to the electron, and Carl Anderson detected this particle in cosmic rays in 1932. What is it called?
What natural material forms the upper layer of the ground where rooted plants can grow? It combines mineral grains such as sand, silt, and clay with organic matter, water, air, and living organisms.
In soil, which kingdom includes molds and yeasts and contains many decomposers that break down organic remains and recycle nutrients? Its organisms are distinct from plants and animals.

Which analytical technique identifies molecular vibrational modes by measuring frequency shifts in light that scatters inelastically from a sample? Named for an Indian physicist whose 1928 discovery revealed this effect, it provides a characteristic spectrum of a material.
In Raman spectroscopy, what term describes the case in which an outgoing photon has less energy and a longer wavelength than the incoming photon, while the molecule gains vibrational energy?
This optical law relates the sines of the angles of incidence and refraction to the refractive indices of the two media. What is the law called?
Snell's law is named for this Dutch mathematician and astronomer, who improved triangulation methods and used them to measure Earth's circumference. Who was he?
Snell's law can be derived by applying this principle, which says that light follows a path requiring stationary travel time. What is the principle called?
In Snell's law, this dimensionless property of a medium is represented by n and equals the speed of light in a vacuum divided by its phase speed in that medium. What is this property called?

When light traveling in a higher-index medium meets a boundary above the angle at which Snell's law permits a transmitted ray, it is reflected entirely back into the original medium. What is this phenomenon called?
These two reddish-brown, bean-shaped organs sit behind the abdominal lining, filter blood, and send the resulting liquid toward the bladder through the ureters. What is the name of this paired organ?

In the kidney, blood filtration begins in a capillary tuft enclosed by Bowman’s capsule, and the filtrate then passes through a tubule that leads toward a collecting duct. What is the kidney’s structural and functional unit?
The kidney produces this liquid containing water and waste products such as urea, which travels through the ureters and is stored in the bladder. What is this liquid called?
When oxygen levels are low, the kidney releases this hormone, which signals the bone marrow to increase red blood cell production. What is the hormone?

This Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium commonly inhabits the lower intestine of warm-blooded animals. Its well-studied genetics and ease of cultivation have made it a standard organism for cloning and recombinant protein production; what species is it?
Some Escherichia coli strains, including O157:H7, produce Shiga toxin that can lead to a serious kidney-damaging complication. What is this complication called?
In an electrochemical cell, this electrode is where reduction occurs, as particles gain electrons. In a galvanic cell, it is the positive electrode. What is it called?

In a galvanic cell, the Cathode and anode are connected externally by a wire, while ion migration through a separate component helps prevent charge imbalance between the half-cells. In a common laboratory setup, this component is a U-shaped glass tube filled with an electrolyte; what is it called?

This facial organ warms and humidifies inhaled air, while its cilia help clear trapped particles toward the throat. Its upper lining also contains sensory cells that detect airborne chemicals. What organ is it?

In the nose, odor-detecting neurons send signals through the cribriform plate to a paired structure at the front of the brain, where the signals are organized into glomeruli before being relayed onward. What is this structure?

This input device uses an array of physical or touch-sensitive keys to enter letters, numbers, punctuation, and commands. In a common layout, the first row of alphabetic keys begins with Q, W, E, R, T, and Y; what device is it?
On a full-size computer keyboard, what is the separate block of keys usually placed to the right of the main typing area, arranged like a calculator for entering numbers and arithmetic operators?

A Chinese-American experimental physicist conducted a landmark 1956 test using polarized cobalt-60 nuclei and beta decay. The results showed that the weak interaction does not preserve mirror-reflection symmetry; who performed the experiment?

In the 1956 cobalt-60 experiment, Chien-Shiung Wu observed that beta particles were emitted preferentially in a direction related to the nuclei’s spin. Which fundamental symmetry of spatial reflection did this evidence show the weak interaction does not respect?
This yellow-orange pigment forms during the breakdown of heme, and excess amounts can cause the yellowing of the skin and eyes associated with jaundice. What is the name of this pigment?
Unconjugated bilirubin is poorly soluble in water, so it travels through the blood bound to a major plasma protein that also helps maintain oncotic pressure. What is this carrier protein?
In a two-input digital logic circuit, the output is high for input pairs 01, 10, and 11, but low for 00. Which logic operation follows this truth table?

In Minecraft redstone logic, three torches linked by dust can produce a gate whose output is true only when both inputs are true. Unlike an OR gate, it does not activate when just one input is true; what gate is this?

This American heavy bomber had four Wright R-3350 engines, a pressurized crew compartment, and remotely operated defensive gun turrets. Introduced into combat in the Pacific during World War II, what aircraft was it?

Among Boeing B-29 Superfortresses, which aircraft did Paul Tibbets pilot on August 6, 1945, when it dropped the atomic bomb known as Little Boy over Hiroshima? The aircraft was named for Tibbets’s mother.
In Boolean logic and programming, which truth value indicates that a proposition or condition does not hold? When it is the tested condition of a conventional while loop, iteration stops.

In Java, when a condition evaluates to Boolean false, which branching construct skips its main block and may instead execute an optional alternative branch? Unlike a loop, this construct chooses between paths rather than repeating code.

In Angels in America, Belize works in this healthcare profession, and One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest gives the same profession to the authoritarian hospital worker Mildred Ratched. What profession involves trained patient care, administering treatments, and supporting medical care?
Belize, a nurse in the two-part play Angels in America, is a drag performer who cares for Prior Walter. The playwright also wrote A Bright Room Called Day; who is he?
When the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, it can block some or all of the Sun from view. What is this astronomical event called?
During a total solar eclipse, a faint, pearly halo can appear around the Moon’s silhouette, normally hidden by the Sun’s bright visible surface. What is this outer layer of the Sun called?

In humans, what cartilaginous airway carries air from the larynx and divides into the two main bronchi before they enter the lungs? Its incomplete C-shaped rings help keep the passage open while allowing the esophagus behind it to expand during swallowing.
The trachea is supported by incomplete C-shaped rings that help prevent the airway from collapsing. What specific tissue makes up these rings?

It includes optical instruments and electron-based methods, and it is used to examine cells and other structures too small to resolve clearly with the unaided eye. What is this broad scientific practice called?

In this form of microscopy, a focused laser scans a fluorescent specimen while a pinhole blocks much of the light coming from outside the focal plane. This optical sectioning is useful for building three-dimensional views of thick samples; what technique is it?

What hypothetical particle would carry an isolated north or south pole, rather than having such poles occur only in a pair? Its existence would make Maxwell’s equations more symmetric, but it has never been observed.

For a magnetic monopole, what named rule requires the product of electric and magnetic charges to be an integer multiple of ℏc/2 in Gaussian units? A 1931 argument used this relation to explain why electric charge occurs in fixed units.
This analytical procedure determines a sample’s water content through a reaction involving iodine and sulfur dioxide. Named for its developer, what method is widely used for moisture analysis?

In Karl Fischer titration, one variant generates the titrant electrochemically inside the cell instead of dispensing a measured volume from a burette. It calculates the water content from the electrical charge passed; what is this measurement mode called?

This American physical chemist proposed a 1916 account of chemical bonding centered on shared electron pairs, and his name became attached to dot diagrams of valence electrons. He also formulated an acid–base definition based on electron-pair acceptance and donation. Identify him.
Gilbert Newton Lewis coined a term in 1926 for the smallest unit of radiant energy. What was the term?
After Gilbert Newton Lewis relocated to the West Coast in 1912, he joined the faculty of this institution and later became dean of its College of Chemistry. Name the institution.

During research connected with isotope separation, Gilbert Newton Lewis purified a sample of this isotopically distinct liquid, whose molecules contain deuterium in place of ordinary hydrogen. Name the substance.

Unlike amorphous materials such as glass, these solids have atoms, ions, or molecules arranged in a repeating pattern with long-range order. Their internal structure can be described by a lattice built from a repeating block. What are these materials called?
In crystals, a small repeating building block generates the lattice throughout the solid. Its side lengths and angles describe the pattern and help classify its symmetry. What is this block called?
What term describes the shower-like descent of dead organisms, phytoplankton, and other organic particles from surface waters toward the deep sea, transporting nutrients as it sinks?

Marine snow carries organic material downward from sunlit waters, including microscopic drifting organisms that use sunlight to photosynthesize and support marine food webs. What are these organisms called?

What quantum-mechanical rule, proposed in 1925 to explain atomic shell structure, says that identical particles with half-integer spin cannot share the same complete quantum state? In atoms, it limits each orbital to two electrons with opposite spin projections.
The Pauli exclusion principle restricts identical particles with half-integer spin, rather than all quantum particles. What is the name of this particle class, which includes electrons and protons?

At Mount Wilson Observatory, this American astronomer used Cepheid variables in Andromeda to show that it lies beyond the Milky Way, then linked galaxy distance with recession speed. He also devised a system for classifying galaxies by shape. Who was he?

Edwin Hubble's galaxy classification chart places elliptical galaxies along one sequence and branches into spiral forms, with barred and unbarred spirals on separate paths. By what familiar visual name is this chart known?

A light wave striking a boundary can return to the medium it came from instead of continuing through the interface. This behavior includes mirror-like redirection as well as scattering from rough surfaces; what is this phenomenon called?
In optical reflection from an ideal plane mirror, the incoming and outgoing rays are measured relative to a line perpendicular to the mirror. What rule states that these two angles are equal?

For optical reflection at a boundary, light moving from a higher-index medium into a lower-index one can be returned wholly to its starting medium once its incidence angle exceeds a particular threshold. What phenomenon causes this, leaving no propagating refracted ray in the second medium?

In optical reflection from a rough, matte surface, tiny surface facets send light in many directions, so an observer can see the surface from different viewing angles rather than seeing a sharp image. What is this non-mirror-like form called?

At an interface, optical reflection and transmission depend on the light’s polarization, incidence angle, and the refractive indices on both sides. What set of formulas, named for a 19th-century French physicist, calculates the reflected and transmitted wave amplitudes under those conditions?
This English natural philosopher became the Royal Society’s Curator of Experiments in 1662 and later reported microscopic observations of tiny boxlike structures in cork. Who was he?
Robert Hooke’s 1665 illustrated account of microscopic observations featured detailed images of a flea and cork. What is the title of this influential work?
Which moon of Jupiter is the largest natural satellite in the Solar System, possesses its own intrinsic magnetic field, and is thought to conceal a subsurface ocean beneath layers of ice?

During its 1990s mission, this NASA probe made multiple close flybys of Ganymede and gathered magnetic measurements that provided evidence for a conductive, salty subsurface ocean. Named for the scientist associated with the first telescopic observations of Jupiter’s four large moons, what was it?

A computer can use one of these procedures to determine whether a target value occurs in a collection or to locate a route through a graph. Sequentially checking entries and repeatedly halving a sorted list are two classic strategies in this family. What is the general name for these procedures?

Within Search Algorithms, which named graph procedure finds routes with the lowest total edge weight when every edge weight is nonnegative? It minimizes the sum of the weights, not necessarily the number of edges.

During a total eclipse, this layer appears as a pearly halo extending far beyond the visible disk of the Sun. It is the outermost part of the Sun’s atmosphere and the source region of major plasma eruptions. What is it called?

An eruption from the Solar Corona sends a vast bubble of magnetized plasma into interplanetary space, and one directed toward Earth can trigger geomagnetic storms and auroras. What is this solar event called?

This amphipathic membrane molecule has a phosphate-containing head that interacts with water and fatty-acid tails that avoid it. When many of these molecules assemble in a cell membrane, their heads face watery surroundings while their tails point inward; what is this molecule called?
A phospholipid has a water-attracting phosphate-containing region and water-repelling fatty-acid chains. What term describes a molecule with both water-attracting and water-repelling regions?

In a solid, atomic nuclei can emit and absorb gamma rays without taking up the usual recoil energy, producing exceptionally narrow resonances useful for measuring tiny energy shifts. What is this nuclear phenomenon called?

The Mössbauer effect enabled a precise test of gravitational redshift by comparing gamma-ray frequencies between the top and bottom of a tower. Conducted at Harvard in 1959–1960 across a 22.5-meter height, what was this measurement called?
This organ filters blood, removes aged red blood cells, and contributes to immune defense. A smaller accessory version occurs in some people, but the primary organ is found in the upper-left abdomen.
The spleen lies next to this hollow digestive organ in the upper abdomen. It mixes food with gastric acid and passes the resulting contents into the small intestine.

An American agronomist working in Mexico bred high-yielding, rust-resistant semi-dwarf wheat varieties that helped transform crop production. He received the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to address world hunger; who was he?

Norman Borlaug’s wheat research became a hallmark of the mid-20th-century agricultural transformation that sharply increased crop yields through improved seeds and farming methods. What is this transformation commonly called?

What computer-science field develops systems that perform tasks associated with human cognitive abilities, such as learning, reasoning, perception, and language generation? It includes both rule-based approaches and methods that learn from data.
Within artificial intelligence, which computer scientist coined the field’s name in 1955? He later organized the 1956 Dartmouth workshop that helped establish the emerging research field.

Stars, including the Sun, are largely made of an electrically conducting matter formed when a gas becomes substantially ionized. Its free electrons and ions respond collectively to electromagnetic fields, making it the fourth classical state of matter. What is this state?
In plasma, electrons oscillate collectively against an almost stationary ion background, with electrostatic forces providing the restoring force. What is the name for this high-frequency mode?

Plasma fills the Sun’s outermost atmospheric layer, which appears as a pearly halo during a total solar eclipse. Eruptions from this layer can launch large amounts of material into space. What is this layer called?

Which aromatic explosive is formed by introducing three nitro groups onto toluene, giving it the formula C₇H₅N₃O₆? Its energy release is commonly used as a benchmark for comparing the power of other explosives.
A German chemist first prepared trinitrotoluene in 1863, decades before it became widely used as a military explosive. What was his name?

Climate scientists estimate this global metric by combining readings from air close to the ground over land with readings from the ocean’s uppermost waters, then averaging across the planet. Its long-term rise is a key measure of greenhouse-driven warming, distinct from any local weather reading. What is it?

When reporting changes in Global Mean Surface Temperature, scientists often give the difference from a chosen climatological baseline instead of an absolute temperature. What is this signed difference called?

What two-dimensional carbon allotrope consists of a single atomic layer arranged in a repeating hexagonal honeycomb and serves as the fundamental sheet that can be stacked to form the pencil-core material graphite? Despite being only one atom thick, it conducts heat and electricity exceptionally well.

Graphene was isolated in 2004 by Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov, who peeled layers from graphite with adhesive tape. At which English institution did they conduct this work, later recognized with the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics?

In 1610, Galileo observed that this planet shows phases ranging from crescent to gibbous, evidence that it orbits the Sun rather than Earth. It is the second planet from the Sun and completes an orbit in about 225 Earth days; which planet is it?
For Venus, what is the name of the near-side alignment that occurs when it lies between Earth and the Sun? This contrasts with the configuration in which the Sun lies between Earth and Venus.
At ordinary atmospheric pressure, what is the solid phase of water that forms when liquid water freezes and makes up most of a glacier’s mass?

Ice moving within glaciers can carry boulders far from their original bedrock source. What are these large rocks, sometimes weighing hundreds of tons, called when a retreating glacier leaves them behind?

What is the common temporary computer resource used as a processor’s working area, where data at any location can be retrieved directly rather than by reading through preceding locations? Its contents disappear when electrical power is removed.

Within Random-Access Memory, which widely used technology stores each bit as charge in a capacitor paired with a transistor, requiring periodic refresh as the charge leaks away? It is commonly used for a computer’s main memory.

This degenerative eye disease damages the macula and causes loss of central vision. It occurs in dry and wet forms, with drusen associated with the dry form and abnormal blood-vessel growth associated with the wet form. What is the disease?
In the wet form of age-related macular degeneration, fragile abnormal blood vessels can grow beneath the retina and leak. What class of medicines suppresses the growth signal driving these vessels?

In an isolated interaction, two bodies exert forces on each other and their total momentum is conserved. Depending on whether kinetic energy is also conserved, this interaction is classified as elastic or inelastic; what is it called?

In a one-dimensional collision, this dimensionless quantity compares the relative speed of separation with the relative speed of approach. It is 1 for an ideal elastic collision and 0 for a perfectly inelastic one; what is this quantity called?

In ecology, what is the feeding interaction in which animals consume plant tissues, often contending with chemical defenses such as tannins and structural defenses such as thorns? It is contrasted with carnivory and includes both grazing on grasses and browsing on woody vegetation.
During herbivory, what is the largest chamber of a ruminant’s four-part stomach, where microbes ferment cellulose-rich plant material? Cattle regurgitate and rechew food from this chamber as cud.

In phosphorus pentachloride, the central phosphorus is bonded to five chlorine atoms: three lie in one plane at 120° intervals, while two occupy positions above and below that plane. What is the name of this five-coordinate arrangement?
In trigonal bipyramidal molecular geometry, a coordinated rearrangement lets axial and equatorial ligands exchange positions as the other ligands move as well. What is this named rearrangement?

In this thermodynamic process, a system exchanges no heat with its surroundings. For a reversible path involving an ideal gas, pressure multiplied by volume raised to a fixed exponent remains constant. What is this process called?

For an ideal gas undergoing an Adiabatic Process, the exponent γ in the relation PV^γ = constant is dimensionless. It equals the heat capacity at constant pressure divided by the heat capacity at constant volume; what is this ratio called?

Sunlight interacting with airborne water droplets can be bent, reflected inside the droplets, and separated into a spectrum, producing a colored arc opposite the Sun. What atmospheric optical phenomenon is this?
In a primary Rainbow, the spectrum places one hue along the outer edge and violet along the inner edge. Which hue appears on the outer edge?

The center of a Rainbow lies along a line extending from the observer directly away from the Sun, so its position shifts as the Sun moves. What is the name for the location in the sky at the center of this geometry?

In acid–base chemistry, what quantity is defined as the negative base-ten logarithm of an acid’s dissociation constant, Ka? At the half-equivalence point of a weak-acid titration, the pH equals this quantity.
In buffer calculations, pKa is added to the base-ten logarithm of the conjugate-base-to-acid concentration ratio to estimate pH. What named equation expresses this relationship?
Which large, flightless bird was endemic to Mauritius and became extinct after human settlement brought introduced animals and other pressures to the island?
The dodo was endemic to which Indian Ocean island nation, located east of Madagascar, where human colonization and introduced animals contributed to its extinction?
What name is given to the rounded marine echinoderms whose bodies are protected by a dense covering of movable spines? Their name comes from an old word for a hedgehog.
Sea urchins use a hard, five-toothed mouth apparatus to scrape algae from rocks and other surfaces. What is this feeding structure traditionally called?

This conventional 15-element metal series spans atomic numbers 57 through 71, from lanthanum to lutetium. It is commonly displayed in a separate row beneath the main body of the periodic table; what is the series called?

As atomic number rises from cerium through lutetium in the lanthanides, electrons progressively occupy a particular electron grouping. Its spectroscopic notation uses principal level four and the letter assigned to angular-momentum quantum number three; what is the grouping called?
What is the name of the long-lived anticyclonic storm in Jupiter’s atmosphere that has been observed for centuries? Although it is shrinking, it remains larger than Earth.
The Great Red Spot is a persistent storm within the banded atmosphere of this rapidly rotating gas giant, the largest planet in the Solar System. Which planet hosts it?
This grasshopper-like insect can shift from a solitary phase to a highly mobile gregarious phase when crowded. Its enormous migratory swarms have repeatedly devastated crops; what insect is it?
The Gospels describe a wilderness preacher who ate locusts and wild honey and later baptized Jesus in the Jordan. Which biblical figure is associated with this dietary reference?

Ecologists estimate total animal abundance by marking a first group, releasing them, and later collecting another group. They compare how many in the later group bear marks to estimate the population size. What is this approach?

Within the Capture-Recapture Method, what named formula estimates population size by multiplying the number marked in the first sample by the size of the second sample, then dividing by the number of marked individuals found in it? It is also known by the surnames of two researchers associated with its development.

For a periodic disturbance, this quantity is found by multiplying its spatial period by its repetition frequency, and it tells how quickly the disturbance propagates. In a dispersive medium, it can refer to either a phase-based or packet-based rate; what is the general name of the quantity?

Wave velocity can be described by a packet-based measure distinct from phase velocity in a dispersive medium. Which measure equals the derivative of angular frequency with respect to wavenumber and tracks the envelope of a wave packet?

This French-Polish scientific family made foundational studies of radioactivity after investigating pitchblende. Its members’ research led to the discovery of polonium and radium and earned multiple Nobel Prizes; which family is it?
The Curie family identified this radioactive element while investigating pitchblende, and Marie Curie named it in honor of her native Poland. What element has atomic number 84?
This optical instrument uses lenses or mirrors to gather and focus light, helping observers study distant objects such as planets and stars. What is this instrument called?
Which Italian astronomer reported observing four moons orbiting Jupiter with a telescope in his 1610 work *Sidereus Nuncius*?

In metabolism, this molecule binds particular substrates and accelerates their conversion into products by lowering the reaction’s activation barrier, yet remains available for another catalytic cycle. What is this biological catalyst, usually made of protein?
The science that investigates enzyme structure, catalytic mechanisms, and reaction rates has a dedicated name. What is this field called?

Most enzyme catalysts are proteins, but some RNA molecules can catalyze reactions; the RNA component responsible for peptide-bond formation in the ribosome is a well-known example. What is the general name for catalytic RNA molecules?

When an enzyme is exposed to high heat or an extreme pH, its folded shape may unravel and its active site cease to function, even though the molecule has not been used up as a reactant. What is the name for this loss of native structure?

For a simple enzyme reaction that follows a saturation-kinetics model, this quantity is the substrate concentration at which the initial rate reaches half its maximum value. What is this kinetic parameter called?
These compact stellar remnants sweep beams of electromagnetic radiation past Earth as they rotate, producing remarkably regular flashes. What are these cosmic objects called?

Pulsars are rapidly rotating examples of compact remnants left behind after some massive stars explode. These remnants are denser than white dwarfs and can undergo crustal “starquakes”; what are they called?

This molecular technique pairs a programmable RNA guide with a DNA-cutting nuclease to target chosen DNA sequences. Adapted from a bacterial immune defense, it lets researchers use cellular repair after the cut to alter DNA at a chosen site.

In developing CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, this French microbiologist collaborated with Jennifer Doudna, building on her research into bacterial immunity and tracrRNA. The two shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this work; who is she?
Produced chiefly during amino-acid breakdown, this nitrogenous waste is carried in the blood to the kidneys and excreted in mammalian urine. What compound has the molecular formula CH4N2O?
In mammals, the biochemical cycle that converts toxic ammonia into urea takes place primarily in which organ, which also detoxifies alcohol and synthesizes many plasma proteins?

In evolutionary theory, what process describes one cell taking up another and retaining it as an internal partner rather than digesting it, with the relationship eventually contributing to the evolution of complex cells?

In the endosymbiosis explanation for eukaryotic cell evolution, which organelle is traced to an ancestral oxygen-using bacterium and now carries out most cellular ATP production? Its own DNA and double membrane are clues to this proposed origin.

This enormous spiral stellar system lies about 2.5 million light-years from Earth and is the nearest major one to the Milky Way. Astronomers predict that it will merge with our home system in roughly 4.5 billion years. What is it?
The Andromeda Galaxy has a compact elliptical satellite close to its central region. This small galaxy is notable for its unusually high central surface brightness. What is the satellite’s name?
This large carnivorous tyrannosaurid lived during the Late Cretaceous. Its scientific name means “tyrant lizard king.” What dinosaur is it?

A nearly complete skeleton of Tyrannosaurus rex, nicknamed Sue after its discoverer, is exhibited at a Chicago institution on the lakefront, close to Shedd Aquarium and Adler Planetarium. What is its name?

A magnitude-9.2 megathrust event struck the south-central region of the U.S. state whose capital is Juneau on Good Friday, March 27, 1964, generating destructive tsunamis across the Pacific. By what commonly used name is this disaster known?

During the 1964 Alaska earthquake, the main rupture occurred offshore in this large coastal inlet east of Anchorage. Coastal communities in the surrounding region, including Valdez and Chenega, suffered severe damage from shaking and resulting tsunamis.
In electrostatics, this vector quantity gives the force experienced by a positive test charge per unit charge. It is also the negative spatial gradient of scalar potential; what is it called?
Electric field lines conventionally point away from sources of one sign and toward negative sources. What sign belongs to the sources they point away from?

Home tests for this condition commonly detect the hormone hCG, and an obstetric ultrasound can check for an embryo or fetus developing in the uterus. Taking folic acid during it helps reduce the risk of neural-tube defects such as spina bifida. What is this condition called?

During pregnancy, some people experience intermittent uterine tightening that remains irregular, does not progressively intensify, and does not cause cervical dilation. What is this non-labor phenomenon called?

This very large subspecies of brown ursid is native to a group of islands off Alaska’s southern coast, where long isolation from mainland populations has helped make it distinct. What subspecies is it?
The Kodiak bear is native to this island group in the Gulf of Alaska, whose largest island shares its name. What is the island group called?
In April 1961, a Soviet pilot launched aboard Vostok 1 and completed one orbit of Earth in a flight lasting about 108 minutes. He became the first human to travel into space; who was he?

Yuri Gagarin's 1961 orbital flight used a Soviet spacecraft with a spherical reentry module and a single-seat cabin. The vehicle completed one orbit before landing near Engels; what was the spacecraft called?
This substance speeds a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy, yet is regenerated rather than consumed overall. What is it called?

In the Contact Process for producing sulfuric acid, the oxidation of sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide is accelerated by a solid compound with the formula V₂O₅. What compound serves as the catalyst in this step?
Many biological catalysts are protein-based and have names that commonly end in “-ase.” What are these biological catalysts called?
This membrane-bound organelle receives digestive enzymes sorted in the Golgi and breaks down macromolecules and worn-out cellular components. What organelle carries out this intracellular digestion?
Which sugar-phosphate tag is added to digestive enzymes in the Golgi and recognized by sorting receptors that direct them to the lysosome?

This biodegradable thermoplastic is an aliphatic polyester whose chains contain ester bonds and can be made from renewable feedstocks such as corn starch or sugarcane. It is widely used as filament in fused-deposition 3-D printing because it is relatively easy to print and tends to warp less than many alternatives. What material is it?

In one common route for making Polylactic Acid, a small cyclic diester is polymerized by ring-opening polymerization to build the polyester chains. What is the name of this cyclic dimer of lactic acid?
What kingdom of primarily photosynthetic organisms includes trees and the model species Arabidopsis thaliana?
In plants, what protein family associated with the RNA-induced silencing complex was first discovered in Arabidopsis thaliana and helps cleave messenger RNA during RNA interference?

In geometrical optics, a ray approaches a surface, and its direction is compared with a line perpendicular to that surface at the point where it arrives. What is the term for the separation between the incoming ray and the perpendicular reference line?

The angle of incidence is used in a named law that predicts how a light ray bends when it passes between media with different refractive indices. Which law states that the first medium’s refractive index times the sine of the incident angle equals the second medium’s refractive index times the sine of the refracted angle?

A newly synthesized polypeptide can begin this process while translation is still underway, and hydrophobic side chains often help drive it by clustering away from water. The amino-acid sequence helps specify the resulting functional three-dimensional shape; what is this process called?
In protein folding, some cellular helper proteins assist chains that do not fold reliably on their own and can reduce misfolding or aggregation. What are these helper proteins called?
In Newtonian mechanics, this vector interaction changes an object's motion, with its net value equal to mass multiplied by acceleration. It is commonly represented by arrows on free-body diagrams.
Force in an ideal spring varies in proportion to displacement from equilibrium, while the spring's restoring effect points in the opposite direction. What named law describes this relationship?

These single-celled fungi convert sugars into carbon dioxide and alcohol, causing dough to rise and supporting many brewing processes. Some are also engineered to produce medicines such as insulin and vaccine components. What group of microorganisms is described?
Among yeasts, which species was the first eukaryote to have its genome fully sequenced, in 1996, and is widely used in baking and brewing?

What is the name for the warming of Earth’s surface and lower atmosphere that occurs when atmospheric gases absorb and re-emit outgoing infrared radiation? This process helps explain why rising concentrations of gases such as carbon dioxide can raise global temperatures.
In explanations of the greenhouse effect, which molecule made of three oxygen atoms forms a layer in the stratosphere that absorbs much of the Sun’s harmful ultraviolet radiation?
What is the lowest layer of Earth’s atmosphere, extending upward from the surface and containing nearly all weather and most atmospheric water vapor?

In the troposphere, air normally grows cooler with increasing height, but sometimes a warmer layer sits above cooler air near the ground. What atmospheric condition suppresses vertical mixing and can keep urban pollution such as smog trapped near the surface?

In Boolean logic, this circuit element produces a true output only when every input is true. For two inputs, its truth table has a true output for 1,1 and false outputs for 0,0, 0,1, and 1,0; what is this component called?

In digital logic, what gate is formed by inverting the output of an AND gate? With two inputs, it produces a false output only when both inputs are true, and it is known as a universal gate because circuits can be built from it alone.
This monosaccharide is found naturally in many fruits and is sweeter than glucose. It is also one of the sugars in a widely used corn-derived sweetener.
Fructose is combined with glucose in a widely used sweetener made by enzymatically altering a liquid produced from the starch of Zea mays. Common formulations contain about 42% or 55% fructose.

Unlike many small research submersibles that make short excursions from a support ship, this self-propelled watercraft is designed to operate underwater for extended periods. It uses ballast tanks to help dive and compressed air to help rise; what is it called?
A submarine can use this system to detect underwater sounds and echoes without rising to periscope depth. What sensing technology helps its crew locate objects and other vessels through the water?

This two-terminal semiconductor component is formed from adjoining p-type and n-type regions. Applying forward bias narrows its depletion layer, while reverse bias strongly suppresses current. What is it?

In a Diode-based full-wave power-supply circuit, four components are arranged so both halves of an alternating input produce output current with the same polarity, without requiring a center-tapped transformer. What is this four-component arrangement called?

These fully aquatic marine mammals evolved from land-dwelling ancestors and breathe at the surface through blowholes. In common usage, what name refers to the larger cetaceans divided into baleen and toothed groups, rather than dolphins and porpoises?
Among whales, this baleen species is the largest animal known ever to have lived. It feeds mainly by filtering krill from seawater through baleen plates. What species is it?
Among toothed whales, this species is the largest toothed predator on Earth and can dive for up to about 90 minutes while pursuing deep-water prey such as squid. What species is it?
Identified in southern Africa in late 2021, this SARS-CoV-2 strain was quickly designated a variant of concern and was notable for its many spike-protein mutations. What is its name?
Within the Omicron variant family, which subvariant rose to become the dominant SARS-CoV-2 strain in the United States during the summer of 2022, following the earlier BA.2 and BA.4 lineages?

In fluid mechanics, engineers use a dimensionless quantity combining a fluid’s speed, density, characteristic length, and viscosity to assess whether its flow is smooth or chaotic. Named after the British physicist who studied flow in pipes, what is this quantity?

In a circular pipe, a Reynolds number above about 4,000 marks the regime in which fluid velocity and pressure fluctuate irregularly rather than remaining orderly in layers. What is this regime of fluid motion?

These highly energetic regions at the centers of some galaxies are powered by matter accreting through a disk around a supermassive black hole. Quasars and blazars are examples of this class of central object. What are they called?

Some active galactic nuclei launch relativistic jets, and in one subclass the jet points almost directly toward Earth. This alignment produces unusually strong, rapidly varying emission; what is that subclass called?

This mathematical system describes the motion of viscous fluids by relating velocity and pressure while enforcing conservation of momentum. Its averaged forms are widely used in computational modeling of fluid flow. What is this system called?

In fluid dynamics, the Navier–Stokes equations can be averaged over time to help model this regime, where irregular eddies occur across many scales and the smallest scales are associated with Kolmogorov microscales. What chaotic kind of flow is contrasted with smooth laminar flow and can cause bumpy airplane rides?

In a classic optics demonstration, a beam of white light enters this transparent object through one angled face and emerges spread into a spectrum because different wavelengths bend by different amounts. What is this object called?

When light passes through a glass Prism, the amount it bends depends on a dimensionless property of the glass that compares the speed of light in a vacuum with its speed in the material. What is this property called?

What is the classic celestial-mechanics challenge of predicting the trajectories of three masses whose motions are coupled by their mutual gravitational attraction? Unlike the simpler case involving only a pair of masses, it generally has no closed-form solution for arbitrary initial conditions.

In the Three-Body Problem, one family of exact solutions keeps three bodies at the vertices of an equilateral triangle as they orbit their common center of mass. Which eighteenth-century mathematician’s name is also attached to the five equilibrium points of the restricted version of this problem?
Which crystalline aluminum oxide mineral has a hardness of 9 on the standard mineral scratch-hardness ranking and includes ruby and sapphire as gem varieties?
Corundum is assigned a value of 9 on which mineral-hardness scale, whose endpoints are talc at 1 and diamond at 10? The scale ranks minerals by their ability to scratch one another.

Replacing an atom in a reacting molecule with a heavier or lighter form of the same element can alter the reaction rate, in part by changing vibrational energies and the likelihood of tunneling. What is this rate-changing phenomenon called?

In experiments measuring the kinetic isotope effect for hydrogen-transfer reactions, researchers often substitute this stable hydrogen isotope for ordinary hydrogen. Its nucleus contains one proton and one neutron, making it roughly twice as massive as protium.

What is the general name for a gravitationally bound astronomical system containing stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, and dust, with much of its mass commonly attributed to dark matter? Such systems are classified by forms including spiral, elliptical, lenticular, and irregular.
Among galaxies in the Local Group, which barred spiral contains the Solar System? It is the largest structure of stars and matter that our planetary system is part of.

Which nearby spiral galaxy is the closest major galactic neighbor to the Milky Way, lying roughly 2.5 million light-years away in the Local Group? It is also one of the most massive members of that group.

Which visual classification scheme for galaxies groups elliptical forms by apparent roundness, separates spirals by arm structure, and places lenticular forms between them? Its branching organization is used to classify galaxies by their visible shapes.

In a galaxy, stars and gas far from the center can orbit faster than the visible contents alone predict. What name is given to the unseen component invoked to explain these flat rotation curves and the gravitational behavior of galaxy clusters?

Which electrochemical equation calculates a redox reaction’s potential under nonstandard conditions by adjusting the standard potential for temperature, electron transfer, and the reaction mixture’s composition? It can be applied to a half-cell or a full-cell reaction.
The Nernst equation is named for which German physical chemist, who received the 1920 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work in thermochemistry?
In the Nernst equation, what quantity—commonly written as Q—is calculated from the activities of products and reactants, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient?

During cardiac arrest, an AED can send a brief, controlled stimulus through pads on the chest to interrupt a chaotic rhythm and help restore coordinated contractions. What form of energy does the device deliver?

When an adult suffers cardiac arrest, responders may begin this procedure while an AED that can deliver electricity is being prepared. It uses repeated chest compressions at least 2 inches deep to help circulate blood.
This colorless, odorless diatomic gas has the formula H₂ and is used in fuel cells and as a feedstock for ammonia synthesis. What is the name of this gaseous form of the element with atomic number 1?
Molecular hydrogen reacts with nitrogen over an iron-based catalyst at elevated temperature and pressure to produce ammonia on an industrial scale. What is the name of this synthesis process?

What is the traditional South Asian system of healing that combines dietary guidance, herbal remedies, and other therapeutic practices? Its Sanskrit name is commonly translated as “knowledge of life.”

In Ayurvedic medicine, health is traditionally understood through three functional principles associated with movement, transformation, and structure. What is the collective Sanskrit term for these principles?

Used to estimate the pH of a weak-acid system, this relation adds the acid’s pKa to the base-10 logarithm of the conjugate-base-to-weak-acid concentration ratio. It is especially useful for choosing reagent proportions when preparing a buffer. What is this equation?

In the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation, this quantity appears as the additive term alongside the logarithm of the conjugate-base-to-acid ratio. It is the negative base-10 logarithm of an acid’s dissociation constant, Ka. What is this quantity?

The Henderson–Hasselbalch equation is commonly used to estimate the pH of this mixture. Made from a weak acid and its conjugate base, it resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added. What is this solution called?
A connected series of rail vehicles travels along fixed tracks to carry passengers or freight, often pulled or pushed by a locomotive. What is this vehicle or connected set called?

A famous American folk ballad linked to the history of the train tells of a steel-driving worker who raced a steam-powered drill while helping bore the Big Bend Tunnel in West Virginia. Which legendary worker is remembered for declaring he would die with his hammer in his hand?
Unlike a conventional train, this high-speed railway system uses magnetic forces to lift vehicles above a guideway and propel them. What is this technology called?

Introduced in a 2008 white paper and launched in 2009, this peer-to-peer digital currency uses a public blockchain and proof-of-work mining to validate transactions without a central bank. What is it?

The 2008 white paper describing Bitcoin was published under this pseudonym. Its author communicated with early developers before disappearing from public view around 2011; what name did the creator use?

This exact SI defining constant converts an amount of substance into a count of specified elementary entities, such as atoms or molecules. Its value is 6.02214076 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; what is its natural name?
In the 2019 revision of the SI, fixing the exact value of the Avogadro constant defined which base unit for amount of substance?
Within the visible spectrum, what short-wavelength portion is scattered more strongly by air molecules than longer red wavelengths and contributes to the daytime sky’s characteristic color?

Blue light is redirected much more strongly than longer-wavelength visible light by molecules in the atmosphere. What named regime of light redirection explains this wavelength-dependent effect and the sky’s daytime appearance?

These relatively small bodies orbit the Sun and are made mainly of rock or metal. The greatest concentration lies in a broad region between Mars and Jupiter; what is the common name for one of these bodies?
Among asteroids in the main belt, this is the largest body, and it is also classified as a dwarf planet. NASA’s Dawn spacecraft entered orbit around it in 2015 after visiting Vesta; what is its name?

In September 2022, NASA deliberately sent this spacecraft into the asteroid moon Dimorphos to test a method of planetary defense. The impact changed Dimorphos’s orbit around Didymos; what was the mission called?

Which essential nutrient is needed for DNA synthesis, normal red blood cell formation, and healthy nervous-system function? Its absorption in the small intestine depends on a binding protein produced by the stomach.

During Vitamin B12 absorption, this glycoprotein made by stomach parietal cells binds the vitamin and enables its uptake in the terminal ileum. Autoimmune destruction of the cells that produce it can lead to pernicious anemia. What is this glycoprotein?

Chemists use this measure to compare how much of a chosen substance is present relative to a specified amount of a solution or mixture. It can be described qualitatively as dilute or concentrated, or quantified using units such as molarity and molality. What is this measure?

One way to express concentration is to divide the moles of dissolved substance by the liters of the entire solution, rather than by the mass of the solvent. Because solution volume can change with temperature, the value expressed in this unit can change as well. What is this unit?
Green political movements support conserving ecosystems and limiting damage to the natural world. Reducing carbon emissions is one way to advance what broad effort?
Environmental protection is a central aim of this philosophy, which combines ecological priorities such as conservation with liberal social positions. What is this approach called?

This coupled pattern links changes in tropical Pacific sea-surface temperatures with shifts in atmospheric pressure and circulation, influencing weather far beyond the Pacific basin. What is this climate phenomenon called?

During the 2010 drought in Venezuela, lightning over Lake Maracaibo temporarily disappeared; the drought was attributed to the warm phase of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation. What is that warm phase called?

What semiconservative process occurs during S phase, beginning at origin sites and producing leading and lagging strands as polymerases build new DNA? Its unwinding creates fork-shaped junctions, while topoisomerases relieve the resulting torsional strain.

During DNA replication, the lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously in short DNA segments, each initiated by an RNA primer. What are these segments called before ligase joins them into a continuous strand?
These Group 18 elements have filled valence shells and usually exist as individual atoms under standard conditions. What family includes helium, neon, and argon?
The first compound involving a noble gas was synthesized in 1962 when chemist Neil Bartlett reacted platinum hexafluoride with this element. It has atomic number 54; which element is it?
Among the noble gases, this element makes up just under one percent of Earth’s atmosphere and is commonly used as a shielding gas in welding. Which element is it?
This lightest member of the noble gases provides buoyancy in scientific balloons and is also recovered as a byproduct of natural-gas extraction. Name the element.
This synthetic member of the noble gases has atomic number 118 and was named in honor of nuclear physicist Yuri Oganessian. What is the element’s name?
Birds in the order Psittaciformes are often brightly colored and have strong, hooked bills. What common name is given to a bird in this group?
In Robert Louis Stevenson’s Treasure Island, Long John Silver keeps a talkative parrot named for the deceased pirate associated with the island’s buried treasure. What is the bird’s name?

For a software project, this is the smallest number of contributors whose sudden unavailability would leave development seriously stalled or unable to continue. What is this project-resilience measure called?
A 2016 study measured the bus factor of 133 popular projects and estimated that 65 percent had a value below three. Which code-hosting platform supplied the projects studied?

This ice giant is the seventh planet from the Sun and has an axial tilt of about 98 degrees, so it rotates nearly on its side. Methane in its atmosphere absorbs red light, giving it a blue-green appearance; which planet is it?
Only one spacecraft has made a close approach to Uranus. It flew past the planet in January 1986 and later continued on to Neptune; which spacecraft was it?

A Scottish engineer and instrument maker inspecting a Newcomen engine realized that repeatedly cooling its cylinder wasted fuel. Which engineer patented an improved design in 1769 that made steam engines substantially more efficient?

James Watt’s major steam-engine improvement allowed the working cylinder to remain hot while steam condensed in a different chamber, reducing heat loss and fuel consumption. What was this component called?
These institutions provide inpatient housing and treatment for people with mental illness, including around-the-clock care that outpatient clinics do not provide. What are they commonly called?

At a New York psychiatric hospital on Blackwell’s Island, this reporter feigned mental illness to investigate patient treatment. She published her findings in *Ten Days in a Mad-House*; which journalist conducted the 1887 investigation?
What process of nuclear division produces two genetically similar daughter cells and is distinct from meiosis? Its stages include metaphase and the separation of duplicated chromosomes.
During mitosis, which phase begins after metaphase, when sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell?

This sulfur-containing blister agent has two 2-chloroethyl groups attached to a sulfur atom and was used as a chemical weapon in World War I. Its common name refers to an odor compared with a familiar condiment. What is the agent?

Mustard gas is part of the history of chemical warfare, while an industrial method transformed fertilizer production by combining atmospheric nitrogen with hydrogen under high pressure to synthesize ammonia. What is this process called?
These molecules consist of a nitrogenous base attached to a sugar and one or more phosphate groups. They serve as the monomers of DNA and RNA, joining through phosphodiester bonds. What are they?
Among Nucleotides, which molecule contains adenine, ribose, and three phosphate groups and is widely known as the cell’s primary energy currency?
This lubricating fluid is produced mainly by glands around the mouth. It helps dissolve chemicals for taste, begins starch digestion, and contains antimicrobial substances.
Which enzyme in saliva begins carbohydrate digestion in the mouth by breaking starch into smaller sugars? Its activity is reduced by the acidic conditions of the stomach.
In computer science, what is the general term for a finite, precisely specified sequence of instructions that produces an output or solves a computational problem?

An algorithm can be carried out by an abstract computational model with an unbounded tape, a read/write head, and a finite set of rules for changing states. What is this model, named after the British mathematician who introduced it?

This elastic polymeric material can be harvested as latex from trees or manufactured in synthetic forms such as neoprene. Sulfur cross-linking can strengthen it through vulcanization, and its flexibility makes it useful in tires and elastic bands; what is this material called?
In rubber processing, an American inventor discovered that heating the material with sulfur could make it stronger and more durable, a treatment known as vulcanization. Who was this inventor?

Geologists use this collective name for loose particles such as sand, silt, pebbles, and mud that can be carried by water, wind, or ice. After deposition, this material may be compacted or cemented into rock. What is it called?
As a glacier moves, it can entrain sediment and other debris as till, then leave that unsorted material in elongated ridges at its margins or terminus. What are these glacial deposits called?
This medical procedure is intended to provide permanent contraception by preventing reproduction, unlike temporary methods that must be used repeatedly. What is it called?
In male sterilization, a surgeon cuts or seals the vas deferens so sperm cannot enter the semen. What is this procedure called?

For a balanced reversible process, this quantity is obtained by dividing product concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients by the corresponding reactant terms. At a specified temperature, it is denoted K and describes the composition when forward and reverse rates match. What is this quantity?

For a mixture that has not yet reached the point where forward and reverse rates balance, chemists calculate this quantity using the same concentration-and-stoichiometric-power form as the equilibrium constant. Comparing it with K helps predict which direction the net change will proceed. What is this quantity called?

Used for tasks such as surveying crops, observing wildfires, and gathering information in hazardous areas, this aircraft has no pilot aboard and may be guided from the ground or fly autonomously. What is this type of aircraft called?

In Federal Aviation Administration terminology, an unmanned aerial vehicle refers to the aircraft itself, while the broader operation includes the aircraft along with the equipment needed to control and support it. What is this complete combination called?

Produced by pancreatic beta cells, this peptide hormone binds a receptor with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity and promotes glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis, lowering blood glucose. Its deficiency underlies type 1 diabetes; what hormone is it?

When insulin is produced in pancreatic beta cells, it is first formed as proinsulin. Cleavage removes a connecting segment that is released alongside mature insulin and can be measured to assess the body’s own insulin production; what is this segment called?

The universe’s expansion has been speeding up, and cosmological measurements attribute roughly 68 percent of the universe’s total contents to a poorly understood component. What is this component called?

In the late 1990s, observations relevant to dark energy compared the brightness of distant stellar explosions with predictions for a universe whose expansion was slowing down. Which class of standardizable explosions provided key evidence that cosmic expansion is accelerating?

Usually transmitted when saliva from an infected mammal enters a bite wound, this nearly always fatal viral disease can travel through the nervous system and cause agitation, difficulty swallowing, and hydrophobia. What disease is it?
In 1885, after a boy named Joseph Meister was bitten by a rabid dog, this French chemist and microbiologist administered a pioneering post-exposure vaccine against rabies. Who was he?
These segmented, ribbon-shaped parasitic flatworms commonly mature in the intestines of vertebrates, including humans and pigs. What are these parasites called?

Tapeworms lack a digestive tract and absorb nutrients through their outer covering. What is the name of the anterior anchoring organ, often equipped with suckers and sometimes hooks, that attaches one to its host’s intestine?

This inherited group of disorders results from gene variants that produce abnormal hemoglobin, which can make red blood cells rigid and crescent-shaped. The misshapen cells may break down early or obstruct small blood vessels, causing anemia and episodes of pain. What is this condition?

In sickle cell disease, a person who inherits one HbS gene and one HbA gene generally has a condition distinct from the disease itself. This inherited status is associated with partial protection against severe malaria, but it does not guarantee immunity. What is it called?

This peptide messenger is released by four small endocrine glands on the back of the thyroid when blood calcium levels fall. It raises blood calcium through effects on bone and kidneys and by stimulating production of active vitamin D. What is it?
Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium partly by increasing bone resorption through signals to bone-forming cells. What are the multinucleated cells that break down mineralized bone called?

This element has atomic number 14 and the chemical symbol Si. A brittle, blue-gray metalloid, it is the principal semiconductor used in conventional microchips and many solar cells. What element is it?
In 1823, this Swedish chemist first prepared and characterized Silicon in pure form, despite the element’s strong affinity for oxygen. Who was he?

Elemental Silicon is a semiconductor, but its synthetic polymer relatives are used in sealants and flexible elastomers. What name is given to polymers with backbones made of alternating silicon and oxygen atoms and organic side groups?

These chemical messengers include proteins such as insulin and lipids such as testosterone, and they regulate processes throughout the body through endocrine signaling. What is the natural name for this class of molecules?

Among Hormones, which peptide is made in the hypothalamus and secreted by the posterior pituitary, where it helps trigger uterine contractions and milk ejection and is also associated with social bonding?

These viruses reproduce by infecting bacterial cells, and many attach to their hosts before injecting genetic material. The T2 virus used in a famous study of viral heredity belongs to this group; what is the group called?

In a landmark 1952 study, researchers used bacteriophage with DNA labeled by radioactive phosphorus and protein coats labeled by radioactive sulfur to infect E. coli, finding that DNA entered the bacterial cells. What is this study commonly called?

This prevailing cosmological model describes the universe’s evolution from an extremely hot, dense early state through expansion and cooling. Evidence for it includes galaxy redshifts, light-element abundances, and relic radiation. What is the model called?
The Big Bang theory incorporates this proposed early period of accelerated expansion to explain the universe’s observed uniformity and near-flat geometry. What is this process called?

A major piece of evidence supporting the Big Bang theory is nearly uniform radiation across the sky, with a temperature of about 2.7 kelvin and a spectrum characteristic of a hot early universe. What is this radiation called?

In 1922, this mathematician derived equations describing a universe that could expand or contract, years before Edwin Hubble published observational evidence of expansion. His work helped establish a mathematical foundation for the Big Bang theory. Who was he?

Supernova redshift measurements revealed that cosmic expansion is accelerating, a finding incorporated into the Big Bang theory by invoking a still-unexplained component estimated to make up about 68% of the universe. What is this component called?

This chemical element has atomic number 47 and the symbol Ag, and it has the highest electrical conductivity of any metal. It tarnishes when it reacts with sulfur-containing compounds; which element is it?
A crystalline compound of silver, this substance is dispersed in clouds to encourage ice formation and was also used in photographic materials. What is the compound?
Which halogen has atomic number 17 and symbol Cl, sits between fluorine and bromine in the periodic table, and is encountered as a yellow-green diatomic gas used in bleach and pool sanitation?
Chlorine is manufactured at industrial scale by electrolyzing concentrated brine, with sodium hydroxide and hydrogen as important coproducts. What is the name of this industrial process?

Chlorine was released by German forces in April 1915 during a major attack in the Flemish salient, opening a gap in Allied lines on the Western Front. What battle is associated with this first large-scale use of poison gas in World War I?

What general term describes a substance that deforms continuously when subjected to shear stress instead of maintaining a fixed shape? This class of matter includes both liquids and gases, whose motion can be modeled using the Navier–Stokes equations.

In the Navier–Stokes equations, what property accounts for a fluid’s internal resistance to shear and flow? The Reynolds number compares inertial effects with effects governed by this property, and setting it to zero yields the idealized Euler equations.

Commissioned for a German knight after he was maimed at the 1504 siege of Landshut, this articulated metal prosthesis is renowned as an early example of sophisticated replacement technology. By what name is the device known?
answer: Iron Hand of Götz von Berlichingen

question: The Iron Hand of Götz von Berlichingen was made after its owner suffered a battlefield injury in 1504. During the siege of which Bavarian city did he lose his hand?

This extinct human relative lived across Eurasia and disappeared roughly 40,000 years ago. Genetic studies show that it interbred with the ancestors of many people alive today; what group is described?

When researchers analyze DNA to identify inherited fragments from Neanderthals, what technique can amplify a target DNA segment before sequencing? It uses repeated heating and cooling in a thermal cycler and a heat-stable enzyme such as Taq.
What is the name of the elongated concentration of stars that crosses a galaxy’s central region and gives a barred spiral its defining structure?
In the Hubble tuning fork, galaxies with a Galactic bar are classified on the lower branch as barred spirals; what two-letter designation marks this classification?

Near Earth’s surface, this quantity describes how quickly a freely falling object’s velocity changes under Earth’s gravitational pull. It is conventionally approximated as 9.8 meters per second squared; what is the quantity called?

In discussions of acceleration due to gravity, a fixed reference value of exactly 9.80665 meters per second squared is used instead of a locally measured value that varies slightly with latitude and elevation. What is this conventional value called?

Born in Vienna in 1887, this Austrian theoretical physicist developed wave mechanics and formulated the equation that describes the evolution of a quantum wave function. He shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac and later proposed a famous thought experiment involving a cat. Who was he?

Erwin Schrödinger developed this approach to quantum theory in the 1920s, describing particles by mathematical functions spread through space rather than by discrete matrices. What is this approach called?

Erwin Schrödinger formulated this equation, whose time-dependent form describes how a quantum system’s wave function evolves. Its solutions help predict the probabilities of measurement outcomes. What is the equation called?
In this 1944 book, Erwin Schrödinger examined heredity through the lens of physics and discussed how genetic information might be carried by an “aperiodic crystal.” What is the title?

In natural convection, engineers use this dimensionless quantity to compare buoyancy-driven forces with viscous resistance. Its value depends on properties such as gravity, thermal expansion, a characteristic length, and the fluid’s kinematic viscosity. What is this number?

In the Grashof number, this effect is compared with viscous forces. Heating makes fluid expand and become less dense, so gravity causes it to rise relative to cooler, denser fluid; what is this effect called?
This endangered great ape is native to forests south of the Congo River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and is closely related to the common chimpanzee. What species is it?
The bonobo’s range lies south of this major Central African river, which flows westward into the Atlantic Ocean. What river is it?
Which group of large waterfowl belongs to the genus *Cygnus* in the family Anatidae, and has geese and ducks among its closest relatives?
In Sibelius’s *Lemminkäinen Suite*, an English-horn solo portrays a bird on the river of the Finnish underworld. What is the movement called, in one of the best-known musical works depicting swans?
Swans often form long-lasting pairs, but their clutch size varies. What numerical range is typical for a single clutch?

Thomas Eakins portrayed Samuel Gross and Hayes Agnew at work in separate scenes set in nineteenth-century operating theaters. What is the name of the broad medical profession practiced by these men, whose members diagnose and treat illness?
Physicians at Jefferson Medical College are shown in an 1875 Thomas Eakins painting of a surgeon leading an operation on a patient's thigh before an audience. Which work is it?

This dense, lustrous, highly malleable noble metal has atomic number 79 and the chemical symbol Au. Its resistance to corrosion has made it useful in jewelry and electrical contacts; what element is it?
A naturally occurring solid solution of Gold and silver can vary in the proportions of the two metals and was used to make ancient coins. What is this alloy called?
Gold resists nitric acid by itself, but it can be dissolved by a highly corrosive mixture of concentrated nitric and hydrochloric acids. What is this mixture called?

In a widely used 1951 citrate-reduction procedure, sodium citrate helps produce a stable colloid of Gold nanoparticles. Named for the researcher who led the work, what is this synthesis procedure called?

Gold’s role in this monetary arrangement involved linking currency values to a fixed quantity of metal, with participating systems maintaining reserves. What arrangement was effectively abandoned internationally after the 1971 Nixon shock?
What term describes a gravitationally bound pair of luminous celestial objects that orbit their common center of mass?
In the binary star system whose primary is the brightest star in Earth’s night sky, the companion is a faint white dwarf nicknamed the Pup. What is the companion’s standard designation?

Developed in 1935 to quantify earthquakes in Southern California, this logarithmic scale estimates quake size from seismic-wave recordings and has largely been superseded by a method based on seismic moment. What is it called?
The Richter magnitude scale was introduced in 1935 by this American seismologist, who developed it with Beno Gutenberg at Caltech. Who was he?

Which operating-system family began as a Bell Labs project in the late 1960s, was later rewritten in C, and became known for combining small programs through pipes? Its portability helped it spread well beyond its original research setting.

Unix was developed at Bell Labs alongside the C programming language. Which computer scientist co-developed Unix with Ken Thompson and later coauthored *The C Programming Language* with Brian Kernighan?

What animals are the largest living land mammals and the only surviving members of the family Elephantidae? Their three living species are recognized by features including a prehensile trunk and tusks.
In adult male elephants, what is the name of the period of elevated testosterone and increased aggression that can help them compete for dominance and reproductive success?
Elephants communicate using some calls that travel long distances and fall below the range of human hearing. What is the term for sound at these very low frequencies?

This invariant sets the rate at which electromagnetic radiation and gravitational waves propagate through empty space, and special relativity assigns it the same value for all inertial observers. Its exact value is 299,792,458 meters per second. What is this quantity?

The speed of light in vacuum provides the fixed reference for defining this SI base unit: it is the distance light travels in vacuum during 1/299,792,458 of a second. Which unit of length is defined this way?

For a transparent material, the speed of light in vacuum divided by its speed through that material gives a dimensionless quantity. For visible light in glass, this value is typically around 1.5. What is this optical quantity?

The speed of light in vacuum was shown to be finite through an astronomical timing argument in 1676. This Danish astronomer explained shifts in predicted eclipses of Jupiter’s moon Io by accounting for light’s travel time as the distance between Earth and Jupiter changed. Who was he?

Formed from the remains of prehistoric organisms buried and transformed by heat and pressure over geological time, these energy sources include coal, petroleum, and natural gas. What is the collective name for this group?
Among fossil fuels, which colorless, odorless fuel is composed mainly of methane and is commonly piped to homes for cooking and heating?
A rotating cylinder carries a continuous helical surface, trapping water between its turns and lifting it along an inclined trough. What is this water-raising machine called?
In an Archimedean screw, what is the name for the spiral blade-like surface wound around the central shaft that forms pockets to carry water upward?

This atmospheric sound may be heard as a sharp crack nearby or a long rumble farther away. It is produced when a lightning discharge rapidly heats the surrounding air, causing it to expand; what is this sound called?

Thunder begins with a sudden pressure disturbance created when lightning rapidly heats the surrounding air. What is the name for this abrupt pressure disturbance as it moves outward before fading into ordinary sound?
Devised in 1822, this ordinal scale ranks ten reference minerals by their resistance to scratching, from the softest mineral at 1 to the hardest at 10. What is this mineral-hardness scale?
On the Mohs scale, this aluminum oxide mineral ranks 9, just below the hardest reference mineral. Its gem varieties include ruby and sapphire; what is it?
This positively charged antiparticle has the same mass as an electron and is emitted in a particular type of radioactive decay. What is it called?
In this nuclear process, a proton changes into a neutron while emitting a positron and an electron neutrino. What is the process called?
This muscular digestive organ lies between the esophagus and small intestine, temporarily stores meals, and uses acid and enzymes to break food down. What is it?
In the stomach, chief cells release this protein-digesting enzyme in an inactive form called pepsinogen, which gastric acid activates. What is the enzyme?

NASA began this crewed lunar exploration effort after Project Gemini to fulfill John F. Kennedy’s goal of landing people on the Moon and returning them safely. It achieved the first human lunar landing in July 1969. What was this effort called?

During the Apollo Program, which mission became the first crewed flight to leave low Earth orbit and orbit another celestial body? Frank Borman, James Lovell, and William Anders circled the Moon on this mission in December 1968.

In the Apollo Program, which mission had its lunar landing canceled after an oxygen-tank explosion on the way to the Moon? Its crew returned safely after using the lunar module as a temporary lifeboat.
In the ancient world, this horse-drawn vehicle combined a light frame with spoked wheels and served in warfare, transport, ceremonies, and racing. What was this vehicle called?

In the history of the chariot, which battle between the forces of Ramesses II of Egypt and the Hittite king Muwatalli II is often cited as the largest clash of chariots? Fought near the Orontes River around 1274 BCE, it was followed eventually by one of the earliest surviving peace treaties.

For a particle undergoing Brownian motion at thermal equilibrium, this formula states that its diffusion coefficient is proportional to its response to an applied force, with the proportionality set by temperature and Boltzmann’s constant. What is this formula called?

The Einstein–Smoluchowski relation links a particle’s diffusion coefficient to its response to an applied force and to thermal energy. What transport property is defined as the particle’s drift velocity per unit applied force?

Instead of supplying a weakened or inactivated pathogen, this immunization approach gives some host cells temporary instructions to make a chosen antigen. The resulting antigen prompts antibody and other immune-cell responses. What genetic-immunization technology is this?

In COVID-19 versions of an mRNA vaccine, host cells translate the delivered instructions into a harmless component of the coronavirus’s outer coat. This viral structure binds ACE2 and helps the virus enter cells. What component is produced for the immune system to recognize?

In general relativity, this rank-two curvature quantity is formed by subtracting one-half the Ricci scalar times the metric from the Ricci curvature. Its covariant divergence vanishes, and it serves as a geometric quantity alongside the stress-energy tensor. What is it?
