The Einstein tensor occupies the geometric side of a fundamental relation in general relativity, where it is proportional to the stress-energy tensor by 8πG/c⁴; a cosmological-constant term can also be included. What is this relation called?

Built across the Yangtze River near Sandouping in Hubei, this hydroelectric megaproject created a reservoir extending far upstream. Its construction required relocating more than a million people. What dam is it?

The Three Gorges Dam spans this river, which flows eastward across China from the Tibetan Plateau and empties into the East China Sea near Shanghai. It is the longest river in China. Which river is it?

Giuseppe Piazzi discovered this body in 1801, and it was initially classified as a planet before later being categorized as an asteroid. It is now the only confirmed dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt.
After studying Vesta, NASA’s ion-propelled spacecraft entered orbit around Ceres in 2015. What was the name of this mission, which explored both bodies?
This isolated, steep-sided mountain on Ceres rises about four kilometers and is thought to be a cryovolcanic dome. What is the name of this prominent formation?

What branch of physics studies light and its interactions, including reflection and refraction by lenses and prisms? It also encompasses historical theories that treated light as streams of particles.

In the history of Optics, what 1704 book by Isaac Newton reports experiments with prisms and examines the refraction and colors of light? Its title is a Latinized spelling distinct from the name of the field.

This primate group is native chiefly to Central and South America and includes capuchins and long-armed, branch-swinging species. Some members have fully prehensile tails, an adaptation that lets them grasp branches. What is this group commonly called?

Within New World monkeys, this family includes spider monkeys, howler monkeys, woolly monkeys, and muriquis. Its members have grasping tails that can help support them as they move through trees. What is the family called?

What web-based cartographic service combines interactive road displays and route directions with satellite imagery and ground-level panoramic views? Its imagery is also used in location-guessing games such as GeoGuessr.
In Google Maps, what small yellow figure can users drag onto a map to reveal locations with ground-level panoramic imagery?

This viral illness often begins in childhood and can damage motor neurons, causing acute flaccid paralysis. In severe cases, weakness of the breathing muscles once made mechanical ventilation in an iron lung necessary. What is the disease?

Which American medical researcher developed an inactivated-virus vaccine against Poliomyelitis, with support from the March of Dimes? Large field trials of his vaccine were declared successful in 1955.

U.S. Air Force projects Sign, Grudge, and Blue Book investigated reports of this kind of sighting. The term is commonly used for an aerial observation that observers cannot identify and is often associated in popular culture with alien spacecraft. What is the standard name for the phenomenon?

The U.S. Air Force ran this investigation from 1952 to 1969, compiling and evaluating reports of an unidentified flying object. Headquartered at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, it was the service’s third major study of these reports. What was the program called?
In digital logic, what combinational circuit produces a sum from two-valued digit inputs? Common designs include one that adds two input bits and another that also accounts for an incoming carry.
In a binary adder, which design accepts two operand bits plus a carry-in from a previous position and produces both a sum bit and a carry-out?

In a ferromagnet, the path traced while increasing an applied magnetic field differs from the path traced while reducing it, so the material’s magnetization depends on its previous treatment. What is this phenomenon, which more generally describes a system whose state depends on its history?

On a ferromagnet’s Hysteresis curve, a specimen can retain magnetization after the applied field is removed. What quantity describes the magnitude of the reverse magnetic field needed to reduce that residual magnetization to zero?

What broad family of measurement techniques determines reaction enthalpy, heat capacity, or phase-transition properties by measuring heat exchanged during a physical or chemical process? Its apparatus can range from an insulated cup to a sealed combustion vessel or a temperature-scanning instrument.

In calorimetry, which technique holds a sample cell at constant temperature while successive small injections of a ligand into a macromolecule-containing solution produce measurable heat signals? Analyzing those signals as the ligand binds can yield the interaction’s affinity and thermodynamic parameters.

In cold regions and high mountains, snowfall that outpaces melting compacts into a persistent mass of land ice that flows downhill under gravity. As it moves, this body can carve U-shaped valleys and reshape the surrounding terrain. What is it?
As a glacier advances and later melts back, it can leave a ridge of unsorted sediment along its side or near its farthest extent. What is this landform, deposited directly by the ice?

What is the term for a fast-moving mixture of water and volcanic ash, rock, and other debris that rushes down a volcano’s slopes and through nearby valleys? It can be triggered by an eruption or by heavy rain.
During the 1985 eruption of Nevado del Ruiz, a lahar swept down the Lagunillas River valley and buried this Colombian town, killing more than 20,000 people. Which town was devastated?

This animal is the largest living member of the deer family, and adult males grow broad, palm-shaped antlers. It inhabits boreal and mixed forests across northern Eurasia and North America. What animal is it?

Moose are more commonly seen in Katahdin Woods and Waters than in this coastal Maine preserve on Mount Desert Island. Its landmarks include Cadillac Mountain and the Beehive Loop, whose route features metal rungs. What place is it?
In a vapor-compression cooling system, this working fluid absorbs heat as it evaporates and releases heat as it condenses. What is the general name for the fluid used in refrigeration and heat pumps?
Refrigerant circulates through this device to carry heat out of a room or vehicle cabin. Often described as a heat pump operating in reverse, what device cools indoor spaces?
In a valence-bond model, one s atomic orbital mixes with two p orbitals to form three coplanar orbitals, while one p orbital remains unhybridized. What is this orbital-mixing scheme called?
At each carbon center in ethene, sp² hybridization produces three bonding directions in one plane, with ideal angles of about 120°. What shape do these directions define around each carbon?

What domesticated ruminant is raised in flocks for its fleece and meat, and has supported major wool industries in Australia and New Zealand? Some breeds are recognized for their distinctive spiral horns.
Among Sheep, which Hungarian breed is known for its long, corkscrew-shaped horns? It is traditionally associated with the Hortobágy region of the Great Hungarian Plain.

This natural electrical discharge can occur between clouds or between a cloud and the ground. Its rapid heating of the surrounding air produces the sound of thunder. What atmospheric phenomenon is this?

In a 1953 laboratory study of the chemical origins of life, researchers circulated water vapor, methane, ammonia, and hydrogen through an apparatus and exposed the mixture to electrical sparks meant to recreate Lightning on early Earth. What was this study called?

In analytical chemistry, this small laboratory vessel is commonly made of porcelain and can withstand intense heat while a sample such as a metal is strongly heated. What is this heat-resistant container called?
A crucible may be heated over an adjustable open-flame laboratory device invented by a German chemist and commonly fueled by natural gas. What is this device called?
Published in 1704, this treatise presents an experimental investigation of light, including its colors, reflection, refraction, diffraction, and the production of spectra. What is the work called?
In Opticks, which English scientist used prism experiments to argue that white sunlight contains rays of different colors and refrangibility?

In the 19th century, an Austrian monk studied this self-pollinating garden crop by tracking traits such as seed shape, flower color, and pod form across generations. Its distinct varieties helped reveal predictable patterns of inheritance.

In monastery garden experiments, this Augustinian friar cross-pollinated pea plants and recorded how traits appeared in successive generations. His findings, published in 1866, later became foundational to genetics; who was he?

This fungal disease affects hibernating bats and can cause mass mortality by disrupting their hibernation. It is associated with a cold-tolerant pathogen that grows on bats’ skin. What is the disease called?
In White-nose syndrome, the causative fungus grows on bats during hibernation and can trigger repeated arousals that drain their energy reserves. What is the scientific name of this pathogen?
In bone tissue, this cell secretes osteoid, the collagen-rich organic matrix, and helps it mineralize. What cell type is this?
Osteoblasts secrete this collagen-rich organic precursor of bone before mineral salts are deposited in it. What is this matrix called?
This planet’s outermost solid layer lies above the mantle. It forms part of the lithosphere, which also includes a portion of the upper mantle. What is this layer?
Beneath Earth’s crust, what process transfers heat as warmer material rises and cooler material sinks through slowly flowing rock? This circulation helps drive tectonic plates.

These compact remnants can be left when a supernova collapses the core of a massive progenitor, producing an object roughly city-sized but with more mass than the Sun. Their extreme density makes degeneracy pressure crucial in resisting further collapse. What are these objects called?

Among neutron stars, this one is the rapidly rotating remnant of the supernova observed in 1054, located at the center of the nebula in Taurus catalogued by Charles Messier as M1. It spins about 30 times per second and emits regular pulses of radiation. What is it called?

This French naturalist published *Philosophie zoologique* in 1809 and argued that organisms could change through the use and disuse of their organs, with acquired changes passed to offspring. Who was he?

Jean-Baptiste Lamarck argued that an organ’s use or disuse could alter it and that modifications acquired during life could be inherited by offspring. What eponymous name is given to this evolutionary theory?

What term names weather events in which powerful winds raise and transport large quantities of fine, dry particles from the ground? They occur on Earth and Mars, where they can sometimes obscure nearly the whole planet.

In November 1971, a spacecraft arrived at Mars while a planet-wide dust storm obscured most surface features. After conditions cleared, it became the first spacecraft to orbit another planet; what was the mission called?

In the late nineteenth century, supporters of AC and DC competed over which electrical system would power homes and businesses. Prominently involving Edison, Westinghouse, and Tesla, what was this rivalry called?

During the War of the Currents, this American industrialist backed alternating-current power and secured rights to use Nikola Tesla’s AC patents. He had earlier become known for developing the railway air brake; who was he?

Introduced in 1908, this affordable automobile had a rugged design and became known by the nickname “Tin Lizzie.” Produced in enormous numbers, it helped make car ownership attainable for ordinary Americans. What vehicle was it?

Production of the Ford Model T was transformed at this Ford factory, which opened in 1910 in a suburb just north of Detroit. The company introduced its moving assembly-line system there in 1913. What was the factory called?

This rocky planet is the Solar System’s smallest and innermost world, completing an orbit in about 88 Earth days. Its 3:2 spin-orbit resonance makes one solar day last about 176 Earth days; what planet is it?
Mercury’s largest impact basin spans about 1,550 kilometers across. What is the established name of this vast feature?

When Mercury’s observed orbit is compared with the Newtonian prediction that includes perturbations from other planets, its closest-approach direction advances slightly more than expected. General relativity accounts for this residual; what orbital phenomenon is being described?
In a circuit, this quantity is defined as the voltage across an element divided by the current through it. Measured in ohms, it characterizes how strongly the element opposes the flow of charge.
Electrical resistance is expressed in an SI unit named for the German physicist whose law relates voltage, current, and resistance. What is this unit, symbolized by Ω?
Electrical resistance has a reciprocal circuit quantity that describes how easily current flows; in SI, this reciprocal is measured in siemens. What is this quantity, commonly denoted G?

Unlike ordinary electrical resistance, a material in this state can carry steady current with zero resistance below a critical temperature. The Meissner effect, in which it expels magnetic fields, is another hallmark of this phenomenon; what is it called?
Which large pheasant species native to South Asia has males with a blue-green neck and a long courtship train marked by eye-shaped spots?

In Indian peafowl, males’ elaborate, eye-spotted trains are costly to produce and can hinder escape, yet may reliably reveal their condition to potential mates. What evolutionary signaling concept explains how such a costly trait can remain an honest signal because lower-quality individuals are less able to sustain it?

This simple machine is a sloping surface used to raise or lower a load. By spreading a vertical lift over a longer path, it reduces the force needed, ideally without reducing the work done. What is it called?

For an inclined plane, compare the distance traveled along the ramp with the vertical height gained; the resulting dimensionless ratio measures how much the machine multiplies input force. What is this quantity called?

This electrostatic law describes the force between two point charges at rest. The force’s magnitude is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them; a French military engineer who used a torsion balance published it in 1785. What is the law called?
In Coulomb’s law, the symbol k represents a proportionality factor for the electrostatic force. In a vacuum, its value is approximately 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²; what is this factor called?

Coulomb’s law and this electrostatic result can be derived from one another. It relates the total electric flux through a closed surface to the charge enclosed within that surface, divided by the vacuum permittivity; what is this result called?

What is the common name for the reflexive expulsion of air through the nose and mouth, often triggered by irritation in the nasal passages? It is the action that commonly prompts someone nearby to say “Bless you.”

Unlike sneezing triggered by nasal irritation, some people begin sneezing when suddenly exposed to bright light, such as stepping out of a dim room into sunshine. What is this light-triggered tendency called?

This cation forms when a water molecule accepts a proton and appears alongside hydroxide when two water molecules self-ionize. It is the strongest acid species ordinarily represented as persisting in aqueous solution.

In water, acids stronger than hydronium ion transfer their protons to solvent molecules, so they do not persist in their original form. What named phenomenon describes this solvent-imposed limit on apparent acid strength?

Which 19th-century Russian chemist organized elements by atomic weight and recurring chemical properties, leaving gaps in his chart for elements not yet discovered? He used those gaps to predict the properties of what he called eka-aluminium, eka-boron, and eka-silicon.

What chart did Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev publish in 1869, arranging elements to show recurring chemical properties? Its empty spaces helped him predict the existence and properties of several undiscovered elements.

This French chemist used quantitative experiments to argue that combustion involves a component of air rather than the release of phlogiston. His work also helped establish conservation of mass and modern chemical nomenclature. Who was he?

In Antoine Lavoisier’s explanation of combustion, what element did he identify as the active component of air involved in burning? It makes up about 21% of Earth’s atmosphere and combines with hydrogen to form water.
A dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scan estimates how much mineral matter is present in the skeleton, helping clinicians assess skeletal strength and fracture risk. What is this measurement called?
When bone density falls substantially, which skeletal disease makes bones weak and brittle and increases the risk of fractures, especially in older adults and postmenopausal women?

An early-19th-century Italian scientist argued that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, helping distinguish atoms from molecules. The constant for particle counts per mole later took his name; who was he?
In modern chemistry, what SI base unit for amount of substance is associated with Amedeo Avogadro’s particle-count constant and contains exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ specified entities?
In alkenes, this linkage joins two atoms of atomic number 6 and restricts rotation around their shared axis. Its structure has a head-on overlap and a sideways overlap of unhybridized p orbitals.

In a carbon–carbon double bond, what orbital arrangement gives each participating atom a trigonal-planar geometry with three electron domains? This arrangement leaves one p orbital on each atom perpendicular to the plane, enabling sideways overlap.
Which Danish physicist reported in 1820 that a compass needle turned when placed near a wire carrying electric current? His observation helped establish that electricity and magnetism are connected.

In Hans Christian Ørsted’s 1820 experiment, a compass needle shifted when current flowed through a nearby wire. What invisible influence produced by the current caused the needle to move, and is measured in teslas?

In the water cycle, these visible atmospheric formations appear when moist air cools and water vapor condenses onto tiny particles. Their heights and shapes vary from low, flat layers to puffy heaps and thin, icy streaks; what are they?
Within the broad family of Clouds, which high-altitude type is recognized by its thin, wispy, featherlike streaks and is composed mainly of ice crystals?

These circulating human cells deliver oxygen from the lungs to tissues and help return carbon dioxide to the lungs. Mature examples have a biconcave disk shape and lack a nucleus; what are they called?
Inside red blood cells, what iron-containing protein binds oxygen for transport and helps give blood its red color? Its oxygen-binding groups are called heme.
This group 1 element has atomic number 3 and is the least dense of all metals. It is a soft, silvery solid that reacts vigorously with water. What element is it?

The element lithium supplies mobile ions in a rechargeable cell design, where ions move between electrodes as the cell charges and discharges. Widely used in phones and electric vehicles, what technology is this?

This laboratory vessel has a stopper at its broad upper opening and a narrow stem with a tap, allowing immiscible liquid layers to be separated by draining one layer at a time. What is this apparatus called?

A separatory funnel has a narrow outlet fitted with a manually operated tap; opening it lets the lower liquid layer drain while the upper layer remains in the vessel. What is this tap commonly called?

In a plant’s epidermis, this microscopic opening allows carbon dioxide to enter and oxygen and water vapor to leave. Its size is regulated by surrounding specialized cells, helping balance gas exchange with water loss. What is this opening called?
A stoma is bordered by a pair of specialized epidermal structures that change shape as their water content shifts, controlling whether the pore opens or closes. What are these structures called?

What is the name for a family of custom-designed, ARM-based system-on-chip processors that began replacing Intel processors in many Mac computers in 2020? The M1 was the first chip in this transition.
Within Apple silicon, which chip debuted in November 2020 and was first used in the MacBook Air, 13-inch MacBook Pro, and Mac mini?

What five-year expedition began in 1831 aboard a British naval survey ship, charted coastlines including those of South America, and visited the Galápagos Islands? Its naturalist’s observations helped shape later ideas about evolution.
During the HMS Beagle voyage, which naval captain commanded the surveying expedition and later published accounts of the journey?

A raised object has this quantity relative to a chosen height, and near Earth’s surface its change is calculated from mass, gravitational acceleration, and height. What broad physical quantity is associated with position or configuration rather than motion?
Potential energy stored in an ideal spring depends on the spring’s stiffness and the square of its displacement from its relaxed length. What specific form of stored energy is represented by ½kx²?
A grooved wheel mounted on an axle lets a taut rope pass over it, redirecting an applied force and sometimes reducing the effort needed to lift a load. What is this simple machine called?

In a pulley arrangement for hoisting a heavy load, some wheels are fixed to a support while others move with the load, and a rope passes between them. What is this compound lifting system, whose mechanical advantage depends on the number of rope segments supporting the moving load?

In animal behavior, what term describes a species-typical pattern performed without being taught, such as the migratory restlessness of hand-reared birds or a goose’s stereotyped effort to roll an egg back to its nest?

In discussions of instinct, what ethological term names a stereotyped sequence triggered by a specific stimulus, such as a greylag goose continuing its egg-rolling motion even after the egg has been removed?

This six-carbon monosaccharide has the formula C6H12O6 and serves as a major fuel broken down during cellular respiration. In humans, rising blood concentrations prompt pancreatic beta cells to release a hormone that helps it enter cells. What sugar is it?

During cellular respiration, cells use energy released from glucose to make this molecule, the cell’s primary energy currency. Its phosphate groups store transferable chemical energy, and breaking off the terminal phosphate can help power cellular work. What molecule is it?
This colorless, odorless element has atomic number 18 and makes up just under one percent of Earth’s atmosphere. It is also used as a fill gas in some radiation detectors. What is the element?

Argon can serve as the fill gas in this detector, where a single ionizing event triggers a discharge that spreads through the gas and produces a pulse largely independent of the event’s energy. What gas-filled radiation detector is it?
What broad human endeavor applies knowledge through tools, equipment, machines, and designed systems to solve practical problems? It ranges from simple implements to complex infrastructure.

In Martin Heidegger’s account of modern technology, what term describes the mode of revealing that orders the world as a stock of resources available for use? He also applies this idea to how people can be treated as resources.
What weak carboxylic acid has the molecular formula CH₃COOH and is formed when acetaldehyde is oxidized during ethanol metabolism? Its common household solution is the principal acid in vinegar.
During ethanol metabolism, this two-carbon aldehyde is produced by alcohol dehydrogenase and then oxidized to acetic acid. What is this intermediate?

This American electrical engineer devised a widely used minimum-redundancy prefix-code method for lossless data compression. His research also extended to the mathematical analysis of paper folding; who was he?

David Albert Huffman’s research extended beyond data compression to the study of paper folding, including the geometry of crease patterns and the conditions for folding a sheet flat. What field of study did this work contribute to?
What common name is given to the stout, often densely hairy bees in the genus Bombus, many of which form annual colonies and pollinate flowers as they forage?

Among bumblebees, one European species is commercially raised to pollinate greenhouse crops. Its queens have buff-colored tail tips, unlike the queens of a similar white-tailed species; which species is it?

This quantum-mechanical rule says that the spreads in a particle’s position and momentum cannot simultaneously be made arbitrarily small, and that their product has a lower bound of ħ/2. It describes an intrinsic limit of the theory rather than merely a flaw in measuring equipment.
In the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, the position–momentum bound uses the symbol ħ, equal to h/(2π). What is the conventional name for this barred-h constant?

This class of chemical elements includes boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony, and tellurium. Its members have properties intermediate between metals and nonmetals and are often found near the zigzag boundary on the periodic table. What is this class called?
In discussions of metalloids, which element has the symbol Si and atomic number 14? Its semiconductor properties make it a key material in transistors and microchips.

Launched in 2011 and arriving at Jupiter in 2016, this NASA spacecraft follows a highly elliptical polar orbit to investigate the giant planet’s atmosphere, interior, gravity, and magnetic field. What mission is it?

Juno used its microwave radiometer during close passes to measure the vertical extent of Jupiter’s enormous, centuries-observed anticyclonic storm in the planet’s southern hemisphere. What long-lived storm did it investigate?

Kidney cells use these membrane proteins to let water cross selectively; in collecting ducts, vasopressin can increase their presence at the cell surface and promote water reabsorption. What is the natural name of this water-channel protein family?
In collecting-duct cells, this hormone triggers insertion of Aquaporin-2 into the apical membrane, increasing water reabsorption. Which hormone is responsible for this response?
This Saturnian moon reflects more sunlight than any other known body in the Solar System, and Cassini detected water-rich jets emerging from fractures near its south pole. Which moon is it?
Which NASA-ESA vehicle made repeated close flybys of Enceladus, sampled material from its south-polar plumes, and ended its Saturn mission in 2017 by plunging into the planet’s atmosphere?
Which nutrient-rich upper layer of soil is typically designated the A horizon and contains substantial decomposed organic matter? It generally lies above the subsoil.
In topsoil, what dark organic material forms as leaves, roots, and other biological remains decompose, helping enrich the soil and retain moisture?
In plants, this green pigment captures light energy for photosynthesis and gives most leaves their familiar color. What is it?
The green pigment Chlorophyll has a metal ion at the center of its molecular structure. A shortage of this nutrient can also cause yellowing in older leaves; which element is it?
Which designation describes red cells lacking A and B antigens as well as the Rh antigen, and is commonly regarded as the universal red-cell transfusion option?

In emergency transfusions, O-negative blood type may be selected before the recipient’s group is known because its erythrocytes lack the major A, B, and Rh antigens. What widely used transfusion designation describes this compatibility role?

Which Indian-American astrophysicist derived a limit of about 1.4 solar masses for stable white dwarfs? He received the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics for theoretical studies of the physical processes important to the structure and evolution of stars.

In Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar’s account of how a white dwarf can resist collapse below its maximum stable mass, what quantum-mechanical resistance to compression, arising from the Pauli exclusion principle, counteracts gravity?
Which fundamental interaction is mediated by charged W bosons and neutral Z bosons, has an extremely short range because these particles are massive, and can change one quark type into another?
In the weak nuclear force, what process occurs when a neutron becomes a proton and emits an electron and an electron antineutrino?

Installed in automobile exhaust systems, these devices use platinum-group metal catalysts to convert pollutants such as carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides into less harmful substances. What are these components called?

Catalytic converters can be poisoned by residues from certain fuel additives. Which organometallic anti-knock additive, widely used in gasoline before unleaded fuel became standard, was phased out in part because it damaged these exhaust systems?
What system arranges days into longer periods such as weeks, months, and years so that dates can be recorded and planned? The Roman system reformed under Julius Caesar is one historical example.
Which calendar reform, instituted under Julius Caesar in 45 BCE, used a 365-day year with an extra day every fourth year to keep dates aligned with the seasons?

These events happen when gases, rock fragments, and molten rock escape from Earth’s interior through a vent; molten rock is called magma below the surface and lava once it emerges. They may be quiet flows or explosive blasts that send ash and fragments skyward, and the largest can temporarily cool the climate. What are these events called?

During major explosive volcanic eruptions, which gas can reach the upper atmosphere and form reflective sulfate aerosols that reduce incoming sunlight, causing temporary cooling? Give the name of the gas, not the aerosol.

During World War II, physiologist Ancel Keys led a study at a public university in Minneapolis in which 36 conscientious objectors underwent 24 weeks of severe caloric restriction followed by controlled refeeding. What landmark study investigated the physical and psychological effects of this restriction and recovery?
In the Minnesota Starvation Experiment, which American physiologist directed the study of 36 conscientious objectors and later led the Seven Countries Study on diet and cardiovascular disease?
What descriptive wind-force scale runs from 0 for calm to 12 for hurricane-force winds, assigning levels by the visible effects of wind on land and sea?

The Beaufort scale expresses wind force through numbered descriptions rather than a direct instrument reading. What instrument, often built with rotating cups or a small propeller, measures wind speed directly?
This mineralized connective material forms most of the vertebrate skeleton and is continually remodeled in response to hormonal signals and mechanical loading. What is it?
In bone tissue, the principle that structure and density adapt over time to mechanical stresses is named for which 19th-century German surgeon?
What term describes the quantized motions of atoms within a molecule as they move around their equilibrium positions? These motions can be studied spectroscopically and occur in distinct modes.

In Millie Dresselhaus’s studies of carbon allotropes such as graphite and nanotubes, which spectroscopic technique was used to probe Molecular Vibrations by measuring frequency shifts in scattered light?
Unlike exponential population change, this model accounts for environmental limits, producing an S-shaped curve as a population nears its finite maximum. What is this model called?

In logistic growth, population increase tapers as the population nears a limit imposed by available resources. What is the name for the maximum population an environment can sustain, often represented by K?
These acid systems are stronger than 100-percent sulfuric acid and are often identified by very low values on the Hammett acidity function. What is this class of exceptionally strong acids called?
Among superacids, which reagent is made by combining fluorosulfuric acid with antimony pentafluoride and is known for stabilizing carbocations in solution?

These mineralized connective structures combine collagen fibers with mineral crystals, supporting the body while protecting organs such as the brain and lungs. Their tissue is continually remodeled by cells that build and resorb it. What are the individual skeletal structures exemplified by the femur, tibia, and ribs?

In compact bones, what cylindrical structural units are organized around central canals that carry blood vessels and nerves? These units are characteristic of dense bone tissue, unlike the lattice-like trabeculae of spongy bone.

Born in Rome in 1901, this Italian-American physicist earned his doctorate at the University of Pisa and received the 1938 Nobel Prize in Physics for discoveries involving radioactive elements and slow neutrons. Who was he?

Enrico Fermi led the construction of this experimental reactor beneath Stagg Field, a university football stadium. On December 2, 1942, it achieved the first human-made, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction. What was it called?
These erupting hot springs periodically discharge jets of heated water and steam, often in volcanic regions. Yellowstone National Park is famous for examples such as Old Faithful.
The word “geyser” comes from Geysir, a famous hot spring in this North Atlantic island nation. A 2010 volcanic eruption there disrupted air travel across Europe; which country is it?

In most female mammals, each cell epigenetically silences one of the two copies of the gene-bearing structure that carries many sex-linked genes, helping balance their expression with males. Descendant cells generally retain the same choice, creating a mosaic of cells expressing different genes. What is this process called?

In female cats carrying different pigmentation alleles on their two copies of the sex-linked genetic material, X-chromosome inactivation causes separate skin-cell patches to produce black or orange fur. By what name is this characteristic feline coloration known?
Which gemstone is the traditional birthstone for May and the green variety of the mineral beryl?
Emerald is the green gem variety of a mineral that also occurs as aquamarine and morganite. What is the name of this mineral species?
This black, porous, carbon-rich material is made by heating wood in an environment with little oxygen. It served as the fuel component in traditional gunpowder. What is this material?

In traditional gunpowder, charcoal is combined with potassium nitrate and this yellow, brittle nonmetal. When burned in air, this element produces a pungent gas that can contribute to acid rain. What is it?

In this stereochemical phenomenon, groups attached to a double bond or positioned in a ring are classified by whether they lie on the same side or opposite sides. What is this type of arrangement called?
Cis–trans isomerism belongs to a class of stereoisomerism in which molecules have the same atom-to-atom connectivity but differ in spatial arrangement. What is this broader class called?
In rod-cell outer segments, this light-sensitive G-protein-coupled receptor begins the signaling cascade that supports vision in dim conditions. What is this visual pigment?

Within Rhodopsin, a light-absorbing molecule is attached to the protein component before a photon triggers a change in its shape. What is the name of this molecule’s bent configuration that isomerizes upon absorbing light?

In classical thermodynamics, this equation relates a gas’s pressure and volume to its amount in moles and absolute temperature through the universal gas constant. What is the name of the relation expressed as PV = nRT?

The Ideal Gas Law treats gas particles as having negligible size and no intermolecular attraction. What named equation of state extends it with constants a and b to represent attractions and finite molecular volume?
This southern constellation is traditionally depicted as an archer and contains the Galactic Center of the Milky Way. What is its natural name?
The constellation Sagittarius contains the Milky Way’s center, where astronomers have detected a compact radio source associated with the Galaxy’s supermassive black hole. What is this source called?
Born in Alabama, this American biologist became known for decades of ant research at Harvard and for helping establish the evolutionary study of animal social behavior. Who was this scientist?
E. O. Wilson helped establish a field that uses evolutionary biology to explain social behavior across animal species. What is this field called?

A rapidly rotating column of air extends from a thunderstorm cloud base to Earth’s surface, sometimes lifting dust and debris near the ground. What is this potentially destructive weather phenomenon called?
A tornado’s damage-based rating system was revised for U.S. use in 2007 to better account for damage indicators and construction quality. What is the name of this updated scale?
The central United States has an informal nickname for a region historically associated with frequent tornadoes, particularly across parts of the Great Plains. What is this region commonly called?

Built through collaboration among NASA, ESA, and ASI, this spacecraft began orbiting Saturn in 2004 and concluded its mission by entering the planet’s atmosphere in 2017. It also delivered a separate probe that descended through the atmosphere of Titan. What was the spacecraft called?

The Cassini spacecraft repeatedly observed this icy Saturnian moon ejecting plumes from its south polar region; measurements including silica grains pointed to interactions between its subsurface ocean and rocky seafloor. Which moon became a key target in considering potentially habitable environments beyond Earth?
What predicted phenomenon is a thermal glow produced by quantum effects near a black hole’s event horizon, implying that the black hole can lose mass and eventually evaporate?

The prediction called Hawking radiation holds that black holes have a temperature and emit particles. Which British physicist later wrote *A Brief History of Time* and communicated using a speech synthesizer after developing motor neurone disease?

Farmers use this planned practice by growing different plant species on the same field in a chosen sequence over several seasons or years. By changing which plants are available as hosts, it can help limit certain pests and diseases while supporting soil fertility.

In crop rotation, peas or clover can benefit a crop planted afterward through a biological process carried out by associated soil bacteria. What is the process by which these bacteria convert the main gas in Earth's atmosphere into compounds plants can use?
What severe infectious disease is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, often reaches people through bites from infected rodent fleas, and can take bubonic, septicemic, or pneumonic forms?
One form of plague commonly causes a painful, swollen lymph node, often in the groin, armpit, or neck. What is this characteristic swelling called?
In polluted urban air, nitrogen oxides and other atmospheric pollutants can contribute to a visible haze that lingers when the air does not disperse. What is this form of air pollution called?
Smog can collect near the ground when a warm layer of air lies above cooler surface air, preventing vertical mixing. What meteorological phenomenon is this arrangement called?

In this idealized periodic system, the restoring force is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and points back toward that equilibrium. A mass attached to a spring is a standard example, while a pendulum approximates this behavior for small swings. What is this system called?
For an ideal spring-and-mass simple harmonic oscillator, what named law says that the spring’s restoring force is proportional to its extension or compression and acts in the opposite direction?
This dense transition metal has atomic number 78 and is prized for jewelry. It is also used in automobile catalytic converters to help reduce harmful exhaust emissions. What element is it?
Platinum is a transition metal with atomic number 78. What is its one-letter-capitalized, two-character abbreviation on the periodic table?
In a food chain, what is the name for an organism that hunts, kills, and eats another organism, typically occupying a higher trophic level than its prey?

Unlike a predator that kills its own prey, what is the name for an organism that feeds on carcasses of animals that died naturally or were left behind after a kill? Vultures and flesh flies are examples.
In climate science, some changes trigger effects that strengthen the original change rather than counteracting it. What is the term for this self-reinforcing process?

A positive feedback loop in the climate system occurs when rising temperatures melt bright, reflective sea ice, leaving darker ocean water exposed to absorb more solar energy and drive additional warming. What is the name of this specific feedback?

In this approach, a tiny fuel pellet is rapidly compressed and heated, so its inward-moving material holds the reacting fuel together briefly rather than relying on magnetic fields. In a common indirect-drive setup, lasers heat a hollow metal cylinder, whose X-rays drive the capsule inward. What is this approach called?
In inertial confinement fusion indirect-drive experiments, what hollow metal cylinder surrounds the fuel capsule and converts incoming laser energy into X-rays that drive the capsule’s implosion?

What is the name for a facility established to carry out systematic astronomical observations, often equipped for tracking celestial bodies? In the medieval Islamic world, major examples were established in Baghdad under al-Ma’mun and in Samarkand under Ulugh Beg.
At the observatory he founded in Samarkand in the 15th century, this Timurid ruler patronized astronomers who compiled the influential Zij-i Sultani star catalog. Which ruler is meant?

In quantum theory, this property belongs intrinsically to particles and is not produced by their motion around a point. It has discrete allowed values and the same units as ordinary angular momentum; what is it?

In the study of Spin, a beam of silver atoms passed through an inhomogeneous magnetic field and separated into two discrete components rather than forming a continuous spread. What 1922 investigation demonstrated this quantization?

The connection between Spin and particle statistics implies that identical electrons cannot occupy the same quantum state. What principle, named for the Austrian physicist who formulated it, states this restriction?

This geological structure is a vent or fissure in a planetary crust through which magma, ash, and gases can escape from an underground reservoir. On Earth, such features occur at plate boundaries and hotspots, and they are also found on other worlds. What is this feature?

Volcanoes form along this underwater divergent boundary, where seafloor spreading creates new oceanic crust. This long submarine mountain chain separates the Americas from Europe and Africa. What is this boundary?

Many volcanoes lie along this broad belt around the world's largest ocean, where activity is often associated with convergent boundaries and subduction. The region is also known for frequent earthquakes. What is this belt called?

Volcanoes occur on other planets as well: this enormous shield volcano on Mars rises more than 20 kilometers above the surrounding terrain. It is the largest known mountain in the solar system. What is it called?

When two interacting species each exert selective pressure on the other, producing reciprocal evolutionary changes over generations, what process is this? It can occur in mutualisms as well as antagonistic relationships such as host–parasite interactions.

In a classic proposed case of coevolution, Charles Darwin reasoned that nectar at the base of Madagascar’s exceptionally long-spurred star orchid must be reached by a pollinator with an extraordinarily long feeding tube. What moth species was later identified as that pollinator?

The heart drives this vertebrate connective tissue through vessels, where it delivers oxygen and nutrients and carries metabolic wastes away. It consists of a liquid portion plus red and white cells and clotting fragments; what is it?

Within Blood, which iron-containing protein in red cells binds oxygen reversibly and helps carry it from the lungs to body tissues? Its oxygen binding also contributes to the bright-red appearance of oxygen-rich arterial fluid.

In Blood, what tiny cell fragments formed from megakaryocytes adhere at damaged vessel walls and aggregate as coagulation begins? Unlike red cells that carry oxygen or leukocytes that fight infection, their chief role is forming an initial plug at a wound.

When Blood is centrifuged, what pale-yellow liquid component separates from its cells and platelets? Mostly water, it carries dissolved electrolytes, hormones, glucose, and proteins such as albumin and fibrinogen.
During this physiological process, coordinated uterine contractions cause the cervix to dilate to about 10 centimeters, creating a passage for the baby to be delivered. What is this process called?

In childbirth, this temporary organ is delivered after the baby during the third stage of labor. Attached to the fetus by the umbilical cord, it transfers oxygen and nutrients from the pregnant parent. What is this organ?
This hardware component turns electrical signals into visible images and is found in devices such as phones, televisions, and computers. What is this component called?

An electronic display can use this older technology, which steers an electron beam through a vacuum onto a phosphor-coated surface to form an image. It was common in bulky televisions and computer monitors before flat-panel designs became widespread; what is the technology?
Which thermoplastic fluoropolymer is known for exceptionally low friction and broad chemical resistance, and is commonly used as a nonstick coating on cookware?
Polytetrafluoroethylene is produced by chain-growth polymerization of a fluorinated alkene. What is the name of its two-carbon monomer with the formula C₂F₄?
What medical emergency has ischemic and hemorrhagic forms, arising either when blood flow to the brain is blocked or when a cerebral blood vessel bleeds?
Within the classification of stroke, what subtype occurs when a clot blocks an artery supplying the brain and deprives brain tissue of oxygen, rather than when a vessel ruptures?

For a collection of particles, this location is calculated by weighting each particle's position according to how much matter it contains. The translational motion of an extended body can be analyzed as though the body's entire quantity of matter were concentrated at this point. What is it called?

For an extended body, the center of mass describes its mass-weighted position, while this point is where the body's total weight can be treated as acting. In a uniform gravitational field, the two points coincide. What is this point called?
During protein synthesis, a ribosome reads messenger RNA in groups of three nucleotide bases. Each group specifies an amino acid or a signal to end translation; what is one such group called?
A codon can signal the end of translation instead of specifying an amino acid. What is the name for this type of codon, whose standard mRNA examples are UAA, UAG, and UGA?

In thermodynamics, what is the collective name for physical changes in which a substance shifts between solid, liquid, and gas as temperature or pressure changes? Melting, freezing, and boiling are familiar examples.
On a phase diagram used to describe phase transitions, what is the condition at which solid, liquid, and gas coexist in equilibrium? For water, it occurs at about 0.01 °C.
This widespread wild canid is the principal large predator in Isle Royale’s well-studied ecosystem, where it hunts a large browsing mammal. Which species is it?

In the Isle Royale ecosystem, Gray wolves prey chiefly on this large browsing member of the deer family. Its population, like theirs, is closely studied as part of the island’s predator–prey system. What animal is it?

Dogs are generally considered the first species to enter this long-term human-animal relationship, in which generations adapt to living alongside people rather than an individual animal simply becoming tame. What is this evolutionary process called?
In the history of domestication, which small mammal became useful to early human settlements by hunting rodents? This familiar companion is known for purring and meowing.

This carbon-rich sedimentary rock forms when ancient plant matter becomes peat and is altered by heat and pressure during deep burial. Its ranks include lignite, bituminous rock, and anthracite; what is it?

When coal seams lie near the surface, workers can remove successive layers of overlying earth in long bands to expose them, a method that can cause extensive landscape damage and soil erosion. What is this surface-extraction method called?

Coal can be transported through pipelines by mixing fine particles with water to create a pumpable suspension. A dam failure sent this mixture down West Virginia’s Buffalo Creek in 1972, killing 125 people; what is the mixture called?
A small stray dog from Moscow was selected by Soviet scientists for an orbital flight in 1957. Unlike animals on earlier suborbital missions, this dog became the first animal to orbit Earth.
Laika rode in a sealed cabin aboard this Soviet spacecraft, launched on November 3, 1957, with no plan to return its passenger to Earth. What was the spacecraft called?
Which cultivated members of the genus Gossypium are grown for the soft fibers attached to their seeds? Those fibers are spun into a major natural textile used around the world.
Among cotton plants, which species is commonly called upland cotton? Domesticated in what is now Mexico, it supplies most of the cotton fiber grown worldwide.

For a substance undergoing first-order decay, this characteristic time is calculated by dividing the natural logarithm of 2 by the rate constant. What is the quantity describing the interval in which an unstable sample declines to 50 percent of its initial amount?

In Half-life-based dating of once-living material, which radioactive isotope is continually produced when cosmic rays interact with the atmosphere, then incorporated into organisms while they are alive? Its decay, with a characteristic interval of about 5,730 years, helps estimate when the material stopped exchanging matter with its surroundings.

This thermodynamic state function combines a system’s internal energy with the product of its pressure and volume. It is especially useful for describing heat transfer under constant-pressure conditions. What is this quantity?
When a process at constant pressure absorbs heat, its change in enthalpy is positive. What is this type of heat-absorbing process called?

Changes in enthalpy are expressed in the SI unit of energy, equivalent to a newton-meter. Its name honors the 19th-century physicist who established the mechanical equivalent of heat. What is this unit?
Which highly corrosive mixture is made by combining concentrated hydrochloric acid with concentrated nitric acid? It is notable for dissolving noble metals such as gold and platinum.

Aqua regia can dissolve this noble metal, whose chemical symbol is Au and whose atomic number is 79. In the Rutherford experiment, alpha particles were fired at a thin sheet of it, revealing the atom’s dense nucleus.
What evergreen coniferous tree is often tall and narrow, and appears in the foreground of Van Gogh’s *The Starry Night* as well as in his paintings of wheat fields?
In Vincent van Gogh’s 1889 nightscape, a dark cypress rises in the foreground beneath a swirling blue sky and crescent moon. What is the painting’s title?

This stable, naturally occurring but relatively scarce form of hydrogen has a nucleus with one proton and one neutron, making it about twice as massive as the most common form, which has no neutron. What is the customary name of this isotope?

In 1931, this American chemist helped identify deuterium through spectroscopic evidence from enriched hydrogen samples, working with George Murphy and Ferdinand Brickwedde. He later received the 1934 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for the discovery of heavy hydrogen. Who was he?

A trimeric protein projects from the virus’s envelope; each unit has an S1 region containing a receptor-binding domain and an S2 region that helps fuse viral and host-cell membranes. What is this protein called?

When the SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein shifts its receptor-binding domain into the exposed “up” position, it can attach to a specific receptor on human cells, enabling viral entry. What is that receptor?

Made chiefly of hydrogen, helium, and cosmic dust, this cloudlike concentration of material occupies the interstellar medium. Some examples are stellar nurseries, while others are shells or debris left by dying stars; what is the general astronomical term for one?

The Crab Nebula is the expanding remnant of a stellar explosion that Chinese astronomers recorded as a “guest star” in 1054 CE; the object was even visible in daylight for weeks. What is the conventional designation of that supernova?
This polyatomic oxygen anion has the formula O₂²⁻, and its salts contain oxygen with an oxidation state of −1. What is its natural name?
In the peroxide ion, the two oxygen atoms are directly connected, and each has an oxidation state of −1. What kind of connection joins the oxygen atoms?

In mechanics, this quantity measures the energy transferred when a force causes an object to move. It is calculated using the component of the force in the direction of displacement multiplied by the distance moved, and is measured in joules. What is this quantity?

When calculating work to raise a box, pushing it up a sloped surface can require less force than lifting it straight upward, though the box travels farther. What simple machine is this surface an example of?
Which NASA rover touched down in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021, with a mission to seek evidence of ancient microbial life and collect Martian samples?

Perseverance carried a compact, solar-powered rotorcraft to Mars as a technology demonstration rather than a science rover. In April 2021, it achieved the first powered, controlled flight on another planet; what was the rotorcraft called?
What branch of science uses simple, reliable reactions to link biomolecules with reporter molecules and other chemical partners? Its name evokes the sound of something snapping into place.

In click chemistry, reporter molecules can be used to mark a class of biomolecular polymers that interact with small molecules such as drugs. What are these polymers, whose amino acid building blocks are connected by peptide bonds?

This condition may be present from birth or result from trauma, disease, or surgical removal, and it can affect part or all of an arm or leg. Rehabilitation may include mobility training and fitting an artificial replacement. What is this condition called?
For people with limb loss, this device can replace some function of a missing limb and may include a socket, a supporting structure, and a specialized hand or foot. What is this device called?

What materials property describes a solid’s ability to undergo deformation when pulled in tension and be drawn into a thin wire without fracturing? It is often contrasted with the ability to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets.

In discussions of ductility, which lightweight metal is extracted from bauxite by first refining it into alumina, then produced by dissolving that oxide in molten cryolite and using electrolysis? It is widely used in conductors and can be drawn into wire.

This group of strepsirrhine primates is native only to Madagascar and includes indris, sifakas, and aye-ayes. Many members have large eyes and long tails, though their sizes and habits vary widely. What are these primates?
Lemurs occur naturally only on this large island nation in the Indian Ocean, separated from mainland Africa by the Mozambique Channel. Its capital is Antananarivo. What is the country?

Among lemurs, this solitary nocturnal species taps on wood and uses an unusually long, slender middle finger to pull insect larvae from crevices. Its incisors also grow continuously. What is this species?

This lemur is recognizable by the alternating black-and-white bands on its long rear appendage and is a flagship species for conservation. It often holds that appendage upright while walking on the ground. What is it?
On the periodic table, this radioactive series occupies a row beneath the lanthanides. It contains 15 elements, running from element 89 through element 103. What is the series called?
Among the actinides, which synthetic element has atomic number 101 and was first produced at Berkeley in 1955? Its name honors the Russian chemist who formulated the periodic law.

Published in 1871, this scientific work applied evolutionary theory to human origins and examined sexual selection, including differences between the sexes. What is the title of Charles Darwin’s book?

The Descent of Man was written by this English naturalist, whose voyage aboard HMS Beagle and observations of species such as Galápagos finches helped shape his theory of natural selection. Who was he?
During mitosis, after duplicated chromosomes have aligned at the cell’s equator, spindle fibers pull their sister chromatids toward opposite poles. What stage of mitosis is this?

In Anaphase, a protein complex assembled at each centromere serves as the attachment site for spindle microtubules and helps transfer their pulling force to the chromatids. What is this complex called?
Which moon is the innermost of Jupiter’s four Galilean satellites? Strong tidal flexing caused by its orbital interactions keeps its interior hot and drives hundreds of active volcanoes.
On Io, which named volcanic depression is the largest of its kind and contains a lava lake known for periodically brightening during episodes of intense activity?

In agriculture, this practice supplements rainfall by deliberately directing water onto cropland. Khmer engineers supported it with large reservoirs called baray, while Sri Lankan kingdoms also built underground canals for the same purpose.
In Khmer water-management systems around Angkor, these large engineered reservoirs collected and stored water for irrigation. What name is given to these reservoirs?

For two-dimensional flow around a body, this aerodynamic theorem gives lift per unit span in terms of the fluid’s density, the free-stream speed, and the circulation around the body. What theorem is it?

In the Kutta–Joukowski theorem, lift per unit span is proportional to fluid density and free-stream speed multiplied by this flow quantity. It is defined by integrating velocity around a closed curve enclosing the body; what is it?

These large, herbivorous aquatic mammals live in warm coastal waters and rivers. Their populations are threatened by habitat loss, pollution, and injuries caused by watercraft. What are they commonly called?
Manatees in Florida are often found with propeller scars, and speed-restricted zones are intended to reduce a major human-caused source of their deaths. What hazard do these zones chiefly address?

A physicist and NASA astronaut, she flew aboard Space Shuttle Challenger in 1983 and became the first American woman in space. She later served on the presidential commission that investigated the Challenger disaster. Who was she?

After the 1986 Space Shuttle Challenger disaster, Sally Ride served on the presidential panel appointed to investigate the accident and recommend safety reforms. By what commonly used name is this panel known?
Used to specify the optical power of eyeglass lenses, this unit is defined as one reciprocal meter. What is the unit called?

In the thin-lens equation, the reciprocal of object distance plus the reciprocal of image distance equals the reciprocal of a third, intrinsic distance associated with the lens. A lens's power in diopters is also the reciprocal of this distance when measured in meters; what is this lens property called?

During gene expression, RNA polymerase uses one strand of DNA as a template to build an RNA molecule, such as messenger RNA. This step occurs before translation and produces RNA rather than a new DNA molecule; what is it called?
During eukaryotic transcription, which nuclear enzyme synthesizes the precursors of most protein-coding messenger RNAs? It is also the enzyme strongly inhibited by the mushroom toxin α-amanitin.
What laboratory technique separates proteins by gel electrophoresis, transfers them to a membrane, and uses antibodies to detect a particular protein in a sample?
In a Western blot, which reagent binds an epitope on the target protein itself before a separately labeled detection reagent binds to it?

This hormone is released by the pineal gland in a daily pattern that rises after darkness and falls with daylight. It conveys information about the light–dark cycle to the body’s internal clock and helps time sleep without acting as an indispensable on/off switch for sleep. Name it.

Melatonin’s nightly production is influenced by light signals arriving from the eyes. What hypothalamic region—a cluster of nerve cells that receives this information and coordinates circadian timing—helps control that production?

These microscopic sacs lie at the ends of the smallest airways in the lungs and are surrounded by tiny blood vessels. Across their thin walls, oxygen enters the blood while carbon dioxide moves into the air to be exhaled. What are these structures called?
In alveoli, what substance secreted by type II pneumocytes reduces surface tension and helps keep the tiny air sacs from collapsing during exhalation?

Researchers studying the gut–brain axis use this term for the community of microorganisms living throughout the gastrointestinal tract. Its members produce metabolites that can influence brain function and disease. What is this community called?

Researchers are investigating how the gut microbiome may affect this neurodegenerative condition, the most common cause of dementia in older adults. It is characterized by beta-amyloid plaques and tau tangles in the brain. What condition is it?
In computer science, this hierarchical data structure connects nodes with edges and has one designated starting node. Nodes with no children are found at its ends. What is this structure called?
In a tree, this kind of structure allows each node to have at most two children, conventionally distinguished as left and right. What is this structure called?
A fluid exerts this upward force on an immersed or floating object, opposing the object's weight. Its magnitude equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the object; what is this force called?

Which named principle of buoyancy states that the upward force on an object equals the weight of the fluid it displaces? The ancient Greek mathematician associated with this principle is also linked to the exclamation “Eureka!”

In explaining buoyancy, what quantity is found by dividing an object's mass by its volume? Comparing this quantity for an object with that of the surrounding fluid helps predict whether the object tends to sink or float.

What is the name for the point at which the weight of the fluid displaced by an object may be treated as acting? In discussions of buoyancy, its position helps describe how the upward force acts on the object.

Which videoconferencing platform became widely used for remote meetings and classes during the COVID-19 pandemic? After criticism of its digital-security features, it paused development of non-security features for 90 days.
Zoom was founded in 2011 by a Chinese-American engineer who had previously served as a vice president at Cisco. Who was this founder, who later led the company as CEO?

A machine in a building or vehicle uses an indoor coil to absorb heat from the surrounding air and an outdoor coil to release that heat elsewhere. What device commonly uses a vapor-compression cycle to cool the enclosed space?
In an air conditioner, what is the circulating working fluid called when it absorbs heat by evaporating in the indoor coil and releases heat by condensing in the outdoor coil?
A sharp sound in a cave or canyon can bounce off a surface and reach the listener again after a noticeable delay. What is this reflected-sound phenomenon called?

In a computer-generated scene designed to reproduce an Echo, what rendering technique follows the paths of light rays and models their reflections? The same approach can be adapted to trace sound through a space, though it is generally slower than scan-line techniques.
What field of computing develops methods to analyze, represent, and generate human language? Its toolkit can include tagging, stemming, statistical modeling, and language models.

In Natural Language Processing, what preprocessing step divides a text sequence into units such as words, subword pieces, or punctuation marks for later processing? Unlike stemming, it does not necessarily reduce words to their root forms.
This domesticated fowl was domesticated thousands of years ago and is now raised worldwide, chiefly for meat and eggs. Its scientific name is Gallus gallus domesticus; what common name identifies it?

Which wild bird native to Southeast Asia is regarded as the principal wild ancestor of the chicken? Unlike a close relative native to Sri Lanka, this bird’s natural range spans Thailand and the Malay Peninsula.
In commercial poultry production, what are chickens bred for rapid growth and raised primarily for meat called? This production type contrasts with hens selected chiefly for egg laying.

In the standard genetic code, this essential aromatic amino acid is uniquely specified by the UGG codon. In bacteria, the genes for its biosynthesis are classically regulated by a repressible operon. What amino acid is it?
Tryptophan is a precursor to this hormone, which is secreted primarily by the pineal gland and helps regulate circadian rhythms. What hormone is it?

Which electrostatics law states that the net electric flux through a closed surface equals the charge enclosed by that surface divided by the permittivity? Its differential form relates the divergence of the electric field to charge density.

In the integral form of Gauss's law, what scalar quantity is obtained by integrating the field's component perpendicular to a surface over that surface? For a closed surface, its value is related to the charge enclosed.
What landform forms when a glacier deposits an accumulation of rock debris and till? It often appears as a ridge or pile in the landscape.
A moraine is built from debris carried and left behind by ice. What is the unsorted mixture of clay, sand, gravel, and stones deposited directly by a glacier called?
What process joins metal pieces by melting a filler alloy whose melting point is lower than that of the pieces being joined? The base metals remain solid during the process, unlike in welding.
In traditional soldering alloys, this dense metal was commonly combined with tin, but health concerns have led to wider use of alternatives without it. Its chemical symbol is Pb.

In circuit analysis, this node rule follows from conservation of charge: the algebraic sum of charge-flow rates at a junction is zero. What law states that the total rate of charge flow into a junction equals the total rate of charge flow out?
Kirchhoff's Current Law is applied by tracking this quantity at a circuit junction. Represented by the symbol I and measured in amperes, it describes the rate at which charge passes a point.

What interdisciplinary field examines how evolution shapes social behavior in animals, including cooperation, altruism, and eusociality? It combines ideas from evolutionary biology and the study of animal behavior.
In sociobiology, which Harvard biologist published the influential 1975 book *Sociobiology: The New Synthesis* and became known for extensive research on ants?

Which state of matter generally retains a definite shape and volume, with particles vibrating near fixed positions rather than moving freely past one another? Unlike a liquid, it does not flow to take the shape of its container.
When a solid changes directly into a gas without first becoming a liquid, what phase change is occurring? This process is the reverse of deposition.
Found in plant primary cell walls and abundant in apples and citrus fruits, this galactose-rich polysaccharide is used to set jams and jellies. What is it?
Pectin helps form the adhesive material that cements neighboring plant cells together, between their primary cell walls. What is this intercellular layer called?

Plants, algae, and cyanobacteria use sunlight to store energy in organic molecules, taking in carbon dioxide; in oxygen-releasing forms, splitting water also releases oxygen. What is this process called?

In plant Photosynthesis, this double-membraned organelle contains chlorophyll-bearing thylakoids, where the light-dependent reactions occur, and a surrounding stroma where carbon fixation takes place. What is the organelle?
During oxygenic Photosynthesis, the oxygen-evolving complex of photosystem II splits this molecule, supplying electrons and protons while releasing oxygen gas. What molecule is split?

In plant Photosynthesis, this series of reactions takes place in the chloroplast stroma and uses ATP and NADPH to incorporate carbon dioxide, with RuBisCO helping catalyze the process. What is this series called?
In Photosynthesis, this green pigment in plant chloroplasts absorbs mainly red and blue wavelengths while reflecting green light, helping give leaves their characteristic color. What is the pigment?

This frozen precipitation forms from ice crystals in clouds and falls in flakes or clusters of flakes. It gives the quiet winter setting for Robert Frost’s poem about a speaker pausing beside woods on an evening.

In a poem by this American poet, falling Snow frames a speaker’s pause beside woods, and the speaker repeats that he has “miles to go before I sleep.” The same writer composed “The Road Not Taken.” Who is he?
These unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon–carbon double bond. What is the name of this class of compounds?

In a qualitative test for Alkenes, an orange-brown solution of a halogen that is liquid at room temperature loses its color as it reacts with the carbon–carbon double bond. Which halogen, whose chemical symbol is Br, is used in this test?

About 252 million years ago, a catastrophic loss of biodiversity wiped out most marine species and many land organisms, coinciding with immense volcanic eruptions in Siberia. What is the name of this largest known global die-off?

The Permian–Triassic Extinction Event is linked to a massive episode of flood-basalt volcanism in northern Siberia. What volcanic province is associated with those eruptions and their release of large quantities of greenhouse gases?

In astrobiology, what region around a star spans orbital distances where a planet could maintain liquid water on its surface, assuming suitable atmospheric conditions? Its inner and outer boundaries depend in part on the star’s luminosity and the planet’s climate.

A planet in the circumstellar habitable zone may always keep the same hemisphere facing its star, creating persistent day and night sides. What is this synchronized rotational state, also seen in the Pluto–Charon system?

This Italian physician and histologist worked at the University of Pavia and shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Santiago Ramón y Cajal for their work on the nervous system. He discovered a cellular organelle and developed a silver-based staining method for nervous tissue. Who was he?

Camillo Golgi developed a silver-based method that can reveal individual cells in nervous tissue, including their branching processes. What excitable cell type, typically made up of a cell body, dendrites, and an axon, communicates with other such cells at synapses?
These African equids are known for their distinctive black-and-white striping. Many travel alongside wildebeest across East Africa in search of fresh grass. What animals are they?

Zebras join wildebeest herds as they move across this vast grassland ecosystem in Tanzania in search of fresh grazing. The migration route extends north toward Kenya’s Maasai Mara. What is this ecosystem called?

Nag and Nagaina, the antagonists in Rudyard Kipling’s “Rikki-Tikki-Tavi,” are members of this venomous snake species native to South Asia. It belongs to the genus Naja and raises a broad hood by spreading its neck ribs when threatened; what is its common name?
Rudyard Kipling’s 1894 story collection includes a tale featuring an Indian cobra named Nag and his mate Nagaina. It also contains stories about Mowgli and Baloo; what is the collection’s title?

Which American aerospace company began in Seattle in 1916 as Pacific Aero Products, adopted a new name the following year, and today spans commercial airliners, defense, space systems, and services? It also developed a crew spacecraft for NASA’s Commercial Crew Program.

Boeing developed which crew spacecraft under NASA’s Commercial Crew Program to carry astronauts and cargo to low Earth orbit and the International Space Station? Its designation uses an abbreviation for “Crew Space Transportation,” while the number refers to the Kármán line’s altitude in kilometers.

During Mars’s 1877 opposition, an Italian astronomer reported a network of narrow, straight-looking lines and used the Italian word *canali*, meaning channels. English-language accounts transformed these optical markings into supposed engineered irrigation waterways; what is the conventional name for the features?

The Martian canals became a famous controversy after reports by this Italian astronomer, who directed Milan’s Brera Observatory and published detailed maps of Mars following the 1877 opposition. Who was he?
These unspecialized biological units can self-renew and differentiate into specialized forms. Those with totipotency have the broadest developmental potential; what is this class called?

Stem cells can be collected from this temporary organ, which exchanges oxygen and nutrients between mother and fetus and connects to the fetus by the umbilical cord. It is expelled during the third stage of labor; what is it?
What idealized object absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation without reflecting any of it and, in thermal equilibrium, emits a spectrum determined only by its temperature?
In 1900, which physicist explained the Blackbody spectrum by proposing that energy is exchanged in discrete amounts, helping lay the groundwork for quantum physics?

A doughnut-shaped chamber and magnetic coils allow this experimental device to confine hot, charged plasma for controlled-fusion research. Its name comes from a Russian acronym referring to a toroidal chamber and magnetic coils; what is the device called?
In tokamak history, the first machine of this design began operating in Russia in 1958. What was the designation of that pioneering device?

In introductory mechanics, this vector force on an object near Earth's surface points toward Earth's center and has magnitude equal to the object's mass multiplied by the local acceleration due to gravity. Unlike mass, it can vary from one location to another. What is this quantity called?

A book rests motionless on a level tabletop, where the table's upward push balances the book's downward weight. In mechanics, what is the term for the upward support exerted perpendicular to the tabletop?
This G2V main-sequence star lies at the center of the Solar System and contains about 99.86% of its total mass. What is the name of this closest star to Earth?
The Sun’s visible surface is the bright background against which sunspots appear dark, and it is the layer from which most of the visible light we see escapes. What is this layer called?
In the Sun’s core, hydrogen nuclei combine to form helium, releasing the energy that ultimately reaches Earth as light and heat. What is this energy-producing process called?

The average distance between Earth and the Sun is about 149.6 million kilometers. What named distance measure, used for comparing distances within the Solar System, is fixed at exactly 149,597,870.7 kilometers?
As its core hydrogen fusion declines, the Sun is expected to expand into this stellar phase before shedding its outer layers and eventually becoming a white dwarf. What is this phase called?

What evolutionary phenomenon occurs when two or more species that are each genuinely toxic, venomous, or otherwise defended evolve similar conspicuous warning signals, so predators that learn to avoid one are more likely to avoid the others?
In Müllerian mimicry, which neotropical butterfly, commonly known as the red postman, is itself unpalatable and shares conspicuous red, yellow, and black warning patterns with a co-mimic?

A skydiver accelerates after leaving a plane, but as air resistance increases it eventually balances the diver’s weight, making the net force and acceleration zero while the descent continues. What is this limiting speed called?

In a calculation of terminal velocity for a tiny sphere settling slowly through a viscous fluid, the sphere’s weight minus buoyant force is balanced by a drag force proportional to its speed. Which named law gives that drag as 6π η r v?

In evolutionary biology, what term describes behavior that increases a recipient’s fitness while reducing the fitness of the individual performing it? The classification depends on these effects on fitness, not on whether the behavior appears caring.

In explanations of biological altruism, which evolutionary rule predicts when a costly act benefiting another can be favored by comparing relatedness (r), the recipient’s benefit (b), and the actor’s cost (c)? Its condition is commonly written rb > c.
This DNA–protein structure packages an organism’s genetic material, with histones helping compact its DNA in eukaryotic cells. It is segregated during cell division. What is it called?

On a duplicated chromosome, this narrowed region holds the two sister chromatids together until they separate. It is also where the kinetochore assembles for spindle attachment. What is this region called?
During mitosis, chromosomes align across the cell’s equatorial plane at this stage, after spindle attachment and before sister chromatids separate. What is this stage called?
