In the history reflected by the name Hubble–Lemaître law, which Belgian priest and astronomer used general relativity to develop an expanding-universe model and connect galaxy redshifts with distance? His analysis preceded Edwin Hubble’s 1929 distance–velocity paper.

In an ideal oscillator, the restoring force points toward equilibrium and grows in direct proportion to the displacement from it. The object's position therefore varies sinusoidally over time; what is this type of periodic behavior called?

For an ideal mass-spring system undergoing simple harmonic motion, the period does not change when the maximum distance from equilibrium is varied, provided the spring remains in its linear range. What is this maximum displacement called?

These toxic armaments injure or kill through the effects of substances dispersed as gases, vapors, or aerosols, rather than primarily through blast or impact. Italian forces used them during the 1935–36 invasion of Ethiopia; what broad class of armaments is described?

After Italian forces used chemical weapons against Ethiopia, Emperor Haile Selassie appealed to this international organization in Geneva. Founded after World War I to promote collective security, it was headquartered in Geneva and dissolved in 1946.

Which geologic period lasted from about 299 to 252 million years ago, formed the final interval of the Paleozoic Era, and ended with the largest known mass extinction? During this period, the supercontinent Pangaea reached its greatest extent.

Near the end of the Permian Period, immense eruptions in what is now Siberia released vast amounts of volcanic gases and are thought to have helped drive global warming and ocean disruption. What large igneous province is associated with those eruptions?
In the pattern A + BC → B + AC, free element A takes the place of element B within compound BC. What is this process called?

In the activity series used to predict whether a single-displacement reaction will occur, potassium and lithium appear among the highly reactive metals near the top. What chemical family do these elements belong to?

This German astronomer and mathematician worked as Tycho Brahe’s assistant in Prague and formulated three laws describing planetary motion, including the paths planets follow around the Sun. Who was this major figure of the Scientific Revolution?

Johannes Kepler’s 1609 book focused on the orbit of Mars and presented evidence that planets travel in elliptical paths. It also describes the rule that a line from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time. What is the title of this work?

Johannes Kepler’s refracting optical instrument uses a convex lens at each end, unlike Galileo’s design with a concave eyepiece. Though it produces an inverted image, it offers a wider field of view. What is this optical design called?

For an ideal elastic element, the restoring force increases in proportion to its displacement from equilibrium, with the proportionality factor commonly written as k. What physical quantity, measured in newtons per meter, describes the element’s resistance to displacement?

The spring constant appears in a relation stating that an ideal spring’s restoring force is proportional to its displacement and points in the opposite direction, often written as F = −kx. What is the name of this law?
What soft, porous variety of limestone is composed mainly of calcite, or calcium carbonate, and was used to create landscape figures such as the Cerne Abbas Giant and the Uffington White Horse?

A massive human figure made of chalk is cut into a Dorset hillside. Although it was long thought to be ancient, soil dating reported in 2021 suggested it was created in the Middle Ages; what is this landmark called?

This generating station near Pripyat in northern Ukraine operated RBMK reactors. Its reactor number four was destroyed in April 1986, leading to the evacuation of the nearby city and the creation of an exclusion zone. What station was it?

At the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, what enormous arch-shaped structure was moved into place over the shelter surrounding reactor number four in 2016? It was designed to contain radioactive material and support the eventual dismantling of the damaged reactor.

What narrow-body jet family was grounded worldwide in March 2019 after crashes of Lion Air Flight 610 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, both associated with a flight-control system that could command nose-down stabilizer trim? It is the re-engined generation of the long-running 737 passenger-jet line.

On the Boeing 737 MAX, what automated flight-control system used angle-of-attack sensor data to command nose-down stabilizer trim? Its operation became central to investigations of the Lion Air and Ethiopian Airlines crashes.

This mechanical disturbance consists of pressure variations and particle motion traveling through a material medium. Humans typically hear it when its frequency is roughly 20 to 20,000 hertz; what is this phenomenon?

A sound wave traveling through air is classified by how the air particles move relative to the wave’s direction. In this type of wave, particles oscillate back and forth parallel to the direction of propagation, unlike in a transverse wave; what is this classification?

For an isolated neutral atom in the gas phase, this quantity describes the energy change when the atom captures a negatively charged subatomic particle. Among the halogens, chlorine has a more favorable value than fluorine because the added particle experiences less repulsion in chlorine’s larger 3p shell. What is this quantity?

In comparisons of electron affinity, this halogen has a more exothermic first electron-addition process than fluorine, even though it lies one period below it. The difference is attributed to the added electron encountering less repulsion in its roomier 3p subshell. Which element is it?

This Indo-Pacific cephalopod has an external, tightly coiled shell partitioned internally by curved walls, with its body occupying the outermost section. It adjusts the contents of the shell’s internal spaces for buoyancy and moves through the water by jet propulsion; what animal is it?
In a chambered nautilus shell, a narrow structure passes through the partitions between chambers and helps regulate buoyancy by managing fluid and gas. What is this structure called?
This freshwater fish was domesticated from the Prussian carp and selectively bred into many ornamental varieties. It is one of the most familiar aquarium and garden-pond pets; what is it?

Goldfish were domesticated from a Eurasian fish species whose populations can reproduce by gynogenesis: sperm from another fish can trigger development of its eggs without contributing DNA. What is this ancestor commonly called?
In mitosis, this stage is marked by chromatin condensing into visible chromosomes while the spindle apparatus begins to form. What is this stage called?
During prophase, microtubules begin organizing into this bipolar apparatus, which later attaches to chromosomes and helps separate sister chromatids. What is this apparatus called?
What term describes uncontrolled fires in vegetation that can generate extreme heat and smoke, and may even create towering pyrocumulonimbus thunderstorms?

During the August 2020 wildfires, the National Weather Service issued its first warning for a tornado produced by a pyrocumulonimbus cloud in Lassen County. In which U.S. state is Lassen County, whose capital is Sacramento?

This group of limbless reptiles has elongated bodies covered in overlapping scales and includes constrictors such as pythons as well as venomous forms such as cobras. What familiar group is being described?
Some snakes cross loose desert sand using a distinctive gait in which sections of the body lift and move sideways, leaving a series of angled tracks. What is this method of locomotion called?

Although snakes have no external limbs, boas and pythons retain small remnants of an ancestral skeletal structure near the rear of the body, sometimes associated with tiny spurs. What is this vestigial structure?
Snakes periodically shed their outer skin, a process that allows a new layer to replace the old one as the animal grows. What is the zoological term for this shedding process?

These electrically charged atoms or molecules form when electrons are gained or lost. In solution, positively charged examples are called cations, while negatively charged examples are called anions. What is the general name for these particles?

In this laser-based mass-spectrometry method, a sample is embedded in an energy-absorbing matrix, and a laser pulse desorbs and ionizes it to create analyte ions with relatively little fragmentation. What is this method called?

Neurons release these chemical messengers across synapses to pass signals to other neurons, muscles, or glands. Acetylcholine is one example of this class of signaling compounds; what is the class called?
Among neurotransmitters, this molecule is released by motor neurons at neuromuscular junctions and helps trigger muscle contraction. Botulinum toxin interferes with its release; what molecule is it?
What term names a large, basin-shaped volcanic depression formed when an eruption removes or withdraws enough magma from a shallow reservoir that the overlying ground loses support and collapses?
Which Oregon volcano erupted about 7,700 years ago, leaving the caldera that later filled with water to become Crater Lake? The resulting basin is about 8–10 km across and roughly 1.2 km deep.
What is the name for an infectious, abnormally folded form of a body protein that can induce normally folded copies to adopt the same shape and accumulate in nervous tissue?
Among conditions caused by prions, which human neurodegenerative illness is named for two physicians and can cause rapidly progressive dementia and involuntary muscle jerks?

Each molecule of this colorless gas has one atom of the element found in graphite and diamond, joined by double bonds to two oxygen atoms. It is released by aerobic respiration and fossil-fuel combustion, and it absorbs infrared radiation in the atmosphere. What compound is it?

A long-running record begun at Mauna Loa Observatory in 1958 shows a seasonal sawtooth pattern superimposed on a decades-long rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide. What is the name of the graph documenting this measurement series?

As carbon dioxide enters seawater, it can be converted into this dissolved ion, with the formula HCO₃⁻. It is the dominant form of dissolved inorganic carbon in much of the ocean and is also found paired with sodium in baking soda. Name the ion.

When additional carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater, it lowers the water’s pH and reduces the availability of carbonate ions needed by corals and other shell-building organisms. What environmental process does this describe?

Which highly corrosive, oily diprotic mineral compound is made by catalytically oxidizing the gas produced when a yellow nonmetal burns in air, then absorbing the resulting oxide? Its aqueous solution serves as the electrolyte in batteries with lead plates.

In the industrial manufacture of sulfuric acid, what process catalytically oxidizes sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide—often using a vanadium-based catalyst—before the trioxide is absorbed to produce the acid?

These medium-sized rodents are common subjects in behavioral laboratories and are larger than mice. Researchers have used them in maze-learning, conditioning, and drug self-administration studies; what animals are they?

In Bruce Alexander’s experiment, rats living in a spacious, socially enriched environment with access to play and companionship consumed less morphine-laced water than rats housed alone. What name was given to this environment?

In vertebrate zoology, these paired skeletal structures attach to the skull and help animals seize, bite, and process food. They are present in most living vertebrates but absent in jawless groups such as lampreys and hagfish. What are they?

Jaws are the defining anatomical feature of a vertebrate group that includes most living vertebrates, from sharks and bony fishes to birds and mammals. What is the formal name of this group, contrasted with jawless vertebrates such as lampreys and hagfish?

Founded in St. Louis in 1901, this company first manufactured saccharin and later became known for glyphosate-based weed control and genetically engineered seeds. Bayer completed its acquisition of the company in 2018. What is the company’s name?
Monsanto introduced this broad-spectrum herbicide in 1974, with glyphosate as its active ingredient. What is the herbicide’s brand name?

Published in 1687, this Latin work presented three laws of motion and a mathematical account of universal gravitation. It applied these principles to the motion of planets, moons, and other celestial bodies. What is its full title?

In the Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, the English mathematician who formulated the three laws of motion also explained gravity as a universal force governing both falling objects and planetary orbits. Who was the author?

In an ideal molecular arrangement, four directions from a central atom point toward the corners of a regular tetrahedron. For methane, the separation between any two directions is approximately 109.5°. What is this geometric quantity called?
The tetrahedral bond angle occurs between the four equivalent carbon–hydrogen bonds in this simplest hydrocarbon. Its single carbon atom is bonded to four hydrogen atoms. What molecule is it?
Formed from calcium-carbonate-rich sediment, this rock commonly contains calcite and can be transformed by heat and pressure into marble. What rock is it?

When groundwater dissolves limestone, it can create caves, sinkholes, and underground streams. What German-derived name is given to terrain shaped by this soluble bedrock and its distinctive surface and underground drainage?

This periodic-table family occupies group 17 and is characterized by seven valence electrons. Its name derives from a term meaning “salt former,” reflecting its tendency to form salts with metals; what is the family called?
Among the halogens, which element is a volatile, reddish-brown liquid at standard temperature and pressure? Its chemical symbol is Br and its atomic number is 35.
Halogens include an element that ranks highest of all elements in electronegativity on the Pauling scale. Which pale-yellow, highly reactive gas has atomic number 9?
Halogens include a laboratory-made element first synthesized in 2010 with atomic number 117. Named for the U.S. state that is home to Oak Ridge National Laboratory, what is this element?
What gas-powered laboratory apparatus mixes fuel with adjustable amounts of air before ignition to produce a controllable open flame used for heating and sterilizing tools?
In the 1850s, the Bunsen burner was developed in Heidelberg by a laboratory mechanic working at Robert Bunsen’s suggestion. He marketed the improved design beginning in 1855; what was his name?

In a clean, two-dimensional electron system at low temperature and under a strong perpendicular magnetic field, the resistance measured perpendicular to the current settles into remarkably precise plateaus instead of changing smoothly. These discrete values are set by a universal resistance scale; what phenomenon is this?

In the Quantum Hall Effect, the resistance plateaus are organized by a universal scale equal to Planck’s constant divided by the square of the elementary charge. What is the conventional name of this constant?

Developed in the late 1920s around Niels Bohr’s institute in Denmark and associated with both Bohr and Werner Heisenberg, this approach to quantum mechanics treats the theory as predicting probabilities for measurement outcomes rather than assigning every system definite classical properties before observation. What is this influential approach called?

In the Copenhagen interpretation, Niels Bohr used what term for the idea that experimental arrangements designed to reveal wave-like and particle-like behavior expose mutually exclusive aspects, each necessary for a fuller account of quantum phenomena?
Which electro-optic phenomenon occurs when applying an electric field changes a material’s refractive index in proportion to the square of the field strength?

In the Kerr effect, an applied electric field changes an optical property that describes how much light slows down in a material compared with its speed in a vacuum. What is this dimensionless property, equal to the speed of light in vacuum divided by its speed in the material?
When an aircraft wing is tilted beyond a threshold relative to the oncoming airflow, the airflow can separate and the wing can lose substantial lift. What is this dangerous flight condition called?

In an aerodynamic stall, the threshold depends on a wing’s orientation relative to the oncoming airflow, not just on its airspeed. What is the greatest such orientation at which the wing can still maintain attached airflow called?

This positively charged radiation is emitted in some radioactive decays and strongly ionizes matter, yet at ordinary decay energies it travels only a few centimeters through air. It contains two protons and two neutrons, making it identical to the nucleus of helium-4; what is it called?

Scattering results involving alpha particles led to a model in which an atom’s positive charge and nearly all its mass occupy a tiny central nucleus. Which New Zealand-born physicist interpreted those results and later won the 1908 Nobel Prize in Chemistry?

In helium-burning stars, this reaction sequence can form carbon-12 from helium nuclei through a short-lived beryllium-8 intermediate. It uses alpha particles as its incoming nuclei; what is this stellar fusion process called?
Built across a river or other watercourse, this engineered barrier can regulate flow, form a reservoir, or drive turbines for hydroelectric power. What is this infrastructure called?
The Aswan High Dam spans the Nile near Aswan and impounds Lake Nasser. In which country is this dam located?
This live attenuated preparation is derived from a strain of Mycobacterium bovis and is used primarily to prevent tuberculosis. What is its standard name?
The Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccine is derived from this mycobacterial species, which causes tuberculosis in cattle. What is the species?
Which physical principle says that the entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease over time? It also accounts for the spontaneous net flow of heat from hotter objects to colder ones.

A famous thought experiment used to probe the Second Law of Thermodynamics imagines an intelligent being that sorts fast and slow gas molecules through a tiny door, apparently lowering the system’s entropy without expending energy. What is this hypothetical being called?

In muscle fibers, this specialized membrane network forms terminal cisternae near transverse tubules and stores calcium using SERCA pumps. It releases that calcium through channels to help initiate contraction; what is this muscle-cell network?

During skeletal-muscle excitation–contraction coupling, the sarcoplasmic reticulum releases calcium through a channel named for its sensitivity to a plant alkaloid. Mutations in this channel can cause malignant hyperthermia; what is the channel called?
In biological taxonomy, this rank falls below domain and above phylum. It traditionally groups organisms into broad sets such as plants, animals, and protists; what is this rank called?
Which Swedish taxonomist’s system placed rocks in a mineral Kingdom alongside the animal and plant groupings?

In chemistry labs, this cone-shaped vessel has a broad opening that narrows into a stem, guiding liquids into containers with small openings. Filter paper can be placed inside some versions to separate solids from liquids. What is this piece of equipment?
Unlike a plain laboratory funnel, this vessel has a stopcock near its outlet and is used to separate immiscible liquid layers after they settle. What is this specialized apparatus called?
This dynamically typed programming language is widely used to add interactive behavior to web pages and can also power server applications through Node.js. What language is it?
In a browser, JavaScript can use a browser-provided model to represent page elements in a hierarchy and respond to events such as clicks. What three-letter name is commonly used for this model?

This puzzle asks why, despite the immense age and scale of the universe—and the expectation that intelligent societies might arise in many star systems—astronomers have found no convincing evidence of extraterrestrial civilizations. It is famously condensed into the question, “Where is everybody?” What is this puzzle called?

The Fermi paradox is often discussed alongside a 1961 framework that estimates the number of detectable civilizations in the Milky Way by combining factors for star formation, planets, life, intelligence, technology, and the longevity of civilizations. What is this framework called?
What is the name of the phenomenon in which mechanical stress on certain materials generates electric charge, while an applied electric field can conversely cause those materials to deform?
Pierre and Jacques Curie investigated this crystalline material while studying piezoelectricity in the 1880s. Also known as potassium sodium tartrate tetrahydrate, what is its common name?
Which elongated, snake-like fishes include conger, moray, gulper, and European forms, and whose mysterious reproduction led Aristotle to believe they arose spontaneously?
European eels make a remarkable transatlantic reproductive migration, and their larvae later drift toward Europe. What sea is their spawning ground?
This positively charged baryon is made of two up quarks and one down quark. The number of these particles in an atom’s nucleus determines which chemical element it is. What particle is it?
For the proton, the number found in a nucleus is represented by Z and distinguishes one chemical element from another. What is this quantity called?
The proton received its name from this nuclear physicist in 1920, after his experiments with alpha particles and nitrogen helped identify the hydrogen nucleus as a nuclear constituent. Who was he?
The proton is a composite hadron rather than an elementary particle. What theory of the strong interaction describes the dynamics of its quarks and gluons?

In the Sun, the dominant fusion pathway begins with hydrogen nuclei—protons—and ultimately converts four of them into a helium nucleus through linked reactions. What is this sequence of reactions called?
At the point where a light ray meets a reflecting surface, what is the reference line drawn perpendicular to the surface, against which the angles of incidence and reflection are measured?

For a ray striking a plane mirror, which optical quantity is determined by the separation between the incoming ray and the normal at the point of contact? Under the law of reflection, it has the same value as the corresponding quantity for the outgoing ray.
This class of pain-relieving drugs includes prescription medicines such as oxycodone as well as heroin and fentanyl. Its use is associated with dependence and overdose. What is this class called?
In 2022, Illinois Governor J.B. Pritzker signed a law eliminating co-pays for this nasal-spray opioid antagonist used to reverse overdoses. What is the medication’s generic name?
Established in Tennessee as a major Manhattan Project site, this U.S. Department of Energy facility remains prominent in nuclear science and broader research. What is its full name?

At Oak Ridge National Laboratory, what Manhattan Project installation began operation in November 1943 and served as a pilot-scale site for demonstrating plutonium production before the Hanford production facilities came online?

What fluid property measures resistance to flow or deformation caused by internal friction between moving layers? In the zero-value limit of this property, the Navier–Stokes equations reduce to the Euler equations.
In problems involving viscosity, what dimensionless ratio compares inertial effects with viscous effects and helps characterize whether a fluid’s flow is laminar or turbulent?

Which broad class of elements occupies much of the left and center of the periodic table? Its members generally conduct heat and electricity, have a distinctive luster, and can be combined to form alloys.
Among metals, which element has atomic number 27 and is a silvery-blue transition element used in some rechargeable battery cathodes and high-strength alloys?

When a saline lake or shallow sea dries in an arid basin, dissolved substances precipitate and accumulate as a chemical sedimentary deposit. What is the general name for this kind of deposit, which can contain halite, gypsum, or borax?
Within an evaporite deposit, which mineral consists of sodium chloride (NaCl), commonly develops cubic crystals, and is mined as rock salt?

This optical surface redirects incident light to form an image and may be flat or curved. Curved versions are used in reflecting telescopes, while flat versions are common in homes for viewing one's appearance. What is this device?

At a mirror's surface, this process sends light back into the medium from which it came. For a smooth surface, the incident and outgoing rays make equal angles with the normal. What is this optical process?
Which lightweight alkaline-earth metal has atomic number 4 and the chemical symbol Be? It is the first element in group 2 of the periodic table.
Beryllium’s atomic number matches the number of hydrogen atoms in a methane molecule. The same count is the number of phosphorus atoms in a molecule of white phosphorus; what is it?

When a nearby star is viewed from opposite sides of Earth’s orbit, its position appears to shift against much more distant background stars. This geometric effect is used to estimate distances to nearby stars; what is it called?
Astronomical parallax provides a direct way to measure distances to nearby stars. What unit is defined as the distance at which a star has an annual parallax of exactly one arcsecond?

During strenuous activity, skeletal muscle converts glucose into a three-carbon product that travels through the blood to the liver, where it is used to make glucose that can return to muscle. What is this named metabolic process linking the tissues and reactions?

In the Cori cycle, working muscle releases this three-carbon product of glycolysis into the blood, and the liver uses it as a substrate to regenerate glucose. What is this molecule, commonly present in its ionized form in the body?

Irregularities in Uranus’s orbit allowed astronomers to calculate the position of a previously unknown planet, which was observed in 1846. This ice giant is the eighth and farthest major planet from the Sun and has a blue appearance partly caused by methane in its atmosphere.

Neptune’s largest moon was discovered shortly after the planet itself in 1846 and travels in an orbit opposite the direction of Neptune’s rotation. Its surface has a landscape of circular depressions thought to have formed through diapirism.

Neptune has had only one spacecraft flyby, which took place in 1989. That encounter confirmed the planet’s fragmented ring arcs and sent back close-up observations of its atmosphere and moons; which spacecraft made the pass?

Urbain Le Verrier calculated Neptune’s predicted position from perturbations in Uranus’s orbit, and this German astronomer made the confirming observation in 1846 from Berlin Observatory. Who was the observer?

This neuroparalytic illness can follow ingestion of improperly preserved food or contamination of a wound, and may cause drooping eyelids followed by descending flaccid paralysis. It results from toxins produced by Clostridium bacteria, especially C. botulinum. What is the disease?
In botulism, which bacterial protein cleaves SNARE proteins at peripheral nerve terminals and prevents the release of acetylcholine?
What is the name of the medical practice that deliberately ends a pregnancy? It is also the subject of continuing ethical, legal, and public-health debates.
In the United States, which 1973 Supreme Court decision recognized a constitutional right to abortion and was overturned in 2022 by Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization?

This oil and gas extraction method injects fluid at high pressure into shale and other low-permeability rock, creating fissures that allow trapped hydrocarbons to flow toward a well. What is this technique called?

In hydraulic fracturing, sand or engineered ceramic grains are mixed into the injected fluid so they lodge in newly created cracks and keep them open after pumping stops. What are these grains called?

At the boundary between a plant root’s cortex and vascular cylinder, this band of hydrophobic material in endodermal cell walls interrupts movement along cell walls. By making water and dissolved minerals cross cell membranes before entering the stele, what structure helps regulate their passage?

After crossing a cell membrane at the Casparian strip, water and dissolved minerals can move inward through the connected cytoplasm of neighboring plant cells. What is this route, linked from cell to cell by plasmodesmata?
On an earthquake map, this surface point lies vertically above the underground focus and gives the quake’s position without specifying depth. What is this point called?
In contrast to the Epicenter, what is the name for the underground point where an earthquake rupture begins, whose location includes depth?

In the giant-impact explanation for the formation of Earth’s natural satellite, a hypothetical protoplanet struck the early Earth more than four billion years ago, and debris from the collision later coalesced into the Moon. What was the protoplanet called?

In the giant-impact account involving Theia, debris from the collision between the early third planet from the Sun and the protoplanet gradually assembled into that planet’s natural satellite. What is the satellite called?

This multiplicative formula combines the Milky Way’s star-formation rate with estimates for planets, life, intelligence, detectable technology, and the duration of detectable signals. It is used to estimate how many technological civilizations might be detectable in our galaxy; what is it called?

In the Drake Equation, one factor is a duration rather than a probability: it represents the average time that a technologically advanced society emits signals detectable across interstellar distances. What is this factor?
What neurological disorder is marked by severe headaches that often come with sensitivity to light and sound? Some attacks are preceded by temporary visual or sensory warning symptoms.
During a migraine, what is the term for a temporary visual or sensory disturbance that can appear before the headache, such as flashing lights or blind spots?

What specialized nuclear division begins after one round of DNA replication, separates homologous chromosome pairs in its first division and sister chromatids in its second, and typically produces four haploid cells for sexual reproduction?
During meiosis, what process in prophase I exchanges DNA segments between non-sister chromatids of paired homologous chromosomes, creating new combinations of alleles?

A dry salt exposed to humid air may take up water vapor, and a strongly affected sample can eventually become wet or dissolve. What material property describes this attraction and retention of atmospheric moisture?

Hygroscopicity is relevant to salts associated with fireworks. Which chloride salt, made with the alkali metal whose atoms have 19 protons, is cited as a compound that can occur in sparkler smoke and pose an inhalation hazard?

Born in Milan, Ohio, in 1847, this American inventor and entrepreneur developed a phonograph that could record and replay sound and helped make incandescent electric lighting practical. What was his name?

At his West Orange complex, Thomas Edison established an early motion-picture studio with a roof that could turn to follow the sunlight. Short films featuring popular variety acts were made there; what was the studio called?
This computing device encodes information in units that can occupy superpositions rather than being limited to classical 0s and 1s. What kind of device uses these units to perform computations?

In photonic approaches to a quantum computer, an optical network can be used to sample the possible outputs of many indistinguishable particles. These particles obey Bose-Einstein statistics and can share the same quantum state; what are they called?

A Renaissance astronomer born in Toruń, then part of Royal Prussia, argued that Earth rotates daily and travels around the Sun rather than occupying the center. His major treatise appeared in print in 1543, the year of his death; who was he?
Nicolaus Copernicus’s landmark astronomical treatise was printed in Nuremberg in 1543 and presented his Sun-centered account of the planetary system. What is the work’s Latin title?
In mechanics, this conserved physical quantity has kinetic and potential forms. The First Law of Thermodynamics expresses its conservation. What quantity is it?

In thermodynamics, the Second Law says that this quantity cannot decrease in an isolated system. Commonly symbolized by S, it is associated with the number of microscopic arrangements and is often discussed alongside energy. What is it?
What data structure assigns a numerical value to each connection to represent quantities such as distance, cost, or travel time? Algorithms can use these values to compare possible routes.

In a weighted graph with nonnegative edge weights, which shortest-path method repeatedly selects the unsettled vertex with the lowest known distance from a starting point and updates the distances to its neighbors? It is named after a Dutch computer scientist.
In human reproduction, this large female gamete is released from an ovarian follicle and can fuse with a sperm during fertilization. What is this gamete commonly called?

An egg cell leaves a mature ovarian follicle during this reproductive event, which is typically triggered by a surge in luteinizing hormone and occurs before the luteal phase. What is this event called?

In paper and thin-layer chromatography, this dimensionless quantity is calculated by dividing the distance a compound’s spot travels from the origin by the distance the liquid phase travels from the origin. Often abbreviated Rf, it helps compare how compounds move through the same chromatographic system. What is this quantity?

When calculating a retention factor in paper or thin-layer chromatography, the denominator is the distance from the origin to the leading edge of the advancing liquid phase. What is this moving boundary called?

This adaptable Asian Old World monkey ranges from Afghanistan across northern India and into China, and it has been widely used in biomedical research. What species, also used in studies of maternal attachment, is it?

In experiments involving the rhesus macaque, this American psychologist compared infant monkeys’ responses to cloth-covered and wire surrogate mothers. Who conducted this controversial research on maternal attachment?
What legendary substance in alchemical lore was sought as an agent that could transmute base metals such as lead into gold and was also credited with producing the Elixir of Life?
In the first Harry Potter novel, which named alchemist is said to have made the Philosopher’s Stone and used its life-extending power with his wife, Perenelle?

Which British mathematician and logician formalized computation with an abstract tape-based machine and showed that no general procedure can decide every halting question? During World War II, he also worked on German naval ciphers and later proposed a test of machine intelligence.
During World War II, Alan Turing led this Bletchley Park section, whose cryptanalysis focused on German naval Enigma communications. What was the unit, identified by a number, called?
After the war, Alan Turing designed a stored-program computer for Britain’s National Physical Laboratory. By what full name was this proposed machine known, abbreviated ACE?

In a postwar paper, Alan Turing modeled how chemical interactions in developing tissue could amplify small irregularities into stable spots, stripes, and other patterns. What biological process of form generation was he explaining?
This British computer scientist proposed a hypertext information-management system while working at CERN and later built the first web browser and server. Who was he?

Tim Berners-Lee developed this global hypertext system at CERN, using web addresses and HTTP to let browsers retrieve linked documents. What is the name of the system, distinct from the underlying internet that carries it?

Which evolutionary theory interprets fossil patterns as long intervals of relative stability within species, interrupted by geologically brief episodes of rapid change? Paleontologists Stephen Jay Gould and Niles Eldredge developed this view as an alternative to continuous gradual change.

In the theory of punctuated equilibrium, which paleontologist partnered with Stephen Jay Gould to argue that species often remain relatively unchanged for long periods, with much evolutionary change occurring around speciation?

This water-soluble nutrient is found in citrus fruits and is essential for producing collagen. A severe deficiency can cause a disease that was once common among sailors on long voyages. What is this nutrient?
Before citrus fruits were included in provisions, this disease caused by inadequate Vitamin C was a major danger on long sea voyages. What is the disease?

In kinetic theory, gas molecules repeatedly undergo this brief interaction with one another and with the walls of their container. In an isolated encounter, momentum is conserved, while kinetic energy is conserved only in the elastic case and may be dissipated in the inelastic case. What is this event called?

In a head-on Collision, what dimensionless quantity compares the relative speed of separation after impact with the relative speed of approach before impact? Its value is 0 for a perfectly inelastic event and 1 for an ideal elastic one.
This genus of great apes is native to rainforests on Borneo and Sumatra; its members are known for reddish hair and a largely arboreal lifestyle. What is the genus’s familiar common name?
Orangutans live on two major Southeast Asian islands, and this one is divided among Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei; the Indonesian part is called Kalimantan. Which island is it?

This long-lived woody plant is typically supported by an upright trunk or several stems bearing a crown of branches and foliage. Its roots anchor it and absorb water and minerals, though there is no universally sharp scientific boundary separating this growth form from shrubs. What is it?
In a tree, what vascular tissue carries water and dissolved minerals from the roots toward the leaves and also helps support the plant’s woody structure?
In this ecological interaction, one organism benefits by living in or on another organism, while the organism it relies on is harmed. What is this relationship called?
In parasitism, one organism lives in or on another and gains resources at its expense. What is the organism that provides this habitat or resources and is harmed by the interaction called?
This synthetic pH indicator is colorless in acidic solution and turns pink or fuchsia in basic solution. Frequently used to signal a color change during acid–base titrations, what is its name?

In an acid–base measurement using phenolphthalein as a visual indicator, the first persistent pale-pink color signals that reagent addition should stop; this observed point approximates the equivalence point. What is this point called?
What property describes a substance’s ability to dissolve in a solvent and form a solution? When a compound lacks this property, it may separate from the solution as a precipitate.

In discussions of solubility, what effect occurs when adding sodium chloride to a solution of lead(II) chloride increases the chloride-ion concentration and causes more lead(II) chloride to precipitate?

Which bacterial group carries out oxygen-releasing photosynthesis and may form filaments containing specialized cells that fix nitrogen? Its membranes can also contain hydrocarbons associated with stabilizing thylakoids.
In cyanobacteria, what straight-chain hydrocarbon has been reported in membranes and may help stabilize thylakoids?

What common collective name describes elongated, soft-bodied invertebrates that includes soil-dwelling compost decomposers, parasitic roundworms, and flatworms, even though these animals belong to several unrelated groups?
The model organism Caenorhabditis elegans is a tiny roundworm widely used to study embryonic development. What phylum does this species belong to?

Assembled in low Earth orbit beginning in 1998 and continuously inhabited since 2000, this collaborative orbital laboratory hosts crews from multiple nations and supports long-term research in microgravity. What is this facility called?

On the International Space Station, this observation module is attached to Tranquility and has seven windows that provide panoramic views of Earth and a vantage point for operating the station’s robotic arm. What is the module called?

Unlike raw concentration, this thermodynamic measure accounts for interactions among particles and allows equilibrium expressions to describe nonideal solutions. What is this effective concentration called?

In models of chemical activity for dilute electrolytes, the Debye–Hückel limiting law relates a charged solute particle’s activity coefficient to its charge and this measure, calculated as one-half the sum of each charged species’ concentration multiplied by its charge squared. What is this measure called?

This copper-based alloy is traditionally made primarily from copper and tin, though its precise recipe can vary. Its increased hardness made it useful for tools and weapons as well as cast artworks. What material is it?

In this method for making bronze sculptures, a wax model is surrounded by a heat-resistant mold, then melted out to leave a cavity. Molten metal is poured into that cavity to form the sculpture. What metalworking method is this?
Bronze versions of *The Thinker* and *The Burghers of Calais* are among the works of this French sculptor. He also created *The Gates of Hell*. Who was he?

Seen from Earth, this barred spiral appears as a hazy band of light because its distant stars blend together to the naked eye. It contains the Solar System and has a central bar and bulge; what is its natural name?

At the center of the Milky Way Galaxy, astronomers observe a compact radio source associated with a supermassive black hole. The Event Horizon Telescope released an image of this object in 2022; what is its astronomical designation?
The Sun lies about 27,000 light-years from the Galactic Center, near the inner edge of a named spiral feature of the Milky Way Galaxy. What is that feature called?

These DNA sequences can relocate within a genome rather than remain at a fixed site. LINEs and SINEs are familiar examples, and together such sequences account for about half of human DNA; what are they called?

While studying patterns of kernel color inheritance in maize, this cytogeneticist discovered mobile genetic sequences—the phenomenon of transposable elements. She later received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for this work; who was she?

Unlike a stationary lander or an orbiting probe, this robotic vehicle travels across the Martian surface and uses onboard instruments to study rocks, soil, and local conditions. What is this type of explorer called?
One Mars rover landed in Jezero crater in February 2021, a site selected for evidence of an ancient river delta, and carries the Mastcam-Z imaging system. What is this rover called?
Which laboratory technique rapidly amplifies a selected DNA region by repeatedly separating DNA strands, allowing short primers to bind, and extending them with a heat-stable enzyme?
In polymerase chain reaction, which thermostable DNA-copying enzyme was originally isolated from a heat-loving bacterium and remains active through repeated high-temperature cycles?
Which scientist developed polymerase chain reaction at Cetus Corporation in 1983 and later shared the 1993 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Michael Smith?
During polymerase chain reaction, what short DNA fragments bind to complementary sequences flanking the target and provide starting points for DNA polymerase to extend?
This reddish transition metal has atomic number 29 and the chemical symbol Cu. Its exceptionally high electrical conductivity makes it a common choice for building wiring.
Copper was deliberately combined with tin to make this alloy, whose production around 3500 BCE helped define a major archaeological age. What is the alloy?
As exposed copper roofing weathers, it can develop this characteristic green coating. What is this corrosion product commonly called?
This bulb-grown flowering plant belongs to the genus Tulipa and became closely associated with extensive cultivation in the Netherlands. What is its common name?

Dutch tulip speculation in the 1630s included an active market in this city, which later became the Netherlands’ capital and housed the principal chamber of the Dutch East India Company. What city is it?

What field studies how electrically conducting fluids, including ionized gases, behave in magnetic fields? It combines ideas from fluid dynamics and electromagnetism to describe phenomena such as magnetic confinement in fusion devices.
In magnetohydrodynamics, what electrically conducting state of matter consists of ionized particles, makes up the Sun, and can be confined in a tokamak?

In paleontology, what term describes a geologically brief, widespread collapse in biodiversity that eliminates an unusually large proportion of species worldwide, rather than the slower loss of species seen during ordinary background turnover?

Among Earth’s major mass extinctions, which event occurred about 252 million years ago at the boundary between two geologic periods, eliminated most marine species, and is linked to massive volcanic eruptions in Siberia?

Astronomers identified this comet in 1993 from images taken at Palomar Observatory, after Jupiter’s gravity had torn it into a chain of fragments. Those fragments plunged into Jupiter in July 1994; what comet was this?
In July 1994, the fragments of Shoemaker–Levy 9 slammed into this planet, leaving temporary dark impact marks in its cloud tops that were observed from Earth. Which gas giant was struck?

Released by the anterior pituitary, this gonadotropin undergoes a sharp mid-cycle rise that prompts release of an oocyte and supports formation of a hormone-secreting structure from the post-ovulatory follicle. What is it?

In humans, what event is induced by the mid-cycle surge of luteinizing hormone, when a mature oocyte is released from an ovarian follicle into the fallopian tube? This event marks the transition toward the luteal phase.

This American engineer and inventor helped make steam-powered navigation commercially practical in the United States. His 1807 Hudson River service used a vessel later popularly known as the Clermont; who was he?

Robert Fulton’s pioneering 1807 steamboat service ran between New York City and Albany, helping establish commercial steam navigation on the Hudson. What was the vessel commonly called, after the Hudson Valley estate of its backer Robert Livingston?

This device amplifies light by stimulated emission, often using a gain medium brought into population inversion. Its coherent, concentrated beam is used in pointers, barcode scanners, and fiber-optic communication. What is the device called?
The first laser, built in 1960 at Hughes Research Laboratories, used a synthetic ruby crystal as its gain medium. Which American physicist constructed that device?
A laser beam’s usefulness in interferometry and precision measurements stems in part from this property: its waves maintain a consistent phase relationship. What is this property of light called?

In 1995, researchers used laser cooling to bring dilute rubidium gas close to absolute zero, causing bosonic atoms to occupy a shared lowest-energy quantum state. What state of matter did they produce?

A transparent material can emit this electromagnetic glow when a charged particle travels through it faster than light’s phase speed in that material, while still remaining slower than light in a vacuum. The emitted light can form a forward-facing cone and appear blue around a reactor; what is this effect called?

In Cherenkov radiation, the emitted light waves form a shape that opens in the direction of the moving charged particle. Its angle depends on the particle’s speed, much like a sonic boom’s shock front; what is this geometric form called?

Used in coordination polymerization of olefins, these catalysts made it possible to produce highly stereoregular polypropylene. Early systems paired a transition-metal halide, such as titanium tetrachloride, with an organoaluminum compound; what family of catalysts is this?

The Ziegler–Natta catalyst takes its second name from an Italian chemist who developed stereospecific polymerization of propylene and shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Karl Ziegler. Who was this chemist?

This separation method selectively vaporizes a liquid mixture and then condenses the vapor, taking advantage of differences in boiling points or relative volatility. It is used in petroleum refining, alcohol production, desalination, and separating gases from air. What is this process?

In distillation, refineries heat crude oil and feed the vapor into a tall tower with a temperature gradient. Hydrocarbons condense at different heights according to their boiling ranges, producing streams for fuels and chemical feedstocks; what type of distillation is this?
Distillation of fermented beverages can enrich a volatile, two-carbon alcohol with the molecular formula C₂H₆O. This molecule is also used in fuels and antiseptics; what is it?

In cryogenic air separation, distillation of liquefied air yields oxygen, nitrogen, and this noble gas. It makes up just under 1% of dry air and is commonly used to provide an inert atmosphere for welding; identify it.

In this traveling disturbance, particles of the medium oscillate parallel to its direction of travel, creating alternating crowded and spread-out regions. Energy moves onward while particles move back and forth around their usual positions. What is this type of disturbance?
In a longitudinal wave traveling through air, some regions have particles farther apart and pressure lower than in the surrounding regions. What is the name for one of these low-pressure regions?
This single-celled protist has no fixed shape and moves by extending temporary parts of its cytoplasm. It can also engulf food particles through phagocytosis. What organism is it?
In an amoeba, what are the temporary extensions of cytoplasm that help it move and capture food called? These projections can form in different directions as the cell changes shape.
This web browser is developed and distributed by the company that also maintains Android, and its offline error page famously features a pixelated dinosaur game. What is this browser?
Google Chrome shares much of its source code with this open-source browser project, whose name also identifies a browser build without Google’s proprietary branding. What is the project?
In computer science, what indexed data structure stores an ordered collection of elements and lets a program retrieve an element by its position, commonly using square-bracket notation in Java?
In Java, the first element of an array is reached using 0, with each later element reached using a number one greater than the previous one. What numbering convention does this use?

This rendering technique constructs an image by following modeled light paths through a virtual scene, accounting for effects such as reflection and refraction. Compared with scan-line methods, it is often more computationally expensive. What is it called?

Although Ray tracing is best known for producing computer graphics, the same general approach can model sound traveling through a space. What is the distinct repetition heard when a reflected sound reaches a listener after the original?

A conductor or semiconductor carries current while a magnetic field is applied perpendicular to that current. The field deflects moving charge carriers sideways, producing a voltage across the material perpendicular to both the current and the field; what is this phenomenon called?

In Hall effect measurements of a semiconductor, an experimenter knows the applied current and magnetic-field strength and measures the transverse voltage. Besides indicating whether electrons or holes dominate through its polarity, what material quantity can the voltage’s magnitude help determine?

In a circuit, this quantity is the net rate at which charge crosses a surface, and its SI measure is one coulomb per second. It may be alternating or direct and is represented by I in Ohm’s law. What is this quantity?
The SI unit used to measure electric current is a base unit symbolized A, and one of these units corresponds to one coulomb passing per second. What is the unit’s name?

Electric current in a circuit can be measured with this instrument, which is connected in series so the same current passes through it as through the component being tested. What is the instrument called?

In routine blood typing, the plus or minus appended to an ABO group reports whether a key red-cell marker is present. What is the name of this blood-group feature, whose D form is most clinically significant?
The Rh factor comprises multiple red-cell markers, but one is the main determinant of the positive or negative designation in standard typing. What is the name of that marker?

Begun with measurements at Mauna Loa Observatory in 1958, this long-term graph tracks atmospheric carbon dioxide and shows seasonal fluctuations layered over a sustained increase. What is this record called?
The Keeling Curve is named for this American geochemist, who established the long-running carbon dioxide measurement program at Mauna Loa Observatory. Who was he?

They include mushrooms, molds, yeasts, and truffles, but unlike plants they do not photosynthesize; instead, they absorb nutrients after releasing digestive enzymes. Their cell walls contain a structural material also found in arthropod exoskeletons. What kingdom are these organisms part of?
Fungi have cell walls built from this tough structural polysaccharide, which is also a major component of arthropod exoskeletons. What is this substance called?
Fungi are the focus of this branch of biology, whose name combines the Greek word for fungus with a suffix meaning the study of something. What is this field called?

Many plants form this symbiotic association between their roots and fungi, which can help plants take up nutrients from the soil. Its two broad forms include arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal associations. What is this relationship called?

This group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve, often in association with elevated pressure inside the eye. It can cause progressive, irreversible vision loss and is a leading cause of blindness. What is this condition?

In open-angle glaucoma, impaired outflow of aqueous humor through this porous tissue near the junction of the cornea and iris can raise intraocular pressure even though the drainage angle remains open. What is this tissue called?

Orbiting the sixth planet from the Sun, whose pale yellow clouds contain ammonia crystals, this prominent system is made mostly of icy particles with some rocky dust. What is this planetary system called?
Within Saturn's rings, what is the broad gap separating the A and B rings, where orbital resonances with the moon Mimas help keep the region relatively clear?

In an electrochemical measurement, what conductive component connects an external circuit to an ionic solution, allowing charge to pass across the conductor–solution interface? The glass sensing element and the stable-potential component in a pH meter are both examples of it.
In a pH meter, one electrode sits in an electrolyte of known composition and provides a stable potential for comparison with the sensing electrode. What is this role-based type of electrode called?
In the Hall-Héroult method of producing aluminum, an external power supply drives a chemical change that would not occur spontaneously. What is the name of this current-driven process?
During electrolysis of molten table salt, positively charged ions move to the negative electrode and gain electrons. Which metal forms there?
In Brønsted–Lowry chemistry, one participant in a proton-transfer reaction accepts an H⁺ ion and becomes the conjugate acid of the original participant. What is this class of substance called?
A base does not need to contain hydroxide ions to accept a proton. In water, this common gas accepts a proton from a water molecule, producing ammonium and hydroxide ions; what is the gas?

This rotating low-pressure storm draws energy from evaporation over warm tropical or subtropical ocean water. Its organized thunderstorms can bring destructive winds, torrential rain, and coastal flooding. In the Atlantic and northeastern Pacific, what is this storm called?

A hurricane’s large-scale spin is deflected by this effect associated with Earth’s rotation. It helps explain why storms turn counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere. What is this effect called?

At the center of a mature hurricane lies a region often marked by comparatively light winds and relatively clear skies, encircled by the storm’s most intense thunderstorms. What is this central region called?
Meteorologists in the United States use this rating system to classify hurricanes by maximum sustained speeds, with Category 5 as its highest category. What is the system called?

When two nearby hurricanes or other tropical cyclones approach within roughly 1,400 kilometers, their circulations can rotate around a shared midpoint and sometimes merge. What is this named interaction called?

In chemical kinetics, this proportionality factor links how quickly a reaction proceeds to reactant concentrations raised to experimentally determined powers. For a given reaction at fixed temperature, it does not vary with reactant concentration, and its units depend on the overall reaction order. What is it called?

In radioactive transformations, a quantity denoted λ relates the frequency of nuclear disintegrations to the number of undecayed nuclei and determines an isotope’s half-life. What is this radioactive counterpart to a rate constant called?

Found in plants, fungi, many algae, and most bacteria, this rigid layer lies outside the plasma membrane, helps organisms withstand osmotic pressure, and is absent from animals. What is this structure?

Bacterial cell walls contain this mesh-like polymer, whose strands are built from alternating N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid residues. Penicillin weakens bacteria by interfering with the formation of this polymer. What is it?
In land-plant cell walls, this polysaccharide forms strong microfibrils that contribute to structural support. Its chains consist of glucose units joined by β-1,4 bonds. What is this polymer?
Fungal cell walls contain this nitrogen-bearing polymer, which is also a major structural component of arthropod exoskeletons. Its repeating units are derived from N-acetylglucosamine. What is it?
This British physicist used cathode-ray tubes to show that atoms contain smaller charged constituents, then proposed a model with negative charges embedded in diffuse positive matter. Who was he?
Joseph John Thomson’s cathode-ray experiments established that these negatively charged subatomic particles were constituents of atoms. What particle did he discover?

What navigational instrument uses a freely pivoting needle whose north-seeking end settles in a consistent direction, allowing travelers to orient themselves without landmarks? Nearby iron objects can disturb its reading.
A magnetic compass points toward magnetic north, which differs from true geographic north by a location-dependent angle. What is this angular difference called?

In VSEPR theory, a central atom with four bonding pairs and no lone pairs places its four attached atoms as far apart as possible in three dimensions. What spatial arrangement do these atoms form, as exemplified by methane?

In tetrahedral molecular geometry, methane has four equivalent C–H bonds directed toward the corners of a regular tetrahedron. What is the approximate angle between any two of those bonds, rounded to one decimal place?

This family of catalytic organic transformations joins two molecular fragments, commonly forming a new carbon–carbon bond, and often relies on a transition-metal catalyst. Its catalytic cycle frequently features oxidative addition, transmetalation, and reductive elimination. What is this family called?

Among cross-coupling reactions, which named method commonly uses a palladium catalyst and a base to join an organoboron reagent, such as a boronic acid, with an organic halide or pseudohalide, forming a carbon–carbon bond? Its organoboron partner distinguishes it from methods that use organotin, organozinc, or organomagnesium reagents.

Classical physics applied to blackbody radiation predicted that emitted energy would grow without bound as the wavelength became shorter, contrary to observation. What name is given to this failure, which helped motivate the development of quantum theory?

The Ultraviolet Catastrophe exposed a serious flaw in classical blackbody theory. Which German physicist addressed it in 1900 by proposing that energy is exchanged in discrete amounts proportional to frequency?

The infectious agent first identified through tobacco plants with mosaic-like leaf discoloration cannot reproduce independently; it must replicate inside living host cells. What class of agents includes HIV and coronaviruses?

In one route of bacteriophage infection, a virus inserts its genetic material into a bacterium’s chromosome, where it can be copied as the host cell divides without immediately bursting it. What is this mode of infection, contrasted with the route that rapidly produces new phages and ruptures the host cell?
Adult members of this amphibian group lack tails, and its members typically develop from aquatic tadpoles through metamorphosis. What kind of animal belongs to the order Anura?

The frog Dan’l Webster appears in a comic tale set in a California mining camp, where Simon Wheeler recounts a betting story. Which author wrote the tale and also wrote *The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn*?

During liquid-liquid extraction, shaking two immiscible liquids can sometimes leave a cloudy third layer between the aqueous and organic phases. What is the name for a mixture in which droplets of one liquid are dispersed throughout another?

When an emulsion complicates liquid-liquid extraction, chemists can use a pear-shaped piece of glassware with a stopcock near its narrow bottom to drain separated layers selectively. What is this apparatus called?

During normal digit development, cells in the tissue between emerging fingers are removed by a regulated process. It activates caspases, causes cells to shrink and form membrane blebs, and packages fragments for nearby cells to engulf rather than causing acute swelling and rupture. What is this process called?
In the intrinsic pathway of apoptosis, which mitochondrial protein is released into the cytosol and binds Apaf-1, helping assemble the apoptosome that activates initiator caspase-9?

Alfred Wegener used matching coastlines and fossils such as Glossopteris to argue that most of Earth’s land had once been joined in one immense landmass. What prehistoric supercontinent later fragmented into Laurasia and Gondwana?

Which German meteorologist and geophysicist proposed continental drift in 1912, using matching coastlines and fossil distributions to support the existence of Pangaea? He later developed his argument in *The Origin of Continents and Oceans*.

This material combines two or more elements, at least one of which is a metal. Its atoms may replace atoms in a metal’s crystal lattice or fit into spaces between them, producing properties unlike those of the ingredients. What is this material called?

Steel is an iron-based alloy whose properties can be changed by varying the amount of a particular nonmetal; chromium and nickel may also be added, but they are metals. Which nonmetal is combined with iron in steel?

In the troposphere, this stable atmospheric condition reverses the usual vertical pattern: air at higher levels within a layer is warmer than air below it. It can suppress convection and keep smoke and other pollutants near the ground. What is this condition called?
A temperature inversion in the stratosphere is associated with air warming at higher altitudes because a particular gas absorbs ultraviolet radiation. Which gas causes this warming?
In seawater’s carbonic-acid buffering system, this negatively charged ion helps neutralize added acid. It has the formula HCO₃⁻ and is the ion paired with sodium in baking soda; what is it?
Bicarbonate paired with sodium forms this familiar kitchen leavening agent, a fine white powder that helps baked goods rise by releasing carbon dioxide. What is its common name?

Unlike B lymphocytes, this adaptive immune lineage completes maturation in the thymus and uses a surface antigen receptor to recognize targets. What is the common name for this lymphocyte, central to cellular immunity?
Which subtype of T cell bears the CD8 surface protein and can directly destroy virus-infected or cancerous cells, rather than primarily coordinating other immune cells?

This specialized T cell helps prevent immune attacks against the body's own tissues by damping immune responses, and tumors may exploit it to reduce immune recognition. What is this cell type, also known as a suppressor T cell?

Which visible-spectrum color is indicated by sodium’s pair of D emission lines and is also the characteristic appearance of potassium chromate solution and solid lead iodide? These three distinct clues point to the same spectral hue.
In the context of Yellow, the two prominent solar D lines lie near 589 nm and are characteristic of an alkali metal’s emission spectrum. Which element produces this pair of lines?
Which small asteroid moon orbits the larger near-Earth asteroid Didymos? NASA’s 2022 kinetic-impact test shortened its orbital period by about 32 minutes.
Dimorphos was the target of NASA’s first full-scale test of using a kinetic impact to change an asteroid’s orbit. What mission sent the spacecraft that deliberately struck it in September 2022?
What is the name for the temperature at which a liquid’s vapor pressure equals the surrounding pressure, causing vaporization throughout the liquid rather than only at its surface?

Water’s boiling point is relatively high for a molecule of its size because neighboring molecules attract when the partially positive end of one molecule is drawn to a lone pair on the oxygen of another. What is the name of this intermolecular attraction?
On April 26, 1986, an explosion and fire at the fourth reactor of a Soviet nuclear power station released radioactive material into the environment. What is this event commonly called?
The Chernobyl disaster occurred at a nuclear power plant in a Soviet republic that became independent in 1991 and has Kyiv as its capital. What modern-day country was the plant located in?
Found in certain anaerobic eukaryotes, this mitochondrion-derived organelle produces ATP and releases molecular hydrogen during anaerobic metabolism. What is this organelle called?
In hydrogenosomes, a three-carbon end product of glycolysis is oxidized to acetyl-CoA, supplying electrons that help drive hydrogen production. Which glycolytic end product is used in this pathway?

When an atom’s s- and p-type electron distributions combine into a new set directed toward bonding, what is this process called? In ethene, carbon has three equivalent bonding directions in one plane, while a p-type distribution remains available for sideways overlap.

In orbital hybridization, what spatial arrangement results when one s orbital and two p orbitals combine to form three equivalent hybrids? They lie in one plane, separated by angles of 120 degrees, while one p orbital remains unhybridized.

An unstable atomic nucleus can spontaneously transform while emitting particles or electromagnetic radiation. The time it takes for half the nuclei in a sample to undergo this process is called its half-life. What is this process?
In radioactive decay of cobalt-60, a neutron in the nucleus turns into a proton while an electron and an antineutrino are emitted. Which specific mode of decay is this?
Tomatoes, potatoes, peppers, eggplants, henbane, and belladonna are all members of one flowering-plant family. What is this family commonly known as?
Within the Nightshade family, which Andean crop is cultivated chiefly for its starchy underground tubers and became a major European staple after Spanish introduction?
This group 13 element has atomic number 5 and is commonly classified as a metalloid. It is the lightest member of that class and has the chemical symbol B; what element is it?

Boron can form electron-deficient compounds in which an atom has only six electrons in its valence shell. What chemical rule, often described as favoring eight valence electrons in a filled shell, do such structures violate?
A medication can use this route without a needle: the patient swallows the dose, and the drug is absorbed through the gastrointestinal tract. What is this method of giving a drug called?
Unlike Oral Administration, Pfizer’s antiviral candidate for COVID-19 was described as requiring delivery through an IV and as inhibiting viral proteases. What is the name of this drug?
Unlike the geocentric model, this astronomical framework places the Sun at or near the center of the solar system and has Earth orbiting it. What is this model called?
Which Polish astronomer advanced heliocentrism in his 1543 work *De revolutionibus orbium coelestium*, presenting a model in which Earth and the other planets orbit the Sun?

What childhood disorder occurs when growing bones fail to mineralize normally, leaving them soft and weak? It can cause bone pain, impaired growth, and bowed legs, and is commonly associated with inadequate vitamin D.
In rickets, deficiency of what nutrient can impair calcium absorption and disrupt mineralization in growing bones? The body can also make this nutrient in the skin after exposure to sunlight.
What carbon molecule has the formula C₆₀ and a cage-like structure of 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons? James Tour used it as the wheels of an early nanocar.
Which British chemist helped identify Buckminsterfullerene through experiments on carbon clusters and later shared the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Robert Curl and Richard Smalley?
Einstein’s theory of gravity treats mass and energy as curving spacetime, with that curvature determining how matter and light move. What is this theory called?
In General Relativity, what phenomenon occurs when a massive object bends light from a more distant source, sometimes producing multiple images or a distorted arc?
What condition causes the skin and whites of the eyes to take on a yellow tint when excess pigment builds up in the bloodstream? It can be a sign of liver or biliary disease.
In jaundice, which yellow-orange pigment can accumulate in the blood when it is not adequately processed or excreted? The liver normally handles this pigment and releases it into bile.
In programming, this construct repeatedly executes a block of code according to a condition or iteration rule; common forms include for, while, and do-while. What is this construct called?
In Java, a while loop continues as long as its condition evaluates to true and stops when the condition has the opposite Boolean value. For example, the expression 1 == 2 evaluates to this value.

This peptide hormone is released by enteroendocrine cells in the small intestine in response to fats and amino acids. It contracts the gallbladder and promotes the release of pancreatic digestive enzymes; what is it called?
In the duodenum and jejunum, a particular enteroendocrine population responds to fats and amino acids by secreting cholecystokinin. What is this population called?
This large, white-coated Arctic mammal has broad paws for traveling across sea ice and hunts seals there. What is its common name?
The polar bear’s scientific name combines the Latin word for “bear” with an epithet meaning “of the sea.” What is this two-word binomial name?

When enormous energy is released in a fraction of a second by splitting heavy atoms, combining light atoms, or both, the event creates extreme heat, a destructive blast wave, intense radiation, and possibly radioactive fallout. What is this event called?
Which Manhattan Project event, conducted at a remote New Mexico site on July 16, 1945, marked the first full-scale nuclear explosion?
What class of lipids forms when one glycerol molecule is esterified to three fatty acids? These molecules make up most dietary fat and are the chief form in which excess energy is stored in the body.

Triglycerides are stored predominantly in clusters of lipid-filled cells found beneath the skin and around internal organs; these deposits also help insulate the body. What is this type of body material called?
This elementary particle is the massless quantum of electromagnetic radiation and carries the electromagnetic force. What is its natural singular name?

A photon’s energy is proportional to its frequency, as expressed by the relation E = hν. What is the constant represented by h, named for the physicist whose work on blackbody radiation introduced energy quanta?

When a photon strikes a metal, it can eject electrons in the photoelectric effect. Which physicist explained this effect in 1905 by treating light energy as discrete quanta, and later received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for that work?
In 1926, this American physical chemist proposed the word “photon” for a unit of radiant energy. What was his name?
This particle class includes the photon; its members have integer spin and are not subject to the Pauli exclusion principle. What is the class called?

In a storage hierarchy, this collection of hardware resources holds data and instructions for processing. It includes working space such as RAM and other levels that trade speed against capacity. What is this resource called?

Within computer memory, what small, fast storage area keeps data the CPU is likely to need soon, reducing the time required to retrieve it from RAM? Web browsers use an analogous structure to retain previously visited pages.

In relativistic particle physics, what hypothetical particle is associated with negative mass-squared and, if it existed as a free particle, would be constrained to move faster than light in a vacuum?

A Tachyon is hypothetical and would outrun light in a vacuum, whereas an ordinary charged particle can exceed light’s speed inside a transparent medium without violating relativity. What is the name of the blue glow produced in that medium, often seen in nuclear reactors?

This vector quantity is defined as the product of an object's mass and its velocity, so it has both magnitude and direction. In an isolated system, its total value is conserved, and an impulse changes it.
For linear momentum, what is the name of the quantity delivered by a force acting over a time interval, equal to the resulting change in momentum?
Linear momentum is measured in SI units equivalent to a newton-second. What is the unit written as the product of mass and velocity?
In quantum mechanics, what principle says that a particle cannot have simultaneously precise position and linear momentum, so sharpening a position measurement makes its momentum less definite?

On a binary phase diagram, what is the name of the composition-and-temperature condition at which a liquid mixture solidifies into two solid phases simultaneously? It is also the condition where that mixture reaches its lowest melting temperature.
In the lead–tin alloy system, the eutectic point occurs at about 61.9% tin by mass, producing the alloy’s minimum melting temperature. At what Celsius temperature does this transition occur?
What process encodes information so it occupies less storage space? It can preserve all the original information or reduce the size by intentionally discarding some of it.

In data compression, which widely used lossy image format is especially associated with digital-camera photographs and images on websites? Its compression can reduce file size by discarding visual detail, with a tradeoff in image quality.

A branching network of vascular bundles runs through a plant’s flattened photosynthetic blade, linking its central midrib to smaller regions. It carries water and minerals into the blade and transports sugars made there away; what is one of these structures called?
A leaf vein contains two principal transport tissues. Unlike xylem, which mainly carries water and minerals, which tissue carries sugars produced by photosynthesis to other parts of the plant?

This group consists of closely related Galápagos songbirds, along with one species from Cocos Island, whose different beak shapes are linked to different feeding habits. Their diversification from a common ancestor is a classic example of adaptive radiation. What are these birds commonly called?

During a severe drought, Peter and Rosemary Grant found that larger-beaked Darwin's finches were more likely to survive because they could crack the hard seeds that remained. What evolutionary process does this change in survival illustrate?

A polypeptide can be described by its exact residue-by-residue order, written from the amino terminus toward the carboxyl terminus. This foundational description does not specify helices or three-dimensional packing; what level of organization is it?

In the primary structure of a protein, adjacent amino acid residues are linked along the backbone by a covalent amide linkage formed between the carboxyl group of one residue and the amino group of the next. What is this linkage called?

This gas giant is the sixth planet from the Sun and the Solar System’s second-largest planet after Jupiter. It takes about 29.45 years to complete one orbit and is known for its extensive system of bright rings. Which planet is it?

Saturn’s most prominent surrounding structures are made mainly of water-ice particles, mixed with rocky debris and dust. The Cassini Division separates two of their broad sections, called the A and B portions. What are these structures?

Saturn’s largest moon is also the second-largest moon in the Solar System, and it is larger than Mercury despite having less mass. It is the only moon known to have a substantial atmosphere. What is its name?
