This joint NASA–ESA mission became the first spacecraft to orbit Saturn and carried a probe that landed on Titan. Its observations revealed lakes of liquid hydrocarbons on the moon’s surface. What was the mission called?

This American astronomer worked with Kent Ford to measure the motion of stars and gas in the Andromeda Galaxy, finding that its outer regions rotated faster than visible matter alone predicted. Her galaxy rotation-curve studies became influential evidence for dark matter; who was she?

Vera Rubin’s studies of galaxies helped shape the science goals of a Chilean facility designed to repeatedly image the southern sky. Located on Cerro Pachón and equipped with the 8.4-meter Simonyi Survey Telescope, what facility was designed to conduct the Legacy Survey of Space and Time?

In 1993, Vera Rubin received this presidential U.S. honor for her contributions to astronomy. It recognizes outstanding contributions across the physical, biological, mathematical, and engineering disciplines, and is distinct from the parallel presidential honor for technological achievement; what award is it?

In a closed system, a measurable quantity such as energy or electric charge can remain unchanged over time, even as it shifts between forms or parts of the system. What is the general name for this kind of physical principle?

A conservation law guarantees that total linear momentum remains unchanged when two objects hit, even though some kinetic energy is converted into heat, sound, or deformation. What is this type of interaction called?

Behind the iris and pupil sits a transparent, flexible structure whose changing curvature helps focus light sharply on the retina. Clouding of this structure is the defining feature of cataracts; what is it called?
For near vision, the lens becomes rounder as the ciliary muscle contracts and tension in the suspensory fibers decreases. What is the name of this adjustment that increases the eye’s optical power?

In aqueous chemistry, this logarithmic quantity expresses acidity based on hydrogen-ion activity, with lower values indicating greater acidity. It is defined as the negative base-10 logarithm of that activity, often approximated using hydrogen-ion concentration. What is it?

Which equation is used to estimate a buffer’s pH from the pKa of its weak acid and the ratio of its conjugate base to that acid? It adds the base-10 logarithm of that ratio to the pKa and is named for two chemists.

An electrically neutral constituent of atomic nuclei, this particle is slightly more massive than a proton and has three valence quarks: one up and two down. Its count can vary among isotopes of the same element, while the proton count stays the same. What particle is it?

In examples showing how neutron counts distinguish isotopes, this radioactive form has six protons and eight neutrons, while its stable counterpart has six protons and six neutrons. What isotope is it?

Scientists estimate the numeric ages of rocks, minerals, and some once-living materials by measuring parent and daughter isotopes produced through predictable radioactive decay. What is the name of this family of isotope-based age-estimation methods?

In radiometric dating, scientists use a radioactive isotope’s known decay rate to estimate when a material formed. What is the term for the time required for the number of radioactive parent atoms in a sample to fall to 50 percent of its initial amount?

This hereditary molecule is built from two antiparallel nucleotide chains twisted into a double helix, with adenine pairing with thymine and cytosine with guanine. What molecule stores genetic instructions and can be copied through complementary base pairing?

In DNA, adenine and thymine are complementary and joined by two hydrogen bonds. Their association is restored when each separated strand serves as a template during replication. Which two-base combination is described?

In DNA, these empirical relationships state that the amount of adenine equals thymine and the amount of cytosine equals guanine. The findings helped constrain early models of the molecule’s double-helix structure. What are these relationships called?

A famous X-ray diffraction image of DNA, made by Raymond Gosling in Rosalind Franklin’s laboratory, displayed an X-shaped pattern characteristic of a helical structure. By what short label is this image commonly known?

This method makes many copies of selected DNA sequences by cycling through denaturation, primer annealing, and extension. It commonly uses a heat-stable enzyme originally isolated from *Thermus aquaticus*; what is the method called?

This class of psychoactive substances includes psilocybin and LSD, and can alter perception and consciousness. Researchers are also studying its potential therapeutic uses, including for depression. What is this class called?

Psychedelic drugs are being studied as possible treatments for this condition, which can follow combat, assault, or abuse. It can involve intrusive memories, avoidance of reminders, and heightened alertness long after the event. What condition is this?

This NASA rover landed on Mars in August 2012 using a sky-crane system. Its instruments investigate the planet’s geology and whether ancient environments could have supported microbial life. What is the rover’s name?

Curiosity has been exploring a roughly 96-mile-wide impact basin on Mars since its 2012 landing. Its route has taken it toward the layered mountain rising from the basin’s floor; what is the basin called?
This soft, highly reactive alkali metal has atomic number 19 and the chemical symbol K. Its compounds are essential plant nutrients and are commonly added to fertilizers; what element is it?

In potassium-based radiometric dating, potassium-40 decays in minerals to produce which isotope of a noble gas? Measuring its abundance relative to the parent isotope helps geologists estimate a rock’s age.

In population biology, this reproductive strategy tends to be favored in environments near their resource limits, where populations are relatively stable. It involves producing fewer offspring while investing more in each one. What is this strategy?

K-selection is often associated with crowded environments where resources are limited. Georgy Gause’s principle says that two species competing for the same limiting resource cannot occupy the same niche indefinitely; what is this principle called?

Which named law of hydrostatics says that a body wholly or partly immersed in a fluid experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces? It helps explain why an object may float in one liquid but sink in another.

In applications of Archimedes' principle, what upward effect on an immersed body results from pressure being greater at its lower surface than its upper surface? A vessel’s ability to adjust this effect can be changed by taking water into or out of its ballast tank.

It examines destination IP addresses and forwards packets between distinct networks, rather than merely repeating signals within one network. In homes, the same device commonly links a local Ethernet network to the Internet and may provide wireless access. What is this network device called?

A Router may have both a broad /16 route and a more narrowly scoped /24 route that apply to the same destination IP. Its forwarding decision favors the /24 entry because it covers a smaller address range; what routing rule describes this choice?
What salt-tolerant trees and shrubs grow in saline or brackish coastal waters? The vast forest of the Sundarbans, formed in the Ganges Delta, is made up largely of them.
Mangroves grow along the coasts of this southeastern U.S. state, whose island chain includes Key West and Key Largo. Miami and Orlando are among its major cities.

These blood-feeding arachnids have four pairs of legs as adults and attach to vertebrate hosts to take a blood meal. Some species can transmit pathogens, including those that cause Lyme disease. What are these animals called?

Ticks can transmit a bacterial illness caused in North America primarily by *Borrelia burgdorferi*. The illness takes its name from a Connecticut town where a cluster of cases was investigated in the 1970s. What is this illness called?

This rotating machine component transmits motion and torque between shafts by meshing its teeth with those of another component. Its size and tooth count can change the output speed and force; what is its common name?
For two meshing gears, this dimensionless quantity is found by comparing their tooth counts and tells how their rotational speeds and torque are related. What is this quantity called?

This third planet from the Sun is the largest and most massive of the four rocky planets, and liquid water covers most of its surface. It is the only astronomical body currently known to support life. What is it?
Earth has one permanent natural satellite whose gravity helps stabilize the planet’s axial tilt and raises ocean tides. What is this satellite?
Earth’s liquid outer core generates the magnetic field that creates this region around the planet, which deflects much of the solar wind. What is this region called?
What are the rigid sections of Earth’s lithosphere, made of crust and uppermost mantle, that move slowly over the softer asthenosphere and interact at boundaries?
Tectonic plates move over this hot, weak part of the upper mantle, which can slowly flow beneath the lithosphere. What is this layer called?
At mid-ocean ridges, tectonic plates move apart as magma cools and adds new oceanic crust. What is this process called?

These biodiverse marine ecosystems are built chiefly by colonies of tiny cnidarian polyps that secrete calcium-carbonate skeletons, while symbiotic photosynthetic algae often supply much of their food. Their structures may fringe coasts, lie offshore beyond lagoons, or ring lagoons; what are they called?
In coral reefs, what name is given to a ring-shaped formation that encloses a lagoon, often remaining after the volcanic island around which it developed subsides below sea level?

Generated mainly by dynamo processes in the planet’s liquid outer core, this influence guides compass needles and deflects charged particles from the solar wind. Its ancient polarity changes are recorded in alternating bands of reversed polarity in ocean-floor rocks. What is it?

Earth’s magnetic field traps energetic charged particles in two broad, doughnut-shaped regions around the planet. Measurements from Explorer 1 helped identify these regions in 1958; what are they called?
What common name describes large birds of prey with hooked bills and powerful talons, including the golden and bald varieties?

Which North American eagle is the national bird of the United States and has a white head and tail contrasting with its dark brown body as an adult? It is also pictured on the Great Seal of the United States.

A French astronomer in the eighteenth century assembled this list to distinguish comet-like fixed objects from comets. Its entries include M31 for the Andromeda Galaxy and M45 for the Pleiades. What is the name of this list?

In the Messier catalog, many fuzzy-looking celestial objects were grouped under a broad label used by eighteenth-century astronomers. Today, only a minority of the catalog’s objects truly belong to that class; M1 and M16 are examples historically nicknamed the Crab and the Eagle. What term did Messier commonly use for these objects?
Released by the adrenal medulla during acute stress, this catecholamine increases heart rate and helps mobilize stored energy. What is the common name of this hormone and neurotransmitter?

Adrenaline is one of the signals involved in the body's rapid adjustment to sudden danger. What is the standard name for the sympathetic pattern that raises alertness and prepares the body for immediate action?
This radioactive actinide has atomic number 92 and the chemical symbol U. One of its naturally occurring isotopes can sustain a nuclear fission chain reaction and fuel reactors. What element is it?

Natural uranium consists mostly of an isotope that is not readily fissile with slow neutrons, while this much rarer isotope makes up about 0.7% of it. This isotope can sustain a thermal-neutron chain reaction and is enriched for many reactor fuels. What isotope is it?

Founded as a partnership on April 1, 1976, by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne, this company introduced the Macintosh in 1984 and later combined phone, music-player, and internet functions in the iPhone. What company also offers services such as iCloud and the App Store?

Apple Inc. introduced this personal computer in 1977 with color graphics and expansion slots, helping it reach customers beyond computer hobbyists. The spreadsheet program VisiCalc helped boost sales of this model; what was it called?
What class of substances consists of positively and negatively charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction, as in crystalline salts such as sodium chloride?

In a solution of lead(II) chloride, adding sodium chloride supplies more chloride ions and causes some lead(II) chloride to precipitate. What named effect explains this reduced solubility of ionic compounds when an ion shared by the solid is added to the solution?

This form of electromagnetic radiation has wavelengths shorter than ultraviolet light but longer than gamma radiation. Its ability to pass through soft tissue while being absorbed more strongly by bone makes it useful for medical radiography.

While studying cathode rays in 1895, this German physicist observed that a nearby fluorescent screen glowed even when shielded from direct light. He called the newly detected rays “X” because their nature was unknown; identify this discoverer of X-rays.

At King's College London, this chemist produced the diffraction image known as Photo 51, whose pattern provided crucial evidence about DNA's helical structure. Which researcher used X-rays to create that image?

At standard conditions, this reactive nonmetal occurs mainly as a colorless, odorless molecule made from two covalently bonded atoms. Its atomic number is 8, and it is essential to aerobic respiration and supports combustion. What element is this?
In the history of Oxygen, which English natural philosopher reported isolating the gas in 1774 by heating mercuric oxide and described it as “dephlogisticated air”?

In atmospheric discussions of Oxygen, what three-atom allotrope is monitored in Dobson units and absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere, while becoming a pollutant near Earth’s surface?
The ordinary diatomic form of Oxygen is attracted to a magnetic field because its molecular orbitals contain two unpaired electrons. What magnetic behavior does this demonstrate?
Which French chemist drew on experiments involving Oxygen to identify it as an element and explain its role in combustion? He also coined its name from Greek roots associated with acid formation.

This carnivorous marsupial is native only to Tasmania, an island south of mainland Australia, and is known for its powerful jaws and harsh calls. Its populations have been severely reduced by a contagious cancer that causes facial tumors. What animal is it?

In populations of the Tasmanian devil, a transmissible cancer spread mainly through biting has caused severe declines and produces abnormal growths around the face and mouth. What condition is commonly abbreviated DFTD?

This U.S. National Science Foundation-supported observatory network operates matched L-shaped detectors in Hanford, Washington, and Livingston, Louisiana, each with two four-kilometer vacuum arms. Rather than collecting images, its instruments split and recombine laser beams to register minute changes in arm length. What facility made the first direct detection of a signal from merging black holes in 2015?

LIGO’s interferometers register these signals when a passing disturbance changes the lengths of their arms and alters the recombined laser-light pattern. Predicted by general relativity, they were first directly detected by LIGO in 2015 from a pair of merging black holes; what are these spacetime ripples called?

This American chemist helped establish quantum chemistry, developed a foundational theory of chemical bonding, and later campaigned against nuclear weapons. He received the 1954 Nobel Prize in Chemistry and the 1962 Nobel Peace Prize, each without sharing it; who was he?
Linus Pauling devised a numerical scale that gives fluorine the highest value and describes how strongly an atom attracts shared electrons in a bond. What property does the scale measure?
In research on protein structure, Linus Pauling helped identify a secondary-structure motif shaped like a coiled spiral and stabilized by hydrogen bonds. What is this motif called?
Cancer can progress when cells leave a primary tumor, travel to another part of the body, and form a secondary tumor there. What is this process of spread called?
During metastasis, tumor cells can enter this network of vessels, which returns excess tissue fluid to the bloodstream and passes through lymph nodes. What is this network called?

This Soviet spacecraft series began with a 1957 launch that placed the first artificial satellite in Earth orbit. Its second mission carried a dog, and a later craft was designed to study the Van Allen radiation belts. What was the name of this series?
Within the Sputnik program, which Moscow stray became the first living creature to orbit Earth aboard its second spacecraft, launched in November 1957?

An English primatologist began studying wild chimpanzees at Gombe Stream in what is now Tanzania in 1960, recording tool use and social behaviors that challenged prevailing assumptions about nonhuman animals. Who was this researcher?

Jane Goodall conducted decades of chimpanzee fieldwork in a protected area along Lake Tanganyika’s eastern shore in western Tanzania. First established as a game reserve in 1943, what is this site’s full official name?

In a Lewis structure, what is the name for two valence electrons localized on one atom instead of shared in a covalent bond? This nonbonding set of electrons can repel bonding regions and influence molecular shape.

In VSEPR descriptions of water, the central oxygen has two O–H bonding regions and two lone pairs, while its electron-domain arrangement is tetrahedral. What shape results, with an H–O–H bond angle of about 104.5°?

In thermodynamics, this state function describes how energy is distributed among a system’s accessible microscopic arrangements. It is central to the second law, which constrains spontaneous changes in an isolated system. What is this quantity?

One statistical interpretation of entropy relates it to the logarithm of the number of microscopic configurations compatible with a macroscopic state. Which Austrian physicist’s tombstone bears the equation expressing that relation, and whose work helped establish statistical mechanics?

The name entropy was introduced in 1865 by a German physicist, who coined it from a Greek root meaning transformation and defined the state function using reversible heat transfer divided by absolute temperature. Which scientist introduced the term?
Which law says that the entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease during spontaneous processes? It helps explain why many macroscopic processes have a preferred direction.

In the statistical-mechanical formula connecting entropy with the natural logarithm of the number of accessible microstates, a universal constant supplies the proportionality factor. What constant is approximately 1.380649 × 10⁻²³ joules per kelvin?
Used by submarines and ships to locate submerged objects, this technology sends out acoustic pulses and detects the echoes that return. What is this method of underwater detection?

In pulse-based Sonar, a system uses the delay between sending an acoustic pulse and detecting its returning echo, along with the speed of sound in water, to calculate an object's range. What is the name for this measured interval?

Which soft carbon allotrope consists of stacked hexagonal sheets held together much more weakly than the bonds within each sheet? Its layers shear onto paper in pencil marks and can be mechanically peeled away one sheet at a time.

Graphite can be peeled with ordinary adhesive tape to isolate a single-atom-thick carbon sheet, a method associated with Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov. What is this two-dimensional material called?

What umbrella term names a group of mental and behavioral conditions in which patterns of food intake are persistently disrupted, sometimes through severe restriction and sometimes through recurrent bingeing or compensatory behaviors? These conditions can significantly impair physical health or psychological and social functioning.

Within eating disorders, one diagnosis involves recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food with a sense of lost control, followed by repeated compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, fasting, or misuse of laxatives. A markedly low body weight is not required for this diagnosis; what is it?

When light shines on a material, electrons can be emitted only if the light exceeds a minimum frequency. Increasing the light’s intensity can increase the number of emitted electrons without increasing their maximum kinetic energy; what is this phenomenon called?

Which physicist explained the photoelectric effect in a 1905 paper by proposing that light transfers energy in discrete packets, and later received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for that explanation?

This branch of analytical chemistry determines which substances are present in a sample rather than measuring their amounts. It uses characteristic reactions, such as distinctive flame colors or the formation of insoluble solids, to identify them. What is this branch called?
In qualitative analysis, a reagent may be added to a solution so that dissolved ions combine to form an insoluble solid that settles out. What is this kind of chemical process called?

A rapidly spreading computer worm appeared in 2000 as an email attachment disguised as a love letter. Once run, it could overwrite files and send copies of itself to addresses in the victim’s contacts. What was this worm commonly known as?
The ILOVEYOU worm arrived in an attachment with a misleading double extension ending in “.vbs,” and its code ran through Windows Script Host. What scripting language does that extension identify?

This family of fibrous proteins is built from amino-acid chains whose cross-links help create durable structures in vertebrate skin. It forms human hair and nails as well as structures such as feathers, beaks, and claws; what is it called?

Within keratin, which structural form has a zigzag, pleated-sheet-like backbone rather than the coiled-coil structure found in the other major form, and occurs in hard structures such as bird beaks and claws?

A molecule can contain polar bonds yet have their bond dipoles cancel because of its shape, leaving no overall molecular dipole. This property is often associated with stronger partitioning into an organic phase than into water; what is it called?

In discussions of nonpolarity, amphiphilic surfactants in water arrange with their water-attracting head groups on the outside and their hydrocarbon tails tucked away from the surrounding water. What is the water-excluding interior of this spherical aggregate called?

Seismic S waves cannot travel through this liquid shell, producing a shadow zone on the far side of the planet. It lies beneath the mantle and surrounds the solid central sphere. What is this layer called?

Earth's outer core contains electrically conductive molten metal, and the movement of this fluid helps sustain the planet's magnetic field. What is the name of the process that generates the field through this motion?
This threshold is commonly symbolized Ea in chemical kinetics; reactant molecules must meet or exceed it to reach the transition state and proceed toward products.
Activation energy was named in work from 1889 by this Swedish scientist, who also developed a mathematical relationship between temperature and reaction rates. Who was he?
Activation energy appears in the exponent of this equation, which relates a reaction’s rate constant to temperature and includes a pre-exponential factor. What is the equation called?

Born in Kiel in 1858, this German theoretical physicist found a mathematical formula for the spectrum of radiation emitted by an ideal absorber in thermal equilibrium. His solution introduced the idea that energy is exchanged in discrete amounts, helping launch quantum theory. Who was he?

In Max Planck’s account of blackbody radiation, the energy of an individual quantum is proportional to its frequency. The proportionality constant, represented by h, is approximately 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ joule-seconds; what is it called?

This enveloped coronavirus caused the COVID-19 pandemic and is a descendant of a virus associated with a major respiratory outbreak that began in southern China in 2002. It can enter human cells by binding to ACE2 receptors; what is its name?

On SARS-CoV-2, this prominent surface structure binds to ACE2 and helps the virus enter cells. Mutations in it have helped define major variants such as Delta and Omicron, and it is encoded by many COVID-19 mRNA vaccines. What is this protein?
This parasitic mite infests honey bees and reproduces inside capped brood cells, where it feeds on developing bees. It also helps spread viruses linked to colony losses; what is its species name?
Varroa destructor transmits this pathogen, which is associated with newly emerged honey bees that have shortened abdomens and malformed flight appendages. What is it called?

These ecosystems have soils that remain saturated or are seasonally inundated, and they include marshes, bogs, fens, and swamps. What broad ecosystem type is exemplified by Florida’s Everglades and Georgia’s Okefenokee Swamp?
Adopted in 1971, this treaty named for an Iranian city established an international framework for conserving wetlands and promoting their “wise use.” What is this agreement called?

Beneath the mantle lies a metallic region made mainly of iron and nickel, with a solid central part and a liquid surrounding part. Convection in its liquid portion helps sustain the planet’s magnetic field; what is the natural name of this entire major layer?
Within Earth’s core, seismic waves reveal a liquid iron-rich shell surrounding the solid inner core; S-waves do not pass through this shell. What is this liquid subdivision called?

In geometry and thermodynamics, this quantity is commonly symbolized by V and describes the three-dimensional space occupied by a solid, liquid, or gas. Its SI unit is the cubic meter, though liters are also commonly used. What is this quantity?
For measurements of Volume, this unit is exactly one cubic decimeter. It is also equal to the space occupied by a cube measuring 10 centimeters on each side. What is the unit?
This budding yeast is widely used in baking and fermentation, and it became the first eukaryote whose complete genome was sequenced. What is its scientific name?

In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, what naturally occurring circular DNA molecule uses Flp recombinase-mediated recombination at FRT sites as part of maintaining its high copy number? This element is a well-studied example of extrachromosomal DNA in a eukaryotic cell.
Made by treating narrow strips with dyes derived from lichens, this familiar pH-testing material changes from blue in basic solutions to red or pink in acidic ones. What is it called?

Litmus paper belongs to a class of substances that reveal whether a solution is below or above neutral pH through a visible color change; phenolphthalein is another example used in titrations. What is this class called?
Certain soil bacteria use the enzyme nitrogenase to reduce atmospheric N₂ into ammonia, which can be incorporated into amino acids and other biomolecules. What is this biological conversion called?

In many legume–bacterium partnerships, nitrogen fixation occurs in rounded swellings attached to the plant’s underground, water-absorbing organs. These swellings house the bacterial symbionts; what are they called?
In organic chemistry, what principle describes the usual ability of the element with atomic number 6 to form four covalent bonds, supporting extensive molecular frameworks?
In the context of Carbon Tetravalence, what orbital mixing state gives a central atom four equivalent bonding directions arranged tetrahedrally, as commonly found at saturated chiral centers?

This American theoretical physicist led the Los Alamos Laboratory during World War II and served as the Manhattan Project’s scientific leader. He was also present at the Trinity test on July 16, 1945, the first detonation of a nuclear device. Who was he?

In 1947, J. Robert Oppenheimer became director of this independent research institution in Princeton, New Jersey, succeeding its founding director, Abraham Flexner. Albert Einstein was among its faculty, and it is separate from Princeton University. What institution was it?

In 1963, J. Robert Oppenheimer received this U.S. government distinction in recognition of his contributions to theoretical physics. Named for an Italian-American physicist who helped lead the first nuclear reactor project, it is one of the nation’s major honors for scientific achievement. What was it?

An English physician and physicist presented evidence for the wave nature of light in 1801, and a version using two narrow openings appeared in his 1807 lectures. In the familiar arrangement, light from the openings overlaps to form alternating bright and dark fringes on a screen; what is the conventional name for this setup?

In Young’s double-slit experiment, bright bands form where light waves arrive in phase and reinforce, while dark bands form where they arrive out of phase and cancel. What wave phenomenon produces this alternating pattern?
A 1938 spectroscopy test examined light from rapidly moving hydrogen canal rays and compared its spectral shifts to predictions for relativistic time dilation. What is this experiment called?

The relativistic correction tested by the Ives–Stilwell experiment predicts a frequency shift for light observed at right angles to the emitter’s motion. What is this relativistic frequency-shift phenomenon called?

This genetic condition is usually caused by extra genetic material from chromosome 21. Its less common forms include cases where only some cells carry the extra material or where it is attached to another chromosome. What is the condition?
In most cases of Down syndrome, the extra chromosome 21 material results from a random error during cell division, when chromosomes do not separate as they should. What is this error called?

Farmers add this material to soil or directly to plants to supply nutrients and support growth when the soil’s existing supply is insufficient. It can be a commercial blend or an organic material such as compost or manure. What is this material called?
In fertilizer, this nutrient appears third in the standard N-P-K label, after nitrogen and phosphorus. It helps plants stay hardy and resist disease; what nutrient is it?

Ecologists use this quantity, often denoted N, to report how many members of one species occupy a defined area at a particular time. It counts individuals rather than expressing them per unit area or volume; what is it called?

In ecology, population size can be compared with an environment’s resource-limited ceiling: unlike a current count, this ceiling is the greatest abundance the habitat can support. What is this concept, commonly represented by K?

In a flower, what is the female reproductive structure that typically includes a pollen-receiving surface, a connecting stalk, and an ovary containing ovules? Pollen must reach this structure for fertilization to proceed.
In a typical flower, which part of the pistil sits at the tip of the style and receives pollen grains? Its often sticky surface helps pollen adhere before growing toward the ovary.
What runtime error occurs when a program exhausts the memory reserved for active function calls, often because recursive calls continue too deeply? It can cause execution to terminate with a crash.

On the programming Q&A site Stack Overflow, what is the name for a recursive routine that repeatedly calls itself without ever reaching a base case? Its growing chain of calls is a common cause of the runtime failure described above.
What is the general name for formal systems used to write instructions for computers, including Ada, Python, Java, and C++?
In the history of programming languages, which U.S. Navy rear admiral helped develop COBOL and is associated with the discovery of a real moth in a computer relay?

This common human commensal yeast is a leading cause of oral thrush and vaginal yeast infections. In laboratory identification, it can be distinguished by forming germ tubes when incubated in serum at body temperature; what species is it?

Candida albicans can remain harmless on mucosal surfaces but cause oral thrush, vulvovaginitis, or invasive disease when host defenses are disrupted. What is the medical term for infections caused by this yeast and related Candida species?

Unlike ordinary software failures, these programs are deliberately created to damage systems, steal information, disrupt operations, or gain unauthorized access. Viruses, worms, trojans, and ransomware are all examples; what broad term names this kind of software?

Discovered in 2010, this worm targeted Siemens Step7 software used to control industrial equipment and manipulated centrifuge speeds at Iran’s Natanz facility. Which malware is associated with that operation?

For a fixed amount of gas kept at constant temperature, this relationship says that pressure and volume vary inversely. The product of the two quantities remains constant, so increasing pressure decreases volume; name the gas law.

Boyle's law is one of the gas relationships combined with Charles's, Gay-Lussac's, and Avogadro's laws to form this equation. Written as PV = nRT, it relates pressure, volume, amount of gas, and absolute temperature; name the law.

Pan helps maintain the Encke Gap, Mimas bears the giant Herschel crater, and Enceladus vents water vapor from fractures near its south pole. What group of natural satellites orbiting the ringed planet includes all three?
Among the Moons of Saturn, which is the largest and has a dense nitrogen-rich atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane and ethane? The Huygens probe descended through its atmosphere to its surface.

This German meteorologist and geophysicist proposed continental drift after comparing matching coastlines and fossil evidence across oceans. He later died during an expedition in Greenland. Who was he?

Alfred Wegener used matching coastlines and fossil distributions on widely separated continents to argue they had once been joined. What supercontinent did he propose, whose name comes from Greek roots meaning “all” and “Earth”?

This active stratovolcano on Sicily’s eastern coast is among Europe’s highest and most frequently erupting volcanoes, and its lava flows have at times threatened the nearby city of Catania. What is the volcano’s name?
Mount Etna stands on the eastern side of this Mediterranean island, whose northeastern tip is separated from mainland Italy by the Strait of Messina. What is the island called?

Name the broad submarine mountain system created as tectonic plates move apart and new oceanic crust forms. These chains commonly extend through ocean basins and are associated with volcanism and shallow earthquakes.

Among the world’s mid-ocean ridges, which named submarine range runs down the center of the ocean basin separating the North American and Eurasian plates in the north from the South American and African plates farther south?

This vector quantity assigns a strength and direction to every point in space and is produced by moving electric charges, currents, or magnetized materials. Commonly represented by B, it can deflect moving charges and exert forces on magnets. What is this quantity called?

When a current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field perpendicular to the current, moving charge carriers are deflected toward opposite sides of the conductor. The resulting transverse voltage lets researchers investigate those carriers. What is this phenomenon called?

In 1820, this Danish physicist noticed that a nearby compass needle moved when current flowed through a wire, revealing a connection between electricity and the magnetic field. Who made this observation?

The SI unit used to measure magnetic field B is named after a Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer born in Smiljan in 1856, known for his work on alternating-current systems. What is this unit?

Unlike conduction through stationary matter or radiation through empty space, this mode of heat transfer carries thermal energy through the bulk motion of a fluid. For example, warmer, less-dense fluid can rise while cooler fluid sinks. What is this process called?

In convection studies, this dimensionless quantity compares heat transfer across a fluid layer with the transfer that would occur by conduction alone. A value of 1 corresponds to conduction alone, while larger values indicate enhanced heat transfer. What is it called?

This small insect became a foundational genetics model through laboratory studies of mutations and sex-linked traits. Its salivary glands contain unusually large polytene chromosomes, and it is commonly associated with fermenting fruit. What species is it?

In Drosophila melanogaster, experiments with a white-eyed mutant helped show that eye color could be inherited along with the X chromosome. Which Columbia University geneticist conducted these influential studies?
A coating made from vertically aligned carbon nanotubes absorbs nearly all visible light, making treated surfaces appear exceptionally black. What is this material called?

Vantablack became controversial in the art world after one sculptor secured exclusive artistic-use rights to it. The British-Indian artist is also known for creating Cloud Gate, the reflective sculpture nicknamed “the Bean” in Chicago; who is he?

Astronomers use this classification scheme to group galaxies by visible shape into elliptical, lenticular, and spiral forms. Its familiar layout places lenticular galaxies between the elliptical and spiral families; what is the scheme called?
In the Hubble Sequence, what is the name of the schematic that places elliptical galaxies along a central stem and shows spiral galaxies branching into groups based on their bar structure?
On Chicago’s Museum Campus, this institution opened in 1930 as the first planetarium in the Western Hemisphere and combines an astronomy museum with an observatory. What institution is it?
The Adler Planetarium includes a public observing facility equipped with a 20-inch reflecting telescope for viewing the night sky. What is this facility called?

This industrial route converts ammonia to nitric acid by first catalytically oxidizing the ammonia, then oxidizing the resulting nitrogen oxides and absorbing them in water. Named for the German chemist who developed it, what is this process called?
In the Ostwald process, ammonia is oxidized at high temperature over a thin, open network of noble metal, producing nitric oxide and water. What catalyst is commonly used for this reaction?

Astronomers use this dimensionless quantity to describe how much a celestial path around a central body departs from a perfect circle. A value of zero indicates a circular path, while larger values indicate increasingly elongated paths.

Among the eight major planets, this smallest and innermost planet has the greatest orbital eccentricity. It also has a 3:2 spin-orbit resonance, rotating three times for every two revolutions around the Sun.
During a titration, this substance shifts visibly between colors across a characteristic pH range, helping show when a reaction has reached its endpoint. What is this type of substance called?

One familiar acid-base indicator is supplied in narrow test strips colored with dyes derived from lichens. These strips turn red in acidic solutions and blue in basic ones; what is the indicator called?

This chronic immune-mediated disease affects the brain and spinal cord, where inflammation damages the insulation around nerve fibers and can leave lesions visible on MRI. Its symptoms may follow relapsing-remitting or progressive courses; what is this disease called?
In multiple sclerosis, immune-mediated damage targets the protective fatty insulation that helps axons in the central nervous system transmit signals efficiently. What is this substance called?

Unlike covalent or ionic bonds that connect atoms within a molecule, these attractions act between separate molecules and depend on their electron distributions. They include induced-dipole attractions and hydrogen bonding; what is this general class called?

Among intermolecular forces, which especially strong attraction occurs when the partially positive end of an N–H, O–H, or F–H bond interacts with a lone pair on N, O, or F in a neighboring molecule? It helps explain water’s unusually high boiling point.

At Columbia, this American geneticist led fruit-fly experiments that supported the chromosome theory of inheritance and helped establish genetic linkage. He received the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning chromosomes’ role in heredity. Who was he?

Thomas Hunt Morgan joined Columbia University’s faculty in 1904, where his research group bred Drosophila melanogaster to investigate inheritance. By what nickname did the laboratory where this work was conducted become known?

Counted among China’s Four Great Inventions, this fibrous sheet material is made from processed plant fibers. Mills producing it appeared in Baghdad after papermaking methods were reportedly learned from Chinese prisoners. What is the material?

Paper-making mills emerged in this medieval city after techniques were reportedly learned from Chinese prisoners. The city was home to the House of Wisdom, whose sack in 1258 inspired the apocryphal story of the Tigris running black with ink. Which modern-day Iraqi capital was it?

A passing siren sounds higher in pitch as it approaches and lower as it recedes because the spacing and arrival rate of wave cycles change with relative motion. What is the natural name for this change in observed frequency or wavelength?
The Doppler effect is named for this Austrian physicist, who described the phenomenon in 1842 and applied its implications to the changing colors of binary stars. Who was he?

The Doppler effect’s transverse form was examined in a 1938 study of light emitted by fast-moving canal rays, designed to test relativistic time dilation. What name is given to this spectroscopy study?

In some populations of the world's largest land mammal, ivory poaching has caused a heritable condition affecting the development of its ivory-bearing projections to rise markedly in frequency, especially among females. What is this trait called?
Tusklessness in elephants became unusually common among females in this Mozambican protected area after intense ivory poaching during the country's civil war. What is the name of this reserve?
Isolated from the thermophile *Thermus aquaticus*, this heat-stable enzyme can extend DNA primers during PCR despite repeated high-temperature denaturation cycles. What is the name of this enzyme?

Taq DNA polymerase performs primer extension in a DNA-amplification method that cycles through strand denaturation, primer annealing, and synthesis, producing many copies of a target sequence. What is this method called?

In ordinary laboratory usage, this condition means a space has pressure below atmospheric pressure, even though real examples still contain some particles. Its ideal limit contains no matter at all, while quantum physics also uses the same term for a system’s lowest-energy state; what is this condition called?

In quantum physics, the vacuum can still contain fluctuating fields rather than being simply empty space. What name is given to the attractive force between two uncharged conducting plates placed extremely close together because the electromagnetic modes available between them differ from those outside?

This broad zone of small rocky bodies lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, separating the inner terrestrial planets from the outer giant planets. It includes the dwarf planet Ceres and the protoplanet Vesta. What is this region called?

Asteroids that share a planet’s orbit around the Sun and gather near its Lagrange points are called that planet’s Trojans. Which gas giant at the outer edge of the asteroid belt has the largest known population of these objects and is also the Solar System’s largest planet?
General relativity describes these extremely compact regions of spacetime as having an event horizon, beyond which even light cannot escape. What are these objects called?

In discussions of black holes, what is the name for the boundary beyond which no signal, including light, can escape? For a nonrotating, uncharged example, its size is given by the Schwarzschild radius.

Quantum field theory predicts a faint thermal emission associated with black holes that slowly reduces their mass when they are not accreting matter. The emission rate increases as the mass decreases; what is this phenomenon called?

As an early case in the study of black holes, which X-ray source in a binary system became the first widely accepted example, supported by observations of its companion star and intense X-ray emission?

Among supermassive black holes associated with galactic centers, what compact radio source at the center of the Milky Way has an estimated mass of about 4.3 million Suns? Astronomers infer its central mass in part from the rapid orbits of nearby stars.

In a traveling wave, this property measures the distance from one crest to the next, or from one trough to the next. In visible light, it is greater for red light than for blue light. What is this property called?

Wavelength and this quantity are linked by the wave-speed equation: in a vacuum, their product for light equals the speed of light. Measured in hertz, it counts how many wave cycles pass a point each second. What is this quantity?
Following an injury to a vessel, circulating platelets adhere at the damaged site and a protein cascade produces a plug that limits fluid loss. What is this physiological process called?

During blood clotting, this vitamin K–dependent serine protease is activated in the intrinsic pathway and helps activate the protein that starts the common pathway. Its inherited deficiency causes hemophilia B. What is it?

These enzymes transfer phosphate groups, often from ATP, to target molecules and thereby alter their activity. Cyclin-dependent members of this enzyme family help regulate progression through the cell cycle. What are they called?

Kinases help regulate cellular processes, but gametes such as human egg and sperm cells are produced by a distinct type of cell division. This process involves two successive divisions and reduces the chromosome number by half. What is it called?

When particles move randomly, the net result is that they spread from a region of higher concentration into one of lower concentration, even without bulk flow carrying them. What is this transport process, commonly modeled by Fick’s laws?

In diffusion, which constitutive transport law states that particle flux is proportional to the negative spatial concentration gradient, with the minus sign indicating transport down that gradient? It relates flux to spatial concentration variation rather than describing how concentration changes over time.
Diffusion can produce a visible, erratic jitter of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid, caused by uneven impacts from surrounding molecules. What is this phenomenon called?

Which domesticated equid descended from African wild asses has a large head, long mobile ears, an erect mane, and a tufted tail? It has long been used to carry people and goods through semi-arid and upland regions.

Genomic studies indicate that donkey domestication occurred once in Africa around 5,000 BCE, before the animals spread through Africa and Eurasia. Which African hoofed member of the horse family is identified as the donkey’s ancestor?
This widespread predatory bird occurs on every continent except Antarctica and is famous for the tremendous speed it reaches in a hunting dive, known as a stoop. What bird of prey is it?
In Jean Craighead George’s novel *My Side of the Mountain*, Sam Gribley trains a Peregrine Falcon to help him hunt while living in the Catskills. What name does Sam give the bird?

This familiar small mammal has brown-to-gray fur, a lighter underside, and a nearly hairless, ring-scaled tail about as long as its head and body combined. It often nests in sheltered spaces near food in buildings and is widely used in biomedical research; what is its common name?

Robert Burns wrote this poem after a plough turned up a small animal’s nest. Its closing reflection says that the best-laid plans of animals and people often go awry; what is the poem’s title about a Mouse?

Originally designed to accelerate 3D image rendering, this specialized processor handles similar calculations across many pixels at the same time. Its parallel architecture is also useful for workloads such as machine learning; what is this component called?

A graphics processing unit can apply similar calculations to many pixels simultaneously rather than handling each pixel one after another. What computing approach describes working on multiple data elements at once?

Programmers can place explanatory text in source files that the compiler generally ignores. In Python, a single-line example often begins with #, while in Java it often begins with //. What are these annotations called?
In Java, specially formatted Comments can include tags such as @param and @return to describe classes and methods. What is the name of the standard tool that generates API documentation from them?

This passive, two-terminal circuit component is specified by a nominal resistance and a manufacturing tolerance. It can limit current, divide voltage, or set operating conditions for other components.
A resistor’s opposition to current is measured in this SI unit. One unit is equal to one volt per ampere.
This three-terminal variable resistor uses a movable contact called a wiper and can function as an adjustable voltage divider. Its rotary form is commonly used to control audio volume.

Four resistors arranged in a diamond form the arms of this circuit, which can measure an unknown resistance by balancing the ratios of its two branches. A detector connected across the middle registers zero at balance.

Osteichthyes and Chondrichthyes are the bony and cartilaginous groups of these aquatic vertebrates, which typically breathe through gills. Most living species belong to the ray-finned lineage. What are these animals called?
This lobe-finned fish was believed to have been extinct for more than 60 million years until a living specimen was found off South Africa in 1938. What is this relict lineage called?
In an electrical schematic, this is a connection point shared by multiple components. Kirchhoff's current law treats the flows meeting there as balanced. What is this feature called?

At a circuit node, the total rate of electric charge flowing into the connection equals the total rate flowing out. This conservation rule concerns flow at a connection rather than potential changes around a closed loop; what is it called?
Which small feline species was domesticated in the Near East around 7500 BCE, became a companion animal and rodent hunter, and is the only domesticated member of the family Felidae?
The domestic cat is classified in the order Carnivora and is the only domesticated species in its family. What is the name of that family?
The domestic cat is often most active around sunrise and sunset, rather than at midday or in the deepest part of night. What term describes this dawn-and-dusk activity pattern?
The domestic cat can keep its sharp, hooked tips sheathed while walking, then extend them for gripping prey or climbing. What is this feline feature called?

Archaeological and genetic evidence places the early domestication of the domestic cat around 7500 BCE in a broad region of southwestern Asia and nearby areas. What region is identified as the setting for this domestication?

Completed in 1970 in southern Egypt, this massive Nile barrier regulates flooding and generates hydroelectric power. Its construction also led to the relocation of the Abu Simbel temples. What is this dam called?
The Aswan High Dam created this vast reservoir in southern Egypt, which extends into Sudan, where its continuation is known as Lake Nubia. What is the reservoir’s name?

In mechanics, this broad quantity of motion has a linear form equal to mass times velocity and a rotational form equal to moment of inertia times angular velocity. Its total value is conserved in an isolated system.

Unlike Momentum itself, what rotational quantity measures how strongly an applied force tends to change an object's angular motion? For a force applied perpendicular to a lever arm, it equals the force multiplied by the distance from the axis.

What fatty insulating layer surrounds many nerve-cell axons and is interrupted by periodic gaps called nodes of Ranvier? These gaps enable nerve impulses to travel rapidly by jumping between exposed sections.

In the central nervous system, immune-mediated damage to the myelin sheath can leave scar-like plaques in white matter. What disease often follows a relapsing-remitting course and is associated with this damage?

This British molecular biologist helped establish the double-helical structure of DNA and proposed a principle describing the flow of information from nucleic acids to proteins. He also predicted that tRNA can pair flexibly with more than one codon.

Francis Crick proposed that a single tRNA can recognize multiple codons because the interaction at a particular position is less strict than standard complementary base matching. What is this flexible decoding phenomenon called?
In a Robert Burns poem prompted by a tiny parasite on a woman’s bonnet at church, the speaker wishes for the gift “to see ourselves as others see us.” What insect is the subject of the poem?
Robert Burns’s poem about a louse uses Scots phrasing such as “crowlan ferlie,” and Burns was born in Alloway in the nation that joined England in 1707 to create Great Britain. Which nation is this?

This specialized nervous-system cell has a nucleus-bearing cell body, branching structures that receive signals, and an extension that carries electrical impulses away. What is this basic signaling unit?
In communication involving a neuron, what is the junction where an axon terminal releases chemical messengers across a narrow gap to affect a neighboring cell, often at one of its dendrites?
This transparent shaped element bends light as it passes through its surfaces, and can bring rays together or spread them apart. What device is used in cameras, eyeglasses, and magnifiers?
For an optical lens, power is calculated as the reciprocal of focal length when that length is expressed in meters. What unit names this optical power and is equivalent to an inverse meter?

On July 16, 1945, a plutonium implosion device was detonated at the Alamogordo Bombing and Gunnery Range in New Mexico, producing the first nuclear explosion in history. What was this landmark test called?
At the Trinity Test, scientists detonated a plutonium implosion device whose design was later used in the weapon dropped on Nagasaki. What codename did the Los Alamos team give this test device?

In an adult, this flexible bony framework has 24 separate vertebrae arranged as 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, and 5 lumbar bones, with the sacrum and coccyx below. Openings in the vertebrae align to form a canal that protects the spinal cord, while discs cushion movement between neighboring vertebrae. What is this structure?
The spine’s four natural curves help provide strength and flexibility, but this condition involves an abnormal sideways curve, often with rotation of the vertebrae. What is this condition called?
This abundant framework silicate is composed of silicon dioxide and has a hardness of 7 on the Mohs scale. Its familiar varieties include amethyst, citrine, and rock crystal; what mineral is it?
Quartz is assigned a value of 7 on this qualitative scratch-resistance scale, whose reference minerals range from talc at 1 to diamond at 10. What is the scale called?
In quartz, applying mechanical stress can create an electrical potential across the crystal, a property used in oscillators that keep watches and clocks precise. What is this property called?

Discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930, this Kuiper Belt dwarf planet was reclassified from the ninth planet in 2006. It has five known moons and the minor-planet number 134340; what is its natural name?
Pluto was discovered at Lowell Observatory after astronomers searched for a predicted distant planet. Which American astronomer found it in 1930 by comparing photographic plates?
Pluto had never been explored up close until this NASA spacecraft flew past it in July 2015, sending back the first detailed images of its surface. What was the spacecraft called?
James Watson and Francis Crick described DNA as two strands joined by complementary nucleotide pairs and winding around one another. What is the name of this molecular structure?
While investigating the DNA double helix, this chemist used X-ray diffraction to produce Photo 51, an image that provided important evidence of DNA’s helical form. Which scientist produced the image?

It has north and south poles, with opposite poles attracting and like poles repelling, and its field can deflect a nearby compass needle. What object can also attract materials such as iron, cobalt, and nickel?
A freely turning magnetized needle inside this navigation instrument aligns with Earth’s magnetic field, helping travelers determine direction. What device uses a magnet in this way?

In 1909, Robert Millikan and Harvey Fletcher used an atomizer to produce tiny droplets and balance them in an electric field, thereby determining the electron’s elementary charge. What is this procedure commonly called?

To account for viscous drag on slowly moving droplets in the oil-drop experiment, Millikan and Fletcher used a law for the motion of small spheres through a fluid. What law gives the drag force as six pi times the fluid’s viscosity, the sphere’s radius, and its speed?

Which diverse reptile clade flourished on land during the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods, with legs positioned beneath the body? It includes animals such as Triceratops and Tyrannosaurus rex, but not pterosaurs.
Dinosaurs largely disappeared in the mass extinction about 66 million years ago, but one lineage survived and is represented by living animals today. What is that lineage?

This mood-related diagnosis involves at least two weeks of persistent depressed mood or loss of interest, often accompanied by difficulties with work, school, sleep, or other parts of daily life. What diagnosis is described?

Clinicians began using the term “major depressive disorder” in the mid-1970s, and it was adopted into this edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders in 1980. Which edition was it?
Major depressive disorder is often treated with this class of antidepressants; fluoxetine and citalopram are two examples. What is this drug class called?

In this display technology, a thin film of carbon-based electroluminescent compounds is electrically excited, and each pixel produces its own visible output rather than relying on a separate panel illuminator. What is this technology called?

In an organic light-emitting diode display, each pixel generates its own light, unlike an LCD that relies on an illumination source behind the image-forming layer. What is that separate light source called?

Discovered by Christiaan Huygens in 1655, this is Saturn’s largest moon and the first moon ever found orbiting that planet. It is also the only moon known to have a dense atmosphere and stable surface lakes.

Which joint space mission studied Saturn and sent a descent probe through Titan’s atmosphere, where it landed in 2005? It was the first mission to enter orbit around Saturn, and its observations revealed hydrocarbon lakes near Titan’s poles.

On Titan, what is the name of the vast, highly reflective equatorial region whose radar-bright terrain contrasts with surrounding dark dune fields? First identified in Hubble observations, it was later mapped in detail by Cassini.

Which NASA rotorcraft mission is planned to fly across Titan’s surface, using a nuclear-powered octocopter to investigate organic chemistry and habitability? Its target area includes the impact crater Selk, and the vehicle is designed to make multiple flights between sites.

What global industrial sector links tapping latex from Hevea trees and processing it with manufacturing synthetic elastomers and finished goods such as tires, hoses, and seals? Its supply chain spans plantations, chemical plants, and product manufacturers.

In the rubber industry, what process makes natural rubber more durable and elastic by heating it with sulfur? Its development is commonly credited to American inventor Charles Goodyear in the 19th century.
Which aromatic hydrocarbon has a benzene ring bearing one methyl group, the molecular formula C₇H₈, and common uses as a solvent in permanent markers and paint thinners?
Nitrating toluene to add three nitro groups at the 2, 4, and 6 positions produces a well-known high explosive. What three-letter abbreviation is commonly used for this compound?

Astronomers first identified this colorless, chemically unreactive element in the Sun’s spectrum in 1868, decades before it was confirmed on Earth in 1895. It is the lightest noble gas and has atomic number 2; what is it?
In a later stage of stellar evolution, what process fuses three helium-4 nuclei to form carbon-12? This reaction is an important stage after hydrogen burning.
A glacier can pick up a large boulder in one area and deposit it far away, where its rock type may differ from the surrounding landscape. What is this transported and deposited boulder called?

Big Rock near Okotoks, Alberta, is a famous glacial erratic carried south by the Laurentide Ice Sheet. This massive block is made of a durable metamorphic rock that contrasts with the local plains; what rock type is it?
In this astronomical alignment, one celestial body passes into the shadow of another; solar and lunar versions are familiar examples. What is this kind of event called?
During an astronomical eclipse of the Sun, what are the short-lived points of sunlight called when they shine through valleys along the Moon’s uneven edge just before or after totality?

This marine invertebrate phylum includes starfish, sea cucumbers, brittle stars, and crinoids. Its adult members commonly have five-part radial symmetry and a water-powered system of tube feet. What phylum is it?
In echinoderms, this network of fluid-filled canals operates the tube feet, which many species use for movement, gripping surfaces, and feeding. What is this specialized system called?
Which group of calcium-phosphate minerals has a standard Mohs hardness of 5 and includes the mineral family from which the principal inorganic material of human bones is formed?
Apatite is assigned a value of 5 on a relative mineral-scratch scale that places talc at 1 and diamond at 10. What is the name of that scale?

At certain contacts between lithospheric plates, the plates move toward one another. Compression at these contacts can cause one plate to descend beneath another or build mountains where continents collide. What type of plate margin is this?
At a convergent boundary, denser oceanic lithosphere can descend beneath another plate and sink into the mantle. What is this process called?

Which evolutionary process gives individuals at both ends of a trait range greater reproductive success while organisms near the middle leave fewer offspring? Rather than shifting a population toward one extreme, this pattern can maintain two contrasting forms.
A classic finch example of disruptive selection describes birds with small or large beaks and few medium-sized individuals. On which Galápagos island is this population found?

In chemistry, the value written as Z counts the positively charged particles in an element’s nucleus. This whole-number property determines the element’s identity, even if its neutron count varies. What is this property called?

In the definition of atomic number, which positively charged subatomic particles are counted in the nucleus? They are found alongside neutrons, and changing their number changes the atom’s elemental identity.

It is the element with atomic number 1 and symbol H, and its diatomic gas is colorless, odorless, and highly combustible under standard conditions. What is this lightest and most abundant element in the universe?

Hydrogen was identified as a distinct gas in 18th-century experiments by this English chemist, who referred to it as “inflammable air.” He also used a torsion-balance experiment to determine Earth’s density. Who was he?

When electrons in hydrogen atoms fall from higher energy levels to the second level, they produce a series of spectral lines that includes several prominent visible lines. Named for the physicist who derived an empirical formula for its wavelengths, what is this series called?

In stars around the Sun’s size, hydrogen is converted into helium mainly through a sequence of nuclear reactions that emit positrons and neutrinos. What is this fusion process, which contrasts with the CNO cycle that dominates in hotter, more massive stars?
The most common isotope of hydrogen contains one proton and no neutrons, unlike deuterium and tritium, which contain one and two neutrons respectively. What is the established name of this isotope?

In SI electromagnetism, what constant denoted ε₀ relates electric displacement to electric field in empty space? It also appears alongside a factor of 4π in the denominator of the electrostatic force coefficient.

Vacuum permittivity appears in the denominator of the SI proportionality constant written as 1/(4π ε₀). What is the name of this constant, which scales the inverse-square force between two point charges?
Which halogen is a reddish-brown liquid at room temperature and is commonly used in laboratory tests for carbon–carbon unsaturation?
In the laboratory test that uses Bromine, the reddish-brown color fades when a sample contains carbon–carbon double bonds. What class of hydrocarbons does this result indicate?

Born in Stockholm in 1833, this Swedish chemist and engineer developed an explosive by stabilizing nitroglycerin and later left his fortune to fund annual awards for achievements in several fields. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel patented this explosive in 1867 after stabilizing nitroglycerin with an absorbent material, making it more practical to handle and use. What was this invention?
What is the general term for inflammation of the body’s largest internal organ, including viral forms conventionally designated A, B, and C?
In hepatitis, inflammation affects which organ that produces bile and helps process nutrients?

At this junction between two neurons, an arriving nerve signal causes one cell to release neurotransmitters, which diffuse across a gap and bind to receptors on the next cell. What type of junction transmits signals in this way, unlike a direct electrical connection?
Within a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters cross a narrow extracellular space between the presynaptic terminal and the postsynaptic membrane. What is this gap called?

This invisible band of the electromagnetic spectrum begins at wavelengths just longer than visible red light and ends before the microwave region. Nearly all energy emitted by objects near room temperature falls within it. What is this band called?

Infrared radiation was identified in 1800 when an astronomer used a prism to spread sunlight and found that a thermometer warmed beyond the red end of the visible spectrum. Which scientist made this discovery?

In this analytical method, infrared radiation is absorbed or transmitted by a sample, and the resulting pattern helps identify molecules through their rotational-vibrational motions. What is the method called?

Building inspectors use infrared radiation to find heat escaping through insulation, while firefighters and electricians use similar equipment to locate hot spots or overheating components. What camera-based technique produces images that map temperature differences?

Infrared radiation lets this NASA observatory peer through cosmic dust and detect highly red-shifted early galaxies. Its first deep-field image, featuring the cluster SMACS 0723, was released in 2022; what observatory, named for a former NASA administrator, produced it?
This international particle-physics research organization is headquartered near Geneva and operates the Large Hadron Collider. What is its commonly used name?
In 2012, experiments at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider announced the discovery of a particle associated with the field that gives the W and Z particles mass. What particle was it?

What syndrome is the most advanced stage of HIV infection, and in the United States can be diagnosed when a person’s CD4 count falls below 200 cells per cubic millimeter or when certain defining illnesses occur? It reflects severe immune damage rather than infection by a separate virus.
For people with AIDS, what treatment uses medicines to control HIV, support immune recovery, and slow or prevent disease progression, even though it does not cure the infection?

This lentivirus targets CD4 T cells and uses reverse transcriptase to copy its RNA into DNA before integrating that DNA into a host cell’s genome. Without treatment, its progressive damage to the immune system can leave a person vulnerable to serious infections.

During infection with human immunodeficiency virus, what is the name of the late stage marked by severe immune-system damage and increased vulnerability to opportunistic infections and some cancers? It is an advanced stage of the infection, not a separate virus.

This highly reactive allotrope of the element with atomic number 15 is made of discrete molecules whose four atoms occupy the corners of a tetrahedron. Unlike the element’s more stable polymeric form, it can glow faintly in air and may ignite spontaneously; what is this allotrope?
White phosphorus is made of discrete molecules rather than a continuous network, and each molecule contains four phosphorus atoms. What molecular formula denotes one such molecule?

These materials are not a single chemical but a broad family of synthetic, moldable substances made primarily from polymers and used in products such as bags, bottles, and straws. What is this material class called?
In plastic manufacturing, some materials soften when heated and can be reshaped, while another class sets into a permanent form and does not remelt reversibly. What is the name for that latter class?
What ecological field examines how island area and isolation affect species diversity and evolutionary change? It also considers patterns such as adaptive radiation and shifts in body size.

Within Island Biogeography, what evolutionary pattern—also called the island rule—describes large-bodied mammals tending to become smaller and small-bodied mammals tending to become larger on islands?

This flexible organ is the body's largest by surface area and forms its outer covering. It consists chiefly of two layers that help limit water loss, block pathogens, sense touch, and regulate temperature. What organ is it?
In human skin, melanocytes in the basal layer produce this pigment and transfer it to neighboring cells. It absorbs ultraviolet radiation and is a major determinant of visible skin color.
Human skin's outer barrier is reinforced by a tough structural protein also abundant in hair and nails. In the epidermis, cells synthesize this protein as they mature toward the surface.
In human skin, this outermost of the two principal layers is made of stratified squamous epithelium and lacks blood vessels. Nutrients reach it by diffusion from deeper tissue. Name this layer.

Human skin cools the body when this widely distributed structure releases a watery secretion directly onto the surface through a duct. It is abundant on the palms and soles and opens directly onto the skin surface, unlike the apocrine type.

This stalk-like part of the brain connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and consists of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. It also helps regulate vital functions such as breathing and heart rate. What is it?
The brainstem includes this most inferior region, which lies between the pons and spinal cord. It contains centers that help regulate breathing and heart rate. What is this region?

A major descending motor pathway passes through the brainstem and carries signals from the cerebral cortex toward the spinal cord. Its fibers also form prominent bundles called the medullary pyramids. What is this pathway?

For an ideal spring within its elastic limit, the restoring force increases in proportion to how far the spring is displaced from equilibrium, and the proportionality constant measures its stiffness. What law describes this relationship?

When a mass attached to a spring obeying Hooke's law moves around its equilibrium position, its acceleration is proportional to its displacement and directed back toward equilibrium. What type of oscillation does it perform?
What domesticated canid, known scientifically as Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris, is a descendant of wolves and has long been bred for companionship and work?
A Russian physiologist studied the domestic dog by pairing food with sounds such as a bell and measuring salivation. What was his name?
Compared with humans, the domestic dog has a particularly well-developed sense for detecting scents. What is this sensory ability called?
In an unfamiliar environment, a domestic dog may lift a leg beside objects, leaving a chemical signal that other dogs can detect. What is this territorial communication behavior called?

Genetic studies suggest that the domestic dog’s relationship with humans began more than 25,000 years ago, before agriculture. In which geological epoch did hunter-gatherers begin selectively breeding dogs?
These ubiquitous, usually single-celled prokaryotes lack a nucleus and include disease-causing organisms such as Salmonella and Escherichia coli. What group of organisms is being described?
In the Hershey–Chase experiment, researchers used viruses that infect bacteria to test whether DNA or protein carries hereditary information. What are these viruses called?
In bacteria, this rigid structure lies outside the plasma membrane and contains peptidoglycan made of alternating sugar residues. Lysozyme can break down this structure. What is it called?

What laboratory instrument quantifies heat transferred during a physical or chemical process? Specialized forms can track thermal transitions in polymers or determine the heat released by combustion in a sealed vessel.

In polymer analysis, which kind of calorimeter measures differences in heat flow between a sample and a reference as temperature changes, revealing transitions such as the glass transition? It commonly uses a programmed heating or cooling scan.
Which French physicist who investigated the magnetic effects of electric currents formulated a law describing the force between current-carrying wires and helped establish electrodynamics?
André-Marie Ampère introduced the name for a long, helical coil of wire whose magnetic field is produced when electric current flows through its turns. What is this device called?
This five-level classification ranks tropical cyclones by maximum sustained speed and associated damage potential. Its highest tier begins at 157 mph (252 km/h); what is the system called?

On the Saffir–Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, which numbered rating applies to a hurricane with maximum sustained winds of at least 157 mph (252 km/h)? This top tier is associated with catastrophic damage.
This contagious childhood disease typically causes an itchy rash that develops into small, fluid-filled blisters. What is its common name?
The pathogen that causes chickenpox can lie dormant in sensory nerve cells and later reactivate as shingles. What is its name?

This nineteenth-century galvanic arrangement produced a steady current using a zinc electrode in zinc sulfate solution and a copper electrode in copper sulfate solution. What is this arrangement called?

In a Daniell cell, the zinc and copper half-cells must remain electrically connected while their solutions are kept from freely mixing. What ion-conducting component allows ions to move between the compartments and maintain electrical neutrality?

Located behind the stomach, this abdominal organ sends digestive enzymes through ducts toward the small intestine. Its endocrine cells also release hormones that help regulate blood sugar; what organ is it?

In the pancreas, small clusters of endocrine cells lie among tissue that produces digestive enzymes. Their alpha and beta cells release glucagon and insulin, respectively; what is the established anatomical name for these clusters?

Planetary scientists use this term for liquid water concealed beneath the icy crust of a moon or another celestial body. Europa and Enceladus are prominent examples, and environments of this kind are studied as possible habitats for life. What is this feature called?

This moon is thought to contain a subsurface ocean and is the largest natural satellite in the Solar System. It also has its own intrinsic magnetic field, a rare feature among moons. Which moon is it?

This bacterial disease most often affects the lungs and spreads through airborne particles released by infectious people when they cough, speak, or sing—not by touching contaminated surfaces. Its infection can remain inactive without symptoms or the ability to spread, and the illness was historically known as “consumption.” What disease is it?
Tuberculosis was historically called this name, associated with the severe wasting and weight loss that often occurred in people with the disease. What was this former name?
What class of materials can carry electrical current with zero resistance below a characteristic critical temperature, and can also expel magnetic fields?

A 2020 report described a room-temperature member of the superconductors family made from carbon, sulfur, and hydrogen under extreme pressure. In the apparatus, two crystals of what exceptionally hard material squeeze the sample?

This physical quantity is calculated by dividing the amount of matter in a sample by the volume it occupies, and it is an intensive property: adding more of the same substance does not change its value. Commonly expressed in kilograms per cubic meter and represented by ρ, what is this quantity?
