Mass density is commonly represented by a lowercase Greek letter in equations for fluids and materials. The same symbol appears in formulas involving hydrostatic pressure and buoyancy; what is the letter?
Mass density can be compared with that of a reference substance by taking a ratio. When the reference is usually water, this dimensionless comparison is called what?

Mass density varies among the elements, and one metallic element is commonly identified as the densest known at standard temperature and pressure. A platinum-group metal with atomic number 76, what is it?

A star reaches this late evolutionary stage after exhausting the hydrogen in its core. Its outer layers expand and cool, giving it a large radius and a reddish appearance. What is this stellar stage called?

In a low-mass star, electron-degeneracy pressure prevents the contracting core from expanding as it heats while the star is a red giant. This can cause fusion in the core to ignite in a sudden runaway; what is this event called?

This colorless, odorless noble gas has atomic number 10 and occurs only in trace amounts in Earth’s atmosphere. When used in a discharge tube, it produces the distinctive red-orange glow associated with illuminated signs. What element is it?
Which Scottish chemist worked with Morris Travers in 1898 to isolate Neon from liquefied air, identifying the new element through its characteristic spectral lines?

Which membrane model describes the cell boundary as a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins that can move laterally, rather than as a rigid, fixed structure? Proposed in 1972, it became a standard framework for explaining membrane organization.
In the 1972 Science paper introducing the Fluid Mosaic Model, which coauthor partnered with S. Jonathan Singer to describe proteins embedded in a lipid bilayer?

In humans, these paired organs sit on either side of the heart, and the right one has three lobes while the left has two. Tiny air sacs within them exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide with the blood. What are these organs?
After air passes through the trachea, it enters a pair of large airways that carry it into the lungs and divide into smaller bronchioles. What are these airways called?
Located beneath the lungs, this dome-shaped muscle contracts and flattens to increase chest volume and draw air in. What is this muscle called?

While researching ergot alkaloids at a Swiss pharmaceutical company, this potent psychedelic was first synthesized by Albert Hofmann in 1938. Its psychoactive effects became known after Hofmann revisited it in 1943, and the CIA later studied it under Project MKULTRA. What is this substance?
After synthesizing lysergic acid diethylamide at Sandoz, which Swiss chemist accidentally absorbed a small amount in 1943 and later recorded a bicycle ride home after deliberately taking it?
Which crystallographic system has unit cells with three equal-length axes that meet at right angles, and includes primitive, body-centered, and face-centered Bravais lattices?
Within the Cubic crystal system, which arrangement places points at the cube’s corners and at the centers of its six square sides, with each point having 12 nearest neighbors?
A swing or plucked string gradually loses amplitude as friction or drag removes mechanical energy, often converting some of it to heat. What is this general process called?
In a car’s suspension, which component provides controlled damping by dissipating energy from spring-driven motion and helping the vehicle stop bouncing after a bump?
Which layered neural tissue lines the inside of the back of the eyeball, where rods and cones detect light and ganglion-cell axons converge to form the optic nerve?
Within the retina, what tiny central depression in the macula has the highest cone density and provides the sharpest visual acuity?

This animal phylum includes clams, snails, and octopuses. Its members commonly have a mantle, a visceral mass, and a muscular foot, although some have reduced or no external shell. What is this phylum called?
In Mollusca, many gastropods feed using a flexible ribbon lined with rows of tiny teeth to scrape food from surfaces. This rasping organ is generally absent in bivalves; what is it called?

In a molecule, what arrangement exists when its positive and negative charge centers are separated, producing a measurable moment? It can be permanent in a polar molecule or arise temporarily from fluctuations in its electron cloud.

A dipole can form momentarily when an electron cloud fluctuates, creating an uneven charge distribution that induces a similar separation in a neighboring particle. What intermolecular attraction results from these temporary, induced charge separations and is especially important among nonpolar substances?
What state do certain materials enter below a critical temperature, exhibiting zero electrical resistance and expelling magnetic fields from their interiors?

In superconductivity, what phenomenon occurs when a material entering its superconducting state expels magnetic flux from its interior? This magnetic response distinguishes superconductors from ideal conductors that merely have zero resistance.
What hypothetical cosmological idea holds that reality consists of multiple universes, which may have different histories, physical laws, or conditions?
Which 2022 film makes the multiverse central to its story, follows Evelyn (played by Michelle Yeoh) across alternate realities, and features Jobu Tupaki’s black-bagel motif?

For a reaction with fixed reactants and products, this principle says the overall enthalpy change is the same whether the reaction occurs in one step or through a sequence of intermediate reactions. It allows measured reaction steps to be combined to determine the enthalpy change of a target reaction.

In Hess's Law calculations, the value associated with a reaction step changes sign when the equation is reversed and scales with its coefficients when the equation is multiplied. What thermodynamic state function, commonly represented by H, is summed across the steps?

What named relationship describes how gravitational or electrostatic force between two point sources falls to one quarter when their separation is doubled? It is the characteristic distance dependence in Newtonian gravitation and the force between stationary point charges.

Which electrostatic law is a classic example of the inverse-square law, describing the force between point charges as proportional to the product of their charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation? Its proportionality constant in vacuum is 1/(4πε₀).

This fundamental interaction attracts masses across unlimited distances, though its strength weakens as they move farther apart. Near a planet, it gives objects weight and helps keep moons and satellites in orbit. What is its natural name?
In 1687, this English scientist published *Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica*, presenting a universal law of gravity as well as three laws of motion. Who was he?
In 1915, this physicist presented a theory that describes gravity through the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Whose theory transformed the modern understanding of gravity?

General relativity predicts that violent events involving massive objects can send ripples through spacetime. LIGO announced the first direct detection of these gravity-related signals in 2016; what are they called?
In discussions of gravity and stellar collapse, what name is given to the roughly 1.4-solar-mass maximum for a stable white dwarf, beyond which electron degeneracy pressure cannot support it?

A puddle can disappear on a cool day even though it never reaches its boiling point, as molecules escape from the liquid’s surface. This process absorbs energy and can cool nearby skin, as it does when sweat dries. What is this phase change from liquid to gas called?

At a fixed pressure, liquid water at its boiling point can keep changing into gas as energy is transferred into it, without its temperature rising during the phase change. In evaporation, what is the name for the energy required per unit mass to make this liquid-to-vapor transition?

When deriving rate laws for multistep reactions, chemists may focus on a reactive intermediate after the initial transient has passed. If its formation and removal are treated as balanced, what kinetic assumption lets its level be treated as nearly unchanged?

In the Steady-State Approximation, an intermediate’s value of a particular quantity is treated as nearly constant because its formation and consumption balance. Often expressed in molarity, what is this quantity?
This colorless, toxic binary gas consists of sulfur bonded to two atoms of the lightest element, and its characteristic odor is often compared with rotten eggs. What is its common name?
In hydrogen sulfide, sulfur is surrounded by two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, and the H–S–H angle is about 92°. Which familiar VSEPR shape do the three atoms adopt?
What band of electromagnetic radiation is detectable by human vision and includes emissions from LEDs and fluorescent lamps?
In the retina, which photoreceptor cells respond to Visible Light under brighter conditions and support color vision, in contrast to rods, which are more useful in dim light?

In this medical procedure, clinicians match a donor’s and recipient’s ABO and Rh classifications to reduce the risk of a dangerous immune reaction. Donated red cells, plasma, or platelets are delivered into a patient’s vein. What is this procedure?

During a blood transfusion, clinicians consider whether a particular antigen is present on a patient’s red blood cells. The plus or minus designation in a blood type indicates whether this inherited antigen is present; it was named for rhesus macaques in which it was first studied. What is it?
Which class of beta-lactam antibiotics blocks bacterial enzymes needed to build peptidoglycan cell walls? Its early members were derived from compounds produced by Penicillium molds.

Penicillins trace their origins to a 1928 observation in which a mold contaminating a laboratory plate stopped nearby staphylococcal colonies from growing. Which Scottish bacteriologist made that observation?
What machine uses wind-driven sails or blades to turn a mechanism that can grind grain or pump water, with some modern versions also producing electricity?

In Miguel de Cervantes’s Spanish novel, an aging man absorbed in tales of chivalry attacks a windmill he imagines is a giant. He also undertakes quests in the name of Dulcinea del Toboso; what is the novel?

Which familiar name is used for the North American marmot with the scientific name *Marmota monax*, a burrowing hibernator also known as a groundhog and featured in a classic tongue twister about chucking wood?
The woodchuck is a marmot native to eastern North America, commonly found in fields and along woodland edges. What two-word Latin binomial identifies this species?

When a dilute gas of bosonic particles is cooled close to absolute zero, a large fraction of its particles occupy the same lowest-energy quantum state and behave collectively. What state of matter is this?
The first dilute-gas Bose-Einstein condensate was created in 1995 at JILA by Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman using a bosonic isotope with mass number 87. What isotope was it?

These plant hormones are transported directionally by PIN proteins, and their uneven distribution contributes to apical dominance, in which the main shoot suppresses lateral buds. They also regulate stem elongation, root growth, and phototropism; what are they called?

Among auxins, which naturally occurring compound is the principal endogenous growth regulator in most plants? It is biosynthesized from the amino acid tryptophan and accumulates asymmetrically as shoots bend toward light.
Published in 1632, this work compares the Ptolemaic geocentric cosmos with the Copernican heliocentric model across four days of discussion. What is the title of Galileo’s work?
answer: Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems

question: In Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems, which interlocutor advances the Copernican case in debates with the Aristotelian-minded Simplicio? Galileo gives this character the role of a learned defender of the heliocentric model.
Which geologic period opened the Mesozoic Era after the end-Permian mass extinction, lasted approximately 252 to 201 million years ago, and came immediately before the Jurassic?

During the Triassic Period, a several-million-year climate interval brought unusually wet conditions across parts of Pangaea. Researchers have linked it to intense volcanism in the Wrangellia terrane and major shifts in terrestrial ecosystems; what is this interval called?

In Lewis structures, this type of chemical interaction is represented by one or more electron pairs shared between atoms, and it commonly occurs between nonmetals. Its single, double, and triple forms differ in how many pairs are shared. What is it called?
A covalent bond can link two cysteine residues in a protein when their sulfur atoms form a cross-link during oxidation. What is this specific linkage called?

This high explosive was developed in the 19th century by making nitroglycerin safer and more practical to handle. It became a powerful alternative to gunpowder and was used extensively in blasting. What is it?
The development of dynamite is associated with this Swedish inventor and industrialist, who patented the explosive in 1867 and established the prizes that bear his name. Who was he?

What class of organic compounds is defined by a hydroxyl group bonded to a saturated carbon? Its members include methanol and ethanol, and the polar group makes them more water-attracting than many hydrocarbons.
In alcohols, which oxygen–hydrogen unit is attached to a saturated carbon and contributes to their affinity for water? It consists of an oxygen atom bonded to a hydrogen atom.

Among alcohols, which two-carbon compound is produced by fermentation and is the intoxicating ingredient in alcoholic beverages? When distilled with water, it forms an azeotrope that limits its concentration to about 96%.

Which complex sterol is an alcohol found in animal cell membranes and serves as a precursor to steroid hormones? It has a single hydroxyl group despite its much larger structure than simple examples such as methanol.
This hardware presents generated text, images, and video on a screen for a user to view. Unlike a printer, it provides visual output without putting that output on paper. What is this device?
Many flat-panel computer monitors use a display technology in which liquid crystals control how much light from a backlight passes through each pixel. What is this technology commonly called?
In a chemical equation, this starting substance appears before the arrow and is consumed or transformed as products form. What is the name for such a substance?

When the quantities of the reactants are compared with the mole ratios in a balanced chemical equation, one may be used up before the others, determining the maximum amount of product that can form. What is this substance called?

This eukaryotic organelle consists of stacks of flattened membrane sacs and receives many newly made proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum. It modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for delivery to other parts of the cell or for release outside it. What is this organelle?

In the secretory pathway, vesicles budding from the endoplasmic reticulum on their way to the Golgi apparatus use this coat complex. It differs from COPI, which commonly helps move cargo in the reverse direction from the Golgi toward the ER. What is this coat complex?
The family Ursidae has eight living species found across North America, South America, and Eurasia. Its members include polar and giant pandas; what is the common name for this group?
Bears belong to a major branch of the order Carnivora that is commonly called the dog-like carnivorans. What is the scientific name of this group?
Among Bears, one species lives in the mountain forests of central China and gets most of its food from bamboo, despite belonging to the order Carnivora. What is this species?

These short projections extend from eukaryotic cell surfaces and are built from microtubules. In human airways, their coordinated beating sweeps mucus and trapped particles toward the throat. What are these hairlike structures called?
Motile cilia commonly have nine outer microtubule doublets surrounding a central pair, unlike the pattern typical of primary cilia. What is the conventional shorthand for this motile-cilia pattern?
In plants and photosynthetic algae, this double-membraned organelle contains chlorophyll-bearing internal sacs and is the site of photosynthesis. What is this organelle?
Within a chloroplast, what is the fluid-filled compartment surrounding the thylakoid stacks, where carbon dioxide is used to build sugars?

These downslope movements can carry rock, soil, debris, or earth, and include both sudden rockfalls and fast-moving debris flows. Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and changes in water pressure within a slope can trigger them. What general term describes these events?

Among landslides, what term describes a fast-moving volcanic mixture of water, ash, and rock fragments that rushes down valleys? Such flows can occur after an eruption or when rain remobilizes volcanic deposits.

Located deep in the brain, this paired structure serves as a major relay station for nearly all sensory input en route to the cerebral cortex and also participates in motor and cognitive functions. What is it?

The thalamus relays most sensory signals toward the cerebral cortex, but one modality initially follows a notable route that bypasses this relay and reaches the olfactory bulb and piriform cortex. Which modality is the exception?

This standard markup language uses elements written with angle-bracket tags to organize headings, paragraphs, links, and other content. Browsers interpret those tags to construct web pages rather than displaying them as ordinary text. What is the language called?
While working at CERN, this British computer scientist developed HTML as part of his work on the World Wide Web and created the first web browser and server. Who was he?
HTML pages can be exposed to scripts through a tree of nodes representing elements, attributes, and text. What programming interface names this structured representation of a webpage?

This highly mineralized tissue forms the outer covering of a tooth crown and is described as the hardest substance in the human body. Its principal mineral is calcium hydroxyapatite, and acids produced by oral bacteria can dissolve it. What tissue is described?
Dental enamel can lose minerals after acid exposure, but a fluid secreted by salivary glands helps neutralize acids and supplies minerals that support repair. What fluid is this?

In classical mechanics, invariance of a system’s action under a differentiable continuous transformation guarantees a corresponding conserved quantity. Time-translation, spatial-translation, and rotational invariance yield conservation of energy, linear momentum, and angular momentum, respectively; what theorem states this connection?

A 1918 paper titled *Invariante Variationsprobleme* established the result now known as Noether’s theorem. Which German mathematician, also renowned for influential work in abstract algebra, wrote it?

In population biology, what measure compares how much an organism or genotype contributes to future generations through reproduction? It is relative to others in the population, and survival counts only insofar as it helps produce offspring.
When heritable traits associated with higher biological fitness lead their bearers to contribute more offspring, what evolutionary mechanism can shift those traits’ frequency across generations?

What scientific approach uses nonhuman species, such as rats and monkeys, as experimental subjects to investigate biological processes, behavior, and aspects of human motivation? It refers to a broad practice, not to any one species or experiment.

Which humanistic psychologist argued that studies of nonhuman animals could not fully account for human motivation and presented a theory later widely known as the hierarchy of needs? Animal models in research were among the approaches he criticized in his work on motivation.

A late-1950s study at General Atomics envisioned a spacecraft propelled by repeated blasts against a broad pusher plate, with shock absorbers smoothing each impulse. What was the name of this proposed propulsion concept?

In Project Orion, the spacecraft would eject small explosive devices behind its pusher plate, transferring the force of each detonation to the vehicle. What kind of devices would provide these repeated bursts of thrust?

What is the water-treatment process that removes dissolved salts from seawater or brackish water to produce potable or otherwise usable freshwater? It can be performed using membrane systems, electrodialysis, or solar stills.

In desalination, which membrane-based method uses pressure to push saline water against a semipermeable barrier, allowing water to pass while retaining most dissolved salts? A plant using this method supplies Key West.
What name is given to composite subatomic particles built from two or more quarks? This family includes both mesons and baryons.
Within hadrons, what class includes the proton and neutron and is made of three valence quarks? This distinguishes it from mesons, which contain a quark and an antiquark.

In ecology, this principle states that two species cannot coexist indefinitely in the same niche under identical limiting conditions. One will eventually displace the other, unless the species differentiate their niches. What is this principle called?

The competitive exclusion principle is associated with this ecologist, whose experiments with Paramecium showed that competing species could not persist together under the same conditions. Who was he?

This electronic system sends radio or microwave signals and detects echoes reflected from objects to determine their location and distance. It is used to track aircraft, monitor storms, and enforce speed limits; what is it called?

Radar systems can detect motion by comparing the frequency of a transmitted wave with the frequency of its returning echo. What named physical effect explains the change in observed frequency when the source and target move relative to each other?

This is the largest internal organ in the human body, located mainly in the upper-right abdomen beneath the diaphragm. It produces a digestive fluid that helps break down dietary fats and is divided mostly into right and left lobes. What organ is it?
Most of the liver’s specialized metabolic work is performed by its abundant parenchymal cells, which process nutrients, detoxify substances, and produce bile. What are these cells called?
The liver produces this fluid, whose salts emulsify dietary fats in the small intestine. The gallbladder stores and concentrates it before releasing it into the duodenum. What is the fluid?
These resident macrophages occupy the liver’s sinusoids and engulf pathogens and worn-out red blood cells. What are these liver-resident macrophages called?

This vessel brings nutrient-rich blood from the digestive organs and spleen to the liver for processing. It is distinct from the artery that supplies the organ with oxygen-rich blood. What is this vessel?

This chromosomal condition is classically associated with a typically male individual carrying one X chromosome beyond the usual XY complement. Its commonly cited karyotype has 47 chromosomes. What is the condition called?
In Klinefelter syndrome, the common karyotype has 47 chromosomes, including two X chromosomes and one Y chromosome. What is the standard shorthand for this karyotype?
Unlike fermions, these particles have integer spin, including zero, and identical members of the family can occupy the same quantum state. What is this particle family called?

Bosons can share a quantum state. In 1995, researchers at JILA used laser and evaporative cooling to make a dilute gas of rubidium atoms enter this macroscopic quantum phase. What phase did they create?

In 1887, this landmark optical test used an interferometer with perpendicular light paths to search for Earth’s motion through a proposed medium for light. Its failure to find the expected directional difference became an important challenge to aether theories and a precursor to modern relativity. What was this investigation called?

The Michelson–Morley experiment was designed to detect Earth’s motion through a hypothetical medium thought to carry light waves. What was this proposed medium, whose existence the experiment’s null result called into question?

The Michelson–Morley experiment was conducted in 1887 at a site in Cleveland, Ohio, where the researchers compared light traveling along perpendicular arms of an interferometer. What present-day institution occupies the historical site?
This American biochemist developed a method for amplifying DNA that became a cornerstone of molecular biology. He received the 1993 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for this work. Who was he?
Kary Banks Mullis conceived a technique that repeatedly separates DNA strands, allows primers to bind, and extends them to amplify a selected DNA sequence. What is this technique called?

This carbon-fixing pathway takes place in the chloroplast stroma and proceeds through carbon fixation, reduction, and regeneration of a five-carbon acceptor molecule. Using ATP and NADPH, it produces G3P, some of which can leave the pathway to contribute to carbohydrate synthesis. What is this pathway?
In the Calvin cycle, this enzyme attaches carbon dioxide to RuBP, forming an unstable intermediate that splits into two molecules of 3-PGA. What is the enzyme?

This autonomous nonlinear electronic oscillator uses a piecewise-linear negative-resistance element and is known for producing a double-scroll attractor. It is a standard physical demonstration of deterministic chaos; what is it called?

In the Chua circuit, a nonlinear resistor with a piecewise-linear current-voltage curve supplies the negative-resistance region that helps produce chaotic dynamics. What is this element conventionally called?
Unlike gymnosperms, this major group of land plants encloses its seeds within ovaries that mature into fruits. Orchids and daisies are familiar examples of which plant group?

In angiosperms, pollen delivers two sperm cells: one fertilizes the egg, while the other fuses with the central cell to form nutritive tissue for the developing seed. What is this reproductive process called?
What term names the flattened disks of ice, dust, and rocky fragments that orbit some planets? Saturn’s conspicuous system is the best-known example.
Planetary rings are especially extensive around this sixth planet from the Sun. Its bright A and B rings are separated by the Cassini Division.

This analytical field examines how matter absorbs, emits, or scatters electromagnetic radiation and uses the resulting spectra to identify substances or infer their structure. What is this field called?
Within spectroscopy, which technique identifies molecular vibrations by measuring energy shifts in laser light scattered inelastically by a sample?

A stream of particles was directed at an ultrathin metal foil to test the plum-pudding model of the atom. Most passed through, but a few were deflected through large angles, suggesting that positive charge and most of the atom’s mass were concentrated in a tiny center. By what name is this investigation known, honoring the physicist who interpreted the results?
In the Rutherford Scattering Experiment, the incoming projectiles were helium-4 nuclei, each containing two protons and two neutrons and carrying a +2 charge. What are these projectiles called?
Produced by the kidneys as they remove dissolved wastes from the blood, this liquid contains urea and is held in the bladder before elimination. What is this bodily waste product called?
Urine is held before elimination in a hollow, muscular organ in the pelvis, whose wall contracts to expel the fluid through the urethra. What is this organ?
What recurring natural state is marked by reduced consciousness and diminished responsiveness, yet supports restoration, memory processing, and health? Its stages include REM and non-REM forms.
Sleep timing is influenced by a hormone secreted by the pineal gland, particularly in response to darkness. This hormone is also taken as a supplement to help people fall asleep; what is it?

Citalopram and fluoxetine are examples of a medication class commonly prescribed for depression and anxiety. These drugs prolong the effects of a chemical messenger by preventing nerve cells from taking it back up; what is the natural name of this class?

Among Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, this medication is notable for an unusually long elimination half-life and an active metabolite that can remain in the body for weeks. It was the first drug in its class approved in the United States in 1987; what is it?

One relation connects electric-field divergence to charge density, while another states that magnetic-field divergence is zero. The other two describe electromagnetic induction and the magnetic effects of currents and changing electric fields; what is the natural name for this set of four relations?
In Maxwell's equations, what term in Ampère's law accounts for a changing electric field contributing to the magnetic field even when no charged particles pass through the region?

What analytical separation family takes its name from Greek roots meaning “color writing” and separates mixture components because they partition differently between a moving fluid and a fixed material, causing different retention times?
In chromatography, what is the name for the flowing gas or liquid that transports the sample through the system, as opposed to the fixed material that retains compounds to differing degrees?
In chromatography, what is the name of the fixed medium—often packed into a column or coated onto a plate—that analytes interact with differently, producing distinct retention?

In paper or thin-layer chromatography, what dimensionless quantity is calculated by dividing the distance traveled by a sample spot by the distance traveled by the solvent front? It is used to compare how far a compound moves under specified conditions.

This domesticated member of the family Equidae is a one-toed, hoofed mammal, and modern domestic populations trace much of their ancestry to the western Eurasian steppes. Humans have long used it for riding, agriculture, transportation, and racing. What animal is it?
In horse terminology, an adult female is given this name, while an adult male used for breeding is called a stallion. A horse’s pregnancy lasts roughly 11 months. What is the adult female called?
A horse in its first year of life is called this, regardless of sex; after its first birthday, it is generally called a yearling. What is this young horse called?
This chestnut racehorse won the 1973 U.S. Triple Crown and set a Belmont Stakes record by winning that race by 31 lengths. What was this famous horse’s name?
This graphical operating-system family includes releases called Vista and XP and is widely used on personal computers. What is the family called?
Within Microsoft Windows, which file system was introduced with Windows NT 3.1 and uses a Master File Table to record information about files and directories?
Produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, this yellowish-green digestive fluid is released into the small intestine, where it helps disperse dietary fats. What is this fluid called?

Bile contains a pigment formed during the breakdown of heme from aging red blood cells. When this pigment builds up in the body, it can cause the yellowing of skin and eyes known as jaundice. What is the pigment?

In chemical kinetics, the rate of this process is proportional to the concentration of one chemical species, and that concentration declines exponentially over time. Its characteristic decay interval remains unchanged when the initial concentration changes. What kinetic order is described?
For a First-Order Reaction, a characteristic time independent of initial concentration is given by ln 2 divided by the rate constant. What is this characteristic time called?

In a galvanic cell, what device containing an electrolyte connects the two half-cells by allowing ions to migrate and maintain electrical neutrality as electrons flow through the external circuit? It is often made as a U-shaped tube filled with electrolyte.
In a Salt Bridge, what gel-forming polysaccharide derived from red algae is commonly used to keep the electrolyte in place? It forms a stable gel in aqueous solution.
What browser programming interface represents a web page as a hierarchy of entries corresponding to its elements, so scripts can inspect and modify the page’s content?
In the Document Object Model, what data structure organizes nodes through parent-child relationships, with one root and potentially many branches? Its terminal nodes are called leaves.
This New World scavenger can locate carrion by detecting a decomposition odor, aided by an unusually large olfactory lobe. Which species is it?
The Turkey Vulture can follow an odor released during decomposition to find carrion, even when the food is hidden from view. What sulfur-containing compound is this scent cue?
Rather than being produced through conventional industrial manufacturing, this kind of weapon is assembled from nonstandard or readily available materials. What general type of weapon is described?
An improvised firearm made from pipes and electrical tape was used by Tetsuya Yamagami at a campaign event in Nara in July 2022. Which former Japanese prime minister was killed in the attack?

This crystalline carbonate rock forms when limestone or dolostone recrystallizes under heat and pressure, producing interlocking grains that can take a high polish. What metamorphic stone, prized for sculpture and monumental architecture, is described?

In discussions of Marble as a sculptural stone, one of its best-known works was carved by Michelangelo from a single block of Carrara stone between 1501 and 1504. The original is displayed at Florence’s Galleria dell’Accademia; what is the sculpture’s title?

This English chemist and X-ray crystallographer earned a Cambridge PhD in 1945 after researching coal, then produced crucial evidence about DNA’s helical structure at King’s College London. Her work was underrecognized during her lifetime. Who was she?

At King’s College London, Rosalind Franklin’s work on DNA yielded a famous X-ray diffraction image taken by her student Raymond Gosling. Maurice Wilkins later showed the image to James Watson without Franklin’s permission; what is it commonly called?

After leaving King’s College London in 1953, Rosalind Franklin moved to Birkbeck College and led pioneering research on a rod-shaped plant pathogen whose particles contain RNA. Which pathogen was the focus of that research?

This electrochemical source converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy through redox reactions. During discharge, electrons flow through an external circuit, and the device may contain one cell or several; what is it called?
A battery can be made from this historically important arrangement, which used zinc and copper electrodes in separate solutions connected by a porous barrier. What is the arrangement called?
In a discharging battery, oxidation occurs at the negative electrode, which releases electrons into the external circuit. What is this electrode called?

In classical mechanics, this state occurs when all forces acting on an object or system cancel, leaving its acceleration at zero. It includes both configurations that return after a small displacement and those that move farther from their original arrangement.

In discussions of Mechanical Equilibrium, a ball at the bottom of a bowl illustrates this classification: after a small displacement, forces tend to move it back toward its original position. Its potential energy is at a minimum there. What is this type of equilibrium?
Which cereal grass was domesticated in Mexico from a wild ancestor? Its pollen-producing tassels grow at the top of the stalk, while ears with pollen-receiving silks grow lower down.
In corn’s domestication history, what wild grass is widely regarded as its ancestor? It bears only a small number of seeds in each pod, though the details of corn’s evolution remain debated.

These paired sensory organs collect light through a clear cornea and regulate its entry with an iris-controlled opening. Their retinas turn light into signals that travel to the brain along the optic nerves. What are these organs called?
In the eyes, what small central region of the macula provides the sharpest vision and has a dense concentration of cone photoreceptors?
In geology, what term names the mountain-building process driven by tectonic forces such as compression, folding, faulting, uplift, and plate collision?

Which Asian mountain range is being raised by the ongoing orogeny caused by the Indian Plate pushing into the Eurasian Plate? It includes the world’s highest peak and stretches across countries including Nepal, Bhutan, India, and China.
For a planar, cyclic, conjugated molecule, this aromaticity criterion predicts aromatic character when the ring contains 4n + 2 π electrons, with n an integer. What is this named rule?
Hückel's rule identifies aromatic rings with 4n + 2 π electrons. Which six-carbon hydrocarbon, with molecular formula C₆H₆, has a conjugated ring containing six π electrons?

During a total solar eclipse on 29 May 1919, astronomers photographed stars close to the Sun and measured their apparent displacement, testing Einstein’s prediction that gravity bends light. What is the established name of this landmark 1919 test?

During the Eddington experiment’s May 1919 eclipse observations, Arthur Eddington and Edwin Cottingham set up their station on this island in the Gulf of Guinea, while a separate British team observed in Brazil. Which island was it?

What name is given to the two broad, doughnut-shaped zones of energetic charged particles held around Earth by its magnetic field, where particles bounce along field lines between polar regions? Detected in 1958, these regions can expose passing satellites to hazardous particles.
Which U.S. spacecraft, launched on January 31, 1958, carried the instrument that first detected the Van Allen radiation belts? Its discovery made it the first successful American satellite.

This naturally occurring mixture of hydrocarbons forms underground over millions of years from buried ancient organisms. Refineries separate it into products such as gasoline, diesel, and kerosene. What resource is it?
In refining crude oil, what process separates its components by heating the mixture and collecting vapors as they condense at different temperatures in a column?

Founded at a conference in Baghdad in 1960 by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela, this intergovernmental organization coordinates member countries’ policies on crude oil production. What organization is it?
What software verification practice examines an individual class, function, or method on its own, using small-scale cases before those components are combined into a larger application?
In Java Unit Testing, which framework provides a Jupiter API where test methods can be marked with `@Test` and checks can be made with assertions such as `assertEquals`?

What term names the long-term rise in Earth’s average temperature, a trend greatly accelerated since the Industrial Revolution by burning coal, oil, and natural gas and associated with melting ice and rising sea levels?
Global warming is amplified when atmospheric gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation emitted by Earth’s surface. What is this heat-trapping atmospheric process called?
What is the hypothesized brief epoch in the very early universe when space expanded extraordinarily rapidly, helping explain why distant regions of the cosmos have similar properties?
Which American physicist proposed cosmic inflation in 1979, partly to address the magnetic-monopole problem in cosmology?
In many models of cosmic inflation, what is the hypothetical scalar field whose energy drives the rapid expansion and whose slow roll occurs along a nearly flat potential?

This nearly uniform, 2.7-kelvin glow of long-wavelength radiation fills the sky and is left over from the era when the early universe became transparent as charged particles formed neutral atoms. What is this relic radiation called?

In the history of the Cosmic Microwave Background, photons began traveling freely after the early universe cooled enough for neutral atoms to form. What is the name of the distant shell from which those photons were emitted?
The Cosmic Microwave Background was discovered serendipitously in 1964 by two radio astronomers at Bell Labs. Which German-born physicist was one of the co-discoverers, alongside Robert Wilson?
To map tiny temperature variations in the Cosmic Microwave Background, NASA launched a satellite in 1989 whose full name was Cosmic Background Explorer. What was the satellite’s acronym?

At the May 1942 Battle of the Coral Sea, aircraft launched from these vessels fought a major naval engagement even though the opposing surface fleets never sighted one another. The USS Abraham Lincoln is a Nimitz-class example of this ship type. What is it?
Which May 1942 battle near Papua New Guinea was the first in which opposing aircraft carriers fought without their fleets ever sighting one another, and halted Japan’s advance toward Port Moresby?

When describing a measurable quantity without reference to particular units, scientists specify how it depends on fundamental kinds such as mass, length, and time. What are these fundamental quantity-types called?

Physical dimensions can be combined as powers of mass, length, and time. What term describes a measurable value whose net powers of all fundamental dimensions cancel to zero, as with the Reynolds number?
Which body system includes the brain and spinal cord as well as nerves that extend throughout the body? It transmits electrical signals to coordinate sensation, movement, and other bodily functions.

Within the nervous system, what long projection of a neuron carries electrical impulses away from the cell body and is often insulated by a myelin sheath? Unlike this projection, a neuron typically has many branching dendrites.

This traveling disturbance transfers energy from one place to another, while particles in many media oscillate around their equilibrium positions rather than traveling with it. Its disturbance may be perpendicular or parallel to its direction of travel.
For a periodic wave, this quantity counts the cycles passing a fixed point per unit time. It is the inverse of the period and is commonly measured in hertz.

This silvery-white element has atomic number 13 and is one of the most abundant metals in Earth’s crust, though it is usually bound in minerals. Industry produces it from bauxite by refining alumina and then electrolyzing it in molten cryolite; what is the element?
In industrial production of Aluminum, this process uses electrolysis to extract the metal from alumina dissolved in molten cryolite. What is the name of this process?

Which Danish physicist introduced a 1913 atomic model in which electrons occupy discrete energy levels around a compact nucleus, helping explain the hydrogen spectrum? He later received the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics.

Niels Bohr helped develop a prominent account of quantum mechanics with Werner Heisenberg and other physicists. It emphasizes the role of experimental arrangements in measurement and the probabilistic nature of quantum predictions; what is this account commonly called?
Unlike insects, this eight-legged arachnid has two main body regions and no antennae. Every member produces silk from spinnerets, although not all use webs to catch prey. What animal is it?
The topic Spider concerns an animal classified in a specific order of arachnids; mites, ticks, and scorpions are arachnids but are not members of that order. What is the order’s scientific name?
An industrial equilibrium process uses steam to convert carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide while producing additional fuel gas. What is this process called?
In the water-gas shift reaction, carbon monoxide reacts with water to form carbon dioxide and a second product. Which diatomic gas is that product and is also combined with nitrogen to make ammonia?

These New World social insects snip fresh leaves and other vegetation into fragments, then use the material to cultivate a food crop in underground nests rather than eating the plant matter themselves. What are they commonly called?

In leafcutter ants, workers tend an underground crop grown on the plant fragments they bring back to the nest; the colony consumes this crop rather than the leaves themselves. What type of organism forms the cultivated food?
This adaptor molecule recognizes messenger-RNA codons with its anticodon and carries the amino acid specified by each codon to the site of protein assembly. What type of RNA performs this role?

Which molecular biologist proposed that Transfer RNA can recognize multiple codons through flexible base pairing, later called wobble pairing, and also formulated the Central Dogma of molecular biology?

Traditionally made from charcoal, sulfur, and potassium nitrate, this combustible mixture was granulated in a process called corning. What material was stored in barrels beneath Parliament during the 1605 plot associated with Guy Fawkes?
The Gunpowder Plot was an attempt to kill this monarch, the first Stuart king of England. He commissioned the English Bible translation that bears his name; who was he?

A severe deficiency of ascorbic acid disrupts collagen production and can lead to bleeding gums, loose teeth, and poor wound healing. What disease was historically common among crews on long-distance sea voyages?
Scurvy became less common among European land-dwellers after a vitamin-C-rich tuber from South America was introduced and widely adopted as food. What crop was it?

What vector quantity is calculated by dividing displacement by elapsed time and includes both magnitude and direction? Its SI unit is meters per second, and it differs from a scalar quantity that records only magnitude.

In contrast to velocity, what scalar quantity describes only the magnitude of an object's motion and gives no direction? It is calculated from distance traveled over elapsed time rather than displacement over elapsed time.

This flattened, membrane-bound compartment inside a chloroplast is where the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis occur. Its disk-like structures can be arranged in stacks called grana; what is the compartment called?

In a thylakoid membrane, this green pigment absorbs mainly blue-violet and red light while reflecting much of the green light. Its molecules are embedded in photosystems that drive the light-dependent reactions; what is the pigment?

This opioid antagonist can displace opioids from receptors and rapidly restore breathing during a potentially fatal overdose, although its effects may wear off before those of the opioid. What is the generic name of the medication commonly administered as a nasal spray for this purpose?

In May 2022, Illinois Governor J.B. Pritzker signed a law eliminating co-pays for a nasal-spray version of naloxone used to reverse opioid overdoses. What familiar brand name is associated with this medication?
This dense, silvery metal is liquid at ordinary room temperature and has the chemical symbol Hg. What element has atomic number 80?
Mercury rarely occurs as a free metal in nature. What red mercury sulfide mineral is its principal ore?
What device uses electromagnetic fields to drive ions or electrons to very high speeds? Researchers use it in experiments probing atomic nuclei and fundamental matter.
At Dubna, researchers used a particle accelerator to bombard americium-243 with calcium-48 ions, producing atoms of the synthetic element with atomic number 115. What element was produced?

In plant–fungus partnerships, fungal filaments connect with a plant’s roots, creating a normally mutualistic exchange: the plant supplies sugars while the fungus improves access to water and mineral nutrients. What is the name of this association?

When describing Mycorrhiza and nutrient movement through forest soils, which Canadian forest ecologist’s work on Douglas-fir networks and so-called “mother trees” brought public attention to connections among trees? Her field research was largely conducted in British Columbia.

In Mycorrhiza, fungi can extend absorptive hyphae beyond a root’s depletion zone, helping a plant obtain this element, often in the poorly mobile phosphate form. Which element is being acquired in exchange for carbon-rich sugars supplied by the plant?

Launched by NASA in 1977, this spacecraft made flybys of Jupiter and Saturn before continuing to Uranus and Neptune. It remains the only spacecraft to have flown past both of those ice giants. Which spacecraft is it?

During Voyager 2’s 1989 flyby, this planet was found to have exceptionally fast winds and a large storm system known as the Great Dark Spot. It is the eighth planet from the Sun and has Triton as its largest moon. Which planet is it?

Guido van Rossum began creating this interpreted, general-purpose programming language in December 1989. It groups statements into code blocks through indentation and offers an extensive standard library. What language is it?

Python’s creator named the language after a British comedy television series, not a reptile. The show’s title combines a comedian’s first name with a term for a troupe of performers and a venue for spectacles; what was it called?

For a pendulum or another repeating motion, this quantity measures the time needed to complete one full cycle. It is the reciprocal of the number of cycles completed per unit time. What is this quantity?
For a periodic motion, the period is the time for one complete cycle. What quantity counts how many cycles occur each second and is measured in hertz?

An English theoretical physicist, he held Cambridge’s Lucasian Professorship from 1979 to 2009 and worked with Roger Penrose on singularities in general relativity. He also predicted that black holes emit radiation and wrote the 1988 book *A Brief History of Time*. Who was this scientist?
Stephen Hawking’s 1988 book for general readers explores the universe’s origin and fate, including cosmology and black holes. What is the title of this book?

This intelligence practice analyzes intercepted encrypted communications to recover their concealed messages, sometimes without knowing the key. Unlike cryptography, which creates protective systems, it seeks to defeat them; what is this practice?

During World War II, this British mathematician and logician worked at Bletchley Park, where his contributions to Codebreaking helped attack German Enigma communications. He is also the namesake of a theoretical machine that models computation; who was he?
Members of the genus Betula are deciduous plants often recognized by pale, peeling bark and hanging catkins. What is their common name?
Among birch trees, one North American species has bright white bark that peels into thin, curling sheets and was traditionally used to make lightweight canoes. What is this species’ scientific name?

Its atoms form a rigid crystal lattice, and the mineral ranks 10 on the Mohs scale. Pure specimens are colorless, while impurities and defects can produce a range of colors. What is this crystalline form of carbon?
Diamond and graphite are both solid allotropes of the same element, whose atomic number is 6 and whose chemical symbol is C. What is that element?

Natural Diamond commonly forms deep in Earth’s mantle and reaches the surface in volcanic pipes made of a dark ultramafic igneous rock named for the South African mining city of Kimberley. What is this rock called?

At room temperature and pressure, Diamond is metastable relative to the thermodynamically stable allotrope of carbon, which has layers of hexagonally arranged atoms and conducts electricity. What is that allotrope?

One laboratory route for producing Diamond starts with hydrocarbon gases and builds a crystal in a low-pressure chamber, rather than compressing carbon at extreme pressure. What is this technique, abbreviated CVD?

Defined by very low precipitation rather than by high temperatures, this biome includes both hot regions such as the Sahara and cold polar regions such as Antarctica. Its landscapes may feature wind-shaped sand seas called ergs and groundwater-fed oases. What biome is it?
In the Sahara Desert, this small canid’s oversized ears help it release body heat and locate prey, while fur on its feet protects them from hot sand. What animal is it?

When a wave crosses at an angle from one material into another where it travels at a different speed, its path changes direction. What is this phenomenon, which makes a partly submerged pencil appear bent?

Refraction at a boundary can be predicted using the refractive indices of the two materials and the angles each ray makes with the perpendicular to that boundary. What law is written as n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂?

Which analytical technique converts sample molecules into gas-phase ions, separates those ions according to their inertia relative to their electric charge, and records their signals as a spectrum? Scientists use its peaks to investigate a sample’s composition and identify substances in complex mixtures.

In mass spectrometry, which method applies a strong electric field to a liquid sample, forming charged droplets that release gas-phase ions as solvent evaporates? It is especially useful for large biomolecules and often produces ions carrying multiple charges.

Which temporary organ forms an interface between a developing fetus and the mother, exchanging oxygen and nutrients with the fetus through a connecting structure? It is expelled from the body during the third stage of labor.
Which structure connects the fetus to the placenta and carries oxygen and nutrients between them during pregnancy? After birth, it is clamped and cut.

A torque-free rigid body's motion can be depicted by an inertia ellipsoid rolling without slipping on a fixed plane while its kinetic energy and angular momentum remain conserved. What is this geometric representation called?

In the Poinsot construction, the contact point of the rolling inertia ellipsoid traces a curve on the fixed plane perpendicular to the conserved angular momentum. Unlike the body-fixed curve called the polhode, what is this plane-fixed curve called?

In thermodynamics, this is energy transferred between systems because they have different temperatures; unlike internal energy, it describes energy in transit rather than something stored in a system. Its familiar modes of transfer are conduction, convection, and radiation. What is this quantity?
Heat travels through a metal spoon from its hot end toward its cooler handle through microscopic interactions, without bulk movement of the material. What mode of heat transfer is this?
This Mediterranean evergreen has aromatic leaves used in cooking and was sacred in antiquity. Its branches were fashioned into crowns to honor victors in Greece and Rome. What tree is it?
Bay laurel was sacred to a Greek deity associated with prophecy, music, and healing. In classical myth, the nymph Daphne was transformed into this tree while fleeing his pursuit. Which deity was it?
In chemistry, this term describes the attractive interaction that holds atoms together. Its major forms include ionic, covalent, and metallic varieties.

One major kind of chemical bond forms when electrons are transferred from a metal to a nonmetal, creating oppositely charged ions. What type of bond is held together by the electrostatic attraction between those ions?

These immune-system components include lymphocytes, neutrophils, and basophils. Unlike the oxygen-carrying red kind, they help defend the body against infection; what broad class of circulating immune components are they?

Within white blood cells, one lymphocyte lineage is named for the organ where it matures. Some of these cells coordinate immune responses as helpers, while others destroy infected targets; what are they called?
This synthetic radioactive actinide has atomic number 99 and the symbol Es. Named for the physicist associated with special relativity, which element is it?
Scientists first identified Einsteinium in radioactive debris from which 1952 U.S. thermonuclear test at Enewetak Atoll? It was the first successful full-scale test of a hydrogen bomb.

This famous X-ray binary pairs a massive blue supergiant with a compact object whose mass places it among the strongest stellar-mass black-hole candidates. Its intense X-ray emission and 5.6-day orbit have made it a landmark system in studies of black holes. What system is it?

In Cygnus X-1, the black-hole candidate is paired with an O-type supergiant whose powerful stellar wind supplies material to the accretion flow. What catalog designation identifies this companion star?

In this dynamic state, the forward and reverse reactions proceed at equal rates, so concentrations remain constant even though reactions continue. Its composition at a fixed temperature is characterized by a constant conventionally written K. What is this state called?

In electrochemical studies of chemical equilibrium, which equation relates electrode potential to the activities or concentrations of reacting species? At equilibrium, it can also relate a redox reaction’s standard potential to its equilibrium constant.
In the Hardy–Weinberg model, the category with frequency 2pq describes individuals carrying two different alleles at one locus. What is this category called?

A heterozygous genotype at the beta-globin gene can help protect people in malaria-endemic regions from severe malaria, even though inheriting two disease-associated copies can cause sickle-cell disease. What evolutionary phenomenon does this example illustrate?

During transcription, this enzyme reads a DNA template and joins ribonucleotides to form an RNA strand. It begins at a promoter and moves along the gene as the RNA molecule grows. What is this enzyme called?

In bacteria, RNA polymerase uses a detachable subunit to recognize promoter DNA, including the characteristic −10 and −35 regions. This subunit commonly dissociates after transcription begins. What is it called?

A spacecraft can alter its path by passing close to a moving planet and exchanging momentum with it, changing its speed and direction without using equivalent propellant. What is this technique called?

During its Grand Tour of the outer planets, which NASA spacecraft used a chain of gravity-assist maneuvers to visit Jupiter and Saturn before becoming the only spacecraft to fly past Uranus and Neptune?

This SI derived unit measures magnetic flux density, the magnetic flux passing through a unit area. It is equal to one weber per square meter and is named in honor of a pioneering figure in electromagnetism. What is the unit?
The tesla is defined as one of these units per square meter. This SI derived unit measures magnetic flux, rather than magnetic flux density. What unit is it?

Which elementary particle, with spin zero, was announced by the ATLAS and CMS collaborations in 2012 after experiments at the Large Hadron Collider? It is an excitation of a quantum field whose interactions give mass to certain fundamental particles, including the W and Z particles.

The Higgs boson is associated with a field that gives mass to certain particles, but this carrier of the electromagnetic force does not interact with that field and remains massless. What particle is it?

In oxygenic photosynthesis, which thylakoid-membrane reaction-center complex absorbs light and extracts electrons from water, releasing molecular oxygen before passing electrons into the transport chain? It is the first major complex in the linear photosynthetic electron-transfer pathway.
In Photosystem II, what is the lumen-facing catalytic assembly that contains a manganese-calcium cluster and cycles through S-states as it removes electrons from water?

What broad class of solid Earth material forms when molten material cools and solidifies, whether magma underground or lava at the surface? Its members are commonly distinguished as intrusive or extrusive, and include both coarse-grained formations and porous volcanic material.
Within igneous rocks, which usually felsic, coarse-grained intrusive rock forms as magma cools slowly beneath Earth’s surface and makes up large portions of the continents?

On the celestial sphere, what coordinate plays the role of longitude on Earth, with its zero point at the vernal equinox and values measured eastward around the sky? It is commonly expressed in hours, minutes, and seconds and is used with a second coordinate to locate stars.

In the equatorial coordinate system, what coordinate is paired with Right Ascension and measures an object's angular distance north or south of the celestial equator? Like terrestrial latitude, it is expressed in degrees and ranges from −90° to +90°.

Unlike wind-driven surface flows, this planet-spanning movement of deep ocean water is driven by seawater density contrasts generated mainly by differences in warmth and dissolved salt. What is this process called?

Thermohaline circulation describes density-driven movement of deep ocean water, while Earth’s rotation also deflects ocean currents. What effect explains why moving water is deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere?

In this atomic process, a heavy atomic nucleus breaks into smaller nuclei, releasing energy and often neutrons that can trigger further reactions. What is this process, which can be sustained when enough fissile material is assembled?
In the history of nuclear fission, which graphite-and-uranium lattice built beneath Stagg Field produced the first controlled, self-sustaining chain reaction in December 1942?

Unlike smooth, layered motion, this irregular regime of liquid or gas flow features fluctuating velocities and pressure, along with swirling structures that mix heat and other material. It is commonly associated with flows at higher values of a dimensionless quantity comparing inertia with viscosity. What is this regime called?

In turbulence, a dimensionless flow parameter compares inertial forces with viscous forces and helps characterize whether irregular motion is favored. What is this parameter, commonly used to describe transitions in pipe flow?
As a comet approaches the Sun, its icy nucleus releases gas and dust, forming a diffuse envelope around the nucleus. What is this surrounding cloud called?
In a cometary coma, sunlight warms frozen material on the nucleus and releases gas directly from the solid state, without passing through a liquid phase. What is this phase change called?
What iron-based alloy gains corrosion resistance from a substantial chromium content and was used for the reflective exterior of Anish Kapoor’s Cloud Gate in Chicago’s Millennium Park?
In stainless steel, which metallic element forms a protective surface oxide that helps the alloy resist corrosion?
These towering formations can extend through much of the troposphere and produce thunderstorms, hail, and lightning. Strong winds near their tops can spread them into a broad, flattened cap.

In August 2020, a pyrocumulonimbus—a fire-generated form of cumulonimbus clouds—spawned a tornado in Lassen County, prompting the National Weather Service’s first-ever warning for a tornado produced by one of these clouds. In which U.S. state did this event occur?

Produced inward by the vascular cambium in woody plants, this vascular tissue carries water and dissolved mineral ions from roots toward stems and leaves. Its main conducting cells include tracheids and vessel elements. What is this tissue called?

When water evaporates from leaf surfaces, the resulting tension draws water upward through a continuous column in xylem, without an active pump in the stem. What is this water-moving mechanism called?

These highly reactive elements occupy Group 1 of the periodic table, typically have one electron in their outermost shell, and include lithium, sodium, and potassium. What is the common name for this family?
Within the Alkali Metals, which element has atomic number 55 and a pale-gold appearance? Its isotope 133 is used to define the second in atomic timekeeping.
This quantized property of matter can be positive or negative and causes objects to experience electromagnetic forces. Its total amount in an isolated system is conserved.
Electric charge is measured in this SI unit. One unit is the amount transferred by a current of one ampere flowing for one second.
Electric charge on an electron or proton has a magnitude equal to this fundamental quantity, approximately 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs. Ordinary charges occur in integer multiples of it.

Electric charge is central to this inverse-square law, which gives the force between two charges as proportional to their product and inversely proportional to the square of their separation. Its namesake investigated the relationship using a torsion balance.
Electric charge was studied in this 1909 measurement, in which Harvey Fletcher helped suspend charged oil droplets against gravity by adjusting an electric field.

This group of seed-producing plants includes conifers, cycads, ginkgo, and gnetophytes. Unlike flowering plants, its ovules and seeds are not enclosed within an ovary. What is this plant group called?

Gymnosperms bear exposed seeds, while members of this other major plant group enclose their seeds within an ovary that typically develops into a fruit. What is this group, which includes flowering plants?
A ferromagnetic substance loses spontaneous magnetization and becomes paramagnetic upon reaching a characteristic thermal threshold. What is the eponymous name of that threshold?

Above the Curie point, ferromagnetic ordering disappears. The molecular-field account of ferromagnetism was developed by a French physicist who also proposed that magnets contain regions of uniform magnetization; which physicist was this?
What optical instrument uses visible illumination passing through glass lenses to magnify specimens? Its stage and eyepiece can be used to examine microorganisms in a drop of pond water.
When viewed under a light microscope, what single-celled organism can change its shape, extend pseudopodia to move, and engulf prey by phagocytosis?

An uncontrolled event occurs when fuel reacts rapidly with an oxidizer, releasing heat and often light and smoke. When it spreads through buildings, vegetation, or industrial facilities, it can cause widespread destruction. What is this event?

Fire requires three essentials for ordinary combustion: a fuel, an oxidizer such as oxygen, and enough heat to sustain the reaction. What model names these three requirements, any one of which can be removed to suppress combustion?
In this circuit arrangement, all components lie along one path, so the same current passes through each resistor. What is the arrangement in which the resistances can be added directly?

For components in a series connection, their individual opposition to current is added to model the entire group as one component with the same effect. What is the name of that single replacement value?

This group of flightless aquatic birds is native to the Southern Hemisphere and includes the Adélie and emperor species. One species lives as far north as the Galápagos Islands. What are these birds called?

Among penguins, which species is the largest living member of the group and breeds in Antarctica during the polar winter? Its males keep the single egg on their feet beneath a brood pouch while incubating it.
Which group of aquatic mammals belongs to the cetaceans and is widely recognized for streamlined bodies, high intelligence, and often social behavior?
Dolphins produce trains of high-frequency clicks and interpret the returning echoes to locate prey and navigate, even when visibility is poor. What is this biological sensing ability called?

The FAA defines this engine-driven, heavier-than-air aircraft as being supported in flight by air acting on fixed wings. As it moves through the atmosphere, its wings generate lift, while a propeller or jet engine provides thrust to counter drag. What kind of aircraft is it?

Built by two brothers who ran a bicycle repair shop, this historic airplane used a gasoline engine to drive two pusher propellers. What aircraft made its first successful powered, controlled flight at Kitty Hawk on December 17, 1903?

While studying at Harvard, he created Facemash and then helped launch a social-networking service for college students in 2004. Which American technology entrepreneur went on to serve as that company’s chief executive?
Mark Zuckerberg co-founded a social network whose engineers developed Hack, a dialect of PHP, and whose user-data practices drew scrutiny in the Cambridge Analytica scandal. What company was it?
On Chicago’s Museum Campus beside Lake Michigan, this public attraction for observing aquatic life opened in 1930 after receiving a major gift from a local businessman. Which institution is it?
Shedd Aquarium stands beside this natural-history institution on Chicago’s Museum Campus. Its collections include Sue, the famous Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton. Which institution is it?

In gaseous BeF₂, a central beryllium atom is bonded to two fluorine atoms. Under VSEPR theory, the two bonding regions arrange themselves as far apart as possible; what is the name of the resulting arrangement?
In examples of linear molecular geometry, which gaseous compound has a central atom with atomic number 4 bonded to two fluorine atoms, while its liquid form adopts a tetrahedral arrangement?

What name is given to accumulated excrement from seabirds or bats, especially deposits prized for their high nitrogen and phosphorus content? Historically, this material was used both to enrich farmland and as a source of ingredients for gunpowder.

Guano became a major export from this South American country during the 19th century, when seabird deposits from its offshore islands were shipped abroad as fertilizer. Which country was at the center of the historic guano trade?
In water-quality monitoring, what quantity describes a liquid’s relative cloudiness or lack of clarity when suspended particles scatter light?

When measuring turbidity in a water sample, technicians may use an optical instrument that shines light into the sample and detects light scattered at roughly a right angle. What is this instrument called?

This transparent, roughly millimeter-long soil nematode became a foundational model organism for studying development and genetics. It was the first multicellular organism to have its complete genome sequenced; what is its scientific name?

In Caenorhabditis elegans, Andrew Fire and Craig Mello showed that introducing double-stranded RNA could silence a gene with a matching sequence. What gene-silencing process did they uncover, for which they later shared the 2006 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine?
On 12 April 1961, a Soviet spacecraft carrying a single cosmonaut completed the first crewed orbital flight around Earth. What was the spacecraft called?
Vostok 1 carried a Soviet Air Force pilot who orbited Earth once in a flight lasting about 108 minutes. What was the pilot’s name?
This airplane component extends laterally from the fuselage and generates lift as it moves through the air. It may carry flaps and ailerons that help control lift and roll. What is it?
For an aircraft wing in an idealized flow, which theorem relates lift per unit span to air density, freestream speed, and circulation? Its equation is commonly written as L′ = ρVΓ.

First synthesized in 1874 and later widely used against mosquitoes and agricultural pests, this persistent organochlorine insecticide became notorious for bioaccumulating and harming wildlife. What insecticide is it?
Rachel Carson’s 1962 book helped focus public opposition to agricultural DDT by warning of its environmental effects. What book is it?
In force since 2004, this international treaty formalized a worldwide ban on agricultural use of DDT while allowing limited public-health use under WHO guidelines. What treaty is it?
This inherited human classification is based on antigens on red blood cells. Its familiar labels combine an ABO designation—A, B, AB, or O—with a positive or negative designation. What is it called?
In discussions of blood type, which common ABO and RhD combination is often called the universal red-cell donor because its red cells have neither A nor B antigens and lack the D antigen?
This family of electroanalytical techniques records current as an applied potential is varied, often using a three-electrode setup to investigate redox behavior. What is this family of techniques?
In voltammetry, which component in a typical three-part cell is the site of analyte oxidation or reduction, and has its potential varied relative to the reference?

This nitrogen-containing structural polysaccharide is built from repeating N-acetylglucosamine units and occurs in fungal cell walls as well as the protective outer skeletons of arthropods. What is it?
In chitin, each repeating unit is a glucose derivative with an acetylated amino group. What is the name of this amino sugar building block?

In quantum mechanics, this mathematical function represents the state of a particle, and its squared magnitude gives the probability density for finding the particle in a particular location. What is this function commonly symbolized by the Greek letter psi?
The wave function evolves according to an equation named for this Austrian physicist, who also proposed a famous thought experiment involving a cat in a sealed box with poison. Who was he?
After a dispute with John Sculley led him to leave Apple, this entrepreneur founded NeXT and became an early force behind Pixar. He later returned to Apple as CEO; who was he?
Steve Jobs invested in this company after it spun out of Lucasfilm’s computer division. Its production logo features a hopping desk lamp, and Disney acquired the company in 2006; what is its name?

This NASA rover landed at Meridiani Planum in January 2004 and continued operating for nearly 15 years, far beyond its planned 90-sol mission. A planet-wide dust storm eventually cut off communications with it in 2018. What was the rover’s name?

Opportunity began exploring Meridiani Planum after landing in a small impact crater, where it examined exposed bedrock and iron-rich spherules nicknamed “blueberries.” What was the name of that landing crater?
In humans, the crown of each is covered by enamel, while its root is anchored in the jaw. Incisors, canines, and molars are specialized forms of these structures. What are they?
In human teeth, this mineralized tissue coats the crown, with dentin beneath it and the pulp chamber deeper inside. What is this protective outer layer?
This tin-based alloy has long been used to make household vessels such as dishes, pitchers, and tankards. What is its traditional name?
In a traditional formulation of pewter, tin is blended with a metalloid whose chemical symbol is Sb. What is this alloying element?

Formaldehyde, benzene, and sugars have very different structures and uses, but all belong to a broad class of carbon-containing substances often associated with biological processes. What is this class called?
Formaldehyde is an organic compound made industrially by oxidizing a particular alcohol. Which simplest one-carbon alcohol, with the formula CH₃OH, is used in this process?

In this type of covalent-bond breaking, the shared electron pair splits evenly, with each bonded atom retaining one electron. This produces radical fragments rather than oppositely charged ions. What is this process called?

In discussions of homolytic cleavage, chemists assign a numerical quantity, usually reported in kJ/mol, that measures the input required to separate a covalently linked pair of atoms into radical fragments. What is this quantity called?

In the Bayer designation system, what Greek-letter name is traditionally assigned to the brightest star in a constellation? The convention is not always followed in practice, as the brightness ranking of Betelgeuse and Rigel illustrates.

In the Bayer system, Alpha is usually assigned to a constellation’s brightest star, but Betelgeuse is its Alpha star while Rigel, its Beta star, often shines brighter. The same constellation is also recognizable by three bright stars forming a belt. Which constellation is it?

Released by motor neurons at the neuromuscular junction, this chemical messenger binds receptors on skeletal-muscle fibers and triggers their contraction. It also acts at receptors in the nervous system; what is it?
Acetylcholine and nicotine both activate a class of ligand-gated ion channels in the nervous system. What is this class called?

On a pressure–temperature phase diagram, this is the unique condition where the solid–liquid, solid–gas, and liquid–gas boundaries meet. For a pure substance, all three phases coexist there in thermodynamic equilibrium. What is this condition called?
Until 2019, the triple point of water provided the defining reference for this SI base unit. Its modern definition fixes the value of the Boltzmann constant. What unit is it?
What term describes the tendency of genes located close together on the same chromosome to be inherited together, though crossing over can sometimes separate them?

Which American geneticist used experiments with fruit flies to map genes to chromosomes and establish classic evidence for Genetic Linkage? He received the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning the role of chromosomes in heredity.

This middle period of the Mesozoic followed the Triassic and preceded the Cretaceous, beginning around 201 million years ago. Its name comes from a European mountain range where characteristic limestone strata were first identified. What period is it?

In the Jurassic, fossils of this feathered animal were found in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria. Its long bony tail and toothed jaws are among the features that made it a key fossil in discussions of the origin of birds. What is it?
During the Jurassic breakup of Pangaea, this northern landmass developed separately from Gondwana and included the ancestors of North America and Eurasia. What was this landmass called?
An English chemist and theologian, he used a lens to heat mercuric oxide in 1774 and collected a gas that he interpreted as “dephlogisticated air” within phlogiston theory. Who was he?
Joseph Priestley isolated a gas in 1774 by heating mercuric oxide and called it “dephlogisticated air.” Antoine Lavoisier later linked this gas to combustion; what is it called today?
